classes.name: console
classes.brief: Prints a value on its own line, so that C# console.log and Console.WriteLine calls port to Ring unchanged.
classes.description: It has two methods, log and WriteLine, which do the same. A list prints one item per line. Build it as new console.
classes.example:
o1.log("hello")
#--> hello
o1.WriteLine(42)
#--> 42

methods.name: log
methods.brief: Prints the value on its own line, as the C# call of the same name does.

parameters.name: str
parameters.role: the value to print

methods.name: WriteLine
methods.brief: Prints the value on its own line, as the C# call of the same name does.

parameters.name: str
parameters.role: the value to print

classes.name: IntObject
classes.brief: Holds the limits of a whole number the way C# int.MinValue and int.MaxValue name them, for porting C# code to Ring.
classes.description: The global int is one of these. The limits are the library's calculable-integer limits, 15 nines, and they come back as text with underscores, so they print well and do not compare. Build one without parentheses: new IntObject() raises R3.

methods.name: getMinValue
methods.brief: Returns the smallest whole number that Ring can compute with exactly, written with underscores.
methods.returns: a text such as -999_999_999_999_999, not a number
notes: the value is the library's calculable limit, not the 32-bit limit of a C# int
warnings: the answer is a text: comparing it with a number or adding to it raises R41 (Invalid numeric string) or joins text; convert it with number() after removing the underscores

methods.name: getMaxValue
methods.brief: Returns the largest whole number that Ring can compute with exactly, written with underscores.
methods.returns: a text such as 999_999_999_999_999, not a number
notes: the value is the library's calculable limit, not the 32-bit limit of a C# int
warnings: the answer is a text: comparing it with a number raises R41 (Invalid numeric string) and adding 1 joins text

classes.name: say
classes.brief: Closes a say { ... } brace of ported Perl or Raku code and prints the answer that a ternary left in the named variable say.
classes.description: In Raku, say prints the value of an expression. Here the brace body is a Softanza ternary: b(condition) '??' bt(trueValue) '!!' bf(falseValue), which stores its answer in the named variable say, and the end of the brace prints it. The global say is already one of these. A brace that holds anything else prints the previous answer, or an empty line.

methods.name: braceend
methods.brief: Prints the value that the last ternary b(...) '??' bt(...) '!!' bf(...) put in the named variable say, when the brace closes.
notes: one empty line when no ternary has run yet
warnings: any other brace body leaves the variable as it was, so say { 5 } prints the previous answer, or an empty line before any

classes.name: stzAccessibilityTree
classes.brief: Holds what a screen reader reads from a screen, emitted from the declared document and the laid-out panel and not inferred.
classes.description: A browser infers an accessibility tree from markup; this emits one from declared intent. Each declaration becomes a node with an id (its name), a role (the ROLE field, or window, label or group by default), a name (the LABEL, a text's content, or for a button and the like the text beneath it), a description (the RATIONALE), its bounds from the laid-out panel, whether a keyboard can reach it, and what can be done there. ToJSON gives the whole tree as data. There is no switch to turn it off. The document must be clean, and the tree needs the layout engine but no GPU and no window.
classes.receiver: cDoc = 'DEFINE PANEL form ( SIZE [300, 200], DIRECTION column, CHILDREN [title, ok_btn] ) RATIONALE "A tiny form."' + char(10) + 'DEFINE TEXT title ( CONTENT "Transfer", SIZE 20, ROLE heading ) RATIONALE "What the form is for."' + char(10) + 'DEFINE BOX ok_btn ( HEIGHT 40, FOCUSABLE yes, ROLE button, CHILDREN [ok_text] ) RATIONALE "The act."' + char(10) + 'DEFINE TEXT ok_text ( CONTENT "Confirm", SIZE 16 ) RATIONALE "button label"' oU = new stzUiDocument(cDoc) oU.UseFont("C:/Windows/Fonts/segoeui.ttf") oP = oU.ToPanel() oP.FocusOn("ok_btn") o1 = new stzAccessibilityTree(oU, oP)
classes.example:
? o1.NodeCount()
#--> 4
? o1.RoleOf("ok_btn")
#--> button
? o1.NameOf("ok_btn")
#--> Confirm
? o1.DescriptionOf("ok_btn")
#--> The act.
? @@( o1.FocusableIds() )
#--> [ "ok_btn" ]
? @@( o1.NodeOf("ok_btn")[:bounds] )
#--> [ 0, 24, 300, 40 ]
? o1.ReadingOrder()[3]
#--> button "Confirm"

methods.name: init
methods.brief: Builds the accessibility tree of a screen from its declared document and, if given, its laid-out panel.

parameters.name: poDoc
parameters.role: the stzUiDocument, which must be clean

parameters.name: poPanel
parameters.role: the stzPanel made from it by ToPanel, or NULL when bounds and focus are not known

methods.returns: nothing; the tree is built when the object is made
notes: there is no flag to switch it off; with NULL for the panel every bounds is empty and no node is focused
warnings: a value that is not a document raises error stzAccessibilityTree: give an stzUiDocument; a document that is not clean raises error ... the document is not clean -- ask Report() why

methods.name: Nodes
methods.brief: Returns every node of the tree in reading order, depth first, in the order the author declared them.
methods.returns: a list of hash lists with the keys id, role, name, description, bounds, focusable, focused, actions, depth and children
notes: the first node is the panel itself, as a window

methods.name: NodeCount
methods.brief: Returns how many nodes the tree holds.
notes: one node for each declaration, the panel included

methods.name: NodeOf
methods.brief: Returns one node by its id.

parameters.name: pcId
parameters.role: the name of the declaration, matched as written

methods.returns: a hash list with the keys id, role, name, description, bounds, focusable, focused, actions, depth and children; [ ] for an id the tree does not hold
notes: bounds is [ x, y, width, height ] from the laid-out panel, or [ ] when no panel was given; actions is focus and click for a focusable node and empty otherwise

methods.name: HasNode
methods.brief: TRUE if the tree holds a node with an id.

parameters.name: pcId
parameters.role: the name of the declaration, matched as written

methods.name: RoleOf
methods.brief: Returns what a screen reader announces a node as.

parameters.name: pcId
parameters.role: the name of the declaration

methods.returns: the role as text such as button, heading or label; the panel is window, a text defaults to label and any other box to group; an empty text for an unknown id
notes: the role comes from the ROLE field of the declaration or from the style it uses

methods.name: NameOf
methods.brief: Returns what a screen reader says for a node.

parameters.name: pcId
parameters.role: the name of the declaration

methods.returns: the name as text: the LABEL, else a text's own content, else for a button, link, heading, label, list item, tab, checkbox or radio the text of its descendants; an empty text for a window, group, textbox or unknown id
notes: name from content is gated by role, as ARIA gates it, so a window is not named after the whole screen

methods.name: DescriptionOf
methods.brief: Returns the sentence saying why a node exists, taken from the declaration's RATIONALE.

parameters.name: pcId
parameters.role: the name of the declaration

methods.returns: the description as text; an empty text for an unknown id
notes: every declaration carries a rationale, so every node has a description

methods.name: FocusableIds
methods.brief: Returns the ids of the nodes a keyboard can reach, in reading order.
methods.returns: a list of text; [ ] when none
notes: it comes from the same FOCUSABLE field that builds the tab ring, so reading order and keyboard order cannot drift

methods.name: ReadingOrder
methods.brief: Returns what a reader would announce, one line per node, as role and then the quoted name.
methods.returns: a list of text such as button "Confirm"; a node with no name gives its role alone
notes: the lines follow the order of Nodes

methods.name: ToJSON
methods.brief: Returns the whole tree as JSON text, one object per node, for a tool or an agent to read.
methods.returns: a JSON text; bounds is null when unknown, never a zero rectangle
notes: the children are stated explicitly, and depth stays so the flat list reads in order

methods.name: SaveTo
methods.brief: Writes the tree as JSON to a file.

parameters.name: pcPath
parameters.role: the path of the file to write

notes: an existing file is overwritten

classes.name: stzAgentDeclaration
classes.brief: Reads and judges a .pia agent file at load, then builds the runnable agent it declares if, and only if, no rule is broken.
classes.description: An agent is a file: name, kind (pi acts, llm proposes), a coverage sentence, a reversibility class, a schedule, optional seed facts, governance, skills in a small closed vocabulary (always, fact, no-fact, recall, learn, forget, propose, ring:), or a proposal for an llm agent. The declaration is judged in the constructor and every broken rule becomes a finding: IsValid, Findings and CiteFindings read the verdict, and ToAgent refuses to build from a refused one. Reading never calls a model or a network. The format version is 2; version 1 is still read.
classes.receiver: c = "pia: 2" + char(10) + "name: kitchen-bot" + char(10) + "kind: pi" + char(10) + "coverage: watches stock" + char(10) + "reversibility: compensable" + char(10) + "schedule:" + char(10) + "  timer: 20" + char(10) + "skills:" + char(10) + "  - name: restock" + char(10) + "    does: learn stock level ordered" o1 = new stzAgentDeclaration(c, "kitchen.pia")
classes.example:
? o1.IsValid()
#--> 1
? o1.Name_()
#--> kitchen-bot
? o1.Schedule()[:timer]
#--> 20
? o1.NumberOfSkills()
#--> 1
? o1.ToAgent().Cycle()
#--> 1

methods.name: init
methods.brief: Reads and judges the text of a .pia agent declaration at once, keeping the findings of every rule it breaks.

parameters.name: pcText
parameters.role: the declaration text, such as "pia: 2" followed by name, kind, coverage and the rest

parameters.name: pcSource
parameters.role: where it came from, shown in a refusal

notes: the judgement happens here, not at the first tick
warnings: a text that cannot be read, a missing version, an unknown key, a missing coverage statement and an unknown verb are findings, not errors: the object is built and IsValid says no

methods.name: IsValid
methods.brief: TRUE if the declaration passed every rule and has no finding.

methods.name: FormatVersion
methods.brief: Returns the version number read from the pia header.
methods.returns: a number; 0 when the header is missing or its version unknown
notes: a version this build does not know is a finding; the current one is 2 and 1 is still read

methods.name: Findings
methods.brief: Returns every refusal, each in the unified rule shape the rule report ingests.
methods.returns: a list of [ :rule, :subject, :where, :severity, :message ] rows; [ ] when valid
notes: the subject is always pi-agent-declaration and the severity error

methods.name: Source
methods.brief: Returns the source label given at construction, such as a file path or (text).

methods.name: Name_
methods.brief: Returns the agent's declared name.
methods.returns: a text; the empty text when the declaration has none

methods.name: Kind
methods.brief: Returns the declared kind of agent: pi, which acts, or llm, which only proposes.
methods.returns: a text, pi or llm; pi when none is declared

methods.name: CoverageStatement
methods.brief: Returns the sentence saying what the agent covers.
methods.returns: a text; the empty text when missing

methods.name: ReversibilityClass
methods.brief: Returns the declared reversibility class of the agent's work.
methods.returns: a text: reversible, compensable or irreversible; the text as written when it is refused

methods.name: Schedule
methods.brief: Returns when the agent ticks.
methods.returns: a list [ :mode, :timer, :channel ]; the mode is timer (with :timer in milliseconds) or event (with :channel), and the empty text before anything is read

methods.name: NumberOfSkills
methods.brief: Returns how many skills the declaration lists.

methods.name: SkillAt
methods.brief: Returns one skill as parsed.

parameters.name: pnIndex
parameters.role: the position of the skill, from 1

methods.returns: a list [ :name, :when, :does, :verify, :effect, :posture, :ringfns ]; each clause is a list [ :verb, :args ]
warnings: an index out of range raises error R2

methods.name: Governance
methods.brief: Returns the governance the declaration states.
methods.returns: a list [ :authority, :risks, :grants ]: the authority word, a list of [ action, tier ] pairs and a list of granted actions

methods.name: Proposes
methods.brief: Returns the proposal an llm agent declares: prompt, input clause, target subject, structure and limits.
methods.returns: a list [ :prompt, :input, :into, :structure, :budget, :retries, :maxtokens, :posture ]; [ ] for a pi agent

methods.name: SeedFacts
methods.brief: Returns the facts the agent starts with in its memory.
methods.returns: a list of [ subject, predicate, object ] triples

methods.name: CiteFindings
methods.brief: Returns the findings as text, one line each, in the form [rule @ where] message.
methods.returns: a text; the empty text when valid

methods.name: Describe
methods.brief: Returns a short report of the declaration: its name, kind, reversibility, coverage, schedule and skills, or the refusal.
methods.returns: a text of several lines; for a refused declaration "REFUSED (source):" followed by the findings

methods.name: ToAgent
methods.brief: Builds the runnable agent a valid declaration describes, from classes that already exist.
methods.returns: a stzDeclaredPIAgent for kind pi, a stzDeclaredLLMAgent for kind llm
notes: a pi agent starts with its seeded facts, risks, grants, authority, skills and reversibility; an llm agent holds no effectful capability
warnings: a refused declaration raises an error citing its findings and builds nothing

classes.name: stzAgentFolder
classes.brief: Reads a folder of agent files, gates each one, and mounts the accepted agents on a host so that dropping a file in the folder deploys it.
classes.description: A .pia file is data: it is judged by stzAgentDeclaration and turned into an agent. A .ring file is a program: the folder does not execute it, the application loads it, and the folder finds its <name>Agent() function and holds the object to the same four gates (it must answer Name_, Cycle, CoverageStatement and ReversibilityClass). A bad file does not stop the others: it is refused, kept in Refusals with the file that caused it, and ReadAgents counts only the accepted. Rescan compares a SHA-256 of each file, since a modification time is not available in this build. The folder does not watch the disk; whoever owns the cadence calls Rescan.
classes.example:
? o1.ReadAgents()
#--> 2
? @@( o1.Names() )
#--> [ "kitchen-bot", "summarizer" ]
? o1.NotationOf("kitchen-bot")
#--> pia
? o1.NumberOfRefusedFiles()
#--> 2

methods.name: init
methods.brief: Builds a folder reader on a path; nothing is read until ReadAgents is called.

parameters.name: pcPath
parameters.role: the folder that holds the agent files (.pia declarations and .ring agents)

methods.name: Path
methods.brief: Returns the folder path given at construction, unchanged.

methods.name: Why
methods.brief: Returns a one-line account of the last read or mount: how many agents were loaded or mounted, or why nothing was.
methods.returns: a text; empty before the first ReadAgents

methods.name: ReadAgents
methods.brief: Reads and gates every .pia and .ring file of the folder, and returns how many were accepted; the rest go to Refusals.
methods.returns: a number, the agents accepted; 0 when the folder does not exist, with the cause in Why
notes: every call starts from empty, so it is also the way to reload
warnings: a .ring file is not executed: the program must already have loaded it, or the file is refused with rule ring-agent-entry; a second file claiming a loaded name is refused as pia-duplicate-name

methods.name: NumberOfAgents
methods.brief: Returns how many agents the last read accepted.

methods.name: NumberOfRefusedFiles
methods.brief: Returns how many files the last read refused.

methods.name: Names
methods.brief: Returns the names of the accepted agents, in lower case, in file-name order.

methods.name: Has
methods.brief: TRUE if an agent of that name was loaded; the match ignores case and surrounding blanks.

parameters.name: pcName
parameters.role: the agent's name

methods.name: AgentQ
methods.brief: Returns the live agent object loaded under that name, so it can be configured before it is mounted.

parameters.name: pcName
parameters.role: the agent's name, matched without regard to case

notes: after MountOn the host ticks its own copy, so configure through this face before mounting
warnings: raises an error naming the folder for a name that was not loaded

methods.name: ScheduleOf
methods.brief: Returns when the agent runs, as declared in its file.

parameters.name: pcName
parameters.role: the agent's name

methods.returns: a list [ :mode, :timer, :channel ]; mode, timer and channel are empty or 0 for an unknown name
notes: a Ring agent without a Schedule method gets mode timer, 50

methods.name: NotationOf
methods.brief: Returns which notation the agent was written in.

parameters.name: pcName
parameters.role: the agent's name

methods.returns: the text pia or ring; an empty text for an unknown name

methods.name: Refusals
methods.brief: Returns every reason a file was refused, in the library's finding shape.
methods.returns: a list of [ :rule, :subject, :where, :severity, :message ] rows; where names the file
notes: a rescan adds a ring-agent-restart row for a changed .ring file

methods.name: RefusedFiles
methods.brief: Returns the refused files with how many findings each one carries.
methods.returns: a list of [ file, number ] pairs

methods.name: CiteRefusals
methods.brief: Returns the refusals as printable lines, one per finding, as [rule @ where] message.
methods.returns: a text; empty when the folder loaded whole
notes: printing it after every read keeps a partly loaded folder from passing for a healthy one

methods.name: Describe
methods.brief: Returns a multi-line summary: the folder, the counts, each agent with its notation and kind, then the refusals.

methods.name: Changes
methods.brief: Returns what differs on disk since the last read, without loading it; files are compared by the SHA-256 of their bytes, not by time.
methods.returns: a list [ :added, :changed, :removed ], each a list of file names
notes: a file that was refused and has not changed is not reported as added again; a missing folder reports every loaded file as removed

methods.name: HasChanged
methods.brief: TRUE if any file was added, changed or removed since the last read.

methods.name: Rescan
methods.brief: Reads the folder again whole and returns what moved since the previous read, so a host can mount what arrived and retire what left.
methods.returns: a list [ :added, :changed, :removed ], as Changes answered before the read
notes: a changed .pia file is re-read
warnings: a changed .ring file is not re-evaluated, because Ring cannot unload a function: the old code keeps running and a ring-agent-restart refusal names the file

methods.name: MountOn
methods.brief: Supervises every loaded agent on a host, each on the schedule its own file declared, and returns how many were mounted.

parameters.name: poHost
parameters.role: an agent host

notes: the agents' own coverage statement and reversibility class are declared on the host first

classes.name: stzAgentGraph
classes.brief: Declares a multi-agent composition as a colored graph and proves it sound before anything runs.
classes.description: Actors (program, language model, hybrid), guardians, effects, tools, trace sinks, inputs and human checkpoints are nodes, each with a fixed capability set and a taint color; edges say who proposes to, guards, feeds, traces or escalates to whom. The invariants checked are: a language-model actor never holds the effectful capability, every effect has a guardian into it and a path to a trace sink, open model text and external data never reach an effect without a guardian on the path. Grant is the governed door, which refuses effectful for an llm actor at the moment it is expressed, and a sealed record of what the doors granted lets Tampering report any property set around them through GraphQ. Declaring an id again replaces the node.
classes.example:
o1.AddLLMActor("writer")
o1.AddGuardian("gate")
o1.AddEffect("send")
o1.AddTraceSink("audit")
? o1.IsSound()
#--> 0
o1.Proposes("writer", "gate")
o1.Guards("gate", "send")
o1.Traces("send", "audit")
? o1.IsSound()
#--> 1
? o1.MayGrant("writer", "effectful")
#--> 0
