methods.name: Violations
methods.brief: Returns every broken invariant of the composition, as a list of findings, empty when the composition is sound.
methods.returns: a list of hash lists with the keys invariant, node, severity and message
notes: the invariants are no-llm-effectful, effects-guarded, open-text-contained, external-data-contained and effects-traced, plus governed-property-tampered for a node edited around the gate

methods.name: RulesAreSound
methods.brief: TRUE if the rule-set check finds no violation.

methods.name: RuleSetQ
methods.brief: Returns a new agent rule set, to which a project can add its own invariants.
methods.returns: a stzAgentRuleSet holding the six built-in rules
notes: the set is not bound to this graph: call its Check with the graph

methods.name: ViolationsViaRules
methods.brief: Returns the broken rules in the unified finding shape, so one report can collect them with any other graph.
methods.returns: a list of hash lists with the keys rule, subject, where, severity and message
notes: it also reports the effects-dominated rule and tampering; a tampering finding names the node in subject, the others name agentic

methods.name: IsSound
methods.brief: TRUE if the composition breaks no invariant and no node was edited around the governed doors.
notes: it answers FALSE for an effect with no guardian or no trace, for an llm actor that reaches an effect unguarded, and after Tampering finds a change

methods.name: Explain
methods.brief: Returns a readable verdict: one sentence when governed, or the list of violations when refused.

classes.name: stzAgentHost
classes.brief: Supervises agents as cancellable, traced, quarantinable and decommissionable jobs ticked on a timer or on events.
classes.description: A host owns a reactor, or shares one. It ticks each supervised agent through its Cycle, on its own timer or once per event of a bus channel, and records a trace. Cancel is a pause anyone can undo; Quarantine is a containment act that only an effectful actor can lift with Release; Retire is permanent and earned, refused until the declared decommission obligations are fulfilled. SetActionBudget caps the acts an agent may take in a window and quarantines a runaway. UseEngineLoop hands the scheduling decision to the engine, which refuses an agent that states neither what it covers nor how reversible it is. UseAgentsFrom mounts agents written as files. The host keeps a copy of each agent: configure it fully before Supervise and reach it afterwards through AgentQ.
classes.example:
o1.Supervise(new stzPIAgent("kitchen-bot"), 20)
? o1.NumberOfAgents()
#--> 1

methods.name: init
methods.brief: Builds a host that owns a new reactor and supervises no agent yet.

methods.name: SetReactor
methods.brief: Shares another host's reactor, such as an app server's loop, instead of owning one; a reactor the host owned is destroyed.

parameters.name: poReactor
parameters.role: the stzReactor to share

methods.returns: the host itself, so calls chain
notes: Shutdown leaves a shared reactor alone

methods.name: ReactorQ
methods.brief: Returns the reactor the host waits on between ticks.
methods.returns: the stzReactor, or an empty text after Shutdown

methods.name: Why
methods.brief: Returns the host's last explanation: what a mount, a rescan, a run to quiet, a retirement or a quarantine did.
methods.returns: a text; empty until something is recorded

methods.name: SetRetirementGovernance
methods.brief: Sets the governance whose decommission contracts gate Retire.

parameters.name: poGov
parameters.role: the stzGovernance that holds the decommission contracts

methods.returns: the host itself, so calls chain
notes: once a governance is set, an agent with no declared contract cannot retire
warnings: the host keeps a COPY of the governance, so declare and fulfil obligations through the host and never on the original

methods.name: DeclareDecommission
methods.brief: Declares what an agent must fulfil before it may retire.

parameters.name: pcName
parameters.role: the agent's name

parameters.name: pacObligations
parameters.role: the obligations to fulfil, as a list of text

methods.returns: the host itself, so calls chain
notes: creates a governance named agent-host when none was set, which makes Retire require a contract for every agent

methods.name: FulfillObligation
methods.brief: Marks one decommission obligation of an agent as fulfilled.

parameters.name: pcName
parameters.role: the agent's name

parameters.name: pcObligation
parameters.role: the obligation to mark, as text

methods.returns: the host itself, so calls chain
notes: retirement is earned once every declared obligation is fulfilled

methods.name: GovernanceQ
methods.brief: Returns the retirement governance the host holds.
methods.returns: the stzGovernance, or an empty text when none was set

methods.name: Supervise
methods.brief: Registers an agent to be ticked on a timer, once every given number of milliseconds.

parameters.name: poAgent
parameters.role: an agent that answers Name_ and Cycle, fully configured

parameters.name: nTickMs
parameters.role: the milliseconds between ticks, at least 1

methods.returns: the host itself, so calls chain
notes: with the engine loop adopted the agent is registered with it at once, and the engine may refuse
warnings: an interval below 1 raises an error; the host keeps a COPY of the agent, so configure it fully first and reach it afterwards through AgentQ

methods.name: SuperviseOnEvent
methods.brief: Registers an agent to be ticked once per event emitted on a channel of the engine event bus, not on a timer.

parameters.name: poAgent
parameters.role: an agent that answers Name_ and Cycle, fully configured

parameters.name: pcChannel
parameters.role: the event bus channel to follow, created when absent

methods.returns: the host itself, so calls chain
notes: events emitted before the call are not replayed

methods.name: ChannelOf
methods.brief: Returns the channel an agent is supervised on.

parameters.name: pcName
parameters.role: the agent's name

methods.returns: a text; empty for a timer-supervised or unknown agent

methods.name: NumberOfAgents
methods.brief: Returns how many agents the host has registered, whether active, cancelled, quarantined or retired.

methods.name: NameAt
methods.brief: Returns the name of the nth supervised agent, so an observer can list agents without holding them.

parameters.name: pnIndex
parameters.role: the position, 1 is the first agent supervised

methods.returns: a text; empty when the position is out of range

methods.name: IsSupervising
methods.brief: TRUE if an agent of that name was registered, retired or not.

parameters.name: pcName
parameters.role: the agent's name

methods.name: IsActive
methods.brief: TRUE if the agent is registered and not cancelled, quarantined or retired; the answer is the number 1 or 0.

parameters.name: pcName
parameters.role: the agent's name

warnings: Resume on a retired agent sets this back to 1 although it never ticks again, so read IsRetired too

methods.name: TicksOf
methods.brief: Returns how many cycles the host has run for an agent.

parameters.name: pcName
parameters.role: the agent's name

methods.returns: a number; 0 for an unknown agent

methods.name: AgentQ
methods.brief: Returns the live supervised agent, the copy to read and not the reference given to Supervise.

parameters.name: pcName
parameters.role: the agent's name

methods.returns: the agent object, or an empty text for an unknown name

methods.name: Trace
methods.brief: Returns the tick trace, one row per cycle the host ran.
methods.returns: a list of [ time in ms, agent name, firings, why ] rows
notes: the why reads tick N or event N (the engine loop can also say mail or nudge); a remade event channel adds a row of its own

methods.name: UseAgentsFrom
methods.brief: Mounts every valid agent file of a folder on this host, each on the schedule its own file declares.

parameters.name: pcPath
parameters.role: the folder that holds the agent files

methods.returns: a number, how many agents were mounted
notes: a file the folder will not admit is not mounted and is reported through AgentLoadRefusals; Why says how many were mounted and refused; UseAgentsFromQ does the same and returns the host, so calls chain

extensions.name: UseAgentsFromQ
extensions.adds: does what the method does, then returns the object, so the call can be chained

methods.name: AgentFolderQ
methods.brief: Returns the folder object mounted by UseAgentsFrom.
methods.returns: the stzAgentFolder, or an empty text when none was mounted

methods.name: IsUsingAgentFolder
methods.brief: TRUE if an agent folder was mounted; the answer is the number 1 or 0.

methods.name: AgentLoadRefusals
methods.brief: Returns every file the folder would not admit, as findings in the unified rule shape.
methods.returns: a list of [ :rule, :subject, :where, :severity, :message ] findings; [ ] with no folder or no refusal

methods.name: CiteAgentLoadRefusals
methods.brief: Returns the refusals of the folder as readable text, one line each.
methods.returns: a text; empty with no folder or no refusal

methods.name: RescanAgents
methods.brief: Re-reads the folder: supervises what arrived and cancels what vanished, and only reports a file that changed under a running agent.
notes: a vanished agent is cancelled and not retired, because retirement is earned; swapping a live agent is never done quietly
warnings: raises an error when no folder was mounted: call UseAgentsFrom first

methods.name: Declare
methods.brief: Declares an agent's coverage statement and reversibility class, which the engine loop demands before it schedules anything.

parameters.name: pcName
parameters.role: the agent's name

parameters.name: pcCoverage
parameters.role: one sentence saying what the agent covers

parameters.name: pcReversibility
parameters.role: reversible, compensable or irreversible

notes: needed only for an agent that does not answer CoverageStatement and ReversibilityClass itself (law 18); DeclareQ does the same and returns the host, so calls chain, and a second call for the same name replaces the first

extensions.name: DeclareQ
extensions.adds: does what the method does, then returns the object, so the call can be chained

methods.name: SetPriority
methods.brief: Sets an agent's priority for the engine loop: a higher number runs first in a pass, and ties run in the order registered.

parameters.name: pcName
parameters.role: the agent's name

parameters.name: pnPriority
parameters.role: the priority, a number

notes: it works before the agent is supervised

extensions.name: SetPriorityQ
extensions.adds: does what the method does, then returns the object, so the call can be chained

methods.name: PriorityOf
methods.brief: Returns the priority set for an agent.

parameters.name: pcName
parameters.role: the agent's name

methods.returns: a number; 0 when none was set

methods.name: UseEngineLoop
methods.brief: Adopts the engine loop as this host's pump: the engine decides who ticks and in what order, Ring still runs the cycles.
notes: opt-in; UseEngineLoopQ does the same and returns the host, so calls chain; agents already supervised are registered now, so the order of calls does not matter
warnings: raises an error carrying the engine's refusal when it will not schedule an agent, but the host then stays in engine mode with that agent unscheduled, so the agent never ticks until UseRingLoop is called

extensions.name: UseEngineLoopQ
extensions.adds: does what the method does, then returns the object, so the call can be chained

methods.name: UseRingLoop
methods.brief: Returns the host to the Ring pump it ran before the engine loop was adopted.
methods.returns: the host itself, so calls chain

methods.name: IsUsingEngineLoop
methods.brief: TRUE if the engine loop is this host's pump; the answer is the number 1 or 0.

methods.name: EngineLoopWhy
methods.brief: Returns the engine's last refusal, verbatim: it names its code, its subject and what to do.
methods.returns: a text; empty until the engine refuses

methods.name: EngineSlotOf
methods.brief: Returns the engine slot an agent occupies.

parameters.name: pcName
parameters.role: the agent's name

methods.returns: a number; -1 when the Ring pump drives it, after retirement, or for an unknown name

methods.name: TickDue
methods.brief: Runs one cycle of every active agent that is due: a timer agent when its interval has elapsed, an event agent once per new event.
methods.returns: a number, the skill firings run this pass
notes: the same call on either pump; every act is counted against its agent's budget, and an agent over it is quarantined in the middle of the pass

methods.name: RunFor
methods.brief: Drives the loop for a number of milliseconds, ticking due agents and waiting on a real timer between ticks.

parameters.name: nMs
parameters.role: how long to run, in milliseconds

methods.returns: the host itself, so calls chain

methods.name: RunToQuiet
methods.brief: Runs rounds until a whole pass fires nothing, or until 200 rounds, whichever comes first.
methods.returns: the host itself, so calls chain
notes: Why says how many rounds ran
warnings: an agent that fires on every cycle never goes quiet and stops at the 200-round cap, yet Why still reads ran to quiet

methods.name: Cancel
methods.brief: Stops ticking an agent without retiring it: a pause anyone can undo.

parameters.name: pcName
parameters.role: the agent's name

methods.returns: the host itself, so calls chain
notes: a quarantine is a containment act, and a cancel is an operator's pause
warnings: raises an error for an agent that is not supervised

methods.name: Resume
methods.brief: Makes a cancelled agent tick again, from now.

parameters.name: pcName
parameters.role: the agent's name

methods.returns: the host itself, so calls chain
warnings: raises an error for an unknown agent and for a quarantined one, which only Release lifts; on a retired agent it sets IsActive back to 1 although the agent never ticks again

methods.name: SetActionBudget
methods.brief: Caps the acts, which are skill firings, that an agent may take in a sliding window; an agent over the cap is quarantined.

parameters.name: pcName
parameters.role: the agent as supervised

parameters.name: pnMaxActs
parameters.role: how many acts the window allows, at least 1

parameters.name: pnWindowMs
parameters.role: the window length, in milliseconds, at least 1

methods.returns: the host itself, so calls chain
notes: threat model R7, OWASP ASI08: both pumps account, and the reason names how far over it went (action_budget_narrated)
warnings: raises an error for an agent that is not supervised and for a value below 1; setting it again starts a fresh window

methods.name: ActionBudgetOf
methods.brief: Returns the budget of an agent and the acts counted in the current window.

parameters.name: pcName
parameters.role: the agent's name, matched without regard to case

methods.returns: a list [ :max, :windowMs, :acts ]; [ ] when the agent has no budget
notes: the count starts again when the window ends or when Release lifts a quarantine

methods.name: Quarantine
methods.brief: Stops an agent and keeps the reason; it stays stopped until an effectful actor releases it.

parameters.name: pcName
parameters.role: the agent's name

parameters.name: pcReason
parameters.role: why it is contained, as text

methods.returns: the host itself, so calls chain
notes: writes agent.quarantined to the ledger when one is open; Resume refuses while it holds (quarantine_part_narrated)
warnings: raises an error for an agent that is not supervised

methods.name: IsQuarantined
methods.brief: TRUE if the agent is under quarantine.

parameters.name: pcName
parameters.role: the agent's name, matched without regard to case

methods.name: QuarantineOf
methods.brief: Returns why and when an agent was quarantined.

parameters.name: pcName
parameters.role: the agent's name, matched without regard to case

methods.returns: a list [ :reason, :at ]; [ ] when it is not quarantined

methods.name: Release
methods.brief: Lifts a quarantine and resumes the agent, on the word of an effectful, non-sandboxed actor only.

parameters.name: pcName
parameters.role: the agent to release

parameters.name: poActor
parameters.role: the actor that releases it, an object that must be effectful and not sandboxed

methods.returns: the host itself, so calls chain
notes: a released agent starts a fresh budget window
warnings: an actor that is not allowed, a language-model actor or a text, raises an error and the refusal reaches the ledger; it also resumes an agent that was merely cancelled and records agent.released although nothing was quarantined

methods.name: Retire
methods.brief: Retires an agent for good when every decommission obligation it declared is fulfilled; it never ticks again.

parameters.name: pcName
parameters.role: the agent's name

methods.returns: TRUE when retired, FALSE when refused, with Why saying what is pending
notes: with no governance at all any agent retires at once; a retired agent frees its engine slot
warnings: raises an error for an agent that is not supervised; with a governance set, an agent that declared no contract is refused

methods.name: IsRetired
methods.brief: TRUE if the agent was retired; the answer is the number 1 or 0.

parameters.name: pcName
parameters.role: the agent's name

methods.name: Shutdown
methods.brief: Destroys the reactor the host owns; a reactor shared through SetReactor is left alone.
methods.returns: the host itself, so calls chain

classes.name: stzAgentHostResponder
classes.brief: Carries out the QuarantinePart action of a response plan by quarantining an agent supervised by a host.
classes.description: A response plan proposes containment as data; a responder performs one verb for real once a committing actor approves. This one answers QuarantinePart only, by calling Quarantine on the host it holds, which stops ticking the agent until an effectful actor releases it. A target written agent:name is accepted. Every other verb raises an error that names the responder to wire. It holds the host by reference.
classes.receiver: oHost = new stzAgentHost() oHost.Supervise(new stzPIAgent("kitchen-bot"), 20) o1 = new stzAgentHostResponder(oHost)
classes.example:
o1.QuarantinePart("agent:kitchen-bot")
? oHost.IsQuarantined("kitchen-bot")
#--> 1
? oHost.QuarantineOf("kitchen-bot")[:reason]
#--> quarantined by a containment plan

methods.name: init
methods.brief: Builds a responder that performs the QuarantinePart action of a response plan on the agents of a host.

parameters.name: poHost
parameters.role: the stzAgentHost whose supervised agents are quarantined, held by reference

notes: keep the host alive as long as the responder is used

methods.name: Owns
methods.brief: TRUE if the verb is QuarantinePart, the only one this responder answers.

parameters.name: pcVerb
parameters.role: the verb, matched without regard to case

methods.name: QuarantinePart
methods.brief: Quarantines a supervised agent, so the host stops ticking it until an effectful actor releases it.

parameters.name: pcTarget
parameters.role: the agent to quarantine, with or without the agent: prefix, which is removed whatever its case

methods.returns: nothing; the host then answers IsQuarantined
notes: the reason kept is quarantined by a containment plan; the host notes the quarantine in the security refusal record
warnings: raises an error for an agent the host does not supervise, and the name is matched with its case here although IsQuarantined ignores case: Rogue-Bot is found and rogue-bot raises not supervising

methods.name: LockAccount
methods.brief: Refuses by raising an error that names the responder to wire, because this responder does not lock accounts.

parameters.name: pcTarget
parameters.role: the account the plan named

warnings: raises an error whatever the target

methods.name: RevokeSession
methods.brief: Refuses by raising an error that names the responder to wire, because this responder does not end sessions.

parameters.name: pcTarget
parameters.role: the actor the plan named

warnings: raises an error whatever the target

methods.name: RotateSecret
methods.brief: Refuses by raising an error that names the responder to wire, because this responder does not rotate secrets.

parameters.name: pcTarget
parameters.role: the secret the plan named

warnings: raises an error whatever the target

methods.name: RevokeCapability
methods.brief: Refuses by raising an error that names the responder to wire, because this responder does not revoke capabilities.

parameters.name: pcTarget
parameters.role: the actor the plan named

warnings: raises an error whatever the target

methods.name: ShedSource
methods.brief: Refuses by raising an error that names the responder to wire, because this responder does not block sources.

parameters.name: pcTarget
parameters.role: the source the plan named

warnings: raises an error whatever the target

classes.name: stzAgentMemory
classes.brief: Holds what an agent knows as facts in its own knowledge graph, each one carrying where and when it was learned.
classes.description: A memory owns a stzKnowledgeGraph, named mem-<agent>, rather than being one: it gives the agent a thin face of subject, predicate, object triples. Text is folded to lower case on the way in, so Fact and Recall ignore case. Every fact records its source (agent:<name> unless the caller says otherwise) and the time learned; nothing invents a confidence. Save and Restore carry the facts and their provenance through a .zknw knowledge file. Restore must be given the full file name with the extension.
classes.example:
o1.Learn("table-4", "wants", "water")
? o1.Fact("table-4", "wants", "water")
#--> 1
? @@( o1.Recall("table-4", "wants") )
#--> [ "water" ]
? o1.ProvenanceOf("table-4", "wants", "water")[1][2]
#--> agent:waiter

methods.name: init
methods.brief: Builds an empty memory for the named agent, backed by its own knowledge graph called mem-<name>.

parameters.name: pcAgentName
parameters.role: the owning agent's name, recorded as the source of every fact it learns

methods.name: GraphQ
methods.brief: Returns the knowledge graph the memory holds, for queries the memory face does not offer.

methods.name: Learn
methods.brief: Stores one fact as a subject, predicate, object triple, in lower case, with the owning agent and the time as its provenance.

parameters.name: pcS
parameters.role: the subject

parameters.name: pcP
parameters.role: the predicate

parameters.name: pcO
parameters.role: the object

methods.returns: the memory itself, so calls chain
notes: learning a fact already held adds nothing; LearnXT takes the caller's own provenance, such as [ :source = "sensor-3", :confidence = 0.8 ], and defaults :source to agent:<name>

extensions.name: LearnXT
extensions.adds: the extended form: more parameters than the base method

methods.name: ProvenanceOf
methods.brief: Returns where a fact came from: the source, the learning time and any confidence recorded with it.

parameters.name: pcS
parameters.role: the subject

parameters.name: pcP
parameters.role: the predicate

parameters.name: pcO
parameters.role: the object

methods.returns: a hash list [ :source, :learnedat ] plus :confidence when given; an empty list for an unknown fact
notes: the source keeps the agent name as it was given

methods.name: Fact
methods.brief: TRUE if the memory holds that exact triple; case is ignored.

parameters.name: pcS
parameters.role: the subject

parameters.name: pcP
parameters.role: the predicate

parameters.name: pcO
parameters.role: the object

methods.name: Recall
methods.brief: Returns every object the memory holds for a subject and predicate, in the order learned.

parameters.name: pcS
parameters.role: the subject

parameters.name: pcP
parameters.role: the predicate

methods.returns: a list of text; empty when nothing is known

methods.name: Forget
methods.brief: Removes one fact; forgetting a fact that is not held changes nothing.

parameters.name: pcS
parameters.role: the subject

parameters.name: pcP
parameters.role: the predicate

parameters.name: pcO
parameters.role: the object

methods.returns: the memory itself, so calls chain

methods.name: NumberOfFacts
methods.brief: Returns how many facts the memory holds.

methods.name: Prove
methods.brief: Asks the graph to prove a triple from recorded facts and lawful chains, with the reasoning narrated.

parameters.name: paTriple
parameters.role: a list [ subject, predicate, object ], in lower case

methods.returns: a hash list [ :verdict, :goal, :steps, :narration, :certainty ]; verdict is 1 when proved, 0 when not derivable

methods.name: Save
methods.brief: Writes the memory, provenance included, to a knowledge file, adding the extension .zknw when it is missing.

parameters.name: pcFile
parameters.role: the path of the file to write

notes: pass a name ending in .zknw to both Save and Restore
warnings: Restore needs the full name: a file saved as mem is written as mem.zknw, and Restore of mem raises error R13 Object is required because the name is read as the text of a knowledge file

methods.name: Restore
methods.brief: Reads a saved memory back, provenance included, and merges its facts into this memory.

parameters.name: pcFile
parameters.role: the path of a .zknw file

methods.returns: a hash list [ :merged, :refused ]; refused rows are [ s, p, o, why ]
notes: merged counts the facts read, including ones already held

classes.name: stzAgentRule
classes.brief: Holds one guardrail over an agent graph as a declared rule, in the agentic domain.
classes.description: An agent rule is a stzGraphRule whose domain is set to agentic; the library's governance invariants are declared with it inside stzAgentRuleSet, and a project can add its own without editing library code.
classes.example:
? o1.Name()
#--> no-llm-effectful
? o1.Domain()
#--> agentic

methods.name: init
methods.brief: Builds a guardrail rule of that name in the agentic domain; it is a graph rule, so the clauses of stzGraphRule apply.

parameters.name: pcName
parameters.role: the rule's name

classes.name: stzAgentRuleSet
classes.brief: Holds the agent guardrails as one set of graph rules, reproducing the hand-written governance checks.
classes.description: It is born with six rules: no-llm-effectful, effects-guarded, open-text-contained, effects-traced, effects-dominated (every path to an effect passes through a guardian) and external-data-contained. A project adds its own with AddRule. It judges an agent graph the way StzCheckAgentGraph does, on the same nodes.
classes.example:
? o1.NumberOfRules()
#--> 6
? o1.Name()
#--> agent-guardrails
? o1.RuleNamed("effects-dominated").Name()
#--> effects-dominated

methods.name: init
methods.brief: Builds the agent-guardrails rule set, already loaded with its six rules.

classes.name: stzAgentSkill
classes.brief: Holds one capability of an agent: a precondition, an action and a check that the action worked.
classes.description: A skill runs only when its precondition holds, and its result counts only when the check confirms it, so no effect goes unchecked. Algorithmic (pi) and prompted (llm) skills share one interface. Apply never throws for the three ordinary outcomes: it answers ran and verified as 0 or 1 with a sentence saying why, so a caller can log all three the same way. The check runs after the action and cannot undo it.
classes.receiver: o1 = new stzAgentSkill("restock") o2 = new stzAgentMemory("shop")
classes.example:
o2.Learn("stock", "level", "low")
o1.SetWhen(func oM { return oM.Fact("stock", "level", "low") })
o1.SetDoes(func oM { oM.Learn("stock", "level", "ordered") return 1 })
o1.SetVerifiedBy(func oM { return oM.Fact("stock", "level", "ordered") })
? o1.Apply(o2)[:why]
#--> skill 'restock' ran and VERIFIED

methods.name: init
methods.brief: Builds a skill with a name and no precondition, action or check; its kind is pi.

parameters.name: pcName
parameters.role: the skill's name, quoted in the why of Apply

methods.name: Name_
methods.brief: Returns the name the skill was built with.

methods.name: SetWhen
methods.brief: Sets the precondition: a function of the memory that must answer true before the skill may run.

parameters.name: fPrecondition
parameters.role: a function taking the memory and returning 1 or 0

methods.returns: the skill itself, so calls chain

methods.name: SetDoes
methods.brief: Sets the action the skill performs on the memory when it runs.

parameters.name: fAction
parameters.role: a function taking the memory

methods.returns: the skill itself, so calls chain

methods.name: SetVerifiedBy
methods.brief: Sets the check run after the action to confirm that it had the intended effect.

parameters.name: fCheck
parameters.role: a function taking the memory and returning 1 when the effect is confirmed

methods.returns: the skill itself, so calls chain
notes: without a check the result counts as verified

methods.name: AsLLMSkill
methods.brief: Marks the skill as prompted rather than algorithmic; the interface and the gates are the same.
methods.returns: the skill itself, so calls chain
notes: it changes the posture reported by Kind, not the way Apply runs

methods.name: Kind
methods.brief: Returns the skill's posture: pi for an algorithmic skill, llm after AsLLMSkill.

methods.name: PreconditionHolds
methods.brief: Runs the precondition on a memory and returns its answer; a skill with no precondition always holds.

parameters.name: poMemory
parameters.role: the agent's memory (a stzAgentMemory)

methods.returns: what the precondition function returned, 1 when none is set
notes: Apply tests the answer against 0, so any other value, such as 2, counts as holding

methods.name: Apply
methods.brief: Runs the action only if the precondition holds, then checks the result, and reports what happened.

parameters.name: poMemory
parameters.role: the agent's memory, which the action may change

methods.returns: a hash list [ :ran, :verified, :why ]; why is a sentence naming the skill
notes: the action runs before the check, and a failed check does not undo it
warnings: a skill with no action reports ran 0 even when its precondition holds; a check must answer exactly 1 to verify

classes.name: stzAgentWorkbench
classes.brief: Gives an agent a safe world to rehearse file changes in: writes land in memory, and only an update plan leads toward the disk.
classes.description: A workbench is an in-memory virtual file system kept in a process-wide table and reached through faces that carry only its id, so copies of a face all reach the one live twin. The rehearsal verbs record operations, and the inspection methods read the twin and never the disk. ReadThrough answers from the twin first, an empty text for a path the rehearsal deleted, and the real disk otherwise. The only export toward reality is GenerateUpdatePlan, which a committing actor executes under the plan's scope, capability and governance gates. Open one with StzOpenAgentWorkbench, or give it to an agent with GiveWorkbench; the owner closes it with StzCloseAgentWorkbench.
classes.example:
o1.SetActor("kitchen-bot")
o1.CreateFile("/shop/orders.txt", "milk")
o1.WriteFile("/shop/orders.txt", "milk, eggs")
? o1.ContentOf("/shop/orders.txt")
#--> milk, eggs
? o1.NumberOfOperations()
#--> 2
o1.DeleteFile("/shop/orders.txt")
? len(o1.ReadThrough("/shop/orders.txt"))
#--> 0
? o1.WasDeleted("/shop/orders.txt")
#--> 1

methods.name: init
methods.brief: Builds a face onto an open workbench, a rehearsal file system held in memory, reached by its numeric id.

parameters.name: pnId
parameters.role: the id returned by StzOpenAgentWorkbench or by Id

notes: the face holds only the id, so copies of it all reach the same one workbench
warnings: an id with no open workbench raises an error naming the id at construction, not at the first write

methods.name: Id
methods.brief: Returns the number of the workbench this face reaches.

methods.name: SetActor
methods.brief: Stamps the workbench with the name of whoever proposes the changes, so the history and the plan show an author.

parameters.name: pcName
parameters.role: the actor's name, shown in brackets after each rehearsed operation

methods.returns: the face itself, so calls chain

methods.name: CreateFile
methods.brief: Rehearses creating a file with some text; nothing touches the disk.

parameters.name: pcPath
parameters.role: the path of the file

parameters.name: pcContent
parameters.role: its text

methods.returns: the face itself, so calls chain
notes: creating a path that already exists is accepted and replaces its content; a later Validate of the plan reports problems with reality

methods.name: WriteFile
methods.brief: Rehearses writing text into a file; nothing touches the disk.

parameters.name: pcPath
parameters.role: the path of the file

parameters.name: pcContent
parameters.role: the new text

methods.returns: the face itself, so calls chain
notes: writing a path the workbench does not hold creates it

methods.name: CreateFolder
methods.brief: Rehearses creating a folder; nothing touches the disk.

parameters.name: pcPath
parameters.role: the path of the folder

methods.returns: the face itself, so calls chain

methods.name: DeleteFile
methods.brief: Rehearses deleting a file, leaving a mark that ReadThrough reads as an empty file.

parameters.name: pcPath
parameters.role: the path of the file

methods.returns: the face itself, so calls chain
notes: deleting a path nobody holds is accepted; Validate on the plan reports that the target is absent in reality

methods.name: DeleteFolder
methods.brief: Rehearses deleting a folder; nothing touches the disk.

parameters.name: pcPath
parameters.role: the path of the folder

methods.returns: the face itself, so calls chain

methods.name: CopyFile
methods.brief: Rehearses copying a file inside the workbench.

parameters.name: pcFrom
parameters.role: the source path

parameters.name: pcTo
parameters.role: the path of the copy

methods.returns: the face itself, so calls chain
notes: a source the workbench does not hold is accepted, and Validate on the plan reports it as absent in reality

methods.name: MoveFile
methods.brief: Rehearses moving a file; the source path then counts as deleted.

parameters.name: pcFrom
parameters.role: the source path

parameters.name: pcTo
parameters.role: the destination path

methods.returns: the face itself, so calls chain

methods.name: MirrorFile
methods.brief: Copies a real file's text into the workbench so it can be changed there; the disk file is only read.

parameters.name: pcPath
parameters.role: the path of a real file

methods.returns: the face itself, so calls chain
notes: a path that does not exist on disk is ignored and records nothing

methods.name: Exists
methods.brief: TRUE if the workbench itself holds the path; the real disk is not asked.

parameters.name: pcPath
parameters.role: the path to test

methods.name: ContentOf
methods.brief: Returns the text the workbench holds for a path; the real disk is not asked.

parameters.name: pcPath
parameters.role: the path of a rehearsed file

methods.returns: a text; empty when the workbench holds no such path

methods.name: NumberOfOperations
methods.brief: Returns how many operations have been rehearsed.

methods.name: HistoryText
methods.brief: Returns the rehearsal as numbered lines, each with its actor, ready to read or log.
methods.returns: a multi-line text starting with Rehearsed operations (n):

methods.name: WasDeleted
methods.brief: TRUE if the rehearsal deleted or moved the path away and the workbench does not hold it now.

parameters.name: pcPath
parameters.role: the path to test

notes: a path deleted and then created again is held, so the answer is FALSE

methods.name: ReadThrough
methods.brief: Returns a file's text as the agent should see it: the workbench's own copy first, an empty text for a deleted path, otherwise the real disk.

parameters.name: pcPath
parameters.role: the path to read

notes: reading is free and never changes the workbench; only writes are confined to it

methods.name: ExistsThrough
methods.brief: TRUE if the file exists as the agent should see it: held by the workbench, or not deleted and present on the real disk.

parameters.name: pcPath
parameters.role: the path to test

methods.name: GenerateUpdatePlan
methods.brief: Returns the rehearsal as an update plan, the one export toward reality, to be validated and committed by an actor that holds the authority.
methods.returns: a stzUpdatePlan listing every rehearsed operation
notes: the plan is built from the history: Validate on it reports operations that do not match the real files

classes.name: stzAmount
classes.brief: Holds an amount of money as whole minor units and an ISO 4217 currency, so it can never be a bare number.
classes.description: An amount cannot be built without a currency, and the library refuses what could not be paid exactly: a fraction finer than the currency's minor unit (50.5 in XOF, because a franc has no fraction), a fractional number, a currency it does not know, and arithmetic or ordering across two currencies. It is never rounded. Money is spelled as text, "12.50", never computed as a float. The exponent is ISO 4217's: 0 for XOF and XAF, 2 for EUR, 3 for TND. An amount is immutable: Plus, Minus, TimesInteger and Negated answer a new amount. Nothing is converted between currencies, and no rate exists.
classes.example:
? o1.Display()
#--> 150 000 FCFA
? o1.MinorUnits()
#--> 150000
? StzAmountQ("12.50", "EUR").MinorUnits()
#--> 1250
? o1.Plus(StzAmountQ("40000", "XOF")).Display()
#--> 190 000 FCFA

methods.name: init
methods.brief: Builds an amount from a value and an ISO 4217 currency code, refusing any value that could not be paid exactly.

parameters.name: pValue
parameters.role: the amount as text such as "12.50", or as a whole number of major units

parameters.name: pcCurrency
parameters.role: an ISO 4217 code such as XOF or EUR, in any case

notes: a whole number is read in major units, so 5 in EUR is 5.00; trailing zeros past the exponent change nothing, so "5000.00" in XOF is 5000
warnings: raises an error for a missing or unknown currency, for a fraction finer than the currency's minor unit ("50.5" in XOF), for a fractional number (50.5), for a value that is neither text nor a number, and beyond 2^53 - 1 minor units; an amount is never rounded

methods.name: Currency
methods.brief: Returns the ISO 4217 code of the amount, in capitals, whatever case it was built with.

methods.name: Exponent
methods.brief: Returns the number of decimals of the currency's minor unit, as ISO 4217 gives it: 0 for XOF, 2 for EUR, 3 for TND.
notes: the exponent is ISO 4217's, not the country table's: a franc CFA has none

methods.name: MinorUnits
methods.brief: Returns the amount as a whole number of the currency's smallest unit: 150000 for 150 000 XOF, 1250 for 12.50 EUR.
methods.returns: a number, negative for a negative amount
notes: this is the figure a payment carries; keep the amount object and read it last

methods.name: IsZero
methods.brief: TRUE if the amount is exactly zero.

methods.name: IsPositive
methods.brief: TRUE if the amount is strictly above zero; zero is not positive.

methods.name: IsNegative
methods.brief: TRUE if the amount is strictly below zero.

methods.name: Content
methods.brief: Returns the amount as plain decimal text with its currency's own number of places and its sign, with no grouping and no currency.
methods.returns: a text such as 1250.50, or 150000 for XOF

methods.name: Display
methods.brief: Returns the amount as a reader of the UEMOA reads it: thousands grouped by spaces, then the currency, FCFA for both XOF and XAF.
methods.returns: a text such as 150 000 FCFA or 1 250.50 EUR

methods.name: Plus
methods.brief: Returns a new amount that is the sum of this one and another of the same currency.

parameters.name: poOther
parameters.role: the amount to add, in the same currency

methods.returns: a new amount; neither operand changes
notes: the symbol + between two amounts calls this
warnings: raises an error for another currency, for something that is not an amount, and for a result beyond 2^53 - 1 minor units; francs and euros are never added

methods.name: Minus
methods.brief: Returns a new amount that is this one less another of the same currency, negative when the other is larger.

parameters.name: poOther
parameters.role: the amount to take away, in the same currency

methods.returns: a new amount; neither operand changes
notes: the symbol - between two amounts calls this
warnings: raises an error for another currency, for something that is not an amount, and for a result beyond 2^53 - 1 minor units

methods.name: TimesInteger
methods.brief: Returns a new amount that is this one repeated a whole number of times, which may be zero or negative.

parameters.name: pn
parameters.role: the whole-number multiplier

notes: a rate would need a rounding rule, and a payment has none to give
warnings: raises an error for a fraction or for something that is not a number, and beyond 2^53 - 1 minor units; there is no rate and no rounding

methods.name: Negated
methods.brief: Returns a new amount of the same size and the opposite sign.

methods.name: Equals
methods.brief: TRUE if the other value is an amount of the same currency and the same size; anything else answers FALSE without an error.

parameters.name: poOther
parameters.role: the value to compare, normally an amount

notes: 150000 XOF and "150000.00" XOF are equal; 150000 XOF and 150000 EUR are not

methods.name: IsGreaterThan
methods.brief: TRUE if this amount is larger than another of the same currency.

parameters.name: poOther
parameters.role: the amount to compare with, in the same currency

warnings: raises an error for another currency or for something that is not an amount: amounts of two currencies have no order

methods.name: IsLessThan
methods.brief: TRUE if this amount is smaller than another of the same currency.

parameters.name: poOther
parameters.role: the amount to compare with, in the same currency

warnings: raises an error for another currency or for something that is not an amount: amounts of two currencies have no order

methods.name: operator
methods.brief: Answers the sum or the difference of two amounts of one currency when they are written with the symbol + or -.

parameters.name: pOp
parameters.role: the symbol, + or -

parameters.name: pValue
parameters.role: the other amount

notes: a + b is Plus and a - b is Minus
warnings: any other symbol raises an error naming TimesInteger for multiples; the symbol = is deliberately not defined, so compare with Equals

classes.name: stzApiKey
classes.brief: Holds an API key as a secret that is redacted everywhere and is presented as a bearer Authorization header only to an effectful actor.
classes.description: A stzSecret of kind apikey. Its descriptor, its Show and any configuration it lands in print only the redacted form. AuthorizationHeader is a governed reveal: a human or pi actor gets Bearer followed by the key, an LLM actor or an unknown actor is refused. Use invented values in code and tests.
classes.example:
? o1.Descriptor()
#--> <secret 'stripe' (apikey) from literal>
? o1.AuthorizationHeader(HumanActor("alice"))
#--> Bearer invented-key-123
? o1.IsRevealableBy(LLMActor("bot"))
#--> 0

methods.name: init
methods.brief: Builds an API key secret with a name, of kind apikey and no source yet.

parameters.name: pcName
parameters.role: the secret's name, shown in its redacted descriptor

methods.name: AuthorizationHeader
methods.brief: Returns the value of an HTTP Authorization header, Bearer followed by the key, which reveals the key.

parameters.name: poActor
parameters.role: the actor asking, which must be effectful and not sandboxed, such as a human or a pi actor

methods.returns: a text such as Bearer plus the key
notes: never print or log the result: Descriptor and Show are the redacted forms
warnings: raises a refusal error for an LLM actor or any other actor, noted in the security ledger, and an error for a key with no source; a value that holds a line break, such as the trailing newline of a file, goes into the header as it is and can add header lines, so trim it first

classes.name: stzApp
classes.brief: Holds an application as a world of meaning: its things, instances, flows, reactions, goals, screens and reach, declared in plain words.
classes.description: Declare things with AddThing and their fields with Has, then instances and relations with AddInstance and Relate: these form a graph. Flows, reactions, goals, screens and refinements are cursor builders, each plain verb acting on the one declared last, and each verb has a Q form that returns the world so a brace can follow: AddGoalQ(:Visited) { Means = "every :Client Has(:visited)" }. A goal is a wanted state of the graph; Pursue measures its gap and proposes how to close it through the reactions, and Live and Pulse fire the reactions themselves. Explain prints the whole world in words. The world only describes: a stzPlatform wraps it to build, generate shells and serve it.
classes.example:
o1.AddThingQ("Client").Has([ "code", "name" ])
? o1.Things()[1][1]
#--> Client
o1.AddInstance("anna", "Client")
o1.AddReactionQ("Client").Propose("Visit")
? o1.Pulse()
#--> 1
? o1.Proposals()[1][4]
#--> anna

methods.name: init
methods.brief: Builds an empty world with the given name and a graph of the same name that holds its things and instances.

parameters.name: pcName
parameters.role: the world's name

methods.name: Name
methods.brief: Returns the name the world was given.

methods.name: GraphQ
methods.brief: Returns the graph that holds the world's things and instances.
notes: the graph ids are in lower case, whatever the case of the names given

methods.name: AddThing
methods.brief: Declares a kind of thing, or selects it if already declared, and makes it the one that Has, IsTrue, Owns and Of describe.

parameters.name: pcName
parameters.role: the thing's name

methods.returns: nothing; use AddThingQ to chain or to open a brace
notes: calling it again with the same name selects the thing and adds no copy

extensions.name: AddThingQ
extensions.adds: does what the method does, then returns the object, so the call can be chained

methods.name: Has
methods.brief: Sets the field names of the thing just added, replacing any set before.

parameters.name: paFields
parameters.role: a list of field names

methods.returns: the world itself, so calls chain
notes: with no thing added yet it does nothing

methods.name: IsTrue
methods.brief: Adds a truth to the thing just added: a field name and the expression that holds for it.

parameters.name: pcField
parameters.role: the field the truth is about

parameters.name: pcExpr
parameters.role: the expression that must hold, such as > 18

methods.returns: the world itself, so calls chain
notes: Explain shows it as true when

methods.name: Owns
methods.brief: Adds the relation owns toward another thing to the thing just added.

parameters.name: pcThing
parameters.role: the thing that is owned

methods.returns: the world itself, so calls chain

methods.name: Of
methods.brief: Adds the relation of toward another thing to the thing just added.

parameters.name: pcThing
parameters.role: the thing that this one belongs to

methods.returns: the world itself, so calls chain

methods.name: AddRelation
methods.brief: Declares a free relation between two things, kept apart from the things' own Owns and Of.

parameters.name: pcFrom
parameters.role: the first thing

parameters.name: pcRelation
parameters.role: the relation's name

parameters.name: pcTo
parameters.role: the second thing

notes: it is shown by Explain only: it adds no edge to the graph, unlike Relate

extensions.name: AddRelationQ
extensions.adds: does what the method does, then returns the object, so the call can be chained

methods.name: AddInstance
methods.brief: Adds a named individual to the graph, linked to its kind of thing by an isa edge.

parameters.name: pcInstance
parameters.role: the individual's name

parameters.name: pcThing
parameters.role: the thing it is an instance of

notes: the nodes are created if absent

extensions.name: AddInstanceQ
extensions.adds: does what the method does, then returns the object, so the call can be chained

methods.name: Relate
methods.brief: Adds a labelled edge between two nodes of the graph, creating either node when absent.

parameters.name: pcFrom
parameters.role: the source node, usually an instance

parameters.name: pcRelation
parameters.role: the label of the edge

parameters.name: pcTo
parameters.role: the target node

methods.returns: the world itself, so calls chain
notes: goals and reactions are judged on these edges

methods.name: AddFlow
methods.brief: Declares that an actor performs a verb on a thing, and makes it the flow that Require and Then complete.

parameters.name: pcActor
parameters.role: who acts

parameters.name: pcVerb
parameters.role: what is done

parameters.name: pcThing
parameters.role: what it is done to

extensions.name: AddFlowQ
extensions.adds: does what the method does, then returns the object, so the call can be chained

methods.name: Require
methods.brief: Adds a required field to the flow just added.

parameters.name: pcField
parameters.role: the field that must be present

methods.returns: the world itself, so calls chain
notes: with no flow added yet it does nothing

methods.name: Keep
methods.brief: Returns the effect list that tells a flow to keep a thing, for Then to take.

parameters.name: pcThing
parameters.role: the thing to keep

methods.returns: a list of two items, the word keep and the thing
notes: it records nothing by itself, and inside a SetBody brace the name Keep also reads as an attribute

methods.name: Then
methods.brief: Adds an effect to the flow just added.

parameters.name: paEffect
parameters.role: the effect, such as the list that Keep returns

methods.returns: the world itself, so calls chain
notes: Explain narrates any effect as then keep followed by the flow's thing

methods.name: AddReaction
methods.brief: Declares a reaction of a kind of thing, and makes it the one that Unseen, Meets and Propose complete.

parameters.name: pcThing
parameters.role: the thing whose instances the reaction watches

extensions.name: AddReactionQ
extensions.adds: does what the method does, then returns the object, so the call can be chained

methods.name: Unseen
methods.brief: Sets the condition of the reaction just added to an instance left unseen for a length of time.

parameters.name: nQty
parameters.role: the length

parameters.name: pUnit
parameters.role: its unit, such as Days

methods.returns: the world itself, so calls chain
notes: the condition is only narrated by Explain: Pulse does not test it

methods.name: Meets
methods.brief: Sets the condition of the reaction just added to an expression that must hold.

parameters.name: pcExpr
parameters.role: the expression, such as total > 100

methods.returns: the world itself, so calls chain
notes: the condition is only narrated by Explain: Pulse does not test it

methods.name: Propose
methods.brief: Adds to the reaction just added the thing it proposes when it fires.

parameters.name: pcThing
parameters.role: the thing to propose

methods.returns: the world itself, so calls chain
notes: Pulse proposes it for each instance that lacks a relation of that name

methods.name: AddGoal
methods.brief: Declares a goal, and makes it the one that the brace assigns Means, ReachedBy, Within and Respecting to.

parameters.name: pcGoal
parameters.role: the goal's name

methods.returns: nothing; use AddGoalQ to chain or to open a brace
notes: the Means is read when the brace closes, so assign it inside AddGoalQ(name) { }

extensions.name: AddGoalQ
extensions.adds: does what the method does, then returns the object, so the call can be chained

methods.name: Goal
methods.brief: Returns a goal as plain data.

parameters.name: pcGoal
parameters.role: the goal's name

methods.returns: a hash list with the keys name, means, reachedby, within and respecting; an empty list for an unknown goal

extensions.name: GoalQ
extensions.adds: does what the method does, then returns the object, so the call can be chained

methods.name: GoalName
methods.brief: Returns the goal's name if the goal is declared.

parameters.name: pcGoal
parameters.role: the goal's name

methods.returns: a text; empty for an unknown goal

methods.name: GoalNames
methods.brief: Returns the names of all declared goals in declaration order.

methods.name: Pursue
methods.brief: Measures the gap between the world graph and the goal, and turns each instance in the gap into a proposal.

parameters.name: pcGoal
parameters.role: the goal's name

methods.returns: a list of proposals such as propose Visit for bilal, empty when the gap is closed or the goal is unknown
notes: the proposal comes from the reaction that proposes for the goal's kind of thing, else the proposal is attend; the list also replaces Proposals
warnings: it prints one pursuing line to the console, and it raises an error when the Means has no every :Thing clause

methods.name: GoalSatisfied
methods.brief: TRUE if the world graph already meets the goal.

parameters.name: pcGoal
parameters.role: the goal's name

warnings: it raises an error when the Means has no every :Thing clause

methods.name: SetBody
methods.brief: Declares where the world is kept, a kind or a list of kinds such as GraphDB, and opens a brace to name its paths.

parameters.name: pBody
parameters.role: a kind or a list of kinds of body

methods.returns: the world itself, so calls chain
notes: inside the brace, assign Graph, Files and Keep, which are read when the brace closes

methods.name: Body
methods.brief: Returns the body as plain data.
methods.returns: a hash list with the keys label, graph, files and keep; an empty list when no body was set

extensions.name: BodyQ
extensions.adds: does what the method does, then returns the object, so the call can be chained

methods.name: Save
methods.brief: Writes the world graph to its graph file when the body includes GraphDB, and does nothing otherwise.
methods.returns: the world itself, so calls chain
notes: with no body it writes nothing
warnings: a path defaults to .stzapp/world.stzgraf in the current folder, which is created if needed

methods.name: AddScreen
methods.brief: Declares a screen, and makes it the one that the To verbs, Shows and Acts describe.

parameters.name: pcName
parameters.role: the screen's name

notes: its intent is understand until a To verb says otherwise

extensions.name: AddScreenQ
extensions.adds: does what the method does, then returns the object, so the call can be chained

methods.name: ToDiscover
methods.brief: Sets the screen just added to the intent discover, about a thing.

parameters.name: pcThing
parameters.role: the thing the screen is about

methods.returns: the world itself, so calls chain

methods.name: ToUnderstand
methods.brief: Sets the screen just added to the intent understand, about a thing.

parameters.name: pcThing
parameters.role: the thing the screen is about

methods.returns: the world itself, so calls chain

methods.name: ToFocus
methods.brief: Sets the screen just added to the intent focus, about a thing.

parameters.name: pcThing
parameters.role: the thing the screen is about

methods.returns: the world itself, so calls chain

methods.name: ToSelect
methods.brief: Sets the screen just added to the intent select, about a thing.

parameters.name: pcThing
parameters.role: the thing the screen is about

methods.returns: the world itself, so calls chain

methods.name: ToAct
methods.brief: Sets the screen just added to the intent act, about a thing.

parameters.name: pcThing
parameters.role: the thing the screen is about

methods.returns: the world itself, so calls chain

methods.name: Shows
methods.brief: Sets what the screen just added shows.

parameters.name: paParts
parameters.role: a list of part names

methods.returns: the world itself, so calls chain
notes: it replaces any parts set before

methods.name: Acts
methods.brief: Adds an action of the screen just added, tied to a flow.

parameters.name: pcAction
parameters.role: the action's name

parameters.name: pcFlow
parameters.role: the flow it triggers

methods.returns: the world itself, so calls chain

methods.name: AddRefinement
methods.brief: Declares a knob that a person may tune, and makes it the one that Bounds and Options describe.

parameters.name: pcKnob
parameters.role: the knob's name

extensions.name: AddRefinementQ
extensions.adds: does what the method does, then returns the object, so the call can be chained

methods.name: Bounds
methods.brief: Sets the lowest and highest value of the knob just added.

parameters.name: pLow
parameters.role: the lowest value

parameters.name: pHigh
parameters.role: the highest value

methods.returns: the world itself, so calls chain
notes: the values are stored as text and Explain narrates them as bounds [1..99]

methods.name: Options
methods.brief: Sets the list of choices of the knob just added.

parameters.name: paOpts
parameters.role: a list of the allowed values

methods.returns: the world itself, so calls chain
notes: Explain shows the options only when no bounds were set

methods.name: Surfaces
methods.brief: Returns the surfaces on which the world appears, as declared by AddReaches.
notes: a surface added as a single text or symbol is stored wrongly today, see AddReaches

methods.name: Things
methods.brief: Returns the declared things with their fields.
methods.returns: a list of lists, each with the thing's name and its list of field names

methods.name: ScreenNames
methods.brief: Returns the names of the declared screens in order.

methods.name: AddReaches
methods.brief: Declares the surfaces, such as web, desktop or mobile, on which the world appears.

parameters.name: paSurfaces
parameters.role: a list of surface names

notes: the list is added to the surfaces already declared
warnings: a single text or symbol is stored as [ [ ] ] today, so give a list: Surfaces then holds an unusable entry and both Explain and a platform's Generate raise an error

extensions.name: AddReachesQ
extensions.adds: does what the method does, then returns the object, so the call can be chained

methods.name: BraceEnd
methods.brief: Writes the pending goal and body assignments of a brace into their records.
notes: it is called for you when a brace closes, and every builder verb does the same first

methods.name: Live
methods.brief: Turns the world on, runs a first Pulse and prints a one-line summary of its things, flows, reactions, goals and proposals.
methods.returns: the world itself, so calls chain
warnings: it prints to the console

methods.name: IsLive
methods.brief: TRUE if Live was called.

methods.name: Pulse
methods.brief: Fires every reaction against the graph, adding one proposal for each instance that lacks the relation the reaction proposes.
methods.returns: a number, how many proposals were added
notes: it is idempotent: a standing proposal is not repeated, and one clears on the next pulse once the instance gets the relation

methods.name: Proposals
methods.brief: Returns the proposals now standing.
methods.returns: a list of lists such as propose Visit for bilal

methods.name: React
methods.brief: Fires the reactions for one instance only, as Pulse does for all.

parameters.name: pcInstance
parameters.role: the instance's name

methods.returns: a number, how many proposals were added
notes: it first drops the proposals that the graph now satisfies

methods.name: Explain
methods.brief: Prints the world in plain words: its things, relations, flows, reactions, goals, screens, knobs and reaches.
methods.returns: the world itself, so calls chain
notes: it raises an error when a surface was added as a single text, see AddReaches
warnings: it prints to the console

methods.name: Show
methods.brief: Prints one thing with its fields, truths and relations.

parameters.name: pcThing
parameters.role: the name of a declared thing

methods.returns: the world itself, so calls chain
notes: an unknown name prints a no such thing line instead of failing
warnings: it prints to the console

classes.name: stzAppBackend
classes.brief: Serves a solution's datasets as live shared state over a real loopback server, so every part reads and writes the same records.
classes.description: A solution model gives each part a role over a dataset, but the datasets are frozen lists. Start turns them into sqlite tables served by a real server in this process, and the parts then Create, Rows, RowCount and Dashboard by real HTTP round trips on the loopback: what one part writes, another sees. Writes are governed (SetActor: only an effectful actor commits; reads stay open) and every crossing is recorded in Traffic with its duration. The same API also drives a backend in another process (ConnectTo, SpawnRemote), signed with a shared key (SetSigningKey), which is required to leave the loopback. Known limits: the reply is parsed by splitting on commas, so a cell containing a comma splits in two; Dashboard expects a dish and a quantity.
classes.receiver: oT = new stzAppTopology("demo") oT.AddDatasetQ("menu", [ [ "Tajine", "clay pot", 15 ] ]) oT.SetDatasetColumnsQ("menu", [ "name", "descr", "price" ]) oT.AddDatasetQ("orders", [ [ "Tajine", 1 ] ]) oT.SetDatasetColumnsQ("orders", [ "dish", "qty" ]) oT.SetPartRoleQ(:phone, "menu", "menu") oT.SetPartRoleQ(:admin, "dashboard", "orders") o1 = new stzAppBackend("demo", oT) o1.Start(0)
classes.example:
? o1.IsLive()
#--> 1
? o1.RowCount(:admin, "orders")
#--> 1
? o1.Create(:phone, "orders", [ [ "dish", "Tajine" ], [ "qty", 2 ] ])
#--> 1
? o1.RowCount(:admin, "orders")
#--> 2
? o1.Dashboard(:admin)[2]
#--> 45
? o1.TrafficCount()
#--> 4
o1.Stop()

the parts' view of the live state

methods.name: init
methods.brief: Builds a backend for a solution model, not yet started, with an empty crossing ledger.

parameters.name: pcName
parameters.role: the backend's name

methods.name: Start
methods.brief: Turns the model's datasets into live sqlite tables and serves them over a real server bound to the loopback, in this process.

parameters.name: pnPortNum

methods.name: StartOn
methods.brief: Starts the backend bound to a chosen interface; the loopback is allowed freely, any other address only once a signing key is set.

parameters.name: pcHostAddr
parameters.role: the interface to bind, "127.0.0.1" for this machine only, or the empty text for the loopback

parameters.name: pnPortNum

methods.brief: Returns the interface the backend is bound to.

methods.brief: Runs the server loop for a number of milliseconds, answering whoever connects; what a hosting process does after Start.

parameters.name: pnMs
parameters.role: how long to serve, in milliseconds

methods.name: ConnectTo
methods.section: remote mode: a backend in another host
methods.brief: Turns the backend into a client of a backend already running at an address, creating no database and no server.

parameters.name: pcHostAddr

parameters.name: pnPortNum

parameters.name: pcKeyId
parameters.role: the identifier of the key

parameters.name: pcSecret

notes: set it on both sides, before Start or ConnectTo

warnings: a value below 1 raises an error

extensions.name: SetMaxSkewQ
extensions.adds: does what the method does, then returns the object, so the call can be chained

methods.name: LastStatus

methods.brief: Returns the HTTP status of the last crossing.

methods.name: Endpoint

parameters.name: pnTimeoutMs

methods.brief: Starts this model as a backend in a child ring process on the loopback and returns its endpoint.

parameters.name: pnPortNum
parameters.role: the port the child listens on

parameters.name: pnTtlMs
parameters.role: how long the child lives before it ends itself, in milliseconds

methods.returns: a text, the endpoint such as 127.0.0.1:38050

methods.section: remote mode: a backend in another host
methods.brief: Starts the model as a child backend bound to a chosen interface, so other machines can reach it.

parameters.name: pcBindHost
parameters.role: the interface to bind, "0.0.0.0" for every interface

parameters.name: pnPortNum
parameters.role: the port

parameters.name: pnTtlMs
parameters.role: the child's lifetime in milliseconds

methods.name: RemoteLaunchCommands

parameters.name: pnTtlMs

parameters.name: pnPortNum

parameters.name: pnTtlMs

notes: the last line says nothing has run yet

methods.name: ReachAt
methods.section: remote mode: a backend in another host
methods.brief: Points a client at another address for the same backend, such as a routable address of a host bound to every interface.

methods.brief: Stops the server and closes the live state, or releases a client or a spawned-host manager.
methods.returns: the backend itself, so calls chain

methods.name: Create
methods.section: the parts' view of the live state
methods.brief: Writes one record into a dataset by a real HTTP POST, on behalf of a part.

parameters.name: pcPart
parameters.role: the part that writes, recorded in lower case

parameters.name: pcDataset
parameters.role: the dataset to insert into

parameters.name: paFields
parameters.role: the record as [ [ column, value ], ... ]

notes: the total changes as other parts write, because it is computed on every call
warnings: raises an error when the backend is not live and, for a dataset that is not two columns of a name and a quantity, error R41 invalid numeric string

methods.brief: Binds the actor on whose behalf parts act, so a write needs an effectful one.

methods.brief: Returns how long the last crossing took, in milliseconds, on a monotonic clock.

notes: refused writes, which cost 0 ms, are left out

methods.name: TrafficCount

methods.name: TrafficOf
methods.brief: Returns the crossings one part made.

parameters.name: pcPart
parameters.role: the part's name, matched without regard to case

methods.name: RefusedCrossings
methods.brief: Returns the writes the governance refused.

methods.brief: Writes the model, never the live state, to a text file that a host process can rebuild it from.

parameters.name: pcPath

classes.name: stzAppBody
classes.brief: Holds a readable snapshot of where an application's world is kept, as oApp.BodyQ returns it.
classes.description: It carries the kinds of body (graph database, files...) and the paths named in the SetBody brace: Graph, Files and Keep. Saving happens on the stzApp, never here.
classes.example:
? o1.Label()
#--> graph + files
? o1.HasKind(:files)
#--> 1

methods.name: init
methods.brief: Builds a body snapshot from the list of kinds of storage the world lives in.

parameters.name: paKinds
parameters.role: the list of kinds of body, such as [ :graphdb, :files ]

methods.name: Label
methods.brief: Returns the kinds joined with a plus sign, an empty text for no kind.
methods.returns: a text such as graph + files

methods.name: HasKind
methods.brief: TRUE if one of the body's kinds equals the given kind, compared without regard to case.

parameters.name: pKind
parameters.role: the kind to look for
