methods.brief: Returns the body as one sentence naming its kinds.
methods.returns: a text such as lives in graph + files

classes.name: stzAppCluster
classes.brief: Declares a fleet of worker processes by facet and proxies requests to them round-robin, with failover, circuit breakers, rate limits and latency telemetry.
classes.description: Ring's virtual machine runs one thread, so CPU-bound work is spread over processes: a cluster is a front object plus worker processes, each its own Ring program serving health and work addresses, started and queried through the reactor. Declare the fleet with WithNLP, WithMath, WithSearch, WithVision or WithFacet (any facet of the catalog), AddProfile for a custom one, or RegisterExternalWorker for a worker that already runs. Start spawns the processes, WaitReady waits for their health answers, and Route sends a path to a ready worker of a facet, failing over to the next worker and opening a circuit on a worker that keeps failing. The declaring, reading and refusing parts of this reference were run; Start, the success path of Route and the scale, restart and kill methods start or contact real processes and were read from the code only.
classes.example:
o1.WithNLP(2).WithMath(1)
? o1.FleetSize()
#--> 3
? o1.WorkersOf("nlp")
#--> 2
? len(o1.Route("nlp", "/work"))
#--> 0
? o1.RouteLastStatus()
#--> -1

methods.name: init
methods.brief: Builds an empty fleet with a worker pool, a reactor, latency telemetry and a rate limiter, and starts no process.
notes: the worker program is later run with the interpreter that is running the script

methods.name: AddProfile
methods.brief: Declares a number of worker processes for a profile, a capability tag with its capabilities, without starting them.

parameters.name: pcTag
parameters.role: the profile name, kept in lower case

parameters.name: paCaps
parameters.role: the list of capabilities of that profile

parameters.name: nWorkers
parameters.role: how many processes to declare, at least 1

notes: declaring the same tag again adds to its worker count, and every row waits with port 0 until Start
warnings: it raises an error for fewer than one worker

extensions.name: AddProfileQ
extensions.adds: does what the method does, then returns the object, so the call can be chained

methods.name: SetMaxTries
methods.brief: Sets how many workers one routed request may try before giving up; it starts at 3.

parameters.name: n
parameters.role: the number of workers to try, a value below 1 being taken as 1

methods.returns: the cluster itself, so calls chain

methods.name: SetCircuitBreaker
methods.brief: Sets how many consecutive failures open a worker's circuit and for how long it then stays skipped; it starts at 3 and 5000 ms.

parameters.name: nThreshold
parameters.role: the number of failures that open the circuit, a value below 1 being taken as 1

parameters.name: nCooldownMs
parameters.role: how long the circuit stays open, in milliseconds

methods.returns: the cluster itself, so calls chain
notes: after the cooldown one probe request decides whether the circuit closes again

methods.name: SetRateLimit
methods.brief: Limits how many requests per second a facet accepts at the front door, so that the excess is refused before any worker is reached.

parameters.name: pcFacet
parameters.role: the facet name

parameters.name: nRatePerSec
parameters.role: the sustained requests per second

parameters.name: nBurst
parameters.role: the largest burst absorbed at once

methods.returns: the cluster itself, so calls chain
notes: a facet with no limit is unlimited, and a refused request gives RouteLastStatus -429

methods.name: RegisterExternalWorker
methods.brief: Adds a worker that already runs somewhere, as a ready member of a facet's pool, without spawning anything.

parameters.name: pcFacet
parameters.role: the facet name

parameters.name: pcHost
parameters.role: the worker's host

parameters.name: nPort
parameters.role: the worker's port

methods.returns: the cluster itself, so calls chain
notes: it is counted as ready at once and is not verified until HealthCheck or a failed request, and Stop and ForceKill leave it alone

methods.name: WithFacet
methods.brief: Declares workers for any facet of the cluster's catalog, taking its capabilities and modules from that catalog.

parameters.name: pcFacet
parameters.role: a facet name present in the catalog, such as nlp, math, graph or vision

parameters.name: n
parameters.role: how many worker processes to declare

methods.returns: the cluster itself, so calls chain
notes: the catalog of this machine held 18 facets, from text and list to vision
warnings: it raises an error for a facet that is not in the catalog

methods.name: CatalogQ
methods.brief: Returns the facet catalog that WithFacet draws from, which can be customised before declaring facets.
methods.returns: a catalog object; its Names lists the facets

methods.name: WithNLP
methods.brief: Declares workers for the nlp facet.

parameters.name: n
parameters.role: how many worker processes

methods.returns: the cluster itself, so calls chain

methods.name: WithMath
methods.brief: Declares workers for the math facet.

parameters.name: n
parameters.role: how many worker processes

methods.returns: the cluster itself, so calls chain

methods.name: WithSearch
methods.brief: Declares workers for the search facet.

parameters.name: n
parameters.role: how many worker processes

methods.returns: the cluster itself, so calls chain

methods.name: WithVision
methods.brief: Declares workers for the vision facet.

parameters.name: n
parameters.role: how many worker processes

methods.returns: the cluster itself, so calls chain

methods.name: SetWorkerTTL
methods.brief: Sets how long each worker process lives before it ends by itself, in milliseconds; it starts at 30000.

parameters.name: nMs
parameters.role: the lifetime in milliseconds

methods.returns: the cluster itself, so calls chain
notes: it applies to workers started afterwards

methods.name: SetBasePort
methods.brief: Sets the first port of the fleet; later workers take the next ports in order.

parameters.name: nPort
parameters.role: the first port, 47100 by default

methods.returns: the cluster itself, so calls chain

methods.name: SetRingExe
methods.brief: Sets the Ring program that launches each worker.

parameters.name: pcPath
parameters.role: the path of the Ring executable

methods.returns: the cluster itself, so calls chain
notes: by default it is the interpreter running the script, or ring

methods.name: Start
methods.brief: Writes the worker script, spawns one process per declared worker on consecutive ports and records their jobs.
methods.returns: the cluster itself, so calls chain
notes: a second call raises an error, and rows added with RegisterExternalWorker are not spawned
warnings: it starts real processes and was not run

methods.name: WaitReady
methods.brief: Polls every worker's health address until all answer or the time runs out, and reports how many are ready.

parameters.name: nTimeoutMs
parameters.role: how long to wait in milliseconds

warnings: it sends requests to the workers' ports, so it was run only on a cluster with no worker, where it returned 0 at once

methods.name: Route
methods.brief: Sends a path to a ready worker of a facet and returns the body, trying other workers of the facet when one fails.

parameters.name: pcTag
parameters.role: the facet name

parameters.name: pcPath
parameters.role: the path and query to request, which must start with a slash and hold no line break

methods.returns: a text, the response body; empty when refused or when every try failed, with Why and RouteLastStatus saying why
notes: an unsafe path gives status -1, no ready worker gives -1, a rate limit gives -429, and each call gets a trace id that is also sent to the worker as the _trace parameter
warnings: the success path sends HTTP to a worker and was not run

methods.name: RouteLastStatus
methods.brief: Returns the HTTP status of the last routed request, or a negative code when none was sent.
methods.returns: a number: the status, -1 for no worker or an unsafe path or an undecidable request, -429 for a rate-limited one

methods.name: Why
methods.brief: Returns the reason of the last Route.
methods.returns: a text such as ok via host:port (attempt 1), no routable worker for facet, or rate limited; empty before any Route
notes: RouteRequest does not update it when it cannot classify the request, so it can then show an older reason

methods.name: TelemetryQ
methods.brief: Returns the telemetry object that holds the latency histograms and recent traces.

methods.name: LastTraceId
methods.brief: Returns the trace id given to the last Route.
methods.returns: a text; empty before any Route

methods.name: LatencyP50
methods.brief: Returns the median latency of a facet's routed requests in milliseconds, as a histogram bucket bound.

parameters.name: pcFacet
parameters.role: the facet name

methods.returns: a number; 0 when no request was timed
notes: a rate-limited request is not timed

methods.name: LatencyP90
methods.brief: Returns the 90th-percentile latency of a facet's routed requests in milliseconds.

parameters.name: pcFacet
parameters.role: the facet name

methods.returns: a number; 0 when no request was timed

methods.name: LatencyP99
methods.brief: Returns the 99th-percentile latency of a facet's routed requests in milliseconds.

parameters.name: pcFacet
parameters.role: the facet name

methods.returns: a number; 0 when no request was timed

methods.name: LatencyStats
methods.brief: Returns a facet's request count and latency percentiles as a hash list.

parameters.name: pcFacet
parameters.role: the facet name

methods.returns: a hash list with the keys facet, count, p50, p90, p95 and p99

methods.name: RecentTraces
methods.brief: Returns the last records of routed requests.

parameters.name: n
parameters.role: how many of the latest records to return

methods.returns: a list of lists, each with the trace id, the facet, the endpoint, the status, the duration in milliseconds and the number of attempts
notes: a refused request is recorded too, with the endpoint ratelimited or none

methods.name: LimiterQ
methods.brief: Returns the rate limiter that admits requests at the front door.

methods.name: RateLimitedCount
methods.brief: Returns how many requests of a facet were refused for exceeding its rate limit.

parameters.name: pcFacet
parameters.role: the facet name

methods.name: TokensAvailable
methods.brief: Returns how many requests a facet can still admit right now.

parameters.name: pcFacet
parameters.role: the facet name

methods.returns: a number; -1 for a facet with no limit
notes: the bucket refills with time, so the figure drifts between two reads

methods.name: CircuitOpenCount
methods.brief: Returns how many workers currently have an open circuit, and so are skipped.

methods.name: FleetSize
methods.brief: Returns how many workers are declared, ready or not.

methods.name: ReadyCount
methods.brief: Returns how many workers are marked ready.

methods.name: WorkersOf
methods.brief: Returns how many workers a profile has declared.

parameters.name: pcTag
parameters.role: the profile name, in any case

methods.returns: a number; 0 for an unknown profile

methods.name: Ports
methods.brief: Returns the port of each worker in declaration order.
methods.returns: a list of numbers; 0 for a worker not yet started

methods.name: PoolQ
methods.brief: Returns the worker pool that holds the profiles and their budgets.

methods.name: ReactorQ
methods.brief: Returns the reactor that spawns the workers and sends the requests.
methods.returns: a stzReactor; an empty text after Stop

methods.name: ClassifierQ
methods.brief: Returns the request classifier bound to this cluster's facet catalog, creating it on first use.

methods.name: RouteRequest
methods.brief: Classifies a request to a facet, then routes its path to a worker of that facet.

parameters.name: pcMethod
parameters.role: the HTTP method

parameters.name: pcPath
parameters.role: the request path

parameters.name: pcContentType
parameters.role: the content type

parameters.name: pcBody
parameters.role: the request body

methods.returns: a text, the response body; empty when the request cannot be classified or no worker is ready
notes: the classifier returned math for /math/solve and nothing for /work?q=hello, and no worker was ready in the run
warnings: an unclassified request leaves RouteLastStatus at -1

methods.name: HealthCheck
methods.brief: Asks every started worker for its health again and refreshes whether it is ready.
methods.returns: a number, the workers ready now
notes: a worker that stops answering turns not ready
warnings: it sends requests to the workers' ports and was run only on a cluster with no started worker, where it returned 0

methods.name: DeadCount
methods.brief: Returns how many started workers are not answering and are not being drained.

methods.name: ScaleUp
methods.brief: Spawns one more worker of a profile on a fresh port.

parameters.name: pcTag
parameters.role: the profile name

notes: the new worker is not ready until WaitReady or HealthCheck sees it answer
warnings: it starts a real process, so only the error for an unknown profile was run

methods.name: ScaleDown
methods.brief: Marks one ready worker of a profile as draining, so it receives no new requests and ends on its own lifetime.

parameters.name: pcTag
parameters.role: the profile name

methods.returns: a number, the drained worker's port; 0 when no ready worker is left to drain
notes: it does not stop the process: only the nothing-to-drain case was run

methods.name: RestartDead
methods.brief: Respawns every dead worker on a fresh port, killing the old process first.
methods.returns: a number, how many workers were restarted
warnings: it starts real processes when a worker is dead, and only the case with none dead was run

methods.name: ForceKill
methods.brief: Kills every spawned worker of a facet at once and marks it not ready.

parameters.name: pcTag
parameters.role: the facet name

methods.returns: a number, how many processes were killed

methods.name: KilledCount
methods.brief: Returns how many worker processes were forcibly killed over the cluster's life.

methods.name: FleetMetrics

methods.brief: Kills every spawned worker and frees the reactor, telemetry and rate limiter.

classes.name: stzAppGoal
classes.brief: Holds a readable snapshot of one goal of an application, as oApp.GoalQ returns it.
classes.description: It carries the goal's name and the attributes assigned in the AddGoalQ brace: Means, ReachedBy (the profile, planning by default), Within and Respecting. It evaluates nothing: the measuring of a goal's gap happens on the stzApp, which holds the live graph.
classes.example:
? o1.Name()
#--> Visited
? o1.Narrate()
#--> wants Visited -> reached by planning

methods.name: init
methods.brief: Builds a goal snapshot with the given name, the default profile planning and no means, window or respected rules.

parameters.name: pcName
parameters.role: the goal's name

methods.name: Name
methods.brief: Returns the goal's name as it was declared.

methods.name: Profile
methods.brief: Returns how the goal is reached, planning unless the declaration said otherwise.

methods.name: Narrate
methods.brief: Returns the goal as one sentence, with its window when it has one and the way it is reached.
methods.returns: a text such as wants Visited within a week -> reached by planning

classes.name: stzAppProfile
classes.brief: Describes one part of a solution: its name, kind, language, sources and the system it deploys to.
classes.description: A part is declared by the profile that owns it (WithApp, WithServer, WithPart), or built alone and added with AddApp. To names the deployment target, and System gives the scope its feature code is written in, kept so that operations accumulate. The part only describes: stzPlatform compiles the sources with the language set here.
classes.example:
? o1.Name()
#--> backend
? o1.Kind()
#--> server
? o1.DeploymentOSName()
#--> linux
? o1.HasScope()
#--> 0

methods.name: init
methods.brief: Builds a part of a solution with a name, the kind app, no language, no source and no deployment target.

parameters.name: pcName
parameters.role: the part's name, kept in lower case

notes: usually made by WithPart of the profile that owns it

methods.name: Name
methods.brief: Returns the part's name, in lower case.

methods.name: SetName
methods.brief: Sets the part's name, kept in lower case.

parameters.name: pcName
parameters.role: the new name

methods.name: Kind
methods.brief: Returns the kind of part: app, server, superapp or another word.

methods.name: SetKind
methods.brief: Sets the kind of part, kept in lower case.

parameters.name: pcKind
parameters.role: the kind, such as server or superapp

methods.returns: the part itself, so calls chain

methods.name: SetLanguage
methods.brief: Sets the language the part's code is written in, so a platform build can compile it.

parameters.name: pcLang
parameters.role: the language, such as c, cpp, zig or ring, kept in lower case

methods.returns: the part itself, so calls chain

methods.name: Language
methods.brief: Returns the language of the part's code.

methods.brief: TRUE if a language is set.

classes.name: stzAppRequest
classes.brief: Holds one HTTP request as a plain value: method, path, headers, body, query pairs and the path parameters a route bound.
classes.description: A server builds it from the parsed wire text and a handler reads it. The query string is split off the path at birth, so Path never carries a ?. Header names are matched without regard to case, while query keys and path parameters are matched with their exact case. WantsClose answers the keep-alive question from the protocol and the Connection header.
classes.example:
? o1.Path()
#--> /users/42
? o1.Query("page")
#--> 2
? o1.Header("host")
#--> shop.test

methods.name: init
methods.brief: Builds a request from its method, path, header pairs and body, and splits any query string off the path.

parameters.name: cMethodVal
parameters.role: the HTTP method as sent, such as GET

parameters.name: cPathVal
parameters.role: the request target, possibly with a ?query part, which is removed from Path

parameters.name: aHeadersVal
parameters.role: a list of [ name, value ] pairs

parameters.name: cBodyVal
parameters.role: the body text

methods.name: Method
methods.brief: Returns the HTTP method exactly as it was given, without changing its case.

methods.name: Path
methods.brief: Returns the path with the query string already removed.

methods.name: Headers
methods.brief: Returns every header as a list of [ name, value ] pairs, in the order they arrived.
methods.returns: a list of [ text, text ] pairs

methods.name: Header
methods.brief: Returns the value of the first header whose name matches, ignoring case.

parameters.name: cName
parameters.role: the header name, in any case

methods.returns: a text; an empty text when the header is absent

methods.name: Body
methods.brief: Returns the body text as it was given.

methods.name: Protocol
methods.brief: Returns the protocol version of the request, HTTP/1.1 until SetProtocol says otherwise.

methods.name: SetProtocol
methods.brief: Sets the protocol version that WantsClose reads.

parameters.name: cProtocolVal
parameters.role: the protocol text, such as HTTP/1.0

methods.returns: the request itself, so calls chain

methods.name: WantsClose
methods.brief: TRUE if the peer asked for the connection to close after the response, by Connection: close or by being HTTP/1.0 without keep-alive.

methods.name: ParseQuery
methods.brief: Moves the ?key=value&key=value part of the path into the query pairs; init already did it, so a second call finds nothing to do.
notes: the first occurrence wins when a key is repeated, as for Query
warnings: a pair without an equals sign is dropped; values are kept as sent, percent escapes are not decoded

methods.name: Query
methods.brief: Returns the value of a query key, or every query pair when the key is empty.

parameters.name: cKey
parameters.role: the query key, matched with its exact case, or an empty text for all pairs

methods.returns: a text, an empty text for an absent key; a list of [ key, value ] pairs for the empty key
notes: a value is returned as it was sent: a%20b stays a%20b

methods.name: SetParams
methods.brief: Stores the path parameters that the router bound for this request, such as the id of /user/:id.

parameters.name: paParams
parameters.role: a list of [ name, value ] pairs

methods.returns: the request itself, so calls chain

methods.name: Params
methods.brief: Returns the path parameters the router bound, as the list of [ name, value ] pairs.
methods.returns: a list of [ text, text ] pairs; empty until SetParams is called

methods.name: Param
methods.brief: Returns the value of a path parameter by its exact name.

parameters.name: cKey
parameters.role: the parameter name, matched with its exact case

methods.returns: a text; an empty text for an absent name

classes.name: stzAppResponse
classes.brief: Holds one HTTP response that a handler fills and the server renders to bytes; it does no socket work itself.
classes.description: Status, Header, Text, Html and Json compose it. Send buffers the body once and marks it sent; HttpBytes renders the HTTP/1.1 wire form with CRLF line endings and a Content-Length counted in bytes. Json uses a simple serializer in which a flat [ key, value, ... ] list is an object; see its warning for the shapes it gets wrong.
classes.example:
o1.Status(201, "Created")
o1.Json([ "id", 7, "name", "Ana" ])
? o1.Body()
#--> {"id":7,"name":"Ana"}
? o1.StatusCode()
#--> 201

methods.name: init
methods.brief: Builds an empty response with status 200 OK and no headers, ready to be filled and sent.

parameters.name: oClientRef
parameters.role: a legacy slot from before the reactor, kept and never used

methods.name: Status
methods.brief: Sets the status code and, when text is given, the reason phrase that HttpBytes writes.

parameters.name: nCode
parameters.role: the status code, such as 404

parameters.name: cText
parameters.role: the reason phrase

methods.returns: the response itself, so calls chain
warnings: an empty cText keeps the previous phrase, so Status(202, "") after Status(201, "Created") reads 202 Created

methods.name: Header
methods.brief: Adds a header to the response; the same name added twice is written twice, never replaced.

parameters.name: cName
parameters.role: the header name

parameters.name: cValue
parameters.role: the header value

methods.returns: the response itself, so calls chain

methods.name: Headers
methods.brief: Returns the headers added so far as a list of [ name, value ] pairs, in order.
methods.returns: a list of [ text, text ] pairs

methods.name: StatusCode
methods.brief: Returns the status code, 200 until Status changes it.

methods.name: IsSent
methods.brief: TRUE if a body has been buffered by Send, Text, Html or Json.

methods.name: Body
methods.brief: Returns the buffered body, an empty text before anything is sent.

methods.name: Json
methods.brief: Serializes a value to JSON, adds the application/json content type and buffers it as the body.

parameters.name: aData
parameters.role: the value: a flat list [ key, value, key, value ] becomes an object, any other list an array

notes: build the object as a flat list and the output is what a client expects
warnings: a Ring hash list of pairs such as [ :a = 1 ] becomes an array of one-pair objects, not an object; a list of two texts becomes an object; a list of an odd number of texts raises R2; texts are not escaped, so a quote inside one gives invalid JSON; an object inside the data becomes ""

methods.name: Text
methods.brief: Adds the text/plain content type and buffers the text as the body.

parameters.name: cText
parameters.role: the text to send

methods.name: Html
methods.brief: Adds the text/html content type and buffers the markup as the body.

parameters.name: cHtml
parameters.role: the HTML text to send

methods.name: Send
methods.brief: Buffers the body and marks the response sent; nothing is written to a socket, and a second call changes nothing.

parameters.name: cContent
parameters.role: the body, a text or a number, kept as text

notes: the server writes HttpBytes through the reactor
warnings: once sent, the body can not be replaced, though Status and Header still change the object

methods.name: HttpBytes
methods.brief: Renders the whole HTTP/1.1 response: status line, headers, a Content-Length counted in bytes, a blank line, then the body, all with CRLF.
notes: a text with an accented e counts 2 bytes in Content-Length

methods.name: NotFound
methods.brief: Sets status 404 and sends the message as plain text, Not Found when the message is empty.

parameters.name: cMessage
parameters.role: the text of the page, or an empty text for the default

methods.name: InternalError
methods.brief: Sets status 500 and sends the message as plain text, Internal Server Error when the message is empty.

parameters.name: cMessage
parameters.role: the text of the page, or an empty text for the default

methods.name: ObjectToJson
methods.brief: Returns the JSON text of a text, a number or a list; this is the simple serializer behind Json.

parameters.name: obj
parameters.role: the value to serialize

notes: numbers keep the library's own formatting, so 3.5 reads 3.50
warnings: the same limits as Json: a list that starts with a text is read as key and value pairs, a text is not escaped and an object becomes ""

classes.name: stzAppRouter
classes.brief: Holds the route table of the application server and finds the handler for a method and a path.
classes.description: Routes are matched exactly first, then by pattern: a :name segment captures one path segment and a trailing * captures the rest of the path. Among patterns the first registered wins, and the method must match too. The router returns the handler and the captured parameters and never calls the handler. Build it without parentheses, as in new stzAppRouter: with () the call raises R19.
classes.example:
o1.AddRoute("get", "/user/:id", "showUser")
? o1.MatchRoute("GET", "/user/42")[2][2]
#--> showUser
? o1.MatchRoute("GET", "/user/42")[3][2][1][2]
#--> 42
? o1.MatchRoute("GET", "/nothing")[1][2]
#--> 0

methods.name: AddRoute
methods.brief: Registers a handler for a method and a path pattern; the method is stored in upper case.

parameters.name: cMethod
parameters.role: the HTTP method in any case

parameters.name: cPath
parameters.role: the path or pattern, such as /user/:id or /static/*

parameters.name: fHandler
parameters.role: the handler to return on a match, a function or any value

methods.name: Routes
methods.brief: Returns every registered route as [ method, pattern, handler ], in registration order.

methods.name: HasRoute
methods.brief: TRUE if a route with exactly that method and exactly that path text was registered; a pattern is not matched, only compared.

parameters.name: cMethod
parameters.role: the HTTP method in any case

parameters.name: cPath
parameters.role: the path text, compared as written

methods.name: GetHandler
methods.brief: Returns the handler registered for exactly that method and path text, an empty text when there is none; patterns are not matched.

parameters.name: cMethod
parameters.role: the HTTP method in any case

parameters.name: cPath
parameters.role: the path text, compared as written

methods.returns: the handler, or an empty text

methods.name: MatchRoute
methods.brief: Returns the route for a request: the exact path first, then :name and trailing * patterns, the first registered winning.

parameters.name: cMethod
parameters.role: the HTTP method in any case

parameters.name: cPath
parameters.role: the request path without its query

methods.returns: a list [ matched, handler, params ]: matched is 1 or 0, params the list of [ name, value ] pairs, with the key * for a wildcard
notes: the request path is read by its non-empty segments, so a trailing slash does not matter; a wildcard also matches nothing after its prefix and then captures an empty text

methods.name: AddMiddleware
methods.brief: Stores a middleware function for a path prefix; nothing in the router or the server ever reads the list, so it never runs.

parameters.name: cPath
parameters.role: the path the middleware should cover

parameters.name: fMiddleware
parameters.role: the function meant to run before the routes

notes: stored and never applied; see stzAppServer.Use

extensions.name: AddMiddlewareQ
extensions.adds: does what the method does, then returns the object, so the call can be chained

methods.name: AddStaticRoute
methods.brief: Stores a URL path and a folder for static files; nothing in the router or the server ever reads the list, so no file is served.

parameters.name: cPath
parameters.role: the URL path meant to map to the folder

parameters.name: cDirectory
parameters.role: the folder of files

notes: stored and never applied; see stzAppServer.Static

extensions.name: AddStaticRouteQ
extensions.adds: does what the method does, then returns the object, so the call can be chained

classes.name: stzAppServer
classes.brief: Hosts routes, a REST floor over a database, raw device streams and supervised agents on one resident event loop, served on a localhost-first HTTP listener.
classes.description: The server is a persistent host rather than a per-request library: Start binds a listener on a reactor (an engine thread), and the serve loop (ServeOne, RunFor or Run) drains framed requests, runs the matching handler and writes the answer back; no callback ever crosses into the Ring VM. One host serves four shapes. WEB: Get_, Post, Put_ and Delete add routes whose handlers receive a request and a response. MBaaS: Expose and ExposeWithKey turn a stzDatabase table into list, count and read, create, update, delete routes. IoT: ListenRaw opens a raw TCP listener whose handler answers with RawWrite. AGENTS: HostAgents attaches an agent host that shares the loop and ticks between serve slices, with a read-only view at GET /agents. /health is always answered and /metrics appears once Observe attaches a perf monitor. Bind to 127.0.0.1 unless the server must be reached from outside, and then call RequireSignedRequests; MountAuth and MountOidcProvider serve a login router and an identity provider from the same listener. Known gaps today, each carried as a warning on its method: Use and Static store their arguments but never act, and Stop leaves Port and Uptime unreset.
classes.example:
o1.Get_("/greet", func oReq, oResp { oResp.Text("hello") })
o1.Start(0, "127.0.0.1")
? o1.IsRunning()
#--> 1
o1.Stop()

sections.title: oidc provider (this server as an idp)
agents: the agent host is the same host

methods.name: init
methods.brief: Builds a stopped server with an empty route table; nothing listens until a start method is called.
notes: Routes, mounts and observation can all be set up before Start

methods.name: Start
methods.brief: Binds an HTTP listener to a host and port, port 0 meaning any free one; raises an error if it cannot bind or already runs.

parameters.name: nPortNum
parameters.role: the port to listen on, 0 for any free port

parameters.name: cHostAddr
parameters.role: the address to bind, "" for 127.0.0.1

notes: Bind to 127.0.0.1 unless the server is meant to be reached from other machines, and then require signed requests

methods.name: StartTls
methods.brief: Binds an HTTPS listener that decrypts each connection before routing; raises an error when a certificate, key or CA file cannot be used.
usage: StartTls(nPortNum, cHostAddr, cCertPath, cKeyPath, cCaPath, bRequireClient)

parameters.name: nPortNum
parameters.role: the port to listen on, 0 for any free port

parameters.name: cHostAddr
parameters.role: the address to bind, "" for 127.0.0.1

parameters.name: cCertPath
parameters.role: the server certificate file

parameters.name: cKeyPath
parameters.role: the private key file

parameters.name: cCaPath
parameters.role: the CA file that checks client certificates, "" for none

parameters.name: bRequireClient
parameters.role: 1 to demand a valid client certificate (mutual TLS)

notes: The failing path was run with missing files (error -13); the success path was read from the body, as no certificate was available

methods.name: StartHttps
methods.brief: Binds a one-way HTTPS listener, with a server certificate and key but no client certificate check.

parameters.name: nPortNum
parameters.role: the port to listen on, 0 for any free port

parameters.name: cHostAddr
parameters.role: the address to bind, "" for 127.0.0.1

parameters.name: cCertPath
parameters.role: the server certificate file

parameters.name: cKeyPath
parameters.role: the private key file

notes: Same as StartTls with an empty CA and no client check

methods.name: Stop
methods.brief: Closes the HTTP and raw listeners and destroys the reactor; does nothing when the server is not running.
methods.returns: the server, so calls can be chained
notes: Routes and mounts are kept for the next Start, but Port and Uptime are not reset (see their notes)

methods.name: IsRunning
methods.brief: TRUE if a listener is bound, from a successful start until the next stop.

methods.name: Port
methods.brief: Returns the port the HTTP listener is bound to, the real one when 0 was asked for.
methods.returns: a number; 0 before the first start
notes: The value is kept after Stop, so it names the last port used rather than a live one

methods.name: Host
methods.brief: Returns the address given to the last start.

methods.name: Uptime
methods.brief: Returns the seconds since the last start, as a number with decimals.
methods.returns: a number of seconds; 0 before the first start
notes: It keeps growing after Stop, because the start time is not cleared

methods.name: RequestCount
methods.brief: Returns how many HTTP requests the server has handled, including malformed ones answered with 400.
notes: The counter is never reset, not even by Stop

methods.name: ReactorQ
methods.brief: Returns the stzReactor that runs the listeners, to read or drive it directly.
methods.returns: an stzReactor; an empty string when the server is not running

methods.name: ServeOne
methods.brief: Waits for one request, HTTP or raw, answers it, and returns; gives up after the timeout.

parameters.name: nTimeoutMs
parameters.role: the longest wait, in milliseconds

methods.returns: TRUE if a request was handled, FALSE on timeout
notes: Accept and close events are drained along the way and do not count as work
warnings: Raises an error when the server is not running

methods.name: RunFor
methods.brief: Serves every request that arrives within a number of milliseconds, ticking hosted agents between slices.

parameters.name: nMs
parameters.role: how long to serve, in milliseconds

notes: With agents hosted, each wait on the socket is cut to AgentSlice ms so the agents keep ticking on an idle socket

methods.name: Run
methods.brief: Serves requests until Stop is called from a handler or the process is killed, ticking hosted agents between slices.
methods.returns: the server, once the server is stopped
notes: Not run here because it blocks: described from its body, a loop of ServeOne(1000) while the server is running

methods.name: Get_
methods.brief: Adds a GET route; its handler is called as fHandler(oReq, oResp) with the request and the response.

parameters.name: cPath
parameters.role: the route path, with :name segments for parameters and a trailing * for the rest

parameters.name: fHandler
parameters.role: the function called with the request and the response

methods.returns: the server, so calls can be chained
notes: A request whose path matches only a route of another method answers 404

methods.name: Post
methods.brief: Adds a POST route; a handler is called as fHandler(oReq, oResp).

parameters.name: cPath
parameters.role: the route path, with :name segments for parameters and a trailing * for the rest

parameters.name: fHandler
parameters.role: the function called with the request and the response

methods.returns: the server, so calls can be chained

methods.name: Put_
methods.brief: Adds a PUT route; a handler is called as fHandler(oReq, oResp).

parameters.name: cPath
parameters.role: the route path, with :name segments for parameters and a trailing * for the rest

parameters.name: fHandler
parameters.role: the function called with the request and the response

methods.returns: the server, so calls can be chained

methods.name: Delete
methods.brief: Adds a DELETE route; a handler is called as fHandler(oReq, oResp).

parameters.name: cPath
parameters.role: the route path, with :name segments for parameters and a trailing * for the rest

parameters.name: fHandler
parameters.role: the function called with the request and the response

methods.returns: the server, so calls can be chained

methods.name: Observe
methods.brief: Records every request into a perf monitor, adds a /metrics page and puts response percentiles and the request rate into /health.

parameters.name: poMonitor
parameters.role: the stzPerfMonitor that receives the timer http.request.ms and the counters http.requests and http.errors

methods.returns: the server, so calls can be chained
notes: The server keeps a copy of the monitor, but its metrics live in the engine, so the caller's monitor reads the same counts

methods.name: IsObserved
methods.brief: TRUE if a perf monitor was attached.

methods.name: ObserveRoutes
methods.brief: Does what the observation above does and also times each route, in a family labeled by method, route and status class.

parameters.name: poMonitor
parameters.role: the stzPerfMonitor that receives the metrics, including the family http.route.ms

methods.returns: the server, so calls can be chained

methods.name: Use
methods.brief: Leaves every request unchanged today instead of running the middleware before the routes under a path.

parameters.name: cPath
parameters.role: the path the middleware should cover

parameters.name: fMiddleware
parameters.role: the function meant to run before the routes

methods.returns: the server, so calls can be chained
notes: Add a route or check inside the handler until the router uses the list
warnings: The middleware is stored in the router but nothing ever reads the list, so it never runs (checked with paths /a, / and *)

methods.name: Static
methods.brief: Leaves a folder unserved today instead of serving its files under a path; a request for a file in it answers 404.

parameters.name: cPath
parameters.role: the URL path meant to map to the folder

parameters.name: cDirectory
parameters.role: the folder of files to serve

methods.returns: the server, so calls can be chained
warnings: The static routes are stored in the router but nothing ever reads the list (checked with paths /files and /)

methods.name: Expose
methods.brief: Serves a table of an open stzDatabase as a REST resource under /api/ followed by the table name, keyed by an id column.

parameters.name: oDb
parameters.role: the open stzDatabase that holds the table

parameters.name: cTable
parameters.role: the table to expose

methods.returns: the server, so calls can be chained
notes: GET lists rows, GET .../count counts, GET/PUT/DELETE .../<id> read, update, delete one row, POST inserts from a form body; values are SQL-escaped, and a route you added yourself wins over the same path
warnings: A table with no id column answers 500 (no such column: id) on the routes that address one row

methods.name: ExposeWithKey
methods.brief: Does the same as the id-keyed exposure but finds single rows through another key column.

parameters.name: cTable

parameters.name: cKeyCol

methods.name: ExposeReadOnly
methods.brief: Serves a table of an open stzDatabase as a REST resource that can only be read, so no route of it changes or removes a row.

parameters.name: oDb
parameters.role: the open stzDatabase that holds the table

parameters.name: cTable
parameters.role: the table to expose

methods.returns: the server, so calls can be chained
notes: Only GET is served: the list, .../count and .../<id> answer as they do under Expose, while POST, PUT and DELETE on the table answer 405 and leave the table untouched; a route you added yourself still wins over the same path

methods.name: ExposeReadOnlyWithKey
methods.brief: Does the same as the read-only exposure but finds single rows through another key column.

parameters.name: oDb
parameters.role: the open stzDatabase that holds the table

parameters.name: cTable
parameters.role: the table to expose

parameters.name: cKeyCol
parameters.role: the column that names one row, such as uuid

methods.returns: the server, so calls can be chained

methods.name: RequireSignedRequests

classes.name: stzAppTopology
classes.brief: The application model of a solution: named datasets, the role each part plays over them, and device models, all held as data.
classes.description: A solution holds datasets (a menu, an order history) and gives each part a role over them: menu, dashboard, api or device. One model drives both the emulator, where each part renders its own app, and the real deployed app. The dashboard figures are genuine computations: orders joined with the menu prices and aggregated by the engine. Names of datasets and parts are stored in lower case. The Q forms (AddDatasetQ, SetPartRoleQ and so on) return the model so that calls chain; the plain forms return nothing. Attach a model to a delivery with SetAppTopology.
classes.receiver: o1 = new stzAppTopology("bistro") o1.AddDataset("menu", [ [ "Couscous", "semolina", 12 ], [ "Tea", "mint", 3 ] ]) o1.AddDataset("orders", [ [ "Couscous", 2 ], [ "Tea", 4 ] ]) o1.SetPartRole("admin", "dashboard", "orders")
classes.example:
? o1.RoleOf("admin")
#--> dashboard
? @@( o1.DashboardOf("admin") )
#--> [ [ [ "Couscous", 2, 24 ], [ "Tea", 4, 12 ] ], 36, "Couscous", 24 ]
? @@( o1.ColumnsOf("orders") )
#--> [ "c1", "c2" ]

classes.name: stzApriori
classes.brief: Finds items that occur together in baskets and states them as readable if-then rules with their support and confidence.
classes.description: Transactions are lists of items. The analyser counts the frequent itemsets of one, two and three items, which are the classic basket sizes, and turns the pairs and triples into rules such as IF jam THEN bread (confidence 1). The count runs in the engine. Items are compared in lower case. A rule's support is the number of transactions that hold all its items and its confidence is that number over the transactions that hold the if part, so every rule can be read back as knowledge.
classes.example:
? o1.NumberOfTransactions()
#--> 6
? @@( o1.FrequentItemsets(3) )
#--> [ [ [ "bread" ], 5 ], [ [ "butter" ], 3 ] ]
aRules = o1.Rules(2, 0.9)
? aRules[1][:if][1] + " -> " + aRules[1][:then]
#--> jam -> bread

methods.brief: Returns every set of one, two or three items that occurs in at least that many transactions, with its count.

parameters.role: the smallest number of transactions an itemset must appear in

methods.returns: a list of [ items, count ] pairs, the items a list in alphabetical order; larger sets are not searched
notes: itemsets come in the order they were first counted, not by size or count

methods.name: Rules
methods.brief: Returns if-then rules from the frequent pairs and triples, keeping those whose confidence reaches the threshold.

parameters.name: nMinCount
parameters.role: the smallest number of transactions an itemset must appear in

parameters.name: nMinConf
parameters.role: the smallest confidence, from 0 to 1

methods.returns: a list of hash lists [ :if, :then, :support, :confidence ]; :if is a list of items, :then one item, :support the itemset's count, :confidence its count divided by the count of the :if items
notes: every item of a frequent set takes a turn as the consequent, so a pair gives two candidate rules

classes.name: stzAuth
classes.brief: Authenticates the users of an app: keeps salted password hashes, opens and ends sessions, and resolves a login into roles and an actor.
classes.description: It holds a credential store (user name to a salted Argon2id hash, never the plaintext) and issues opaque 64-character session tokens. Around the password it offers a second factor (TOTP with recovery codes), passwordless doors (magic link, emailed code, passkey), external sign-in (OpenID Connect, SAML), a brute-force lockout, an administrative lock, password reset by mail, and roles that turn a live session into the stzSystemActor that governance reasons about. The store is in memory unless SetStore is given a database store. Every flow has an At form that takes the moment as epoch seconds, which makes expiry and lockout testable; the plain forms read the clock. Failures answer an empty text, 0 or [ ] instead of raising, except for a missing mail port, relying party, provider or client, which raise.
classes.example:
? o1.Authenticate("alice", "demo-pass-one")
#--> 1
? o1.Authenticate("alice", "wrong")
#--> 0

classes.name: stzAuthDbStore
classes.brief: Keeps the users, sessions, two-factor rows, challenges, roles, passkeys and locks of stzAuth in a sqlite database, so they outlive the process.
classes.description: It answers the same calls as stzAuthMemoryStore. Its only state is a stzDatabase, whose connection is an engine handle, so a copied store still writes the same database. Every statement binds its values and none is spliced into SQL text. Give it a file path to be durable, or :memory: for a real sqlite that lives only in the process.
classes.example:
o1.PutUser("alice", "hash-of-alice")
o1.GrantRole("alice", "editor")
? o1.HasUser("alice")
#--> 1
? @@( o1.RolesOf("alice") )
#--> [ "editor" ]

classes.name: stzAuthMemoryStore

classes.description: It is the default store of stzAuth and the reference for the store contract: PutUser, UserHash, PutSession, Session and the rest. Nothing outlives the process; stzAuthDbStore answers the same calls over sqlite. Pass a database store, never a shared memory one, to production: Ring copies an object on assignment, so a memory store handed in from outside diverges from the caller's copy.
classes.example:
o1.PutUser("alice", "hash-of-alice")
o1.GrantRole("alice", "editor")
? o1.HasUser("alice")
#--> 1
? @@( o1.RolesOf("alice") )
#--> [ "editor" ]

classes.name: stzAuthResponder
classes.brief: Carries out the LockAccount and RevokeSession actions of a response plan on a stzAuth.
classes.description: A response plan proposes containment as data; a responder performs verbs for real once a committing actor approves. This one answers the two that authentication owns: LockAccount closes every login path of an account with the reason locked by a containment plan, and RevokeSession ends every session of a user. The other four verbs raise an error that names the responder to wire. It holds the stzAuth by reference, so the caller's object sees the change.
classes.receiver: oAuth = new stzAuth() oAuth.Register("dana", "invented-pw") o1 = new stzAuthResponder(oAuth)
classes.example:
cTok = oAuth.LoginAt("dana", "invented-pw", 1700000000)
o1.RevokeSession("dana")
? oAuth.NumberOfSessions()
#--> 0
o1.LockAccount("dana")
? oAuth.IsAccountLocked("dana")
#--> 1

methods.brief: Closes the named account until UnlockAccount: every login path refuses it.

parameters.name: pcTarget

methods.returns: nothing; the stzAuth then answers IsAccountLocked
notes: the lock carries the reason locked by a containment plan, and the stzAuth notes it in the security refusal record
warnings: an unknown user name is locked too and no error is raised; the sessions already open are kept and work again after UnlockAccount

classes.name: stzBarPlot
classes.brief: Draws a list of numbers, or labelled numbers, as vertical bars: as text for a terminal, as SVG, or as a PNG picture.
classes.description: One plot object answers three ways. ToString (and Show) draws block characters, axes and labels in text; ToSVG needs no graphics device; ToPNG draws on the GPU. The setters (height, bar width and spacing, axes, labels, values, percentages, average line, characters) shape the text picture only: the SVG and PNG carry the values, the labels, AddValues and AddAverage and nothing else, and print no text unless a :Font option is given. Bars are scaled so the largest value fills the height. Setters answer nothing, so they cannot be chained. stzHBarPlot (sideways bars) and stzMBarPlot (grouped bars) inherit from it. Several settings store a value no picture reads today (SetWidth, SetMaxWidth and the width of SetSize), SetMaxLabelWidth does not truncate, and SetLabelChar renames labels taken from the keys; see their warnings. Gallery: doc/gallery/stzBarPlot/basic.png (average line), values.png (values above twelve bars) and nofont.png (no font: bars and gridlines only), each with its .ring script, seen right by stzlib-docs visual pass (a model reading the PNG), 2026-10-05, not a person; terminal.txt is the text picture, read as text and judged right.

classes.name: stzBinaryNumber
classes.brief: Holds a number written in binary and converts it to decimal, octal and hexadecimal, or builds it from them.
classes.description: It is the binary form behind stzNumber.ToBinaryForm: a stzNumber builds one with new stzBinaryNumber(cText), and you can build one yourself with new stzBinaryNumber("0b1011") or StzBinaryNumberQ("0b1011"). The text starts with b or 0b, followed by binary digits and optionally a dot and more digits; an empty text gives zero. Content returns the text as given, prefix included. ToDecimalForm, ToOctalForm and ToHexForm convert (by hand 0b1011 is 8+2+1 = 11 = 0o13 = 0xB), and FromDecimalForm, FromHexForm and FromOctalForm replace the number in place, the last two needing the 0x and 0o prefixes. The Bitwise methods work on the decimal value and answer a number. Whole numbers convert exactly; the fractional part is exact in decimal and octal but ToHexForm drops it. Several methods are broken today and each says so in its own entry: IntegerPart and Reversed raise R24 when a dot is present, WithPrefix doubles the prefix, the reversals reverse the prefix with the digits, ToScientificNotationForm raises R14, and an uppercase 0B prefix reads as 0.
classes.example:
? o1.ToDecimalForm()
#--> 11
? o1.ToOctalForm()
#--> 0o13
? o1.ToHexForm()
#--> 0xB
? o1.BitwiseAND(6)
#--> 2
? o1.BitwiseLeftShift(2)
#--> 44
o2 = new stzBinaryNumber("0b101.11")
? o2.ToDecimalForm()
#--> 5.75
o3 = new stzBinaryNumber("")
o3.FromDecimalForm(12500)
? o3.Content()
#--> 0b11000011010100

methods.name: init
methods.brief: Builds a binary number from a text such as 0b1011, or a zero binary number from an empty text.

parameters.name: cNumber
parameters.role: the number as a text starting with b or 0b, followed by binary digits and optionally a dot and more digits, or an empty text for zero, anything else raises an error

notes: an empty text gives the content b0; it is reached from stzNumber.ToBinaryForm and from StzBinaryNumberQ(cNumber)
warnings: the uppercase prefix 0B is accepted but its value is read as 0: new stzBinaryNumber("0B101").ToDecimalForm() answers 0 where 5 is right; -0b101 is accepted and reads as -5, but 0b-101, the text FromDecimalForm(-5) builds, is refused

methods.name: Content
methods.brief: Returns the binary number as it was written, prefix included.
notes: Value and BinaryNumber are the same call

methods.name: BinaryNumber
methods.brief: Returns the binary number as it was written, prefix included.
notes: the same call as Content

methods.name: WithPrefix
methods.brief: Returns the content with the binary prefix put in front of it.
notes: use Content to read the number; the prefix comes from BinaryNumberPrefix(), 0b by default
warnings: the prefix is added even though the content already starts with one: 0b1011 answers 0b0b1011 and b1111 answers 0bb1111

methods.name: operator
methods.brief: Applies a bitwise operator written as text to the number and a second number.

parameters.name: pOp
parameters.role: the operator as text, one of & (and), a pipe (or), ^ (xor), ~ (complement), << or >>

parameters.name: pValue
parameters.role: the second operand, ignored by ~

methods.returns: a number, the result of the operation; an empty text for an operator that is not listed
notes: 0b1011 with & and 6 gives 2, with << and 1 gives 22
warnings: an unknown operator such as + answers an empty text without an error

methods.name: BitwiseAND
methods.brief: Returns the bitwise AND of the number and another number.

parameters.name: nOtherNumber
parameters.role: the second operand, a decimal number

notes: by hand 1011 and 0110 give 0010: 0b1011 with 6 answers 2

methods.name: BitwiseOR
methods.brief: Returns the bitwise OR of the number and another number.

parameters.name: nOtherNumber
parameters.role: the second operand, a decimal number

notes: by hand 1011 or 0110 give 1111: 0b1011 with 6 answers 15

methods.name: BitwiseXOR
methods.brief: Returns the bitwise exclusive OR of the number and another number.

parameters.name: nOtherNumber
parameters.role: the second operand, a decimal number

notes: by hand 1011 xor 0110 give 1101: 0b1011 with 6 answers 13

methods.name: BitwiseOnesComplement
methods.brief: Returns the bitwise complement of the number, which is minus the number minus one.

parameters.name: nOtherNumber
parameters.role: required by the signature but ignored

methods.returns: a number, negative for a positive number
notes: 0b1011 (11) answers -12 and 0b110 (6) answers -7, whatever the argument is

methods.name: BitwiseLeftShift
methods.brief: Returns the number shifted left by some bits, which doubles it once per bit.

parameters.name: nOtherNumber
parameters.role: how many bits to shift

notes: 0b1011 shifted by 2 gives 44, by hand 101100

methods.name: BitwiseRightShift
methods.brief: Returns the number shifted right by some bits, which halves it once per bit, dropping the remainder.

parameters.name: nOtherNumber
parameters.role: how many bits to shift

notes: 0b1011 shifted by 1 gives 5, by hand 101

methods.name: IntegerPart
methods.brief: Returns the part of the content before the dot; a number without a dot is returned whole.
methods.returns: a text, with its prefix kept
notes: the prefix is part of the answer: 0b1011 gives 0b1011
warnings: with a fractional part it raises error R24 (uninitialized variable _oTempStr_) instead of answering the part before the dot: 0b101.11 and b10.1 both raise

methods.name: FractionalPart
methods.brief: Returns the binary digits after the dot, or an empty text when there is no dot.
methods.returns: a text of digits, without the dot
notes: 0b101.11 gives 11

methods.name: Reversed
methods.brief: Returns the number written backwards, integer part and fractional part each reversed, joined by a dot.
notes: use IntegerPartReversed on a number without a fraction only to turn the digits, and ignore the prefix at its end
warnings: the prefix is reversed with the digits, so 0b1011 answers 1101b0, which is not a binary number, and with a fractional part it raises error R24 as IntegerPart does

methods.name: HasFractionalPart
methods.brief: TRUE if the number has digits after the dot.
notes: ContainsFractionalPart is the same call

methods.name: FractionalPartReversed
methods.brief: Returns the digits after the dot written backwards.
methods.returns: a text of digits; empty without a dot
notes: 0b11.01 gives 10

methods.name: IntegerPartReversed
methods.brief: Returns the integer part written backwards, prefix included.
notes: with a fractional part it raises error R24 as IntegerPart does
warnings: the prefix is reversed with the digits: 0b1011 answers 1101b0 and b1111 answers 1111b

methods.name: ToStzNumber
methods.brief: Returns the value as a stzNumber, read from its decimal form.
notes: 0b1011 gives the number 11

methods.name: ToStzString
methods.brief: Returns the binary text, prefix included, as a stzString.

methods.name: IntegerPartToDecimalForm
methods.brief: Returns the integer part converted to decimal, as text.
notes: by hand 1011 is 8+2+1: 0b1011 gives 11 and 0b101.11 gives 5; IntegerPartToDecimal is the same call

methods.name: FractionalPartToDecimalForm
methods.brief: Returns the fractional part converted to decimal, as a text such as 0.75.
methods.returns: a text; 0 when there is no fraction
notes: by hand .11 is 1/2+1/4: 0b101.11 gives 0.75 and 0b11.01 gives 0.25; FractionalPartToDecimal is the same call

methods.name: FractionalPartToDecimalFormWithoutZeroDot
methods.brief: Returns the decimal digits of the fractional part without the leading 0.
methods.returns: a text of digits such as 75
notes: 0b101.11 gives 75; FractionalPartToDecimalWithoutZeroDot is the same call
warnings: it raises an error (indexes out of range) when the number has no fractional part: 0b1011 and 0b0 both raise

methods.name: ToDecimalForm
methods.brief: Returns the number converted to decimal, as text.
notes: by hand 0b101.11 is 5+0.75: it answers 5.75; 0b1111111111111111 answers 65535; ToDecimal is the same call

methods.name: ToOctalForm
methods.brief: Returns the number in octal, prefixed with 0o.
notes: by hand 11 is 1 times 8 plus 3: 0b1011 answers 0o13 and 0b11111111 answers 0o377; 0b101.11 answers 0o5.6; ToOctal is the same call

methods.name: ToHexForm
methods.brief: Returns the number in hexadecimal, prefixed with 0x.
notes: exact for whole numbers: 0b1011 answers 0xB and 0b11111111 answers 0xFF; ToHex is the same call
warnings: the fractional digits are lost: 0b101.11 (5.75) answers 0x5. where 0x5.C is right, and 0b10.1 answers 0x2. where 0x2.8 is right

methods.name: ToUnicodeHexForm
methods.brief: Returns the number as a Unicode code point notation, U+ followed by hexadecimal digits.
notes: 0b1011 gives U+B and 0b11111111 gives U+FF; ToUnicodeHex is the same call

methods.name: ToScientificNotationForm
methods.brief: Raises error R14 today instead of returning the number in scientific notation.
notes: ToScientificNotation is the same call and raises too
warnings: it forwards to a stzNumber method of that name, which does not exist, so every call raises R14

methods.name: IntegerPartToBaseNForm
methods.brief: Returns the integer part written in another base.

parameters.name: _n_
parameters.role: the base, from 2 to 36, another value raises an error

methods.returns: a text of digits in the base, lower-case letters from 10
notes: by hand 11 is 102 in base 3, 13 in base 8 and b in base 16: 0b1011 answers each; 255 in base 32 is 7v; IntegerPartToBaseN is the same call

methods.name: ToBytes
methods.brief: Returns the number as the 8 bytes of a 64-bit floating-point value, in a raw text.
methods.returns: a text of 8 bytes, not printable
notes: 0b1011 (11.0) gives the bytes 00 00 00 00 00 00 26 40 in hexadecimal, as stored on this machine

methods.name: FromDecimalForm
methods.brief: Replaces the number by the binary form of a decimal number, in place.

parameters.name: _n_
parameters.role: the decimal number, whole or with a fraction

notes: by hand 12500 is 11000011010100 and 5.75 is 101.11: it gives 0b11000011010100 and 0b101.11; a negative number gives 0b-101, which the constructor itself refuses (-0b101 is the spelling it accepts); FromDecimal is the same call

methods.name: FromDecimal
methods.brief: Replaces the number by the binary form of a decimal number, in place.

parameters.name: _n_
parameters.role: the decimal number, whole or with a fraction

notes: the same call as FromDecimalForm: 12500 gives 0b11000011010100

methods.name: FromHexForm
methods.brief: Replaces the number by the binary form of a hexadecimal number, in place.

parameters.name: cHex
parameters.role: the number as a text starting with 0x, such as 0x0E22

notes: by hand 0x0E22 is 3618, which gives 0b111000100010; 0xFF gives 0b11111111; FromHex is the same call
warnings: the text must start with 0x: x0E22, which the class description shows, raises an error, and so does a hex number with a dot such as 0x1.8

methods.name: FromHex
methods.brief: Replaces the number by the binary form of a hexadecimal number, in place.

parameters.name: cHex
parameters.role: the number as a text starting with 0x, such as 0xFF

notes: the same call as FromHexForm: 0xFF gives 0b11111111
warnings: the text must start with 0x, as for FromHexForm: x0E22 raises an error

methods.name: FromOctalForm
methods.brief: Replaces the number by the binary form of an octal number, in place.

parameters.name: cOctal
parameters.role: the number as a text starting with 0o, such as 0o2077

notes: by hand 0o2077 is 1087, which gives 0b10000111111; 0o17 gives 0b1111; FromOctal is the same call
warnings: the text must start with 0o: o2077, which the class description shows, raises an error

methods.name: FromOctal
methods.brief: Replaces the number by the binary form of an octal number, in place.

parameters.name: cOctal
parameters.role: the number as a text starting with 0o, such as 0o17

notes: the same call as FromOctalForm: 0o17 gives 0b1111
warnings: the text must start with 0o, as for FromOctalForm: o2077 raises an error

classes.name: stzBpmnDiagram
classes.brief: Lays a stzWorkflow out by the BPMN layout law and emits the conformance digest that two implementations are held to.
classes.description: It no longer draws: the shared renderer does that. What it keeps is the law, a column, a row and an arrow class for every step, and LayoutDigest, the text record compared cell by cell with the second implementation. The spine, the happy path, takes row 0; steps off it go below; each arrival at an ending gets its own marker. It reads the workflow's Steps(), so a workflow built only with AddStateXTT yields an empty digest. MarkEnding and MarkResume declare the endings before the layout is computed.
classes.receiver: oWf = new stzWorkflow("order") oWf.AddStep_("receive") oWf.AddStep_("check") oWf.AddStep_("done") oWf.ConnectSteps("receive", "check") oWf.ConnectSteps("check", "done") o1 = new stzBpmnDiagram(oWf)
classes.example:
o1.MarkEnding("done", :terminal, :success)
? o1.EntryStep()
#--> receive
? o1.IsEnding("done")
#--> 1
? o1.EndingId("done", 2)
#--> terminal_done__2
? o1.KindOf("check")
#--> invoke

parameters.name: poWorkflow
parameters.role: the stzWorkflow whose steps are laid out

notes: the diagram reads Steps() and Transitions(), not the states: a workflow built only with AddStateXTT has no steps and lays out nothing

parameters.name: pcName
parameters.role: the id of the step that ends the process

parameters.name: pcKind
parameters.role: terminal or suspension, case ignored

parameters.name: pcOutcome
parameters.role: the outcome label such as success or fail, case ignored

methods.returns: nothing; the ending is recorded. MarkEndingQ returns the diagram for chaining
notes: the kind and outcome are stored in lower case; marking a name again adds a second record and the first one is the one read back

extensions.name: MarkEndingQ
extensions.adds: does what the method does, then returns the object, so the call can be chained

notes: the return arrow only appears in the layout when some step arrives at that ending

methods.name: Layout
methods.brief: Places every step in a column and a row by the written BPMN layout law, once.
methods.returns: nothing; the placement is kept inside the diagram
notes: a second call does nothing until MarkEnding or MarkResume resets it; an empty entry step leaves the layout empty

methods.name: EntryStep
methods.brief: Returns the id of the step nothing points at, or the first declared step.
methods.returns: the step id as text; an empty text when the workflow has no steps
notes: a workflow built only with AddStateXTT answers an empty text, because it reads Steps()

parameters.name: pcStep
parameters.role: the id of the step the arrows leave

methods.returns: a list of [ label, target, exceptional ] triples; [ ] when none leave
notes: it reads the transitions when the workflow has any, else its plain edges with their label and a flag of 0

methods.name: IsEnding
methods.brief: TRUE if a step has been declared a process ending.

parameters.name: pcName
parameters.role: the step id to test

methods.name: EndingKind
methods.brief: Returns whether an ending is a terminal or a suspension.

parameters.name: pcName
parameters.role: the ending to ask about

methods.returns: the kind as text; terminal for a name that is not an ending
notes: the answer for an unknown name is terminal, not an empty text

methods.name: EndingOutcome
methods.brief: Returns the outcome label an ending was declared with.

parameters.name: pcName
parameters.role: the ending to ask about

methods.returns: the outcome as text, in lower case; an empty text for a name that is not an ending

methods.name: EndingId
methods.brief: Returns the element id of the nth marker drawn for an ending.

parameters.name: pcName
parameters.role: the ending name

parameters.name: n
parameters.role: the arrival number, from 1

notes: the id is terminal_ or suspended_ followed by the name, with __n added from the second arrival on

methods.brief: Returns the BPMN node kind of a step from its type property.

parameters.name: pcStep
parameters.role: the step id to classify

methods.returns: one of gateway, timer-wait, event-wait, compensate, human or invoke, as text
notes: a decision or gateway type gives gateway, usertask or an assignedTo gives human, and anything else is invoke

methods.name: LayoutDigest
methods.brief: Returns the conformance record of the layout: entry, nodes, endings and arrows, one sorted line each.
methods.returns: a multi-line text starting with LAWVER 1.0.0
notes: lines are sorted by character code; a workflow with no steps gives the header and an E line only

classes.name: stzBPMRuleBase
classes.brief: Holds the four best-practice rules of a business process and judges a workflow against them.
classes.description: The set, named BPM Best Practices in the bpm domain, carries bpm_no_orphans (a step with no connection in or out), bpm_single_start (exactly one start), bpm_decision_branches (a decision has at least two ways out) and bpm_assignment_required (a step is assigned to an actor), each of severity error. Check(oWorkflow) answers the findings in the house shape and IsSound answers whether none is an error.
classes.receiver: oWf = new stzWorkflow("order") oWf.AddStepXT("receive", "Receive order") oWf.AddStepXT("pack", "Pack") oWf.AddStepXT("lone", "Lone") oWf.ConnectSteps("receive", "pack") o1 = new stzBPMRuleBase()
classes.example:
? o1.Name()
#--> BPM Best Practices
? len(o1.Rules())
#--> 4
? o1.Check(oWf)[1][:rule]
#--> bpm_no_orphans
? o1.Check(oWf)[1][:where]
#--> lone
? o1.IsSound(oWf)
#--> 0

methods.name: init
methods.brief: Builds the set of four business-process best-practice rules, in the BPM Best Practices set.
notes: the rules are bpm_no_orphans, bpm_single_start, bpm_decision_branches and bpm_assignment_required, all of severity error; Check(oWorkflow) answers the findings

classes.name: stzBuilder
classes.brief: Describes what to build and for which system, then compiles it with Zig's drop-in C compiler, cross-compiling with one target flag.
classes.description: Declare sources, language (C, C++, Zig or Ring), executable or library, target, optimisation, definitions, includes and libraries, with the fluent Q forms. The target can be a stzSystemProfile, a friendly name such as :LinuxServer or :ESP32, or a raw Zig triple. Args and ToCommand show the command before anything runs, which is the rehearsal. Build then runs the compiler in a managed child process and keeps the output, the error output and the exit code. TargetWeb builds a freestanding wasm module for stzWebBundle. Build starts the Zig compiler and writes the output and the compiler cache: the documentation run declared and read builders only and did not run any Build.
classes.receiver: o1 = new stzBuilder("hello") o1.AddSource("hello.c") o1.SetTarget("x86_64-linux-gnu") o1.OptimizeFast()
classes.example:
? @@( o1.Args() )
#--> [ "cc", "hello.c", "-o", "hello", "-target", "x86_64-linux-gnu", "-O3" ]
? o1.Target()
#--> x86_64-linux-gnu
? o1.IsWeb()
#--> 0
? o1.Failed()
#--> 1

classes.name: stzBuildPlan
classes.brief: Holds the rehearsed placement plan of a solution: per part, each capability with its delivery vector, its reason and its size.
classes.description: It is what stzDelivery.Plan returns, and it changes nothing when read. VectorFor says how a capability reaches a part, EngineCapsFor and EngineKbFor say what the on-device engine of a part carries and weighs, and Explain tells the whole story in plain lines, with the external dependencies, the fakes that remain and the credentials production will need, by name. It is plain data, so it survives copying, and the emulator reads its Parts to render each part.
classes.receiver: d = new stzDelivery("shop"); d.AddApp("web", "browser"); d.NeedsIn("web", [ :Json, :Pattern ]); o1 = d.Plan()
classes.example:
? o1.VectorFor("web", "Json")
#--> native
? @@( o1.EngineCapsFor("web") )
#--> [ "pattern" ]
? o1.EngineKbFor("web")
#--> 5
