classes.name: stzBytes
classes.brief: Holds a binary buffer in the engine and reads, cuts, edits and encodes it as Base64, hexadecimal or percent text.
classes.description: Positions and sizes count bytes from 1, never characters, so a Hebrew letter is 2 bytes and an emoji 4. Reads (Left, Right, Mid, ToHex...) return text and leave the buffer alone; Append, Insert, Remove, Replace, Fill, Resize, Clear and the From... methods change it in place, and their Q forms return the object for chaining. Found today: string/stzBytes.ring is not loaded by stzlib.ring, and it defines a class named stzBytes that clashes with the alias class of stzListOfBytes.ring, so new stzBytes(...) builds the stzListOfBytes alias and none of the methods below exist on it (R14); a negative count, size or length, a Fill value above 255, and a number given to Append stop the Ring process; FromHex empties the buffer on a bad text. The examples were run on an identical copy of the class under another name.
classes.example:
? o1.ToHex()
#--> 48656c6c6f
? o1.Mid(2, 3)
#--> ell
o2 = new stzBytes("שלום")
? o2.Size()
#--> 8
? o2.ToPercent()
#--> %D7%A9%D7%9C%D7%95%D7%9D
o3 = new stzBytes("a😀b")
? o3.ToHex()
#--> 61f09f988062

methods.name: init
methods.brief: Builds an engine-backed byte buffer holding the bytes of a text; any other value gives an empty buffer.

parameters.name: pData
parameters.role: the text whose bytes fill the buffer

notes: the bytes are the text as stored, so a Hebrew letter is 2 bytes and an emoji 4
warnings: stzlib.ring does not load this file: new stzBytes(...) builds the alias of stzListOfBytes, which has no ByteAt (R14), and loading this file beside it raises C26 because both define a class named stzBytes

methods.name: Content
methods.brief: Returns the whole buffer as a text.

methods.name: Size
methods.brief: Returns how many bytes the buffer holds, not how many characters.
notes: NumberOfBytes and Count are the same call; the Hebrew word shalom is 8 bytes

methods.name: IsEmpty
methods.brief: TRUE if the buffer holds no byte at all.

methods.name: ByteAt
methods.brief: Returns the value of the byte at a position, from 0 to 255.

parameters.name: n
parameters.role: the 1-based position of the byte

methods.returns: a number; -1 for a position outside the buffer, including 0
notes: At is the same call; Hello at 2 gives 101

methods.name: Left
methods.brief: Returns the first bytes of the buffer as a text.

parameters.name: n
parameters.role: how many bytes to take from the start

methods.returns: a text; the whole buffer when n is larger than it
notes: the cut is by bytes, so 2 bytes of a Hebrew text are one letter and an odd count splits a letter
warnings: a negative n stops the Ring process with a Zig panic in stz_bytes.dll instead of returning an error

methods.name: Right
methods.brief: Returns the last bytes of the buffer as a text.

parameters.name: n
parameters.role: how many bytes to take from the end

methods.returns: a text; the whole buffer when n is larger than it
notes: Right(0) gives an empty text
warnings: a negative n stops the Ring process with a Zig panic in stz_bytes.dll instead of returning an error

methods.name: Mid
methods.brief: Returns a run of bytes starting at a position, as a text.

parameters.name: nStart
parameters.role: the 1-based position of the first byte

parameters.name: nLen
parameters.role: how many bytes to take

methods.returns: a text; empty when nStart is 0 or past the end, and shorter when the run reaches the end
notes: Section is the same call; Mid(2, 3) of Hello is ell
warnings: a negative nLen stops the Ring process with a Zig panic in stz_bytes.dll; a negative nStart returns an empty text

methods.name: Append
methods.brief: Adds a text at the end of the buffer, in place.

parameters.name: cData
parameters.role: the text whose bytes are added

methods.returns: nothing; the buffer changes. AppendQ returns the object for chaining

extensions.name: AppendQ
extensions.adds: does what the method does, then returns the object, so the call can be chained

methods.name: Insert
methods.brief: Puts a text into the buffer in front of the byte at a position, in place.

parameters.name: nPos
parameters.role: the 1-based position the text goes in front of

parameters.name: cData
parameters.role: the text to insert

methods.returns: nothing; the buffer changes. InsertQ returns the object for chaining
notes: Insert(1, "XY") on Hello gives XYHello
warnings: a position of 0, a negative one or one past the end plus one changes nothing and raises no error

extensions.name: InsertQ
extensions.adds: does what the method does, then returns the object, so the call can be chained

methods.name: Remove
methods.brief: Deletes a run of bytes starting at a position, in place.

parameters.name: nStart
parameters.role: the 1-based position of the first byte to delete

parameters.name: nLen
parameters.role: how many bytes to delete

methods.returns: nothing; the buffer changes. RemoveQ returns the object for chaining
notes: Remove(6, 99) on abcdefg keeps abcde
warnings: a position of 0 or below changes nothing and raises no error

extensions.name: RemoveQ
extensions.adds: does what the method does, then returns the object, so the call can be chained

methods.name: Replace
methods.brief: Overwrites a run of bytes with a text, in place; the text may be longer or shorter than the run.

parameters.name: nStart
parameters.role: the 1-based position of the first byte replaced

parameters.name: nLen
parameters.role: how many bytes are replaced, up to the end

parameters.name: cData
parameters.role: the text that takes their place

methods.returns: nothing; the buffer changes. ReplaceQ returns the object for chaining
notes: Replace(1, 2, "__") on Hello gives __llo
warnings: a negative nLen stops the Ring process with a Zig panic in stz_bytes.dll; a position past the end changes nothing

extensions.name: ReplaceQ
extensions.adds: does what the method does, then returns the object, so the call can be chained

methods.name: Fill
methods.brief: Replaces the whole buffer with a number of copies of one byte value, in place.

parameters.name: nByte
parameters.role: the byte value, 0 to 255

parameters.name: nCount
parameters.role: how many copies

methods.returns: nothing; the buffer changes. FillQ returns the object for chaining
notes: Fill(65, 3) gives AAA, and a count of 0 gives an empty buffer
warnings: the old content is dropped, not extended; a nByte above 255 or a negative nCount stops the Ring process with a Zig panic in stz_bytes.dll

extensions.name: FillQ
extensions.adds: does what the method does, then returns the object, so the call can be chained

methods.name: Resize
methods.brief: Cuts the buffer to a size, or pads it with zero bytes up to that size, in place.

parameters.name: nNewSize
parameters.role: the size in bytes the buffer will have

methods.returns: nothing; the buffer changes. ResizeQ returns the object for chaining
notes: Resize(5) on a 2 byte buffer adds three bytes of value 0
warnings: a negative size stops the Ring process with a Zig panic in stz_bytes.dll

extensions.name: ResizeQ
extensions.adds: does what the method does, then returns the object, so the call can be chained

methods.name: Clear
methods.brief: Empties the buffer, in place.
methods.returns: nothing; the buffer is empty. ClearQ returns the object for chaining

extensions.name: ClearQ
extensions.adds: does what the method does, then returns the object, so the call can be chained

methods.name: ToLower
methods.brief: Returns the buffer as a text with the ASCII capitals made small.
methods.returns: a text; the buffer is not changed
notes: Hello Wörld gives hello wörld
warnings: only the 26 ASCII letters change: A with a diaeresis and the Hebrew letters stay as they are

methods.name: ToUpper
methods.brief: Returns the buffer as a text with the ASCII small letters made capital.
methods.returns: a text; the buffer is not changed
notes: Hello Wörld gives HELLO WöRLD
warnings: only the 26 ASCII letters change: o with a diaeresis stays small

methods.name: ToBase64
methods.brief: Returns the buffer as Base64 text, with = padding.
methods.returns: a text; empty for an empty buffer
notes: Hello gives SGVsbG8=

methods.name: FromBase64
methods.brief: Replaces the buffer with the bytes a Base64 text stands for, in place.

parameters.name: cBase64
parameters.role: the Base64 text, padded with = to a multiple of 4

methods.returns: nothing; the buffer changes. FromBase64Q returns the object for chaining
notes: SGVsbG8= gives Hello
warnings: an invalid or unpadded text changes nothing and raises no error

extensions.name: FromBase64Q
extensions.adds: does what the method does, then returns the object, so the call can be chained

methods.name: ToHex
methods.brief: Returns the buffer as lower case hexadecimal text, two digits per byte and no prefix.
methods.returns: a text; empty for an empty buffer
notes: Hello gives 48656c6c6f; the Hebrew word shalom gives d7a9d79cd795d79d

methods.name: FromHex
methods.brief: Replaces the buffer with the bytes a hexadecimal text stands for, in place.

parameters.name: cHex
parameters.role: the digits, two per byte, upper or lower case, with no prefix and no space

methods.returns: nothing; the buffer changes. FromHexQ returns the object for chaining
notes: 48656c6c6f21 gives Hello!
warnings: a text with an odd count, a 0x prefix, a space or a non-digit EMPTIES the buffer and raises no error, whereas a bad Base64 text keeps it

extensions.name: FromHexQ
extensions.adds: does what the method does, then returns the object, so the call can be chained

methods.name: ToPercent
methods.brief: Returns the buffer as percent-encoded text, every byte outside A-Z a-z 0-9 and - _ . ~ written as %XX.
methods.returns: a text; the buffer is not changed
notes: a space becomes %20, o with a diaeresis %C3%B6 and the Hebrew letter shin %D7%A9

methods.name: FromPercent
methods.brief: Replaces the buffer with the bytes a percent-encoded text stands for, in place.

parameters.name: cPercent
parameters.role: the text, with %XX escapes

methods.returns: nothing; the buffer changes. FromPercentQ returns the object for chaining
notes: a%20b%C3%A9 gives a bé
warnings: a malformed escape such as %zz is kept as written and a + stays a +, not a space

extensions.name: FromPercentQ
extensions.adds: does what the method does, then returns the object, so the call can be chained

methods.name: Free
methods.brief: Releases the engine handle behind the buffer; the buffer then reads as empty.
notes: calling it twice is harmless; there is no finalizer, so a program that builds many buffers should call it

classes.name: stzCache
classes.brief: Remembers the result of a function call, keyed by the function's name and its arguments, in a text file.
classes.description: A cache entry is one line of the cache file: the function name, the argument values as text and the result, joined by a bar (build it with ComposeLine, store it with AddLine). A lookup answers from the first line whose name and arguments both match exactly, upper and lower case included, so the same call after storing is a hit and any other argument is a miss. The file is "cache/<name>.txt" under the current folder, created when the cache is built, and it outlives the object: a new cache of the same name reads what an earlier one stored. A cache starts NOT activated and an inactive cache answers no lookup: call Activate first. Only the :InFile storage is implemented; :InMemory and :InDatabase are accepted by the constructor but keep nothing, and AddLine and CacheOpen raise for them.
classes.example:
o1.Activate()
o1.AddLine( o1.ComposeLine([ "Add", "2,3", "5" ]) )
? o1.CacheGetCachedResult("Add", "2,3")
#--> 5
? o1.CacheFindEntry("Add", "2,4")
#--> 0

methods.name: Content
methods.brief: Returns the cached content, which nothing in the class ever sets.

methods.name: init
methods.brief: Builds a cache whose entries are kept in the file "cache/<name>.txt", creating the folder and the file when missing.

parameters.name: pcCacheName
parameters.role: the cache's name, used as the file's name; it may not be empty, hold a slash, a backslash or a colon, or contain two dots in a row

parameters.name: pcStorageType
parameters.role: where entries are kept: :InFile is the only one implemented

methods.returns: the new cache, which is NOT activated
notes: the file is relative to the current folder; an existing file is kept as it is
warnings: :InMemory and :InDatabase build an object that keeps nothing, and a name or type that is not text raises; any other type raises

methods.name: StorageType
methods.brief: Returns where the cache keeps its entries, as the constructor was given it.
methods.returns: the storage type as lower-case text, such as infile for :InFile

methods.name: Activate
methods.brief: Marks the cache as activated, so that lookups answer.

methods.name: Deactivate
methods.brief: Marks the cache as not activated, so that lookups answer nothing.

methods.name: IsActivated
methods.brief: TRUE if the cache was marked as activated and not deactivated since.
methods.returns: TRUE or FALSE; FALSE on a new cache

methods.name: CacheOpen
methods.brief: Makes sure the cache's file exists and returns its handle.
methods.returns: the handle of the cache file, which is its path
warnings: raises an error for :InMemory and :InDatabase, which have no file and no database layer behind them

methods.name: CacheFileHandler
methods.brief: Returns the handle of the cache's file, which is the path of that file.
methods.returns: the path "cache/<name>.txt", or the empty text for a storage that has no file
notes: the library's file functions work on paths, so the path is the handle

methods.name: CacheFileClose
methods.brief: Releases the cache's file, which here holds nothing open between calls.
notes: every call opens and closes the file by itself, so the file survives closing and can be read at once; CacheFileColse is the same call under the old misspelling

methods.name: CacheFindEntry
methods.brief: Returns the number of the first line stored for a function called with given arguments, or 0 when there is none.

parameters.name: pcFunc
parameters.role: the name of the function whose result is cached

parameters.name: pcParamValues
parameters.role: the argument values of the call, as text

methods.returns: the line number from 1, or 0 on a miss
warnings: answers 0 on a cache that is not activated, whatever the file holds; both parts must match exactly, upper and lower case included

methods.name: CacheGetCachedResult
methods.brief: Returns the result stored for a function called with given arguments.

parameters.name: pcFunc
parameters.role: the name of the function whose result is cached

parameters.name: pcParamValues
parameters.role: the argument values of the call, as text

methods.returns: the stored result, as text, or the empty text when the cache is not activated
warnings: raises an error when the cache is activated and holds no entry for that call; a stored number comes back as its text

methods.name: CacheGetResultInLineNumber
methods.brief: Returns the result held on one line of the cache file, whether or not the cache is activated.

parameters.name: pnLineNumber
parameters.role: the number of the line to read, from 1

methods.returns: the third part of that line, as text, with its escapes undone
warnings: raises an error when the line does not exist or has fewer than three parts

methods.name: CacheFileLines
methods.brief: Returns the lines of the cache file, as they are written, one text per line.
methods.returns: a list of texts; empty when the file is missing or empty
notes: a line keeps its bars and escapes; a carriage return before the end of a line is dropped, and so is the empty text after the last end of line

methods.name: CacheFileLineNumber
methods.brief: Returns one line of the cache file, as it is written.

parameters.name: _n_
parameters.role: the number of the line to read, from 1

warnings: raises an error when the file has no such line

methods.name: CacheFileNumberOfLines
methods.brief: Returns how many lines the cache file holds.
methods.returns: a number, 0 for a missing or empty file

methods.name: ComposeLine
methods.brief: Joins the parts of an entry into one line, with a bar between the parts.

parameters.name: paParts
parameters.role: the parts of the entry, as a list of texts or numbers; a part that is a list is first joined with commas

methods.returns: the line, in which each backslash, bar, line feed and carriage return of a part is escaped so that it reads back unchanged; a number is written as Ring writes it as text, so 3.5 becomes 3.50
warnings: raises an error when paParts is not a list or a part is an object

methods.name: AddLine
methods.brief: Appends one entry to the end of the cache file.

parameters.name: pcEntry
parameters.role: the entry to append, as one line of text, such as the answer of ComposeLine

warnings: raises an error for a line that holds a line feed or a carriage return, for a text that is not a string, and for :InMemory and :InDatabase, which keep nothing

classes.name: stzCacheStorage
classes.brief: Holds where a stzCache keeps its entries: the storage type, the folder, the file name and the file's handle.

For :InFile it builds the folder and an empty file when they are missing and leaves an existing file untouched; the handle of the file is its path, since the library's file functions work on paths. For :InMemory and :InDatabase it builds nothing and the handle is the empty text.

parameters.name: pcStorageType

classes.name: stzCalendar
classes.brief: Holds a period of days (a year, a quarter, a month or a date range) with working days, holidays, breaks and business hours, and counts available days and hours.
classes.description: Build it from a year (2026), a month ([ 2026, 3 ] or the text 2026-03), a quarter (2026-Q2 or [ 2026, "Q2" ]), a date range ([ [ "Start", "2026-03-10" ], [ "End", "2026-03-20" ] ]) or a single date. Set the working weekdays with SetWorkingDays (Monday to Friday is the default, set the first time IsWorkingDay runs), the hours with SetBusinessHours (09:00:00 to 17:00:00 by default), and add holidays with AddHoliday and daily breaks with AddBreak. Then ask for working days, available days and available hours of the whole period or of one day (AvailableHoursOnN), check that a task fits (CanFit, FirstAvailableSlot), attach a stzTimeLine to look for conflicts, compare two calendars, and export the facts with ToHash, ToJSON and ToCSV or draw them with Show, ShowHeatMap and ShowTable. Hours are whole hours, rounded down day by day. Month and year navigation moves the calendar itself, and GoTo moves a year, quarter or month calendar to the period of a date. Day navigation (NextDay, GoToNextDay, PreviousDay, GoToPreviousDay) works on a calendar built from one single date, because the class keeps no day cursor. Known gaps today, each carried as a warning on its method: the WorkingDaysBetween family raises once working days are set; FirstAvailableSlot ends its slot from midnight; ContainsBusinessHours is always FALSE; going to the next or previous year from a range calendar ends in year 1 or -1.
classes.example:
? o1.TotalDays()
#--> 31

sections.title: navigating the calendar back and forth

methods.name: init
methods.brief: Builds the calendar of a year, a month, a quarter, a date range or a single date, with Monday to Friday and 09:00 to 17:00 as defaults.

parameters.name: p
parameters.role: what the calendar covers: a year above 1900 such as 2026, a text such as 2026-03, 2026-Q2 or 2026-03-15, a list such as [ 2026, 3 ] or [ 2026, "Q3" ], or named pairs such as [ [ "Start", "2026-03-10" ], [ "End", "2026-03-20" ] ] or [ :Year = 2026, :Month = 3 ]

notes: named pairs accept Start or From, End or To, Year, Month, Quarter; the working days stay empty until SetWorkingDays or the first IsWorkingDay, which sets Monday to Friday; the locale key is never read
warnings: a year of 1900 or less, a number with decimals, [ ] and [ 2026, 13 ] raise; 2026-q4 with a lowercase q raises R41 (only Q3 as the second list item is case- free); [ 2026, "Spring" ] silently gives the whole year; a plain list of two dates [ "2026-03-10", "2026-03-20" ] and a list holding only a Start pair leave the calendar empty; any other text, such as gregorian, becomes a one-day range whose dates cannot be read

methods.name: Start
methods.brief: Returns the first day of the calendar as it was given or built, as a date text.
notes: StartQ answers the same day as a stzDate object

extensions.name: StartQ
extensions.adds: does what the method does, then returns the object, so the call can be chained

methods.name: End_
methods.brief: Returns the last day of the calendar as it was given or built, as a date text.
notes: the name carries a trailing underscore because End is a Ring keyword; EndQ answers a stzDate

methods.name: EndQ
methods.brief: Returns the last day of the calendar as a stzDate object, so date questions can be chained.
notes: raises when the end is not a readable date, as for a calendar built from gregorian

methods.name: Year
methods.brief: Returns the year of a year, quarter or month calendar, and 0 for a range or a single date.
notes: a calendar built from a start and an end has no year

methods.name: MonthNumber
methods.brief: Returns the month number of a month calendar, from 1 to 12, and 0 for a year, quarter or range.

methods.name: MonthName
methods.brief: Returns the English name of the month of a month calendar, and an empty text for any other view.
methods.returns: a month name such as March, or an empty text

methods.name: QuarterNumber
methods.brief: Returns the quarter of a quarter calendar, from 1 to 4, and 0 for any other view.
notes: only calendars built with a quarter have one

methods.name: TotalDays
methods.brief: Returns how many days the calendar spans, both end days counted.
methods.returns: a number of days; 31 for March 2026
notes: a range whose end comes before its start gives a negative count

methods.name: ContainsDays
methods.brief: TRUE if the calendar spans at least one day.
notes: FALSE only for a reversed range

methods.name: HasDays
methods.brief: TRUE if the calendar spans at least one day, as ContainsDays says.

methods.name: TotalWeeks
methods.brief: Returns the number of 7-day blocks needed to cover the calendar, the day count divided by 7 and rounded up.
methods.returns: a number of weeks; 5 for 31 days
notes: counts blocks of 7 days, not calendar weeks: 28 days is 4 and 29 days is 5

methods.name: ContainsWeeks
methods.brief: TRUE if the calendar spans at least one 7-day block.

methods.name: HasWeeks
methods.brief: TRUE if the calendar spans at least one 7-day block, as ContainsWeeks says.

methods.name: Content
methods.brief: Returns the calendar's main facts, period, totals, holidays, hours and breaks, as a list of [ key, value ] pairs.
methods.returns: a list of pairs; keys are lowercase text
notes: the keys are start, end, year, month, quarter, totaldays, workingdays, holidays, businesshours, breaks
warnings: the workingdays value is 0 until working days are configured, while ToHash reports the count of available days under the same idea

methods.name: SetWorkingDays
methods.brief: Sets which weekdays count as working days, from a list of day names or the word DEFAULT for Monday to Friday.

parameters.name: pDays
parameters.role: a list of English day names such as [ "Monday", "Wednesday" ], or the text DEFAULT

methods.returns: nothing; the object changes in place
notes: day names are case-free, so monday and :Monday work; an empty list leaves no working day until the next IsWorkingDay sets Monday to Friday; the cache of available hours and days is cleared
warnings: names that are not English day names are skipped, and numbers are ignored; a text other than DEFAULT, or a number, changes nothing

methods.name: ContainsWorkingDays
methods.brief: TRUE if working days have been set, either by SetWorkingDays or by a first IsWorkingDay call.
notes: FALSE on a new calendar: the default Monday to Friday is only set the first time IsWorkingDay is called

methods.name: HasWorkingDays
methods.brief: TRUE if working days have been set, as ContainsWorkingDays says.
notes: FALSE on a new calendar until IsWorkingDay or SetWorkingDays runs

methods.name: WorkingDaysN
methods.brief: Returns how many weekdays are set as working days, from 0 to 7.
notes: 0 on a new calendar until IsWorkingDay or SetWorkingDays runs; it counts weekdays of the week, not days of the calendar

methods.name: NumberOfWorkingDays
methods.brief: Returns how many weekdays are set as working days, from 0 to 7.
notes: counts weekdays of the week, not days of the calendar

methods.name: HowManyWorkingDays
methods.brief: Returns how many weekdays are set as working days, from 0 to 7.
notes: counts weekdays of the week, not days of the calendar

methods.name: CountWorkingDays
methods.brief: Returns how many weekdays are set as working days, from 0 to 7.
notes: counts weekdays of the week, not days of the calendar; WorkingDays lists the days of the calendar

methods.name: IsWorkingDay
methods.brief: TRUE if the weekday of the date is one of the working days, holidays not looked at.

parameters.name: pDate
parameters.role: the day, as a date text such as 2026-03-16 or 16/03/2026

notes: a holiday on a Monday is still a working day here; DateInfo tells both
warnings: sets Monday to Friday when no working day has been set yet; a list such as [ 2026, 3, 16 ] raises R21 and a text that is no date raises Cannot parse date string

methods.name: FirstWorkingDay
methods.brief: Returns the first working day of the calendar, found by stepping from the start; holidays are not skipped.
notes: the answer is the start itself in its own format when that day works, otherwise a dd/MM/yyyy text

methods.name: LastWorkingDay
methods.brief: Returns the last working day of the calendar, found by stepping back from the end; holidays are not skipped.
notes: the answer is the end itself in its own format when that day works, otherwise a dd/MM/yyyy text

methods.name: WorkingDaysBetween
methods.brief: Returns the working days between two dates, meant as a list of dates.

parameters.name: pStart
parameters.role: the first day of the range, as a date text such as 2026-03-01

parameters.name: pEnd
parameters.role: the last day of the range, as a date text such as 2026-03-31

methods.returns: a list; [ ] while no working day has been set
notes: on a calendar with no working day set it answers [ ] without looking
warnings: raises R5 (Can't access the list item, Object is not list) as soon as working days are set, because it reads each weekday number as a list; WorkingDays lists the working days of the calendar itself

methods.name: WorkingDaysBetweenN
methods.brief: Returns the number of working days between two dates, meant as a count.

parameters.name: pStart
parameters.role: the first day of the range, as a date text such as 2026-03-01

parameters.name: pEnd
parameters.role: the last day of the range, as a date text such as 2026-03-31

notes: 0 on a calendar with no working day set
warnings: raises R5 as WorkingDaysBetween does once working days are set

methods.name: ContainsWorkingDaysBetween
methods.brief: TRUE if any working day lies between two dates, meant as a test on the range.

parameters.name: pStart
parameters.role: the first day of the range, as a date text such as 2026-03-01

parameters.name: pEnd
parameters.role: the last day of the range, as a date text such as 2026-03-31

notes: FALSE on a calendar with no working day set
warnings: raises R5 as WorkingDaysBetween does once working days are set

methods.name: HasWorkingDaysBetween
methods.brief: Returns the number of working days between two dates, where a yes or no was meant.

parameters.name: pStart
parameters.role: the first day of the range, as a date text such as 2026-03-01

parameters.name: pEnd
parameters.role: the last day of the range, as a date text such as 2026-03-31

methods.returns: a number, not TRUE or FALSE
notes: answers the count, so a nonzero number stands for yes
warnings: raises R5 as WorkingDaysBetween does once working days are set

methods.name: AddHoliday
methods.brief: Records a holiday date with its name, or a whole list of [ date, name ] pairs.

parameters.name: pHolidayOrLabel
parameters.role: a date text such as 2026-03-10, or a list of [ date, name ] pairs

parameters.name: pName
parameters.role: the holiday name, or an empty text to get Holiday (ignored for a list)

methods.returns: nothing; the object changes in place
notes: a name that is a number is stored as text; the cache of available hours and days is cleared
warnings: both arguments are required: calling with only the date raises R19; the date is stored as written, and IsHoliday and HolidayName compare text, so the same day in dd/MM/yyyy is not found; a number, and a list with items that are not pairs, are skipped silently

methods.name: ContainsHolidays
methods.brief: TRUE if at least one holiday has been added.

methods.name: HasHolidays
methods.brief: Returns the number of holidays added, where a yes or no was meant.
methods.returns: a number, not TRUE or FALSE
notes: answers the count, so 0 stands for no and a nonzero number for yes

methods.name: IsHoliday
methods.brief: TRUE if the date was added as a holiday, compared as text with the stored date.

parameters.name: pDate
parameters.role: the day as a date text, in the same format as when added, such as 2026-03-10

notes: a holiday on a weekend is still a holiday
warnings: the same day written 10/03/2026 is not found when it was added as 2026-03-10

methods.name: HolidayName
methods.brief: Returns the name given to a holiday date, or an empty text when the date is no holiday.

parameters.name: pDate
parameters.role: the day as a date text, in the same format as when added, such as 2026-03-10

methods.returns: a name as text, or an empty text
notes: an unnamed holiday is named Holiday
warnings: text comparison: 10/03/2026 does not find a holiday added as 2026-03-10

methods.name: Holidays
methods.brief: Returns every holiday added, in order, as a list of [ date, name ] pairs.
methods.returns: a list of [ date, name ] pairs
notes: [ ] when none was added

methods.name: HolidaysN
methods.brief: Returns how many holidays have been added.
notes: counts all of them, inside the calendar range or not

methods.name: NumberOfHolidays
methods.brief: Returns how many holidays have been added.

methods.name: CountHolidays
methods.brief: Returns how many holidays have been added.

methods.name: HolidaysBetween
methods.brief: Returns the holidays that fall between two dates, both included, as [ date, name ] pairs.

parameters.name: pStart
parameters.role: the first day of the range, as a date text such as 2026-03-01

parameters.name: pEnd
parameters.role: the last day of the range, as a date text such as 2026-03-31

methods.returns: a list of [ date, name ] pairs
notes: dates are compared as dates, so dd/MM/yyyy and ISO bounds both work; an end before the start gives [ ]

methods.name: HolidaysBetweenN
methods.brief: Returns how many holidays fall between two dates, both included.

parameters.name: pStart
parameters.role: the first day of the range, as a date text such as 2026-03-01

parameters.name: pEnd
parameters.role: the last day of the range, as a date text such as 2026-03-31

methods.name: NumberOfHolidaysBetween
methods.brief: Returns how many holidays fall between two dates, both included.

parameters.name: pStart
parameters.role: the first day of the range, as a date text such as 2026-03-01

parameters.name: pEnd
parameters.role: the last day of the range, as a date text such as 2026-03-31

methods.name: CountHolidaysBetween
methods.brief: Returns how many holidays fall between two dates, both included.

parameters.name: pStart
parameters.role: the first day of the range, as a date text such as 2026-03-01

parameters.name: pEnd
parameters.role: the last day of the range, as a date text such as 2026-03-31

methods.name: ContainsHolidaysBetween
methods.brief: TRUE if at least one holiday falls between two dates, both included.

parameters.name: pStart
parameters.role: the first day of the range, as a date text such as 2026-03-01

parameters.name: pEnd
parameters.role: the last day of the range, as a date text such as 2026-03-31

methods.name: HasHolidaysBetween
methods.brief: TRUE if at least one holiday falls between two dates, as ContainsHolidaysBetween says.

parameters.name: pStart
parameters.role: the first day of the range, as a date text such as 2026-03-01

parameters.name: pEnd
parameters.role: the last day of the range, as a date text such as 2026-03-31

methods.name: SetBusinessHours
methods.brief: Sets the daily opening and closing times that available hours are counted between.

parameters.name: pStart
parameters.role: the opening time as HH:mm:ss text such as 08:30:00, or a [ label, time ] pair such as the From item of BusinessHours

parameters.name: pEnd
parameters.role: the closing time as HH:mm:ss text such as 17:45:00, or a [ label, time ] pair

methods.returns: nothing; the object changes in place
notes: the default is 09:00:00 to 17:00:00; HH:mm is read as well; the cache of available hours and days is cleared
warnings: the times are not checked: a text without colons breaks the hour counts later

methods.name: BusinessHours
methods.brief: Returns the opening and closing times as a list of two [ label, time ] pairs.
notes: the labels are the lowercase text from and to

methods.name: ContainsBusinessHours
methods.brief: Returns FALSE for every calendar, where a test that business hours are set was meant.
notes: business hours always exist, defaulting to 09:00:00 to 17:00:00
warnings: answers FALSE even after SetBusinessHours: the test reads start is not empty and end is empty

methods.name: HasBusinessHours
methods.brief: Returns FALSE for every calendar, where a test that business hours are set was meant.
notes: business hours always exist
warnings: answers FALSE even after SetBusinessHours, as ContainsBusinessHours does

methods.name: AddBreak
methods.brief: Records a daily break with its start, end and label, or a whole list of breaks.

parameters.name: pBreakStart
parameters.role: the break start as HH:mm:ss text such as 12:00:00, or a list of [ start, end, label ] breaks

parameters.name: pBreakEnd
parameters.role: the break end as HH:mm:ss text such as 13:00:00 (ignored for a list)

parameters.name: pLabel
parameters.role: the break label, or an empty text to get Break (ignored for a list)

methods.returns: nothing; the object changes in place
notes: the break is daily and subtracted from every working day; the cache is cleared
warnings: all three arguments are required: calling with fewer raises R19; a list item shorter than 2 is skipped silently

methods.name: Breaks
methods.brief: Returns every break added, in order, as a list of [ start, end, label ] items.
methods.returns: a list of [ start, end, label ] items
notes: [ ] when none was added

methods.name: BreaksN
methods.brief: Returns how many breaks have been added.

methods.name: NumberOfBreaks
methods.brief: Returns how many breaks have been added.

methods.name: CountBreaks
methods.brief: Returns how many breaks have been added.

methods.name: ContainsBreaks
methods.brief: TRUE if at least one break has been added.

methods.name: HasBreaks
methods.brief: Returns the number of breaks added, where a yes or no was meant.
methods.returns: a number, not TRUE or FALSE
notes: answers the count, so 0 stands for no and a nonzero number for yes

methods.name: BreaksBetween
methods.brief: Returns the breaks that fall between two dates, meant as a list.

parameters.name: pStart
parameters.role: the first day of the range, as a date text such as 2026-03-01

parameters.name: pEnd
parameters.role: the last day of the range, as a date text such as 2026-03-31

methods.returns: a list; [ ] while no break exists
notes: breaks are daily times, not dated, so a range makes no sense for them; Breaks lists them
warnings: raises R41 (Invalid numeric string) as soon as a break exists, because it reads the break time as a date; the source also holds typos (@a Breaks) that would stop it after that

methods.name: BreaksBetweenN
methods.brief: Returns how many breaks fall between two dates, meant as a count.

parameters.name: pStart
parameters.role: the first day of the range, as a date text such as 2026-03-01

parameters.name: pEnd
parameters.role: the last day of the range, as a date text such as 2026-03-31

notes: 0 when no break exists
warnings: raises R41 as BreaksBetween does once a break exists

methods.name: HowManyBreaksBetween
methods.brief: Returns how many breaks fall between two dates, meant as a count.

parameters.name: pStart
parameters.role: the first day of the range, as a date text such as 2026-03-01

parameters.name: pEnd
parameters.role: the last day of the range, as a date text such as 2026-03-31

notes: 0 when no break exists
warnings: raises R41 as BreaksBetween does once a break exists

methods.name: CountBreaksBetween
methods.brief: Returns how many breaks fall between two dates, meant as a count.

parameters.name: pStart
parameters.role: the first day of the range, as a date text such as 2026-03-01

parameters.name: pEnd
parameters.role: the last day of the range, as a date text such as 2026-03-31

notes: 0 when no break exists
warnings: raises R41 as BreaksBetween does once a break exists

methods.name: ContainsBreaksBetween
methods.brief: TRUE if any break falls between two dates, meant as a test on the range.

parameters.name: pStart
parameters.role: the first day of the range, as a date text such as 2026-03-01

parameters.name: pEnd
parameters.role: the last day of the range, as a date text such as 2026-03-31

notes: the call that was meant is BreaksBetween
warnings: raises R14 (Calling Method without definition: reaksbetween) every time, with or without breaks, because the source calls This. reaksBetween

methods.name: HasBreaksBetween
methods.brief: Returns the number of breaks between two dates, where a yes or no was meant.

parameters.name: pStart
parameters.role: the first day of the range, as a date text such as 2026-03-01

parameters.name: pEnd
parameters.role: the last day of the range, as a date text such as 2026-03-31

methods.returns: a number, not TRUE or FALSE
notes: answers 0 when no break exists
warnings: raises R41 as BreaksBetween does once a break exists

methods.name: AvailableHours
methods.brief: Returns every free one-hour slot of the calendar as date and time texts, oldest first.
methods.returns: a list of texts such as 2026-03-02 09:00:00, one per free whole hour
notes: a holiday and a day that is not a working weekday give no slot; a slot that overlaps a break is left out; slots start at the opening time, so hours from 09:30 to 17:30 give slots at 09:30, 10:30 and so on up to 16:30; the date part is always yyyy-MM-dd
warnings: when breaks sit in different hours the list can be shorter than AvailableHoursN, which takes the break minutes away before rounding down (two ten-minute breaks in different hours give 6 slots against 7 hours)

methods.name: AvailableHoursN
methods.brief: Returns the total number of working hours of the calendar, summing the whole hours of every available day.
methods.returns: a number of hours; 176 for March 2026 with the default hours
notes: each day counts the whole hours between opening and closing minus the breaks, rounded down (09:00 to 17:00 with a one hour break is 7); the answer is cached and cleared by AddHoliday, AddBreak, SetBusinessHours, SetWorkingDays and InvalidateCache
warnings: a holiday is subtracted only when it is the first day of the calendar: the days after it come as dd/MM/yyyy text and no longer match a holiday stored as 2026-03-10; AvailableHoursBetweenN stores its sub-range answer in the same cache, so a call to it makes this method return that sub-range total until the cache is cleared

methods.name: ContainsAvailableHours
methods.brief: TRUE if the calendar has at least one available working hour.
notes: built on AvailableHoursN, so it shares its caveats

methods.name: HasAvailableHours
methods.brief: TRUE if the calendar has at least one available working hour, as ContainsAvailableHours says.

methods.name: AvailableHoursBetween
methods.brief: Returns the free one-hour slots from one date to another, both included, as date and time texts.

parameters.name: pStart
parameters.role: the first day of the range, as a date text such as 2026-03-01 or 01/03/2026

parameters.name: pEnd
parameters.role: the last day of the range, written in the same way

methods.returns: a list of texts such as 2026-03-02 09:00:00, oldest first; [ ] when the range holds none
notes: the range may reach before or after the calendar; holidays and breaks follow the calendar; a range whose end comes before its start gives [ ]

methods.name: AvailableHoursBetweenN
methods.brief: Returns the working hours between two dates, both included, summing the whole hours of each available day.

parameters.name: pStart
parameters.role: the first day of the range, as a date text such as 2026-03-01

parameters.name: pEnd
parameters.role: the last day of the range, as a date text such as 2026-03-31

methods.returns: a number of hours; 35 for 2026-03-09 to 2026-03-13 with one hour of break a day
warnings: a holiday is subtracted only on the first day of the range (the next days come as dd/MM/yyyy text); the answer is stored in the cache of the WHOLE calendar, so AvailableHoursN, AvailableMinutesN and the Contains and Has tests answer this sub-range after it until the cache is cleared

methods.name: ContainsAvailableHoursBetween
methods.brief: TRUE if the range between two dates holds at least one available working hour.

parameters.name: pStart
parameters.role: the first day of the range, as a date text such as 2026-03-01

parameters.name: pEnd
parameters.role: the last day of the range, as a date text such as 2026-03-31

warnings: shares the caveats of AvailableHoursBetweenN, including its cache effect on AvailableHoursN

methods.name: HasAvailableHoursBetween
methods.brief: TRUE if at least one whole working hour is free between two dates, both included.

parameters.name: pStart
parameters.role: the first day of the range, as a date text such as 2026-03-01

parameters.name: pEnd
parameters.role: the last day of the range, as a date text such as 2026-03-31

notes: the same answer as ContainsAvailableHoursBetween; holidays, days off and breaks are taken out first

methods.name: AvailableHoursOn
methods.brief: Returns the free one-hour slots of one day as date and time texts; [ ] on a holiday or a day off.

parameters.name: pDate
parameters.role: the day, as a date text such as 2026-03-10 or 10/03/2026

methods.returns: a list of texts such as 2026-03-11 09:00:00, one per free whole hour, oldest first
notes: a slot that overlaps a break is left out; the date part is always yyyy-MM-dd
warnings: a text that is no date raises; with breaks in different hours the list can be shorter than AvailableHoursOnN, as AvailableHours explains

methods.name: AvailableHoursOnN
methods.brief: Returns the whole working hours of one day: 0 on a holiday or a day off, else opening to closing minus the breaks.

parameters.name: pDate
parameters.role: the day, as a date text such as 2026-03-10

methods.returns: a number of hours; 8 on a Monday with the default hours, 7 with a one hour break
notes: rounded down to whole hours: 09:00 to 17:45 is 8
warnings: the date must be written as the holiday was added (2026-03-10): 10/03/2026 is not found as a holiday and answers the full hours; a text that is no date raises

methods.name: ContainsAvailableHoursOn
methods.brief: TRUE if the day has at least one whole working hour free, holidays, days off and breaks taken out.

parameters.name: pDate
parameters.role: the day, as a date text such as 2026-03-10 or 10/03/2026

notes: built on AvailableHoursOnN, so a day whose free time is under one hour answers FALSE; HasAvailableHoursOn gives the same answer

methods.name: HasAvailableHoursOn
methods.brief: TRUE if the day has at least one whole working hour free, as ContainsAvailableHoursOn says.

parameters.name: pDate
parameters.role: the day, as a date text such as 2026-03-10 or 10/03/2026

notes: a holiday, a day off and a day whose free time is under one hour answer FALSE

methods.name: AvailableDaysN
methods.brief: Returns how many days of the calendar are working days and not holidays.
methods.returns: a number of days; 22 for March 2026
notes: default Monday to Friday unless SetWorkingDays changed it; the answer is cached
warnings: a holiday is subtracted only when it is the first day of the calendar: the other days come as dd/MM/yyyy text and no longer match a holiday stored as 2026-03-10

methods.name: AvailableDays
methods.brief: Returns the working days of the calendar that are not holidays, as a list of date texts.
notes: the first date keeps the calendar's own format (2026-03-02) and every later date is dd/MM/yyyy; the list is ordered
warnings: a holiday is removed only when it is the first day of the calendar, for the reason given in AvailableDaysN

methods.name: ContainsAvailableDays
methods.brief: TRUE if the calendar has at least one available day.
notes: built on AvailableDaysN, so it shares its caveat on holidays

methods.name: HasAvailableDays
methods.brief: TRUE if the calendar has at least one available day, as ContainsAvailableDays says.

methods.name: AvailableDaysBetween
methods.brief: Returns the working days that are not holidays from one date to another, both included.

parameters.name: pStart
parameters.role: the first day of the range, as a date text such as 2026-03-01 or 01/03/2026

parameters.name: pEnd
parameters.role: the last day of the range, written in the same way

methods.returns: a list of yyyy-MM-dd texts, oldest first; [ ] when the range holds none
notes: the range may reach before or after the calendar and cross a month, a year or a leap day; a range whose end comes before its start gives [ ]

methods.name: AvailableDaysBetweenN
methods.brief: Returns the number of working days that are not holidays between two dates, both included.

parameters.name: pStart
parameters.role: the first day of the range, as a date text such as 2026-03-01

parameters.name: pEnd
parameters.role: the last day of the range, as a date text such as 2026-03-31

methods.returns: a number of days, 0 when the range holds none

methods.name: ContainsAvailableDaysBetween
methods.brief: TRUE if at least one working day that is not a holiday lies between two dates, both included.

parameters.name: pStart
parameters.role: the first day of the range, as a date text such as 2026-03-01

parameters.name: pEnd
parameters.role: the last day of the range, as a date text such as 2026-03-31

notes: HasAvailableDaysBetween gives the same answer

methods.name: HasAvailableDaysBetween
methods.brief: TRUE if at least one working day that is not a holiday lies between two dates, as ContainsAvailableDaysBetween says.

parameters.name: pStart
parameters.role: the first day of the range, as a date text such as 2026-03-01

parameters.name: pEnd
parameters.role: the last day of the range, as a date text such as 2026-03-31

methods.name: AvailableWeeks
methods.brief: Returns the weeks of the calendar that hold an available day, each as its first and last available day.
methods.returns: a list of [ first, last ] pairs of yyyy-MM-dd texts, oldest first
notes: weeks run from Monday to Sunday; the pair holds the first and the last available day of that week inside the calendar, so a week cut by the calendar edge or by holidays is shorter (March 2026 ends with [ 2026-03-30, 2026-03-31 ]); a week with no available day is left out
warnings: the list can have a different length than AvailableWeeksN, which divides the available days by 5 and rounds up

methods.name: AvailableWeeksN
methods.brief: Returns the number of 5-day working weeks the available days make up, rounded up.
methods.returns: a number of weeks; 5 for 22 days
notes: the available day count divided by 5, whatever the working days set are
warnings: shares the caveat of AvailableDaysN on holidays

methods.name: ContainsAvailableWeeks
methods.brief: TRUE if the available days make up at least one working week.

methods.name: HasAvailableWeeks
methods.brief: TRUE if the available days make up at least one working week, as ContainsAvailableWeeks says.

methods.name: AvailableMinutesN
methods.brief: Returns the total working minutes of the calendar, its available hours times 60.
methods.returns: a number of minutes; 10560 for 176 hours
notes: AvailableMinutes gives the same number
warnings: shares the caveats of AvailableHoursN, cache included

methods.name: AvailableMinutes
methods.brief: Returns the total working minutes of the calendar as a number, its available hours times 60.
methods.returns: a number of minutes, not a list
notes: the one available method that answers a number, on purpose
warnings: shares the caveats of AvailableHoursN, cache included

methods.name: CanFit
methods.brief: TRUE if the available hours of the day are at least as long as the duration.

parameters.name: pDate
parameters.role: the day, as a date text such as 2026-03-10

parameters.name: pDuration
parameters.role: the length in hours, as a number such as 4 or a text such as 3.5

notes: holidays follow the date-format caveat of AvailableHoursOnN
warnings: compares with the whole available hours of the day, rounded down; a duration of 0 fits any day, even a day off

methods.name: FirstAvailableSlot
methods.brief: Returns the start and end times of the first day that has room for a duration, from the start of business hours.

parameters.name: pDuration
parameters.role: the length in hours, as a number such as 4

methods.returns: a list [ start, end ] of date and time texts, or [ ] when no day fits
notes: the start is the opening time; the date part keeps the calendar's format for the first day and is dd/MM/yyyy for later days
warnings: the end is wrong: it counts the duration from midnight, so a 4-hour slot from 09:00:00 ends at 04:00:00; holidays after the first day are not skipped; a duration above a full day gives [ ]

methods.name: ConsecutiveWorkingDaysAvailable
methods.brief: Returns the run of working days that starts at the given date and stops at the first day off or holiday.

parameters.name: pDate
parameters.role: the first day of the run, as a date text such as 2026-03-04, or a pair [ :StartingFrom, date ]

notes: the given date comes back as written and the others as dd/MM/yyyy; a day off at the start gives [ ]
warnings: a holiday is seen only on the first day of the run (the later days come as dd/MM/yyyy text); the walk is not stopped at the end of the calendar but one day past it (from 2026-03-31 it lists 01/04/2026 too)

methods.name: ConsecutiveWorkingDaysAvailableN
methods.brief: Returns how many working days run in a row from the given date.

parameters.name: pDate
parameters.role: the first day of the run, as a date text such as 2026-03-04, or a pair [ :StartingFrom, date ]

notes: 0 when the first day is a day off
warnings: shares the caveats of ConsecutiveWorkingDaysAvailable

methods.name: RangeInfo
methods.brief: Returns a summary of the days between two dates: totals, working days, weekend days, holidays and available hours.

parameters.name: pStart
parameters.role: the first day of the range, as a date text such as 2026-03-01

parameters.name: pEnd
parameters.role: the last day of the range, as a date text such as 2026-03-31

methods.returns: a list of [ key, value ] pairs with the keys startdate, enddate, totaldays, workingdays, weekenddays, holidays, availablehours, overlappingevents
notes: weekenddays counts days off that are not holidays, whatever the working days set are
warnings: a holiday is counted only on the first day of the range, as in AvailableDaysN; overlappingevents is always [ ]; an end before the start gives negative totals and zero counts

methods.name: NextDay
methods.section: navigating the calendar back and forth
methods.brief: Returns the day after the one day a single-date calendar covers, as yyyy-MM-dd text, without moving the calendar.

warnings: a year, quarter, month or range calendar has no current day, because the class keeps no day cursor, so the call raises; what the current day of a longer period is has not been decided

methods.name: GoToNextDay

warnings: a year, quarter, month or range calendar has no current day to move, so the call raises and the calendar stays as it was; GotoNextMonth moves a month calendar

classes.name: stzCan
classes.brief: Answers whether a value can be a given kind, by checking it against every constraint declared for the kind.
classes.description: CanQ(42).BeA("score") is 1 when 42 satisfies all the constraints of score. The verdict is certain, since a check is deterministic, it joins the session's ask-record, and Why() says which constraint failed. A kind with no declared constraint answers 0 and says nothing is known about it.
classes.example:
? o1.BeA("scoreB")
#--> 1
? CanQ(-5).BeA("scoreB")
#--> 0
? Why()
#--> no: -5 is not positive (constraint 2 of 'scoreb')

methods.name: init
methods.brief: Starts the question whether a value can be a given kind, keeping the value to check.

parameters.name: pValue
parameters.role: the value to check against the constraints of a kind

methods.name: BeA
methods.brief: TRUE if the value satisfies every constraint declared for the kind; the reason is left for Why and the verdict joins the ask-record.

parameters.name: pcKind
parameters.role: the kind, such as score, matched without regard to case

methods.returns: 1 or 0, numbers; 0 when the kind has no constraint
notes: BeAn and Be are the same call; the certainty is always 1, the check being deterministic
warnings: an unknown descriptor among the constraints raises Unknown constraint descriptor

classes.name: stzCancelToken
classes.brief: Holds a cancellation flag in the engine: one side raises it, the other side polls it and stops early.
classes.description: A token starts lowered. Cancel() (or Signal()) raises it and IsCancelled() reads it; the flag lives in the engine, so it can be passed to long-running engine work without a callback into Ring. Destroy() frees it.
classes.example:
? o1.IsCancelled()
#--> 0
o1.Cancel()
? o1.IsCancelled()
#--> 1

methods.name: init
methods.brief: Builds a cancel token, an engine flag that one party raises and another polls to stop a long job early.

methods.name: Handle
methods.brief: Returns the engine pointer of the token, to hand to an engine call that accepts a cancel handle.

methods.name: Cancel
methods.brief: Raises the cancel flag, so every holder of the token sees IsCancelled() answer TRUE from now on.
methods.returns: the token itself, so calls chain
notes: raising the flag twice changes nothing

methods.name: Signal
methods.brief: Raises the cancel flag, exactly as the call that has the other name does.
methods.returns: the token itself, so calls chain

methods.name: IsCancelled
methods.brief: TRUE if the flag has been raised.

methods.name: Destroy
methods.brief: Frees the engine flag of the token and marks it unusable.
methods.returns: the token itself, so calls chain
notes: a later call that needs the handle builds a new flag

classes.name: stzCanvas
classes.brief: Holds a 2D picture described once, as shapes and text, and gives it back as vector SVG or as pixels drawn on the graphics device.
classes.description: The Add methods remember the shape instead of posting it, so Fill, Stroke, Color and SetFont can still reach the last shape added; the shape is posted when the next one arrives or an output is asked for. Fill and Stroke called before any shape set the default for every shape added after. The plain form of a method acts and answers nothing, and its Q twin answers the canvas so calls can be chained; only the pick, identity and region setters answer the canvas without the Q. Text needs a font from SetFont. ToSVG needs no device and is the floor of the tier ladder; ToPNG and ToPixels go through the GPU and answer an empty string when none is available. Coordinates are pixels from the top-left corner, sizes run from 1 to 16384, and the SVG output draws circles, rounded rectangles, ellipses and strokes as polygons and polylines.
classes.example:
? o1.ShapeCount()
#--> 1

classes.name: stzCapabilityCatalog
classes.brief: Holds what the delivery planner knows about each Softanza capability, as data, and decides how a capability reaches a target.
classes.description: Each record says whether a capability is unique to Softanza, whether it is compute or ergonomics, how heavy it is, how well a browser, a server and a microcontroller already do it, and how many KB its engine adds. VectorFor reads those records and answers native, engine, construct or server with the reason in words: a server hosts the engine, a heavy capability goes to the backend, a strong non-unique one defers to the platform, an ergonomic one becomes a construct on the web, the rest folds into the on-device engine. A name the catalog does not know is assumed to be Softanza- differential and platform-weak.
classes.example:
? o1.Has("PivotTable")
#--> 1
? o1.SizeOf("neural")
#--> 900
? @@( o1.VectorFor("Json", "browser") )
#--> [ "native", "Json: the target-platform is strong at it -> use its own" ]

classes.name: stzCapabilityResponder
classes.brief: Performs the :RevokeCapability action of a response plan by cutting an actor's paths to the effectful capability in a security graph.
classes.description: The graph is what audits and incidents ask, the live actor is what the runtime gates ask, so the responder cuts both: the graph edges, and the effectful kind of each registered live actor of the same name. Register live actors one at a time with AddLiveActor, because an object placed in a list literal is copied and revoking a copy changes nothing. It answers no other verb: each of those raises an error that names the responder to wire. Other actors that use the same tool keep their capability.
classes.example:
g.AddActor("billing-agent", "trusted")
g.AddTool("deploy-tool")
g.AddCapability("effectful")
g.Uses("billing-agent", "deploy-tool")
g.Grants("deploy-tool", "effectful")
? g.ReachesEffectful("billing-agent")
#--> 1
o1.RevokeCapability("billing-agent")
? g.ReachesEffectful("billing-agent")
#--> 0
? @@( o1.LastCut() )
#--> [ [ "billing-agent", "uses", "deploy-tool" ] ]

classes.name: stzCardPaymentsAdapter
classes.brief: Plays a card gateway in memory with the state machine a real one enforces, so double captures and over-refunds fail in a test.
classes.description: Authorize gives an authorized or declined answer, Capture takes an authorized amount once, and Refund gives back only what was captured, never more. The rules are yours and deterministic: a ceiling under which everything is approved, a ceiling over which everything is declined, tokens that always decline, and one outage on demand. Every movement is recorded, so a test asserts on what happened to the money and not on a return value. Money is a positive whole number of minor units, 4200 for 42.00, never a float. This is the double only: the live side, a client of a real card processor, is not shipped, and the registry refuses a double in production. It is not the UEMOA payments port, whose verbs are pay, request to pay, return, cancellation and bulk: see stzPaymentsPort.
classes.example:
aA = o1.Authorize(4200, "tok_visa")
? aA[:status]
#--> authorized
o1.Capture(aA[:id])
o1.RefundAmount(aA[:id], 1000)
? o1.NetCaptured()
#--> 3200

methods.brief: Makes the next Authorize, Capture or Refund fail as if the gateway were unreachable; only that one call fails.
notes: an outage is not a decline: the answer carries ok = 0, status refused and no id, and nothing was recorded
warnings: the failure is taken by the next of those calls even if that call would have been refused anyway, and it is not recorded in the ledger

extensions.name: FailNextQ
extensions.adds: does what the method does, then returns the object, so the call can be chained

methods.name: Authorize
methods.brief: Asks the gateway to approve an amount against a payment token and answers approved or declined, recording the movement.

parameters.name: pnAmount
parameters.role: the amount in minor units, a positive whole number

parameters.name: pcToken
parameters.role: the payment token the customer presented

methods.returns: a list [ ok, id, status, amount, why ]: status is authorized or declined, id is auth_1, auth_2 and so on, why says the cause of a decline
notes: nothing is captured yet: Capture takes the money
warnings: an amount that is zero, negative, fractional or not a number is refused with ok = 0, status refused and an empty id; a decline is an answer that takes an id and counts in NumberOfDeclines, and the rules apply in the order token, decline ceiling, approval ceiling

methods.name: Capture
methods.brief: Takes the whole amount that was approved on an authorization; the money can be taken only once.

parameters.name: pcId
parameters.role: the id returned by Authorize

methods.returns: a list [ ok, id, status, amount, why ]: status is captured, or refused with the cause in why
warnings: a declined, unknown or already captured authorization is refused and the ledger does not move

methods.name: CaptureAmount
methods.brief: Takes part of an authorization, or all of it when the amount is 0; a capture may not exceed what was authorized and happens once.

parameters.name: pcId
parameters.role: the id returned by Authorize

parameters.name: pnAmount
parameters.role: the amount to take in minor units, 0 for the whole authorization

methods.returns: a list [ ok, id, status, amount, why ]: status is captured, or refused with the cause in why
warnings: capturing less than the authorized amount closes the authorization: the rest cannot be captured later

methods.name: Refund
methods.brief: Gives back the rest of what was captured on an authorization.

parameters.name: pcId
parameters.role: the id returned by Authorize

methods.returns: a list [ ok, id, status, amount, why ]: status is refunded, or refused with the cause in why
notes: StatusOf still reads captured after a refund; the refunded sum is read with RefundedOf
warnings: an authorization with nothing left to refund is refused, but the reason says an amount must be a positive whole number, which is true and is not the cause

methods.name: RefundAmount
methods.brief: Gives back part of the captured money, or all that is left when the amount is 0; the total refunded never exceeds what was captured.

parameters.name: pcId
parameters.role: the id returned by Authorize

parameters.name: pnAmount
parameters.role: the amount to give back in minor units, 0 for what is left

methods.returns: a list [ ok, id, status, amount, why ]: status is refunded, or refused with the cause in why
warnings: an authorization that was never captured, or an amount over what is left, is refused and the ledger does not move

methods.name: StatusOf
methods.brief: Returns the state of an authorization: authorized, declined or captured.

parameters.name: pcId
parameters.role: the id returned by Authorize

methods.returns: a text; empty for an unknown id
notes: a refund does not change it: the state stays captured

methods.name: AmountOf
methods.brief: Returns the amount that was asked for in the authorization.

parameters.name: pcId
parameters.role: the id returned by Authorize

methods.returns: a number in minor units; 0 for an unknown id

methods.name: CapturedOf
methods.brief: Returns how much of an authorization was captured.

parameters.name: pcId
parameters.role: the id returned by Authorize

methods.returns: a number in minor units; 0 when nothing was captured or the id is unknown

methods.name: RefundedOf
methods.brief: Returns how much of an authorization has been given back.

parameters.name: pcId
parameters.role: the id returned by Authorize

methods.returns: a number in minor units; 0 when nothing was refunded or the id is unknown

methods.name: NumberOfAuthorizations
methods.brief: Returns how many authorizations the gateway holds, declined ones included.
notes: a call refused before an id was given, such as a bad amount or an outage, is not counted

methods.name: TotalAuthorized
methods.brief: Returns the sum asked for by the authorizations that were approved, whether or not they were captured since.
notes: declined authorizations are left out, and a refund does not lower it

methods.name: TotalCaptured
methods.brief: Returns the sum captured across every authorization.
notes: a refund does not lower it: NetCaptured does

methods.name: TotalRefunded
methods.brief: Returns the sum given back across every authorization.

methods.name: NetCaptured
methods.brief: Returns what the merchant keeps: the captured sum less the refunded sum.

methods.name: NumberOfDeclines
methods.brief: Returns how many authorizations were declined, by a token or by a ceiling.

methods.name: Movements
methods.brief: Returns the ledger of what happened to the money, oldest first, one record per authorize, decline, capture or refund.
methods.returns: a list of records [ seq, kind, id, amount ] where kind is authorize, decline, capture or refund
notes: a refused call leaves no record: a test asserts on what the money did, not on the return value

methods.name: NumberOfMovements
methods.brief: Returns how many records the ledger holds.

methods.name: Show
methods.brief: Prints one summary line of the gateway: how many authorizations, and the captured, refunded and net sums.
notes: the line begins with stzPaymentsSandbox, whatever the class used

classes.name: stzCCode
classes.brief: Holds a piece of conditional code, the Ring expression of a W or WXT condition, and rewrites it to its basic form.
classes.description: The code is written with the keywords @i and This[@i], or with friendlier words such as @CurrentItem, @NextItem and @PreviousItem. Transpiled turns the friendly words into the basic forms; ExecutableSection says over which positions of a list the code can run without reading outside it.
classes.example:
? o1.Transpiled()
#--> This[@i] = This[@i + 1]
? o1.Content()
#--> @CurrentItem = @NextItem

notes: start moves up with the deepest look-behind (This[@i-2] gives 3) and end moves down with the deepest look-ahead (This[@i+2] gives -2, counted from the last position)
