classes.name: stzChainOfTruth
classes.brief: Wraps one value in a chain of near-natural questions, such as _("ring").Is(:String)._, whose closing underscore answers 1 or 0.
classes.description: Each step (Is, Which, Where) puts one question to the value and tags the chain true or false, and returns the chain, so steps read as a sentence; the closing _ attribute returns 1 or 0. A chain that was tagged false stays false: later steps do not run, so build a new chain for a new question. The surface is frozen legacy: the same idea lives on as interrogative narrations in stzNatural, and part of this class does not work today: the negative forms (IsNot, IsNotAn, IsNotThe, IsNotA) and the function-call forms of Is and IsA. Containment (Containing, ContainingNo) and the nth item (Nth and the ordinal forms st, nd, rd, th) work.
classes.example:
? o1.Is(:String)._
#--> 1
? _("Ring").Is(:Lowercase)._
#--> 0
? _(1234).Is(:Number).Which(:IsEven)._
#--> 1
? _("Ring").Where('NumberOfChars() = 4')._
#--> 1
? _("Ring").Is(:Number).Where('NumberOfChars() = 4')._
#--> 0

sections.title: checking the value identity with is(), isa(), and isthe()
checking a condition on the value

methods.name: init
methods.brief: Builds a chain around one value of any type and wraps it in the library object of its type, so the chain can ask that object questions.

parameters.name: p
parameters.role: the value the chain reasons about: a number, a text, a list or an object

notes: the chain is a frozen legacy surface; new vocabulary belongs to the interrogative narrations of stzNatural
warnings: the chain is usually built by the function _( ), as in _("ring").Is(:String)._

methods.name: Value
methods.brief: Returns the value the chain was built with, unchanged.
methods.returns: the held value, of any type

methods.name: StzObjectQ
methods.brief: Returns the library object that wraps the held value: a stzNumber, stzString, stzList or stzObject.
notes: the questions of Which and Where are put to this object

methods.name: ShouldBeNegated
methods.brief: Returns whether the next step of the chain is read as its opposite.
notes: it is 0 in every chain tested, since no step sets it

methods.name: NeightherFunction
methods.brief: Returns the name of the method Nor will call, as set by IsNeighther, IsNor or ContainingNo.
methods.returns: a text such as isnot; empty text until one of them is used

methods.name: ShouldContinue
methods.brief: Returns whether the chain has not yet reached a verdict.
methods.returns: 1 while no step has decided, 0 once the chain is tagged true or false

methods.name: ShouldReturnTRUE
methods.brief: Returns whether the last step tagged the chain as true.

methods.name: ShouldReturnFALSE
methods.brief: Returns whether a step tagged the chain as false, which makes every later step stay false.

methods.name: SetChainToReturn
methods.brief: Tags the chain with its verdict: 1 for true, 0 for false, or :CONTINUE to clear it.

parameters.name: p
parameters.role: the verdict, 1 or 0, or :CONTINUE

notes: after 0 every later step answers false whatever it tests, so a chain cannot be reused once it failed
warnings: any other value changes nothing

methods.name: Is
methods.section: checking the value identity with is(), isa(), and isthe()
methods.brief: Tests the held value against a type word, a trait word, a value or a list of trait words, tags the chain true or false and returns it.

parameters.name: pThing
parameters.role: what to test: a type such as :String, a trait such as :Lowercase, a value equal to the held one, or a list of traits that must all hold

methods.returns: the chain itself; close it with the _ attribute to read 1 or 0
notes: a value is equal to the held one without regard to case; an unknown word gives a false chain, not an error
warnings: the form with a function call such as 'LetterOf("HUSSEIN")' raises error R14 today, because the string object it asks has no IsLetterOf method; once the chain is false, later steps stay false

methods.name: IsNot
methods.section: checking the value identity with is(), isa(), and isthe()
methods.brief: Returns 0 whatever it is asked, because it negates the chain object that Is returns instead of its verdict.

parameters.name: pThing
parameters.role: what to test, as for Is

warnings: tested with "ring" against :Number and against :String, and both answered 0, where the first should be true

methods.name: IsA
methods.section: checking the value identity with is(), isa(), and isthe()
methods.brief: Tests the held value like Is, with a rule for function calls ending in in or of; for any other word it behaves exactly like Is.

parameters.name: pThing
parameters.role: what to test, as for Is

methods.returns: the chain itself; close it with the _ attribute to read 1 or 0
warnings: the form 'LetterOf("HUSSEIN")' raises error R3 Calling Function without definition: functionnamefinishes..., because the helper it calls has another name

methods.name: IsNotA
methods.section: checking the value identity with is(), isa(), and isthe()
methods.brief: Raises error R24 on every call, because its body reads the name pThing while its parameter is called pcThing.

parameters.name: pcThing
parameters.role: what to test

warnings: tested with :Number and with :String, and both raised error R24 Using uninitialized variable: pthing

methods.name: IsNotAn
methods.section: checking the value identity with is(), isa(), and isthe()
methods.brief: Returns 0 whatever it is asked, because it negates the chain object that IsAn returns instead of its verdict.

parameters.name: pThing
parameters.role: what to test, as for Is

warnings: tested with :Object and with :String, and both answered 0

methods.name: IsNotThe
methods.section: checking the value identity with is(), isa(), and isthe()
methods.brief: Returns 0 whatever it is asked, because it negates the chain object that IsThe returns instead of its verdict.

parameters.name: pThing
parameters.role: what to test, as for Is

warnings: tested against "rang" and against "ring" for the value "ring", and both answered 0

methods.name: IsNeighther
methods.section: checking the value identity with is(), isa(), and isthe()
methods.brief: Records that the next Nor call is a negative test, ignores its argument and returns the chain.

parameters.name: pcThing
parameters.role: a word that is not used

warnings: the argument is not tested, so IsNeighther(:Number) does not check that the value is not a number

methods.name: IsNor
methods.section: checking the value identity with is(), isa(), and isthe()
methods.brief: Records that the next Nor call is a negative test, ignores its argument and returns the chain.

parameters.name: pcThing
parameters.role: a word that is not used

notes: the same call as IsNeighther
warnings: the argument is not tested

methods.name: Which
methods.section: checking the value identity with is(), isa(), and isthe()
methods.brief: Calls one method of the wrapped object on the held value, such as :IsEven, tags the chain with the answer and returns it.

parameters.name: pcMethod
parameters.role: the name of the method to call on the wrapped object, with or without its brackets

methods.returns: the chain itself; close it with the _ attribute to read 1 or 0
notes: once the chain is false, later steps stay false
warnings: a name that does not exist raises a Syntax Error naming Which

methods.name: Where
methods.section: checking a condition on the value
methods.brief: Evaluates a condition on the wrapped object, such as NumberOfChars() = 4, tags the chain with the answer and returns it.

parameters.name: pcCondition
parameters.role: a Ring condition about the wrapped object, written without braces and starting with one of its methods

methods.returns: the chain itself; close it with the _ attribute to read 1 or 0
notes: Having and That are the same call
warnings: a condition between braces, as '{ NumberOfChars() = 4 }', raises Syntax error! Check the condition, because the braces are sent to the evaluator; an invalid condition raises the same error

methods.name: Containing
methods.brief: Tags the chain true when the held text includes p as a part or the held list has p as an item, else false, and returns the chain.

parameters.name: p
parameters.role: what to look for: a text when the chain holds a text; any item (a text, a number or a list) when it holds a list

methods.returns: the chain itself, tagged 1 or 0; close it with the _ attribute to read the answer
notes: a text holds p when p occurs in it as a part, compared by codepoints and telling A from a; every text holds the empty text; a p that is not a text is never held by a text

a list holds p only as a whole item of the same type, so 2 is not found in a list that holds the text "2", and a list item is compared member by member; a number or an object holds nothing, so the chain is tagged false
once the chain is false, later steps stay false; Contains and IsContaining are the same call

methods.name: ContainingNo
methods.brief: Tags the chain true when the held text lacks p as a part or the held list lacks p as an item, else false, and returns the chain.

parameters.name: p
parameters.role: what should be absent: a text when the chain holds a text; any item (a text, a number or a list) when it holds a list

methods.returns: the chain itself, tagged 1 or 0; close it with the _ attribute to read the answer
notes: the exact complement of the containment test for a text or a list, with the same rules for case, empty text, types and nested lists; a number or an object holds nothing and lacks nothing, so for it both tests tag the chain false
once the chain is false, later steps stay false; ContainsNo, ContainsNeighther, IsContainingNo, DoesNotContain and ContainingNeighther are the same call

methods.name: Nor
methods.brief: Runs the method named by NeightherFunction on p and returns its answer: 0 after IsNeighther or IsNor, the chain after ContainingNo.

parameters.name: p
parameters.role: the thing to test: as for Is after IsNeighther or IsNor, as for ContainingNo after it

methods.returns: 0 after IsNeighther or IsNor; the chain itself, tagged 1 or 0, after ContainingNo
warnings: after IsNeighther or IsNor the answer is 0 whatever p is, since the method it calls is IsNot; on a chain where none of these steps came first the method name is empty and the call raises error R42 Error in eval() function

methods.name: st
methods.brief: Returns the item at the rank held by the chain, such as the 21st letter of a call, when that number ends in 1, else nothing.

parameters.name: pcThing
parameters.role: a function call as text, such as 'LetterOf("HUSSEIN")'

methods.returns: what the nth-item step answers, a new chain or this chain tagged false, when the chain holds a number ending in 1; an empty text for any other value
notes: the rank is the held number; 21 asks for the 21st letter, which HUSSEIN does not have

methods.name: nd
methods.brief: Returns the item at the rank held by the chain, such as the 22nd letter of a call, when that number ends in 2, else nothing.

parameters.name: pcThing
parameters.role: a function call as text, such as 'LetterOf("HUSSEIN")'

methods.returns: what the nth-item step answers, a new chain or this chain tagged false, when the chain holds a number ending in 2; an empty text for any other value

methods.name: rd
methods.brief: Returns the item at the rank held by the chain, such as the 23rd letter of a call, when that number ends in 3, else nothing.

parameters.name: pcThing
parameters.role: a function call as text, such as 'LetterOf("HUSSEIN")'

methods.returns: what the nth-item step answers, a new chain or this chain tagged false, when the chain holds a number ending in 3; an empty text for any other value

methods.name: th
methods.brief: Returns the item at the rank held by the chain, such as the 7th letter of a call, when its last digit is 2 to 9, else nothing.

parameters.name: pcThing
parameters.role: a function call as text, such as 'LetterOf("HUSSEIN")'

methods.returns: what the nth-item step answers, a new chain or this chain tagged false, when the chain holds a number whose last digit is 2 to 9; an empty text for any other value
notes: a number ending in 0 or 1 gives an empty text, so 10 asks for nothing here

methods.name: Nth
methods.brief: Returns a new chain holding the nth item, such as the 7th letter of HUSSEIN, or this chain tagged false when there is none.

parameters.name: pcThing
parameters.role: for a chain holding the number n: a function call as text, such as 'LetterOf("HUSSEIN")', that gets Nth in front of its name and n as first argument; for a chain holding a text or a list: the number n itself

methods.returns: a new chain holding the item, read with the _ attribute or Value; this chain tagged false when n is not a whole number from 1 to 2147483647, when there is no item at n, or when pcThing does not fit the held value
notes: the letter of a text is a codepoint, not a byte, so the 2nd letter of an accented text is whole; the call text is evaluated as Ring code, so pass only text you wrote, and a call that cannot be evaluated raises a message that names it

methods.name: get_
methods.brief: Returns 1 if the chain was tagged true, 0 if false, and the held value if no step decided; it answers the closing underscore.
notes: _("ring").Is(:String)._ reads this method

methods.name: get_@
methods.brief: Returns the held value in the form Ring code would write it, such as "ring" with its quotes; it runs when the _@ attribute is read.
notes: a number 5 gives the text 5 and a list gives its bracketed form

methods.name: getAmongOthers
methods.brief: Returns the chain unchanged, so the words AmongOthers can sit in a sentence without effect.

methods.name: getAtTheSameTime
methods.brief: Returns the chain unchanged, so the words AtTheSameTime can follow a list of traits in Is without effect.

methods.name: pvtFunctionParam
methods.brief: Returns the text between the first brackets of a call written as text, quotes included.

parameters.name: pcFunctionCall
parameters.role: a call as text, such as 'LetterOf("HUSSEIN")'

notes: private; run through a subclass

methods.name: pvtFunctionName
methods.brief: Returns the part of a call written as text that comes before its first bracket.

parameters.name: pcFunctionCall
parameters.role: a call as text, such as 'LetterOf("HUSSEIN")'

notes: private; run through a subclass

methods.name: pvtFunctionNameFinishesWithOneOfThese
methods.brief: Returns 1 when the called name ends in in or of, whatever list it is given.

parameters.name: pcFunctionCall
parameters.role: a call as text

parameters.name: paSubStr
parameters.role: the endings meant to be tested, which are ignored

notes: private; run through a subclass
warnings: the list paSubStr is ignored: the endings in and of are fixed in the code, so [ "per" ] does not make Upper("H") answer 1

methods.name: pvtFunctionParamType
methods.brief: Returns the type of the first argument of a call written as text: STRING, LIST or NUMBER.

parameters.name: pcFunctionCall
parameters.role: a call as text, such as 'LetterOf("HUSSEIN")'

methods.returns: the text STRING, LIST or NUMBER
notes: private; run through a subclass
warnings: an argument that is not quoted, bracketed or numeric, such as F(abc), raises error R41 Invalid numeric string, so the OBJECT answer in the code is unreachable

methods.name: pvtFunctionParamTypeIsOneOfThese
methods.brief: Returns 1 when the type of the first argument of a call written as text is in the given list.

parameters.name: pcFunctionCall
parameters.role: a call as text

parameters.name: paSubStr
parameters.role: the list of type names to look in, such as [ "STRING", "LIST" ]

notes: private; run through a subclass

methods.name: pvtHolds
methods.brief: Returns 1 when the held text includes p as a part, or the held list has p as an item, else 0.

parameters.name: p
parameters.role: what to look for, as for Containing

methods.returns: 1 or 0; 0 for a held number or object
notes: private; run through a subclass; the empty text is held by every text, a p that is not a text is never held by a text, and a list is asked through its checker, which compares by type and member, telling A from a

classes.name: stzChainOfValue
classes.brief: Watches one variable of the caller and runs a piece of code only if the variable meets a condition, written as a near-natural chain.
classes.description: A chain is born from an initiator function (Whatever, OnlyWhen, Until, Since, SometimesWhen) that names the variable as a symbol, and each link returns the chain itself: Is compares the value, DoThis runs the code. A link that is not satisfied does not raise an error, it stops the chain: ChainStatus then answers stopped, WhyChainStopped carries the reasons as a list of texts, and DoThis on a stopped chain runs nothing. OnlyWhen runs the code once when the values are equal; Until repeats it until the variable equals the stop value; Since waits for Becomes to name where it ends. The loop mode, the run flag and the stop value are shared by every chain of the process, and a new initiator call resets them. The value held is a snapshot taken when the chain is built. The type questions IsANumber, IsAString, IsAList and IsAnObject answer 1 or 0 and exactly one of them holds for any value; ThisValue builds a chain over a value that is not in a variable.
classes.example:
? o1.ChainStatus()
#--> ongoing
o1.DoThis('{ v = v + 10 }')
? v
#--> 15
? o1.CodeStatus()
#--> hasbeenexecuted
? @@( OnlyWhen(:v).Is(6).WhyChainStopped() )
#--> [ "Because value provided is not equal to main value!" ]
Until(:v).Is(20).DoThis('{ v = v + 1 }')
? v
#--> 20

sections.title: getting the code of the chain of value

methods.name: init
methods.brief: Builds a chain over the caller's variable named by the text, reading its value now; an unknown name starts the chain already stopped.

parameters.name: pcVarName
parameters.role: the NAME of the caller's variable the chain watches, as text, such as :v for the variable v

notes: when the variable does not exist the chain is stopped and WhyChainStopped names it, so no error is raised
warnings: the initiator functions Whatever, OnlyWhen, Until, Since and SometimesWhen build the chain for you and also set the shared flags that decide whether the code runs once or in a loop

methods.name: VarName
methods.brief: Returns the name of the caller's variable that this chain watches.

methods.name: Value
methods.brief: Returns the value read from the watched variable when the chain was built, or the last value given to Update.
methods.returns: the held value, of any type
notes: it is a snapshot: changing the caller's variable afterwards does not change it

methods.name: Copy
methods.brief: Builds a new chain over the same variable name, reading the variable's current value again.
warnings: the copy forgets Update: it holds what the caller's variable holds now, not the value given to Update; a chain built by ThisValue has no variable, so its copy holds the value the chain holds

methods.name: Update
methods.brief: Replaces the value the chain holds; the caller's variable is left as it is.

parameters.name: pValue
parameters.role: the new value to hold

notes: UpdateQ is the same call and returns the chain; the type questions follow the new value, and a pair such as [ :With, 7 ] holds its second item

extensions.name: UpdateQ
extensions.adds: does what the method does, then returns the object, so the call can be chained

methods.name: UpdateWith
methods.brief: Replaces the value the chain holds; the caller's variable is left as it is.

parameters.name: pValue
parameters.role: the new value to hold

notes: the same call as Update

extensions.name: UpdateWithQ
extensions.adds: does what the method does, then returns the object, so the call can be chained

methods.name: UpdateBy
methods.brief: Replaces the value the chain holds; the caller's variable is left as it is.

parameters.name: pValue
parameters.role: the new value to hold

notes: the same call as Update

extensions.name: UpdateByQ
extensions.adds: does what the method does, then returns the object, so the call can be chained

methods.name: UpdateUsing
methods.brief: Replaces the value the chain holds; the caller's variable is left as it is.

parameters.name: pValue
parameters.role: the new value to hold

notes: the same call as Update

extensions.name: UpdateUsingQ
extensions.adds: does what the method does, then returns the object, so the call can be chained

methods.name: Updated
methods.brief: Returns the value it is given, unchanged, and touches neither the chain nor the caller's variable.

parameters.name: pValue
parameters.role: the value to hand back

methods.returns: the same value as the argument
notes: UpdatedWith, UpdatedBy and UpdatedUsing are the same call

methods.name: Code
methods.section: getting the code of the chain of value
methods.brief: Returns the text of the code given to the last DoThis, with its surrounding braces removed.
methods.returns: a text; empty before any DoThis

methods.name: StopValue
methods.section: getting the code of the chain of value
methods.brief: Returns the value at which a looping chain stops, as last set by Until(...).Is, Becomes or StopWhen.
methods.returns: the stop value, of any type; empty text before one is set
notes: it is shared by every chain of the process, not kept per chain

methods.name: getIs
methods.section: getting the code of the chain of value
methods.brief: Returns the chain after switching off negation and one-pass mode; it runs when the Is attribute of the chain is read.
methods.returns: the chain itself, so calls chain
notes: reading Whatever(:v).Is and then calling DoThis is the near-natural form of this call

methods.name: getIsNot
methods.section: getting the code of the chain of value
methods.brief: Returns the chain after switching negation on and one-pass mode; it is meant to run when the IsNot attribute is read.
methods.returns: the chain itself, so calls chain
warnings: reading the attribute IsNot raises error R12 property not found, because the attribute is named _IsNot_; call getIsNot() itself to get the chain

methods.name: get_Not
methods.section: getting the code of the chain of value
methods.brief: Returns the chain after switching negation on and one-pass mode; it runs when the _Not attribute is read.
methods.returns: the chain itself, so calls chain

methods.name: getBecomes
methods.section: getting the code of the chain of value
methods.brief: Returns the chain after putting the process in many-loops mode; it runs when the Becomes attribute is read.
methods.returns: the chain itself, so calls chain
notes: the loop mode is a flag shared by every chain

methods.name: Is
methods.section: getting the code of the chain of value
methods.brief: Compares the held value with pValue and stops the chain when the initiator's condition is not met; otherwise lets it go on.

parameters.name: pValue
parameters.role: the value the held value must equal, of the same type

methods.returns: the chain itself, so calls chain
notes: IsEqualTo and Equals are the same call
warnings: with Whatever the call always stops the chain, with the reason that Whatever does not support Is; with Until the chain stops when the values are equal, and otherwise remembers pValue as the stop value

methods.name: Becomes
methods.section: getting the code of the chain of value
methods.brief: Sets the value at which the chain stops looping, or, after DoThis on a Since chain, runs the stored code until the variable reaches it.

parameters.name: pValue
parameters.role: the value the variable must reach, of the same type as the held value

methods.returns: the chain itself, so calls chain
notes: BecomesEqualTo is the same call
warnings: before DoThis, the chain stops when the types differ or when the held value already equals pValue, with the reason in WhyChainStopped

methods.name: BecomesIsUsedBeforeDoThis
methods.section: getting the code of the chain of value
methods.brief: TRUE if Becomes was called before any DoThis, which makes it set the stop value instead of running code.
notes: 0 until Becomes is called

methods.name: BecomesIsUsedAfterDoThis
methods.section: getting the code of the chain of value
methods.brief: TRUE if Becomes was not called before DoThis, which is also the answer when it was never called.

methods.name: StopWhen
methods.section: getting the code of the chain of value
methods.brief: Sets the value at which a looping chain stops, then returns the chain.

parameters.name: p
parameters.role: the stop value, of any type

methods.returns: the chain itself, so calls chain
notes: the stop value is shared by every chain of the process

methods.name: DoThis
methods.section: getting the code of the chain of value
methods.brief: Runs the code given as text, once or in a loop, when the chain is still ongoing; a stopped chain runs nothing.

parameters.name: pcCode
parameters.role: the Ring code to run, as text, usually between braces such as '{ v++ }'

methods.returns: the chain itself, so calls chain
notes: the braces are removed, the code is evaluated in the caller's scope, and the watched variable is re-read after each pass
warnings: the code runs once after OnlyWhen, Whatever or SometimesWhen, and repeats until the variable equals the stop value after Until; after it ran once the shared run flag is off and a later DoThis only stores its code

methods.name: Do_
methods.section: getting the code of the chain of value
methods.brief: Runs the code given as text, once or in a loop, when the chain is still ongoing; a stopped chain runs nothing.

parameters.name: pcCode
parameters.role: the Ring code to run, as text, usually between braces

methods.returns: the chain itself, so calls chain
notes: the same call as DoThis

methods.name: GetDo_
methods.section: getting the code of the chain of value
methods.brief: Returns the chain after switching on the shared flag that allows code to run.
methods.returns: the chain itself, so calls chain

methods.name: GetCodeExecute
methods.section: getting the code of the chain of value
methods.brief: Returns the chain after switching on the shared flag that allows code to run.
methods.returns: the chain itself, so calls chain
notes: the same call as GetDo_

methods.name: This_
methods.section: getting the code of the chain of value
methods.brief: Runs the code through DoThis only when the shared run flag is on, and does nothing otherwise.

parameters.name: _cCode_
parameters.role: the Ring code to run, as text

methods.name: ValueInitiator
methods.section: getting the code of the chain of value
methods.brief: Returns the name of the function that opened the chain, in lower case.
methods.returns: a text such as whatever, onlywhen, until, since or sometimeswhen
notes: it is a process-wide value: the last initiator called, not a property of this chain

methods.name: StopChain
methods.section: getting the code of the chain of value
methods.brief: Stops the chain and keeps the given reasons, so that nothing later runs.

parameters.name: paStopInfo
parameters.role: the list of reasons, usually one text such as [ "Because ..." ]

notes: a stopped chain stays stopped

methods.name: ChainStatus
methods.section: getting the code of the chain of value
methods.brief: Returns whether the chain is still allowed to run code.

methods.name: WhyChainIsStopped
methods.section: getting the code of the chain of value
methods.brief: Returns the reasons a chain was stopped, or a text saying it was not.
methods.returns: a list of texts when stopped; the text Chain is not stopped! otherwise
notes: WhyChainStopped is the same call

methods.name: OneOrManyLoops
methods.section: getting the code of the chain of value
methods.brief: Returns whether the next DoThis runs the code once or in a loop.
notes: it is shared by every chain of the process

methods.name: RequiresStopValue
methods.section: getting the code of the chain of value
methods.brief: Returns 1 when the initiator needs a stop value before its code can run, which only Since does.
notes: it is shared by every chain of the process

methods.name: CodeStatus
methods.section: getting the code of the chain of value
methods.brief: Returns whether the code given to DoThis has run.

methods.name: WhyCodeNotYetExecuted
methods.section: getting the code of the chain of value
methods.brief: Returns the reason the code has not run yet, or a text saying it has run.
notes: WhyCodeHasNotBeenExecuted is the same call
warnings: when DoThis was called on a stopped chain the reason is the placeholder Because... and not the reason the chain stopped; ask WhyChainStopped for that

methods.name: WhyCodeHasNotBeenExecuted
methods.section: getting the code of the chain of value
methods.brief: Returns the reason the code has not run yet, or a text saying it has run.
notes: the same call as WhyCodeNotYetExecuted

methods.name: CodeHasBeenCalled
methods.section: getting the code of the chain of value
methods.brief: TRUE if DoThis was called on this chain, whether or not the code then ran.

methods.name: CodeHasBeenExecuted
methods.section: getting the code of the chain of value
methods.brief: TRUE if the code given to DoThis has run.

methods.name: CodeIsStillWaitingForExecution
methods.section: getting the code of the chain of value
methods.brief: TRUE if the code given to DoThis has not run, which includes the case where DoThis was never called.

methods.name: ToStzObject
methods.section: getting the code of the chain of value
methods.brief: Returns the held value wrapped in the library class of its type: stzNumber, stzString, stzList or stzObject.
methods.returns: a stzNumber, a stzString, a stzList or a stzObject

methods.name: IsANumber
methods.section: getting the code of the chain of value
methods.brief: TRUE if the held value is a number; a text such as 12 is a text, not a number.
notes: the test is on the type of the value: a numeric text, an empty list and an object all answer 0; ANumber is the same call, and IsANumberQ stops the chain instead of answering

methods.section: getting the code of the chain of value

notes: NotANumber is the same call

extensions.adds: does what the method does, then returns the object, so the call can be chained

extensions.name: NotANumberQ
extensions.adds: does what the method does, then returns the object, so the call can be chained

methods.name: IsAString
methods.section: getting the code of the chain of value
methods.brief: TRUE if the held value is a text, which includes a numeric text such as 12 and the empty text.
notes: AString is the same call, and IsAStringQ stops the chain instead of answering

extensions.name: IsAStringQ
extensions.adds: does what the method does, then returns the object, so the call can be chained

extensions.name: AStringQ

methods.name: IsNotAString
methods.section: getting the code of the chain of value
methods.brief: TRUE if the held value is not a text.
notes: NotAString is the same call

extensions.name: IsNotAStringQ
extensions.adds: does what the method does, then returns the object, so the call can be chained

extensions.adds: does what the method does, then returns the object, so the call can be chained

methods.name: IsAList
methods.section: getting the code of the chain of value
methods.brief: TRUE if the held value is a list, which includes the empty list and a list of lists.
notes: an object is not a list, and a text is not a list whatever it looks like

methods.name: IsAnObject

methods.brief: TRUE if the held value is an object of any class, library or user made.
notes: the test is on the type of the value, so it does not depend on which copy of the object the chain holds

methods.name: init
methods.brief: Reads a chapter's markdown file and splits it at once into prose, runnable cells, exercise references and stored-output fences.

parameters.name: pcFile
parameters.role: the path of the chapter file, NN-<id>.<lang>.md

parameters.name: pcLang
parameters.role: the language code of this edition, used only to read the chapter's id from the file name and to report Language

notes: the chapter's title is its first line that starts with "# "
warnings: raises error R35 (the file cannot be opened) when pcFile does not exist; the cells are not run here

methods.name: File
methods.brief: Returns the path the chapter was read from, exactly as given.

methods.name: Id
methods.brief: Returns the chapter's id, read from its file name by removing the NN- number prefix and the .<lang>.md tail.
warnings: a file name that does not end with .<lang>.md for the language given keeps the .md tail: 99-plain.en.md opened as fr gives plain.en.md

methods.name: Language
methods.brief: Returns the language code this edition of the chapter was opened with.

methods.name: Title
methods.brief: Returns the chapter's title, the text of its first "# " line.
methods.returns: a text; an empty text when the file has no such line

methods.name: Blocks
methods.brief: Returns the chapter in reading order as pairs of a kind and a value: prose, cell, exercise or fence.
methods.returns: a list of pairs; a cell pair holds the cell's number, an exercise pair its id, a prose or fence pair its text

methods.name: Cells
methods.brief: Returns the source of every runnable cell, the ring fences, with their #--> lines.
methods.returns: a list of text, in reading order

methods.name: NumberOfCells
methods.brief: Returns how many runnable ring cells the chapter holds.

methods.name: Cell
methods.brief: Returns the source of one runnable cell, with its #--> lines.

parameters.name: n
parameters.role: the cell's number, from 1

warnings: raises an index error (R2) for a number below 1 or above NumberOfCells

methods.name: CellPromises
methods.brief: Returns the values a cell promises, the text after each #--> line.

parameters.name: n
parameters.role: the cell's number, from 1

methods.returns: a list of text; [ ] when the cell carries no promise
warnings: raises an index error (R2) for a number below 1 or above NumberOfCells

methods.name: ExerciseIds
methods.brief: Returns the ids of the exercises the chapter points to with {{exercise:id}} lines.
methods.returns: a list of text, in reading order

methods.name: NumberOfStoredOutputs
methods.brief: Returns how many fenced blocks of stored output the chapter holds: fences marked output, text, console or out.
methods.returns: a number; a guard refuses a chapter where it is above 0, because a chapter must show no output it did not just produce

methods.name: HasStoredOutput
methods.brief: TRUE if the chapter holds at least one fenced block of stored output.

methods.name: CalledNames
methods.brief: Returns the names the chapter's cells call, read from the code: what the chapter teaches.
methods.returns: a list of text without repeats, in order of first use; a name is a word of four characters or more written right before "(", so a class name after new is included and sort is not

methods.name: RecapAchieved
methods.brief: Returns the first bullet of the chapter's last "## " section, without its bold label, joined on one line.
methods.returns: a text; an empty text when the file has no "## " section
warnings: the last "## " section is taken whatever its title, so a chapter that does not end with its recap returns the first bullet of that other section

methods.name: RunProgram
methods.brief: Returns the Ring program that Run executes, for a runner that batches several chapters.

parameters.name: pcWorldFile
parameters.role: the path of a world file to use, or an empty text for none

methods.returns: a text: it loads the library by absolute path, prepares Hausa, optionally uses a world, then runs every cell inside its own try/catch between @@EDU-CELL markers
warnings: nothing is run by this call

methods.name: WhereProgram
methods.brief: Returns the plain-Ring program that ObserveWhere executes: the same cells, without the library and without a world.
warnings: nothing is run by this call

methods.name: Run
methods.brief: Runs every cell in one fresh process with the library loaded and records each cell's output, error and promise verdict.

parameters.name: pcWorldFile
parameters.role: the path of a world file for the cells that read the world, or an empty text for none

methods.returns: nothing; RunQ is the same call and returns the chapter
notes: the cells run on the desktop only
warnings: a failing cell does not stop the others; with no world, a cell that asks for one fails with "No world is in use" and the chapter is then not AllCellsRan; the child process loads the whole library, so a run takes seconds

extensions.name: RunQ
extensions.adds: does what the method does, then returns the object, so the call can be chained

methods.name: AcceptRun
methods.brief: Takes the result of RunProgram run elsewhere, [ stdout, exit code, stderr ], and records each cell's output, error and promise verdict.

parameters.name: paRun
parameters.role: the list [ stdout, exit code, stderr ] of the run

warnings: a cell the output never reached keeps the error "(not reached)" and an empty output; the exit code is not read

methods.name: HasRun
methods.brief: TRUE if Run or AcceptRun has been called on this chapter.

methods.name: CellOutput
methods.brief: Returns what one cell printed in the last run, one line per print, each ended by a line break.

parameters.name: n
parameters.role: the cell's number, from 1

warnings: raises an index error (R2) before any run, and for a number out of range

methods.name: CellError
methods.brief: Returns the error one cell raised in the last run.

parameters.name: n
parameters.role: the cell's number, from 1

methods.returns: a text; an empty text when the cell ran cleanly, and "(not reached)" for a cell the run never got to
warnings: raises an index error (R2) before any run

methods.name: CellRan
methods.brief: TRUE if one cell raised no error in the last run.

parameters.name: n
parameters.role: the cell's number, from 1

warnings: raises an index error (R2) before any run

methods.name: CellKept
methods.brief: Returns whether one cell kept its promises in the last run.

parameters.name: n
parameters.role: the cell's number, from 1

methods.returns: 1 when every #--> value was printed in order, 0 when one was not, -1 when the cell carries no promise
warnings: raises an index error (R2) before any run

methods.name: AllCellsRan
methods.brief: TRUE if no cell raised an error in the last run.
warnings: raises an index error (R2) before any run

methods.name: AllPromisesKept
methods.brief: TRUE if no cell broke a promise in the last run; cells without a promise do not count.
methods.returns: TRUE or FALSE; TRUE before any run, because nothing is broken yet
warnings: call HasRun first: before a run the answer says nothing about the chapter

methods.name: NumberOfPromises
methods.brief: Returns how many #--> promises the chapter's cells hold in all.
methods.returns: a number; it needs no run

methods.name: WorldDependentCells
methods.brief: Returns the numbers of the cells that carry no promise, whose output depends on the world and so may not be shown on a page.
methods.returns: a list of numbers; [ ] before any run
warnings: a cell that carries no promise is listed whether or not it ran

methods.name: ObserveWhere
methods.brief: Runs the cells in plain Ring, without the library, and marks each one browser or desktop from what happened.
notes: the mark is observed, never typed by an author; the cells run on the desktop only
warnings: a cell is marked browser when it raised no error and either carries no promise or keeps its promises; a cell that calls any library class is therefore marked desktop, which is every cell of chapter 1

methods.name: AcceptWhere
methods.brief: Takes the result of WhereProgram run elsewhere, [ stdout, exit code, stderr ], and marks each cell browser or desktop.

parameters.name: paRun
parameters.role: the list [ stdout, exit code, stderr ] of the plain-Ring run

warnings: the exit code is not read

methods.name: RunsWhere
methods.brief: Returns where one cell was observed to run.

parameters.name: n
parameters.role: the cell's number, from 1

warnings: raises an error saying where a cell runs is observed, never assumed, when ObserveWhere or AcceptWhere has not been called

methods.name: Where
methods.brief: Returns the observed place of every cell, in order.
methods.returns: a list of text, browser or desktop; [ ] before ObserveWhere

classes.name: stzChar
classes.brief: Holds one Unicode char, exactly as stzStringChar does, and reports its own type name, stzchar.
classes.description: A thin subclass: the only thing it adds to stzStringChar is StzType, which answers :stzChar instead of the stzstring it would inherit. Every other method is stzStringChar's.
classes.example:
? o1.StzType()
#--> stzchar

methods.name: StzType
methods.brief: Returns the type name of this subclass, stzchar, where the parent class stzStringChar answers stzstring.

classes.name: stzClusterSupervisor
classes.brief: Keeps a cluster of worker processes healthy and sized to its load: restarts dead workers, scales up under high load, drains under low.
classes.description: Set a Policy (a minimum and a maximum per tag), the water marks, and report the demand with ReportLoad or FeedLoadFrom. Decide is a pure function from fleet metrics to a list of actions and touches nothing; Supervise applies those actions to the live cluster and Cycle is Supervise as a tickable job for an agent host. Dead workers are restarted before any scaling; scaling stops at the policy bounds. Only Decide is safe to call on its own; Supervise and Cycle start and stop processes.
classes.receiver: o1 = new stzClusterSupervisor("") o1.Policy("nlp", 1, 4) o1.SetWaterMarks(0.25, 0.75) o1.ReportLoad("nlp", 0.9)
classes.example:
? @@( o1.Decide([ [ :tag = "nlp", :ready = 2, :dead = 1 ] ]) )
#--> [ [ "restart", "nlp" ], [ "scaleup", "nlp" ] ]
? o1.LoadOf("nlp")
#--> 0.90

methods.name: init
methods.brief: Builds a supervisor for a cluster of worker processes; it reads the cluster's health and scales it, and does nothing until it is asked.

parameters.name: poCluster
parameters.role: the cluster to supervise, an object with HealthCheck, FleetMetrics, RestartDead, ScaleUp and ScaleDown, such as a stzAppCluster

methods.name: Name_
methods.brief: Returns the supervisor's name, 'cluster-supervisor' unless SetName changed it.

methods.name: SetName
methods.brief: Sets the name by which an agent host knows the supervisor.

parameters.name: pcName
parameters.role: the new name, as text

methods.returns: the supervisor itself, so calls chain

methods.name: ClusterQ
methods.brief: Returns the cluster the supervisor was given.

methods.name: Policy
methods.brief: Sets how many workers a tag may have, at least nMin and at most nMax; the tag is matched without regard to case.

parameters.name: pcTag
parameters.role: the facet or profile tag the policy covers

parameters.name: nMin
parameters.role: the fewest workers to keep, raised to 1 if smaller

parameters.name: nMax
parameters.role: the most workers to start, raised to nMin if smaller

methods.returns: the supervisor itself, so calls chain
warnings: a second call for the same tag replaces the bounds

methods.name: SetWaterMarks
methods.brief: Sets the two load ratios that trigger scaling: below nLow the supervisor scales down, above nHigh it scales up.

parameters.name: nLow
parameters.role: the low-water load ratio, 0.25 by default

parameters.name: nHigh
parameters.role: the high-water load ratio, 0.75 by default

methods.returns: the supervisor itself, so calls chain
warnings: one pair of marks serves every tag

methods.name: ReportLoad
methods.brief: Records the demand observed for a tag, as a ratio from 0 to 1, replacing the earlier figure.

parameters.name: pcTag
parameters.role: the facet or profile tag, matched without regard to case

parameters.name: nRatio
parameters.role: the observed load from 0 to 1

methods.returns: the supervisor itself, so calls chain

methods.name: LoadOf
methods.brief: Returns the last load ratio reported for a tag; 0 when none was reported.

parameters.name: pcTag
parameters.role: the tag to look up, matched without regard to case

methods.name: FeedLoadFrom
methods.brief: Reads the load ratio from a performance profile and reports it for a tag, so the signal is measured and not typed in.

parameters.name: pcTag
parameters.role: the tag the load belongs to

parameters.name: poProfile
parameters.role: an object that answers LoadRatio(), such as a stzPerfProfile

methods.returns: the supervisor itself, so calls chain

methods.name: Decide
methods.brief: Returns the actions the policy calls for given the fleet metrics, without touching the cluster.

parameters.name: aMetrics
parameters.role: the fleet metrics, a list of hashlists such as [ :tag = 'nlp', :ready = 2, :dead = 1 ]

methods.returns: a list of [ kind, tag ] pairs, kind being :restart, :scaleup or :scaledown
notes: read from the code and run with invented metrics; no cluster was involved
warnings: a tag with a policy but no entry in the metrics is skipped; a dead worker gives a restart first, then the load decides; a tag at its bound gives no scaling

methods.name: Supervise
methods.brief: Runs one pass: checks the cluster's health, reads its metrics, decides, and applies the actions to the cluster.
methods.returns: the list of actions taken, as Decide returns it
notes: one restart call heals every dead worker, however many restart actions there are
warnings: it calls HealthCheck, RestartDead, ScaleUp and ScaleDown on the cluster, so it changes a live fleet; it was run here only against an invented stand-in object, never a real cluster

methods.name: LastActions
methods.brief: Returns the actions taken by the last Supervise pass; empty before the first.
methods.returns: a list of [ kind, tag ] pairs

methods.name: Cycle
methods.brief: Runs one Supervise pass and returns how many actions it took, so an agent host can tick the supervisor as a job.
methods.returns: a number; 0 when the fleet was quiescent
notes: run here only against an invented stand-in object
warnings: same warning as Supervise: it acts on the cluster it was given

classes.name: stzClusterTelemetry
classes.brief: Records the requests a cluster routes: a bounded list of traces, and a latency histogram per facet for p50 to p99.
classes.description: Each routed request gets a trace id from NewTraceId and is recorded with RecordRequest: facet, endpoint, status, duration and attempts (more than one means a failover happened). Percentiles come from the engine histogram, one per facet, so a heavy facet's tail does not smear a light one; they are bucket bounds, not exact values. The recorder keeps the latest 512 traces. It is a plain recorder: no reactor, no process.
classes.example:
? o1.LatencyCount("nlp")
#--> 2
? o1.LatencyP99("nlp")
#--> 50
? @@( o1.LastTrace() )
#--> [ "r2", "nlp", "127.0.0.1:47002", 200, 40, 2 ]
? len(o1.FailoverTraces())
#--> 1

methods.name: init
methods.brief: Creates an empty recorder of request traces and per-facet latency histograms for a cluster, under a name.

parameters.name: pcName
parameters.role: the recorder's name, shown in Narrate

methods.name: Name_
methods.brief: Returns the recorder's name.

methods.name: NewTraceId
methods.brief: Returns a fresh trace id of the form t-<start time in ms>-<sequence number>, unique within this recorder.
warnings: the part after t- starts from the wall clock when the recorder is created, so the full id differs between runs

methods.name: RecordRequest
methods.brief: Records one routed request as a trace and, if it was attempted at least once, adds its duration to the histogram of its facet.
usage: RecordRequest(pcId, pcFacet, pcEndpoint, pnStatus, pnDurMs, pnAttempts)

parameters.name: pcId
parameters.role: the trace id of the request

parameters.name: pcFacet
parameters.role: the facet that served it, matched without regard to case

parameters.name: pcEndpoint
parameters.role: the endpoint that answered

parameters.name: pnStatus
parameters.role: the final status

parameters.name: pnDurMs
parameters.role: the total duration in milliseconds

parameters.name: pnAttempts
parameters.role: how many endpoints were tried, more than 1 meaning a failover

classes.brief: Holds the project rules plus no-cyclic-calls, the opt-in set for a deeper and slower audit.
classes.description: no-cyclic-calls needs call edges and finds a pair of methods in one class that call each other. Its cost grows with the square of the calls times the methods, so it is opt-in through StzCheckProjectDeep, and the default gate documents that it omits it.
classes.example:
? o1.NumberOfRules()
#--> 7
? o1.RuleNames()[7]
#--> no-cyclic-calls

classes.name: stzCodeGraph
classes.brief: Turns source code into a graph of classes, methods, functions, imports and calls, and answers questions about inheritance and impact.
classes.description: This is the shared head of the code graph family: it holds the model and every query, and each language is a subclass that knows how to read its source (stzRingCodeGraph, stzPyCodeGraph, stzJsCodeGraph). Build a graph with one of their functions, such as StzPyCodeGraphFromSource, then ask: Classes, MethodsOf, OwnersOf, AncestryOf, SubclassesOf, DescendantsOf, ImpactOf (who defines a method and who inherits it) and Cascade (how far a change to a class reaches). The call questions, CallersOf, CalleesOf, DeadCode and CyclicCalls, need call edges, which only a real parse such as ScanSourceViaTreeSitter records; without them DeadCode and CyclicCalls raise an error instead of guessing. The base class cannot parse by itself: Language raises, and so do Stats and any scan. CheckRules and RulesAreSound work on a Ring graph only.
classes.receiver: o1 = StzPyCodeGraphFromSource('class Animal:' + char(10) + '    def speak(self):' + char(10) + '        return 1' + char(10) + 'class Dog(Animal):' + char(10) + '    def speak(self):' + char(10) + '        return 2' + char(10) + 'class Puppy(Dog):' + char(10) + '    pass')
classes.example:
? @@( o1.Classes() )
#--> [ "Animal", "Dog", "Puppy" ]
? @@( o1.AncestryOf("Puppy") )
#--> [ "Puppy", "Dog", "Animal" ]
? @@( o1.DescendantsOf("Animal") )
#--> [ "Dog", "Puppy" ]
? @@( o1.OwnersOf("speak") )
#--> [ "Animal", "Dog" ]
? @@( o1.ImpactOf("speak")[:inheritedBy] )
#--> [ "Puppy" ]
? o1.Cascade("Animal")[:blastRadius]
#--> 2

classes.description: no-dead-code names a defined method or function that no recorded call reaches. It is name-based and cannot see a call through a variable, so it reports candidates and not proof; a graph without call edges yields nothing. The slow no-cyclic-calls rule is not here, so the set is cheap enough for a per-commit gate.
classes.example:
? o1.NumberOfRules()
#--> 6
? o1.RuleNames()[6]

classes.name: stzCodeRule
classes.brief: Holds one code rule, a graph rule over a code graph, whose finding carries the line of the offending code.
classes.description: A code rule is a stzGraphRule in the code domain. Its checker queries a stzCodeGraph, which models real method definitions and real call edges, instead of scanning text, so a comment that says def len is not a method and a method definition named substr is not a call. The house rules are declared in stzCodeRuleSet, and StzCheckCode runs them over source.
classes.example:
? o1.Name()
#--> no-len-method
? o1.Domain()
#--> code

classes.name: stzCodeRuleSet
classes.brief: Holds the house rules of the library that a code graph can check, as one graph rule set in the code domain.
classes.description: Five rules are loaded: no-len-method, no-aggressive-verbs, engine-first, q-has-plain-twin and no- case-collision. The sixth house rule, q-returns-object, needs a model of return statements that the code graph does not have, so StzCheckCode runs it as a text pass and merges the findings. The project set adds no-dead-code, and the deep set adds the slow no-cyclic-calls.

#--> 5

classes.name: stzCoeffExtractor
classes.brief: Reads the coefficient of a variable in a linear expression, for the solvers that turn text into numbers.
classes.description: For a plain linear expression such as 5*x + 3*y - 2*z it reads each term and gives 5, 3 and -2; a variable written without a star has coefficient 1 or -1, an absent one 0. A non-linear expression is meant to be handled by nudging the variable around the point where every variable is 10, but that path raises today. The plain path matches names as substrings, so give variables names that are not parts of one another. Building it sets Ring's display precision to 4 decimals until a brace ends or BraceEnd is called.
classes.example:
? o1.extract("5*x + 3*y - 2*z", "z")
#--> -2
? o1.extractAllCoefficients("5*x + 3*y - 2*z")[2]
#--> 3
? o1.extract("3*y", "x")
#--> 0

parameters.name: pnDelta
parameters.role: the step, a small positive number

methods.name: BraceEnd
methods.brief: Puts Ring's display precision back to what it was when the extractor was built, at the closing of a brace.
warnings: called by hand it has the same effect

notes: ExtractCoefficient and ExtractCoeff are the same call

parameters.name: _cVarName_

classes.name: stzCommitScope
classes.brief: Bounds what an update plan may commit: the operation types, the path prefixes and the number of operations.
classes.description: A human usually commits with no scope; a script or an agent commits only inside a declared, auditable one, by the same mechanism. A new scope admits everything. Each AllowType and AllowUnder narrows it: once a type is allowed, any other type is refused, and once a prefix is allowed, every path an operation touches must start with one of them. Reason says why an operation is refused and Allows says whether it is. The limit on the number of operations is applied by the plan while it commits.
classes.example:
o1.AllowUnder("/w/").AllowType("create_file")
? o1.Allows(new stzVirtualOperation("create_file", [ [ "path", "/w/a.txt" ], [ "content", "" ] ]))
#--> 1
? o1.Reason(new stzVirtualOperation("delete_file", [ [ "path", "/w/a.txt" ] ]))
#--> operation type 'delete_file' is not allowed by this scope

methods.name: init
methods.brief: Builds an unlimited scope, which admits every operation until a bound is added.

methods.name: AllowUnder

parameters.name: pcPrefix
parameters.role: the path prefix to admit, matched as text from the start

methods.returns: the scope itself, so calls chain
warnings: the match is on text, not on folders: /w also admits /work/z, so end a folder prefix with a slash

methods.name: AllowType
methods.brief: Adds an operation type that is admitted; once one is added, any other type is refused.

parameters.name: pcType
parameters.role: the type to admit, such as create_file, matched without regard to case

methods.returns: the scope itself, so calls chain

methods.name: SetMaxOperations
methods.brief: Sets the most operations one plan may commit under this scope.

parameters.name: pnMax
parameters.role: the limit

methods.returns: the scope itself, so calls chain

methods.name: MaxOperations
methods.brief: Returns the most operations one plan may commit under this scope.
methods.returns: a number; 0 when there is no limit

methods.name: AllowedPrefixes

methods.returns: a list of text; empty when paths are unrestricted

methods.name: Reason
methods.brief: Returns why an operation is refused, or nothing when it is admitted.

parameters.role: the stzVirtualOperation to judge

methods.name: Allows

parameters.name: oOp
parameters.role: the stzVirtualOperation to judge

notes: the limit on the number of operations is checked by the plan at commit time, not here

classes.name: stzComplex
classes.brief: Holds a complex number, a real part plus an imaginary part, and does its arithmetic: sum, product, quotient, modulus, argument, conjugate.
classes.description: Build one with new stzComplex(re, im). It follows the Softanza forms: an active verb (Conjugate, Negate) changes the number in place; the passive form (Conjugated, Negated, Plus, Times ...) returns the result as a [ re, im ] pair and leaves the number alone; the Q twin (ConjugatedQ, PlusQ ...) returns a new stzComplex to chain on. The other operand of Plus, Minus, Times, DividedBy and Equals may be a number, a pair or another stzComplex. Log, inverse trigonometry and general powers are absent on purpose. The factory function StzComplexQ(re, im) written at the end of the file is not reachable as a function today (error R3).

methods.name: init
methods.brief: Builds a complex number from a real part and an imaginary part; a part that is not a number becomes 0.

parameters.name: pnReal
parameters.role: the real part, or a pair [ re, im ] that carries both

parameters.name: pnImaginary
parameters.role: the imaginary part (give 0 when pnReal is a pair)

warnings: Both arguments are required: new stzComplex([2, -3]) with the pair alone raises R19 (less number of parameters), so give new stzComplex([2, -3], 0); a text for a part is silently read as 0: ("x", "y") builds 0+0i

methods.name: RealPart
methods.brief: Returns the real part of the number.

methods.name: ImaginaryPart
methods.brief: Returns the imaginary part of the number, the coefficient of i.

methods.name: Parts
methods.brief: Returns the real and imaginary parts together as a pair.

methods.name: Content
methods.brief: Returns the number written as text, such as 3+4i or 3-4i, a bare 3 when the imaginary part is 0, 5i when the real part is 0.
notes: i and -i stand for an imaginary part of 1 and -1

methods.name: IsReal
methods.brief: TRUE if the imaginary part is 0.
notes: 0 itself is real

methods.name: IsImaginary
methods.brief: TRUE if the real part is 0 and the imaginary part is not.
notes: 0 is not imaginary

methods.name: IsZero
methods.brief: TRUE if both parts are 0.

methods.name: Modulus
methods.brief: Returns the distance of the number from 0, the length sqrt(re^2 + im^2), computed so that very large parts do not overflow.
notes: Magnitude is the same method; 3+4i has modulus 5

methods.name: Argument
methods.brief: Returns the angle of the number from the positive real axis, in radians, between minus pi (excluded) and pi.
notes: 0 for the number 0; -1 gives pi

methods.name: Conjugate
methods.brief: Changes the number into its conjugate in place, the imaginary part changing sign.
notes: Conjugated leaves the number alone

extensions.name: ConjugateQ
extensions.adds: does what the method does, then returns the object, so the call can be chained

methods.name: Conjugated
methods.brief: Returns the conjugate as a pair [ re, -im ], leaving the number unchanged.
notes: ConjugatedQ answers a new stzComplex

extensions.name: ConjugatedQ
extensions.adds: does what the method does, then returns the object, so the call can be chained

methods.name: Negate
methods.brief: Changes the number into its opposite in place, both parts changing sign.

extensions.name: NegateQ
extensions.adds: does what the method does, then returns the object, so the call can be chained

methods.name: Negated
methods.brief: Returns the opposite as a pair [ -re, -im ], leaving the number unchanged.
notes: NegatedQ answers a new stzComplex

extensions.name: NegatedQ
extensions.adds: does what the method does, then returns the object, so the call can be chained

methods.name: Plus
methods.brief: Returns the sum with another number as a pair [ re, im ], leaving this number unchanged.

parameters.name: pZ
parameters.role: the other number: a plain number, a pair [ re, im ] or a stzComplex

notes: PlusQ answers a new stzComplex to chain on; any other kind of value raises "Give me a number, a [re, im] pair, or another stzComplex."

extensions.name: PlusQ
extensions.adds: does what the method does, then returns the object, so the call can be chained

methods.name: Minus
methods.brief: Returns the difference with another number as a pair [ re, im ], leaving this number unchanged.

parameters.name: pZ
parameters.role: the number to subtract: a plain number, a pair [ re, im ] or a stzComplex

notes: MinusQ answers a new stzComplex

extensions.name: MinusQ
extensions.adds: does what the method does, then returns the object, so the call can be chained

methods.name: Times
methods.brief: Returns the product with another number as a pair [ re, im ], leaving this number unchanged.

parameters.name: pZ
parameters.role: the factor: a plain number, a pair [ re, im ] or a stzComplex

notes: TimesQ answers a new stzComplex; 3+4i times i is -4+3i

extensions.name: TimesQ
extensions.adds: does what the method does, then returns the object, so the call can be chained

methods.name: DividedBy
methods.brief: Returns the quotient by another number as a pair [ re, im ], leaving this number unchanged, using a form that does not overflow.

parameters.name: pZ
parameters.role: the divisor: a plain number, a pair [ re, im ] or a stzComplex, not zero

notes: dividing by 0 raises "Can't divide a complex number by zero."; DividedByQ answers a new stzComplex

extensions.name: DividedByQ
extensions.adds: does what the method does, then returns the object, so the call can be chained

methods.name: Equals
methods.brief: TRUE if the other number has the same real and imaginary parts.

parameters.name: pZ
parameters.role: the number to compare with: a plain number, a pair [ re, im ] or a stzComplex

notes: the comparison is exact, with no tolerance for rounding

classes.name: stzComputeFederation
classes.brief: Governs a constellation of compute hosts: it discovers who offers a facet, clears the caller by bond and governance, then transports the call.
classes.description: Member hosts join with an endpoint and the facets they offer. A federated call to a facet is discovered (an active host must offer it), governed (a bond must permit the caller, and the governance lattice must clear the action use-facet against the caller's permission and authority) and only then transported to the first offering host over the reactor, signed when the caller has a registered key, and over mutual TLS when SetMutualTls was called. A refusal returns an empty text, sets the status to -1, says why in Why and is noted to the security ledger. The receiver side checks a signed request with VerifyInbound. The registry, bonds, governance and verification read and run in memory; a call that clears all gates contacts the host, so this reference only ran the refusal paths.
classes.receiver: o1 = new stzComputeFederation("acme-grid"); o1.Join("gpu-farm", "10.0.0.7:8080", [ :neural, :vision ]) o1.Join("math-farm", "10.0.0.8:8080", [ :math ]); o1.Bond("web- host", :neural)
classes.example:
? @@(o1.MembersOffering(:neural))
#--> [ "gpu-farm" ]
? o1.AreBonded("web-host", :neural)
#--> 1
? len(o1.FederatedCall("stranger", :neural, "/work", ""))
#--> 0
? o1.Why()
#--> no bond lets 'stranger' request facet 'neural'
? o1.CallLastStatus()
#--> -1

methods.brief: Builds an empty federation of compute hosts with its own governance, reactor and request signer.

parameters.name: pcName

methods.brief: Finds a host that offers a facet, lets the bond and governance clear the caller, then sends the request to the first such host.

notes: with a registered key the request is signed, and with SetMutualTls it goes over a mutually authenticated TLS channel instead of plain HTTP

classes.name: stzComputePipeline
classes.brief: Declares a workflow as a chain of facet stages, each transforming the running value, and runs inputs through the chain.
classes.description: A stage is a function tagged with the facet that handles it, so a document flow such as vision, nlp, knowledge, search is declared and not hand-wired. Run threads an input through every stage; RunBatch does it for many inputs. When a worker pool is attached with SetPool, each stage is admitted into its own facet's budget, so a heavy facet cannot starve a light one. A stage that raises stops the run and is reported by Failed and Why. The stages run in-process; running a stage on a fleet worker needs a worker that implements the facet.
classes.receiver: o1 = new stzComputePipeline("doc-intake") o1.Stage("vision", "ocr", func x { return StzReplace(x, "scan:", "") }) o1.Stage("nlp", "entities", func x { return x + " [entities]" })
classes.example:
? o1.Run("scan:acme invoice")
#--> acme invoice [entities]
? o1.Narrate()
#--> pipeline doc-intake: vision -> nlp
? o1.Failed()
#--> 0
? @@( o1.ValidateAgainst(new stzFacetCatalog()) )
#--> [ ]
