classes.name: stzConditionalRegexMaker
classes.brief: Builds an if-then-else regular expression, a conditional pattern, from a condition, a then part and an optional else part.
classes.description: The condition is one of the If calls (IfMatch, IfNotMatch, IfStartsWith, IfEndsWith, IfContains, IfPrecededBy, IfFollowedBy); the last one called wins. ThenMatch and ElseMatch give the two branches, and Pattern joins them as (?(?=condition)then|else). The pattern stays empty until a condition is set. IfStartsWith, IfEndsWith and IfContains take literal text and escape it; the other calls take a pattern. IfCaptured does not build a conditional today, and the pair forms of IfCaptured and IfPrecededBy raise an error.
classes.example:
o1.IfMatch("\d").ThenMatch("\d+").ElseMatch("[a-z]+")
? o1.Pattern()
#--> (?(?=\d)\d+|[a-z]+)
o2 = new stzRegex(o1.Pattern())
o2.MatchFirst("abc 123")
? @@( o2.Matches() )
#--> [ "abc", "123" ]
o1.Reset()
? o1.IfStartsWith("+").ThenMatch("\d+").Pattern()
#--> (?(?=^\+)\d+)

methods.name: init
methods.brief: Builds a conditional pattern maker with no condition, no then part and no else part.

methods.name: Reset
methods.brief: Empties the condition, the then part and the else part.
notes: unlike the look-around maker's Reset, it does not return the maker

methods.name: IfMatch
methods.brief: Sets the condition to a look-ahead: the then part applies when pcPattern matches at the current position.

parameters.name: pcPattern
parameters.role: the pattern the text must match at this point, such as \d

methods.returns: the maker itself, so calls chain
notes: a second If call replaces the condition
warnings: a value that is not a text raises Incorrect param type! pcPattern must be a string

methods.name: IfNotMatch
methods.brief: Sets the condition to a negative look-ahead: the then part applies when pcPattern does not match at the current position.

parameters.name: pcPattern
parameters.role: the pattern the text must not match at this point

methods.returns: the maker itself, so calls chain
notes: a second If call replaces the condition
warnings: a value that is not a text raises Incorrect param type! pcPattern must be a string

methods.name: IfCaptured
methods.brief: Sets a condition on a capture group, but builds the text (?1 or (?<name> instead of a conditional, so the pattern is not a conditional.

parameters.name: pcGroupName
parameters.role: the group's number or name, as text

methods.returns: the maker itself, so calls chain
notes: b) for the group 1, where a conditional is written (?(1)a
warnings: with ThenMatch and ElseMatch it gave (?1a

methods.name: ThenMatch
methods.brief: Sets the pattern that applies when the condition holds.

parameters.name: pcPattern
parameters.role: the pattern for the then part

methods.returns: the maker itself, so calls chain
notes: without an If call, Pattern stays empty
warnings: a value that is not a text raises Incorrect param type! pcPattern must be a string

methods.name: ElseMatch
methods.brief: Sets the pattern that applies when the condition does not hold.

parameters.name: pcPattern
parameters.role: the pattern for the else part

methods.returns: the maker itself, so calls chain
warnings: a value that is not a text raises Incorrect param type! pcPattern must be a string

methods.name: IfStartsWith
methods.brief: Sets the condition to the text starting here, taking pcText as literal text whose special characters are escaped.

parameters.name: pcText
parameters.role: the literal text the subject must start with

methods.returns: the maker itself, so calls chain
notes: IfStartsWith("+") builds the condition (?=^\+)
warnings: a value that is not a text raises Incorrect param type! pcText must be a string

methods.name: IfEndsWith
methods.brief: Sets the condition to the text ending here, taking pcText as literal text whose special characters are escaped.

parameters.name: pcText
parameters.role: the literal text the subject must end with

methods.returns: the maker itself, so calls chain
notes: IfEndsWith(".edu") builds the condition (?=\.edu$)
warnings: a value that is not a text raises Incorrect param type! pcText must be a string

methods.name: IfContains
methods.brief: Sets the condition to the text appearing somewhere ahead, taking pcText as literal text whose special characters are escaped.

parameters.name: pcText
parameters.role: the literal text the subject must contain

methods.returns: the maker itself, so calls chain
notes: IfContains("a.b") builds the condition (?=.*a\.b.*)
warnings: a value that is not a text raises Incorrect param type! pcText must be a string

methods.name: IfPrecededBy
methods.brief: Sets the condition to a look-behind: the then part applies when pcPattern ends just before the current position.

parameters.name: pcPattern
parameters.role: the pattern that must come before this point

methods.returns: the maker itself, so calls chain
notes: the condition built is a look-ahead around a look-behind
warnings: the pair form [ :pattern, "x" ] raises error R24 Using uninitialized variable, because the code reads a name that is not the parameter; a value that is not a text raises Incorrect param type!

methods.name: IfFollowedBy
methods.brief: Sets the condition to a look-ahead built from pcPattern, which is the same condition IfMatch builds with a nested look-ahead.

parameters.name: pcPattern
parameters.role: the pattern that must come after this point

methods.returns: the maker itself, so calls chain
notes: IfFollowedBy("x") builds (?(?=(?=x))
warnings: a value that is not a text raises Incorrect param type! pcPattern must be a string

methods.name: Pattern
methods.brief: Returns the conditional pattern as one text: the condition, the then part, and the else part after a bar when there is one.
warnings: Info, IfMatch, ThenMatch, ElseMatch

methods.name: Info
methods.brief: Returns the condition, the then part, the else part and the finished pattern, as a hashlist.
methods.returns: a hashlist with the keys condition, then, else and pattern
notes: the keys are lower case when listed

classes.name: stzConstraint
classes.brief: Pairs an object with a condition, written as Ring code in a text, that the object is expected to obey, and checks it on demand.
classes.description: The condition says @ for the guarded object: '{ @.IsLowercase() }' or the same without braces. The braces are optional and only one enclosing pair is taken off. A constraint is built even when the object does not obey the condition (CheckConstraint answers 0 then); it is refused only when the condition cannot run on the object at all.
classes.example:
? o1.CheckConstraint()
#--> 1

methods.name: init
methods.brief: Builds a constraint from the object to guard and the condition text, refusing a condition that cannot run on that object.

parameters.name: pObject
parameters.role: the object the constraint guards; the constraint keeps a copy of it

parameters.name: pConstraint
parameters.role: the condition as Ring code in a text, braced or not, such as '{ @.IsLowercase() }', where @ stands for the object

methods.returns: nothing; the constraint is built, unnamed
notes: a condition the object does not obey is accepted, only one that cannot run on it is refused; the condition is run once here to find out
warnings: the text is executed as Ring code: give it only trusted text. A pObject that is not an object or a pConstraint that is not a text raises Incorrect types of object params!, an empty condition raises Constraint can't be empty!, and a condition that raises on the object (a syntax error, a missing method) raises Constraint can't be evaluated on the given object!

methods.name: Content
methods.brief: Returns the condition text exactly as it was given, braces included.

methods.name: Object
methods.brief: Returns the guarded object, the one the condition is checked against.

methods.name: Name
methods.brief: Returns the label given to the constraint, or an empty text when it has none.
notes: it is the constraint's own label, set with SetName; VarName, the variable name every object carries, is a different field and is not changed by SetName

extensions.name: NameQ
extensions.adds: does what the method does, then returns the object, so the call can be chained

methods.name: SetName
methods.brief: Gives the constraint a label that Name reads back, replacing any earlier one.

parameters.name: pcName
parameters.role: the label as a text; an empty text clears it

methods.returns: nothing; SetNameQ returns the constraint for chaining
warnings: a label that is not a text raises Incorrect param type! pcName must be a string.

extensions.name: SetNameQ
extensions.adds: does what the method does, then returns the object, so the call can be chained

methods.name: Expression
methods.brief: Returns the Ring code that tests the condition on @ and raises Constraint unverified! when it fails.
methods.returns: a text of Ring code: the condition without its braces, inside an if, with a branch that raises when the condition is false
notes: the text is trimmed and one enclosing pair of braces is taken off, so braced, unbraced and multi-line forms of the same condition give the same code
warnings: the code is run by CheckConstraint, so it is as trusted as the condition text

methods.name: CheckConstraint
methods.brief: Tells whether the guarded object obeys the condition, 1 when it does and 0 when it does not.
notes: 0 also covers a condition that raises when it is run (the object failed inside the condition); Verdict and LastError tell that case apart from a plain violation

methods.name: Verdict
methods.brief: Runs the check and says what happened: holds, violated, or broken when the condition itself raised.
methods.returns: "holds" when the object obeys the condition, "violated" when the condition ran and answered no, "broken" when running it raised an error of its own
notes: the Ring error of a broken check is kept for LastError; a holding or a violated check clears it. A condition that raises the exact text Constraint unverified! is read as a violation

methods.name: LastError
methods.brief: Returns the Ring error kept by the last check that was broken, or an empty text.
methods.returns: a text; empty before any check, after a check that holds, and after a violated one

classes.name: stzConversation
classes.brief: Runs a governed question-and-answer session in a knowledge space: the system asks from the gaps of a goal, and answers are admitted by law.
classes.description: A conversation happens inside a stzKnowledgeGraph and never owns one: the space is handed in on each call. You hand the session exactly one goal; NextQuestion is born from the first gap and says why it asks, and Reply admits each answer through the space governed door, so a law such as :Unique refuses a value and the refusal becomes a checkpoint for a human. A number picks an offered option, text such as X and Y is split into values, and a list is taken as data. The goal moves from pursuing to fulfilled when no gap remains, or to revoked; Conclude then writes the space to a knowledge file, and refuses while gaps remain. It needs no model: neural wording is used only when a generative model is really loaded.
classes.receiver: oKB = new stzKnowledgeGraph("restaurant"); oKB.Know("margherita", "dish") o1 = new stzConversation("setup"); o1.SetGoal(StzGoalQ().RequireEach("dish", "contains"))
classes.example:
? o1.NextQuestion(oKB)
#--> What does 'margherita' have for 'contains'?  (why: every dish needs 'contains')
? len(o1.Reply(oKB, "tomato and mozzarella")[:admitted])
#--> 2
? o1.GoalState()
#--> fulfilled

methods.name: init
methods.brief: Builds a conversation session on a topic, with no goal, plain fluency and an empty transcript.

parameters.name: pcTopic
parameters.role: the topic name, which also tags the source of every answer admitted

methods.name: Topic
methods.brief: Returns the topic the session was built with.

methods.name: SetGoal
methods.brief: Hands the session the one goal it is accountable for, and starts pursuing it.

parameters.name: poGoal
parameters.role: the stzGoal to pursue, such as StzGoalQ().RequireEach(dish, contains)

methods.returns: the conversation itself, so calls chain
notes: after a goal is revoked or fulfilled a new one may be set
warnings: raises an error for a value that is not a stzGoal and while another goal is still being pursued

methods.name: GoalQ
methods.brief: Returns the goal object the session is accountable for.
warnings: raises an error while no goal is set, so test HasGoal first

methods.name: HasGoal
methods.brief: TRUE if a goal was handed over.

methods.name: GoalState
methods.brief: Returns where the goal stands: none, pursuing, fulfilled or revoked.

methods.name: GoalWhy
methods.brief: Returns why the goal ended as it did.
methods.returns: a text; empty while none or pursuing

methods.name: IsPursuingGoal
methods.brief: TRUE if a goal is set and neither fulfilled nor revoked.

methods.name: IsGoalFulfilled
methods.brief: TRUE if no gap remains for the goal in the space.

methods.name: IsGoalRevoked
methods.brief: TRUE if the goal was abandoned on the record.

methods.name: RevokeGoal
methods.brief: Abandons the goal with a reason, clearing the pending question.

parameters.name: pcWhy
parameters.role: the reason, kept in GoalWhy and written to the transcript

methods.returns: the conversation itself, so calls chain
notes: a revoked goal asks nothing more and cannot be concluded
warnings: raises an error unless the goal is being pursued

methods.name: MonitorGoal
methods.brief: Re-reads the goal against the space and marks it fulfilled once no gap remains.

parameters.name: poSpace
parameters.role: the stzKnowledgeGraph the conversation runs in

methods.returns: a text, the goal state after the check
notes: NextQuestion and Reply call it themselves

methods.name: History
methods.brief: Returns the transcript lines, in order.
methods.returns: a list of [ speaker, text, certainty ] rows, speaker being system, user or verdict

methods.name: NumberOfTurns
methods.brief: Returns how many turns have passed: one for each question asked and each reply given.

methods.name: Gaps
methods.brief: Returns the facts the goal still lacks in the space.

parameters.name: poSpace
parameters.role: the stzKnowledgeGraph the conversation runs in

methods.returns: a list of [ subject, relation, why ] rows; [ ] when the goal is met
warnings: raises an error while no goal is set

methods.name: NextQuestion
methods.brief: Returns the next question, born from the first gap, and remembers it as the pending one.

parameters.name: poSpace
parameters.role: the stzKnowledgeGraph the conversation runs in

methods.returns: a text, the question with its reason; empty when the goal is fulfilled or revoked
notes: NextQuestionXT gives the same question as data: question, force, subject, relation, options and why
warnings: raises an error while no goal is set

extensions.name: NextQuestionXT
extensions.adds: the extended form: more parameters than the base method

methods.name: Options
methods.brief: Returns the values offered with the pending question.
methods.returns: a list of text; [ ] when the question is open
notes: values that the relation already takes elsewhere in the space become numbered options

methods.name: Force
methods.brief: Returns the kind of the pending question: which for a closed choice, what for an open one.
methods.returns: a text; empty when nothing is pending

methods.name: SetFluency
methods.brief: Chooses plain or neural wording of the questions.

parameters.name: pcMode
parameters.role: plain or neural, without regard to case

methods.returns: the conversation itself, so calls chain
notes: neural wording needs a generative model loaded; without one the plain wording is kept
warnings: raises an error for any other mode

methods.name: Fluency
methods.brief: Returns the fluency that was asked for.

methods.name: IsFluencyNeural
methods.brief: TRUE if neural wording was asked for and a generative model is really loaded.
notes: FALSE means the questions are on the deterministic floor

methods.name: Reply
methods.brief: Answers the pending question; each value passes the space governed admission, and refusals become checkpoints.

parameters.name: poSpace
parameters.role: the stzKnowledgeGraph that admits the values

parameters.name: pAnswer
parameters.role: a number or list of numbers that pick offered options, text such as X and Y, or a list of text

methods.returns: a hash-list [ :admitted, :refused, :narration, :goalState ]; :refused holds [ value, reason ] rows
notes: values are split at commas and the word and; one admitted value is enough to clear the pending question
warnings: raises an error when no question is pending; a number that matches no offered option is refused and checkpointed, not guessed

methods.name: Why
methods.brief: Returns the explanation of the last admission or refusal.
methods.returns: a text; empty before the first reply

methods.name: SetCheckpointTTL
methods.brief: Sets for how many turns a refusal checkpoint stays live.

parameters.name: nTurns
parameters.role: the number of turns, or 0 for never expiring

methods.returns: the conversation itself, so calls chain
notes: nothing is deleted; AllCheckpoints keeps the full record
warnings: raises an error for a negative number

methods.name: CheckpointTTL
methods.brief: Returns for how many turns a checkpoint stays live.
methods.returns: a number; 0 means it never expires

methods.name: Checkpoints
methods.brief: Returns the refusal checkpoints still live, which a human has yet to see.
methods.returns: a list of hash-lists with subject, relation, attempted, why and turn

methods.name: AllCheckpoints
methods.brief: Returns every refusal checkpoint ever raised, expired or not.
methods.returns: a list of hash-lists with subject, relation, attempted, why and turn

methods.name: NumberOfExpiredCheckpoints
methods.brief: Returns how many checkpoints have outlived the TTL.

methods.name: Conclude
methods.brief: Writes the finished knowledge space to a file, once the goal has no gap left.

parameters.name: poSpace
parameters.role: the stzKnowledgeGraph the session grew

parameters.name: pcKnowFile
parameters.role: the base path of the knowledge file, written as .zknw

warnings: raises an error while no goal is set, when the goal was revoked, and when gaps remain

methods.name: Save
methods.brief: Writes the topic and the transcript to a .zcnv file.

parameters.name: pcFile
parameters.role: the path to write

methods.returns: a text, the path written, with .zcnv added when missing
notes: the goal state and checkpoints are not written, and the class has no Load

methods.name: Transcript
methods.brief: Returns the transcript as dialogue text, SOFTANZA and YOU lines with each verdict under its answer.

extensions.name: TranscriptQ
extensions.adds: does what the method does, then returns the object, so the call can be chained

classes.name: stzCorpus
classes.brief: Holds a collection of texts and counts their words, scores texts with a bigram language model and ranks the terms of each document by TF-IDF.
classes.description: Your texts are the corpus: pass one text or a list of texts, each one a document, and nothing is downloaded. The counting itself runs in the Zig engine, built on the first question and kept up to date as documents are added; FreeModel releases it. Words are cut and lowercased by the engine with Unicode rules, so Hebrew, Arabic and emoji count like any other word. Documents are numbered from 1. A stzString or stzText is not needed to build one, and the corpus is the entry object of the corpora shelf of the linguistic domain.
classes.receiver: o1 = new stzCorpus([ "the fox jumps over the dog", "the dog sleeps", "שלום עולם שלום" ])
classes.example:
? o1.NumberOfDocuments()
#--> 3
? o1.FreqOf("the")
#--> 3
? o1.FreqOf("שלום")
#--> 2
? @@( o1.MostFrequent(1) )
#--> [ [ "the", 3 ] ]

methods.name: init
methods.brief: Builds a corpus from one text or a list of texts; empty and non-text entries are dropped without a message.

parameters.name: p
parameters.role: a text, or a list of texts, each one a document

notes: the engine model is not built here but at the first question

methods.name: AddDocument
methods.brief: Appends one text to the corpus as a new document, and feeds it to the engine model if that model already exists.

parameters.name: pcText
parameters.role: the text of the new document

notes: newlines in the text are turned into spaces when it reaches the model, so a document stays one document

extensions.name: AddDocumentQ
extensions.adds: does what the method does, then returns the object, so the call can be chained

methods.name: Documents
methods.brief: Returns the documents of the corpus as they were given, in order.
notes: documents are numbered from 1 in TfOf, TfIdfOf and TopTermsOf

methods.name: NumberOfDocuments
methods.brief: Returns how many documents the corpus holds.

methods.name: FreeModel
methods.brief: Frees the engine model of the corpus. The next question builds it again from all the documents.
notes: Ring has no destructors, so a program that is done with a large corpus calls it; nothing is lost, since the texts stay in the object

methods.name: FreeLm
methods.brief: Frees the engine model of the corpus, under the name the language model part of this class used to have.

methods.name: NumberOfWords
methods.brief: Returns how many words, repeats included, the whole corpus has.
notes: words are cut and lowercased by the engine, with Unicode rules

methods.name: Vocabulary
methods.brief: Returns every distinct word of the corpus, lowercased.
methods.returns: a list of texts, in no particular order
notes: for the words by rank use MostFrequent

methods.name: VocabularySize
methods.brief: Returns how many distinct words the corpus has.

methods.name: FreqOf
methods.brief: Returns how many times a word occurs in the whole corpus, ignoring case; 0 when it is absent.

parameters.name: pcWord
parameters.role: the word to count

notes: counted in every document together; for one document use TfOf

methods.name: MostFrequent
methods.brief: Returns the n commonest words with their counts, the highest first.

parameters.name: n
parameters.role: how many words to return

methods.returns: a list of [ word, count ] pairs; [ ] when n is 0
notes: words with equal counts come in no fixed order

methods.name: BigramProbability
methods.brief: Returns the chance that pcW2 follows pcW1 in this corpus, smoothed so that a pair never seen still gets a small chance.

parameters.name: pcW1
parameters.role: the first word of the pair

parameters.name: pcW2
parameters.role: the word that should follow it

notes: the smoothing is Laplace: (count of the pair + 1) / (count of pcW1 + vocabulary size)

methods.name: LogProbability
methods.brief: Returns the natural logarithm of the chance of a whole text under the bigram model; it is 0 or negative, and nearer 0 means likelier.

parameters.name: pcText
parameters.role: the text to score

methods.name: Perplexity
methods.brief: Returns how surprising a text is to the corpus, as exp of minus the average log chance per word pair; lower means more like the corpus.

parameters.name: pcText
parameters.role: the text to score

methods.returns: a number, 1 or more; 0 when the text has fewer than two words
notes: a text of 0 or 1 word answers 0, which reads as the best score and means no score

methods.name: NumberOfDocumentsWith
methods.brief: Returns in how many documents a word occurs at least once (its document frequency).

parameters.name: pcWord
parameters.role: the word to look for

methods.name: TfOf
methods.brief: Returns how many times a word occurs in one document, counted from 1.

parameters.name: pcWord
parameters.role: the word to count

parameters.name: nDoc
parameters.role: the document number, from 1

methods.returns: a number; 0 when the word is absent or the document number is out of range
notes: a document number that does not exist (0 or too large) answers 0 and raises nothing

methods.name: IdfOf
methods.brief: Returns the smoothed inverse document frequency of a word: log of (1 + documents) / (1 + documents holding it), plus 1.

parameters.name: pcWord
parameters.role: the word whose rarity is asked

methods.returns: a number; the largest for a word that is in no document

methods.name: TfIdfOf
methods.brief: Returns the weight of a word in one document: its count there times its inverse document frequency.

parameters.name: pcWord
parameters.role: the word to weigh

parameters.name: nDoc
parameters.role: the document number, from 1

methods.name: TopTermsOf
methods.brief: Returns the n most distinctive words of one document, the highest TF-IDF weight first.

parameters.name: nDoc
parameters.role: the document number, from 1

parameters.name: n
parameters.role: how many words to return

methods.returns: a list of [ word, weight ] pairs; [ ] when the document number does not exist
notes: fewer than n pairs when the document has fewer distinct words

classes.name: stzCounter
classes.brief: Counts in cycles: it starts at a number, steps by a number, and starts over when a limit is reached or after a number of values.
classes.description: Give it a hashlist of options and ask for the first N numbers. :WhenYouReach names the value at which the count restarts, :AfterYouSkip names how many values to skip before it restarts, and :RestartAt is the value it restarts from. The options :StartAt and :Step alone are not enough today: without one of the two cycle options every number comes out as 0.

methods.name: init
methods.brief: Builds a cyclic counter from a hashlist of options that say where to start, how far to step and when to start over.

parameters.name: paParams
parameters.role: a hashlist with any of :StartAt, :Step, :WhenYouReach, :AfterYouSkip and :RestartAt, for example [ :StartAt = 1, :WhenYouReach = 4, :RestartAt = 0 ]

methods.name: Counting
methods.brief: Returns the first N numbers the counter produces, as a list, restarting at RestartAt each time a cycle ends.

parameters.name: _nNumber_
parameters.role: how many numbers to produce, or [ :To = n ]

notes: with :WhenYouReach = 4 and :RestartAt = 0 the count runs 1, 2, 3, 0, 1, 2, 3, 0; with :AfterYouSkip = 2 it runs 1, 2, 0, 1, 2, 0
warnings: without :WhenYouReach or :AfterYouSkip every number is 0 today, whatever :StartAt and :Step say (checked with three different option sets)

classes.name: stzCountry
classes.brief: Holds one country of the world and answers its codes, languages, scripts and currency.
classes.description: Build it from any identifier the library knows: a name such as Niger, a two- or three-letter code, a number, a phone code or a language name. The names are lowercase English, the codes uppercase. The currency questions come from the country row, and the symbol, the abbreviation and the native currency name from the country's locale. NativeName raises an error today (it calls a function that does not exist), and Script and ScriptNumber answer only for a country whose default language has a script row of the same name. The Engine methods read the engine's reference table directly.
classes.example:
? @@( o1.Name() )
#--> "niger"
? @@( o1.ShortAbbreviation() )
#--> "NE"
? @@( o1.PhoneCode() )
#--> "+227"
? @@( o1.DefaultLanguage() )
#--> "french"
? @@( o1.Languages() )
#--> [ "zarma", "tasawaq" ]
? @@( o1.CurrencyAbbreviation() )
#--> "XOF"
? o1.CurrencyBase()
#--> 100
? @@( o1.EngineField("alpha3") )
#--> "NER"

classes.name: stzCourse
classes.brief: Holds one course of a program as a path through its chapters, and answers what a learner or a teacher asks of it.
classes.description: A learner opens a chapter in a language (ChapterQ) or runs it (RunChapterQ); a teacher asks what a chapter needs first (Prerequisites), what it trains (Trains), where a name is first taught (TeachesWhere) and which planned chapters have no text yet (UnwrittenChapterIds). The course is made of two manifests: course.zknw says what ships, in order, and curriculum.zknw says what is planned, with its trains and requires facts; an overlay's course.zknw is merged into the core's, never shadowing it. A course is taken from a program with CourseQ and holds a COPY of that program, so the overlay and the world must be set before. A chapter with no text in a language raises an error, never a quiet fallback to English. LIMITS, stated where you meet them: the translations (fr, ar, ha) are drafts, 0 of 35 units of each reviewed by a person when this was written; the cells of a chapter run on the desktop only, not in a browser, and the Run methods start Ring processes whose executable path must not contain a space; no institution has adopted the system.
classes.example:
? o1.TitleOf("find-then-apply", "fr")
#--> Trouver, puis agir
? @@( o1.Prerequisites("say-it-in-your-language") )
#--> [ "read-the-name-as-a-sentence", "a-first-sentence", "find-then-apply" ]
? o1.TeachesWhere("FindDuplicates")
#--> find-then-apply
? @@( o1.Trains("find-then-apply") )
#--> [ "ex-01", "ex-02", "ex-03" ]

classes.name: stzCurrency
classes.brief: Holds the currency of one country, with its codes, its names and its fractional unit, read from the locale data.
classes.description: The object is built from a country name, spelled as the locale data spells it (lower case, with underscores for spaces), and answers the currency that country uses: its name, its three-letter code, its native symbol, its fractional unit and the number of those units in one. Because it starts from a country, the country stays exact even for a currency many countries share. Building it from a currency name, a symbol or a locale abbreviation is not supported today.
classes.example:
? o1.Currency()
#--> west_african_cfa_franc
? o1.ISOSymbol()
#--> XOF
? o1.FractionalUnit()
#--> Centime
? o1.CountryLocaleAbbreviation()
#--> fr-NE

methods.name: init
methods.brief: Builds a currency object from the name of a country, written as in the locale data: lower case with underscores.

parameters.name: pcCurrencyIdentifier
parameters.role: a country name such as niger or united_states

notes: spelling and case are free for a country that is in the data, so Niger and niger are the same
warnings: a currency name such as euro, a symbol such as XOF or a locale abbreviation such as fr-NE is not understood today: the currency-name test compares against country names, so the name is refused with error R3 (the error function stzCurrencyError is not loaded), and a locale abbreviation is accepted but builds an empty object whose Currency answers N

methods.name: ISOSymbol
methods.brief: Returns the international three-letter code of the currency, as the country's locale spells it.

methods.name: NativeSymbol
methods.brief: Returns the symbol the country's locale writes for the currency.
methods.returns: a text such as CFA or the pound sign

methods.name: Currency
methods.brief: Returns the currency's name in the library's spelling, lower case joined by underscores.

methods.name: NativeName
methods.brief: Returns the currency's name as the country's own locale words it, with spaces.
methods.returns: a text such as west african cfa franc

methods.name: Value
methods.brief: Returns the currency name, the value of the object.

methods.name: FractionalUnit
methods.brief: Returns the name of the currency's fractional unit.

methods.name: Base
methods.brief: Returns how many fractional units make one unit of the currency.

methods.name: Country
methods.brief: Returns the country the object was built from.
notes: a country name is exact; for a currency shared by many countries, such as the euro, this is why the object remembers the country it started from

methods.name: CountryLocaleAbbreviation
methods.brief: Returns the locale code of the country, language and region joined by a hyphen.

classes.name: stzCurrentSystem

classes.description: It is a stzSystemProfile filled at construction from the operating system, the environment, the engine's memory readings and the Ring version, with the role runtime. Compare it with stzDevSystem, which reads the same machine with the role development. Only reads are made; nothing on the machine changes.
classes.example:
? o1.Role()
#--> runtime
? o1.Name()
#--> this-machine

methods.name: init
methods.brief: Describes the machine this program runs on, filled live from the operating system, the engine's memory readings and the Ring version.
warnings: the role is runtime, the name is this-machine, and the capabilities are the defaults of the system class (windows, linux and macos give desktop)

classes.name: stzDatabase
classes.brief: Opens a SQLite database, a file or a store in memory, to run statements, read rows and keep transactions.
classes.description: Exec runs a statement and Rows reads a query, with every cell as text; the With forms bind their values to ? marks instead of splicing them into the text, which is the way to put user data in. TypedRowsWith returns numbers for numeric cells. Begin takes the write lock at once and Commit or Rollback ends the transaction. A failed call raises, and Why keeps the engine's last message. The engine does the work; this is the Ring face the application server and agents persist through.
classes.example:
o1.Exec("CREATE TABLE dish(name TEXT, price REAL)")
o1.ExecWith("INSERT INTO dish VALUES (?, ?)", [ "margherita", 8.5 ])
? o1.Rows("SELECT name, price FROM dish")[1][1]
#--> margherita
? o1.ValueWith("SELECT price FROM dish WHERE name = ?", [ "margherita" ])
#--> 8.5
? o1.TypedRowsWith("SELECT price FROM dish", [])[1][1] + 1
#--> 9.50

methods.name: init
methods.brief: Opens a SQLite database, a file path or :memory: for a store that lives only in this process, and raises if it can not be opened.

parameters.name: pcPath
parameters.role: the database file, or :memory:

methods.name: Path
methods.brief: Returns the path the database was opened with.

methods.name: IsOpen
methods.brief: TRUE if the database handle is still open, which Close ends.

methods.name: Why
methods.brief: Returns the text of the last error that a failed call recorded, such as the table that was not found.
methods.returns: a text; empty before any error
notes: after a failed Exec the text is the engine's bare message, after a failed query or bound call it starts with sql error:

methods.name: Exec
methods.brief: Runs one DDL or DML statement and returns how many rows it changed; raises on a SQL error.

parameters.name: pcSql
parameters.role: the statement text, with its values written in

notes: values spliced into the text are the caller's to escape; use ExecWith to bind them
warnings: raises SQL error: with the engine's message, for a malformed statement and on a closed database

methods.name: Rows
methods.brief: Returns the rows of a query, each as a list of cells that are all text, NULL being an empty text.

parameters.name: pcSql
parameters.role: the SELECT text

methods.returns: a list of rows; [ ] when the query matches nothing
notes: a REAL cell reads 9.5 or 10.0, as SQLite writes it
warnings: raises on a malformed query and on one that fails partway; a tab or a line break in a value stays inside its cell

methods.name: Value
methods.brief: Returns the first cell of the first row of a query, an empty text when there is none.

parameters.name: pcSql
parameters.role: the SELECT text

methods.name: ExecWith
methods.brief: Runs one statement whose ? marks are bound to the given values and returns how many rows it changed.

parameters.name: pcSql
parameters.role: the statement with ? marks

parameters.name: paParams
parameters.role: the values in order: a text binds as TEXT, a whole number as INTEGER, any other number as REAL

notes: no value can change what the statement says, and none needs escaping
warnings: raises when the count of values does not fit, with a message that always says the statement has -1 parameters, whatever its real count

methods.name: RowsWith
methods.brief: Returns the rows of a query whose ? marks are bound to the given values, every cell as text.

parameters.name: pcSql
parameters.role: the SELECT text with ? marks

parameters.name: paParams
parameters.role: the values in order, as for ExecWith

methods.returns: a list of rows of text cells
notes: a value such as x' OR '1'='1 matches nothing, being data
warnings: raises on a count mismatch with the same -1 message as ExecWith

methods.name: TypedRowsWith
methods.brief: Returns the rows of a bound query with INTEGER and REAL cells as Ring numbers and TEXT and NULL cells as text.

parameters.name: pcSql
parameters.role: the SELECT text with ? marks

parameters.name: paParams
parameters.role: the values in order

notes: a NULL still comes back as an empty text, not as a number

methods.name: ValueWith
methods.brief: Returns the first cell of the first row of a bound query, an empty text when there is none.

parameters.name: pcSql
parameters.role: the SELECT text with ? marks

parameters.name: paParams
parameters.role: the values in order

methods.name: Begin
methods.brief: Starts a transaction and takes the write lock at once, so a busy database refuses here.
methods.returns: the database itself, so calls chain
notes: one transaction at a time; there is no nesting
warnings: raises when a transaction is already open and on a closed database, with the engine's reason

methods.name: Commit
methods.brief: Makes the changes of the open transaction permanent.
methods.returns: the database itself, so calls chain
warnings: raises when no transaction is active

methods.name: Rollback
methods.brief: Undoes the changes of the open transaction.
methods.returns: the database itself, so calls chain

methods.name: LastInsertId
methods.brief: Returns the rowid of the last row inserted on this connection.
methods.returns: a number; 0 on a closed database

methods.name: Close
methods.brief: Closes the database; closing twice is harmless.
methods.returns: the database itself, so calls chain
warnings: after Close every query raises no such database handle

classes.name: stzDataSet
classes.brief: Holds a list of numbers or categories and answers descriptive, distribution, relation and quality questions about it, with rules that turn the figures into written insights.
classes.description: The data type is detected when the set is built (numeric, categorical, mixed or empty) and missing markers such as NA are dropped. Numeric statistics answer 0 for data that is not numeric, and the count-based ones need two to four values. The methods fall in groups: the descriptive ones (Mean, Median, Mode, spread, quartiles, Percentile), frequency and diversity for categories, shape and outliers (Skew, Kurtosis, Outliers, ZScores, TrendAnalysis), relation to a second data set given as an argument (CorrelationWith, RegressionCoefficients, ChiSquareWith, MutualInformation), scaling (Normalize, Standardize, RobustScale), and the insight layer: domain rules (AddInsightRule, InsightsOfDomain), plans (MakePlan, ExecutePlan) and Summary. The tables of rules and plan templates are global, shared by every data set of the process, and ExecutePlan and AdaptiveAnalysis print as they work. Known gaps today, each carried as a warning on its method: Percentile makes the engine panic for a percent below 0 or far above 100, WMean overflows the stack, NonParametricCorrelation and PlanSummary raise errors, and MutualInformation misreads values that contain an underscore.

methods.name: ClassName
methods.brief: Returns the name of the class, in lowercase.

methods.name: init
methods.brief: Builds a data set from a list, dropping missing markers such as NA or an empty text and detecting the data type; a non-list raises an error.

parameters.name: paData
parameters.role: the list of values, numbers or text or both

notes: the type is numeric, categorical, mixed or empty, and most statistics answer 0 unless it is numeric

methods.name: Mean
methods.brief: Returns the arithmetic mean of the values, or 0 when the data is not entirely numeric.
methods.returns: a number; 0 for non-numeric or empty data

methods.name: Median
methods.brief: Returns the middle value of the sorted data, or the average of the two middle ones when the count is even.
methods.returns: a number; 0 for non-numeric or empty data

methods.name: Mode
methods.brief: Returns the most frequent value, as text; the first value to reach the top count wins a tie.
methods.returns: text, a number kept as text such as "4"; "" for empty data
notes: it also works on categorical data

methods.name: StandardDeviation
methods.brief: Returns the sample standard deviation, dividing by n minus 1.
methods.returns: a number; 0 for non-numeric data or fewer than two values
notes: StdDev is another name

methods.name: StandardDeviationSample
methods.brief: Returns the sample standard deviation, dividing by n minus 1, the library default named outright.
methods.returns: a number; 0 for non-numeric data or fewer than two values

methods.name: StandardDeviationPopulation
methods.brief: Returns the population standard deviation, dividing by n, as the square root of the population variance.
methods.returns: a number; 0 for non-numeric or empty data

methods.name: Variance
methods.brief: Returns the sample variance, dividing by n minus 1.
methods.returns: a number; 0 for non-numeric data or fewer than two values

methods.name: VarianceSample
methods.brief: Returns the sample variance, dividing by n minus 1, the library default named outright.
methods.returns: a number; 0 for non-numeric data or fewer than two values

methods.name: VariancePopulation
methods.brief: Returns the population variance, dividing by n.
methods.returns: a number; 0 for non-numeric or empty data

methods.name: Range
methods.brief: Returns the largest value minus the smallest.
methods.returns: a number; 0 for non-numeric or empty data

methods.name: Min
methods.brief: Returns the smallest value.
methods.returns: a number; "" for non-numeric or empty data

methods.name: Max
methods.brief: Returns the largest value.
methods.returns: a number; "" for non-numeric or empty data

methods.name: Sum
methods.brief: Returns the total of the values.

methods.name: Count
methods.brief: Returns how many values the data set holds, after the missing ones were dropped.

methods.name: GeometricMean
methods.brief: Returns the geometric mean, the nth root of the product of the values.
methods.returns: a number; 0 for non-numeric or empty data, or when any value is 0 or negative

methods.name: HarmonicMean
methods.brief: Returns the harmonic mean, the count divided by the sum of the inverses.
methods.returns: a number; 0 for non-numeric or empty data, or when any value is 0

methods.name: CoefficientOfVariation
methods.brief: Returns the sample standard deviation as a percentage of the absolute mean.
methods.returns: a number in percent; 0 for non-numeric data or a mean of 0

methods.name: CompareWith
methods.brief: Compares this data set with another and returns sentences on mean, variability and correlation, or on diversity for categories.

parameters.name: _oOtherStats_
parameters.role: the stzDataSet to compare with

methods.returns: a list of text; the text "Cannot compare with empty dataset" when either is empty
notes: the correlation sentence appears only for equal lengths and a correlation above 0.7 in size

methods.name: Compare
methods.brief: Compares this data set with another, given alone or as [ "with", other ]; the same answer as the comparing call.

parameters.name: _oOtherStats_
parameters.role: the stzDataSet to compare with, or [ "with", dataset ]

methods.name: SimilarityScore
methods.brief: Returns how alike two data sets are from 0 to 1: by mean and spread for numbers, by shared values for categories.

parameters.name: _oOtherStats_
parameters.role: the stzDataSet to compare with

methods.returns: a number from 0 to 1; 0 when the types differ or one is empty
notes: a non-object raises error R13

methods.name: SimScoreWith
methods.brief: Returns how alike two data sets are from 0 to 1; another spelling of the similarity score.

parameters.name: _oOtherStats_
parameters.role: the stzDataSet to compare with

methods.name: ConfidenceInterval
methods.brief: Returns the Student t confidence interval for the mean, as [ low, high ].

parameters.name: _nConfidence_
parameters.role: the level in percent, above 0 and below 100

methods.returns: a list of two numbers; [ 0, 0 ] with fewer than two numbers
notes: a level of 100 raises an error; the XT form adds the critical value and the degrees of freedom

extensions.name: ConfidenceIntervalXT
extensions.adds: the extended form: more parameters than the base method

methods.name: ConfInt
methods.brief: Returns the 95 percent Student t confidence interval for the mean, as [ low, high ].
methods.returns: a list of two numbers; [ 0, 0 ] with fewer than two numbers

methods.name: WeightedMean
methods.brief: Returns the mean of the values, each counted as often as its weight says.

parameters.name: aWeights
parameters.role: a list of weights, one per value

methods.returns: a number; 0 for non-numeric data or when the weights add up to 0
warnings: raises an error when the number of weights differs from the number of values

methods.name: TrimmedMean
methods.brief: Returns the mean after dropping a share of the smallest and of the largest values.

parameters.name: nTrimPercent
parameters.role: the percentage cut from each end, from 0 up to but below 50

methods.returns: a number; 0 for non-numeric or empty data
warnings: a value outside that range raises an error

methods.name: PercentileRank
methods.brief: Returns the percentage of values below a value, counting half of those equal to it.

parameters.name: nValue
parameters.role: the value to place in the data

methods.returns: a number from 0 to 100; 0 for non-numeric or empty data

methods.name: FrequencyTable
methods.brief: Returns how often each value occurs, as [ value, count ] pairs where the value is kept as text.

methods.name: RelativeFrequency
methods.brief: Returns the share of each value, from 0 to 1, as [ value, share ] pairs.

methods.name: PercentageFrequency
methods.brief: Returns the share of each value, in percent, as [ value, percent ] pairs.

methods.name: UniqueCount
methods.brief: Returns how many distinct values the data holds.

methods.name: UCount
methods.brief: Returns how many distinct values the data holds; another spelling of the count.

methods.name: UniqueValues
methods.brief: Returns the distinct values, in the order they first appear.

methods.name: Diversity
methods.brief: Returns the distinct values divided by all values, from 0 up to 1.

methods.name: EntropyIndex
methods.brief: Returns the Shannon entropy of the value frequencies, in bits.

methods.name: ContingencyTable
methods.brief: Counts how often each value of this set meets each value of another set of the same length.

parameters.name: oOtherDataSet
parameters.role: the stzDataSet to cross with

methods.returns: a list [ the distinct values of the other set, a list of [ value, counts ] rows ]
warnings: a non-object or a set of another length raises an error

methods.name: ModeCount
methods.brief: Returns how many times the most frequent value occurs.

methods.name: Percentile
methods.brief: Returns the value at a percentile of the sorted data, interpolating linearly between neighbours.

parameters.name: nPercent
parameters.role: the percentile, from 0 to 100

methods.returns: a number; 0 for non-numeric or empty data
notes: PercentileXT takes the same percent and clamps it
warnings: a percent that is not a number from 0 to 100 raises an error

extensions.name: PercentileXT
extensions.adds: the extended form: more parameters than the base method

methods.name: Q1
methods.brief: Returns the first quartile, the 25th percentile.
methods.returns: a number; 0 for non-numeric or empty data

extensions.name: Q1XT
extensions.adds: the extended form: more parameters than the base method

methods.name: Q2
methods.brief: Returns the second quartile, which is the median.
methods.returns: a number; 0 for non-numeric or empty data

extensions.name: Q2XT
extensions.adds: the extended form: more parameters than the base method

methods.name: Q3
methods.brief: Returns the third quartile, the 75th percentile.
methods.returns: a number; 0 for non-numeric or empty data

extensions.name: Q3XT
extensions.adds: the extended form: more parameters than the base method

methods.name: IQR
methods.brief: Returns the interquartile range, the third quartile minus the first.
methods.returns: a number; 0 for non-numeric or empty data

extensions.name: IQRXT
extensions.adds: the extended form: more parameters than the base method

methods.name: Quartiles
methods.brief: Returns the three quartiles as [ Q1, Q2, Q3 ].

extensions.name: QuartilesXT
extensions.adds: the extended form: more parameters than the base method

methods.name: Skew
methods.brief: Returns the sample-adjusted skewness: positive when the long tail is on the right.
methods.returns: a number; 0 for non-numeric data, fewer than three values or no spread

methods.name: Skewness
methods.brief: Returns the sample-adjusted skewness; another spelling of the skewness call.
methods.returns: a number; 0 for non-numeric data, fewer than three values or no spread

methods.name: Kurtosis
methods.brief: Returns the excess kurtosis, which is 0 for a normal distribution.
methods.returns: a number; 0 for non-numeric data, fewer than four values or no spread

methods.name: Kurtos
methods.brief: Returns the excess kurtosis; another spelling of the kurtosis call.
methods.returns: a number; 0 for non-numeric data, fewer than four values or no spread

methods.name: ContainsOutliers
methods.brief: TRUE if some value lies beyond 1.5 interquartile ranges from the quartiles.

methods.name: Outliers
methods.brief: Returns the values that lie beyond 1.5 interquartile ranges below the first or above the third quartile.
methods.returns: a list; [ ] for non-numeric data or when there is none

methods.name: IsOutlier
methods.brief: TRUE if the value is one of the outliers of the data.

parameters.name: nValue
parameters.role: the value to look for among the outliers

classes.name: stzDataWrangler
classes.brief: Cleans, checks and reshapes a list or a table of values step by step, and keeps a log of what it did.
classes.description: Give it a flat list or a table (a list of rows, with the column names). The operations change the data in place and answer how many values they touched: RemoveDuplicates, HandleMissingValues, TrimWhitespace, NormalizeCase, ConvertDataTypes, NormalizeNumeric and EncodeCategories. The checks, ValidateRanges, DetectOutliers and ValidateDataTypes, report problems and record them as issues. ExecutePlan, QuickClean and the other Quick methods run a whole plan of steps at once, and GetData returns the result. Several things fail today on a table that holds text: ValidateDataTypes, GetDataProfile and ShowReport raise, the analysis plan does not resolve, and the export plan reports errors; each method says so in its own warning.
classes.example:
? o1.RemoveDuplicates()
#--> 1
? @@( o1.ValidateRanges([ [ "age", 0, 30 ] ]) )
#--> [ "Row 1, age: 31 outside range [0, 30]" ]
? o1.NormalizeCase("upper")
#--> 2
? o1.NormalizeNumeric("minmax")
#--> 2
? @@( o1.GetData() )
#--> [ [ "ANN", 1 ], [ "BOB", 0 ] ]
? @@( o1.GetHeaders() )
#--> [ "name", "age" ]
? @@( o1.GetIssues()[1][:type] )
#--> "range_violation"

classes.name: stzDate
classes.brief: Holds one calendar date (year, month, day) with no time of day, moves it by days, months or years, compares it and writes it in several formats.
classes.description: A stzDate is three numbers. Build it from a text (2026-03-15, 15/03/2026, 15.03.2026, 15032026, today, in 3 days), from a list [ 2026, 3, 15 ], from a hash with :Year, :Month and :Day, or from an empty text for today. A text with a 4-digit first part is read year-first, any other text day- first, so 03/15/2026 raises. The Add and Subtract methods move the object itself and return nothing (the Q forms answer the object so calls chain); the Next, Previous, Start and End methods answer a text in dd/MM/yyyy and leave the object alone (their Q forms answer a copy). Measure with DaysTo, WeeksTo, MonthsTo and YearsTo, compare with IsBefore, IsAfter, IsEqualTo and IsBetween, and write it with ToString (dd/MM/yyyy), ToISO8601, ToAmerican, ToLong or ToStringXT with a format such as yyyy-MM-dd. Dates before 1970 work, because the engine counts civil days and not Unix seconds. Today follows StzFreezeClock, so a test can pin it. Known gaps today, each carried as a warning on its method: MonthsTo, YearsTo, IsSameWeek, IsSameMonth, IsSameYear and IsBetween raise for anything but a stzDate object; DaysTo and the Is comparisons overwrite a list or hash variable of the caller; PreviousWeekday answers a Saturday from a Sunday; Age counts year numbers only; a language given with a capital (French) falls back to English; a list or hash given to the constructor is not validated.

methods.name: init
methods.brief: Builds the date from a date text, a [ year, month, day ] list, a hash with :Year, :Month and :Day, or today when the text is empty.

parameters.name: pcDate
parameters.role: a date text such as 2026-03-15 or 15/03/2026, the words today, yesterday or tomorrow, a phrase such as in 3 days, a list [ 2026, 3, 15 ], or a hash [ :Year = 2026, :Month = 3, :Day = 15 ]

notes: text with 4 digits first is read year-first (yyyy-MM-dd, yyyy/M/d), otherwise day-first (dd/MM/yyyy, dd.MM.yyyy, ddMMyyyy); an empty text is today and follows StzFreezeClock; dates before 1970 are fine here, unlike stzDateTime
warnings: a text is checked (2026-02-30 raises Invalid date provided!) but a list or hash is not (13 as month is stored and IsValid answers FALSE); text with the month first such as 03/15/2026 is read day-first and raises; a number, or a list that is not 3 numbers, raises Can't create the stzDate object; a two- digit year (15-03-26) raises R41; a phrase with a unit other than day, week, month, year, decade or century leaves the date empty without an error

classes.name: stzDateTime
classes.brief: Holds one date and time, to the millisecond, and adds to it, compares it, measures distances from it and writes it in many formats.
classes.description: A stzDateTime is made of seven numbers (year, month, day, hour, minute, second, millisecond) that read as one instant with no time zone: ToUTC and ToLocalTime change nothing. Build it from a text (2026-03-15 14:30:00, 15/03/2026 2:30 PM, an ISO text with a T), from a number of seconds since 1970, from a hash of parts, or from an empty text for the current clock. The Add and Subtract methods move the object itself and answer the new text; the Q forms answer the object so calls chain. Compare with IsBefore, IsAfter, IsEqualTo and IsBetween; measure with the DurationTo family (against another datetime) and the DurationSince family (against a named origin such as :UnixEpoch or :YearOne). The To... methods write it as text: ToIso for storage, ToStandard and ToAmerican for display, ToHuman and ToRelative in words. Instants before 1970 and origins such as :YearOne are read as dates like any other.

classes.name: stzDecimalToBinary
classes.brief: Converts a decimal number, given as text, into its binary form such as 0b1010.101.
classes.description: It is the converter behind ToBinaryForm of stzNumber. Build one with new stzDecimalToBinary("10.625") or StzDecimalToBinary("10.625"); the number must be a text, and a number or a text that is not a decimal raises an error. The integer part is converted through the engine and the fractional part by repeated doubling, cut at 19 binary digits. A negative number is converted as its positive twin with a minus sign in front. StzBinaryNumber hands the result to a stzBinaryNumber.
classes.example:
? o1.ToBinaryForm()
#--> 0b1010.101
? o1.IntegerPartToBinaryForm()
#--> 1010
? o1.FractionalPartToBinaryForm()
#--> 101

methods.name: init
methods.brief: Builds a converter from a decimal number written as text, such as "10.625".

parameters.name: cNumber
parameters.role: the decimal number as a text

notes: negative numbers are converted as the positive number with a minus sign in front, not in two's complement
warnings: the number must be passed as a text: new stzDecimalToBinary("5"), not 5

methods.name: ToStzNumber
methods.brief: Returns the decimal number as a stzNumber.

methods.name: ToStzString
methods.brief: Returns the decimal number as a stzString, the text it was given.

methods.name: StzBinaryNumber
methods.brief: Returns the binary form of the number as a stzBinaryNumber.

methods.name: ToBinaryForm
methods.brief: Returns the number in binary, with the 0b prefix: 0b1010.101 for 10.625, 0b-110.1 for -6.5.
notes: a fraction is cut at 19 binary digits, so 0.1 gives 0b0.0001100110011001100

methods.name: IntegerPartToBinaryForm
methods.brief: Returns the binary digits of the integer part, with a minus sign for a negative number, and an empty text when that part is 0.
methods.returns: a text of 0 and 1; "" when the integer part is 0
notes: 0.625 and -0.625 give "" here, while ToBinaryForm writes the 0 back

methods.name: FractionalPartToBinaryForm
methods.brief: Returns the binary digits of the part after the decimal point, at most 19 of them.
methods.returns: a text of 0 and 1; "0" for a whole number
notes: the sign is not included, 0.625 and -0.625 both give 101

classes.name: stzDecisionTree
classes.brief: Learns a decision tree over categorical features by ID3 and explains each answer as the path it followed.
classes.description: The tree splits on the feature with the greatest information gain and ends in the majority label. It is the most explainable learner of the module: Why narrates the exact path of the last classification, and ToGraph returns the tree as a real stzGraph that the rest of the library can query. Feature values compare without regard to case. A value never seen during training falls to the majority label of the node it reached, and Why says so. The build runs in the engine; the choices are deterministic, with the first feature to reach the highest gain winning a tie. Numeric features are treated as categories, so each distinct number is its own value.
classes.example:
o1.SetFeatureNames([ "outlook", "humidity" ])
o1.Train()
? o1.Classify([ "sunny", "high" ])
#--> no
? o1.Why()
#--> humidity='high' -> outlook='sunny' -> 'no'
? o1.Classify([ "Rainy", "normal" ])
#--> yes

methods.name: init
methods.brief: Builds an untrained decision tree over a training set of categorical features.

parameters.name: poTrainingSet
parameters.role: a stzTrainingSet

methods.name: TrainingSetQ
methods.brief: Returns the training set the tree holds, the one to grow if more examples are wanted.
warnings: growing the set you passed to the constructor does not reach the tree, because it keeps a copy; grow it here and call Train again

methods.name: SetFeatureNames
methods.brief: Sets a name for each feature, so that Why and ToGraph can speak of outlook instead of f1.

parameters.name: pacNames
parameters.role: a list of text, one name per feature in the order of the examples

methods.returns: the tree itself, so calls chain
notes: an unnamed feature is called f1, f2 and so on

methods.name: Train
methods.brief: Builds the tree by ID3, choosing at each node the feature with the greatest information gain; the build runs in the engine.
methods.returns: the tree itself, so calls chain
notes: values compare without regard to case; calling it again rebuilds the tree from the set
warnings: raises an error for an empty set, for examples with no features, and for an example whose width differs from the first one, naming it

methods.name: Tree
methods.brief: Returns the learned tree as nested lists: [ :feature, :branches, :default ] for a decision and [ :leaf ] for an answer.
methods.returns: a nested list; :feature is the position of the feature, :branches a list of [ value, subtree ] pairs, :default the majority label
notes: an untrained tree answers an empty list

methods.name: Classify
methods.brief: Returns the label the tree gives to a feature list, and keeps the path it followed for Why.

parameters.name: paFeatures
parameters.role: the feature values, in the order of the training examples

notes: values compare without regard to case
warnings: raises an error telling to call Train first; a value never seen at a node falls to that node's majority label, which Why says

methods.name: Why
methods.brief: Returns the path of the last classification as text, such as humidity='high' -> outlook='sunny' -> 'no'.
methods.returns: a text; empty before the first Classify
notes: an unseen value is marked in the path with unseen value and the default it fell to

methods.name: ToGraph
methods.brief: Returns the learned tree as a real graph of decision nodes, value edges and leaf nodes.
methods.returns: a stzGraph; nodes n1, n2 and so on, each with a kind (decision or leaf) and a label
notes: the graph can be queried like any other graph
warnings: raises an error telling to call Train first

classes.name: stzDeclaredLLMAgent
classes.brief: An llm agent that came from a declaration: it proposes structured facts into its own memory and can cause no effect.
classes.description: On a tick it reads its input from memory, asks its model function for an answer in the declared structure and learns the fields as facts under the declared subject. It holds no effectful capability. An answer that does not satisfy the structure lands nothing. Seed the answer with SeedProposal to run it without a model; with no seed and no loaded model the tick is refused and WhyLastTick says so.
classes.receiver: o1 = new stzDeclaredLLMAgent("summarizer") o1.SetDeclared("proposes a topic", "reversible")
classes.example:
? o1.CoverageStatement()
#--> proposes a topic
? o1.Cycle()
#--> 0
? o1.WhyLastTick()
#--> no proposal is declared
? o1.ProposalsMade()
#--> 0

methods.name: SetDeclared
methods.brief: Gives the agent the two answers the engine loop asks of every agent: what it covers and how reversible its work is.

parameters.name: pcCoverage
parameters.role: one sentence saying what the agent covers

parameters.name: pcReversibility
parameters.role: reversible, compensable or irreversible

methods.returns: the agent itself, so calls chain
warnings: neither value is checked here: the declaration court does it

methods.name: CoverageStatement
methods.brief: Returns the sentence saying what the agent covers.
methods.returns: a text; the empty text before SetDeclared

methods.name: ReversibilityClass
methods.brief: Returns the reversibility class given to the agent.
methods.returns: a text; the empty text before SetDeclared

methods.name: SetProposal
methods.brief: Gives the agent what it proposes and builds the model function that will answer; no model is called.

parameters.name: paProposes
parameters.role: the proposal list of a declaration, as Proposes of stzAgentDeclaration returns it

methods.returns: the agent itself, so calls chain
warnings: paProposes holds the prompt, the input clause, the target subject, the structure and the limits; a later tick with no seed and no loaded model is refused

methods.name: SeedProposal
methods.brief: Seeds the answer the agent's function will give for an input, so a tick needs no model.

parameters.name: pcInput
parameters.role: the text the input clause will produce

parameters.name: pValue
parameters.role: the answer, as "field: value" lines that satisfy the declared structure

methods.returns: the agent itself, so calls chain
notes: it seeds the agent's own function, which is the one that ticks
warnings: raises an error before the proposal is declared, and for an answer that does not satisfy the declared structure

methods.name: FunctionQ
methods.brief: Returns the model function the agent asks, or the empty text before SetProposal.
methods.returns: a stzLLMFunction object, or the empty text
warnings: a copy taken from it is not the agent's own function: seed through SeedProposal instead

methods.name: ProposalsMade
methods.brief: Returns how many ticks made a proposal that was validated.

methods.name: WhyLastTick
methods.brief: Returns, in words, what the last tick did or why it did nothing.
methods.returns: a text; the empty text before any tick
notes: the texts include "no proposal is declared", "nothing to propose about", "the proposal was REFUSED" and "proposed n field(s)"

methods.name: Cycle
methods.brief: Runs one tick: reads the input from memory, asks the function for a structured answer and learns its fields as facts.
methods.returns: 1 (TRUE) when a proposal was made and validated; 0 otherwise, and WhyLastTick says why
notes: the facts land as [ target subject, field, value ]
warnings: with no seeded answer and no loaded model the tick returns 0 and the refusal is in WhyLastTick; the agent writes only into its own memory and never causes an effect

classes.name: stzDeclaredPIAgent
classes.brief: A pi agent that came from a declaration, which also answers for its coverage and reversibility class.
classes.description: It adds only the two answers the engine loop's registration asks of every agent, so a declared agent needs no separate declaration on a host. Everything else, the tick, the governance gate and the trace, is the stzPIAgent runtime. A pi agent acts: it holds the effectful capability.

#--> watches stock
? o1.ReversibilityClass()

classes.name: stzDeclaredSkill
classes.brief: Holds a skill read from a declaration as three data clauses and runs them against an agent memory.
classes.description: A closure cannot be read out of a file, so this skill keeps its when, does and verify clauses as lists of a verb and its arguments and interprets them. Apply checks the precondition, performs the action on the memory it is given and verifies the result, answering a list that says whether it ran and whether it verified.
classes.receiver: m = new stzAgentMemory("demo") m.Learn("stock", "level", "low") o1 = new stzDeclaredSkill("restock") o1.SetClauses([ :verb = "fact", :args = [ "stock", "level", "low" ] ], [ :verb = "learn", :args = [ "stock", "level", "ordered" ] ], [ :verb = "fact", :args = [ "stock", "level", "ordered" ] ])
classes.example:
? o1.PreconditionHolds(m)
#--> 1
? o1.Apply(m)[:why]

classes.name: stzDeepList
classes.brief: Navigates a nested list by paths: lists every location, finds an item wherever it hides, and reads the item at a path.
classes.description: A path is a list of 1-based positions that locates an item: [2,3,1] is the 1st item of the 3rd item of the 2nd item. stzDeepList is a stzList, so every list method is still there; this subclass adds the path vocabulary, and the recursive work runs in the Zig engine. Build one with new stzDeepList(aList) or DeepListQ(aList). The path utilities that do not need a list (IsSubPathOf, CommonPath, SortPaths) are globals in stzListPaths.ring.

methods.name: Paths
methods.brief: Returns the path of every item in the nested list, parents before their children, as lists of 1-based positions.
methods.returns: a list of paths; [ ] for an empty list
notes: a sublist is itself an item, so [2] and [2,1] are both listed

methods.name: DeepFind
methods.brief: Returns the paths of every item equal to the given one, at any depth.

parameters.name: pItem
parameters.role: the item to look for, a text, a number or a list

methods.returns: a list of paths; [ ] when the item is absent
notes: the comparison is case-sensitive: "X" does not find "x"; a sublist is found as a whole, as an item of its parent

methods.name: DeepContains
methods.brief: TRUE if the item occurs anywhere in the nested list, at any depth.

parameters.name: pItem
parameters.role: the item to look for

methods.name: DeepFindAt
methods.brief: Returns the path back if the item at that path equals the given item, and [ ] when it does not or when the path does not exist.

parameters.name: pItem
parameters.role: the item expected at the path

parameters.name: paPath
parameters.role: the path to test, as 1-based positions

methods.returns: the path when the item is there, else [ ]

methods.name: ItemAtPath
methods.brief: Returns the item found by following a path of 1-based positions down the nested list.

parameters.name: paPath
parameters.role: the path, such as [2,3,1] for the 1st item of the 3rd item of the 2nd item

methods.returns: the item; a list when the path ends on a sublist
warnings: an unreachable path (a position past the end, 0, or a step below a plain item) raises "Invalid path! it goes deeper than the structure."; a path that is not a list raises "Incorrect param!"

methods.name: ItemsAtPaths
methods.brief: Returns the items at several paths at once, in the order of the paths, leaving out the paths that lead nowhere.

parameters.name: paPaths
parameters.role: a list of paths, each a list of 1-based positions

notes: unlike ItemAtPath it never raises: a bad path is skipped silently, so the answer can be shorter than the list of paths

methods.name: LongestPaths
methods.brief: Returns the paths that go deepest into the nested list, all of the same length.
methods.returns: a list of paths; [ ] for an empty list

methods.name: PathsAtDepth
methods.brief: Returns the paths of exactly the given depth, a path of one position being depth 1.

parameters.name: nDepth
parameters.role: the number of positions in the paths wanted

methods.returns: a list of paths; [ ] when the depth is 0 or deeper than the list

methods.name: ExpandPath
methods.brief: Returns the given path followed by the paths of everything beneath it, as a list of paths.

parameters.name: paPath
parameters.role: the path of the item to open up

methods.returns: a list of paths; just the given path when it is a plain item
notes: a path that does not exist answers itself unchecked, as the only path of the list

methods.name: CollapsePath
methods.brief: Returns the one-position path of the top-level item that contains the given path.

parameters.name: paPath
parameters.role: a path of any depth

methods.returns: a list holding the first position; [ ] for an empty path

classes.name: stzDelivery
classes.brief: Plans where each part of a solution runs and what each ships, before a byte is built, by reasoning from the target platform of each part.
classes.description: You describe the solution: its parts, the target of each (a server, a phone, a browser, a microcontroller) and the Softanza capabilities each uses. Plan rehearses the placement: per capability and target it picks a delivery vector, native, engine, construct or server, says why, and sizes the on-device engine. The same capability lands differently per target, so the target platform is the invisible frame the planner makes visible. UseServices adds the external dependencies and the credentials production will need, and Deploy commits the plan: it is refused while a service is still bound to a fake, and an actor that is not effectful only gets a rehearsal. Read Plan freely; Deploy builds and, in production, launches for real.
classes.example:
o1.AddBackend("api", "LinuxServer").AddSuperApp("phone", "Android")
o1.NeedsIn("phone", [ :Unicode, :PivotTable, :Neural ])
? o1.NumberOfParts()
#--> 2
? o1.Plan().VectorFor("phone", "PivotTable")
#--> engine
? o1.Plan().VectorFor("phone", "Neural")
#--> server

classes.name: stzDeployment
classes.brief: Sends each part of a delivery plan to its site, stores it, launches it and reports back, all governed by the actor's authority.
classes.description: Bind parts to stzDeploymentSite objects with SetTarget, order them with RunAfter, attach real build outputs with Artifact, and set an actor. Only an effectful actor commits: with no actor, or with a language-model actor, Store, Launch and Run are rehearsals that touch nothing and say so in their rows. Steps gives the ordered plan (provision, store, launch, verify per part), Run executes it with a verify gate and rolls the completed steps back in reverse on a failure, and Feasibility asks whether each host has room. Explain and Plan are pure reading. With an effectful actor Store, Launch and Run write to sites, start parts and can provision hosts: the documentation run used only the rehearsing path.
classes.receiver: oD = new stzDelivery("bistro") oD.AddBackend(:api, :LinuxServer) oS = new stzDeploymentSite("local-api") oS.SetKindQ(:LocalRepo).SetStoreAtQ("deploy_demo/site_api") o1 = new stzDeployment(oD) o1.SetTarget(:api, oS) o1.SetActor(LLMActor("assistant"))
classes.example:
? o1.MayCommit()
#--> 0
? len(o1.Steps())
#--> 3
? @@( o1.Store() )
#--> [ 0, [ [ "api", "local-api", "rehearsed (not committed)" ] ] ]
aRun = o1.Run()
? aRun[1]
#--> 0
? o1.WasRun()
#--> 1
? o1.WasCommitted()
#--> 0

methods.name: WasCommitted

methods.name: Run
methods.brief: Executes the ordered plan under the actor's authority, with a verify gate and rollback on failure, and returns each step's outcome.
methods.returns: a list [ committed, rows ], each row [ step, outcome ] with done, rehearsed, FAILED or skipped
notes: a failed step makes the later steps skipped
warnings: effectful with an effectful actor: it stores, launches and may provision hosts and roll back; it was run here only without an actor and with a language-model actor, where every step read rehearsed and nothing happened; a part whose requirement declares a GPU is checked before its first step, and on a local site that probes this machine's GPU, which was not exercised

methods.name: Feasibility

methods.returns: a list of lists, fits being 1 or 0
warnings: the requirements of the parts on one site are added up; a site with no declared capacity is assumed to fit, and a scriptable site is assumed to be provisioned

methods.name: Feasible
methods.brief: TRUE if every site can host its parts, by its capacity or by being provisioned.
warnings: Run does not check it: a deployment with a shortfall still rehearses

classes.name: stzDeploymentSite
classes.brief: Describes where a solution is deployed and how to reach and drive that place: kind, endpoint, protocol, authentication, storage, commands and capacity.
classes.description: A site is configuration first: set it with the Set methods (each has a Q form that returns the site to chain), read it back as data with Config, as lines with ConfigText or as JSON with ConfigJson, and see the commands it would run with Commands, TransferCommand and LaunchCommandLine before anything runs. Authentication is a plain reference, a stzSecret kept behind a redacted descriptor, or a secret held by name in a stzSecretStore and revealed through ResolveAuthVia so that the store audits it. Store, Launch, Status and Rollback act on the target: a local folder is written directly, a git site runs git, a server runs scp and ssh, and registry, device and object- store sites have commands listed but no store backend. A stzDeployment drives sites under a governed actor. The runs behind this reference only configured and read sites; nothing was stored to, launched on or rolled back.
classes.example:
o1.SetKindQ("server").SetEndpointQ("deploy@api.example.test:/srv/api")
? o1.Protocol()
#--> ssh
? o1.TransferCommand()
#--> scp -r <staged>/. deploy@api.example.test:/srv/api
? o1.IsLocal()
#--> 0
