classes.name: stzDetection
classes.brief: Declares one rule over a sequence of security events and judges a ledger against it, answering findings.
classes.description: Four shapes, each computable over a bounded ledger without a query language: a burst (n events of one kind inside a window), a sequence (one kind followed by another), any (one occurrence is the story) and unusual (the newest window judged against the same kind's own history, so the threshold is learned instead of written down). The unusual shape is honest: the newest window is judged against the windows before it, a cold start says nothing, and a flood that evicted its own baseline is reported as a warning. Findings come in the unified shape [ :rule, :subject, :where, :severity, :message ], so they join stzRuleReport. Corroborated holds an error back to a warning until two distinct event kinds agree. A detection with nothing watched raises when asked to judge.
classes.example:
o1.WhenKind("auth.login.failed").PerActor().Repeats(5).Within(60000)
? o1.Shape()
#--> burst

methods.name: init
methods.brief: Builds a detection of that name, which watches nothing yet and reports its findings at error severity.

parameters.name: pcName
parameters.role: the detection's name, which becomes the rule of its findings

methods.name: Name
methods.brief: Returns the detection's name, the rule its findings carry.

methods.name: Kind
methods.brief: Returns the event kind the detection watches, trimmed and in lower case.
methods.returns: a text; empty until WhenKind sets it

methods.name: Shape
methods.brief: Returns which shape the detection has: burst, sequence, any or unusual.
methods.returns: a text; empty until a declaring call sets it

methods.name: Severity
methods.brief: Returns the severity its findings carry, which is error until AsWarning or AsInfo changes it.

methods.name: Meaning
methods.brief: Returns the sentence given by Explaining, which is added to every finding message.
methods.returns: a text; empty until Explaining sets it

methods.name: WhenKind
methods.brief: Sets the event kind to watch, and makes the shape any when no shape was chosen yet.

parameters.name: pcKind
parameters.role: the event kind to watch, trimmed and put in lower case

methods.returns: the detection itself, so calls chain
notes: start every detection with it
warnings: the kind is not checked against the catalog, so a misspelled kind watches nothing and never fires

methods.name: Repeats
methods.brief: Makes the detection a burst: this many events of the watched kind inside the window fire it.

parameters.name: pnTimes
parameters.role: how many events make a burst

methods.returns: the detection itself, so calls chain
notes: the BURST shape of stzDetection
warnings: without Within the window is 0 ms, so only events stamped with the same millisecond count together

methods.name: Within
methods.brief: Sets the window of a burst or a sequence, in milliseconds of event wall time.

parameters.name: pnMs
parameters.role: the window length, in milliseconds

methods.returns: the detection itself, so calls chain

methods.name: PerActor
methods.brief: Counts events actor by actor instead of across all actors, for a burst or an unusual rate.
methods.returns: the detection itself, so calls chain
notes: credential stuffing is per account, not per installation

methods.name: ThenKind
methods.brief: Makes the detection a sequence: an event of this kind must follow one of the watched kind.

parameters.name: pcKind
parameters.role: the event kind that must follow, trimmed and put in lower case

methods.returns: the detection itself, so calls chain
warnings: the kind is not checked against the catalog, so a misspelled kind never follows and the detection never fires

methods.name: BySameActor
methods.brief: Requires both events of a sequence to come from the same actor.
methods.returns: the detection itself, so calls chain
notes: without it the whole ledger counts as one actor and a sequence gives one finding in all

methods.name: OnAnyOccurrence
methods.brief: Makes the detection fire on any single event of the watched kind, for kinds where one occurrence is already the story.
methods.returns: the detection itself, so calls chain
notes: one finding per matching event, at most 16

methods.name: Unusual
methods.brief: Makes the detection judge the newest window of the watched kind against the history of that same kind.
methods.returns: the detection itself, so calls chain
notes: the defaults are windows of 60000 ms, a baseline of 12 windows, 3 sigma and a floor of 3 (threat model R9)

methods.name: Buckets
methods.brief: Sets the width of one window of the unusual shape, in milliseconds.

parameters.name: pnMs
parameters.role: the window width, in milliseconds, at least 1

methods.returns: the detection itself, so calls chain
notes: the baseline is this width times AgainstBaseline
warnings: a width below 1 raises an error, and a value that is not a number raises R41

methods.name: AgainstBaseline
methods.brief: Sets how many windows before the newest one form the baseline of the unusual shape.

parameters.name: pnBuckets
parameters.role: the number of baseline windows, at least 3

methods.returns: the detection itself, so calls chain
notes: the newest window is judged against the windows before it, never against a baseline that includes itself
warnings: fewer than 3 raises an error; until the ledger reaches back over 3 baseline windows nothing is said, because a cold start is not an anomaly

methods.name: Sigma
methods.brief: Sets how many standard deviations above the baseline mean make a window unusual.

parameters.name: pnZ
parameters.role: the number of standard deviations

methods.returns: the detection itself, so calls chain
notes: on a flat baseline, where the windows before all hold the same count, sigma is not used: any count above that mean and at or over the floor fires

methods.name: AtLeast
methods.brief: Sets the floor of the unusual shape: a window with fewer events than this never fires.

parameters.name: pnCount
parameters.role: the smallest number of events in the newest window that can fire

methods.returns: the detection itself, so calls chain

methods.name: AsOf
methods.brief: Judges the unusual shape at a given wall time instead of at the newest event, so a guard can be exact.

parameters.name: pnWallMs
parameters.role: the moment of judgement, in epoch milliseconds, 0 for the newest event

methods.returns: the detection itself, so calls chain

methods.name: Corroborated
methods.brief: Marks the detection so that an error finding drops to a warning unless the matched events span two distinct kinds.
methods.returns: the detection itself, so calls chain
notes: the corroboration law: one anomalous signal is a rumor, and the message says it is a single signal

methods.name: Explaining
methods.brief: Sets the one-sentence meaning that is added to every finding message and to the explanation.

parameters.name: pcMeaning
parameters.role: what the detection means, as text

methods.returns: the detection itself, so calls chain

methods.name: AsError
methods.brief: Sets the severity of the findings to error.
methods.returns: the detection itself, so calls chain

methods.name: AsWarning
methods.brief: Sets the severity of the findings to warning.
methods.returns: the detection itself, so calls chain

methods.name: AsInfo
methods.brief: Sets the severity of the findings to info.
methods.returns: the detection itself, so calls chain

methods.name: CheckAgainst
methods.brief: Judges a ledger and returns the findings in the unified rule shape, ready for stzRuleReport.

parameters.name: poLedger
parameters.role: the stzSecurityLedger to judge, read through its retained window

methods.returns: a list of [ :rule, :subject, :where, :severity, :message ] findings; [ ] when nothing matches
notes: the subject is security and where is the detection name, then a slash and the actor when there is one; at most 16 findings, so a storm reports and does not flood
warnings: raises an error when nothing is watched, so call WhenKind first

methods.name: LastEvidence
methods.brief: Returns the events that matched in the last check, so an incident can build its timeline from them.
methods.returns: a list of records; [ ] before any check or when nothing matched

methods.name: Explain
methods.brief: Returns the detection told as lines of text: its shape with its numbers, and its meaning when given.
notes: the first line reads Detection name [severity] followed by the shape

methods.name: Show
methods.brief: Prints the lines Explain returns, one per line.

classes.name: stzDiagram
classes.brief: Holds a flow diagram of typed, coloured nodes and labelled edges, and draws it as SVG or PNG with no graphviz, or exports it as DOT, Mermaid, JSON or the native .stzdiag text.
classes.description: A stzDiagram is a stzGraph with a look: a theme, a layout direction, edge routing, pen and arrow settings, 24 node shapes (AddCircle, AddBox, AddDiamond and so on, each a node with a type and a label equal to its id), clusters drawn as boxes behind their nodes, annotators, and visual rules over node and edge properties. The inherited stzGraph methods (AddNodeXTT, Connect, AddEdgeXT, NodeProperty, Edges) build the content. ToCanvas lays the diagram out and draws it natively; ToSVG, ToPNG and ToPages are the outputs, and after ToCanvas the Render methods report where everything was drawn and PickAt answers what lies under a pixel. On top of that picture sits a headless editor: OnPress, OnMove, OnRelease and OnCancel feed a pointer into a state machine, Edit runs commands that Undo and Redo take back, and Pin fixes a node in the layout. Ids are folded to lowercase. Known defects, each carried as a warning: ComputeMetrics divides by zero for a diagram with no path of two nodes; ToSVG and ToPNG leave the last picture freed, so picking fails after them; ImportDiag into a diagram that holds the first node adds duplicates; the pen-width setters are named the wrong way round. Display and View need graphviz and a viewer and Step and RunIn need a window; none of the three was run.
classes.receiver: o1 = new stzDiagram("flow"); o1.AddNodeXTT("start", "Order Received", [ :type = "start" ]); o1.AddNodeXT("validate", "Validate"); o1.AddNodeXTT("done", "Done", [ :type = "endpoint" ]); o1.AddEdgeXT("start", "validate", "next"); o1.AddEdge("validate", "done")
classes.example:
? @@( o1.Edges()[1][:label] )
#--> "next"

parameters.name: pcStyle
parameters.role: A pen style such as solid, dashed, dotted, bold or invis, or several joined by + or a comma

methods.name: SetArrowHead
methods.brief: Sets the arrowhead shape at the end of every edge, kept in lowercase without a check.

parameters.name: pcStyle
parameters.role: An arrow shape such as normal, vee, diamond, dot, inv, curve, box, crow, tee or none

methods.name: SetArrowTail
methods.brief: Sets the arrow shape at the start of every edge, kept in lowercase without a check.

parameters.name: pcStyle
parameters.role: An arrow shape such as normal, vee, diamond, dot, inv, curve, box, crow, tee or none

methods.name: SetSplines
methods.brief: Sets how edges are routed: ortho, spline, polyline, curved, line or none; any other value is ignored and the earlier one stays.

parameters.name: pcType
parameters.role: The routing name, as text, case ignored

methods.name: SetEdgeLineStyle
methods.brief: Sets the edge routing when given a routing name, or the edge pen style when given a pen style name; anything else changes nothing.

parameters.name: pcType
parameters.role: A routing name such as ortho or curved, or a pen style name such as dashed or dotted

notes: its getter EdgeLineStyle answers the routing, not the pen style

methods.name: SetEdgeLineType
methods.brief: Sets the edge routing or the edge pen style by the name given; another spelling of the line-style call.

parameters.name: pcType
parameters.role: A routing name such as ortho or curved, or a pen style name such as dashed or dotted

methods.name: SetEdgeSpline
methods.brief: Sets the edge routing; another spelling of the routing call.

parameters.name: pcType
parameters.role: The routing name, as text

methods.name: SetNodeSeparation
methods.brief: Sets the spacing between nodes of the same rank, in inches; zero, a negative number or a non-number is ignored.

parameters.name: pnValue
parameters.role: The separation, a number above 0

methods.name: SetRankSeparation
methods.brief: Sets the spacing between ranks, in inches; zero, a negative number or a non-number is ignored.

parameters.name: pnValue
parameters.role: The separation, a number above 0

methods.name: SetConcentrate
methods.brief: Turns edge merging on or off, so that edges sharing a path are drawn as one.

parameters.name: pbValue
parameters.role: 1 to merge edges, 0 not to

notes: the value is stored without a check

methods.name: SetLayoutPreset
methods.brief: Applies a named bundle of routing and spacing settings; an unknown name changes nothing.

parameters.name: pcPreset
parameters.role: A preset name, as text: orgchart, orgchart_compact, compact, spacious or flowchart

notes: orgchart also sets the edge colour to gray; compact also turns edge merging on

methods.name: SetTitle
methods.brief: Sets the title of the diagram; it is stored as given.

parameters.name: pcTitle
parameters.role: The title, as text, stored as given.

warnings: seen in the gallery: the native canvas tier does not draw the title; the Dot tier does

methods.name: SetSubtitle
methods.brief: Sets the subtitle of the diagram; it is stored as given.

parameters.name: pcSubtitle
parameters.role: The subtitle, as text, stored as given.

methods.name: SetOutputFormat
methods.brief: Sets the image format asked of graphviz by Display, kept in lowercase without a check.

parameters.name: cFormat
parameters.role: The format name, as text, such as svg or png

methods.name: SetOutput
methods.brief: Sets the image format asked of graphviz by Display; another spelling of the output-format call.

parameters.name: cFormat
parameters.role: The format name, as text, such as svg or png

methods.name: SetTooltip
methods.brief: Stores the tooltip configuration without checking it.

parameters.name: paConfig
parameters.role: The tooltip settings, as a list

methods.name: DisableTooltip
methods.brief: Clears the tooltip configuration.

methods.name: NodePenWidth
methods.brief: Returns the pen width of the nodes; a pair is returned when the node and edge widths differ, and then both numbers are the node width.
methods.returns: a number, or a list of two numbers when the widths differ
notes: 1 until set
warnings: the pair repeats the node width twice instead of giving [ node, edge ]

methods.name: EdgePenWidth
methods.brief: Returns the pen width of the edges; 1 until set.

methods.name: NodePenStyle
methods.brief: Returns the pen style of the node outlines; solid until set.

methods.name: EdgePenStyle
methods.brief: Returns the pen style of the edges; solid until set.

methods.name: ArrowHead
methods.brief: Returns the shape drawn at the end of each edge; normal until set.

methods.name: ArrowTail
methods.brief: Returns the arrow shape at the start of the edges; none until set.

methods.name: Splines
methods.brief: Returns the edge routing; spline until set.

methods.name: NodeSeparation
methods.brief: Returns the spacing between nodes of a rank, in inches; 0.6 until set.

methods.name: RankSeparation
methods.brief: Returns the spacing between ranks, in inches; 0.8 until set.

methods.name: Concentrate
methods.brief: Returns 1 when edge merging is on and 0 when it is off, the default.

methods.name: Theme
methods.brief: Returns the colour scheme in force, in lowercase; neutral until set.

methods.name: Layout
methods.brief: Returns the direction the diagram is laid out in, as stored in lowercase; topdown until set.

methods.name: EdgeColor
methods.brief: Returns the colour of the edges as a #rrggbb code.

methods.name: NodeStrokeColor
methods.brief: Returns the outline colour of the nodes, gray until set; an empty text means no outline.

methods.name: EdgeStyle
methods.brief: Returns the style name of the edges; normal until set.

methods.name: Font
methods.brief: Returns the typeface in force, in lowercase; helvetica until a theme or a setter changes it.

methods.name: FontSize
methods.brief: Returns the point size of the text in force; 12 until a theme or a setter changes it.

methods.name: PenWidth
methods.brief: Returns the general pen width of the diagram, the number the pen-width setter writes.
methods.returns: a number, in pixels; 1 until set
notes: it is the node outline width: SetPenWidth writes that width, and the edge width is read by EdgePenWidth
warnings: NodePenWidth answers a pair when the node and edge widths differ; this one always answers a single number

methods.name: EdgeSplines
methods.brief: Returns the edge routing; another spelling of the routing getter.

methods.name: SplineType
methods.brief: Returns the edge routing; another spelling of the routing getter.

methods.name: EdgeLineStyle
methods.brief: Returns the edge routing, not the edge pen style, whatever its name suggests.
notes: EdgePenStyle answers the pen style
warnings: named like the pen style but answers the routing, so after SetEdgeLineStyle("dashed") it still says the old routing

methods.name: EdgeLineType
methods.brief: Returns the edge routing, not the edge pen style, whatever its name suggests.
warnings: answers the routing, not a pen style

methods.name: Title
methods.brief: Returns the heading of the diagram; empty until set.

methods.name: Subtitle
methods.brief: Returns the second heading of the diagram; empty until set.

methods.name: OutputFormat
methods.brief: Returns the output format set for Display; the text NULL until one is set.
warnings: the default comes from a global that is never defined, so a diagram that never called SetOutputFormat answers the text NULL

methods.name: TooltipConfig
methods.brief: Returns the tooltip configuration; an empty list until set.

methods.name: ResolveFontColor
methods.brief: Returns black or white, whichever reads better on a given background colour.

parameters.name: pBgColor
parameters.role: The background colour, as a name or a #rrggbb code

methods.name: ContrastingTextColor
methods.brief: Returns black or white, whichever reads better on a given colour, by its luminance.

parameters.name: _cColor_
parameters.role: A colour: a name, a semantic name such as success, or a #rrggbb code.

methods.name: ColorToRGB
methods.brief: Returns the red, green and blue values of a colour; an unknown colour name gives white.

parameters.name: _cColor_
parameters.role: A colour: a name, a semantic name such as success, or a #rrggbb code.

methods.returns: a list of three numbers from 0 to 255

methods.name: NodeStrokeColorForTheme
methods.brief: Returns black for the print and gray themes and an empty text for every other, case included.

parameters.name: _cTheme_
parameters.role: A theme name, as text; case matters.

methods.name: ConvertColorTogray
methods.brief: Returns the grey of the same brightness as a colour, as a #rrggbb code.

parameters.name: _cColor_
parameters.role: A colour: a name, a semantic name such as success, or a #rrggbb code.

parameters.name: oAnnotation
parameters.role: A stzDiagramAnnotator object.

parameters.name: pcType
parameters.role: The annotation type, as text, in the case it was created with

methods.returns: a list of stzDiagramAnnotator objects; [ ] when none

methods.brief: Returns the types of the attached annotators, in the order attached.
notes: AnnotationsQ answers the annotator objects themselves

extensions.name: AnnotationsQ

methods.name: AddTemplate
methods.brief: Stores a template object for ApplyTemplates, without checking it.

parameters.name: oTemplate
parameters.role: A template object that has an Apply method taking the diagram.

warnings: the object must have an Apply method taking the diagram, or ApplyTemplates raises R14

methods.name: ApplyTemplates
methods.brief: Calls Apply on every stored template, passing the diagram.
warnings: raises R14 (method without definition: apply) when a stored object has no Apply method

methods.name: RegisterVisualRule
methods.brief: Stores a visual rule that ApplyVisualRules later tests against each node and edge; the definition is not checked.

parameters.name: pcRuleName
parameters.role: The name of the rule, as text.

parameters.name: paDefinition
parameters.role: The rule, as a hash list [ :conditionType, :conditionParams, :effects ]; conditionType is property_range, property_equals, property_exists or tag_exists.

notes: a rule is a hash list [ :conditionType, :conditionParams, :effects ]; the types are property_range [ key, min, max ], property_equals [ key, value ], property_exists [ key ] and tag_exists [ tag ]
warnings: seen in the gallery: the rules reach the Dot output only; the native canvas tier draws every node in the default colour

methods.name: ApplyVisualRules
methods.brief: Tests every rule against every node and edge and records the effects of those that match, which NodesAffectedByVisualRules then lists.
methods.returns: nothing; the recorded effects are replaced
notes: the effects are kept in the diagram for NodesAffectedByVisualRules to list; nothing here paints them

methods.name: NodesAffectedByVisualRules
methods.brief: Returns the ids of the nodes that a rule matched at the last ApplyVisualRules.
methods.returns: a list of text; [ ] before any application

methods.name: VisualRulesApplied
methods.brief: Returns a summary of the registered rules: each name, condition type and number of effects.
notes: it lists the registered rules, whether or not they were applied

methods.name: NodesWithProperty
methods.brief: Returns the ids of the nodes that have a property, whatever its value.

parameters.name: pcProp
parameters.role: A property name, as text.

methods.name: NodesWith
methods.brief: Returns the ids of the nodes whose property satisfies a comparison with a value; a node without the property never matches.

parameters.name: pcProp
parameters.role: A property name, as text.

parameters.name: pcOp
parameters.role: The comparison, as text: =, !=, <, >, <=, >=, contains, startswith, endswith, in or not_in

parameters.name: pValue
parameters.role: The value to compare with; a list for in and not_in

methods.returns: a list of text, in node order; [ ] when nothing matches
notes: = and != compare numbers as numbers and texts exactly, case included; an order comparison holds only between numbers; contains, startswith and endswith ignore case and need texts
warnings: any other comparison raises an error

methods.name: NodesWithTag
methods.brief: Returns the ids of the nodes whose :tags property lists a tag, matched exactly.

parameters.name: pcTag
parameters.role: A tag, as text, as found in a node's :tags list.

methods.name: EdgesWithProperty
methods.brief: Returns the edges that have a property, as "from->to" text, whatever its value.

parameters.name: pcProp
parameters.role: A property name, as text.

methods.returns: a list of text such as "a->b"

methods.name: EdgesWithPropertyValue
methods.brief: Returns the edges whose property equals a value, as "from->to" text.

parameters.name: pcProp
parameters.role: A property name, as text.

parameters.name: pValue
parameters.role: The value the property must equal

methods.returns: a list of text such as "a->b"

methods.name: propertiesLegend
methods.brief: Returns the registered visual rules as text lines: a heading, then for each rule its condition, its parameters and its effects.

classes.name: stzDLM
classes.brief: Answers questions about one small domain from recorded facts, refuses everything outside it, and can train a tiny neural model on its own sentences.
classes.description: The first rung has no neurons: entities, relations and facts are kept as lists, every answer is a lookup with a reason, and a question about anything unknown is refused with the domain's name rather than guessed. It can be filled by hand, forged from a knowledge graph with StzDlmQ, and saved to a self-contained .zdlm file that another model reads back with LoadFrom. The second rung is a bigram network trained only on the sentences GenerateCorpus renders from the facts, with no remote teacher; it predicts and generates words but does not own the truth, which stays with Ask. Known limits today: names learned by hand are matched in lower case only, and the recorded laws are saved but not applied by Ask.
classes.example:
o1.LearnEntity("margherita", "dish")
o1.LearnEntity("basil", "ingredient")
o1.LearnFact("margherita", "contains", "basil")
? o1.Ask("what is margherita")
#--> Margherita is a dish.
? o1.Ask("margherita contains?")
#--> Margherita contains basil.
? o1.Ask("what is the weather")
#--> That is outside the 'restaurant' domain (I know 2 entities and 1 relations).
? o1.Complete("margherita")[1]
#--> contains

? o1.Complete("what is margherita")[:text]
#--> Margherita is a dish.

#--> dlm

classes.name: stzDotCode
classes.brief: Turns Graphviz graph text into a picture file by running the dot program, and can open the picture.
classes.description: You set the graph in the dot language, choose a format (svg by default; png, pdf and about fifty others), and Execute writes the graph to a working file in the temp folder and runs dot, leaving the picture in the output folder as diagram_ plus a number. The dot program is taken from $aStzLibConfig[:DotPath] or from d:/Graphviz/bin/dot.exe, and SetDotPath overrides it. Graphviz must be installed. View opens the picture in the program the system associates with it; it was read but not run, because it opens a window. Three defects are recorded in the methods: SetOutputFormat refuses upper case, SetOutput does not check, and CleanupAll does not delete the picture.
classes.example:
o1.SetCode("digraph G { a -> b; b -> c; }")
o1.SetOutputFormat("dot")
o1.Execute()
? StzFindFirst("a -> b", o1.ReadFile(o1.OutputFile())) > 0
#--> 1

classes.name: stzDuration
classes.brief: Holds a length of time, independent of any date, and reads it back as parts, as words or as clock text.
classes.description: A duration is built from a number of seconds, from a text such as 1 hour 30 min, or from a hash list of days, hours, minutes, seconds and milliseconds. It answers totals (TotalHours counts past one day) and parts (Hours is the hour of the day), compares with other durations, numbers or texts, and is changed in place by Add, Subtract, Multiply and Divide, which return the duration so calls chain. Limits today: the fraction of a second is lost when it is built from a number or a text, and AddMilliseconds, Copy and the operator results do not carry milliseconds; a negative duration answers wrong parts.
classes.receiver: o1 = new stzDuration("1 day 2 hours 3 minutes 4 seconds")
classes.example:
? o1.TotalSeconds()
#--> 93784
? o1.ToHuman()
#--> 1 day, 2 hours, 3 minutes, and 4 seconds
? o1.ToString()
#--> 26:03:04

methods.name: init
methods.brief: Builds a length of time from seconds, from text such as 1 hour 30 min, or from a hash list of parts.

parameters.name: p
parameters.role: the length: a number of seconds, a text of numbers followed by day, hour, minute, second or ms units, or a hash list with the keys days, hours, minutes, seconds and milliseconds

notes: an empty text gives a zero duration
warnings: the fraction of a second is lost today for a number or a text: 90.5 and 90 seconds 250 ms both answer Milliseconds 0; only a hash list with a milliseconds key keeps it, and Copy or Add then drop it

methods.name: TotalSeconds
methods.brief: Returns the whole length counted in seconds, dropping any fraction.
notes: 1 day 2 hours 3 minutes 4 seconds is 93784

methods.name: ToSeconds
methods.brief: Returns the whole length counted in seconds, dropping any fraction.
notes: the same value as TotalSeconds

methods.name: TotalMinutes
methods.brief: Returns the whole length counted in minutes, rounded down.
notes: 93784 seconds is 1563 minutes

methods.name: ToMinutes
methods.brief: Returns the whole length counted in minutes, rounded down.
notes: the same value as TotalMinutes

methods.name: TotalHours
methods.brief: Returns the whole length counted in hours, rounded down, and without wrapping at one day.
notes: 93784 seconds is 26 hours, where Hours answers 2

methods.name: ToHours
methods.brief: Returns the whole length counted in hours, rounded down, and without wrapping at one day.
notes: the same value as TotalHours

methods.name: TotalDays
methods.brief: Returns the whole length counted in days, rounded down.
notes: 93784 seconds is 1 day

methods.name: ToDays
methods.brief: Returns the whole length counted in days, rounded down.
notes: the same value as TotalDays

methods.name: Days
methods.brief: Returns the number of whole days in the length.
notes: the same value as TotalDays
warnings: a negative duration gives a wrong part: -90 seconds answers Days -1, not 0

methods.name: Hours
methods.brief: Returns the hours left over after whole days are taken out, from 0 to 23.
notes: 26 hours total is 2 here
warnings: a negative duration gives a wrong part: -90 seconds answers Hours -1

methods.name: Minutes
methods.brief: Returns the minutes left over after whole hours are taken out, from 0 to 59.
warnings: a negative duration gives a wrong part: -90 seconds answers Minutes -2

methods.name: Seconds
methods.brief: Returns the seconds left over after whole minutes are taken out, from 0 to 59.
notes: 90 seconds answers 30
warnings: a negative duration gives a wrong part: -90 seconds answers Seconds -30

methods.name: Milliseconds
methods.brief: Returns the milliseconds part kept with the length, from 0 to 999.
warnings: stays 0 for a duration built from a number or a text, and AddMilliseconds does not change it: only the milliseconds key of a hash list sets it

methods.name: Components
methods.brief: Returns the length split into its parts, as a hash list of days, hours, minutes, seconds and milliseconds.
methods.returns: a hash list with the keys days, hours, minutes, seconds and milliseconds
notes: 93784 seconds gives 1, 2, 3, 4 and 0
warnings: a negative duration gives negative parts, which do not add back to the length

methods.name: ToString
methods.brief: Returns the length as clock text, hours in total then minutes and seconds in two digits, such as 26:03:04.
methods.returns: a text, h:mm:ss by default; ToStringXT takes a format of your own
notes: ToStringXT reads d, H, h, m, s and z for the parts and dd, HH, hh, mm, ss and zzz for the padded ones, where H is the hour of the day, h the total hours and zzz the milliseconds; a letter that touches another letter stays as written, and Duration and Content are the same call

extensions.name: ToStringXT
extensions.adds: the extended form: more parameters than the base method

methods.name: ToHuman
methods.brief: Returns the length in words, such as 1 day, 2 hours, 3 minutes, and 4 seconds.
methods.returns: a text; 0 seconds for a zero length
notes: whole weeks and a few long spans have their own phrase: 7 days is 1 week, 14 days is 2 weeks, 30 days with 23:59:59 is 1 month, 183 days with 23:59:59 is 6 months and 365 days with 23:59:59 is 1 year, while exactly 30 or 365 days stay in days
warnings: a negative duration answers 0 seconds

methods.name: ToCompact
methods.brief: Returns the length in short units, such as 1d 2h 3m 4s, leaving out the parts that are zero.
methods.returns: a text; 0s for a zero length
notes: milliseconds are not shown; 100 days is 100d

methods.name: ToSimple
methods.brief: Returns the length as h:m:s, or as m:s under one hour, with minutes and seconds padded by spaces.
notes: the padding is a space, not a zero, so 90 seconds gives a leading space; ToString pads with zeros

methods.name: operator
methods.brief: Combines or compares the duration with another value by a sign, giving a new duration or TRUE or FALSE.

parameters.name: cOp
parameters.role: the operator as text: +, -, *, /, <, <=, >, >=, = or !=

parameters.name: pValue
parameters.role: the right-hand side: a number of seconds, a text of units or a stzDuration, where * and / take a number only

methods.returns: a stzDuration for + - * /, TRUE or FALSE for < <= > >= = !=, an empty text for any other operator or a division by zero
notes: 90 seconds plus 2 minutes is 210 seconds
warnings: the duration itself is not changed; the result of + - * / drops the milliseconds

methods.name: Compare
methods.brief: Compares the length with another and returns -1, 0 or 1.

parameters.name: pOther
parameters.role: a number of seconds, a text of units or a stzDuration

methods.returns: a number: -1 if shorter than pOther, 0 if equal, 1 if longer
warnings: a value of another kind counts as zero seconds, so the answer is 1 for any positive duration

methods.name: IsEqualTo
methods.brief: TRUE if the length equals another, given as seconds, text or a stzDuration.

parameters.name: pOther
parameters.role: a number of seconds, a text of units or a stzDuration

notes: 90 seconds equals 1 minute 30 seconds

methods.name: IsLessThan
methods.brief: TRUE if the length is shorter than another.

parameters.name: pOther
parameters.role: a number of seconds, a text of units or a stzDuration

methods.name: IsGreaterThan
methods.brief: TRUE if the length is longer than another.

parameters.name: pOther
parameters.role: a number of seconds, a text of units or a stzDuration

methods.name: IsBetween
methods.brief: TRUE if the length is within a range, both ends included.

parameters.name: pMin
parameters.role: the shortest accepted length

parameters.name: pMax
parameters.role: the longest accepted length

notes: 90 seconds is between 90 and 90
warnings: a reversed range, with pMin above pMax, is never satisfied

methods.name: IsZero
methods.brief: TRUE if the length is exactly zero seconds.

methods.name: IsPositive
methods.brief: TRUE if the length is above zero.

methods.name: IsNegative
methods.brief: TRUE if the length is below zero, as after subtracting more than was there.
notes: the parts of a negative duration are wrong: see Days

methods.name: Add
methods.brief: Adds a length to the duration in place; the length is a number of seconds, a text of units or a stzDuration.

parameters.name: p
parameters.role: the length to add

methods.returns: the duration itself, so calls chain
notes: 90 seconds plus 30 is 120

methods.name: Subtract
methods.brief: Takes a length off the duration in place; the length is a number of seconds, a text of units or a stzDuration.

parameters.name: p
parameters.role: the length to remove

methods.returns: the duration itself, so calls chain
warnings: the duration can go below zero

methods.name: Multiply
methods.brief: Multiplies the duration by a number, in place.

parameters.name: n
parameters.role: the factor, a number

methods.returns: the duration itself, so calls chain
notes: 100 seconds times 3 is 300

methods.name: Divide
methods.brief: Divides the duration by a number, in place.

parameters.name: n
parameters.role: the divisor, a number

methods.returns: the duration itself, so calls chain
notes: 300 seconds divided by 4 is 75
warnings: a division by zero is ignored without an error

methods.name: AddDays
methods.brief: Adds a number of days to the duration, in place.

parameters.name: n
parameters.role: the number of days, which may be negative

methods.returns: the duration itself, so calls chain

methods.name: AddHours
methods.brief: Adds a number of hours to the duration, in place.

parameters.name: n
parameters.role: the number of hours, which may be negative

methods.returns: the duration itself, so calls chain

methods.name: AddMinutes
methods.brief: Adds a number of minutes to the duration, in place.

parameters.name: n
parameters.role: the number of minutes, which may be negative

methods.returns: the duration itself, so calls chain

methods.name: AddSeconds
methods.brief: Adds a number of seconds to the duration, in place.

parameters.name: n
parameters.role: the number of seconds, which may be negative

methods.returns: the duration itself, so calls chain

methods.name: AddMilliseconds
methods.brief: Adds a number of milliseconds to the duration, in place, but the sub-second part is not shown.

parameters.name: n
parameters.role: the number of milliseconds

methods.returns: the duration itself, so calls chain
notes: adding 1500 ms to 93784.5 s gives 93786 s
warnings: the milliseconds go into a hidden fraction of the total: 500 ms added to 93784 s leaves Milliseconds 0 and ToString unchanged, and only a later carry into a whole second shows

methods.name: ParseDurationString
methods.brief: Returns the number of seconds written in a text such as 2 hours 30 min, ignoring case.

parameters.name: _cStr_
parameters.role: the text to read: numbers followed by the units day, hour or hr, minute or min, second or sec, millisecond or ms

methods.returns: a number of seconds, which may have a decimal part; 0 when no unit is found
notes: 1.5 hr is 5400 and 250 ms is 0.25
warnings: the units week, month and year are not understood and give 0; a number with no unit is ignored

methods.name: Copy
methods.brief: Returns a new duration of the same length, independent of the first.
notes: changing the copy does not change the original
warnings: the milliseconds are dropped from the copy

methods.name: Clone
methods.brief: Returns a new duration of the same length, independent of the first.
notes: the same call as Copy
warnings: the milliseconds are dropped from the copy

methods.name: JoinParts
methods.brief: Joins phrases such as 1 hour and 2 minutes into one sentence, with commas and a last and.

parameters.name: _aParts_
parameters.role: the list of phrases, as text

methods.returns: a text: one phrase as it is, two joined by and, three or more separated by commas ending with and
notes: ToHuman is the public way to reach it
warnings: private: calling it from outside the class raises an error R26

classes.name: stzEarcons
classes.brief: Turns a meaning (danger, warning, info, success, muted) into a short sound and decides when it may play, so a screen state is corroborated by ear.
classes.description: An author names a meaning and gets a motif: ToSoundOf returns it as data, with no audio device, and the audibility and priority questions are answered by pure functions (WouldFireAt, IsAudible, PriorityOf). Muted renders as silence. Start opens a sound pool and Fire plays a cue through the device, dropping it when the same value repeats inside the refractory period or a louder alert is still sounding; Say queues a cue and a spoken phrase, which are only heard through TickSpeech or SpeakQueueToEnd. A sound is not the acknowledgement: it arrives about 419 ms after Fire, against the 100 ms the screen has, so it must repeat what another channel already shows. Every example of this reference rendered to buffers; none played through a device, and what a person hears of the motifs has not been recorded here.
classes.example:
? o1.IsSilentValue(:Muted)
#--> 1
? o1.PriorityOf(:Danger)
#--> 4
? o1.ToStepOf("Danger.Alert")
#--> alert
? o1.WouldFireAt(:Danger, 10)
#--> 1

methods.name: init
methods.brief: Builds the vocabulary of four motifs for danger, warning, info and success, with muted left silent; no device is opened.
notes: the motifs are rendered by the engine at 48000 Hz into ordinary sample buffers

methods.name: ToSoundOf
methods.brief: Returns the motif that a meaning sounds like, as a sound buffer that needs no audio device.

parameters.name: pMeaning
parameters.role: a semantic value (danger, warning, info, success, muted) as a name or a text, optionally followed by .cue or .alert

methods.returns: a stzSound; an empty text for muted and for a meaning that is refused, with LastError telling which half was wrong
notes: the danger motif lasts 0.18 seconds at 48000 Hz

methods.name: IsSilentValue
methods.brief: TRUE if the meaning is muted, the one value whose rendering is silence.

parameters.name: pMeaning
parameters.role: a semantic value, optionally with a step

methods.returns: TRUE or FALSE; FALSE for an unknown meaning

methods.name: ToStepOf
methods.brief: Returns the step a meaning asks for, cue when none is written.

parameters.name: pMeaning
parameters.role: a semantic value, optionally followed by a dot and a step

methods.returns: a text, cue or alert or ambient; an empty text when the meaning is refused

methods.name: PriorityOf
methods.brief: Returns how severe a meaning is, from 4 for danger down to 1 for success.

parameters.name: pMeaning
parameters.role: a semantic value, optionally with a step

methods.returns: a number: danger 4, warning 3, info 2, success 1, and 0 for muted or an unknown meaning

methods.name: SetAmbientFloor
methods.brief: Declares the loudness of the room in dB against which audibility is judged; it is never measured.

parameters.name: pnDb
parameters.role: the declared ambient level in dB, -40 being a quiet office

methods.returns: the earcons object itself, so calls chain
notes: a louder floor lowers every margin and can turn IsAudible to FALSE

methods.name: DeclaredFloor
methods.brief: Returns the ambient level in dB that margins are measured against.
methods.returns: a number, -40 until SetAmbientFloor changes it

methods.name: MarginMetric
methods.brief: Returns the name of the loudness measure that the audibility margin uses.
methods.returns: a text naming a K-weighted level over the sound's own length, which the text says is not an integrated LUFS figure

methods.name: LevelOf
methods.brief: Returns the K-weighted level of a meaning's motif over its own length, in dB.

parameters.name: pMeaning
parameters.role: a semantic value, optionally with a step

methods.returns: a number; -1000 for muted and for a refused meaning
notes: the danger motif measured -13.13 and the success motif -14.31

methods.name: AudibilityMarginOf
methods.brief: Returns how many dB a meaning's motif lies above the declared ambient floor.

parameters.name: pMeaning
parameters.role: a semantic value, optionally with a step

methods.returns: a number; -1000 when the meaning has no sound
notes: the danger margin was 26.87 over the default floor of -40

methods.name: RequiredMarginOf
methods.brief: Returns the headroom over the floor that a meaning must have: 10 for a cue and 20 for an alert.

parameters.name: pMeaning
parameters.role: a semantic value, optionally followed by .alert

methods.name: IsAudible
methods.brief: TRUE if the meaning's motif clears the required margin over the declared floor; muted counts as audible.

parameters.name: pMeaning
parameters.role: a semantic value, optionally with a step

methods.returns: TRUE or FALSE; FALSE for an unknown meaning
notes: muted answers TRUE because silence is lawful

methods.name: WouldFireAt
methods.brief: TRUE if the playing rules let the meaning sound at the given time, and records the reason.

parameters.name: pMeaning
parameters.role: a semantic value, optionally with a step

parameters.name: pnNow
parameters.role: the time in seconds on the player's clock

methods.returns: TRUE or FALSE; LastReason says why, ok when TRUE
notes: it refuses ambient steps, muted, the same value twice inside the refractory period, and a quieter meaning while an alert is still sounding

methods.name: RecordFireAt
methods.brief: Records that a meaning sounded at a time, so later decisions see the refractory period and any alert in force.

parameters.name: pMeaning
parameters.role: a semantic value, optionally with a step

parameters.name: pnNow
parameters.role: the time in seconds when it sounded

methods.returns: the earcons object itself, so calls chain
notes: an alert holds the floor for three times its motif length, and nothing happens for a refused meaning

methods.name: CountDropAt
methods.brief: Adds one to the count of dropped cues for a meaning.

parameters.name: pMeaning
parameters.role: a semantic value, optionally with a step

methods.returns: the earcons object itself, so calls chain
notes: Fire calls it for you when WouldFireAt says no

methods.name: DropsOf
methods.brief: Returns how many cues of that meaning were dropped.

parameters.name: pMeaning
parameters.role: a semantic value, optionally with a step

methods.returns: a number, 0 for an unknown meaning

methods.name: LastReason
methods.brief: Returns why the last decision about a cue or a phrase went the way it did.
methods.returns: a text such as ok, muted renders as silence, or a refractory message; empty before any decision

methods.name: SetRefractory
methods.brief: Sets the period in seconds inside which a repeat of the same value counts as one event; it starts at 0.15.

parameters.name: pnSeconds
parameters.role: the refractory period in seconds

methods.returns: the earcons object itself, so calls chain

methods.name: Start
methods.brief: Opens the sound pool so cues can be heard, and does nothing when it is already open.
methods.returns: the earcons object itself, so check IsStarted afterwards
notes: when the device cannot open, LastError says why and IsStarted stays FALSE
warnings: it opens the audio device and plays through it, which no run of this reference did

extensions.name: StartQ
extensions.adds: does what the method does, then returns the object, so the call can be chained

methods.name: Fire
methods.brief: Plays the cue for a meaning if the rules allow it, ducks the quieter voices, and counts a drop otherwise.

parameters.name: pMeaning
parameters.role: a semantic value, optionally with a step

methods.returns: the earcons object itself, so calls chain
notes: before Start it plays nothing, sets LastError to Fire: call Start() first and counts a refusal
warnings: it sounds through the audio device and was not run started

extensions.name: FireQ
extensions.adds: does what the method does, then returns the object, so the call can be chained

methods.name: SetDuckDepth
methods.brief: Sets how many dB quieter a lower-priority cue becomes while a higher one sounds; it starts at -12.

parameters.name: pnDb
parameters.role: the attenuation in dB, which must be negative

methods.returns: the earcons object itself, so calls chain
warnings: a positive value is refused: the depth is unchanged, LastError says to give a negative value, and a refusal is counted

methods.name: DuckDepthDb
methods.brief: Returns by how many dB a voice is turned down when a louder cue ducks it.
methods.returns: a number, -12 until SetDuckDepth changes it

methods.name: SetDuckRampMs
methods.brief: Sets the time in milliseconds over which a duck or an unduck moves, so that it cannot click; it starts at 10.

parameters.name: pnMs
parameters.role: the ramp length in milliseconds, a negative value being taken as 0

methods.returns: the earcons object itself, so calls chain

methods.name: DuckRampMs
methods.brief: Returns the length of the duck ramp in milliseconds.
methods.returns: a number, 10 until SetDuckRampMs changes it

methods.name: SetDucking
methods.brief: Switches ducking on or off; it is on by default.

parameters.name: pbOn
parameters.role: TRUE to duck quieter voices when a louder cue fires, FALSE to leave them alone

methods.returns: the earcons object itself, so calls chain

methods.name: IsDucking
methods.brief: TRUE if quieter voices are turned down when a louder cue fires.

methods.name: DucksApplied
methods.brief: Returns how many times a duck was applied, so that a sudden quiet has a number behind it.

methods.name: GainOf
methods.brief: Returns the gain that the player now applies to a meaning's voice.

parameters.name: pMeaning
parameters.role: a semantic value, optionally with a step

methods.returns: a number, 1 at unity and lower while ducked; -1 before Start or for a refused meaning
notes: only the not-started answer was run, since reading a live gain needs the open pool

methods.name: DuckUnder
methods.brief: Turns down every voice that is quieter in meaning than the given one, on the duck ramp.

parameters.name: pMeaning
parameters.role: the semantic value that is sounding, optionally with a step

methods.returns: the earcons object itself, so calls chain
notes: it changes nothing before Start or while ducking is off, and only that no-op was run because ducking needs the open pool

methods.name: Unduck
methods.brief: Brings every voice back to unity gain on the duck ramp.
methods.returns: the earcons object itself, so calls chain
notes: it changes nothing before Start, and only that no-op was run

methods.name: SetVoiceLanguage
methods.brief: Chooses the language in which phrases are spoken, and refuses a language the machine has no voice for.

parameters.name: pcTag
parameters.role: the language tag such as en-US or fr-FR

methods.returns: TRUE if the language was accepted, FALSE if it was refused with LastError naming the languages the machine has
notes: it never falls back to another language

methods.name: VoiceLanguage
methods.brief: Returns the language phrases are spoken in.
methods.returns: a text, empty until a language has been accepted

methods.name: CanSpeak
methods.brief: TRUE if this machine has a usable speech voice.
notes: the first call loads the voice engine, which is created only on first use

methods.name: ToSoundOfSaying
methods.brief: Returns one buffer holding the meaning's cue, a short gap, then the spoken phrase, with no audio device needed.

parameters.name: pMeaning
parameters.role: a semantic value, optionally with a step

parameters.name: pcPhrase
parameters.role: the text to speak

methods.returns: a stzSound; the plain cue when no voice is usable or the phrase is empty, and an empty text when both are silent or the meaning is refused
notes: the buffer takes the phrase's sample rate (22050 Hz on the run) and ends in 0.2 seconds of silence so the last syllable is not cut

methods.name: Say
methods.brief: Queues a cue and its phrase, higher priority first, and cancels a quieter phrase that is being spoken.

parameters.name: pMeaning
parameters.role: a semantic value, optionally with a step

parameters.name: pcPhrase
parameters.role: the text to say

methods.returns: the earcons object itself, so calls chain
notes: muted queues nothing and gives the reason in LastReason, and a refused meaning is counted as a refusal; nothing is heard until TickSpeech or SpeakQueueToEnd
warnings: the queue holds four by default and a fifth is dropped and counted in SpeechDrops

extensions.name: SayQ
extensions.adds: does what the method does, then returns the object, so the call can be chained

methods.name: TickSpeech
methods.brief: Advances the speech queue by one step: reaps a finished phrase, or starts the next one.
methods.returns: the earcons object itself, so calls chain
notes: with an empty queue it does nothing, and that was the only case run
warnings: it starts a transport on the audio device when a phrase is queued, which no run of this reference did

methods.name: SpeakQueueToEnd
methods.brief: Speaks everything queued as one buffer through one device and returns when it has finished.
methods.returns: the earcons object itself, so calls chain
notes: with an empty queue it returns at once, and that was the only case run
warnings: it occupies the thread and plays through the audio device, which no run of this reference did

methods.name: IsSpeaking
methods.brief: TRUE if a phrase is being spoken now.

methods.name: SpeechQueueDepth
methods.brief: Returns how many phrases wait in the speech queue.

methods.name: SpeechDrops
methods.brief: Returns how many phrases were dropped because the queue was full or a louder one cancelled them.

methods.name: SpeechSpoken
methods.brief: Returns how many phrases were spoken.

methods.name: SpeechGapSeconds
methods.brief: Returns the silence in seconds between a cue and its phrase, and between queued announcements.

methods.name: SetSpeechQueueMax
methods.brief: Sets how many phrases the speech queue holds before it drops more.

parameters.name: pn
parameters.role: the queue capacity, a value below 1 being ignored

methods.returns: the earcons object itself, so calls chain
notes: the capacity starts at 4

methods.name: TriggerToEarMs
methods.brief: Returns the milliseconds between firing a cue and hearing it on this pipeline, a stated figure and not a measurement.
methods.returns: a number, 419: 329 for the ring plus 90 for the device
notes: the answer is a constant in the code, whether or not the player is started

methods.name: CanAcknowledgeWithin
methods.brief: TRUE if a sound can arrive within the given time, which on this pipeline it cannot do inside 100 ms.

parameters.name: pnMs
parameters.role: the deadline in milliseconds

notes: 100 gave FALSE and 500 gave TRUE

methods.name: Stop
methods.brief: Stops the sound pool if it is open and marks the object as not started.
methods.returns: the earcons object itself, so calls chain
notes: before Start it only clears the flag

methods.name: Release
methods.brief: Stops playing and frees the pool and the motif buffers it holds.
methods.returns: nothing; it returns an empty text
notes: call it once, when you are done with the object

methods.name: IsStarted
methods.brief: TRUE if the sound pool is open.

methods.name: LastError
methods.brief: Returns the reason of the last refusal or failure.
methods.returns: a text, empty when there was none
notes: ToSoundOf also sets it when a meaning is refused

methods.name: Refusals
methods.brief: Returns how many calls were refused, for example Fire before Start or a positive duck depth.

classes.name: stzEduReader
classes.brief: Builds one self-contained HTML page for a course, which stores no output and says where each cell runs.
classes.description: The page follows the chapters that were run and observed, one article per language edition, switched by the URL hash; it needs no build tool and loads nothing from the network. It never holds an output: each cell carries a fixed sentence saying so, and keeps the author's promise lines, which are an expectation and not a result. Each cell is labelled where it ran as the guard observed it, and the cells run on the desktop, not in the browser: running them in the browser waits on ringscript. A translation is marked a draft until a native speaker has signed the unit off: the fr, ar and ha editions are drafts, 0 of 35 units reviewed by a person in each language. No institution has adopted the system yet.
classes.example:
o1.AddChapter( oC.RunChapterInQ("find-then-apply", [ "en" ])[1] )
? o1.NumberOfWorldPages()
#--> 0
? StzFindFirst("stores no output", o1.Html()) > 0
#--> 1

methods.name: init
methods.brief: Starts a reader for a course: an empty page to which observed chapters, world pages and questions are then added.

parameters.name: poCourse
parameters.role: the stzCourse the page is about: its slug titles the page and its exercises are shown after the cells

notes: the page it builds loads nothing from the network and stores no output

methods.name: AddChapter
methods.brief: Adds one edition of a chapter, already run and observed, to the reader, as an entry of its language's menu.

parameters.name: poChapter

classes.name: stzEngineTimeline
classes.brief: Keeps named events with timestamps in the engine and answers questions about them, such as how many fall in a range.
classes.description: The store lives in the engine and is shared by every stzEngineTimeline object of the process, so call Clear() first when you want a fresh one. Positions are counted from 0, in the order the events were added. Timestamps are plain numbers in the unit you choose. Duration() answers 0 today. It is not the stzTimeLine class of the datetime module.
classes.receiver: o1 = new stzEngineTimeline() o1.Clear() o1.AddEvent("start", 100) o1.AddEvent("build", 200)
classes.example:
? o1.EventCount()
#--> 2
? o1.EventLabel(1)
#--> build
? o1.EventsBetween(100, 150)
#--> 1
o1.Clear()

methods.name: init

parameters.role: the event's name, a non-empty text

parameters.name: nTimestamp
parameters.role: when it happened, as a number in any unit you choose

notes: events keep the order in which they were added

extensions.name: AddEventQ
extensions.adds: does what the method does, then returns the object, so the call can be chained

methods.name: EventCount
methods.brief: Returns how many events the timeline holds.

parameters.name: nIndex
parameters.role: the position of the event, starting at 0

methods.returns: a text; empty when the position is out of range

methods.name: EventTime
methods.brief: Returns the timestamp of the event at a position, counted from 0 in the order the events were added.

parameters.name: nIndex
parameters.role: the position of the event, starting at 0

methods.returns: a number; 0 when the position is out of range

methods.name: EventsBetween
methods.brief: Returns how many events have a timestamp from nStartTime to nEndTime, both included.

parameters.name: nStartTime
parameters.role: the lower end of the time range

parameters.name: nEndTime
parameters.role: the upper end of the time range

notes: it answers a count, not the events themselves

classes.name: stzEntity
classes.brief: Holds one named thing as a hash-list of properties: it always has a name, a type and a creation stamp, and answers questions about them.
classes.description: Build it from a hash-list such as [ :name = "Ana", :type = "person", :age = 30 ]. A missing name becomes @noname and a missing type becomes undefined, and the created stamp is set to now. Properties are read and set by name without regard to case, so Property("AGE") and Property("age") are one property, and the @ method reads, sets one or sets several in a single door. Name and type are single words that keep their case, but HasName and IsOfType compare without regard to case, so Ana and ana are one name and Person and person are one type. IsEmpty is TRUE when nothing is held beyond the name, the type and the creation stamp. Known gap, in the w13 defect file: ContainsPropertyOrValue raises for an argument that is not text.
classes.example:
? o1.Property("AGE")
#--> 30
o1.SetProperty("city", "Niamey")
? o1.ContainsValue("Niamey")
#--> 1
? o1.HasName("ANA")
#--> 1
? @@(o1.Properties())
#--> [ "name", "type", "age", "created", "city" ]

classes.name: stzEnvironment
classes.brief: Reads and changes the environment of the running process: variables, working folder, host name, user name and CPU count.
classes.description: It holds no state; every call goes to the operating system through the engine. SetVar and UnsetVar change the environment of this process only and of the processes it starts, never the machine's saved settings. ChangeDirectory moves the whole process, and Ring's load resolves relative paths against the working folder. A variable set to an empty text counts as not set for HasVar. Variables can contain secrets, so print names, not values.
classes.example:
? o1.HasVar("STZ_DOC_INVENTED")
#--> 0
? o1.SetVar("STZ_DOC_INVENTED", "hello")
#--> 1
? o1.Var("STZ_DOC_INVENTED")
#--> hello
? o1.UnsetVar("STZ_DOC_INVENTED")
#--> 1
? o1.HasVar("STZ_DOC_INVENTED")
#--> 0
? o1.CpuCount() > 0
#--> 1

warnings: the object holds no state, so every method reads the process itself

methods.brief: Returns how many variables the process has.

parameters.name: pcName
parameters.role: the variable's name

parameters.name: pcValue
parameters.role: its new value

warnings: both must be texts, else an error is raised; the real environment of the machine is not changed

extensions.name: SetVarQ
extensions.adds: does what the method does, then returns the object, so the call can be chained

parameters.name: pcName
parameters.role: the variable's name

classes.name: stzEnvironmentBridge
classes.brief: Is the one door from the environment twin to the live process: it reads variables and directory, and commits operations.
classes.description: The reads (RealVar, RealHasVar, RealCwd, CurrentRealityState) are free. ExecuteOperation is the only call that changes reality: it sets or removes a real variable, changes the real directory, or starts a real command and waits for it. Reach it only through a plan, after the narration and the risks have been read. VerifyOutcome checks afterwards that a variable is as asked.
classes.example:
? o1.RealHasVar("STZ_DOC_INVENTED_VAR")
#--> 0
? @@( o1.Capabilities() )
#--> [ "set_var", "unset_var", "change_dir", "spawn_process" ]

methods.name: init
methods.brief: Builds the bridge to the live process environment, the only door by which this twin family reaches reality.

methods.name: RealVar
methods.brief: Returns the value of a variable of the live environment.

parameters.name: pcName
parameters.role: the variable name

methods.returns: a text; an empty text when the variable is not set
notes: it reads the live environment and changes nothing

methods.name: RealHasVar
methods.brief: TRUE if the live environment has that variable.

parameters.name: pcName
parameters.role: the variable name

methods.name: RealCwd
methods.brief: Returns the working directory of the running process.

methods.name: CurrentRealityState
methods.brief: Returns a new state holding the live variables and directory, each marked as mirrored.
notes: the live environment can hold secrets: show counts and names, never values

methods.name: Constraints
methods.brief: Returns the facts that bound what the bridge acts on, which is the working directory.

methods.name: Capabilities
methods.brief: Returns the operation types the bridge can commit.
methods.returns: a list of text: set_var, unset_var, change_dir, spawn_process

methods.name: ExecuteOperation
methods.brief: Commits one operation to the live process: sets or removes a variable, changes the directory, or starts a command and waits for it.

parameters.name: oOp
parameters.role: the stzVirtualOperation to commit

methods.returns: the result of the real call for a variable or a directory change, 1 once a spawned command has finished, 0 for another type
notes: a spawned command has its output read and discarded
warnings: not run: it changes the real environment and starts real processes, so reach it only through a plan that was narrated and reviewed

methods.name: VerifyOutcome
methods.brief: Checks after a commit that reality holds what the operation asked for.

parameters.name: oOp
parameters.role: the stzVirtualOperation that was committed

methods.returns: TRUE or FALSE; checked for a variable being set or removed, and always TRUE for the other types

classes.name: stzEnvironmentState
classes.brief: Holds an in-memory environment: variables with their origin, a working directory, and a queue of commands waiting to run.
classes.description: It is the state the environment twin changes. Each variable is a [ name, value, origin ] row, the origin being mirrored for a value read from reality and virtual for one born in the twin, which is what a diff against reality needs. Apply is the hook the generic twin calls to rehearse an operation, and Clone gives the independent copy a snapshot or a rebuild starts from. Names are matched with case. Nothing here touches the real environment.
classes.example:
o1.PutVar("MODE", "dev", "virtual")
o1.SetCwd("/srv/app", "virtual")
o1.AddSpawn("make test")
? o1.VarValue("MODE")
#--> dev
? o1.Cwd()
#--> /srv/app
? o1.NumberOfPendingSpawns()
#--> 1

methods.name: init
methods.brief: Builds an empty environment state: no variables, no working directory and no pending spawns.

methods.name: HasVar
methods.brief: TRUE if a variable of that exact name is in the state.

parameters.name: pcName
parameters.role: the variable name, matched with case

methods.name: VarValue
methods.brief: Returns the value of a variable.

parameters.name: pcName
parameters.role: the variable name, matched with case

methods.returns: a text; an empty text when the variable is absent

methods.name: OriginOfVar
methods.brief: Returns where a variable came from.

parameters.name: pcName
parameters.role: the variable name, matched with case

methods.returns: mirrored for one read from reality, virtual for one born in the twin; an empty text when absent

methods.brief: Sets a variable, adding it or replacing its value.

parameters.role: the variable name

parameters.name: pcValue
parameters.role: the value, as text

parameters.role: mirrored or virtual, kept only when the variable is new

parameters.name: pcName
parameters.role: the variable name, matched with case

methods.brief: Returns the working directory of the state.
methods.returns: a text; empty until one is set

methods.name: CwdOrigin
methods.brief: Returns where the working directory came from.
methods.returns: mirrored or virtual; an empty text until one is set

methods.name: SetCwd
methods.brief: Sets the working directory and where it came from.

parameters.name: pcPath
parameters.role: the directory, as text

parameters.name: pcOrigin
parameters.role: mirrored or virtual

parameters.name: pcCommand
parameters.role: the command line, as text

methods.returns: a list of [ name, value, origin ] rows, in the order added

methods.brief: Returns a copy of the variable rows, so a clone does not share them.
methods.returns: a list of [ name, value, origin ] rows

methods.brief: Returns a copy of the queued commands.

methods.name: SetVars

parameters.name: paVars
parameters.role: a list of [ name, value, origin ] rows

methods.name: SetSpawns
methods.brief: Replaces all the queued commands at once.

parameters.name: paSpawns
parameters.role: a list of command lines

methods.name: SetCwdRaw
methods.brief: Sets the working directory and its origin without any judgement, as Clone needs.

parameters.name: pcCwd
parameters.role: the directory

parameters.name: pcOrigin
parameters.role: mirrored or virtual

methods.name: Clone
methods.brief: Returns an independent copy of the state, which a snapshot or a rebuild starts from.

methods.name: Show
methods.brief: Prints one summary line: the number of variables, the directory and the queued commands.

classes.name: stzErDiagram
classes.brief: Holds a database schema as entities, keys and relations, draws it in crow's-foot notation and checks its rules about keys.
classes.description: An entity is a box with a name band and a compartment of attributes shown as PK, FK and plain columns; a relation is an undirected line whose ends carry the cardinality. Relate reads the kind from the first entity: OneToMany, ManyToOne, OneToOne or ManyToMany. Four rules judge the schema through GovernanceFindings: every entity declares a primary key, every foreign key names an entity of the diagram, every relation is backed by a foreign key (a junction for a many-to-many), and a participation declared at a key's target end agrees with the column's nullability. A note is drawn but is not an entity and owes no key. Weak entities, inheritance and Chen's diamonds are not here. ToCanvasXT draws the diagram.
classes.receiver: o1 = new stzErDiagram("shop") o1.AddEntity("customer", "Customer") o1.AddKey("customer", "id") o1.AddEntity("order", "Order") o1.AddKey("order", "id") o1.AddForeignKey("order", "customer_id", "customer")
classes.example:
o1.Relate("customer", "order", :OneToMany)
? len(o1.Entities())
#--> 2
? o1.Relations()[1][:kind]
#--> onetomany
? @@( o1.GovernanceFindings() )
#--> [ ]
? o1.GovernanceIsSound()
#--> 1
o1.AddEntity("tag", "Tag")
? len(o1.GovernanceFindings())
#--> 1
? o1.GovernanceIsSound()
#--> 0

Build one yourself with a name, set its severity, message and checker like any stzGraphRule, and add it to a stzErRuleSet.
classes.example:
? o1.Name()
#--> every_entity_named
? o1.Domain()
#--> er

methods.name: init
methods.brief: Builds a schema rule with the given name, in the er domain.

parameters.name: pcName
parameters.role: the name of the rule, such as entity_has_key

notes: a stzGraphRule whose domain is set to er; the four built-in schema rules are made this way

classes.name: stzErRuleSet
classes.brief: Holds the four rules a schema must keep and judges a graph made from an entity-relationship diagram.
classes.description: The set carries entity_has_key and foreign_key_resolves as errors, relation_backed_by_key and participation_matches_nullability as warnings, in the er-governance set of the er domain. stzErDiagram builds one for GovernanceFindings and hands it the graph from AsRuleGraph; use the set directly to add a rule of your own before checking.
classes.example:
? o1.Name()
#--> er-governance
? o1.Domain()
#--> er
? len(o1.Rules())
