methods.name: init
methods.brief: Builds the set of the four schema rules of an entity-relationship diagram, in the er-governance set.
notes: the rules are entity_has_key, foreign_key_resolves, relation_backed_by_key and participation_matches_nullability; Check(oGraph) judges a graph made by AsRuleGraph

classes.name: stzEventBus
classes.brief: Gives access to the engine's process-wide event bus: named channels, subscribers, and payloads emitted to them.
classes.description: Channels live in the engine and are global to the process, so an emitter and an agent host in the same process communicate through two handles on one bus. An agent supervised on a channel has its perceive-and-act loop driven by emitted events and not only by a timer. Emit counts the event and keeps the payload even with no subscriber and answers how many were delivered. A consumer polls EventCount to detect new work; because DestroyChannel and ClearAll restart the count, it compares ChannelGeneration, which never repeats, to notice a channel that was remade. ClearAll resets channels other code may be watching.
classes.receiver: o1 = StzEventBus() o1.ClearAll() o1.Channel("orders") nSub = o1.Subscribe("orders")
classes.example:
? o1.SubscriberCount("orders")
#--> 1
? o1.Emit("orders", "burger")
#--> 1
? o1.EventCount("orders")
#--> 1
? o1.LastEvent("orders")
#--> burger
? o1.Unsubscribe(nSub)
#--> 0
? o1.Emit("orders", "tajine")
#--> 0
? o1.EventCount("orders")
#--> 2
? o1.EventCount("nowhere")
#--> -2

methods.name: init
methods.brief: Builds a handle on the engine's process-wide event bus; the handle holds no state of its own.
notes: StzEventBus builds the same object; two handles in one process see the same channels

methods.name: Channel
methods.brief: Declares a channel by name, doing nothing if it already exists.

parameters.name: pcName
parameters.role: the name of the channel, such as orders

methods.returns: the bus itself, so calls chain
notes: Subscribe and Emit also declare a channel they are given

methods.name: HasChannel
methods.brief: TRUE if a channel with a name exists.

parameters.name: pcName
parameters.role: the name of the channel

notes: a channel exists from its first declaration until DestroyChannel or ClearAll

methods.name: Subscribe
methods.brief: Subscribes to a channel, declaring it if needed, and returns the subscriber's id.

parameters.name: pcName
parameters.role: the name of the channel

methods.returns: a number above 0, the subscriber id
notes: ids are unique and rise; the same caller may subscribe twice and is then two subscribers

methods.name: Unsubscribe
methods.brief: Removes a subscriber by its id.

parameters.name: nSubId
parameters.role: the id Subscribe gave

methods.returns: 0 when removed; -2 for an id that is not subscribed, including one already removed

methods.name: Emit
methods.brief: Publishes a payload on a channel, declaring it if needed.

parameters.name: pcName
parameters.role: the name of the channel

parameters.name: pcData
parameters.role: the payload, turned into text

methods.returns: how many subscribers it was delivered to; 0 when there are none
notes: the event is counted and kept as the last event even when nobody is subscribed

methods.name: EventCount
methods.brief: Returns how many events were emitted on a channel since it was created.

parameters.name: pcName
parameters.role: the name of the channel

methods.returns: a number; -2 for a channel that does not exist
notes: it rises while the channel lives but DestroyChannel and ClearAll put it back to 0 or remove it, so a consumer that only tests for a bigger number than last time must treat a smaller one as a new channel and compare ChannelGeneration

methods.name: SubscriberCount
methods.brief: Returns how many subscribers a channel has.

parameters.name: pcName
parameters.role: the name of the channel

methods.returns: a number; -2 for a channel that does not exist

methods.name: LastEvent
methods.brief: Returns the most recent payload emitted on a channel.

parameters.name: pcName
parameters.role: the name of the channel

methods.returns: the payload as text; an empty text when none was emitted or the channel does not exist
notes: a number emitted is read back as text, 42 as 42

methods.name: ChannelGeneration
methods.brief: Returns which incarnation of a name a channel is, a number that never repeats in the process.

parameters.name: pcName
parameters.role: the name of the channel

methods.returns: a number above 0; -2 when no channel has the name
notes: a channel destroyed and declared again has a different generation, which is exact where a falling count can be missed

methods.name: NumberOfChannels
methods.brief: Returns how many channels exist.
notes: the bus is process-wide, so channels made by other parts of the process count

methods.name: DestroyChannel
methods.brief: Removes a channel and its subscribers.

parameters.name: pcName
parameters.role: the name of the channel

methods.returns: 0 when removed; -2 for a channel that does not exist
notes: its event count restarts from 0 if it is declared again

methods.name: ClearAll
methods.brief: Removes every channel in the process.
methods.returns: the bus itself, so calls chain
notes: useful for test isolation, but it resets channels that other parts of the process are watching

methods.name: init
methods.brief: Opens an exercise folder and reads what is needed to judge a program against it: the promises, the facts and the optional harness.

parameters.name: pcFolder
parameters.role: the exercise folder, with or without a trailing slash

notes: a check.ring turns the exercise into a harness exercise, where the learner hands in a file that is not a program
warnings: raises an error naming the exercise when the folder has no promise.ring, and another when promise.ring holds no #--> line; exercise.zknw and check.ring are optional

methods.name: Id
methods.brief: Returns the exercise's id, the last segment of its folder path.

methods.name: Folder
methods.brief: Returns the exercise's folder path, without a trailing slash.

methods.name: Promises
methods.brief: Returns the values the learner's program must print, the text after each #--> line of promise.ring.
methods.returns: a list of text, in the order they must appear
warnings: these are the expected values, the teacher's side: never show them to the learner, whose Why() never repeats them

methods.name: NeededSteps
methods.brief: Returns the steps of the mental model the exercise needs, from its needs-step facts.
methods.returns: a list of text such as finds and applies; [ ] when exercise.zknw names none

methods.name: StepWords
methods.brief: Returns the words in a learner's code that show a step of the exercise was attempted.
methods.detail: They are the <step> | seen-by | <word> facts of exercise.zknw. The three steps of chapter 1 (asks, finds, applies) keep default words when the exercise declares none; any other step without them is never seen, so the tutor always asks about it.

parameters.name: pcStep
parameters.role: the step's name, as written in a needs-step fact

methods.returns: a list of text; [ ] for a step with no declared words

methods.name: GapText
methods.brief: Returns the question the tutor asks about a step of the exercise, in a language.
methods.detail: It is the <step>: line of the exercise's own gaps.<lang>.md; failing that, the built-in text of the three chapter-1 steps. A step with no question in that language raises, and is never answered in another one.

parameters.name: pcStep
parameters.role: the step's name, as written in a needs-step fact

parameters.name: pcLang
parameters.role: the language code

warnings: raises when the exercise has no question for the step in that language

methods.name: Task
methods.brief: Returns the task text a learner reads, in one language, with carriage returns removed so that a CRLF checkout reads like an LF one.

parameters.name: pcLang
parameters.role: the language code of the task.<lang>.md file

warnings: raises an error naming the exercise and the language when there is no task file in that language; the fr, ar and ha tasks are drafts, 0 of 35 units reviewed by a person

methods.name: HasTaskIn
methods.brief: TRUE if the exercise has a task file in one language.

parameters.name: pcLang
parameters.role: the language code of the task.<lang>.md file

methods.name: Check
methods.brief: Runs a learner's program in a fresh Ring process with the library loaded and returns the verdict on it as a stzExerciseCheck.

parameters.name: pcCode
parameters.role: the learner's program, as text

methods.returns: a stzExerciseCheck: Passed() says whether every promise was kept, Why() says in the learner's terms what to look at; the call itself does not raise when the program fails
notes: the program is judged by running it, never by reading it or comparing strings; the cells and checks run on the desktop only
warnings: one process per call, so it takes seconds: the child loads the whole library; temporary _edu_run_ files are written in the current folder and removed; CheckMany does the same for a list of programs, at most 4 side by side; a line number in an error counts two library lines the learner never wrote

extensions.name: CheckMany
extensions.adds: works on a collection of items instead of one

methods.name: HasHarness
methods.brief: TRUE if the exercise has a check.ring, so that it judges a submitted file with the library's own court instead of running it as a program.

methods.name: SubmissionExtension
methods.brief: Returns the extension of what a learner hands in for this exercise.
methods.returns: .ring for a program; for a harness exercise the extension its submits fact names, such as .pia

methods.name: CheckFile
methods.brief: Reads a file and returns the verdict on its content, as Check does.

parameters.name: pcFile
parameters.role: the path of the file to read

warnings: raises a file error when pcFile cannot be opened

methods.name: WrongAnswers
methods.brief: Returns the paths of the known wrong answers, the files of the wrong subfolder.
methods.returns: a list of text, sorted by name and limited to files with the submission extension; [ ] when there is no wrong folder

methods.name: RightAnswers
methods.brief: Returns the paths of the known right answers, the files of the right subfolder.
methods.returns: a list of text, sorted by name and limited to files with the submission extension; [ ] when there is no right folder

methods.name: ProveItself
methods.brief: Runs every known wrong and right answer through the checker and counts the ones it judged correctly.
methods.returns: a hash list with wrong, wrongrefused, right, rightaccepted, failures and checks; failures names each wrong answer that passed and each right answer that failed, and checks holds a file and its verdict for every answer
warnings: one fresh process per answer, at most 4 side by side; an exercise that accepts a wrong answer or refuses a right one is a red guard

methods.name: IsProven
methods.brief: TRUE if the exercise has at least one wrong and one right answer and the checker refuses every wrong one and accepts every right one.
methods.returns: TRUE or FALSE; FALSE for an exercise with no wrong answer or no right answer

methods.name: ForbiddenWords
methods.brief: Returns the words a tutor must not say before the learner passes: the names the right answers call and the promised values.
methods.returns: a list of text without repeats; the promised values are normalized, with their spaces removed
warnings: names are the words of four characters or more written right before "(" in the right answers

methods.name: SetKind
methods.brief: Sets whether the check judged a program or a declaration that a harness court examined, which changes the wording of Why.

parameters.name: pcKind
parameters.role: decl for a submission a harness judged, an empty text for a program

warnings: the exercise sets it itself for a harness exercise; a kind other than decl reads as a program

methods.name: init
methods.brief: Builds the verdict on a learner's program: matches the promises against its run and stamps the code's SHA-256 and the time.

parameters.name: pcId
parameters.role: the exercise's id

parameters.name: pacPromises
parameters.role: the promised values, in order

parameters.name: pcCode
parameters.role: the learner's program, hashed for the evidence

parameters.name: paRun
parameters.role: the list [ stdout, exit code, stderr ] of a run already made, or [ ] to run pcCode now in a fresh process

warnings: the promises must appear in order; a promise written error: followed by a text is kept by an error that contains the text, and then a non-zero exit still passes

methods.name: Id
methods.brief: Returns the id of the exercise this verdict belongs to.

methods.name: Passed
methods.brief: TRUE if every promise was kept in order and the program exited cleanly, or the exercise promises an error.

methods.name: Output
methods.brief: Returns everything the program printed, one line per print, each ended by a line break.
methods.returns: a text; an empty text when it printed nothing
warnings: for a program that stopped with an error the text also holds the error report, including the name of the temporary file it ran from: show a learner Why, not this

methods.name: Error
methods.brief: Returns the first line of the run that reports an error.
methods.returns: a text such as Line 5 Error (R14) : Calling Method without definition: withouttwins; an empty text when the exit code was 0; "the program stopped (exit code not 0)" when the exit was not 0 and no line reports an error
warnings: the line number counts the two library lines placed before the learner's code, so it is 2 more than the line the learner wrote

methods.name: ExitCode
methods.brief: Returns the exit code of the run.
methods.returns: a number; 0 for a clean run

methods.name: Report
methods.brief: Returns, for every promise in order, whether it was kept.
methods.returns: a list of pairs of the promised text and 1 or 0
warnings: each pair holds the expected value, the teacher's side: never show it to a learner

methods.name: Hash
methods.brief: Returns the SHA-256 of the checked code, as 64 hexadecimal characters.

methods.name: CheckedAtMs
methods.brief: Returns the wall-clock time at which the verdict was built.
methods.returns: a number of milliseconds since the epoch

methods.name: Evidence
methods.brief: Returns the evidence a progress fact carries: what was run, and when.
methods.returns: a hash list with exercise, sha256, checkedatms and passed

methods.name: Why
methods.brief: Returns, in English and in the learner's own terms, what went well or what to look at, never the expected value.
methods.returns: a text a learner reads: a statement that every promise was kept, the error the program raised, or the first three lines it printed joined with a slash
warnings: a program that printed nothing reads as (nothing), in English also in fr, ar and ha

methods.name: WhyIn
methods.brief: Returns the same message as Why, in one language.

parameters.name: pcLang
parameters.role: en, fr, ar or ha

methods.returns: a text in that language: the passed message, the error line, or the first three printed lines, normalized with their spaces removed
warnings: raises an error, saying a missing translation is red and never English, for any other language; the fr, ar and ha messages are drafts, 0 of 35 units reviewed by a person

classes.name: stzExterCode
classes.brief: Runs a snippet of another language and brings its answer back as a Ring value, through a result file.
classes.description: Supports python, r, julia, c, prolog and nodejs, found by the paths in $aStzLibConfig or by SetRuntimePath. You set the code, which must assign its answer to a variable named res, and Execute wraps it with a translator, runs it with the language's program in the current folder, and writes the answer as Ring text; Result reads that text back and evaluates it, so a number, a text and nested lists cross the boundary. Output and errors of the program go to a log file. Limits seen on this machine: the R translator is rejected by R 4.5.1, and the run script is started by its bare name, which fails where NoDefaultCurrentDirectoryInExePath is 1. julia, c and prolog were not run, their programs being absent.
classes.example:
o1.SetCode("var res = [1, 2, 3].reduce((a, b) => a + b, 0);")
o1.Execute()
? o1.Result()
#--> 6

methods.name: Init
methods.brief: Builds a runner for one external language: python, r, julia, c, prolog or nodejs, in any letter case.

parameters.name: cLang
parameters.role: the language name

warnings: raises error Language 'x' is not supported for any other name

methods.name: IsLanguageSupported
methods.brief: TRUE if the runner knows the language, whatever the letter case.

parameters.name: cLang
parameters.role: the language name to test

methods.name: SetRuntimePath
methods.brief: Sets the program that runs this object's language, in place of the configured path such as d:/nodejs/nodejs-22.20/node.exe.

parameters.name: cPath
parameters.role: the full path of the interpreter or compiler

notes: the path is used inside a batch file unquoted, so a folder name with a space breaks the run (use the short 8.3 form)
warnings: the path is not checked, so a wrong one shows only when Execute fails

methods.name: SetCode
methods.brief: Stores the source text to run, in memory only; nothing is written to disk until Prepare or Execute.

parameters.name: cNewCode
parameters.role: the program text in the external language, which must assign its answer to the result variable

methods.brief: Stores the source text to run, in memory only, exactly as SetCode does.

parameters.name: cNewCode
parameters.role: the program text in the external language

methods.name: SetVerbose
methods.brief: Turns on or off the report that Execute prints after a run: command, log, working folder and file checks.

parameters.name: bVerbose
parameters.role: 1 to print the report, 0 to keep quiet

methods.name: SetResultVar
methods.brief: Chooses the name of the variable that your external code must fill with its answer; res unless changed.

parameters.name: cResVar
parameters.role: the variable name in the external language, an empty text being ignored

methods.name: Prepare
methods.brief: Deletes the files of an earlier run, then writes the source file: the translator, your code and the lines that save the answer.

methods.name: Execute
methods.brief: Writes the source, runs it with the language's program in the current folder and records the run; the answer is then read with Result.
methods.returns: nothing; the answer is kept in a result file
notes: files are created in the current folder: temp plus the language's extension, a run script, the result file and log.txt
warnings: it runs real code with a real program, so run only code you trust; with no code set it writes the source and returns without running; it raises an error naming the log when the program produced no result file, which a syntax error in your code or a missing program also causes; the run script is started by its bare name, so where the environment variable NoDefaultCurrentDirectoryInExePath is 1 the command shell refuses it and the log is missing; the R translator is itself rejected by R 4.5.1, so the language r always fails

methods.name: Run
methods.brief: Writes the source and runs it, exactly as Execute does.
methods.returns: nothing; the answer is kept in a result file
warnings: same as Execute

methods.name: Exec
methods.brief: Writes the source and runs it, exactly as Execute does.
methods.returns: nothing; the answer is kept in a result file
warnings: same as Execute

methods.name: CleanupFiles
methods.brief: Deletes the source file, the result file and the log file of this object from the current folder.
notes: the run script is deleted by Execute itself
warnings: a file that is not there is skipped without an error

methods.name: Cleanup
methods.brief: Deletes the source file, the result file and the log file of this object, as CleanupFiles does.

methods.name: CleanupRequired
methods.brief: TRUE if the language's settings ask for the files to be deleted once Result has read them.
methods.returns: TRUE or FALSE; FALSE for all six languages as shipped

methods.name: LastCallDuration
methods.brief: Returns how long the last run took, in seconds.

methods.name: Duration
methods.brief: Returns how long the last run took, in seconds.

methods.name: CallTrace
methods.brief: Returns the history of runs made by this object, oldest first.
methods.returns: a list of hash lists with language, timestamp, duration, log, exitcode and mode
warnings: the exit code is always recorded as 0, even for a run that failed

methods.name: Trace
methods.brief: Returns the history of runs made by this object, oldest first.
methods.returns: a list of hash lists with language, timestamp, duration, log, exitcode and mode
warnings: same as CallTrace

methods.name: Result
methods.brief: Reads the answer the external code saved and turns it into a Ring value: a number, a text or a list.
methods.returns: the value; an empty text when the result file is empty

classes.name: stzFacetCatalog
classes.brief: Registers the facets a cluster knows: logical competences such as graph or nlp, with their capabilities and the modules that realize them.
classes.description: A facet is a competence a cluster routes along, not a physical module. A fresh catalog holds the 18 standard facets; Define and DefinePolyglot add or override one and Drop removes one. The catalog belongs to its instance, so two clusters in one process can have different facets. MappingKindOf says whether a facet is grounded in one module, composed from several, external (served by a tool such as python) or purely logical.
classes.example:
? o1.NumberOf()
#--> 18
? @@( o1.CapabilitiesOf("graph") )
#--> [ "paths", "centrality", "planner", "rules", "orgchart" ]
? o1.MappingKindOf("vision")
#--> external
? o1.MappingKindOf("knowledge")
#--> composed
o1.Define("audio", [ "transcribe" ], [])
? o1.MappingKindOf("audio")
#--> logical

classes.name: stzFaculty
classes.brief: Declares one named, typed capability of a flow, with a deterministic floor, optional model implementations and a golden set.
classes.description: A faculty says what is done (a payload type in, a payload type out) and never which model does it, so an implementation can be swapped, or dropped to the floor, without touching the flow. Every faculty needs a floor, a plain function that always answers; a model is chosen only when it strictly beats the floor on the faculty's golden set. Every answer is judged by a court for its output type before it leaves, and an answer the court refuses comes back as a refusal and not as a value. The definition is kept in one process-wide table and the object is only a handle on its row, so copies of it agree. Scores, goldens and certainties are computed by the class from what the implementations state; no person has judged the quality of any model output.
classes.example:
? o1.Why()
#--> faculty 'position': text -> number; implementations: last (floor); golden set v1 of 0 item(s)
? @@( o1.Problems() )
#--> [ "no golden set: no model may be auto-selected without one" ]
? o1.Run("b", [ "a", "b", "c", "b" ])
#--> 4

classes.name: stzFalseObject
classes.brief: Stands for a premise that did not hold: the object a failed natural chain returns, which keeps the chain going without turning true.
classes.description: A check written as a chain, such as Q("AnnIE").AtMost(2).VowelNBQ(), answers a stzFalseObject when it fails, so the next words of the sentence can still be read without raising an error. It carries two things: the sentence that tells why the chain stopped (WhyStopped) and the object that was judged (Origin). Every counting, comparing and quantifier device answers 0 or the false object itself, so a false premise absorbs the rest of the chain. Two devices bring it back to life: Otherwise runs an action on the origin and returns it, and OrQ returns the origin so a second alternative is tried. A false object has the content 0. A chain that fails without giving a reason reads a premise in the chain did not hold. To build one honestly, let a real check fail; SetOrigin and SetWhyStopped build one by hand.
classes.example:
? o1.WhyStopped()
#--> no: expected atmost 2, found 3
? o1.Content()
#--> 0
? o1.IfSo(:Uppercase).Content()
#--> 0
? o1.Otherwise(:Lowercase).Content()
#--> annie

classes.brief: Holds the five rules a family tree is judged by: no one is their own ancestor, a union has two partners, a child has one union, parents are older, partners are not kin.
classes.description: Check takes the rule graph of a tree (AsRuleGraph) and answers the findings. A tree asks for this through its own GovernanceFindings, so a rule set is built by hand only to add a rule of your own or to run the rules on a graph. A single parent, a union with one partner, is a warning and not an error.

methods.brief: Builds the family-tree governance, the set of five rules a family tree is judged by.

classes.name: stzFamilyTree
classes.brief: Draws a family tree and answers kinship questions: a person is a box with the years beneath the name, and every child hangs from a union dot.
classes.description: A union is a small dot between two partners and every child hangs from a union, which is what makes two parents drawable: the child has one line up, to the dot, and the dot has one line to each partner. Marry joins two people and answers the union's identifier, Child and ChildOf hang children from it, and the kinship questions (PartnersOf, ChildrenOf, ParentsOf, SiblingsOf, AncestorsOf, DescendantsOf, GenerationOf) are read off the tree. Five rules judge it. Not here: adoption, step-relations, ordering siblings by birth, and dates (years are numbers). ToCanvasXT draws the tree.
classes.example:
o1.AddPersonXT("anna", "Anna", 1930, 2001)
o1.AddPersonXT("boris", "Boris", 1928, 0)
o1.AddPerson("carl", "Carl")
o1.AddPerson("dora", "Dora")
o1.AddPerson("eva", "Eva")
o1.AddPerson("fred", "Fred")
o1.ChildOf("anna", "boris", "carl")
o1.ChildOf("anna", "boris", "dora")
o1.ChildOf("carl", "eva", "fred")
? @@( o1.ChildrenOf("anna") )
#--> [ "carl", "dora" ]
? @@( o1.SiblingsOf("carl") )
#--> [ "dora" ]
? o1.GenerationOf("fred")
#--> 3
? len(o1.AncestorsOf("fred"))
#--> 4
? o1.GovernanceIsSound()
#--> 1

classes.brief: Holds the five rules a fault tree is judged by: one top, gates with two inputs, leaves with a probability, developed events, no event its own cause.
classes.description: Check takes the rule graph of a tree (AsRuleGraph) and answers the findings. A tree asks for this through its own GovernanceFindings, so a rule set is built by hand only to add a rule of your own or to run the rules on a graph.

methods.name: init
methods.brief: Builds the fault-tree governance, the set of five rules a fault tree is judged by.
warnings: the rules are one_top_event, gate_has_two_inputs, basic_event_has_probability, event_is_developed and no_event_causes_itself, in that order

classes.name: stzFaultTree
classes.brief: Draws a fault tree and computes it: the probability of the top event and the minimal cut sets, from gates and basic events.
classes.description: A fault tree says how an undesired event, the top, comes about through AND and OR gates down to basic events of known probability. Read up it is a picture of causes; computed up it is the probability of the top and the minimal cut sets, the smallest sets of basic events that bring the top about. An AND gate multiplies its inputs and an OR gate takes one minus the product of their complements, both assuming independence; where a basic event repeats under two gates that number is an approximation and CutSetProbability gives the exact one. Five rules judge the tree. Not here: NOT gates, voting gates, inhibit gates, transfer symbols, common-cause groups and importance measures. ToCanvasXT draws the tree; the probability is written inside each basic event and its name beneath.
classes.example:
o1.AddTop("top", "Pump fails to start")
o1.AddEvent("power", "No power")
o1.AddBasicXT("seized", "Motor seized", 0.05)
o1.AddBasicXT("mains", "Mains out", 0.1)
o1.AddBasicXT("battery", "Battery flat", 0.2)
o1.Develop("top", :Or, [ "power", "seized" ])
o1.Develop("power", :And, [ "mains", "battery" ])
? fabs(o1.ProbabilityOf("power") - 0.02) < 0.000001
#--> 1
? fabs(o1.TopProbability() - 0.069) < 0.000001
#--> 1
? @@( o1.MinimalCutSets() )
#--> [ [ "seized" ], [ "mains", "battery" ] ]
? o1.GovernanceIsSound()
#--> 1

methods.brief: Returns the probability of an event or a gate, computed up from the basic events.

warnings: an AND gate multiplies its inputs and an OR gate takes 1 minus the product of their complements, both assuming the inputs independent; it raises an error for a basic event with no probability, for an undeveloped event, for an event with no gate, for a gate with no input, for an unknown identifier and for an event among its own causes

methods.name: TopProbability

methods.returns: a list of lists of identifiers, the smallest sets first, each set in the order its events were added

methods.name: CutSetProbability

methods.returns: a number from 0 to 1; 0 when there is no cut set
notes: it differs from TopProbability when a basic event appears under two gates: 0.044 against 0.0494 for a sensor repeated under two branches
warnings: it raises an error beyond twelve minimal cut sets and when no top is declared; every basic event is taken independent of the others

classes.name: stzFileBlobStore
classes.brief: Stores binary objects by key in a folder on disk, the four verbs of an S3 bucket over a flat key namespace.
classes.description: Save, Fetch, Exists and Remove are the whole port; listing is by prefix. A key is never a file name: each object is a file named by the SHA-256 of its key, with the real key kept in a .key file beside it, so keys that differ only by case stay distinct, a key such as ../x cannot leave the folder, and slashes are ordinary characters. Keys are limited to 1024 bytes, as in S3. It is a real store, not a fake, and it survives a restart. It has no presigned URLs, no versioning and no replication.
classes.example:
o1.Save("photos/2026/a.jpg", "abcde")
o1.Save("Photo.JPG", "XY")
? o1.NumberOfBlobs()
#--> 2
? o1.Fetch("photos/2026/a.jpg")
#--> abcde
? o1.Exists("photo.jpg")
#--> 0
? @@( o1.KeysWithPrefix("photos/") )
#--> [ "photos/2026/a.jpg" ]
o1.Clear()

classes.description: Reach for it to act on the file as an object on the disk rather than on its text. The copy and move methods answer 1 or 0 and never touch the original when they fail; a move or rename makes FileName follow the new path. IsExecutable goes by the extension on Windows only; LastModified reads the time through stzFileInfo.

classes.name: stzFileTree
classes.brief: Holds an in-memory tree of files and folders: a flat map of paths to nodes, each with a type, content and origin.
classes.description: It is the state the file twin changes. A node is [ path, type, content, origin ], the origin being mirrored for a node read from the disk and virtual for one born in the twin, which is the seam a diff against reality needs. A node keeps its first origin when its content is replaced. Apply is the hook the generic twin calls to rehearse an operation, and Clone gives the independent copy a snapshot or a rebuild starts from. Paths are matched exactly and the tree is flat: removing a folder does not remove the nodes below it. Nothing here touches the disk.
classes.example:
o1.PutFile("/w/a.txt", "alpha", "virtual")
o1.PutFolder("/w", "virtual")
? o1.IsFile("/w/a.txt")
#--> 1
? o1.SizeOf("/w/a.txt")
#--> 5
? @@( o1.Paths() )
#--> [ "/w/a.txt", "/w" ]

Building the object has the effect of that class (an overwrite or erase intent empties the file at once, a create intent refuses an existing file). The spellings manage, manager and the old mange are accepted; an unknown intent raises an error.
classes.receiver: write("demo_note.txt", "alpha" + char(10) + "beta gamma" + char(10) + "end") o1 = new stzFileXT("demo_note.txt", "info")

? o1.Intent().Exists()
#--> 1
? o1.Intent().Size()
#--> 20

parameters.name: pcIntent
parameters.role: info, read, append, create, overwrite, erase, modify or manage (case ignored)

methods.returns: nothing; the object is built, and Intent() gives it

classes.name: stzFlow
classes.brief: Wires faculties into a data flow whose stages are checked before they run and whose results are parcels.
classes.description: A flow names faculties and never models, so any stage can be pinned to one implementation, to a set of them, or to its floor without touching the rest. It composes an stzGraph, and CheckRules, ResolvePlan and Why run nothing. Run feeds the input to the stages that have no predecessor, passes each parcel to the stage after it, stops at the first stage that refuses, and returns the value of the last stage in order, or the findings when the flow was refused. This slice has no merge, so a stage with several predecessors is a finding. Nothing here has been run against a real model: the examples use plain functions as stand-ins.
classes.receiver: f1 = StzFacultyQ("flowpos")  f1.SetInputType(:text)  f1.SetOutputType(:number) f1.SetFloor("last", "StzFindLast")  o1 = StzFlowQ("positions")  o1.AddStage("find", "flowpos", [ "a", "b", "c", "b" ])
classes.example:
? @@( o1.StageIds() )
#--> [ "find" ]
? o1.IsSound()
#--> 1
? o1.Run("c")
#--> 3
? o1.StageParcelQ("find").Why()
#--> flowpos -> last (floor) | certainty unknown

methods.name: init
methods.brief: Builds an empty flow of that name, with an empty stzGraph of its own to hold the stages.

notes: impl, floor and set hold the pins of the stage: the registry decides when all three are empty

classes.name: stzFlowParser
classes.brief: Reads the text or file of a .stzflow document and builds the stzWorkflow it records.
classes.description: The document is a workflow header with the quoted id, a type line, then sections: steps, each with label, assignedto, duration and sla lines, flow, one from -> to line per arrow, actors with name and role, and roles. The parser keeps no state and it is what ImportFlow uses; ToWorkflow writes the same format. Today a duration of two or more digits is read as text, and an assignedTo line, the spelling ToWorkflow writes, is not read.
classes.receiver: o1 = new stzFlowParser() cText = 'workflow "order"' + char(10) + "type: sequential" + char(10) + "steps" + char(10) + "receive" + char(10) + "duration: 5" + char(10) + "pack" + char(10) + "flow" + char(10) + "receive -> pack"
classes.example:
oWf = o1.Parse(cText)
? oWf.Id()
#--> order
? len(oWf.Steps())
#--> 2
? len(oWf.Edges())
#--> 1
? oWf.Steps()[1][:duration]
#--> 5

notes: one parser can read any number of texts and files

methods.brief: Reads a .stzflow file from disk and builds the workflow it describes.

parameters.name: pcFilename
parameters.role: the path of the file to read

methods.returns: a stzWorkflow; an empty text for an empty file
notes: it does not check the extension
warnings: a path that cannot be opened raises error R35 Can't create/open the file; a file with no workflow header raises error R13 Object is required, as Parse does

methods.name: Parse
methods.brief: Reads .stzflow text, a workflow header then steps, flow, actors and roles sections, and builds the workflow it describes.

parameters.name: pcContent
parameters.role: the text, a header line such as workflow "order" followed by type: and the sections

methods.returns: a stzWorkflow; an empty text for an empty text
notes: blank lines and lines starting with # are ignored; actors are read after steps, so an assignment may name an actor not yet known, which the workflow does not check
warnings: text with sections but no workflow header raises error R13 Object is required; a duration or sla of two or more digits, such as 30, comes back as text "30" and not as a number, because the reader tests the whole value with isdigit, which looks at one character; a step line assignedTo: ana is not read, because the reader compares the key with assignedto and Ring compares text case by case, and the text that ToWorkflow writes spells it assignedTo, so a written and re-read workflow loses its assignments; the same line spelt assignedto: ana is read

classes.name: stzFolder
classes.brief: Holds a folder as a position you can walk, and lists, finds, searches, edits, creates, copies and deletes the files and folders under it.
classes.description: A stzFolder is built on a path, created when it is missing, and keeps a current position, a home to return to (GoHome) and a history (GoBack). Listings are of the position, in lowercase: Files and Folders give the direct children as /name and /name/, DeepFiles and DeepFolders walk the whole tree. Find, Search and Modify come in three reaches: this folder (FindFiles, SearchInFiles, ModifyInRoot), one named child folder, and the Deep forms below. A path given to a method is read from the current position, never from the process folder, so sub1/d.txt, /sub1/d.txt and the absolute path name the same file; only the constructor, the In methods that take a folder path to search (DeepCountFilesIn and the like) and the file functions outside the class read the process folder. Whether a path is held here is decided on disk, at any depth below the position, and the . and .. segments are folded first, so a path cannot step out of the position. Many file methods finish by moving the position into the folder of the file when it is below the position; SetBatchMode(1) turns that off. The delete methods are real: DeleteFolder, DeleteAll, Erase, DeepRemoveAll, DeepErase, DeepDeleteFile and DeepDeleteFolder remove what they name, and GoUp can lift the position above the home, so point an object at a folder you can afford to lose. GoTo does not check that the folder exists, and CollapseFolders has no visible effect, each carried as a warning on its method.
classes.example:
? o1.IsReadable()
#--> 1

methods.name: IsBatchMode
methods.brief: TRUE if batch mode is on, so file and folder operations leave the current position alone.
methods.returns: TRUE or FALSE; FALSE by default

methods.name: SetBatchMode
methods.brief: Turns batch mode on or off; on, the create, delete, read and write methods no longer try to move into the folder they touched.

parameters.name: b
parameters.role: 1 to turn batch mode on, 0 to turn it off

methods.returns: nothing; the object is changed in place
notes: With it off (the default) the file methods end by moving the position into the folder of the file they touched, when that folder is below the position
warnings: Raises an error for any value but 1 or 0

methods.name: GetDirectoryPath
methods.brief: Returns the absolute path of the folder that holds a path, read from the current position.

parameters.name: _cPath_
parameters.role: a file or folder name or path, relative to the position or absolute

notes: Pure text work; the path need not exist

methods.brief: Returns the current position as text with a trailing slash, so a relative name can be joined to it directly.
notes: WorkingDirectory and pwd are the same method

methods.name: GoTo
methods.brief: Moves the current position to a folder below it, writing the old position to the history; the folder is not checked to exist.

parameters.name: _cPath_
parameters.role: a name or a path strictly below the current position

notes: MoveTo and cd are the same method; GoTo('..') is accepted as text and leaves a path with .. in it
warnings: Raises an error for an empty text or for a path that is not strictly below the position, an absolute path included when it is the position itself or above

methods.name: GoUp
methods.brief: Moves the current position to its parent folder, writing the old one to the history; it may leave the home folder.
notes: Nothing stops it going above the folder the object was created with, and the delete methods then act on that parent; Up and cdUp are the same method
warnings: Raises an error at a drive or filesystem root

methods.name: GoHome
methods.brief: Moves the current position back to the folder the object was created with, writing the old one to the history.
notes: GoToHome, GoToRoot and GoRoot are the same method

methods.name: GoBack
methods.brief: Moves the current position back to the last one in the history and removes that entry.
notes: Back and Previous are the same method
warnings: Raises an error when the history is empty

methods.name: PathHistory
methods.brief: Returns the positions the object has left, oldest first.
notes: NavigationHistory is the same method; every GoTo, GoUp, GoHome adds one

methods.name: ClearHistory
methods.brief: Empties the history of positions.
methods.returns: nothing; the object is changed in place

methods.name: IsAtHome
methods.brief: TRUE if the current position is the folder the object was created with.
notes: IsAtRoot is the same method

methods.name: RelativePathFromHome
methods.brief: Returns the path that leads from the home folder to the current position, "." at home.
methods.returns: text, such as sub1/deep1; one .. per level when GoUp has left the home folder

methods.name: DistanceFromHome
methods.brief: Returns how many folder levels lie between the home folder and the current position, 0 at home.
methods.returns: a number; a level above home counts as one, like a level below

methods.name: NavigationInfo
methods.brief: Returns pairs describing the position: home, current, relativefromhome, distancefromhome and history.
methods.returns: a list of [ key, value ] pairs

classes.name: stzFolderWatcher
classes.brief: Watches a folder in a worker thread of the engine and hands back the files added, modified or deleted since the last look.
classes.description: Watch starts the worker, which polls the folder about every 250 ms. Drain, called on your own schedule, returns the queued events as [ kind, name ] pairs, kind being ADD, MOD or DEL, and empties the queue. Stop ends the worker. Events carry the file name inside the folder, not a full path.
classes.example:
? o1.IsRunning()
#--> 0
? len(o1.Drain())
#--> 0

parameters.role: the folder to watch

notes: a second Watch on a running watcher keeps the first folder
warnings: a folder that does not exist is accepted as well: IsRunning becomes 1 and LastError stays empty, so check the folder first

methods.brief: Returns the events queued since the last call, files added, modified or deleted in the folder, and empties the queue.
methods.returns: a list of events, each [ [ kind, ADD or MOD or DEL ], [ name, the file name ] ]; [ ] when nothing happened or no watch runs
notes: poll it on your own schedule; an event appears within about a quarter of a second of the change

methods.name: Stop
methods.brief: Ends the polling worker and returns the watcher to the idle state; stopping an idle watcher changes nothing.

classes.name: stzFont
classes.brief: Holds a loaded TTF or OTF typeface and measures text with it: widths, glyph positions, caret rectangles, and which glyphs a fallback chain had to borrow.
classes.description: The font is bytes you loaded, shaped by the engine's own pipeline (bidirectional analysis, HarfBuzz, stb_truetype), so a width can be trusted for layout in any script, Arabic included. Sizes are in pixels. A text that one font cannot draw comes out as hollow boxes, one per character; AddFallback puts other fonts behind it and CoverageOf counts what was borrowed and what is still missing. The caret and hit-test queries (RectsOfRange, CaretRectAt, IndexAtPoint) count bytes, not characters. The object holds one number, the engine's id for the face, so copies of the object share the same loaded font; after Free every measurement answers 0 or an empty list (and DrawsEveryGlyphOf answers TRUE, which is misleading). A stzCanvas draws text with a font set by SetFont.

classes.name: stzForEachObject
classes.brief: Runs a piece of Ring code once for each item of a list, binding the item's values to named loop variables.
classes.description: Build it with @ForEach(p, pIn), giving the variable name or names and the data as :In = ... Then Exec (or Run, X, @) takes the code as text and evaluates it once per item. With several names, each item of the list is a list and every name is a variable inside the code; with one name, read the item through v(:Name), because the name itself is not bound. ExecN runs the code only at chosen positions, and @SetIterations narrows every later Exec to a list of positions. The code is evaluated inside the object, so collect results in a global variable. A text can be walked with a single name, but byte by byte, and an empty list or text raises an index error when run.
classes.example:
aOut = []
o1.Exec('aOut + (Char + Number)')
? @@( aOut )
#--> [ "A1", "B2", "C3" ]
aOut = []
o1.ExecN([ 3, 1 ], 'aOut + v(:Char)')
? @@( aOut )
#--> [ "C", "A" ]
? @@( o1.@Vars() )
#--> [ "char", "number" ]
? o1.@NumberOfIterations()
#--> 3
? @@( o1.@Content() )
#--> [ [ "char", [ "A", "B", "C" ] ], [ "number", [ 1, 2, 3 ] ] ]
o1.@SetIterations([ 2 ])
aOut = []
o1.Exec('aOut + v(:Number)')
? @@( aOut )
#--> [ 2 ]

classes.brief: Holds a sequence of samples and answers what frequencies it is made of: its spectrum, magnitudes, phases, dominant frequency and convolution.
classes.description: Build one with new stzFourier(aSamples), numbers or [ re, im ] pairs. Any length is transformed exactly, with a radix-2 FFT for a power of two and Bluestein's algorithm for the others, and never padded. The convention is NumPy's: the forward transform is unscaled, the inverse carries the 1/n. The Transform, Magnitudes, Phases and PowerSpectrum answers have one entry per bin; bin 1 holds the mean. Content, Real and Imaginary give back the samples. InverseTransform inverts the sequence it holds, which is the spectrum when you built the object from one.

methods.name: init
methods.brief: Builds a sequence for frequency analysis from a list of numbers, or of [ re, im ] pairs for complex samples.

parameters.name: paSequence
parameters.role: the samples, numbers or [ re, im ] pairs

warnings: anything but a list raises "give me a list of numbers (or of [re, im] pairs)", and a sample of another kind raises an error naming its position

methods.name: Content
methods.brief: Returns the real parts of the samples as a list of numbers.
notes: the imaginary parts are not in it, ask Imaginary; Real is the same method

methods.name: Real
methods.brief: Returns the real parts of the samples as a list of numbers.

methods.name: Imaginary
methods.brief: Returns the imaginary parts of the samples as a list of numbers, 0 for plain numbers.

methods.name: Count
methods.brief: Returns how many samples the sequence has.

methods.name: IsRadix2Length
methods.brief: TRUE if the number of samples is a power of two, the case that takes the plain radix-2 path.
methods.returns: TRUE or FALSE; FALSE for an empty sequence
notes: informational only: any length is transformed exactly, never padded

methods.name: Transform
methods.brief: Returns the spectrum of the sequence: one [ re, im ] pair per frequency bin, unscaled, with the NumPy sign convention.
methods.returns: a list of [ re, im ] pairs; [ ] for an empty sequence
notes: Spectrum and DFT are the same method; a 5-sample sequence gets the 5-point transform, not a padded one

methods.name: InverseTransform
methods.brief: Treats the sequence as a spectrum and returns the signal it comes from, as [ re, im ] pairs scaled by 1/n.
methods.returns: a list of [ re, im ] pairs; [ ] for an empty sequence
notes: it inverts THIS sequence, not its transform: to round-trip build a new object, new stzFourier(o.Transform()).InverseTransform() gives back 1 2 3 4 with zero imaginary parts; InverseDFT is the same method

methods.name: Magnitudes
methods.brief: Returns the size of each frequency bin, how much of that frequency is present, ignoring phase.
methods.returns: a list of numbers, one per bin

methods.name: Phases
methods.brief: Returns the phase angle of each frequency bin, in radians.
methods.returns: a list of numbers, one per bin

methods.name: PowerSpectrum
methods.brief: Returns the energy of each frequency bin, the square of its size.
methods.returns: a list of numbers, one per bin

methods.name: DominantBin
methods.brief: Returns the bin, counted from 1, that carries the most energy; bin 1, the mean, and the mirrored second half are left out.
methods.returns: a number from 2; 0 for a sequence of fewer than 2 samples
notes: a pure sine of 3 cycles over 16 samples answers 4, because bin 1 is the mean

methods.name: DominantFrequency
methods.brief: Returns the dominant frequency in cycles per sample interval, the dominant bin minus 1 over the number of samples.
methods.returns: a number; 0 for fewer than 2 samples
notes: multiply by the sampling rate to get hertz; 3 cycles in 16 samples gives 0.1875

methods.name: ConvolvedWith
methods.brief: Returns the linear convolution of the real parts with another list of numbers, which is also the product of two polynomials' coefficients.

parameters.name: paOther
parameters.role: the other list of numbers, not empty

methods.returns: a list of numbers, as long as both lists together minus 1
notes: an empty list raises "give me a non-empty list of numbers"; ConvolvedWithQ answers a stzFourier to chain on; 1 2 3 4 convolved with 1 1 is 1 3 5 7 4, up to rounding

extensions.name: ConvolvedWithQ
extensions.adds: does what the method does, then returns the object, so the call can be chained

classes.name: stzFrameGraph
classes.brief: Holds the render passes of a frame and the resources they read and write, and derives their order, lifetimes and shared targets.
classes.description: A pass declares what it reads and writes; a pass that reads what another writes must run after it, which is an edge, and the order is a topological sort over an ordinary stzGraph. A resource is live from its first write to its last read, and two resources whose lives do not overlap share one physical target, which is memory a hand-ordered frame pays for. Compile derives all of that and proves the frame: acyclic, no read before write, no resource written and never read. Findings go into a stzRuleReport. Execute runs the bodies in order inside one frame on the graphics device, with no window; without a device it answers 0.
classes.receiver: o1 = new stzFrameGraph(16, 8) o1.AddPass("Geometry", [ :Writes = [ "colour", "depth" ] ]) o1.AddPass("Blur", [ :Reads = [ "colour" ], :Writes = [ "blurred" ] ]) o1.AddPass("Composite", [ :Reads = [ "colour", "blurred" ], :Writes = [ "screen" ] ]) o1.Compile()
classes.example:
? @@( o1.Order() )
#--> [ "Geometry", "Blur", "Composite" ]
? o1.ResourceCount()
#--> 4
? o1.PhysicalTargets()
#--> 3
? o1.TargetsSaved()
#--> 1
? @@( o1.Lifetimes()[3] )
#--> [ "blurred", 2, 3 ]
? o1.Findings()[1][:message]
#--> 'depth' is written but never read
? o1.IsSound()
#--> 1

methods.name: init
methods.brief: Builds an empty frame of a given size in pixels, to which render passes are added.

parameters.name: pnW
parameters.role: the width of every render target, in pixels

parameters.name: pnH
parameters.role: the height of every render target, in pixels

notes: StzFrameGraphQ builds the same object
warnings: a width or height that is not a number raises error stzFrameGraph: give a width and a height in pixels; one below 1 raises error stzFrameGraph: a frame needs area

methods.name: AddPass
methods.brief: Declares a render pass with the resources it reads and writes, and optionally the body that draws.

parameters.name: pcName
parameters.role: the name of the pass, unique in the frame, in any letter case

parameters.name: paSpec
parameters.role: a hash list with :Reads and :Writes, each a list of resource names, and :Body, a function called as fBody(oFrameGraph, cPassName)

methods.returns: nothing; the pass is added and the graph must be compiled again. AddPassQ returns the frame graph for chaining
notes: the body only draws: the graph decides when it runs and what it draws into
warnings: a name used twice, in any letter case, raises error stzFrameGraph: pass ... is declared twice; a pass that reads nothing and writes nothing raises error ... it cannot be scheduled, because it has no edges to anything

extensions.name: AddPassQ
extensions.adds: does what the method does, then returns the object, so the call can be chained

methods.name: PassCount
methods.brief: Returns how many passes have been declared.

methods.name: ResourceCount
methods.brief: Returns how many distinct resources the passes read or write.
notes: a resource is counted once however many passes use it

methods.name: Compile
methods.brief: Derives the execution order, the lifetimes and the aliasing from the declarations, and proves the frame sound.
methods.returns: the frame graph itself, so calls chain
notes: the findings are an acyclic error when the passes form a cycle, a read_before_write error for a resource no pass writes, and a dead_resource warning for a resource written and never read, except one named screen; adding a pass afterwards makes every question refuse until the next Compile
warnings: a frame with no pass raises error stzFrameGraph.Compile: no passes declared

methods.name: Order
methods.brief: Returns the passes in the order they must run, derived so that a pass that reads a resource runs after the pass that writes it.
methods.returns: a list of pass names; [ ] when the passes form a cycle
notes: the names come back as they were declared, and a name written as a symbol such as :Geometry is the lower-case text geometry
warnings: calling it before Compile raises error stzFrameGraph: call Compile() first

methods.name: Lifetimes
methods.brief: Returns, for each resource, the step where it is first written and the step where it is last read.
methods.returns: a list of [ resource, first step, last step ] triples, steps counted from 1 in execution order
notes: a resource never read is live for its one writing step
warnings: calling it before Compile raises error stzFrameGraph: call Compile() first

methods.name: Aliasing
methods.brief: Returns which physical target each resource lives on, two resources sharing one when their lives do not overlap.
methods.returns: a list of [ resource, slot ] pairs, slots counted from 1
notes: a greedy placement over the lifetimes; a slot is reused only by a resource that starts after the previous one ended
warnings: calling it before Compile raises error stzFrameGraph: call Compile() first

methods.name: PhysicalTargets
methods.brief: Returns how many physical render targets the frame needs after aliasing.
notes: for a chain a, b, c, d where each pass reads the previous pass's output it is 2 for 4 resources
warnings: calling it before Compile raises error stzFrameGraph: call Compile() first

methods.name: TargetsSaved
methods.brief: Returns how many render targets the schedule saves against giving every resource its own.
methods.returns: a number, the resource count minus the physical targets
notes: it is the number the kill criterion of the design asks for: 0 means aliasing bought nothing
warnings: calling it before Compile raises error stzFrameGraph: call Compile() first

methods.name: Findings
methods.brief: Returns the proofs that failed or warned, in the house finding shape.
methods.returns: a list of hash lists with rule, subject framegraph, where as widthxheight, severity and message; [ ] for a clean frame
notes: the rules are acyclic, read_before_write and dead_resource
warnings: calling it before Compile raises error stzFrameGraph: call Compile() first

methods.name: IsSound
methods.brief: TRUE if the compiled frame has no finding of severity error.
notes: a dead_resource warning does not make it false
warnings: calling it before Compile raises error stzFrameGraph: call Compile() first

methods.name: Report
methods.brief: Returns the findings as a stzRuleReport, so the frame is judged by the same gate as code and security rules.
warnings: calling it before Compile raises error stzFrameGraph: call Compile() first

methods.name: Execute
methods.brief: Runs the passes in the derived order inside one frame, with one physical target for each alias slot.
methods.returns: 1 when the frame ran; 0 when no graphics device is available
notes: it needs a graphics device but opens no window; targets are made at each call, and a pass body asks TargetOf where its writes landed; release them with FreeTargets
warnings: calling it before Compile raises error stzFrameGraph: call Compile() first; a frame with an error finding raises error stzFrameGraph.Execute: the frame has ERRORS

methods.name: TargetOf
methods.brief: Returns the physical target a resource lives on during a frame, for a pass body to draw into or sample.

parameters.name: pcResource
parameters.role: the resource name, matched as written

methods.returns: the engine handle as a number; 0 before Execute, after FreeTargets, or for a name the frame does not know
notes: two resources in one alias slot answer the same handle

methods.name: FreeTargets
methods.brief: Releases the physical targets that Execute made.

classes.name: stzFunctionTask
classes.brief: Holds one call of a function with a list of up to ten parameters, recording its status, result and error.
classes.description: It is the task a stzReactiveFunc makes. Execute calls the function with the parameters and records completed with the result, or error with the real reason; it refuses a params value that is not a list and more than ten parameters with a message saying so. Then_ and Catch_ come from stzReactiveTask. The error mode is the default, which prints a failure to the console.
classes.receiver: oEngine = new stzReactive() o1 = new stzFunctionTask("add", func a, b { return a + b }, [ 2, 3 ], oEngine)
classes.example:
? o1.Status()
#--> pending
o1.Execute()
? o1.Status()
#--> completed
? o1.Result()
#--> 5
? o1.Succeeded()
#--> 1

methods.name: Init
methods.brief: Builds a task that will call a function with a list of parameters, in the pending state.

parameters.name: id
parameters.role: the task's identifier

parameters.name: f
parameters.role: the function to call

parameters.name: params
parameters.role: the arguments, a list of up to 10 values

parameters.name: engine
parameters.role: the reactive engine it belongs to

methods.returns: nothing; the task is built and not run
notes: the error mode is the default, ERROR_LOG

methods.name: Execute
methods.brief: Calls the function with the parameters and records the outcome on the task.
methods.returns: nothing; read the outcome with Status, Result and Error
notes: on success the status is completed, the result is kept and Then_ is called; on failure the status is error, the reason is on the task, and the console prints it in the default mode
warnings: a params value that is not a list records the error Reactive call params must be a list; more than 10 records Reactive call has too many params: N (the limit is 10); a failure inside the function records its real reason

classes.name: stzGDPRRuleBase
classes.brief: Holds the GDPR compliance rules for an org chart, ready to pass to CheckCompliance.
classes.description: Holds the four universal org rules and no rule of its own yet: only the name tells it from the other regimes.
classes.example:
? o1.NumberOfRules()
#--> 4

methods.name: init
methods.brief: Builds the GDPR rule base: the four universal org rules under the name GDPR; it adds no rule of its own.
methods.returns: nothing; the rule base is built
warnings: only the name tells the regimes apart today

classes.name: stzGeoAtlas
classes.brief: Binds the names and codes a caller types to the shapes of a boundary file the caller loaded, and reports what did not bind instead of guessing.
classes.description: A business table has a column of place names and wants a map: the user types USA and a shape appears. This class does the tedious and safe half: folding case, accents and punctuation, knowing that Burma and Myanmar are one country (about 50 aliases, each a fact about language, not about a border), finding a numeric id in a file that writes names, and a 2 or 3 letter code through the library's country table. The shapes are the CALLER'S file, never vendored here: the boundary data carries a position on every disputed border, a vintage and a licence the library will not own (test/graphics/atlas/README.md). A near miss is reported by Unresolved and never guessed, because a map that silently colours Niger for Nigeria is worse than one with a hole. IndexOf tries, in order, the file's id as written, the file's own name folded, an alias in either direction, then a country code. ValuesFor answers one value per feature, in the file's order, with the empty text where nothing bound: exactly what stzGeoMap.SetValues takes, so a table becomes a choropleth in two calls. Pictures, each looked at by 'stzlib-docs visual pass (a model reading the PNG)' on 2026-10-05: doc/gallery/stzGeoAtlas/table_to_map.png, a typed table drawn on the world with the unbound keys listed and the unmentioned countries hatched, RIGHT; how_a_key_resolves.png, the page of 21 keys and what each found, RIGHT; niger_regions_table.png, a table with a misspelt region, RIGHT (the misspelt region and the forgotten one are hatched and named). Index: doc/gallery/INDEX_geo.md.
classes.example:
? o1.IndexOf("AGADEZ")
#--> 1
? o1.IndexOf("Tillabery")
#--> 0

methods.name: Bind
methods.brief: Binds the atlas to a boundary file the caller loaded and indexes its names and ids; raises an error when it is not an object.

parameters.name: poFeatures
parameters.role: the stzGeoFeatures the caller loaded: the atlas carries names and never shapes

notes: StzGeoAtlas(oFeatures) builds and binds in one call

methods.name: Features
methods.brief: Returns the boundary file the atlas is bound to.

methods.name: Count

methods.name: Names
methods.brief: Returns every name the bound file uses, folded as the atlas compares them: lowercase, no accents, no punctuation.
methods.returns: a list of text, one per named feature; "fiji" first for the 110m world
notes: What a caller compares their own column against when a name will not bind

methods.name: IndexOf
methods.brief: Returns the position of the feature a key stands for: its id, its name, an alias or a country code; 0 when nothing matches.

parameters.name: pKey

notes: Order: the file's id as written, the file's own name folded, an alias in either direction, then a 2 or 3 letter code. "Brasil" does not find Brazil: no fuzzy match

methods.name: Has
methods.brief: TRUE if a key stands for a feature of the bound file.

parameters.name: pKey
parameters.role: the key as the caller typed it

methods.brief: Returns the bound file's own name for the feature a key stands for.

parameters.name: pKey

methods.returns: a list of flat lon, lat rings, the outer edge first; [ ] when nothing matches
notes: Largest by point count

methods.name: PartsOf
methods.brief: Returns every part of the feature a key stands for, islands included.

parameters.name: pKey
parameters.role: the key as the caller typed it

methods.returns: a list of parts, each a list of rings; [ ] when nothing matches

methods.brief: Returns a place for a label or a symbol: the mean of the points of the largest ring of the feature a key stands for.

methods.name: ValuesFor
methods.brief: Turns a table of key and value rows into one value per feature, in the file's order: what stzGeoMap.SetValues takes.

methods.returns: a list with one item per feature: the row's value, or "" where no row bound

methods.returns: a list of text, [ ] when everything bound
notes: Brasil and Atlantis come back from a table that also holds Brazil

classes.name: stzGeoEllipsoid
classes.brief: Holds one reference ellipsoid by name and measures on it: shortest and constant-bearing paths, destinations, meridian and parallel lengths, ECEF and ENU frames, areas.
classes.description: Fifteen ellipsoids are known (WGS84, GRS80, WGS72, GRS67, Airy1830, AiryModified, Bessel1841, Clarke1866, Clarke1880, International1924, Krassovsky1940, Everest1830, AustralianNational, SouthAmerican1969 and Sphere) and WGS84 is the default everywhere, because it is what a GPS reports. The engine speaks metres and degrees: a method ending Km answers kilometres, one ending M metres. Mind the axis order: the point methods take LATITUDE FIRST, then longitude (DistanceKm, Azimuth, DestinationKm, MidpointOf ...), while every flat list of places (AreaKm2, PathLengthKm and the Flat methods) and every stzGeoProjection method take LONGITUDE FIRST; swapping them raises nothing and measures another pair of places. Niamey to Paris is 3919.43 km on WGS84 and 3931.58 km if the arguments are swapped. A shortest path (geodesic) is not a constant-bearing path (rhumb line): New York to London is 5585.2 km by the first and 5809.8 km by the second. Pictures, each looked at by 'stzlib-docs visual pass (a model reading the PNG)' on 2026-10-05: doc/gallery/stzGeoEllipsoid/geodesic_vs_rhumb.png, a geodesic and a rhumb line on a Mercator, RIGHT (the rhumb line is straight, the geodesic bows toward the pole); doc/gallery/stzGeoEllipsoid/rings_and_areas.png, rings made with DestinationKm on an azimuthal equidistant map, RIGHT (they are true circles); ellipsoids_compared.png, six ellipsoids as the gap from WGS84 in metres and km2, RIGHT (the Sphere is 10.8 km long on Niamey to Paris). Index: doc/gallery/INDEX_geo.md.

methods.name: init
methods.brief: Builds the ellipsoid called pcName (case ignored) or the one at that place in the catalogue; raises an error for an unknown name.

parameters.name: pcName
parameters.role: the ellipsoid's name such as WGS84, Airy1830 or Sphere, or its 1-based position in StzGeoEllipsoids()

notes: An empty text builds WGS84. The catalogue holds fifteen ellipsoids; the error names them all

methods.name: Name
methods.brief: Returns the catalogue name of this ellipsoid as the engine spells it.

methods.name: Content
methods.brief: Returns the name and the defining numbers of this ellipsoid, the lengths in metres.
methods.returns: a hash list [ :name, :a, :f, :b ]: name, equatorial radius, flattening, polar radius

methods.name: EquatorialRadius
methods.brief: Returns the radius at the equator, the semi-major axis a, in metres.
methods.returns: a number of metres, 6378137 for WGS84

methods.name: PolarRadius
methods.brief: Returns the distance from the centre to a pole, the semi-minor axis b, in metres.
methods.returns: a number of metres, 6356752.3142 for WGS84

methods.name: Flattening
methods.brief: Returns how much the poles are flattened, (a - b) / a, a pure ratio.
methods.returns: a number, 0.0033528 for WGS84 and 0 for the sphere

methods.name: InverseFlattening
methods.brief: Returns one over the flattening, the form a geodesy table quotes.
methods.returns: a number, 298.257224 for WGS84, and 0 for the sphere

methods.name: Eccentricity
methods.brief: Returns the first eccentricity e, the square root of its square.

methods.name: EccentricitySquared
methods.brief: Returns the first eccentricity squared, e2 = f (2 - f).

methods.name: SecondEccentricitySquared
methods.brief: Returns the second eccentricity squared, e'2 = e2 / (1 - e2).

methods.name: ThirdFlattening
methods.brief: Returns n = (a - b) / (a + b), the quantity the meridian-arc series are written in.

methods.name: IsSphere
methods.brief: TRUE if the flattening is zero, which only the catalogue entry Sphere has.

methods.name: SurfaceAreaKm2
methods.brief: Returns the area of the whole surface of the ellipsoid in square kilometres.

methods.name: AuthalicRadiusKm
methods.brief: Returns the radius in km of the sphere that has the same surface area as this ellipsoid.
methods.returns: a number of km, 6371.007181 for WGS84

methods.name: QuarterMeridianKm
methods.brief: Returns the distance from the equator to a pole along a meridian, in km.
methods.returns: a number of km, 10001.965729 for WGS84

methods.name: GeodesicBetween

classes.name: stzGeoFeatures
classes.brief: Holds the polygons, lines and points of a boundary file whole, every part and every hole, read from GeoJSON or TopoJSON, and answers what lies where.
classes.description: Build one with StzGeoFeaturesFromJson, StzGeoFeaturesFromTopoJson or StzGeoFeaturesFromJsonWhere, which also compute the boxes that make point-in-region tests fast. Each feature is a kind, an id, a hash list of properties and its parts; a polygon part is a list of rings, the first the outer edge and every one after it a hole. Every ring is closed, whichever format it came from. Coordinates are longitude then latitude, degrees, as both formats require, and every place-taking method here is LONGITUDE FIRST (Contains, IndexAt, Within). Nothing is simplified or reprojected, and this library vendors no boundary data: the atlas files are the caller's (test/graphics/atlas/README.md). Areas are measured on WGS84. One trap in the windows: a feature that crosses the antimeridian (Fiji, Russia, Antarctica) has a bounding box 360 degrees wide whose middle falls anywhere, so Within and IndicesWithin take Fiji for an Africa window. Pictures, each looked at by 'stzlib-docs visual pass (a model reading the PNG)' on 2026-10-05: doc/gallery/stzGeoFeatures/parts_holes_lookup.png, parts, holes, an IndexAt raster of Niger and South Africa's hole, RIGHT; doc/gallery/stzGeoFeatures/window_and_areas.png, the areas panel RIGHT and the Within panel WRONG (Fiji is taken, see FINDINGS_geo.md); lines_points_kinds.png, a river, wells and a lake with a hole read from GeoJSON, RIGHT. Index: doc/gallery/INDEX_geo.md.

? o1.Count()

#--> Berea
? o1.IndexAt(8, 5)
#--> 2

classes.name: stzGeoField
classes.brief: Holds a quantity that has a value everywhere, a grid of numbers over longitude and latitude, and draws it as a classed raster, as contours and with its legend.
classes.description: The grid is [ lon0, lat0, dlon, dlat, nx, ny ] with row 0 the SOUTH row, and an unknown node is the empty text, never a number: the commonest way an elevation map acquires a trench eleven kilometres deep is a NODATA of -9999 read as a depth. A field comes from StzGeoDensityField (the kernel density of a stzGeoPoints, in places per km2, edge-corrected and clipped to the window), from StzGeoFieldFromAsciiGrid (an ESRI ASCII grid, whose first text row is the north row and whose xllcorner is turned into a node centre) or from stzGeoSamples (inverse distance weighting and kriging). Classes must be set before DrawOn, which raises otherwise. The raster is resampled through the projection pixel by pixel, so a conic does not turn cells into wrong quadrilaterals. A field in per km2 refuses a projection that does not preserve area (FindingsOn). Set classes, ramp and unit on the field BEFORE putting it in a list: Ring copies an object it stores, so a change made through the list does not reach the original. Pictures, each looked at by 'stzlib-docs visual pass (a model reading the PNG)' on 2026-10-05: doc/gallery/stzGeoField/rain_kriging.png, IDW, kriging and kriging variance of invented gauges, RIGHT (the variance is low at each gauge and high in the gaps); density_and_contours.png, a kernel density as raster and contours, RIGHT; ascii_grid_terrain.png, an ASCII grid read three ways, WRONG in one detail (a scatter of white pixels in the lowest class, see FINDINGS_geo.md; the library no longer draws it, counted by pixels on 2026-10-18, but this picture predates that and is to be redrawn and looked at again). Index: doc/gallery/INDEX_geo.md.

classes.name: stzGeoMap
classes.brief: Holds a map made of layers: a projection and a set of features, with values, classes, groups, labels, insets, legends, scale bar, sun and flows drawn on a canvas.
classes.description: Build it with StzGeoMap(oProjection, oFeatures) after fitting the projection to the features. The data layer takes one value per feature (SetValues, from stzGeoAtlas.ValuesFor, CountPointsIn or ValuesFromArea) or named groups (SetGroups), the classes are the author's (SetClasses, SetRamp, SetOpenTop) and a region with no value is hatched, never coloured as zero. SetPaper tells the map its sheet and should be the first call: labels are kept on it and the scale bar and the stream- density raster are measured over it. DrawSheetOn is the statistical map: dark hairline borders, the no-data hatch and the selection outlined; DrawLabelsOn writes a name inside its region or numbers it with a key; AddInset magnifies a place too small to label. A map judges itself (Findings, IsSound): a choropleth, a membership map or hexagon bins on a projection that is not equal-area is an error, as is a number with no key. Behaviour to know: with values set and no classes, ClassOf, ColourOf and the Draw methods that colour raise an error that names SetClasses (the edges are the author's, so there is no default scheme); an inset takes the parent's open top; with no SetPaper the scale bar and the stream-density raster use the extent of the features; DensityPointsIn is per 10000 km2, not per km2. Pictures, each looked at by 'stzlib-docs visual pass (a model reading the PNG)' on 2026-10-05: doc/gallery/stzGeoMap/niger_density.png, a density choropleth with inset, legend, scale bar and north arrow, CORRECTED 2026-10-16 (the Niamey inset was grey instead of red because DrawInsetsOn ignored SetOpenTop; redrawn after the fix, the inset matches the parent, see FINDINGS_geo.md); world_area.png, country areas on Equal Earth with a hatched no-data region, RIGHT; africa_blocs.png, a membership map, RIGHT; daynight_world.png, the night side and twilight on 2026-10-05, RIGHT; hexbin_flows.png, hexagon bins, area-true circles and great-circle routes, RIGHT; wind_streams.png and wind_arrows.png, an invented wind field, RIGHT as far as a picture can say. Index: doc/gallery/INDEX_geo.md.
classes.receiver: o1 = StzGeoMap(oP, oN)  # oN = StzGeoFeaturesFromJson(read("../graphics/niger_adm1.geojson")), oP = StzGeoConicFor(oN, :ConicEqualArea) fitted to oN
classes.example:
? o1.Features().Count()
#--> 8
? o1.LabelMode()
#--> auto

classes.name: stzGeoPoints
classes.brief: Holds a list of places and the window they were observed in, and answers whether they are clustered, scattered or random, where their middle is and which way they spread.
classes.description: A pattern is never a bare list: it is the places AND the region, because a hundred wells in Tunisia and the same hundred in Niger are one list and two opposite answers. The places are one flat list lon, lat, lon, lat, ... (longitude first); distances are kilometres on a sphere of 6371 km, areas on WGS84. The measures are Clark-Evans (edge-corrected by Donnelly), Ripley's K, L, G and F, the null band by simulation (Envelope, 39 simulations being the classic count), the mean centre, the spatial median and the standard deviational ellipse. Three generators make patterns whose truth is known, all seeded so a picture does not move: Sample (uniform), SampleClustered (Matern) and SampleDispersed (hard core); StzGeoProcess is the general form. A point outside the window is reported by Outside and Findings, never dropped. Pictures, each looked at by 'stzlib- docs visual pass (a model reading the PNG)' on 2026-10-05: doc/gallery/stzGeoPoints/three_patterns.png, three invented patterns in Niger with ellipse, centres and Clark-Evans verdicts, RIGHT (random, clustered and dispersed are named as the patterns were made); ripley_g_f.png, L with its band, G and F, RIGHT (L climbs far above the band for clusters, G stays at 0 below the hard-core distance for the dispersed pattern); outside_the_window.png, places across the border counted but flagged, RIGHT. Index: doc/gallery/INDEX_geo.md.

classes.name: stzGeoProcess
classes.brief: Holds one of seven point processes, a mechanism for putting points down, with its parameters, and generates patterns from it and judges a pattern against it.
classes.description: The seven are Poisson (no interaction, random count), Binomial (the same with a fixed count), Inhomogeneous (no interaction, varying intensity from a surface), MaternCluster (parents you never see, children in a disc), Thomas (children scattered by a Gaussian, so a cluster has a scale but no edge), MaternII (inhibition by deletion, which has a ceiling) and SSI (inhibition by refusal, which keeps packing). Asking whether a pattern is more clustered than a model that already explains something, not than complete spatial randomness, is the point. The setters write three shared slots, shown by Content: a (intensity, count or parent intensity), b (mean children) and c (radius, sigma or hard-core distance). GenerateIn throws one pattern in the window of a stzGeoPoints; EnvelopeOf, EscapesOf and VerdictOn judge an observed pattern against the band the process makes: 39 simulations being the classic count, and the band widens with the count. Counts of the cluster processes vary widely between seeds (a standard deviation of about 90 on a mean of 190). Known gaps: PatternIn raises today, and ExpectedCount for Inhomogeneous is the mean of the whole grid times the window area. Pictures, each looked at by 'stzlib-docs visual pass (a model reading the PNG)' on 2026-10-05: doc/gallery/stzGeoProcess/seven_processes.png, one pattern from each process, RIGHT (clusters compact, inhibited processes evenly spaced, the inhomogeneous one follows its field); null_models.png, one pattern against three nulls, RIGHT (it escapes Poisson and Binomial everywhere and never the MaternCluster that made it); matern_ii_ceiling.png, survivors against proposal rate, RIGHT (MaternII levels off near the ceiling, SSI packs about twice as many). Index: doc/gallery/INDEX_geo.md.
