classes.name: stzGeoProjection
classes.brief: Holds the choice of how to flatten the sphere: one of 44 named projections with its rotation, parallels, scale and clip, and answers where a place goes on paper and what place a pixel is.
classes.description: The object keeps eleven numbers (Params) and crosses the bridge to the engine with them on every call, so the Ring object is the single source of truth. Project takes LONGITUDE FIRST, then latitude, and answers paper units with y growing downward, or an empty list for a place behind a globe or without an image; Invert goes back. A new projection has scale 150 and translation 480, 250: use a Fit method (FitToSphere, FitSphereIn for the world, FitFeaturesIn, FitPointsIn, FitFeatureIn for a place) to put the picture in the box you draw in. Lines come back as pieces, cut where a flat map's seam or a globe's horizon cuts them. The sphere is a sphere: no projection here uses an ellipsoid (stzGeoEllipsoid measures on one). IsEqualArea and IsConformal say what the projection claims, Distortion and HoldsItsClaim measure it, and stzGeoMap refuses a choropleth on a projection that is not equal-area. Pictures, each looked at by 'stzlib-docs visual pass (a model reading the PNG)' on 2026-10-05: doc/gallery/stzGeoProjection/projections_compared.png, six projections with Tissot circles, RIGHT (Mercator circles swell toward the poles, the equal-area ones keep their size and squash); globe_routes.png, an orthographic globe with great-circle routes and range rings, RIGHT; niger_conic_utm.png, Niger on a conic and on a Mercator, RIGHT (the printed area scales 1.06 and 1.18 are the secant squared of 13.5 and 23 degrees). Index: doc/gallery/INDEX_geo.md.

methods.name: init
methods.brief: Builds the projection called pKind (case ignored) with default parameters; raises an error naming all 44 kinds when pKind is unknown.

parameters.name: pKind
parameters.role: the projection's name as text or a symbol, such as :Mercator, :EqualEarth or :Orthographic

notes: The defaults are scale 150, translation 480, 250, no rotation. The conics start with parallels 30 and 30; the others with 0 and 0

methods.name: Name
methods.brief: Returns the canonical name of the projection, as the engine spells it.

methods.name: KindNumber
methods.brief: Returns the engine's own index of the projection, counted from 0 in the order StzGeoProjectionKinds lists them.
methods.returns: a number from 0 to 43, 1 for Mercator

methods.name: Params
methods.brief: Returns the eleven numbers that define the projection, in the order the engine reads them.
methods.returns: a list [ kind, yaw, pitch, roll, parallel1, parallel2, scale, translateX, translateY, clipAngle, precision ]
notes: The object holds nothing else, so this list is the whole truth about it

methods.name: DistortionAt
methods.brief: Returns how the projection distorts the map at one place: scales along and across, area scale and bending.

parameters.name: pnLon
parameters.role: longitude in degrees east

parameters.name: pnLat
parameters.role: latitude in degrees north

methods.returns: a hash list [ :h, :k, :a, :b, :areal, :angular, :crossing ]: meridian and parallel scale, greatest and least scale, area scale, largest angle bent in degrees, angle at which they cross
notes: On Mercator at 70 N the area scale is 8.55 and no angle is bent. 1 means true

methods.name: ArealScaleAt
methods.brief: Returns how many times larger or smaller than on the ground a small area at this place is drawn.

parameters.name: pnLon
parameters.role: longitude in degrees east

parameters.name: pnLat
parameters.role: latitude in degrees north

methods.returns: a number, 1 where true, 8.55 for Mercator at 70 degrees north, 0 when the place has no image
notes: Equal-area projections answer 1 everywhere

methods.name: AngularDistortionAt
methods.brief: Returns the largest angle, in degrees, that the projection bends at this place.

parameters.name: pnLon
parameters.role: longitude in degrees east

parameters.name: pnLat
parameters.role: latitude in degrees north

methods.returns: a number of degrees, 0 for a conformal projection and 0 when the place has no image

methods.name: Distortion
methods.brief: Returns the area and angle distortion of the whole map, weighted by the ground each cell covers, over a 72 by 36 grid.
notes: Mercator: mean area x3.11 and largest x58.7; EqualEarth: area 1 everywhere and mean bend 29.1 degrees

extensions.name: DistortionXT
extensions.adds: the extended form: more parameters than the base method

methods.name: HoldsItsClaim
methods.brief: TRUE if the measured distortion agrees with what the projection claims: area scale 1 for equal-area, no bend for conformal.
notes: A check on the formulas, not on a map

methods.name: IndicatrixAt
methods.brief: Returns the projected outline of a small circle of true radius pnRadiusDeg around a place, Tissot's indicatrix, 48 points.

parameters.name: pnLon
parameters.role: longitude in degrees east of the circle's centre

parameters.name: pnLat
parameters.role: latitude in degrees north of the circle's centre

parameters.name: pnRadiusDeg
parameters.role: radius of the circle on the ground, in degrees of arc

methods.returns: a flat list of 96 numbers x, y, x, y, ... in paper units, to draw as a closed polygon
notes: Built by projecting the circle, so it shows the bending an ellipse could not

extensions.name: IndicatrixAtXT
extensions.adds: the extended form: more parameters than the base method

methods.name: IsEqualArea
methods.brief: TRUE if the projection preserves areas, so a region of the ground has the same area on paper everywhere.
notes: A choropleth of a density wants this

methods.name: IsConformal
methods.brief: TRUE if the projection preserves angles, so small shapes keep their form.

methods.name: IsAzimuthal
methods.brief: TRUE if the projection is azimuthal, drawing the sphere around one centre point.

methods.name: IsConic
methods.brief: TRUE if the projection is a cone developed on two standard parallels, whose name starts with Conic.
notes: Polyconic is not counted

methods.name: Rotate
methods.brief: Turns the sphere under the map by yaw, pitch and roll, in degrees, as d3 does; a missing roll is 0.

parameters.name: paLPG
parameters.role: the rotation as [ yaw, pitch, roll ] in degrees, or [ yaw, pitch ]

notes: To put a place at (lon, lat) in the middle rotate by [ -lon, -lat, 0 ]. A roll puts north somewhere other than up

extensions.name: RotateQ
extensions.adds: does what the method does, then returns the object, so the call can be chained

methods.name: CenterOn
methods.brief: Rotates the sphere so the place at (pnLon, pnLat) sits in the middle of the map.

parameters.name: pnLon
parameters.role: longitude in degrees east of the new centre

parameters.name: pnLat
parameters.role: latitude in degrees north of the new centre

notes: The same as Rotate([ -pnLon, -pnLat, 0 ])

extensions.name: CenterOnQ
extensions.adds: does what the method does, then returns the object, so the call can be chained

methods.name: Parallels
methods.brief: Sets the standard parallels, in degrees north; a single number serves for both.

parameters.name: paP

extensions.name: ParallelsQ

methods.name: Scale

methods.name: Translate

methods.name: ClipAngle

methods.name: Precision

classes.name: stzGeoSamples
classes.brief: Holds measurements at places, rain gauges say, and estimates the value in between by inverse distance weighting or ordinary kriging, with the error kriging owes.
classes.description: The measurements are one flat list lon, lat, value, ... and the window is the ground the estimate is made over and clipped to. Three answers, in the order an analyst uses them: IDWField (needs no model, tells nothing of its error, never leaves the measured range), Variogram with FitVariogram (the curve everything else is read from: nugget, sill and range) and KrigeFields, which returns TWO fields, the estimate and its variance, together on purpose: the variance depends only on where the gauges are and on the variogram, never on the values. A model must be adopted (FitAndUse) before GammaAt, KrigeAt, KrigeFields and CrossValidate, which raise otherwise. Kriging expects a field without a trend: for gauges whose value rises or falls steadily the Gaussian fit makes an estimate that leaves the measured range by tens of thousands. Nothing is clamped, and Findings reports it as an error, so IsSound is FALSE: use a bounded model or take the trend out first. Pictures, each looked at by 'stzlib-docs visual pass (a model reading the PNG)' on 2026-10-05: doc/gallery/stzGeoSamples/variogram_and_fit.png, gauges over an IDW surface beside the variogram and its three fitted models, RIGHT; kriging_transect.png, the estimate with isohyets and the doubt along a line, RIGHT (the band pinches at gauges and swells in gaps); kriging_on_a_trend.png, the same method on a trend, WRONG (white inside the country marks kriged values far outside the classes, see FINDINGS_geo.md; Findings now says so as an error). Index: doc/gallery/INDEX_geo.md.

parameters.name: pnI
parameters.role: the position of the measurement, from 1

methods.brief: Returns the lowest measured value.

methods.name: MaxValue
methods.brief: Returns the highest measured value.

methods.name: IDWField
methods.brief: Returns an inverse-distance-weighted surface over the window as a stzGeoField, clipped to the window.

parameters.name: pnCellKm
parameters.role: the size of a grid cell in km

parameters.name: pnPower
parameters.role: how fast a gauge's vote falls with distance, 2 being usual and a higher power giving bullseyes

methods.returns: a stzGeoField, 28 columns by 22 rows for Niger at 60 km
notes: Raises an error for a power of 0 or less. A weighted mean never leaves the measured range, and says nothing of its own error

methods.name: Variogram
methods.brief: Returns half the mean squared difference of pairs of measurements, against their distance, in pnLags bins.

parameters.name: pnLags
parameters.role: how many distance bins

parameters.name: pnMaxKm
parameters.role: the greatest distance in km, 0 for half of the greatest distance in the data

methods.returns: a list of [ h, gamma, pairs ]: the bin's distance in km, its semivariance and the number of pairs
notes: The diagnostic almost nobody draws: near 0 for close pairs, rising to a plateau, the sill, at the range

methods.name: FitVariogram
methods.brief: Fits a variogram model to the data's 12-lag variogram and returns it, without adopting it.

parameters.name: pcModel
parameters.role: the model to fit: :Spherical, :Exponential, :Gaussian, or :Best to fit all three and keep the least weighted residual

methods.returns: a hash list [ :model, :nugget, :sill, :range, :rss ]; model is "spherical", "exponential" or "gaussian"
notes: Raises an error for another name or for fewer than two bins. Data with a trend can fit a Gaussian model that makes kriging leave the measured range; Findings reports it once the model is adopted

extensions.name: FitVariogramXT
extensions.adds: the extended form: more parameters than the base method

methods.name: SetModel
methods.brief: Adopts a fitted model as the one kriging uses.

parameters.name: paModel
parameters.role: a model as FitVariogram answers it, with at least four items

notes: Raises an error for anything shorter

extensions.name: SetModelQ
extensions.adds: does what the method does, then returns the object, so the call can be chained

methods.name: Model
methods.brief: Returns the model kriging will use.
methods.returns: a hash list [ :model, :nugget, :sill, :range, :rss ], or [ ] until one is set

methods.name: FitAndUse
methods.brief: Fits a variogram model and adopts it in one move.

parameters.name: pcModel
parameters.role: the model to fit: :Spherical, :Exponential, :Gaussian, or :Best

notes: Kriging and GammaAt raise an error until a model is adopted. The fit is not bounded: on gauges with a trend a Gaussian fit makes kriging answer tens of thousands outside the measured range, and nothing here clamps it
warnings: Check Findings or IsSound after adopting: they now flag that estimate as an error, and the cure is a bounded model (:Spherical or :Exponential) or a detrended set

methods.name: GammaAt
methods.brief: Returns the adopted model's semivariance at a distance, for drawing the curve over the variogram.

parameters.name: pnHkm
parameters.role: the distance in km

notes: Raises an error until a model is adopted

methods.name: KrigeFields
methods.brief: Returns the ordinary-kriging estimate and its variance as two fields, from one factorisation.

parameters.name: pnCellKm
parameters.role: the size of a grid cell in km

methods.returns: a list of two stzGeoField: the estimate, then the kriging variance with the unit "kriging variance"
notes: Raises an error with no model, with two gauges at one place that read differently, or past 1200 gauges
warnings: The estimate is NOT held to the measured range. On gauges with a trend the Gaussian fit can make it leave that range by tens of thousands, and it is returned as computed, never clamped. Findings reports it as an error from the moment this has run

methods.name: KrigeAt
methods.brief: Returns the kriging estimate and its variance at one place.

parameters.name: pnLon
parameters.role: longitude in degrees east

parameters.name: pnLat
parameters.role: latitude in degrees north

methods.returns: a list [ estimate, variance ]; the variance is 0 at a gauge
notes: LONGITUDE FIRST. Raises an error until a model is adopted. Far outside the window it answers about the mean with a variance near the sill

methods.name: CrossValidate
methods.brief: Predicts every gauge from all the others and returns the average error and the root mean square error.
methods.returns: a hash list [ :bias, :rmse ] in the units of the values
notes: The honest test of an interpolator. Raises an error until a model is adopted

methods.name: Findings
methods.brief: Returns what is wrong with the set and its fit, as entries of severity warning or error.
notes: Gauges outside the window and fewer than 20 gauges are warnings. The range rule is an error beyond the window's diagonal and a warning beyond half of it. Once a model is adopted the estimate is checked too: it is an ERROR (rule the_estimate_is_inside_the_data) when kriging leaves the measured range by more than the spread of the data itself, read from the last KrigeFields or else from a 6 by 6 lattice of probes (up to 200 gauges; beyond that only a KrigeFields run is checked)

methods.name: IsSound
methods.brief: TRUE if the set has no finding of severity error.
notes: Warnings do not count. A kriging that leaves the measured range by more than the spread of the data is an error, so such a set is not sound

classes.name: stzGoal
classes.brief: Holds the target shape of a domain model, so the gap between it and a knowledgebase says which question to ask next.
classes.description: A goal is a pure specification and reads no global world: Gaps(oKB) is given the knowledgebase and answers what is missing in that one graph. RequireEach demands a relation of every entity of a type, RequireOne of one named subject. The graph is deliberately not stored, because a stored object is copied and would go stale. Build it with new stzGoal() or StzGoalQ().
classes.example:
oKB = new stzKnowledgeGraph("menu")
oKB.Know("margherita", "dish")
o1.RequireEach("dish", "contains")
? o1.Gaps(oKB)[1][3]
#--> every dish needs 'contains'
oKB.KnowRelation("margherita", "contains", "tomato-sauce")
? o1.IsSatisfied(oKB)
#--> 1

methods.name: init
methods.brief: Builds a goal with no requirement yet, which any knowledgebase satisfies.

methods.name: RequireEach
methods.brief: Adds the schema requirement that every entity of a type bears a relation; both names are trimmed and lowercased.

parameters.name: pcType
parameters.role: the entity type, such as dish

parameters.name: pcRel
parameters.role: the relation every entity of that type must bear, such as contains

methods.returns: the goal itself, so calls chain

methods.name: RequireOne
methods.brief: Adds the requirement that one named subject bears a relation; both names are trimmed and lowercased.

parameters.name: pcSubject
parameters.role: the entity that must bear the relation

parameters.name: pcRel
parameters.role: the relation, such as run-by

methods.returns: the goal itself, so calls chain

methods.name: Requirements
methods.brief: Returns the requirements added so far, the each pairs and the one pairs.
methods.returns: a list [ [ each, pairs ], [ one, pairs ] ], every pair being [ name, relation ]

methods.name: Gaps
methods.brief: Returns the slots of the goal that a knowledgebase does not fill yet, each with the reason, so the next question can be asked.

parameters.name: poKB
parameters.role: the stzKnowledgeGraph to read, passed in and never stored

methods.returns: a list of [ subject, relation, why ] rows; empty when nothing is missing
notes: the order is the schema rows first, then the one-subject rows
warnings: raises an error when the argument is not a stzKnowledgeGraph; a subject missing under both RequireEach and RequireOne is listed twice, once with each reason

methods.name: IsSatisfied
methods.brief: TRUE if the knowledgebase leaves no gap, which an empty goal always does.

parameters.name: poKB
parameters.role: the stzKnowledgeGraph to read

classes.name: stzGovernance
classes.brief: Holds governance as declared contracts: risk tiers, permissions, authority levels, commitments, decommissioning, postures and reversibility, with a decision lineage.
classes.description: Permission (what an actor can do) is kept apart from authority (what it should do alone). MayProceed composes both with the action's risk tier before anything happens, and every verdict is explained by Why. The same object holds forward-only commitments, decommission contracts, trust postures, reversibility classes (MayExecuteFor composes the last two) and a registration gate (MayRegister). Every decision can be recorded with the authority and risk of that moment, kept in a bounded lineage you can query by id, actor, action or time. Save and LoadFrom keep the regime and the lineage in a .zgov file. The data lives in a shared table, so copies of the object see the same regime.
classes.receiver: o1 = new stzGovernance("kitchen-ops") o1.DeclareRisk("send-invoice", 3) o1.GrantPermission("billing-agent", "send-invoice") o1.SetAuthority("billing-agent", :Delegated)
classes.example:
? o1.MayProceed("billing-agent", "send-invoice")
#--> 0
? o1.Why()
#--> refused: 'billing-agent' holds 'delegated' authority (level 2) but 'send-invoice' is risk tier 3 (SHOULD does not cover it)
o1.SetAuthority("billing-agent", :Autonomous)
? o1.MayProceed("billing-agent", "send-invoice")
#--> 1
? o1.Why()
#--> allowed: permission held AND 'autonomous' authority (level 3) covers risk tier 3

methods.name: init
methods.brief: Builds a governance of declared contracts under a name, with an empty regime and an empty decision lineage.

parameters.name: pcName
parameters.role: the governance's name, as text

notes: the regime and the lineage live in a shared table, so copies of the object see the same data; only Name_ and Why belong to each copy
warnings: build it with parentheses: without them init is skipped and every table call raises

methods.brief: Returns the sentence that explains the last verdict this object gave.

parameters.role: :Advisory (level 1), :Delegated (2), :Autonomous (3) or :EmergencyOverride (4)

classes.name: stzGpu
classes.brief: The doorway to the GPU plane: describe a computation with stzKernelMaker, hand it data, get data back, and calibrate where the GPU pays.
classes.description: Run is data in, data out; UploadQ and ApplyOnQ keep vectors resident to chain kernels without transfers. A one-shot Run pays upload, dispatch and readback, and for elementwise work the CPU usually wins: the GPU pays in the resident form and in compute-dense work. The device opens lazily on the first call that needs it; on a machine with no GPU IsAvailable answers FALSE and the data paths raise a clear error, while kernel authoring needs no device. Calibrate, CalibrateShaped, the Foundry methods and Verify measure the machine and persist their findings in the calibration file that later sessions load. Wake lifts an idle laptop GPU out of its power state before a timing. Only FirstError, LastError and ClearErrors were run for this documentation: the GPU sleeps on this machine and was left alone, so every other method was read from the code.
classes.example:
o1.ClearErrors()
? len(o1.FirstError())
#--> 0

methods.name: init
methods.brief: Creates a handle on the GPU plane; the device itself is opened lazily by the first call that needs it.
notes: nothing touches the device here

methods.name: IsAvailable
methods.brief: TRUE if a GPU device was found and initialised, which the first call pays for once.
notes: not run: it uses the GPU, which sleeps on this machine and was left alone; read from the code
warnings: initialises the device on its first use, which can wake a sleeping GPU

methods.name: DeviceName
methods.brief: Returns the name of the selected GPU adapter, or an empty text when there is none.
notes: not run: it uses the GPU, which sleeps on this machine and was left alone; read from the code
warnings: initialises the device on its first use

methods.name: AdapterCount
methods.brief: Returns how many GPU adapters the engine found.
notes: not run: it uses the GPU, which sleeps on this machine and was left alone; read from the code
warnings: initialises the device on its first use

methods.name: UploadQ
methods.brief: Uploads a list of numbers to the device as one resident buffer and returns the buffer.

parameters.name: paNumbers
parameters.role: a non-empty list of numbers, stored as f32

notes: not run: it uses the GPU, which sleeps on this machine and was left alone; read from the code
warnings: a buffer lives on the device until Free is called, or until the engine evicts it under pressure; raises an error when no GPU device is available on the machine; an empty or non-list argument raises an error

methods.name: Run
methods.brief: Runs an elementwise kernel over bound vectors and returns the result as a list of numbers, freeing every temporary.

parameters.name: poKernel
parameters.role: the stzKernelMaker that describes the computation

parameters.name: paBindings
parameters.role: a list such as [ :A = aNumbers, :alpha = 2.5 ] that binds each declared vector to a list and each scalar to a number

notes: not run: it uses the GPU, which sleeps on this machine and was left alone; read from the code
warnings: a one-shot run pays upload, dispatch and readback, so for elementwise work the CPU usually wins; a missing binding or vectors of unequal lengths raise an error naming them; raises an error when no GPU device is available on the machine

extensions.name: RunQ
extensions.adds: does what the method does, then returns the object, so the call can be chained

methods.name: ApplyOnQ
methods.brief: Runs a multi-input kernel over buffers that are already resident, with no transfer, and returns the result as a new resident buffer.

parameters.name: poKernel
parameters.role: the stzKernelMaker that describes the computation

parameters.name: paBindings
parameters.role: a list such as [ :A = oBuf1, :B = oBuf2, :alpha = 2 ] that binds each vector to a stzGpuBuffer and each scalar to a number

notes: not run: it uses the GPU, which sleeps on this machine and was left alone; read from the code
warnings: buffers of different lengths, or a vector not bound to a buffer, raise an error; raises an error when no GPU device is available on the machine

methods.name: Calibrate
methods.brief: Measures where the GPU starts to beat the CPU on this machine for pairwise distances, stores the crossover and saves it.
methods.returns: a list [ nThreshold, report ], the report holding [ size, cpuMs, gpuMs ] per rung
notes: not run: it uses the GPU, which sleeps on this machine and was left alone; read from the code
warnings: writes the calibration file, which later sessions load; wakes the device with heavy work; takes seconds

methods.name: CalibrateWith
methods.brief: Does the same as the call without arguments, on a ladder of corpus sizes chosen by the caller, the dimension being fixed at 64.

parameters.name: paRungs
parameters.role: the corpus sizes to measure, as a list of numbers, from small to large

notes: not run: it uses the GPU, which sleeps on this machine and was left alone; read from the code
warnings: the crossover is the first rung where the GPU wins by 30 percent; if it never wins, everything routes to the CPU; writes the calibration file

methods.name: Verify
methods.brief: Checks a candidate kernel against a reference kernel on the same inputs and on a hidden second shape, and returns a report.

parameters.name: poRef
parameters.role: the reference stzKernelMaker

parameters.name: pCand
parameters.role: the candidate, a stzKernelMaker on the same declarations or raw WGSL on the same binding contract

parameters.name: paBindings
parameters.role: a list that binds the vectors and scalars, as for Run

methods.returns: a hashlist with :verdict among verified, mismatch, mismatch-hidden, impossible, reference-impossible and error
notes: not run: it uses the GPU, which sleeps on this machine and was left alone; read from the code
warnings: timing is taken by the engine, never by this face, and a time faster than the measured bus is refused as impossible; raises an error when no GPU device is available on the machine

methods.name: VerifyWith
methods.brief: Does the same as the call without options, with the repetitions and the numeric band chosen by the caller.

parameters.name: poRef
parameters.role: the reference stzKernelMaker

parameters.name: pCand
parameters.role: the candidate, a stzKernelMaker or raw WGSL

parameters.name: paBindings
parameters.role: a list that binds the vectors and scalars

parameters.name: paOptions

classes.name: stzGpuBuffer
classes.brief: A vector that lives on the GPU, so that kernels can be chained on it with no transfer until it is downloaded once.
classes.description: Obtain one from stzGpu.UploadQ, chain single-input kernels with ApplyQ, read the result with Download, and call Free when done. The object holds two numbers, the generation-keyed engine id and the element count, so a copy shares the same device buffer and a stale id after Free or eviction is reported as stale and never answers with another buffer's data. Every method except init, Id_, Count and IsAlive needs the GPU, which sleeps on this machine, so they were read from the code and not run.
classes.example:
? o1.Count()
#--> 5
? o1.IsAlive()
#--> 0

classes.name: stzGraph
classes.brief: Holds a directed graph of named nodes and labelled edges, and answers questions about its paths, metrics, rules and changes.
classes.description: A node has an id (folded to lowercase, no space), a label and properties; an edge runs from one node to another with a label and properties. The graph is simple: a second edge between the same ordered pair is refused. Paths, components and the centrality metrics run in the engine, on a copy that is rebuilt after most changes (a few removal methods do not refresh it, see their warnings). Rules come in two forms: the three typed stores filled by UseRulesFrom, and attached stzGraphRule objects judged by CheckRules. The graph reads and writes .stzgraf, .stzrulz, .stzsim and GraphML files and writes DOT, JSON and YAML. Many methods fold an id to lowercase and some do not (the removals, Incoming, SetNodeProperty), so ids are safest given in lowercase. The file also holds stzGraphFinder, stzGraphAsciiVisualizer and stzGraphComparison, which the graph builds for you. A number of methods carry a warning today.
classes.receiver: o1 = new stzGraph("g1"); o1.AddNodeXT("a", "Alpha"); o1.AddNodeXT("b", "Beta"); o1.AddNodeXT("c", "Gamma"); o1.Connect("a", "b"); o1.Connect("b", "c")

methods.returns: a list of text, at most the count asked for

methods.name: NodesByType

parameters.name: pVal
parameters.role: A value.

methods.name: EdgesWhere

methods.brief: Returns the [ from, to ] pairs of the edges whose property or label meets a comparison, such as weight > 2.

parameters.name: pcProp
parameters.role: The property to test, as text; label, id and the node's own properties are accepted.

parameters.name: pcOp

parameters.role: A value.

methods.brief: Returns the paths of Paths for which a function answers TRUE.

notes: the function is called once per path of the whole graph

methods.name: QueryQ
methods.section: advanced quryies - based on stzgraphquery class
methods.brief: Returns a stzGraphQuery on this graph, for queries the finder cannot express.

methods.name: ShortestPath
methods.brief: Returns the path with the fewest edges from one node to another, as ids; [ ] when there is none or an id is unknown.

parameters.name: pcFromNodeId
parameters.role: The id of the node the edge starts from.

parameters.name: pcToNodeId
parameters.role: The id of the node the edge ends at.

notes: the same node twice answers a path of that one node

methods.name: BFS
methods.brief: Returns the node ids in breadth-first visit order from a node, the start first; [ ] when the node is unknown.

parameters.name: pcNodeId
parameters.role: The node id, as text.

methods.name: DFS
methods.brief: Returns the node ids in depth-first visit order from a node, the start first; [ ] when the node is unknown.

parameters.name: pcNodeId
parameters.role: The node id, as text.

methods.name: IsBipartite
methods.brief: TRUE if the nodes can be split into two groups so that every edge joins the two, reading edges without direction.
methods.returns: TRUE or FALSE; TRUE for an empty graph

methods.name: StronglyConnectedComponents
methods.brief: Returns the groups of nodes that all reach one another, as lists of ids; a node on no cycle forms a group of its own.
methods.returns: a list of lists of text

methods.name: NumberOfStronglyConnectedComponents
methods.brief: Returns how many groups of mutually reachable nodes the graph has.

methods.name: MSTWeight
methods.brief: Returns the total weight of a minimum spanning tree over the undirected graph, using the :weight property, 1 by default.
methods.returns: a number; -1 when the graph has no edge or is not connected

methods.name: MSTEdges
methods.brief: Returns the edges of a minimum spanning tree as [ from, to, weight ] triples; a graph in several pieces gives a forest.
methods.returns: a list of triples; [ ] when there is no edge
notes: the pair order is the engine's and may be the reverse of the edge's direction

methods.name: ArticulationPoints
methods.brief: Returns the ids of the nodes whose removal would split the graph, reading edges without direction.

methods.name: Bridges
methods.brief: Returns the edges whose removal would split the graph, as [ u, v ] pairs, reading edges without direction.
methods.returns: a list of pairs of ids

methods.name: WeightedShortestPath
methods.brief: Returns the cheapest path from one node to another by the :weight of the edges, 1 when an edge has none, as ids.

parameters.name: pcFromNodeId
parameters.role: The id of the node the edge starts from.

parameters.name: pcToNodeId
parameters.role: The id of the node the edge ends at.

methods.returns: a list of node ids; [ ] when none or unknown

methods.name: WeightedShortestPathLength
methods.brief: Returns the total weight of the cheapest path from one node to another, by the :weight of the edges.

parameters.name: pcFromNodeId
parameters.role: The id of the node the edge starts from.

parameters.name: pcToNodeId
parameters.role: The id of the node the edge ends at.

methods.returns: a number; -1 when unreachable or unknown

methods.name: ShortestPathLength
methods.brief: Returns the number of edges on the shortest path from one node to another.

parameters.name: pcFromNodeId
parameters.role: The id of the node the edge starts from.

parameters.name: pcToNodeId
parameters.role: The id of the node the edge ends at.

methods.returns: a number; 0 when there is no path, which cannot be told from the same node

methods.name: ConnectedComponents
methods.brief: Returns the groups of nodes found by walking out-edges from each node not seen yet, as lists of ids, in node order.
methods.returns: a list of lists of text
warnings: edges are followed in their direction only, so b to a and c to a give three groups, although IsConnected, which ignores direction, answers TRUE

methods.name: TopologicalSort
methods.brief: Returns the node ids ordered so that every node comes before the nodes it points to; [ ] when the graph has a cycle.

methods.name: InDegree
methods.brief: Returns how many edges arrive at a node; the id is matched in lowercase, and an unknown node gives 0.

parameters.name: pcNodeId
parameters.role: The node id, as text.

methods.name: OutDegree
methods.brief: Returns how many edges leave a node; the id is matched in lowercase, and an unknown node gives 0.

parameters.name: pcNodeId
parameters.role: The node id, as text.

methods.name: NumberOfConnectedComponents
methods.brief: Returns how many groups ConnectedComponents finds, counted by the engine, following edge direction.

methods.name: IsConnected
methods.brief: TRUE if every node can be reached from the first when edges are read without direction; one node or none is connected.

methods.name: BetweennessCentrality
methods.brief: Returns how often a node lies on the shortest paths between other node pairs, computed by the engine; 0 for an unknown node.

parameters.name: pcNodeId
parameters.role: The node id, as text.

methods.name: BetweennessCentralityAll
methods.brief: Returns the betweenness of every node as [ id, value ] pairs, in node order.
methods.returns: a list of [ id, value ] pairs

methods.name: ClosenessCentrality
methods.brief: Returns how close a node is to the nodes it reaches: reachable count over the sum of distances; 0 when unknown or isolated.

parameters.name: pcNodeId
parameters.role: The node id, as text.

methods.name: ClosenessCentralityAll
methods.brief: Returns the closeness of every node as [ id, value ] pairs, in node order.
methods.returns: a list of [ id, value ] pairs

methods.name: CoreNumber
methods.brief: Returns the core number of a node: the largest k for which it stays in the k-core of the undirected view; 0 for an unknown node.

parameters.name: pcNodeId
parameters.role: The node id, as text.

methods.name: CoreNumbers
methods.brief: Returns the core number of every node as [ id, value ] pairs, in node order.
methods.returns: a list of [ id, value ] pairs

methods.name: PageRank
methods.brief: Returns the PageRank score of a node, by power iteration with damping 0.85; 0 for an unknown node.

parameters.name: pcNodeId
parameters.role: The node id, as text.

methods.name: PageRankAll
methods.brief: Returns the PageRank score of every node as [ id, value ] pairs, in node order.
methods.returns: a list of [ id, value ] pairs

methods.name: AStarPath
methods.brief: Returns the cheapest path from a start to a goal by A*, using the :weight of edges and the :x and :y of nodes as the heuristic when present.

parameters.name: pcStart
parameters.role: The id of the node the search starts from.

parameters.name: pcGoal
parameters.role: The id of the goal node, where the search ends.

methods.returns: a list of node ids; [ ] when none or unknown
notes: without coordinates it behaves like the weighted shortest path

methods.name: AStarPathManhattan
methods.brief: Returns the cheapest path from a start to a goal by A* with the Manhattan heuristic over the :x and :y of nodes.

parameters.name: pcStart
parameters.role: The id of the node the search starts from.

parameters.name: pcGoal
parameters.role: The id of the goal node, where the search ends.

methods.returns: a list of node ids; [ ] when none or unknown

methods.name: AStarPathWeighted
methods.brief: Returns the cheapest path by A* with a heuristic scaled to the edge weights, so the path stays optimal when weights are not distances.

parameters.name: pcStart
parameters.role: The id of the node the search starts from.

parameters.name: pcGoal
parameters.role: The id of the goal node, where the search ends.

parameters.name: nMode
parameters.role: The heuristic: 1 for Euclidean distance between the :x and :y coordinates, 2 for Manhattan.

methods.returns: a list of node ids; [ ] when none or unknown

methods.name: SetEdgeWeight
methods.brief: Overrides the weight of an edge in the engine copy only, the stored :weight property staying as it is.

parameters.name: pcFrom
parameters.role: The id of the node the edge starts from.

parameters.name: pcTo
parameters.role: The id of the node the edge ends at.

parameters.name: nWeight
parameters.role: The new weight, as a number.

methods.returns: 1 when the edge is known, 0 when it is not
warnings: the override is lost when the engine copy is rebuilt, which most graph changes cause, and the ids are matched in lowercase

methods.name: AStarPlan
methods.brief: Returns the route and the explored nodes of one A* search as [ route, explored ], mode 0 being plain Dijkstra.

parameters.name: pcStart
parameters.role: The id of the node the search starts from.

parameters.name: pcGoal
parameters.role: The id of the goal node, where the search ends.

parameters.name: nMode
parameters.role: The heuristic: 1 for Euclidean distance between the :x and :y coordinates, 2 for Manhattan.

methods.returns: a list of two lists of ids; [ [ ], [ ] ] when a node is unknown
notes: when the goal cannot be reached the route is [ ] and the explored list still shows the nodes visited

methods.name: Diameter
methods.brief: Returns the longest of all the shortest paths between reachable pairs, counted in edges.
methods.returns: a number; 0 for a graph without edges

methods.name: Radius
methods.brief: Returns the smallest eccentricity among the nodes that reach others.

methods.name: Eccentricity
methods.brief: Returns the length in edges of the longest shortest path from a node to any node it reaches; 0 for an unknown node.

parameters.name: pcNodeId
parameters.role: The node id, as text.

methods.name: Eccentricities
methods.brief: Returns the eccentricity of every node as [ id, value ] pairs, in node order.
methods.returns: a list of [ id, value ] pairs

methods.name: AveragePathLength
methods.brief: Returns the mean length of the shortest paths over all reachable pairs of nodes.

methods.name: MaxFlow
methods.brief: Returns the maximum flow from a source to a sink, taking the :weight of each edge as its capacity, 1 by default.

parameters.name: pcSource
parameters.role: The id of the node the flow starts from.

parameters.name: pcSink
parameters.role: The id of the node the flow ends at.

methods.returns: a number; 0 when a node is unknown or no flow can pass

methods.name: MinCut
methods.brief: Returns the saturated edges that separate the sink from the source, as [ from, to ] pairs, by max-flow and min-cut.

parameters.name: pcSource
parameters.role: The id of the node the flow starts from.

parameters.name: pcSink
parameters.role: The id of the node the flow ends at.

methods.returns: a list of pairs of ids; [ ] when a node is unknown

methods.name: Communities
methods.brief: Returns the communities found by label propagation on the undirected view, as lists of node ids.
methods.returns: a list of lists of text

methods.name: NumberOfCommunities
methods.brief: Returns how many communities label propagation finds.

methods.name: MinCostMaxFlow
methods.brief: Returns the maximum flow from a source to a sink and its cost, :weight being the capacity and :cost the price per unit.

parameters.name: pcSource
parameters.role: The id of the node the flow starts from.

parameters.name: pcSink
parameters.role: The id of the node the flow ends at.

methods.returns: a pair [ flow, cost ]; [ 0, 0 ] when a node is unknown

methods.name: ClusteringCoefficient
methods.brief: Returns the share of the possible links among a node's neighbours that exist, on the undirected view; 0 for an unknown node.

parameters.name: pcNodeId
parameters.role: The node id, as text.

methods.name: ClusteringCoefficients
methods.brief: Returns the clustering coefficient of every node as [ id, value ] pairs, in node order.
methods.returns: a list of [ id, value ] pairs

methods.name: PathWeight
methods.brief: Returns the sum of the :weight of the edges along a path; a step with no edge in the graph is skipped.

parameters.name: pacPath
parameters.role: A path as a list of node ids; the last id names the node.

warnings: an edge on the path that has no :weight property raises an error, because the weight is read with EdgeProperty

methods.name: ToHashlist
methods.brief: Returns the graph as one hash list [ :id, :nodes, :edges, :properties ], for conversion or inspection.

methods.name: ExportToDOT

extensions.adds: does what the method does, then returns the object, so the call can be chained

methods.name: ExportToJSON
methods.brief: Returns the graph as JSON text holding its id, nodes, edges and a metrics block with counts, density, longest path and cycles.
notes: the metrics block uses the density and the longest path of this class, so it inherits their limits

methods.name: ExportToYAML
methods.brief: Returns the graph as YAML text with its nodes, edges and the names of the node properties.
notes: node property values and edge properties are not written, only the node property names

methods.name: ExportToGraphML
methods.brief: Returns the graph as GraphML text, with node labels, edge labels and properties written as data keys.
notes: LoadFromGraphML reads this text back to the same nodes, edges, labels and properties

methods.name: SaveToGraphML
methods.brief: Writes the graph to a file as GraphML text, replacing any file there.

parameters.role: A file or folder path, as text.

methods.name: SaveAsGraphML
methods.brief: Writes the graph to a GraphML file; another spelling of the save.

parameters.name: pcPath
parameters.role: A file or folder path, as text.

methods.name: LoadFromGraphML
methods.brief: Replaces the content of the graph by the nodes, edges, labels and properties of a GraphML file, taking its id and type.

parameters.name: pcPath
parameters.role: The path of the GraphML file, as text; an error is raised when there is no such file.

notes: it reads what ExportToGraphML writes, and the plain dialect of other tools: an empty node or edge tag, a node with no label (labelled by its id)
warnings: a property value is read back as a number only when it is a whole number, so 12.5 comes back as the text "12.5"; attributes must be in double quotes

methods.name: LoadGraphML
methods.brief: Replaces the content of the graph by that of a GraphML file; another spelling of the load.

parameters.name: pcPath
parameters.role: The path of the GraphML file, as text.

methods.name: ImportFromGraphML
methods.brief: Brings a GraphML file into the graph, replacing what it held; another spelling of the load.

parameters.name: pcPath
parameters.role: The path of the GraphML file, as text.

methods.name: ImportGraphML
methods.brief: Brings in a GraphML file in place of the current content; another spelling of the load.

parameters.name: pcPath
parameters.role: The path of the GraphML file, as text.

methods.name: Show
methods.brief: Prints the graph as boxes and arrows in the console, vertically, with the bottleneck nodes marked by exclamation marks.
notes: raises error R1 on a graph without nodes

methods.name: Shwo
methods.brief: Prints the graph as boxes and arrows; a misspelled alternative form of the display call.

methods.name: AsciiArt
methods.brief: Returns the vertical picture of the graph as text instead of printing it, the same drawing the display call prints.
methods.returns: text; each line ends with a line break
warnings: raises error R1 on a graph without nodes seen in the gallery: a branching graph prints as separate chains split by //// with shared nodes repeated, so the fork and the join cannot be seen although every edge is present

methods.name: AsciiArtHorizontal
methods.brief: Returns the horizontal picture of the graph as text: boxes in a row joined by labelled arrows.
warnings: raises error R1 on a graph without nodes seen in the gallery: on a branching graph (8 nodes, fork and join) it follows the first path only and drops the other nodes and edges without a hint

methods.name: Rendition
methods.brief: Returns the graph as a rendition value of kind graph, holding its DOT text, for a consumer to lay out.

methods.name: RenditionKinds
methods.brief: Returns the kinds of rendition a graph can give: graph and text.

methods.name: RenditionAs
methods.brief: Returns the graph as a rendition of the given kind: graph holds the DOT text, text holds a one-line count of nodes and edges.

parameters.name: pcKind
parameters.role: The kind of rendition: "graph" or "text".

warnings: any other kind raises an error

methods.name: Display
methods.brief: Writes the graph as DOT code and opens it in the external Graphviz viewer; it returns nothing.
notes: not checked here: it starts an external Graphviz viewer

methods.name: View
methods.brief: Opens the graph in the external Graphviz viewer; an alternative form of the display call.
notes: not checked here: it starts an external Graphviz viewer

methods.name: Veiw
methods.brief: Opens the graph in the external Graphviz viewer; a misspelled alternative form of the display call.
notes: not checked here: it starts an external Graphviz viewer

methods.name: ShowHorizontal
methods.brief: Prints the graph in the console as a row of boxes joined by labelled arrows.
notes: raises error R1 on a graph without nodes

methods.name: ShowH
methods.brief: Prints the graph as a row of boxes; the short spelling of the horizontal display.

methods.name: ShowVertical
methods.brief: Prints the graph as a column of boxes joined by arrows, the default layout of the display.

methods.name: ShowV
methods.brief: Prints the graph as a column of boxes; the short spelling of the vertical display.

methods.name: Explain
methods.brief: Returns a hash list of short sentences about the graph in five sections: general, bottlenecks, cycles, metrics and rules.
methods.returns: a hash list [ :general, :bottlenecks, :cycles, :metrics, :rules ] of lists of text
notes: the longest-path line inherits the limits of LongestPath
warnings: the density line prints the 0-to-1 ratio followed by a percent sign, so 0.20 reads as 0.20%; raises error R1 on an empty graph and R5 on a graph with nodes but no edge

methods.name: ExplainPath
methods.brief: Returns one sentence per edge of the first path found between two nodes, with the edge label as the reason; [ ] when there is no path.

parameters.name: pcFrom
parameters.role: The id of the node the edge starts from.

parameters.name: pcTo
parameters.role: The id of the node the edge ends at.

notes: a path of more than 10 edges is not found, as for Path

methods.name: AttachedRules

methods.name: NumberOfAttachedRules
methods.section: the graph owns its rules (softanza orientation)

methods.returns: a stzGraphRule object; empty text when none matches

methods.name: RulesReport

methods.brief: Detaches every attached rule object and returns the graph.

methods.brief: Runs the completeness rule group and returns its verdict: pass when the graph is connected and has no orphan node.

classes.name: stzGraphAsciiVisualizer
classes.brief: Draws a graph in the console as boxed labels joined by arrows, vertically or horizontally, or hands the drawing back as text.
classes.description: Built by stzGraph.Show and AsciiArt, or on its own over a graph. The vertical drawing starts a tree at every node that nothing points to and writes a CYCLE marker where a path comes back; the horizontal drawing follows the first out-edge of each node. Nodes whose degree is above the average are wrapped in exclamation marks. The Show forms print and the AsciiArt forms return the same text. A graph with no node raises error R1.
classes.receiver: g1 = new stzGraph("g1"); g1.AddNodeXT("a", "Alpha"); g1.AddNodeXT("b", "Beta"); g1.Connect("a", "b"); o1 = new stzGraphAsciiVisualizer(g1)
classes.example:
? o1.AsciiArtHorizontal() != ""
#--> 1

methods.name: init

parameters.name: poGraph
parameters.role: The stzGraph to draw.

notes: stzGraph.Show builds one for you

methods.brief: Returns the vertical drawing as text instead of printing it: boxed labels joined by arrows, one tree per node nothing points to.
methods.returns: text; each line ends with a line break
notes: nodes above the average degree wear exclamation marks, and a graph with no node raises error R1

methods.name: AsciiArtHorizontal
methods.brief: Returns the horizontal drawing as text: boxes in a row joined by arrows that carry the edge labels.
notes: only the first out-edge of each node is followed, and a graph with no node raises error R1

methods.name: Show
methods.brief: Prints the vertical drawing: boxed labels joined by arrows and edge labels, a CYCLE marker where a path comes back.
notes: the bottleneck nodes are wrapped in exclamation marks, and a graph with no node raises error R1

methods.name: ShowVertical
methods.brief: Prints the vertical drawing; the explicit spelling of the default display.

methods.name: ShowV
methods.brief: Prints the vertical drawing; the short spelling of the vertical display.

methods.name: ShowHorizontal
methods.brief: Prints the horizontal drawing: a row of boxes joined by arrows that carry the edge labels.

methods.name: ShowH
methods.brief: Prints the horizontal drawing; the short spelling of the horizontal display.

classes.name: stzGraphCanvas
classes.brief: Draws a graph so that what each node looks like is computed from the graph's own shape, its impact, depth or degree.
classes.description: SizeBy and ColorBy bind to properties the graph computes about itself, not to attributes set by hand: :Impact is how many nodes fail downstream if this one does, :Depth is the layer, :Degree the edge count. A node is big because it is important, and it is important because of the graph's shape. Layouts are hierarchical (longest-path layers with a crossing-reducing sweep, the default), force, ring, modes, sequence and mesh, and the raw coordinates are fitted into the canvas with a margin. ToCanvas answers a stzCanvas, so ToSVG works with no device and ToPNG goes through the graphics device without opening a window. The metrics are computed in the engine.
classes.receiver: oG = new stzGraph("supply") oG.AddNodes([ "mine", "smelt", "chip", "car", "wheel" ]) oG.AddEdge("mine", "smelt") oG.AddEdge("smelt", "chip") oG.AddEdge("chip", "car") oG.AddEdge("wheel", "car") oG.AddEdge("smelt", "wheel") o1 = new stzGraphCanvas(oG, [ :SizeBy = :Impact, :ColorBy = :Impact, :Width = 400, :Height = 300 ])
classes.example:
? @@( o1.MetricValues(:Impact) )
#--> [ 4, 3, 1, 0, 1 ]
? @@( o1.MetricValues(:Depth) )
#--> [ 0, 1, 2, 3, 2 ]
? o1.LayerCount()
#--> 4
? o1.Width()
#--> 400
? @@( o1.Positions()[1] )
#--> [ "mine", 200, 70 ]
? left(o1.ToSVG(), 4)
#--> <svg
o1.SetSize(200, 150)
? o1.Height()
#--> 150

methods.name: init
methods.brief: Lays a graph out and works out the size and colour of every node from the graph's own shape.

parameters.name: poGraph
parameters.role: the stzGraph to draw

parameters.name: paOptions
parameters.role: a hash list, such as :Layout = :Hierarchical (also :Force, :Ring, :Modes, :Sequence, :Mesh), :SizeBy and :ColorBy = :Impact, :Depth, :Degree, :InDegree or :OutDegree, :Width, :Height, :Background, :EdgeColor, :Font, :LabelSize and :LabelColor

methods.returns: nothing; the layout is computed when the object is built
notes: the size defaults to 1000 by 620 and both metrics to :Degree; nodes are circles, edges are straight lines, and labels are drawn only when a :Font is given
warnings: a value that is not a graph raises error stzGraphCanvas: give me an stzGraph; a graph with no node raises error stzGraphCanvas: that graph has no nodes to draw; binding :Depth on a graph with a cycle raises an error saying a node cannot be deeper than itself

methods.name: Width
methods.brief: Returns the width of the drawing, in pixels.
methods.returns: a number, 1000 unless :Width or SetSize gave another

methods.name: Height
methods.brief: Returns the height of the drawing, in pixels.
methods.returns: a number, 620 unless :Height or SetSize gave another

methods.name: EdgeRoutes
methods.brief: Returns the route each long edge takes through the ranks it crosses, in the same space as Positions.
methods.returns: a list of [ from, to, [ [ x, y ], ... ] ]; [ ] when every edge joins neighbouring ranks
notes: an edge a to d over three ranks is one route with two bend points

methods.name: RawSpanX
methods.brief: Returns how wide the layout was before it was fitted to the canvas.
methods.returns: a number in layout units; 1 for one minimum separation

methods.name: RawSpanY
methods.brief: Returns how tall the layout was before it was fitted to the canvas.

methods.name: LayerCount
methods.brief: Returns how many layers, ranks from top to bottom, the layout has.
methods.returns: a number; 1 for the layouts that have no layers
notes: the chain mine, smelt, chip, car has 4

methods.name: IsUnitX
methods.brief: TRUE if the horizontal positions of the layout are in true slot units, not ordinal.
notes: it is 1 for the hierarchical layout and 0 for the modes, sequence, mesh and ring layouts

methods.name: LayoutCrossings
methods.brief: Returns how many edge crossings the drawn order contains.
methods.returns: a number; -1 when no hierarchical layout has run, as with the force layout
notes: the count is of the order that is drawn, after the sweep and after clusters are compacted

methods.name: SetSize
methods.brief: Changes the size of the drawing and lays the graph out again for it.

parameters.name: pnW
parameters.role: the new width in pixels, at least 1

parameters.name: pnH
parameters.role: the new height in pixels, at least 1

methods.returns: nothing; the layout is recomputed. SetSizeQ returns the object for chaining
notes: a window reports 0x0 while minimised, so skip that frame rather than call it
warnings: a size below 1, such as 0 by 5, raises error stzGraphCanvas.SetSize: refused ... a drawing needs area; a value that is not a number raises error stzGraphCanvas.SetSize: give a width and a height

extensions.name: SetSizeQ
extensions.adds: does what the method does, then returns the object, so the call can be chained

methods.name: MetricValues
methods.brief: Returns a property the graph computes about itself, one number per node, in node order.

parameters.name: cWhich
parameters.role: the property, one of :Impact, :Depth, :Degree, :InDegree or :OutDegree, in any letter case

methods.returns: a list of numbers: :Impact counts the nodes that fail downstream, :Depth the layer, :Degree the edges in or out, :InDegree and :OutDegree each side
notes: for the chain mine, smelt, chip, car with a wheel branch, mine has an impact of 4
warnings: any other name, such as betweenness, raises error stzGraphCanvas: I do not compute ...; :Depth on a cyclic graph raises an error, since no layering exists

methods.name: Positions
methods.brief: Returns where every node sits on the canvas.
methods.returns: a list of [ id, x, y ] in node order, in pixels
notes: positions are fitted into the canvas with a margin, so they change with SetSize

methods.name: RawPositions
methods.brief: Returns the horizontal position each node had in the layout before it was fitted to the canvas.
methods.returns: a list of [ id, x ] in node order
notes: for the hierarchical layout this is the space a pin lives in

methods.name: ToCanvas
methods.brief: Builds a stzCanvas of the picture, edges first, then nodes sized and coloured by their metrics, then labels.
notes: labels need a :Font option; the colours run from green for a low value to red for a high one; ToCanvasQ is the same call

extensions.name: ToCanvasQ
extensions.adds: does what the method does, then returns the object, so the call can be chained

methods.name: ToSVG
methods.brief: Returns the picture as SVG text; no graphics device is needed.

methods.name: ToPNG
methods.brief: Draws the picture on the graphics device and writes it to a PNG file.

parameters.name: pcPath
parameters.role: the path of the file to write

methods.returns: the PNG bytes as text; empty when no graphics device is available
notes: it needs a device but opens no window, and the temporary canvas is freed; do not print the answer, it is binary

methods.name: ModeOf
methods.brief: Returns the mode each node landed in, for the modes layout.
methods.returns: a list of mode numbers in node order; [ ] for the other layouts
notes: a mode of two or more states is drawn as a region by the face

methods.name: ModeCount
methods.brief: Returns how many modes the modes layout found.
methods.returns: a number; 0 for the other layouts
notes: on the five-node supply chain with a branch the modes layout gave five modes of one node each

classes.name: stzGraphComparison
classes.brief: Compares a baseline graph with several variations and ranks them by what changed: nodes, edges, density, cycles and bottlenecks.
classes.description: Built by stzGraph.CompareWithManyQR(..., :stzGraphComparison) or directly. It runs the comparison once when built and answers from the stored rows: Summary for a text report, MostImpactful and LeastImpactful, ByMetric to sort, Recommend for a suggestion, ToStzTable for a table, WithCycles and WithoutCycles to split the variations by whether their graph holds a cycle.
classes.receiver: g1 = new stzGraph("g1"); g1.AddNode("a"); g1.AddNode("b"); g1.Connect("a", "b"); o1 = new stzGraphComparison(g1, [ g1 ])
classes.example:
? o1.LeastImpactful()
#--> V1

methods.name: init
methods.brief: Compares a baseline graph with each variation at once and keeps the results; variations are named V1, V2 and so on unless given as pairs.

parameters.name: oBaseline
parameters.role: the baseline stzGraph

parameters.name: paoGraphs
parameters.role: the variations: [ g1, g2 ] or named [ [ "name", g1 ], ... ]

notes: the comparison runs when the object is built

methods.name: ToStzTable
methods.brief: Returns the comparison as a stzTable with one column per variation and one row per metric, such as NodesAdded and HasCycles.

methods.name: Show
methods.brief: Prints the comparison table, one column per variation, in the console.

methods.name: Display
methods.brief: Prints the comparison table; another spelling of the display call.

methods.name: Data
methods.brief: Returns the whole comparison as a hash list holding the rows, the baseline id and the count of variations.

methods.name: Content
methods.brief: Returns the comparison data exactly as Data does: the rows, the baseline id and the count of variations.

methods.name: Comparisons
methods.brief: Returns one hash list per variation with its name and its counts of nodes and edges added and removed.

methods.name: Summary
methods.brief: Returns a text report naming the baseline and the count of variations, with one bulleted line per variation explaining its change.

methods.name: MostImpactful
methods.brief: Returns the name of the variation with the most node and edge changes, added plus removed; empty when none changed anything.
methods.returns: text; empty when every variation is unchanged

methods.name: LeastImpactful
methods.brief: Returns the name of the variation with the fewest node and edge changes, the first one on a tie.

methods.name: WithCycles
methods.brief: Returns the names of the variations whose graph contains a cycle, in the order they were given; an empty list when none does.
methods.returns: a list of text; empty when every variation is acyclic
notes: the rows keep the cycle field as the text TRUE or FALSE; the test reads that text and also accepts the numbers 1 and 0

methods.name: WithoutCycles
methods.brief: Returns the names of the variations whose graph stays acyclic, in the order they were given; an empty list when none does.
methods.returns: a list of text; empty when every variation has a cycle
notes: together with the names that WithCycles returns it covers every variation once

methods.name: ByMetric
methods.brief: Returns the variation names from the highest to the lowest value of one column, such as :nodesAdded; an unknown column raises an error.

parameters.name: cMetric
parameters.role: The metric to sort by, such as :nodesAdded, :edgesAdded or :hasCycles.

notes: numbers sort by value; a text column such as the density change sorts by the byte order of its text, so :hasCycles puts the cyclic variations first

methods.name: Recommend
methods.brief: Scores each variation and returns the best with a reason; the score rewards acyclic graphs, fewer bottlenecks and denser links.
notes: the reason text is the same for every answer

classes.name: stzGraphex
classes.brief: Matches a graph pattern written as text, such as {@Node(a) -> @Edge(x) -> @Node(b)}, against a stzGraph and answers TRUE or FALSE.
classes.description: The pattern is compiled into a small graph of tokens (@Node, @Edge, @Cycle, @Path, with an optional label, a {property constraint}, a quantifier, an alternation in parentheses, a @! negation and a @cs: case mark). A match flattens the target graph into label paths and looks for the pattern labels in order along one path, then checks the property constraints on the target nodes. Labels match without regard to case by default, results are cached per target graph, and the quantifiers are parsed but not yet used by the match.
classes.receiver: g1 = new stzGraph("g1"); g1.AddNodeXT("n1", "Start"); g1.AddNodeXT("n2", "Done"); g1.ConnectXT("n1", "n2", "flows"); o1 = new stzGraphex("{@Node(start) -> @Edge(flows) -> @Node(done)}", g1)

methods.name: init
methods.brief: Compiles a graph pattern into a pattern graph and keeps the target graph; a non-text pattern or a non-graph raises an error.

parameters.name: _cPattern_
parameters.role: The pattern, as text, such as "{@Node(a) -> @Edge(x) -> @Node(b)}"

parameters.name: oTargetGraph
parameters.role: The stzGraph the pattern is matched against

notes: Match takes the graph again, so the target given here is only the default

methods.name: NormalizePattern
methods.brief: Returns the pattern trimmed and wrapped in braces when it is not already.

parameters.name: _cPattern_
parameters.role: The pattern, as text

methods.name: BuildPatternGraph
methods.brief: Parses a pattern and adds one node per token to the pattern graph, joined by sequences edges; an alternation fans out to every branch.

parameters.name: _cPattern_
parameters.role: The braced pattern, as text

notes: init calls it once; a second call grafts the new tokens onto the first pattern
warnings: the nodes are added to the graph already held, not in place of it, and their ids restart at :p1

methods.name: ParsePattern
methods.brief: Splits a braced pattern at -> into token lists, one per part, with an alternation in parentheses becoming a single alternation token.

parameters.name: _cPattern_
parameters.role: The pattern, as text, with its outer braces

methods.returns: a list of tokens, each a hash list
notes: each token holds type, label, min, max, setvalues, unique, negated and cs
warnings: the first and last characters are removed without a check, so a pattern without braces loses its first and last letters

methods.name: ParseSingleToken
methods.brief: Parses one token such as @Node(a)+ into a hash list of its type, label, quantifier, set values and flags; [ ] if unreadable.

parameters.name: _cTokenStr_
parameters.role: One token, as text: @Node, @Edge, @Cycle or @Path, with an optional (label), {set}, quantifier and @! or @cs: prefix

warnings: the quantifier gives min and max (+ is 1 to 999999, * is 0 to 999999, ? is 0 to 1) but matching never reads them

methods.name: ListifyGraph
methods.brief: Returns every path of a graph as a list of alternating node and edge labels, with isolated nodes and @Cycle paths added.

parameters.name: oGraph
parameters.role: The stzGraph to turn into label paths

warnings: paths run between every pair of distinct reachable nodes, so a chain of three nodes gives three branches

methods.name: Match
methods.brief: Tells whether the pattern occurs in a graph: its labels in order along one path, no negated label on it, and the property constraints met.

parameters.name: oTargetGraph
parameters.role: The stzGraph to look in

notes: labels match without regard to case unless the token starts with @cs:; a negated label only rules out the path that holds it, so another path may still match
warnings: the result is cached under a signature made of the node and edge counts and the node ids, so a second graph with the same ids but other labels answers from the cache: call ClearCache between graphs; labelless tokens (a bare @Node or @Edge, @Cycle, @Path) match anything and quantifiers are not read

methods.name: CacheStats
methods.brief: Returns how many target graphs are cached and how many matches were answered from the cache.

methods.name: CacheEntries
methods.brief: Returns the number of target graphs held in the match cache.

methods.name: ClearCache
methods.brief: Empties the match cache and sets its hit count back to 0.

methods.name: SetCacheSize
methods.brief: Sets how many results the match cache keeps, the oldest dropped first; a value that is not a number is ignored.

parameters.name: nSize
parameters.role: The most results to keep

methods.returns: the matcher itself, so calls can be chained
warnings: with 0 or a negative number the cache is no longer trimmed and so has no bound

methods.name: CacheInfo
methods.brief: Returns the cache state: entry count, size limit and hit count.

methods.name: ListifyPatternGraph
methods.brief: Returns the pattern graph as label paths from each root to each end, one path per branch of an alternation.
warnings: the labels read node(Start) or edge(flows), with the token type and its label in parentheses

methods.name: TraversePatternNode
methods.brief: Walks the pattern graph depth-first from a node and appends each complete label path to the list given as third argument.

parameters.name: _cNodeId_
parameters.role: The id of the pattern node to start from, such as :p1

parameters.name: aCurrentPath
parameters.role: The labels already on the path, as a list

parameters.name: _aBranches_
parameters.role: The list that receives each finished path

parameters.name: acVisited
parameters.role: Ids already visited, kept for the call and not read

methods.returns: nothing; the branches list is filled
notes: give [ ] for aCurrentPath and acVisited
warnings: an id that is not a pattern node raises error Node does not exist, because the check after the lookup never runs

methods.name: MatchBranches
methods.brief: Tells whether any pattern branch has its labels in order inside any target branch, with none of its negated labels there.

parameters.name: _aPatternBranches_
parameters.role: Pattern label paths, such as node(a) and edge(x) entries

parameters.name: _aTargetBranches_
parameters.role: Target label paths, as ListifyGraph gives them

warnings: the case flags are read from the pattern graph held by the object, so branches that did not come from it are all matched without regard to case

methods.name: IsSubsequenceSimple
methods.brief: TRUE if every pattern label appears in the target in the same order, not necessarily next to each other; labels are compared with case.

parameters.name: _aPattern_
parameters.role: The labels to find, as a list

parameters.name: aTarget
parameters.role: The labels to look in, as a list

warnings: an empty pattern is TRUE

methods.name: IsSubsequence
methods.brief: TRUE if the pattern labels appear in order in the target; a flag per label marks it negated, and then only the next target item is checked.

parameters.name: _aPattern_
parameters.role: The labels to find, as a list

parameters.name: aTarget
parameters.role: The labels to look in, as a list

parameters.name: aPatternNegations
parameters.role: One flag per pattern label, 1 for a negated label and 0 otherwise

warnings: a negated label that occurs later in the target is not noticed, since the negation uses up the next target item and the scan goes on

extensions.name: IsSubsequenceCS
extensions.adds: takes a case-sensitivity flag

methods.name: TokensToListexPattern
methods.brief: Turns branch labels such as node(a) into their bare labels, with the text any for a label that has no parentheses or is not text.

parameters.name: _aBranch_
parameters.role: A list of labels such as node(a) and edge(x)

warnings: the unmatched parenthesis case "bar(" also gives any

methods.name: ShowPatternGraph
methods.brief: Prints the pattern graph as boxes and arrows, one box per token joined by sequences arrows; a negated token is shown between ! marks.
warnings: seen in the gallery: the middle token of any pattern is printed between ! marks, negated or not, so a negated token and a plain one cannot be told apart

methods.name: EnableDebugMode
methods.brief: Sets the debug flag on; it changes nothing visible today, since no code reads the flag to print.
notes: EnableDebug is the same call
warnings: the debug branches of the matcher are empty, so debug mode prints nothing

methods.name: EnableDebug
methods.brief: Sets the debug flag on; it changes nothing visible today, since no code reads the flag to print.
warnings: the debug branches of the matcher are empty, so debug mode prints nothing

methods.name: DisableDebugMode
methods.brief: Sets the debug flag off, which is its state at the start.
notes: DisableDebug is the same call

classes.name: stzGraphFinder
classes.brief: Filters the nodes or the edges of a graph by key, comparison and property, then answers the ids that match.
classes.description: Built by stzGraph.FindQ and chained: each filter call adds a condition and returns the finder, and Run answers the elements that pass every condition, node ids for a node search and [ from, to ] pairs for an edge search. A key is looked up on the element first (id, label, from, to) and then among its properties, and dots reach nested values. For queries it cannot express, use stzGraphQuery.
classes.receiver: g1 = new stzGraph("g1"); g1.AddNodeXTT("a", "Alpha", [ :priority = 10 ]); g1.AddNodeXTT("b", "Beta", [ :priority = 5 ]); o1 = g1.FindQ("nodes")

methods.name: Where

parameters.name: pValue

classes.name: stzGraphGoal
classes.brief: Holds a wanted state of a graph, that every instance of a type has an outgoing edge of a given label, and reports who breaks it.
classes.description: A goal is declarative: RequireEveryHas(type, relation) or FromMeans("every :Type Has(:relation)") sets the pattern, and GapOn(graph) returns the instances that do not meet it. An instance is a node joined to the type's node by an edge labelled isa. The goal never stores a graph, it judges the live one passed in. Time qualifiers such as Within are not evaluated; a sentence without the every and Has clauses is refused with an error.
classes.receiver: o1 = new stzGraphGoal("priced") o1.RequireEveryHas("Dish", "Price") oG = new stzGraph("menu") oG.AddNode("dish") oG.AddNode("tajine") oG.AddNode("couscous") oG.AddNode("price") oG.AddEdgeXT("tajine", "dish", "isa") oG.AddEdgeXT("couscous", "dish", "isa") oG.AddEdgeXT("tajine", "price", "price")
classes.example:
? o1.Narrate()
#--> goal priced: every dish has(price)
? @@( o1.GapOn(oG) )
#--> [ "couscous" ]
? o1.SatisfiedOn(oG)
#--> 0
oG.AddEdgeXT("couscous", "price", "price")
? o1.SatisfiedOn(oG)
#--> 1

classes.name: stzGraphPlanner
classes.brief: Plans the cheapest route through a graph under named plans, criteria and profiles, then explains, compares and filters the plans.
classes.description: A planner takes a copy of a stzGraph when it is built. Each plan has a start and a goal (a node, or a function that tests nodes), criteria to minimise or maximise over the edge properties (or a profile: fastest, safest, cheapest, shortest, balanced, efficient) and, once executed, a result: the actions, their total cost and the route. The search runs in the engine as a uniform-cost search, so the route is the cheapest for non-negative costs. Every execution is also kept in a history. The comparison, ranking, filtering and history calls work on the executed plans, and stzGraphPlanner has a very large set of alternative spellings for the same calls.
classes.receiver: g1 = new stzGraph("g1"); g1.AddNodeXTT("a", "A", [ :x = 0 ]); g1.AddNodeXTT("b", "B", [ :x = 1 ]); g1.AddNodeXTT("c", "C", [ :x = 2 ]); g1.AddEdgeXTT("a", "b", "r", [ :distance = 5, :cost = 1 ]); g1.AddEdgeXTT("b", "c", "r", [ :distance = 5, :cost = 9 ]); g1.AddEdgeXTT("a", "c", "r", [ :distance = 20, :cost = 2 ]); o1 = new stzGraphPlanner(g1); o1.AddPlan("short"); o1.Walk("a", "c"); o1.Minimize("distance"); o1.Execute(); o1.AddPlan("cheap"); o1.Walk("a", "c"); o1.Minimize("cost"); o1.Execute()

warnings: a node or an edge added to the graph afterwards is not seen by the planner: Execute then raises, for example, Node 'c' does not exist

notes: the criteria are fastest: time .7 and distance .3; safest: danger .8 and risk .2; cheapest: cost .8 and distance .2; shortest: distance 1; balanced: time .4, cost .3, distance .3; efficient: energy .6 and time .4

classes.name: stzGraphQuery
classes.brief: Builds a MATCH, WHERE, SELECT query over a stzGraph with a chain of calls, runs it and returns the matching rows.
classes.description: A query is a definition, a hash list of 11 parts that the Match, Where, Select, OrderBy, Create, Set and Delete calls fill in; nothing touches the graph until Select, Execute, ToGraphQ or ToViewQ runs it. Rows are lists of [ field, value ] pairs, or of [ alias, node ] pairs for a bare alias. Queries that create, set or delete change the source graph on every run. For plain filters on nodes or edges, stzGraphFinder is lighter.
classes.receiver: g1 = new stzGraph("g1"); g1.AddNodeXTT("a", "Person", [ :name = "Ann", :age = 30 ]); g1.AddNodeXTT("b", "Person", [ :name = "Bob", :age = 25 ]); o1 = new stzGraphQuery(g1)
classes.example:
? @@( o1.MatchQ([ :node = "n", :labeled = "Person" ]).WhereQ([ :age, ">", 26 ]).Select("n.name") )
#--> [ [ [ "n.name", "Ann" ] ] ]

classes.name: stzGraphRule
classes.brief: States one rule about a graph, as clauses over node properties or as a checker function, and reports its findings in the house shape.
classes.description: A rule has a name, a type, a domain, a severity and a message. Its scope is the When clauses, which select nodes by a property test and are combined with AND. With no Then clause, every node in scope is a finding, a prohibition; with Then clauses, each node in scope that fails a requirement is a finding, an implication. A rule too rich for clauses takes a checker function with UseChecker, which owns the whole decision. Check returns rows [ :rule, :subject, :where, :severity, :message ], the shape stzRuleReport gates on, and Register compiles the rule into the shared registry. The setters have a plain form that returns nothing and a Q form that returns the rule, so chains use SetSeverityQ, WhenQ and ThenQ; SetReadsQ, SetWritesQ and SetOrderQ exist only in the Q form. Known defects: the greaterequal and lessequal operators match every node when the property or the value is text, and Register called twice adds the entry twice.
classes.receiver: o1 = new stzGraphRule("llm-needs-owner"); o1.WhenQ("kind", "equals", "llm_actor"); o1.ThenQ("owner", "exists", ""); o1.ThenViolationQ("an LLM actor must name an owner")
classes.example:
oG = new stzGraph("agents")
oG.AddNodeXTT("planner", "Planner", [ :kind = "llm_actor" ])
oG.AddNodeXTT("deployer", "Deployer", [ :kind = "service" ])
? @@( o1.SubjectsIn(oG) )
#--> [ "node:planner" ]
? o1.NumberOfFindings(oG)
#--> 1
? o1.Check(oG)[1][:message]
#--> an LLM actor must name an owner

classes.description: A view is a stzGraph made from the chosen nodes of a parent and every edge between them, so everything stzGraph answers it answers about the cut. Edits stay in the view until Commit writes them into the parent; Rollback drops them. Changes says what a commit would do before it is done. The view is a snapshot: later changes of the parent do not reach it.
classes.receiver: oP = new stzGraph("main") oP.AddNodeXT("a", "Alpha") oP.AddNodeXT("b", "Beta") oP.AddNodeXT("c", "Gamma") oP.AddEdgeXT("a", "b", "ab") oP.AddEdgeXT("b", "c", "bc") o1 = new stzGraphView(oP, [ "a", "b" ])
classes.example:
? @@( o1.NodesIds() )
#--> [ "a", "b" ]
? o1.IsView()
#--> 1
o1.AddNodeXT("z", "Zed")
? @@( o1.Changes()[:nodesadded] )
#--> [ "z" ]
? oP.NodeExists("z")
#--> 0
o1.Commit()
? oP.NodeExists("z")
#--> 1

classes.name: stzGrid
classes.brief: Tracks a position on a grid of columns and rows, moves it in six directions, and finds routes around obstacles.
classes.description: A grid holds no data of its own. It keeps a current position counted from 1 at the top left, a direction, a set of obstacles and a stored path, and draws them as text. Positions are always [ column, row ], the column first. Reach for it to walk a board, a maze or a map: move by steps, ask for the cell above, below or beside, list the neighbours, test whether two cells connect, split the grid into regions, or ask for a route. Moves that would leave the grid or land on an obstacle change nothing, without an error, while the Node and NthNode readers raise an error outside the grid. ManhattanPath and ZigZagPath raise when an obstacle is on the way; see their warnings.

? @@( o1.NodeRight() )
#--> [ 2, 1 ]
? o1.DistanceTo(4, 3)
#--> 5

classes.name: stzGridNav
classes.brief: Holds a named grid of rows and columns with a current cell that moves, and never leaves the grid.
classes.description: The class wraps the engine's grid navigation module: a position, moves that refuse to leave the grid, a neighbour count, a validity test and a Manhattan distance. Rows and columns are counted from 0, so a 3 by 4 grid has rows 0 to 2 and columns 0 to 3, and a new grid starts on row 0, column 0. The engine holds ONE grid at a time, so the object keeps its own size and position and hands them to the engine again before every call: several objects can live side by side, and a copy of an object moves on its own. The directions of the class are 0 up, 1 down, 2 left, 3 right (the engine reads 0 up, 1 right, 2 down, 3 left, and the class converts).
classes.example:
? o1.CurrentRow()
#--> 0
o1.MoveDown()
o1.MoveRight()
? [ o1.CurrentRow(), o1.CurrentCol() ]
#--> [ 1, 1 ]
? o1.NeighborCount()
#--> 4
? o1.DistanceTo(2, 3)
#--> 3

classes.name: stzHashList
classes.brief: Holds a list of [ key, value ] pairs and finds, reads and groups them by key or by value.
classes.description: A hash list is the Ring list [ :name = "Ali", :age = 30 ] made into an object: keys are looked up without regard to case, values can be of any type and repeat, and the pairs keep their order. Reach for it when you read the pairs by position or by value as often as by key.
