The average line is not drawn in the text picture, SetBarHeight spaces the bars out instead of thickening them, and SetBarInterSpace and SetHeight change nothing; see their warnings. In the pixel pictures the label column has a fixed width, so a long label is clipped at the left edge. Gallery: doc/gallery/stzHBarPlot/ranked.png (six bars with values), seen right by stzlib- docs visual pass (a model reading the PNG), 2026-10-05, not a person; longlabels.png (long labels clipped at the left edge), seen wrong by the same pass; terminal.txt is the text picture, read as text and judged right.

methods.name: PlotKind

methods.name: SetSize
methods.brief: Sets how wide the longest bar may be and how tall the plot is asked to be; only the width changes the picture.

parameters.name: nWidth
parameters.role: The length of the longest bar in characters, raised to 20 when smaller

parameters.name: nHeight
parameters.role: The height in rows, raised to 4 when smaller

notes: the plot is as tall as its bars need
warnings: The height is stored but the picture has one row per bar whatever it says

methods.name: Size
methods.brief: Returns the height and the width the plot is set to, in that order.

notes: the defaults are [ 12, 18 ]

methods.name: SizeHV

methods.name: SizeVH

methods.name: SetBarHeight

methods.name: SetBarInterSpace
methods.brief: Stores the gap between two bars, which the horizontal picture never reads, so it changes nothing today.

parameters.name: n

methods.returns: nothing; the value is only remembered

methods.name: SetBarSpace

methods.name: SetInterBarSpace

parameters.name: n

methods.returns: nothing; the value is only remembered

methods.name: SetWidth
methods.brief: Sets the length of the longest bar in characters; the other bars are drawn in proportion to it.

parameters.name: n
parameters.role: The length of the longest bar, raised to 10 when smaller

methods.name: SetHVAxis
methods.brief: Shows or hides the horizontal axis and the vertical axis, and shows the bar labels only while the vertical axis is shown.

parameters.name: bHShow

methods.name: Width

methods.brief: Limits how many bars are drawn; the bars after the limit are left out without a message.

methods.name: SetVAxisLabels

methods.name: AddVAxisLabels

methods.name: WithoutAxisLabels

methods.name: WithoutVAxisLabels
methods.brief: Hides the labels at the left of the bars, under the V name.

classes.name: stzHexNumber
classes.brief: Holds a hexadecimal number and writes it in decimal, binary, octal or any base up to 36.
classes.description: Built from text with or without a prefix (FF, 0xFF, U+0041); the digits are kept without the prefix and WithPrefix adds 0x back. The conversions go through a floating-point number, so they are exact up to 9007199254740992 and rounded above. The From... methods replace the number in place from a decimal, octal or binary value. Checked by hand: 0xFF is 255, 0b11111111 and 0o377; 0x1A3 is 419, 0b110100011 and 0o643; 0xDEADBEEF is 3735928559. Found today: FractionalPart and ToScientificForm raise R14; IntegerPartWithoutPrefix keeps a stray 0 (0xFF gives 0FF); ToUnicodeHexForm keeps the 0x inside the U+ (U+0x41); and FromDecimalForm stores -1 and FF. for a negative and a fraction.
classes.example:
? o1.ToDecimalForm()
#--> 255
? o1.ToBinaryForm()
#--> 0b11111111
? o1.ToOctalForm()
#--> 0o377
o2 = new stzHexNumber("1A3")
? o2.WithPrefix()
#--> 0x1A3
? o2.ToDecimalForm()
#--> 419
o2.FromDecimalForm(4096)
? o2.Content()
#--> 1000

methods.name: init
methods.brief: Builds a hexadecimal number from text, with a 0x prefix, a U+ prefix or none, and keeps the digits without the prefix.

parameters.name: cNumber
parameters.role: the hex digits 0-9 A-F in either case, optionally written 0x.. or U+..

notes: 1A3 and 0x1A3 and U+0041 are all accepted; the case of the digits is kept
warnings: a fractional text such as 0x1F.8, a sign, a text of only 0x and a bare x prefix raise Can't create the hex number, and a value that is not text raises Incorrect param type

methods.name: Content
methods.brief: Returns the digits as stored, without any prefix.
notes: WithoutPrefix is the same call; 0xFF gives FF and ff stays ff

methods.name: Value
methods.brief: Returns the digits as stored, without any prefix.

methods.name: WithPrefix
methods.brief: Returns the digits with the 0x prefix in front.
notes: HexNumber is the same call; FF gives 0xFF, and an empty number gives 0x

methods.name: IntegerPart
methods.brief: Returns the part before a point, written with the 0x prefix.
notes: IntPart is the same call; as a number cannot hold a point today this is the whole number: ABC gives 0xABC

methods.name: IntegerPartWithoutPrefix
methods.brief: Returns the integer digits with the prefix removed, but with a stray 0 in front.
notes: use Content for the digits alone
warnings: it removes the prefix letter x before the prefix 0x, so the 0 of 0x stays: 0xFF gives 0FF, 0xabc gives 0abc and 0x0 gives 00; the value is unchanged, so ToDecimalForm is right

methods.name: FractionalPart
methods.brief: Raises error R14 today instead of returning the digits after the point.
notes: confirmed with 0xFF and 0x41
warnings: it calls HexNumberWithoutPrefix, a method that does not exist, so FractionalPart and FractPart raise for every input; init also refuses a text with a point, so there is never a fraction to return

methods.name: ToStzNumber
methods.brief: Returns the value as a stzNumber.
methods.returns: a stzNumber holding the decimal value
notes: 0xFF gives 255

methods.name: ToStzString
methods.brief: Returns the number written with its 0x prefix, as a stzString.
notes: 0x41 gives 0x41 as a text

methods.name: ToDecimalForm
methods.brief: Returns the value in decimal, as a text.
notes: ToDecimal is the same call; 0xFF gives 255, 0x1A3 gives 419, 0xDEADBEEF gives 3735928559, an empty number gives 0
warnings: the value goes through a floating-point number, so it is exact up to 9007199254740992 and rounded above: 0x7FFFFFFFFFFFFFFF gives 9223372036854775808.00 instead of ...807

methods.name: ToUnicodeHexForm
methods.brief: Returns the number written with a U+ in front, but with the 0x prefix kept inside.
methods.returns: a text such as U+0x41 for 0x41
notes: ToUnicodeHex is the same call
warnings: the 0x prefix is not dropped, so the result is not a valid code point text: 0x41 gives U+0x41 where U+0041 is meant; confirmed with 0xFF and U+0041

methods.name: ToBinaryForm
methods.brief: Returns the value in binary with the 0b prefix.
notes: ToBinary is the same call; 0xFF gives 0b11111111; 0x1A3 gives 0b110100011; 0x0 gives 0b0

methods.name: ToBinaryFormWithoutPrefix
methods.brief: Returns the value in binary, without a prefix.

methods.name: ToOctalForm
methods.brief: Returns the value in octal with the 0o prefix.
notes: ToOctal is the same call; 0xFF gives 0o377; 0x1A3 gives 0o643; 0xabc gives 0o5274

methods.name: ToOctalFormWithoutPrefix
methods.brief: Returns the value in octal, without a prefix.
notes: 0xFF gives 377; 0xDEADBEEF gives 33653337357

methods.name: IntegerPartToBaseNForm
methods.brief: Returns the whole number written in any base from 2 to 36, in lower case and without prefix.

parameters.name: n
parameters.role: the base, from 2 to 36

notes: IntegerPartToBaseN is the same call; 0xFF in base 2 gives 11111111, in base 36 gives 73; 0x41 in base 32 gives 21

methods.name: ToScientificForm
methods.brief: Raises error R14 today instead of returning the value in scientific notation.
notes: ToScientific is the same call
warnings: it forwards to stzNumber.ToScientificForm, a method that does not exist, and passes an undefined variable; stzNumber itself raises the same R14; confirmed with 0xFF and 0x41

methods.name: ToBytes
methods.brief: Returns eight raw bytes: the value stored as an IEEE 754 double, least significant byte first.
notes: 0xFF gives the bytes 00 00 00 00 00 E0 6F 40, since 255.0 is 0x406FE00000000000; these are not the bytes of the hex digits

methods.name: FromDecimalForm
methods.brief: Replaces the number with the hex digits of a decimal value, in place.

parameters.name: n
parameters.role: the decimal value, an integer of 0 or more

notes: 255 gives FF, 4096 gives 1000, 1000000 gives F4240, 0 gives 0; the digits come out in capitals
warnings: a negative value stores -1 and a fraction such as 255.5 stores FF., neither of which init would accept; a text that is not a number raises the stzNumber error Can not create decimal number

methods.name: FromDecimal
methods.brief: Replaces the number with the hex digits of a decimal value, in place.

parameters.name: n
parameters.role: the decimal value, an integer of 0 or more

warnings: same limits as FromDecimalForm

methods.name: FromOctalForm
methods.brief: Replaces the number with the hex digits of an octal value, in place.

parameters.name: n
parameters.role: the octal text, with or without the 0o prefix

notes: 0o17 and 17 both give F; 377 gives FF

methods.name: FromOctal
methods.brief: Replaces the number with the hex digits of an octal value, in place.

parameters.name: n
parameters.role: the octal text, with or without the 0o prefix

notes: 377 gives FF

methods.name: FromBinaryForm
methods.brief: Replaces the number with the hex digits of a binary value, in place.

parameters.name: n
parameters.role: the binary text, which must carry the 0b prefix

notes: 0b1010 gives A; 11111111 raises
warnings: a binary text without the 0b prefix raises Can't create binary number, whereas FromOctalForm accepts both forms

methods.name: FromBinary
methods.brief: Replaces the number with the hex digits of a binary value, in place.

parameters.name: n
parameters.role: the binary text, which must carry the 0b prefix

notes: 0b101 gives 5
warnings: a binary text without the 0b prefix raises Can't create binary number

methods.name: IsHexNumber
methods.brief: TRUE if the object is a hexadecimal number, which it always is.
notes: exists for the chain-of-truth checks; the function IsHexNumber("0xFF") tests a text

classes.name: stzHIPAARuleBase
classes.brief: Holds the HIPAA compliance rules for an org chart, ready to pass to CheckCompliance.
classes.description: Holds the four universal org rules and no rule of its own yet: only the name tells it from the other regimes.
classes.example:
? o1.NumberOfRules()
#--> 4

methods.name: init
methods.brief: Builds the HIPAA rule base: the four universal org rules under the name HIPAA; it adds no rule of its own.
methods.returns: nothing; the rule base is built
warnings: only the name tells the regimes apart today

classes.name: stzHistogram
classes.brief: Bins a list of numbers into equal-width classes and draws the counts, or another aggregate, as touching bars.
classes.description: Built from raw measurements, it cuts the range into 5 or more bins by Sturges' rule, or into the number SetBinCount gives, and each bar shows how many values fall in its bin; UseSum, UseAverage, UseMin and UseMax make it show another aggregate. ToString draws the text picture (bin edges in two rows under the bars), ToSVG and ToPNG the pixel picture; Mean, StandardDeviation, Median, Mode and DataCount describe the data. The text picture is drawn by the engine, except when statistics are on or the horizontal axis is off, when the slower Ring renderer takes over and obeys SetHeight, SetMaxWidth and AddValues, which the engine route ignores. SetBinRange gives the wrong number of bins, SetAggregation with an unknown name leaves the histogram unusable, and the X and Y axis names are the reverse of the usual ones; see the warnings. Gallery: doc/gallery/stzHistogram/normal.png (200 values, 9 bins), bins20.png (20 bins) and sums.png (UseSum), each with its script, seen right by stzlib-docs visual pass (a model reading the PNG), 2026-10-05, not a person; terminal.txt is the text picture, read as text and judged right.

methods.name: init
methods.brief: Bins a list of numbers into equal-width classes, 5 or more by Sturges' rule, and prepares them to be drawn as bars.

parameters.name: paData
parameters.role: The raw measurements, a list of numbers

notes: text or a non-list raises "paData must be a list of numbers"
warnings: An empty list raises "paData must contain only numbers", which does not say it is empty, and a list of equal numbers gives a last bin whose upper edge is below its lower edge

methods.name: ToCanvasQ
methods.brief: Draws the bin counts and the bin labels as touching bars on a new canvas and answers it, so the histogram can become SVG or PNG.

parameters.name: paOptions
parameters.role: A list of options [ :Width = , :Height = , :Title = , :Font = an stzFont, :Color = , :Background = , :Grid = , :ShowValues = , :Min = , :Max = ]

notes: the count above each bar is written unless :ShowValues = 0
warnings: The bins, the aggregation and the labels carry over, while percentages, axis switches, characters and spacing do not

methods.name: ToSVG
methods.brief: Returns the histogram as SVG text, with no graphics device needed.

parameters.name: paOptions
parameters.role: A list of options [ :Width = , :Height = , :Title = , :Font = an stzFont, ... ], as for ToCanvasQ

methods.returns: the SVG document as a string
notes: the default size is 900 by 500 and text needs a Font

methods.name: ToPNG
methods.brief: Draws the histogram on the graphics device and returns the PNG bytes, writing them to a file when a path is given.

parameters.name: pcPath
parameters.role: The file to write, or an empty text to write none

parameters.name: paOptions
parameters.role: A list of options [ :Width = , :Height = , :Title = , :Font = an stzFont, ... ], as for ToCanvasQ

methods.returns: the PNG bytes as a string, empty when no device is available

methods.name: SetBinCount
methods.brief: Splits the data into n equal-width bins again; a value of 0 or less is ignored.

parameters.name: n
parameters.role: The number of bins

methods.returns: nothing; the bins and the picture change
notes: the default is 5 or more by Sturges' rule
warnings: A count that is not a whole number drops the largest values, because the last bin then ends before the maximum

methods.name: SetBarCount
methods.brief: Splits the data into n equal-width bins, under the bar name.

parameters.name: n
parameters.role: The number of bins, ignored when 0 or less

methods.returns: nothing; the bins and the picture change

methods.name: SetClassCount
methods.brief: Splits the data into n equal-width bins, under the class name of statistics.

parameters.name: n
parameters.role: The number of bins, ignored when 0 or less

methods.returns: nothing; the bins and the picture change

methods.name: DivideToNClasses
methods.brief: Splits the data into n equal-width bins, worded as a division into classes.

parameters.name: n
parameters.role: The number of bins, ignored when 0 or less

methods.returns: nothing; the bins and the picture change

methods.name: DivideToNGroups
methods.brief: Splits the data into n equal-width bins, worded as a division into groups.

parameters.name: n
parameters.role: The number of bins, ignored when 0 or less

methods.returns: nothing; the bins and the picture change

methods.name: SetBinRange
methods.brief: Cuts the data into ceil((largest count - smallest count) / n) bins, usually one, instead of bins n wide.

parameters.name: n
parameters.role: The wanted width of a bin, ignored when 0 or less

notes: use SetBinCount for a number of bins
warnings: The bin count is worked out from the range of the bar heights, not of the data, so SetBinRange(10) on values from 12 to 70 gives one bin and SetBinRange(3) gives two

methods.name: SetClassRange
methods.brief: Cuts the data into the same wrong number of classes as SetBinRange does, usually one, instead of classes n wide.

parameters.name: n
parameters.role: The wanted width of a class, ignored when 0 or less

warnings: Same cause: the count comes from the bar heights, so the result is one or two bins

methods.name: SetHeight
methods.brief: Sets the height the Ring renderer draws, which the engine renderer fixes at 10 rows and so ignores.

parameters.name: n
parameters.role: The height in rows

methods.returns: nothing; only the Ring renderer changes
notes: the default is 10
warnings: The usual ToString ignores it, and obeys it only when statistics are on or the horizontal axis is off, since those use the Ring renderer

methods.name: SetValues
methods.brief: Shows or hides the count above each bar, but only the Ring renderer draws it.

parameters.name: bShow
parameters.role: 1 to write the counts, 0 to stop

methods.returns: nothing; only the Ring renderer changes
notes: the counts appear when statistics are on or the horizontal axis is off
warnings: ToString never draws the counts because the engine renderer reads a flag nothing sets, so use AddPercent or ToStringInRing

methods.name: IncludeValues
methods.brief: Turns the count above each bar on, but only the Ring renderer draws it.
methods.returns: nothing; only the Ring renderer changes
warnings: ToString never draws the counts

methods.name: AddValues
methods.brief: Turns the count above each bar on, but only the Ring renderer draws it.
methods.returns: nothing; only the Ring renderer changes
warnings: ToString never draws the counts

methods.name: WithoutValues
methods.brief: Turns the count above each bar off.

methods.name: SetAggregation
methods.brief: Chooses what each bar shows: the count of values in the bin or their sum, mean, smallest or largest.

parameters.name: cType
parameters.role: The aggregation, in lower case: "frequency", "sum", "average", "min" or "max"

notes: an empty bin shows 0
warnings: Any other text, "SUM" with capitals included, raises R2 from max() and leaves the histogram empty, so ToString then raises too

methods.name: AggregationType
methods.brief: Returns which aggregation the bars show now.
notes: the default is "frequency"

methods.name: Aggregation
methods.brief: Returns which aggregation the bars show now, under a shorter name.

methods.name: AggregationTypes
methods.brief: Returns the five aggregations a histogram accepts.

methods.name: UseFrequency
methods.brief: Makes each bar show how many values fall in its bin.
notes: this is the default

methods.name: UseFreq
methods.brief: Makes each bar show how many values fall in its bin, under a shorter name.

methods.name: UseSum
methods.brief: Makes each bar show the sum of the values in its bin.
notes: Mode then names the bin with the largest sum

methods.name: UseAverage
methods.brief: Makes each bar show the mean of the values in its bin, 0 for an empty bin.

methods.name: UseMin
methods.brief: Makes each bar show the smallest value in its bin, 0 for an empty bin.

methods.name: UseMax
methods.brief: Makes each bar show the largest value in its bin, 0 for an empty bin.

methods.name: SetStats
methods.brief: Shows or hides four lines under the picture giving the mean, standard deviation, median and count of the data.

parameters.name: bShow
parameters.role: 1 to add the lines, 0 to remove them

notes: it switches the drawing to the Ring renderer, which obeys SetHeight and SetValues

methods.name: AddStats
methods.brief: Adds four lines under the picture giving the mean, standard deviation, median and count of the data.

methods.name: IncludeStats
methods.brief: Adds the statistics lines under the picture, under the Include name.

methods.name: SetVAxis
methods.brief: Shows or hides the vertical axis with its arrow, the one that runs up beside the bars.

parameters.name: bShow
parameters.role: 1 to show it, 0 to hide it

notes: the bars and labels keep their place

methods.name: AddVAxis
methods.brief: Shows the vertical axis with its arrow.

methods.name: IncludeVAxis
methods.brief: Shows the vertical axis with its arrow, under the Include name.

methods.name: WithoutVAxis
methods.brief: Hides the vertical axis and its arrow.

methods.name: SetXAxis
methods.brief: Shows or hides the VERTICAL axis, under the X name kept for old code.

parameters.name: bShow

methods.name: AddXAxis
methods.brief: Shows the VERTICAL axis, under the X name kept for old code.

methods.name: IncludeXAxis
methods.brief: Shows the VERTICAL axis, under the X name and the Include name.
warnings: The X name here means the vertical axis

methods.name: WithoutXAxis
methods.brief: Hides the VERTICAL axis, under the X name kept for old code.

methods.name: SetHAxis

parameters.name: bShow

notes: hiding it switches the drawing to the Ring renderer and keeps the bin labels

methods.name: AddHAxis
methods.brief: Shows the horizontal axis line under the bars.

methods.name: IncludeHAxis
methods.brief: Shows the horizontal axis line under the bars, under the Include name.

methods.name: WithoutHAxis
methods.brief: Hides the horizontal axis line, its arrow and its origin mark.

methods.name: SetYAxis
methods.brief: Shows or hides the HORIZONTAL axis, under the Y name kept for old code.

parameters.name: bShow

methods.name: AddYAxis
methods.brief: Shows the HORIZONTAL axis, under the Y name kept for old code.

methods.name: IncludeYAxis
methods.brief: Shows the HORIZONTAL axis, under the Y name and the Include name.
warnings: The Y name here means the horizontal axis

methods.name: WithoutYAxis
methods.brief: Hides the HORIZONTAL axis, under the Y name kept for old code.

parameters.name: bShow

methods.name: IncludeLabels
methods.brief: Shows the two rows of bin labels under the bars, under the Include name.

methods.name: WithoutLabels

methods.name: IncludePercent
methods.brief: Writes each bar's share of all the data above it, under the Include name.

parameters.name: nWidth

methods.name: Mean
methods.brief: Returns the arithmetic mean of the raw data.

methods.name: StandardDeviation
methods.brief: Returns the sample standard deviation of the raw data, dividing by n minus 1.
notes: 0 for one value or none

methods.name: Median
methods.brief: Returns the middle value of the raw data, or the mean of the two middle ones.

methods.name: Mode
methods.brief: Returns the lower and upper edge of the bin with the largest bar, the first one when several tie.
methods.returns: a list of two numbers [ low, high ]
notes: it reads the bar heights, so after UseSum it names the bin with the largest sum

methods.name: DataCount
methods.brief: Returns how many values the histogram was built from.

methods.name: Show
methods.brief: Prints the histogram as text on the console.

methods.name: ToString
methods.brief: Returns the histogram as text, with bars that follow the bins, a vertical axis, and the bin edges written in two rows.
notes: it hands over to the Ring renderer when statistics are on or the horizontal axis is off
warnings: Raises an error when the engine cannot render the histogram

methods.name: ToStringInRing
methods.brief: Returns the histogram as text drawn by the Ring code the engine renderer was ported from.
notes: it honours SetHeight, SetValues and SetStats, which ToString only does by falling back to it

classes.name: stzHistoricalComparison
classes.brief: Compares an executed plan with the planner's history of executions: its gain over the average cost and the best past plan.
classes.description: It is built by stzGraphPlanner.CompareWithHistoryQ. The history includes the compared plan's own run.
classes.receiver: g1 = new stzGraph("g1"); g1.AddNodeXTT("a", "A", [ :x = 0 ]); g1.AddNodeXTT("b", "B", [ :x = 1 ]); g1.AddNodeXTT("c", "C", [ :x = 2 ]); g1.AddEdgeXTT("a", "b", "r", [ :distance = 5, :cost = 1 ]); g1.AddEdgeXTT("b", "c", "r", [ :distance = 5, :cost = 9 ]); g1.AddEdgeXTT("a", "c", "r", [ :distance = 20, :cost = 2 ]); o1 = new stzGraphPlanner(g1); o1.AddPlan("short"); o1.Walk("a", "c"); o1.Minimize("distance"); o1.Execute(); o1.AddPlan("cheap"); o1.Walk("a", "c"); o1.Minimize("cost"); o1.Execute(); o2 = o1.CompareWithHistoryXTQ("short")
classes.example:
? o2.IsImprovement()
#--> 0

methods.name: init
methods.brief: Builds a comparison of a plan's result with the planner's history of executions, which the planner supplies.

parameters.name: poPlanner
parameters.role: The stzGraphPlanner whose history is used

parameters.name: pcCurrentPlan
parameters.role: The name of the plan compared

parameters.name: paCurrentResult
parameters.role: The result list of that plan

parameters.name: paHistory
parameters.role: The history entries of the planner

warnings: usually reached through stzGraphPlanner.CompareWithHistoryQ

methods.name: Explain
methods.brief: Returns the plan's cost and steps next to the history's averages, an observation in percent and the best past plan.
warnings: the history includes the plan's own run, so the average is never fully independent of it

methods.name: IsImprovement
methods.brief: TRUE if the plan's cost is below the historical average cost.

methods.name: Improvement
methods.brief: Returns the plan's gain over the historical average cost as a ratio: positive when cheaper, negative when dearer.
warnings: 0 when the average is 0; ImprovementRatio is the same call

methods.name: ImprovementPercentage
methods.brief: Returns the plan's gain over the historical average cost in percent: positive when cheaper, negative when dearer.
warnings: 0 when the average is 0; Improvement100 is the same call

classes.name: stzHtml
classes.brief: Parses HTML text with the engine and finds its elements by tag, id or class, giving their text and attributes.
classes.description: Reach for it to read a page: Find takes a tag name, #id or .class and returns node handles (stzHtmlNode) whose Text and Attr read the element. Text on the document gives all the visible text with scripts and styles removed. The parser is read-only, so the document cannot be changed, and there are no selector combinators: use ElementsWhere to combine a tag, a class and an id. It holds text, it does not fetch pages; HtmlQ(text-or-file) is the shortcut.
classes.receiver:
o1 = new stzHtml('

Hello

Two
')
classes.example:
? o1.CountByTag("div")
#--> 2
? o1.FindFirst("#main").Klass()
#--> box big
? len(o1.Find(".box"))
#--> 2
? len(o1.ElementsWhere([ :Tag = "div", :Class = "big" ]))
#--> 1

methods.name: init
methods.brief: Builds a document object by parsing HTML text with the engine; a value that is not a text raises an error.

parameters.name: pcHtml
parameters.role: the HTML source as text

notes: the error text is Incorrect param type! pcHtml must be a string.; broken markup is accepted and repaired by the parser

methods.name: Content
methods.brief: Returns the HTML source the object was built from, unchanged.

methods.name: Reload
methods.brief: Parses new HTML text and drops the previous document.

parameters.name: pcHtml
parameters.role: the new HTML source as text

notes: Content, Text and every Find now answer for the new source

extensions.name: ReloadQ
extensions.adds: does what the method does, then returns the object, so the call can be chained

methods.name: Text
methods.brief: Returns the visible text of the whole document, without tags, scripts or styles; neighbouring elements run together.
notes: a div holding two p elements, Hello and World, reads HelloWorld; a document without any element gives its plain text back

methods.name: NumberOfElements
methods.brief: Returns how many elements the parser found, html, head and body included when the parser adds them.
notes: text without tags answers 0

methods.name: CountByTag
methods.brief: Returns how many elements have a given tag, ignoring the case of the tag.

parameters.name: pcTag
parameters.role: the tag name, such as div

notes: CountByTag("DIV") and CountByTag("div") agree

methods.name: Find
methods.brief: Returns the elements matching a selector: a tag name, #id or .class; an empty text, a non-text or no match gives an empty list.

parameters.name: pcSelector
parameters.role: a tag such as div, an id such as #main, or a class such as .box

notes: only these three forms exist: no combinators and no attribute selectors

extensions.name: FindQ
extensions.adds: does what the method does, then returns the object, so the call can be chained

methods.name: FindFirst
methods.brief: Returns the first element matching a selector, in document order.

parameters.name: pcSelector
parameters.role: a tag, #id or .class, as for Find

methods.returns: a stzHtmlNode; the empty text when nothing matches
notes: test the result with isObject before calling a method on it

methods.name: IsValid
methods.brief: Returns TRUE if the parse succeeded and produced at least one element.
notes: the empty text and plain text without tags answer FALSE

methods.name: Elements
methods.brief: Returns every element of the document as a node, in document order.
notes: a page of 12 elements gives 12 nodes, the first being html

methods.name: HasTag
methods.brief: Returns TRUE if at least one element has the tag.

parameters.name: pcTag
parameters.role: the tag name, such as table

notes: the case of the tag does not matter

methods.name: HasBody
methods.brief: Returns TRUE if the document has a body element.

methods.name: HasHead
methods.brief: Returns TRUE if the document has a head element.

methods.name: TagsUsed
methods.brief: Returns the distinct tag names, lower case, in the order they first appear.
notes: for a full page it starts with html, head, title

methods.name: ElementsWhere
methods.brief: Returns the elements matching every given constraint among :Tag, :Class and :Id.

parameters.name: paCriteria
parameters.role: a hash list such as [ :Tag = "div", :Class = "box" ]

notes: an empty list of criteria gives every element; a value that is not a list gives an empty list; a class matches one word of the class attribute

classes.name: stzHtmlBuilder
classes.brief: Assembles an HTML document from nodes added under a current position, and gives the text or writes it to a file.
classes.description: Reach for it to build a page piece by piece: AppendToCurrent adds a node under the current node, GoToLastChild or SetCurrent moves inside the node just added, GoUp comes back out, and Build gives the HTML text. The document lives in the builder itself, not in node objects, so chaining works: each method returns the builder itself. A node handed to AppendToCurrent is copied at that moment, so changes made to the original afterwards are not seen. The position is a number, readable as a path of child numbers with CurrentPath. Text and attribute values are written as given, with no escaping: that is the rule of the node class.
classes.receiver: o1 = new stzHtmlBuilder() d1 = o1.CreateNode("div") p1 = o1.CreateNode("p") p1.SetText("x") o1.AppendToCurrent(d1).GoToLastChild().AppendToCurrent(p1)
classes.example:
? o1.Build() #-->

x

? @@( o1.CurrentPath() ) #--> [ 1 ]

methods.name: init
methods.brief: Starts an empty document: a tag-less root container that is also the current node.

methods.name: CreateNode
methods.brief: Returns a new detached node with the tag; it is not part of the document until it is appended.

parameters.name: pcTag
parameters.role: the tag name, such as ul

notes: the node is a separate object: changes made to it after it was appended are not seen in the document

methods.name: AppendToCurrent
methods.brief: Adds a copy of a node, with all its descendants, as the last child of the current node.

parameters.name: poNode
parameters.role: the stzHtmlBuildNode to add; it may already have children, and the same node may be added again, which adds another copy

methods.returns: the builder itself, so that calls can be chained
notes: the current node does not move: call GoToLastChild to go inside the node just added; changes made to the original node after the call are not seen in the document

extensions.name: AppendToCurrentQ
extensions.adds: does what the method does, then returns the object, so the call can be chained

methods.name: SetCurrent
methods.brief: Moves the current position to a node of the document, given as the node itself or as a path.

parameters.name: pNodeOrPath
parameters.role: a stzHtmlBuildNode equal to one already in the document, or a path as a list of child numbers counted from the root, such as [ 2, 1 ]; the empty list is the root

notes: a node is found by what it contains (tag, text, attributes and descendants), not by identity, because Ring copies objects: of two equal nodes the one added last wins, and Root() gives the root; a node that is not in the document raises an error

extensions.name: SetCurrentQ
extensions.adds: does what the method does, then returns the object, so the call can be chained

methods.name: SetCurrentPath
methods.brief: Moves the current position to the node at a path of child numbers counted from the root.

parameters.name: paPath
parameters.role: a list of child numbers, one per level, such as [ 2, 1 ] for the first child of the second child of the root; the empty list means the root

notes: a number that is not a child position of its level raises an error and leaves the position where it was

methods.name: CurrentPath
methods.brief: Returns where the current node lies, as the child numbers to follow from the root.
methods.returns: a list of numbers, empty when the current node is the root

methods.name: GoToLastChild
methods.brief: Makes the last child of the current node the current one, to build inside the node just added.
notes: a current node without children raises an error and the position stays

methods.name: GoUp
methods.brief: Makes the parent of the current node the current one; at the root it stays where it is.
notes: at the root nothing is raised, as with a path that cannot go higher

methods.name: GoToRoot
methods.brief: Makes the root the current node, so that the next node is added at the top of the document.

methods.name: Current
methods.brief: Returns a copy of the node that new children are added to, with everything below it.
notes: it is a snapshot: a change made to it does not reach the builder

methods.name: Root
methods.brief: Returns a copy of the tag-less root container of the document, with everything below it.
notes: it is a snapshot taken at the call: a change made to it does not reach the builder

methods.name: NodeCount
methods.brief: Returns how many nodes the document holds, the root container not counted.
notes: a node added with children counts for itself and each descendant

methods.name: Build
methods.brief: Returns the HTML text of the document: the children of the root, one after the other.
methods.returns: a text, empty when nothing was added
notes: it is the text the node class gives with ToHtml, with no escaping of its own

methods.name: BuildToFile
methods.brief: Writes the HTML text of the document to a file, exactly the bytes the text holds.

parameters.name: pcPath
parameters.role: the file to write, which is replaced if it exists

notes: nothing is added to the text: no byte order mark, and a line break is written as the text holds it; a path that cannot be written raises an error

classes.name: stzHtmlBuildNode
classes.brief: Holds one element of an HTML tree to be written out: a tag, a text, attributes and child nodes.
classes.description: Reach for it to produce HTML without pasting strings: create a node, SetText, SetAttr and AppendChild, then call ToHtml on the top node. A node whose tag is the empty text is a container that writes only its children. Texts and attribute values are written as given, with no escaping, and a child is stored as a copy, so build each child fully before appending it.
classes.receiver: o1 = new stzHtmlBuildNode("ul") li = new stzHtmlBuildNode("li") li.SetText("one") li.SetAttr("class", "x") o1.AppendChild(li)
classes.example:
? o1.ToHtml() #-->
  • one
? len(o1.Children()) #--> 1

methods.name: init
methods.brief: Builds a node with a tag, no text, no attribute and no child; the empty tag makes a container written without a tag of its own.

parameters.name: pcTag
parameters.role: the tag name, or the empty text for a container

methods.name: Tag
methods.brief: Returns the tag name as it was given.

methods.name: SetText
methods.brief: Sets the text written inside the node before its children and returns the node.

parameters.name: pcText
parameters.role: the text, written as given

notes: the text is not escaped: a < stays a <, so do not pass untrusted text

extensions.name: SetTextQ
extensions.adds: does what the method does, then returns the object, so the call can be chained

methods.name: Text
methods.brief: Returns the text of the node, not counting its children.

methods.name: SetAttr
methods.brief: Adds an attribute and returns the node.

parameters.name: pcName
parameters.role: the attribute name

parameters.name: pcValue
parameters.role: the value, written between double quotes

notes: the value is not escaped, so a double quote inside it breaks the markup; setting a name twice writes it twice

methods.name: Attrs
methods.brief: Returns the attributes of the node as a list of [ name, value ] pairs, in the order they were set.
methods.returns: a list, empty when no attribute was set
notes: it is a copy: a change made to it does not reach the node

methods.name: AppendChild
methods.brief: Adds a node as the last child and returns the node.

parameters.name: poNode
parameters.role: the node to add

notes: the child is stored as a copy, so changes made to the original afterwards do not appear in the output

methods.name: Children
methods.brief: Returns the list of child nodes, in the order they were added.

methods.name: ToHtml
methods.brief: Returns the node as HTML: opening tag with attributes, the text, the children, then the closing tag.
notes: a node with the empty tag gives only its children; a node without text or children gives an empty element such as

methods.name: ChildrenHtml
methods.brief: Returns the HTML of the children only, one after the other, without the tag of this node.

classes.name: stzHtmlNode
classes.brief: Points at one element of a parsed HTML document and reads its tag, text, id, class and attributes.
classes.description: A handle is the document, a tag name and the rank of the element among elements of that tag. It is made by Find, FindFirst, Elements and ElementsWhere of stzHtml. The document is read-only, so a node cannot change anything.
classes.receiver:
d1 = new stzHtml('
link
') o1 = d1.FindFirst("#main")
classes.example:
? o1.Tag()
#--> div
? o1.HasKlass("big")
#--> 1
? o1.Text()
#--> link
? d1.FindFirst("a").Attr("href")
#--> /u

methods.name: init
methods.brief: Builds a handle to the n-th element with a given tag in a stzHtml document.

parameters.name: oDoc
parameters.role: the stzHtml document that owns the element

parameters.name: pcTag
parameters.role: the tag name

parameters.name: nOccurrence
parameters.role: which element of that tag, counted from 1

notes: normally made by Find, FindFirst or Elements of stzHtml

methods.name: Tag
methods.brief: Returns the tag name in lower case.

methods.name: Text
methods.brief: Returns the text inside the element, descendants included.
notes: text of child elements runs together: a paragraph with a bold part reads World x; a script element gives its code

methods.name: Attr
methods.brief: Returns the value of one attribute of the element; the empty text when it is absent.

parameters.name: cName
parameters.role: the attribute name, such as href

notes: an attribute present with an empty value looks absent

methods.name: HasAttr
methods.brief: Returns TRUE if the element has the attribute with a value that is not empty.

parameters.name: cName
parameters.role: the attribute name

notes: it is the test of Attr(name) against the empty text

methods.name: Id
methods.brief: Returns the id attribute of the element; the empty text when there is none.

methods.name: Klass
methods.brief: Returns the whole class attribute as one text; the empty text when there is none.
notes: the classes box and big come as one text: box big

methods.name: HasKlass
methods.brief: Returns TRUE if one of the words of the class attribute equals the class.

parameters.name: pcClass
parameters.role: the class name to look for

notes: box big has box and big but not bo

classes.name: stzHttpClient
classes.brief: Sends HTTP and HTTPS requests through the engine and keeps the last answer, with settings for headers, cookies, auth, proxy and timeouts.
classes.description: Configure the client with the Set methods, each of which returns the client so calls chain, then send with Get_, Post, Put_, Delete, Head, Options, PostForm or PostJson and read the answer with ResponseCode, ResponseBody and ResponseHeaders. A status of 4xx or 5xx is an answer, not an error; a request that never reached a server gives ResponseCode -1 and sets LastError. GetMany fetches up to 32 addresses in one parallel call. The requests need a network: to try the class offline, start the engine's loopback fixture with StzEngineTestServerStart(0) and stop it with StzEngineTestServerStop(), as test/network/73_http_loopback_narrated.ring does.
classes.example:
o1.SetTimeout(5)
? o1.Timeout()
#--> 5
? o1.RequestTimeout()
#--> 5000

methods.name: init
methods.brief: Builds a client with no headers, no cookies, the user agent Softanza-HTTP/1.0 and the engine default timeouts.
notes: every field starts from its declared default

methods.name: SetUserAgent
methods.brief: Sets the User-Agent header sent with every later request, replacing Softanza-HTTP/1.0.

parameters.name: cAgent
parameters.role: the User-Agent text

methods.returns: the client itself, so calls chain

methods.name: SetHeader
methods.brief: Adds one request header, sent with every later request, after the headers already added.

parameters.name: cName
parameters.role: the header name

parameters.name: cValue
parameters.role: the header value

methods.returns: the client itself, so calls chain
notes: adding the same name twice sends both lines; a header named Authorization reaches the server (a loopback /auth answered 200)

methods.name: SetHeaders
methods.brief: Replaces all the custom headers with a list of ready-made Name: Value lines.

parameters.name: aHeaders
parameters.role: a list of texts, each Name: Value

methods.returns: the client itself, so calls chain
notes: headers added earlier through SetHeader are dropped

methods.name: SetCookie
methods.brief: Adds one name=value cookie, sent in a single Cookie header with every later request.

parameters.name: cName
parameters.role: the cookie name

parameters.name: cValue
parameters.role: the cookie value

methods.returns: the client itself, so calls chain
notes: two cookies are joined as sid=abc; k=v (a loopback /checkcookie answered that text)

methods.name: SetCookies
methods.brief: Replaces all the cookies with a list of ready-made name=value texts.

parameters.name: aCookies
parameters.role: a list of texts, each name=value

methods.returns: the client itself, so calls chain
notes: cookies added earlier through SetCookie are dropped

methods.name: SetTraceParent
methods.brief: Sets the W3C traceparent header so a downstream service can place the request in the caller's trace.

parameters.name: cTraceParent
parameters.role: a traceparent value such as 00-<trace id>-<span id>-01

methods.returns: the client itself, so calls chain
notes: the value is not validated, it is sent as given

methods.name: StartTrace
methods.brief: Starts a fresh sampled trace, adds it as the traceparent header and returns its value.
methods.returns: a text, the new traceparent value
notes: each call makes a new trace id, and the header is added, not replaced, so a second call sends two traceparent lines

methods.name: SetTimeout
methods.brief: Sets the overall request timeout in seconds, so that Timeout and RequestTimeout both report it.

parameters.name: nSeconds
parameters.role: the timeout in seconds, stored in milliseconds for the engine

methods.returns: the client itself, so calls chain
notes: SetTimeout(5) makes RequestTimeout answer 5000

methods.name: SetConnectTimeout
methods.brief: Sets how long the client waits to open a connection, in milliseconds.

parameters.name: nMs
parameters.role: the connect timeout in milliseconds, 0 keeps the engine default of 5 seconds

methods.returns: the client itself, so calls chain

methods.name: SetRequestTimeout
methods.brief: Sets how long one whole request may take, in milliseconds.

parameters.name: nMs
parameters.role: the request timeout in milliseconds, 0 keeps the engine default of 30 seconds

methods.returns: the client itself, so calls chain
notes: a request that outlives it ends with ResponseCode -1 (loopback test 73_http_loopback_narrated)

methods.name: ConnectTimeout
methods.brief: Returns the connect timeout this client was given, in milliseconds.
methods.returns: a number; 0 when the engine default applies

methods.name: RequestTimeout
methods.brief: Returns the request timeout this client was given, in milliseconds.
methods.returns: a number; 0 when the engine default applies

methods.name: SetDefaultTimeouts
methods.brief: Sets the engine-wide default connect, request and idle timeouts for every client in the process.

parameters.name: nConnectMs
parameters.role: the default connect timeout in milliseconds

parameters.name: nRequestMs
parameters.role: the default request timeout in milliseconds

parameters.name: nIdleMs
parameters.role: the idle timeout of pooled connections in milliseconds

methods.returns: the client itself, so calls chain
notes: a value of 0 leaves that default unchanged, and the change outlives this client

methods.name: Shutdown
methods.brief: Closes the idle keep-alive connections held in the engine pool and counts them.
methods.returns: a number, how many idle sockets were closed
notes: requests in flight are not touched, and 0 is the normal answer when every server closed its connection after the reply

methods.name: PoolStats
methods.brief: Returns the connection pool counters as a hash list of opens, reuses, idle and active connections.
methods.returns: a hash list with the keys opens, reuses, idle and active, all numbers
notes: the counters are process-wide, not per client

methods.name: FollowRedirects
methods.brief: Switches the following of 3xx redirects on or off for later requests; it is on by default.

parameters.name: bFollow
parameters.role: TRUE to follow redirects, FALSE to receive the 302 itself

methods.returns: the client itself, so calls chain
notes: with it off, a 3-hop redirect chain answers 302, with it on 200

methods.name: VerifySSL
methods.brief: Switches the check of the server's TLS certificate on or off for later requests; it is on by default.

parameters.name: bVerify
parameters.role: TRUE to check certificates, FALSE to accept any

methods.returns: the client itself, so calls chain
notes: not run against a TLS server: only plain loopback HTTP was called, where it changes nothing

methods.name: SetProxy
methods.brief: Routes later requests through a proxy, given as host:port.

parameters.name: cProxy_
parameters.role: the proxy address such as 127.0.0.1:3128, an empty text removes the proxy

methods.returns: the client itself, so calls chain
notes: pointing at a port with nothing listening makes the request fail with ResponseCode -1

methods.name: SetProxyAuth
methods.brief: Stores the user and password the client presents to its proxy, sent as user:password.

parameters.name: cUser
parameters.role: the proxy user name

parameters.name: cPass
parameters.role: the proxy password

methods.returns: the client itself, so calls chain
notes: it matters only while a proxy is set, and no authenticating proxy was available to run it against

methods.name: SetAuth
methods.brief: Sets the user and password for HTTP authentication, Basic unless SetAuthType says otherwise.

parameters.name: cUser
parameters.role: the user name

parameters.name: cPass
parameters.role: the password

methods.returns: the client itself, so calls chain
notes: a loopback /auth endpoint that wants any Authorization header answered 401 without it and 200 with it

methods.name: SetAuthType
methods.brief: Chooses the HTTP authentication scheme that SetAuth uses.

parameters.name: cType
parameters.role: basic, digest, ntlm, negotiate or any, in any case

methods.returns: the client itself, so calls chain
notes: the text is stored in lower case, and only basic was run because the other schemes need a server that asks for them

methods.name: SetBearer
methods.brief: Sets an OAuth2 bearer token sent as the Authorization header of later requests.

parameters.name: cToken
parameters.role: the bearer token

methods.returns: the client itself, so calls chain
notes: the token travels in clear on plain HTTP, and a loopback /auth endpoint answered 200

methods.name: SetClientCert
methods.brief: Sets the client certificate and private key used for mutual TLS.

parameters.name: cCertPath
parameters.role: the path of the PEM certificate file

parameters.name: cKeyPath
parameters.role: the path of the PEM private key file

methods.returns: the client itself, so calls chain
notes: not run against a TLS server: on plain HTTP with missing files the request still answered 200, so the paths are not read there

methods.name: SetCookieFile
methods.brief: Sets a Netscape cookie file from which later requests read their cookies.

parameters.name: cPath
parameters.role: the path of the cookie file

methods.returns: the client itself, so calls chain
notes: give SetCookieJar the same path to keep cookies between requests

methods.name: SetCookieJar
methods.brief: Sets the cookie file in which cookies received from servers are saved.

parameters.name: cPath
parameters.role: the path of the file to write

methods.returns: the client itself, so calls chain
notes: with the same path as SetCookieFile, a cookie set by /setcookie came back on the next request

methods.name: AcceptEncoding
methods.brief: Asks servers for compressed answers and decompresses them, for the encodings named.

parameters.name: cEnc
parameters.role: the encodings to advertise such as gzip, an empty text advertises every one the engine supports

methods.returns: the client itself, so calls chain
notes: compression is off until this or AcceptGzip is called, and the loopback server never compresses, so only the call was checked

methods.name: AcceptGzip
methods.brief: Asks servers for compressed answers in every encoding the engine supports and decompresses them.
methods.returns: the client itself, so calls chain
notes: the loopback server never compresses, so only the call was checked

methods.name: Get_
methods.brief: Sends a GET request and keeps the answer in the client.

parameters.name: cUrl
parameters.role: the address to fetch

methods.returns: the client itself, so read the answer with ResponseCode and ResponseBody
notes: the name ends in an underscore because Get is taken by the language
warnings: a transport failure gives ResponseCode -1 and sets LastError, while a 4xx or 5xx status is not an error, only a code

methods.name: Post
methods.brief: Sends a POST request with a body, content type application/octet-stream, and keeps the answer.

parameters.name: cUrl
parameters.role: the address to post to

parameters.name: cData
parameters.role: the request body as text

methods.returns: the client itself, so read the answer with ResponseBody
notes: a loopback /echo answered with the same body

methods.name: Put_
methods.brief: Sends a PUT request with a body, content type application/octet-stream, and keeps the answer.

parameters.name: cUrl
parameters.role: the address to put to

parameters.name: cData
parameters.role: the request body as text

methods.returns: the client itself, so read the answer with ResponseBody
notes: the name ends in an underscore because Put is taken by the language

methods.name: Delete
methods.brief: Sends a DELETE request and keeps the answer.

parameters.name: cUrl
parameters.role: the address to delete

methods.returns: the client itself, so read the answer with ResponseCode

methods.name: Head
methods.brief: Sends a HEAD request, which returns the status and headers but no body.

parameters.name: cUrl
parameters.role: the address to ask about

methods.returns: the client itself, so read the answer with ResponseHeaders
notes: ResponseBody stays empty

methods.name: Options
methods.brief: Sends an OPTIONS request and keeps the answer.

parameters.name: cUrl
parameters.role: the address to ask about

methods.returns: the client itself, so read the answer with ResponseHeaders

methods.name: PerformRequest
methods.brief: Does nothing and returns the client; it exists only so that older code that calls it still runs.
notes: it sends no request, because it does not know which verb to use

methods.name: Response
methods.brief: Returns the last answer as a hash list with its body, status code, header text and connection info.
methods.returns: a hash list with the keys body, code, headers and info
notes: before any request the code is 0 and the body is empty, and after a failed request the code is -1

methods.name: ResponseCode

methods.name: ResponseTime

methods.name: PostForm

methods.returns: the client itself, so read the answer with ResponseBody

methods.name: DownloadFile

parameters.name: cLocalPath
parameters.role: the path of the file to write

notes: only a transport failure stops the write, an answer with status 404 is still written to the file
warnings: the file is overwritten if it exists

methods.name: GetMany
methods.brief: Fetches several addresses in one parallel call, each with this client's headers, options and timeouts.

parameters.name: aUrls
parameters.role: a list of at most 32 addresses

methods.returns: a list of hash lists, each with body, code, headers and info

classes.name: stzHttpSandbox
classes.brief: Stands in for an HTTP service offline, answering from rules you script or answers you recorded, and journals every request.
classes.description: It follows the HTTP port contract: any object with Request(method, url, body) that returns a list with status, body and from. Scripted mode drives behaviour, with a rule per method and address pattern, first match winning. Replay mode keeps what a real service said, filed under a hash of method, address and body, and a recording wins over a rule. By default an unscripted, unrecorded request raises an error, because a double that silently answers makes a test pass for the wrong reason; SetStrict(0) answers 501 instead. Every request is journalled, so a test can check what the code tried to do. The state lives in a table shared by copies, so a copy of the sandbox sees the same rules.
classes.example:
o1.Script("GET", "https://api.test/rates", 200, '{"eur":0.92}')
? o1.GetFrom("https://api.test/rates")[:body]
#--> {"eur":0.92}
? o1.NumberOfCallsTo("https://api.test/rates")
#--> 1

methods.name: init
methods.brief: Builds an offline HTTP double with no rules, no recordings, an empty journal and strict mode on.

methods.name: IsSandbox
methods.brief: TRUE if the object is a fake, which is how a service registry tells it from a live client.

methods.name: Script
methods.brief: Adds a rule: requests with that method and a matching address get that status and body.

parameters.name: pcMethod
parameters.role: the HTTP method, kept in upper case

parameters.name: pcUrlPattern
parameters.role: an exact address, a prefix ending in *, or a part between a * at each end

parameters.name: pnStatus
parameters.role: the status number to answer with

parameters.name: pcBody
parameters.role: the response body

notes: ScriptQ is the same call and returns the sandbox
warnings: rules are tried in the order added and the first match wins, so put a general rule last; a pattern with a * only at its start, such as */rates, is taken as an exact address and never matches; the method matches without regard to case but the address with it; a status given as text stays text

extensions.name: ScriptQ
extensions.adds: does what the method does, then returns the object, so the call can be chained

methods.name: ScriptFailureQ
methods.brief: Adds a rule that makes matching requests answer with a failure status and an empty body.

parameters.name: pcMethod
parameters.role: the HTTP method

parameters.name: pcUrlPattern
parameters.role: the address pattern, as for Script

parameters.name: pnStatus
parameters.role: the failure status, such as 503

methods.returns: the sandbox itself, so calls chain
warnings: the way to test a service that fails, which a real vendor will not do on demand

methods.name: NumberOfScripts
methods.brief: Returns how many rules the sandbox holds.

methods.name: SeedResponse
methods.brief: Keeps a recorded answer for an exact method, address and request body, replacing an earlier one for the same three.

parameters.name: pcMethod
parameters.role: the HTTP method

parameters.name: pcUrl
parameters.role: the exact address

parameters.name: pcReqBody
parameters.role: the exact request body

parameters.name: pnStatus
parameters.role: the status to replay

parameters.name: pcRespBody
parameters.role: the body to replay

notes: SeedResponseQ is the same call and returns the sandbox
warnings: a recording is found only for the same body, and it wins over any rule

extensions.name: SeedResponseQ
extensions.adds: does what the method does, then returns the object, so the call can be chained

methods.name: RecordFrom
methods.brief: Sends a request to another client once and keeps the answer, so that the sandbox replays it from then on.

parameters.name: poClient
parameters.role: any object with a Request(method, url, body) method, such as a second sandbox or stzReactorHttpClient

parameters.name: pcMethod
parameters.role: the HTTP method

parameters.name: pcUrl
parameters.role: the address

parameters.name: pcReqBody
parameters.role: the request body

methods.returns: the answer of the client, a list with status, body and from
notes: the sandbox's own journal does not note the request, only the client's
warnings: an error raised by the client, such as a strict miss, passes through and nothing is recorded

methods.name: NumberOfRecordings
methods.brief: Returns how many recorded answers the sandbox holds.

methods.name: HasRecording
methods.brief: TRUE if an answer is kept for exactly that method, address and body.

parameters.name: pcMethod
parameters.role: the HTTP method, matched without regard to case

parameters.name: pcUrl
parameters.role: the exact address

parameters.name: pcReqBody
parameters.role: the exact request body

methods.name: RequestKey
methods.brief: Returns the key a recording is filed under: a SHA-256 hash of the method in upper case, the address and the body.

parameters.name: pcMethod
parameters.role: the HTTP method

parameters.name: pcUrl
parameters.role: the address

parameters.name: pcReqBody
parameters.role: the request body

warnings: the same method in another letter case gives the same key

methods.name: Request
methods.brief: Answers a request from a recording first, then from the first matching rule, and notes the request in the journal.

parameters.name: pcMethod
parameters.role: the HTTP method, matched without regard to case

parameters.name: pcUrl
parameters.role: the address

parameters.name: pcReqBody
parameters.role: the request body

methods.returns: a hash list with status, body and from, from being replay, scripted or miss
notes: with strict mode off a miss answers status 501 with from miss
warnings: in strict mode, which is the default, a request with no recording and no rule raises an error naming the method and address; it is still journalled

methods.name: GetFrom
methods.brief: Sends a GET request with no body through Request.

parameters.name: pcUrl
parameters.role: the address

methods.returns: a hash list with status, body and from

methods.name: PostTo
methods.brief: Sends a POST request with a body through Request.

parameters.name: pcUrl
parameters.role: the address

parameters.name: pcBody
parameters.role: the request body

methods.returns: a hash list with status, body and from

methods.name: SetStrict
methods.brief: Chooses whether a request that matches nothing raises an error (1) or answers a 501 miss (0).

parameters.name: pbOn
parameters.role: 1 for strict, 0 to let misses through

warnings: SetStrictQ is the same call and returns the sandbox

extensions.name: SetStrictQ
extensions.adds: does what the method does, then returns the object, so the call can be chained

methods.name: IsStrict
methods.brief: TRUE if a request that matches nothing raises an error.

methods.name: Calls
methods.brief: Returns the journal of every request made, oldest first, those that raised an error included.
methods.returns: a list of rows [ method, url, body ], the method in upper case

methods.name: NumberOfCalls
methods.brief: Returns how many requests the journal holds.

methods.name: LastCall
methods.brief: Returns the most recent request of the journal.
methods.returns: a hash list with method, url and body; an empty list when the journal is empty

methods.name: NumberOfCallsTo
methods.brief: Returns how many journalled requests asked for exactly that address, whatever the method.

parameters.name: pcUrl
parameters.role: the exact address

warnings: the way to catch a request repeated too often

methods.name: WasCalled
methods.brief: TRUE if the journal holds a request with that method and exact address.

parameters.name: pcMethod
parameters.role: the HTTP method, matched without regard to case

parameters.name: pcUrl
parameters.role: the exact address

methods.name: ClearCalls
methods.brief: Empties the journal; rules and recordings stay.
warnings: ClearCallsQ is the same call and returns the sandbox

extensions.name: ClearCallsQ
extensions.adds: does what the method does, then returns the object, so the call can be chained

methods.name: Show
methods.brief: Prints one line giving the number of rules, recordings and journalled requests.

classes.name: stzHttpTask
classes.brief: Holds one HTTP request, its method, address and body, with a status, a body result and an error, run by the blocking path.
classes.description: A task of the reactive client when no reactor is set. Execute sends the request through the engine and records completed with the response body for a 2xx status, or error with the message HTTP request failed, the status in parentheses when one was received. Anything but GET, POST, PUT or DELETE makes no request and ends in error. Then_ and Catch_ come from stzReactiveTask. The four Perform methods are the requests; none was run for this reference because they reach the network. The example runs the one path that makes no request.
classes.receiver: oEngine = new stzReactive() o1 = new stzHttpTask(HTTP_TASK_GET, "http://example.invalid/", "PATCH", "", oEngine)
classes.example:
? o1.Status()
#--> pending
o1.Execute()
? o1.Status()
#--> error
? o1.Error()
#--> HTTP request failed
? o1.HasFailed()
#--> 1

methods.name: Init
methods.brief: Builds a task for one HTTP request with its method, address and body, in the pending state.

parameters.name: id
parameters.role: the task's identifier, such as http_get

parameters.name: url
parameters.role: the address

parameters.name: method
parameters.role: GET, POST, PUT or DELETE as the HTTP_GET, HTTP_POST, HTTP_PUT and HTTP_DELETE constants

parameters.name: data
parameters.role: the body to send, or an empty text

parameters.name: engine
parameters.role: the reactive engine it belongs to

methods.returns: nothing; the task is built and no request is made
notes: the error mode is the default, ERROR_LOG

methods.name: Execute
methods.brief: Sends the request by the blocking path and records the outcome on the task.
methods.returns: nothing; read the outcome with Status, Result and Error
notes: success is a 2xx status with a body: the status is completed, the body is the result and Then_ is called; anything else is an error whose message is HTTP request failed, with the status in parentheses when one was received, and Catch_ is called
warnings: not run against a real address: it reaches the network; a method that is none of the four makes no request and ends the task in error with the message HTTP request failed, which was run

methods.name: PerformHttpGet
methods.brief: Sends a GET request through the engine and returns the body, or an empty text on failure.

parameters.name: url
parameters.role: the address to fetch

methods.returns: the response body as text; an empty text for a status outside 200 to 299 or an empty body
notes: the status of the response is kept on the task for the failure message; this blocking path is what the client uses when it has no reactor
warnings: not run: it reaches the network

methods.name: PerformHttpPost
methods.brief: Sends a POST request with a body through the engine and returns the response body, or an empty text on failure.

parameters.name: url
parameters.role: the address to post to

parameters.name: data
parameters.role: the body to send, text

methods.returns: the response body as text; an empty text for a status outside 200 to 299 or an empty body
notes: a body that is not text is sent as an empty body
warnings: not run: it reaches the network

methods.name: PerformHttpPut
methods.brief: Sends a PUT request with a body through the engine and returns the response body, or an empty text on failure.

parameters.name: url
parameters.role: the address to put to

parameters.name: data
parameters.role: the body to send, text

methods.returns: the response body as text; an empty text for a status outside 200 to 299 or an empty body
notes: a body that is not text is sent as an empty body
warnings: not run: it reaches the network

methods.name: PerformHttpDelete
methods.brief: Sends a DELETE request through the engine and returns the response body, or an empty text on failure.

parameters.name: url
parameters.role: the address to delete

methods.returns: the response body as text; an empty text for a status outside 200 to 299 or an empty body
notes: a successful delete that answers with no body counts as a failure here
warnings: not run: it reaches the network

classes.name: stzImgToAscii
classes.brief: Turns an image into text art (ansi, ascii, svg or html) by running the external im2ansi tool, and keeps the text or the file.
classes.description: Give the image, set the options (format, height, width, ramp, invert, no colour, seed, characters, output file), then read Content or call Show; Execute runs the tool and the other two run it when nothing ran yet. The tool is started as a program with a list of arguments, with no shell between, so a path holding spaces reaches it intact. The class is loaded by naming its file; no loader of the library does it.
classes.example:
o1.Format("ascii")
? o1.Content()

methods.name: init
methods.brief: Builds the converter, with the image to convert when one is given, and creates its temp and output folders.

parameters.name: pcImage
parameters.role: the path of the image to convert, an empty text for none

warnings: the parameter is required, since Ring has no default values: give an empty text for none; an image path that does not exist raises the error Image not found; the folders temp and output are created in the current folder

methods.name: EnsureDirs
methods.brief: Creates the temp and output folders of the converter when they are missing.
warnings: the folders are named relative to the current folder; a folder that cannot be created raises the error Cannot create folder

methods.name: Image
methods.brief: Sets the image the tool will convert, after checking that the file exists, and returns the object.

parameters.name: pc
parameters.role: the path of the image file, as text

warnings: a path that is not an existing file raises the error Image not found

methods.name: Format
methods.brief: Chooses the kind of text the tool produces and returns the object.

parameters.name: pc
parameters.role: the format, as text: ansi, ascii, svg or html, in any case

notes: svg and html are written to a file; ansi and ascii are printed by the tool
warnings: any other format raises the error Unsupported format

methods.name: Height
methods.brief: Sets the height asked of the tool, sent as its -s option, and returns the object.

parameters.name: n
parameters.role: the height, as a number; 30 when never set

methods.name: Width
methods.brief: Sets the width asked of the tool, sent as its -w option, and returns the object.

parameters.name: n
parameters.role: the width, as a number; no width is sent when never set

methods.name: Chars
methods.brief: Sets a custom set of characters, sent as the -c option of the tool, and returns the object.

parameters.name: pc
parameters.role: the characters, as text; none is sent when never set

methods.name: Ramp
methods.brief: Sets the ramp number sent to the tool as its -r option for the ascii format, and returns the object.

parameters.name: n
parameters.role: the ramp number, from 1 to 12; 1 when never set

warnings: a number outside 1 to 12 raises the error Ramp 1-12 only

methods.name: Invert
methods.brief: Asks the tool to invert the image, with its -i option, and returns the object.

methods.name: SetInvert
methods.brief: Turns the inversion on or off and returns the object.

parameters.name: b
parameters.role: 1 to invert, 0 to leave the image as it is

methods.name: NoColor
methods.brief: Asks the tool for plain output, with its --no-color option, and returns the object.

methods.name: SetNoColor
methods.brief: Turns the colourless output on or off and returns the object.

parameters.name: b
parameters.role: 1 for no colour, 0 for colour

methods.name: Seed
methods.brief: Sets the seed sent to the tool as its --seed option and returns the object.

parameters.name: n
parameters.role: the seed, as a number; none is sent when never set

methods.name: Verbose
methods.brief: Makes the next runs print the command line and the output file they use, and returns the object.

methods.name: SetVerbose
methods.brief: Turns the printing of the command line on or off and returns the object.

parameters.name: b
parameters.role: 1 to print, 0 to stay silent

methods.name: SetOutputFile
methods.brief: Sets the file the tool writes its result to, instead of printing the text, and returns the object.

parameters.name: pc
parameters.role: the path of the file, as text; an empty text goes back to the default

methods.name: Execute
methods.brief: Runs the im2ansi tool on the image and keeps the text it prints, or the file it writes for svg, html or a chosen output file.
methods.returns: nothing; read Content or OutputFile afterwards
notes: Run and Go are the same call; the output file defaults to a name in the output folder for the svg and html formats; a run that fails leaves no text and no file kept
warnings: needs the real im2ansi tool (not in the library) and starts it as a real program; with no image set it raises the error No image set, and a tool that exits with a code other than 0, or writes no file when one was asked, raises the error im2ansi failed

methods.name: Run
methods.brief: Runs the tool on the image, exactly as the main call does.
methods.returns: nothing; read Content or OutputFile afterwards
warnings: needs the real im2ansi tool, not in the library, see Execute

methods.name: Go
methods.brief: Runs the tool on the image, exactly as the main call does.
methods.returns: nothing; read Content or OutputFile afterwards
warnings: needs the real im2ansi tool, not in the library, see Execute

extensions.name: GoXT
extensions.adds: the extended form: more parameters than the base method

methods.name: Content
methods.brief: Returns the converted image as text, running the tool first when it did not run yet.
methods.returns: a text: what the tool printed, or the content of the file it wrote; an empty text when the file holds nothing
warnings: needs the real im2ansi tool (not in the library) the first time, see Execute

methods.name: Show
methods.brief: Prints the converted image, or opens the file the tool wrote in the program the system associates with it.
warnings: needs the real im2ansi tool (not in the library) when nothing ran yet; for the svg and html formats, or an output file chosen with OutputFile, it starts the viewer of the operating system and opens a window, unless the environment variable STZ_NO_VIEW is set

methods.name: View
methods.brief: Prints the converted image or opens its file, exactly as the main call does.
warnings: can open a window on the screen, see Show

methods.name: Display
methods.brief: Prints the converted image or opens its file, exactly as the main call does.
warnings: can open a window on the screen, see Show

methods.name: ExecuteAndShow
methods.brief: Runs the tool, then prints the converted image or opens its file, and returns nothing.
