warnings: needs the real im2ansi tool and can open a window, see Execute and Show

methods.name: RunAndView
methods.brief: Runs the tool, then prints the converted image or opens its file.
warnings: needs the real im2ansi tool and can open a window, see Execute and Show

methods.name: XT
methods.brief: Runs the tool, then prints the converted image or opens its file.
warnings: needs the real im2ansi tool and can open a window, see Execute and Show

methods.name: OutputFile
methods.brief: Returns the path of the file the last run kept.
methods.returns: a text; empty when the last run kept no file (a run that printed the text, or none)

methods.name: OpenViewer
methods.brief: Opens a file in the program the system associates with it, and does nothing when the environment variable STZ_NO_VIEW is set.

parameters.name: pcFile
parameters.role: the path of the file to open

warnings: opens a window on the screen

methods.name: BuildArgs
methods.brief: Builds the list of command-line options for the im2ansi tool from the settings, one text per argument.
methods.returns: a list of texts: the image path, then the options in the order -f -s -w -i --no-color --seed -c -r, each only when its setting asks for it
notes: no quoting is added, since the list reaches the tool one argument at a time

classes.name: stzIncident
classes.brief: Holds an investigator's case file: a fired detection correlated into a wall-ordered story, with a response status that only moves forward.
classes.description: Build it from a sentinel's case and the ledger it fired on (StzIncidentFromCase), or from a bare finding. It takes the actor's own events and everything that shares a trace id with them, up to 64, and keeps their descriptors, never values. Give it a security graph and it also answers the attack path and the blast radius of the secrets involved. Status runs open, contained, closed and never back: a reopened incident is a new incident. ToOcsfFindingJson exports it as an OCSF security finding.
classes.example:
o1.FromFinding([ :where = "guess/billing-agent", :rule = "guess", :severity = "error", :message = "a guess" ], StzSecurityLedger(16))
o1.Contain("session revoked")
? o1.Actor()
#--> billing-agent
? o1.Status()
#--> contained

methods.name: init
methods.brief: Builds an empty case file with the given identifier, status open and the opening time set to now.

parameters.name: pcId
parameters.role: the incident's identifier, such as INC-1

methods.name: FromCase
methods.brief: Fills the incident from a sentinel case and the ledger it fired on, and correlates the story of the case's actor.

parameters.name: paCase
parameters.role: a sentinel case, a hash-list with rule, where, severity, message, headDigest, at and recent (from a sentinel's LastCase)

parameters.name: poLedger
parameters.role: the stzSecurityLedger the case fired on

methods.returns: the incident itself, so calls chain
notes: the actor is the text after the first slash of the case's where; with no actor the case's recent events are the seed; the story is bounded at 64 events, oldest dropped

methods.name: FromFinding
methods.brief: Fills the incident from a bare finding judged outside a sentinel, taking a snapshot of the ledger at this moment.

parameters.name: paFinding
parameters.role: a hash-list with where, rule, severity and message

parameters.name: poLedger
parameters.role: the stzSecurityLedger to correlate against

methods.returns: the incident itself, so calls chain
notes: the opening time is now, not the time of the finding

methods.name: WithGraph
methods.brief: Gives the incident a security graph so that it can answer the attack path and the blast radius.

parameters.name: poSecurityGraph
parameters.role: the stzSecurityGraph that knows the actors, tools, capabilities and secrets

methods.returns: the incident itself, so calls chain
notes: the graph is read, never changed

methods.name: Id
methods.brief: Returns the identifier the incident was built with.

methods.name: Rule
methods.brief: Returns the name of the detection rule that fired.
methods.returns: a text, empty before the incident is filled

methods.name: Where
methods.brief: Returns the place the detection pointed at, such as rule/actor.
methods.returns: a text, empty before the incident is filled

methods.name: Severity
methods.brief: Returns how serious the firing was, such as error or warning.

methods.name: Message
methods.brief: Returns the sentence the detection gave to explain what it saw.
methods.returns: a text, empty before the incident is filled

methods.name: Actor
methods.brief: Returns the single actor the story is about, taken from the text after the first slash of the where.
methods.returns: a text; empty when the where names no actor

methods.name: OpenedAt
methods.brief: Returns the moment the incident opened, in epoch milliseconds.

methods.name: HeadDigest
methods.brief: Returns the ledger's chain head as it stood when the detection fired, to compare with the ledger's later head.

methods.name: Events
methods.brief: Returns the correlated story as the ledger's event records, in wall-clock order.
methods.returns: a list of event records, at most 64

methods.name: NumberOfEvents
methods.brief: Returns how many events the correlated story holds.

methods.name: Timeline
methods.brief: Returns the story as plain rows, oldest first.
methods.returns: a list of [ atWall, kind, actor, subject, reason ] rows
notes: wall time is only as good as the clocks across processes

methods.name: Actors
methods.brief: Returns the distinct actors that appear in the story, in order of first appearance.

methods.name: Subjects
methods.brief: Returns the distinct subjects that the story touched, in order of first appearance.

methods.name: Kinds
methods.brief: Returns the distinct kinds of event that the story holds, in order of first appearance.

methods.name: TraceIds
methods.brief: Returns the distinct trace ids that the story touched, to hand to stzLog.OfTrace.
methods.returns: a list of text; empty when no event carried a trace

methods.name: SecretsInvolved
methods.brief: Returns the names of the secrets that appear among the story's subjects, with the secret: prefix removed.
methods.returns: a list of text (descriptors, never values)

methods.name: AttackPath
methods.brief: Returns the route by which the actor could reach an effectful capability, as the graph sees it.
methods.returns: a list of node names from the actor to the capability; [ ] with no graph, no actor or no route

methods.name: ReachesEffectful
methods.brief: TRUE if the graph says that the actor can reach an effectful capability.
methods.returns: TRUE or FALSE; FALSE with no graph or no actor

methods.name: BlastRadius
methods.brief: Returns, for each secret in the story, the graph nodes that the secret exposes.
methods.returns: a list of [ secret, [ nodes ] ] rows; [ ] with no graph

methods.name: Status
methods.brief: Returns where the response stands: open, contained or closed.

methods.name: IsOpen
methods.brief: TRUE if no response step has been taken yet.

methods.name: IsClosed
methods.brief: TRUE if the incident has been closed.

methods.name: Contain
methods.brief: Moves an open incident to contained and records the note with the time.

parameters.name: pcNote
parameters.role: what was done to contain it

methods.returns: the incident itself, so calls chain
notes: status moves forward only; a reopened incident is a new incident

classes.name: stzIntSeq
classes.brief: Wraps a sequence of integers held in the engine, so sums, extremes and counts are computed there without building a Ring list.
classes.description: Obtain one from stzCounter.CountingQ. The sequence stays in the engine: Sum, Min, Max, At and CountValue read it directly, and ToList copies it out when a Ring list is needed. Positions count from 1. The object owns the engine sequence and Release frees it; Disown hands the ownership away.

methods.name: init
methods.brief: Wraps an engine integer sequence that already exists, taking ownership of it so Release can free it.

parameters.name: pHandle
parameters.role: the engine handle of the integer sequence, as produced by an engine call such as the one behind CountingQ

methods.name: Handle
methods.brief: Returns the engine handle of the sequence, a number that identifies it in the engine.
methods.returns: a number; an empty text once released

methods.name: Release
methods.brief: Frees the engine sequence, unless the object was told to disown it, and empties the handle.
notes: a disowned object keeps the engine sequence alive, so it stays readable and is never freed by this object
warnings: after Release the sequence reads as empty

methods.name: Disown
methods.brief: Tells the object that it no longer owns the engine sequence, so Release will not free it.

methods.name: NumberOfItems
methods.brief: Returns how many numbers the sequence holds.

methods.name: At
methods.brief: Returns the number at a position, counted from 1; 0 when the position is below 1, beyond the end or not a number.

parameters.name: n
parameters.role: the position of the item, starting at 1

warnings: 0 is also a real value of a cycle, so At(5) of a short sequence cannot be told from a stored 0

methods.name: First
methods.brief: Returns the first number of the sequence.

methods.name: Last
methods.brief: Returns the last number of the sequence.

methods.name: Sum
methods.brief: Returns the total of all the numbers, computed in the engine.

methods.name: Min
methods.brief: Returns the smallest number of the sequence.

methods.name: Max
methods.brief: Returns the largest number of the sequence.

methods.name: CountValue
methods.brief: Returns how many times a number occurs in the sequence; 0 when it is not a number.

parameters.name: n
parameters.role: the value to count

methods.name: ToList

classes.name: stzISO27001RuleBase
classes.brief: Holds the ISO 27001 compliance rules for an org chart, ready to pass to CheckCompliance.
classes.description: Holds the four universal org rules and no rule of its own yet: only the name tells it from the other regimes.
classes.example:
? o1.NumberOfRules()
#--> 4

methods.name: init
methods.brief: Builds the ISO 27001 rule base: the four universal org rules under the name ISO 27001; it adds no rule of its own.
methods.returns: nothing; the rule base is built
warnings: only the name tells the regimes apart today

classes.name: stzItem
classes.brief: Meant to follow an item inside a text; today only its accessors work, because its list methods need a list.
classes.description: It is the text twin of stzItemCS: both the item and the text it belongs to must be texts (new stzItem("an", "banana") or StzItemQ("an", "banana")), and the case flag is fixed at 1. It inherits every method of stzItemCS, but those methods build a stzList from the stored text and so raise the error paList must be a list; only Item, List and CaseSensitive answer. The named form [ :In = text ] is rejected. For an item in a text use stzString.Find; for an item in a list use stzItemCS.
classes.example:
? o1.Item()
#--> an
? o1.List()
#--> banana
? o1.CaseSensitive()
#--> 1

methods.name: init
methods.brief: Builds an item-in-a-text object from two texts, the item and the text it belongs to; it works for Item, List and CaseSensitive only.

parameters.name: pItem
parameters.role: the item, which must be a text

parameters.name: paList
parameters.role: the text the item is looked for in, which must be a text too

notes: use stzString.Find for an item in a text, or stzItemCS for an item in a list
warnings: the object keeps the text as its list, and every method that needs a list (Positions, NumberOfOccurrence, FirstPosition, IsLowercased...) raises an error "paList must be a list"; the named form [ :In = text ] is rejected as not being a text; the case flag is fixed at 1

classes.name: stzItemCS
classes.brief: Follows one item inside a list: where it occurs, how often, its neighbours, and the list with it changed.
classes.description: Build one with TheItemInQ(item, list), ItemInCSQ(item, list, flag), StzItemCSQ(item, list, flag) or new stzItemCS(item, list, flag): the three arguments are the item, the list it is looked for in, and a case flag. Reads: Item, List, Positions, Sections, NumberOfOccurrence, NthPosition, FirstPosition, LastPosition, OccurrencesXT, IsBoundedBy, IsBetween, IsLowercased and IsUppercased (for a text item present in the list), and NumberOfItems (for an item that is itself a list). Positions count from 1 and an absent item gives 0 or an empty list. The case flag you give is read by the plain methods (1 compares with case, 0 ignores it) and the CS forms take their own flag, which wins. The Ed forms (ReplacedWith, Removed, Uppercased, Lowercased, BoundedBy, and the InsertedBefore and InsertedAfter family) return a COPY of the list and leave the object and the list you gave unchanged. The named form [ :In = list ] is not unpacked by new stzItemCS, only by the ItemInCSQ family. Text items of any script are compared as whole characters.
classes.example:
? @@( o1.Positions() )
#--> [ 1, 5 ]
? o1.NumberOfOccurrence()
#--> 2
? @@( o1.PositionsCS(0) )
#--> [ 1, 3, 5 ]
? o1.NthPosition(2)
#--> 5
? @@( o1.Removed() )
#--> [ "b", "A", "c", "b", "b" ]
? @@( o1.InsertedBefore("X") )
#--> [ "X", "a", "b", "A", "c", "X", "a", "b", "b" ]
o2 = new stzItemCS("שלום", [ "שלום", "عالم", "😀", "שלום" ], 1)
? @@( o2.Positions() )
#--> [ 1, 4 ]
o3 = new stzItemCS("😀", [ "😀", "عالم", "😀" ], 1)
? o3.LastPosition()
#--> 3

methods.name: init
methods.brief: Builds an item-in-a-list object from an item, the list it belongs to and a case flag.

parameters.name: pItem
parameters.role: the item to follow, of any type

parameters.name: paList
parameters.role: the list the item is looked for in (the named form :In = list is accepted but not unpacked, see the warning)

parameters.name: pCaseSensitive
parameters.role: 1 or 0, stored, read by the plain methods and readable with CaseSensitive

notes: built by TheItemInQ(item, list), ItemInCSQ(item, list, flag), StzItemCSQ(item, list, flag) or new stzItemCS(item, list, flag); TheItemInQ stores the text casesensitive as its flag, which means with case; any flag other than 0, or a text such as caseinsensitive, is read as with case
warnings: the named form [ :In = list ] given to new stzItemCS is not unpacked, the list stays [ [ "in", list ] ] and nothing is found in it; a paList that is not a list raises an error; the call needs all three arguments

methods.name: Item
methods.brief: Returns the item being followed.
methods.returns: the item as given, of any type
notes: Content and Value are the same call; ItemQ returns it as a Softanza object

extensions.name: ItemQ
extensions.adds: does what the method does, then returns the object, so the call can be chained

methods.name: Value
methods.brief: Returns the item being followed.
methods.returns: the item as given, of any type
notes: the same call as Item

methods.name: List
methods.brief: Returns the list the item is looked for in.
notes: ListQ returns it as a stzList

extensions.name: ListQ
extensions.adds: does what the method does, then returns the object, so the call can be chained

methods.name: CaseSensitive
methods.brief: Returns the case flag given when the object was built.
notes: the plain methods read it (1 compares with case, 0 ignores it); the CS forms take their own flag instead

methods.name: NumberOfItems
methods.brief: Returns how many items the followed item contains when it is itself a list.
notes: Size, CountItems and HowManyItems are the same call
warnings: an item that is a text or a number raises error R14, because the text and number objects have no method of that name; only a list item works: [ 1, 2 ] answers 2

methods.name: NumberOfOccurrence
methods.brief: Returns how many times the item occurs in the list, with the case rule given to init.
methods.returns: a number; 0 when the item is absent
notes: in a, b, A, c, a the item a gives 2; NumberOfOccurrenceCS(0) gives 3; NumberOfOccurrences and HowManyOccurrence are the same call

extensions.name: NumberOfOccurrenceCS
extensions.adds: takes a case-sensitivity flag

extensions.name: NumberOfOccurrencesCS
extensions.adds: takes a case-sensitivity flag

extensions.name: HowManyOccurrenceCS
extensions.adds: takes a case-sensitivity flag

methods.name: Positions
methods.brief: Returns the positions of the item in the list, with the case rule given to init.
methods.returns: a list of numbers, positions counted from 1; empty when absent
notes: in a, b, A, c, a the item a gives [ 1, 5 ] and PositionsCS(0) gives [ 1, 3, 5 ]; built with the flag 0, Positions gives [ 1, 3, 5 ] too; Occurrences is the same call

extensions.name: PositionsCS
extensions.adds: takes a case-sensitivity flag

extensions.name: OccurrencesCSXT
extensions.adds: takes a case-sensitivity flag; the extended form: more parameters than the base method

extensions.name: OccurrencesCSQ
extensions.adds: takes a case-sensitivity flag; does what the method does, then returns the object, so the call can be chained

extensions.name: OccurrencesXT
extensions.adds: the extended form: more parameters than the base method

extensions.name: OccurrencesXTQ
extensions.adds: the extended form: more parameters than the base method; does what the method does, then returns the object, so the call can be chained

methods.name: Sections
methods.brief: Returns the runs of consecutive positions of the item as [ start, end ] pairs.
methods.returns: a list of [ number, number ] pairs; an item alone gives [ n, n ]; [ ] when absent
notes: in x, a, a, a, y, a the item a gives [ [ 2, 4 ], [ 6, 6 ] ] where Positions gives [ 2, 3, 4, 6 ]; it is the opposite of stzList.AntiFindAsSections; the case rule is the one given to init, and PositionsAsSections is the same call

extensions.name: SectionsCS
extensions.adds: takes a case-sensitivity flag

extensions.name: PositionsAsSectionsCS
extensions.adds: takes a case-sensitivity flag

methods.name: NthPosition
methods.brief: Returns the position of the nth occurrence of the item, counting occurrences from 1.

parameters.name: _n_
parameters.role: which occurrence, from 1

methods.returns: a number; 0 when there is no nth occurrence, and for n = 0
notes: in a, b, A, c, a the item a gives 1 for n = 1, 5 for n = 2 and 0 for n = 3; the CS form takes the case flag, and the plain form reads the one given to init

extensions.name: NthPositionCS
extensions.adds: takes a case-sensitivity flag

methods.name: FirstPosition
methods.brief: Returns the position of the first occurrence of the item in the list.
methods.returns: a number; 0 when the item is absent
notes: the FirstPositionCS form takes the case flag, and the plain form reads the one given to init

extensions.name: FirstPositionCS
extensions.adds: takes a case-sensitivity flag

methods.name: LastPosition
methods.brief: Returns the position of the last occurrence of the item in the list.
methods.returns: a number; 0 when the item is absent
notes: the LastPositionCS form takes the case flag, and the plain form reads the one given to init

extensions.name: LastPositionCS
extensions.adds: takes a case-sensitivity flag

methods.name: IsBoundedBy
methods.brief: Tells whether an occurrence of the item sits right between the two items of a pair.

parameters.name: paBounds
parameters.role: the pair, [ item before, item after ], each right next to the occurrence

notes: in <, a, >, x, a, y the item a is bounded by [ <, > ] and by [ x, y ] but not by [ <, y ]; an item at the start or the end of the list has only one neighbour and so is bounded by nothing; the case rule is the one given to init, and IsBoundedByCS takes its own flag
warnings: a paBounds that is not a list of two items raises an error

extensions.name: IsBoundedByCS
extensions.adds: takes a case-sensitivity flag

methods.name: IsBetween
methods.brief: Tells whether an occurrence of the item lies after one given item and before another.

parameters.name: pBound1
parameters.role: the item that must come earlier in the list

parameters.name: pBound2
parameters.role: the item that must come later in the list

notes: the bounds need not touch the item: in <, a, x, y the item a is between < and y, where IsBoundedBy needs them right next to it; the case rule is the one given to init, and IsBetweenCS takes its own flag

extensions.name: IsBetweenCS
extensions.adds: takes a case-sensitivity flag

methods.name: BoundedBy
methods.brief: Returns a copy of the list with a pair of bounding items put around each occurrence of the item.

parameters.name: paBounds
parameters.role: the pair, [ item before, item after ]

methods.returns: a list, longer by two items per occurrence; the object and its list are unchanged
notes: in a, b, c, b the item b with [ [, ] ] gives a, [, b, ], c, [, b, ]; the case rule is the one given to init, and BoundedByCS takes its own flag; it is the opposite of stzString.BoundedBy, which finds what stands between bounds
warnings: a paBounds that is not a list of two items raises an error

extensions.name: BoundedByCS
extensions.adds: takes a case-sensitivity flag

methods.name: ReplacedWith
methods.brief: Returns a copy of the list with every occurrence of the item replaced by another item.

parameters.name: pcOtherItem
parameters.role: the item that takes its place, of any type

methods.returns: a list; the object and its list are unchanged
notes: in a, b, A, c, a the item a replaced by Z gives Z, b, A, c, Z; the case rule is the one given to init, and ReplacedWithCS takes its own flag; Replaced and ReplacedBy are the same call; an absent item gives a copy of the list

extensions.name: ReplacedWithCS
extensions.adds: takes a case-sensitivity flag

extensions.name: ReplacedCS
extensions.adds: takes a case-sensitivity flag

extensions.name: ReplacedByCS
extensions.adds: takes a case-sensitivity flag

methods.name: Removed
methods.brief: Returns a copy of the list without any occurrence of the item.
methods.returns: a list; the object and its list are unchanged
notes: in a, b, A, c, a the item a gives b, A, c; the case rule is the one given to init, and RemovedCS takes its own flag; an absent item gives a copy of the list

extensions.name: RemovedCS
extensions.adds: takes a case-sensitivity flag

methods.name: IsLowercased
methods.brief: TRUE if the item is a lower-case text and the list contains it.
notes: IsInLowercase is the same call; an item absent from the list gives FALSE; a Hebrew word is not cased, so it gives FALSE here and in IsUppercased
warnings: a number or a list as the item raises error R14, because only a text can be asked

methods.name: IsUppercased
methods.brief: TRUE if the item is an upper-case text and the list contains it.
notes: IsInUppercase is the same call; an item absent from the list gives FALSE
warnings: a number or a list as the item raises error R14, because only a text can be asked

methods.name: Uppercased
methods.brief: Returns a copy of the list with each occurrence of the item written in upper case.
methods.returns: a list; the object and its list are unchanged
notes: in ab, Ab, AB, ab the item ab gives AB, Ab, AB, AB; only the occurrences change, not the other items; an item that is not a text, and a text with no case such as Hebrew, give a copy of the list; the case rule is the one given to init, and UppercasedCS takes its own flag

extensions.name: UppercasedCS
extensions.adds: takes a case-sensitivity flag

methods.name: Lowercased
methods.brief: Returns a copy of the list with each occurrence of the item written in lower case.
methods.returns: a list; the object and its list are unchanged
notes: in ab, Ab, AB, ab the item Ab gives ab, ab, AB, ab; only the occurrences change, not the other items; an item that is not a text gives a copy of the list; the case rule is the one given to init, and LowercasedCS takes its own flag

extensions.name: LowercasedCS
extensions.adds: takes a case-sensitivity flag

methods.name: InsertedBefore
methods.brief: Returns a copy of the list with a new item put right before each occurrence of the item.

parameters.name: p
parameters.role: the item to insert, of any type; a list goes in as one item

methods.returns: a list, longer by one item per occurrence; the object and its list are unchanged
notes: in a, b, a, c the item a with X gives X, a, b, X, a, c; the case rule is the one given to init, and InsertedBeforeCS takes its own flag; InsertedBAt is the same call

classes.name: stzJsCodeGraph
classes.brief: Holds JavaScript source as a code graph, parsed by the tree-sitter grammar in the engine with no Node runtime.
classes.description: A sibling of stzPyCodeGraph under stzCodeGraph: it inherits the whole query surface (classes, methods, owners, ancestry, call edges, dead code, cyclic calls) and declares only its own identity. Build one from a source string with StzJsCodeGraphFromSourceTS or from a directory of .js files with StzJsCodeGraphTS.
classes.receiver: o1 = StzJsCodeGraphFromSourceTS("class Worker { run() { this.step(); } step() {} }")
classes.example:
? o1.Language()
#--> javascript
? o1.FileExtension()
#--> .js
? @@( o1.Classes() )
#--> [ "Worker" ]
? @@( o1.MethodsOf("Worker") )
#--> [ "run", "step" ]

methods.name: Language
methods.brief: Returns the name of the language this graph models.

methods.name: FileExtension
methods.brief: Returns the file extension of the source files it scans, with the dot.

classes.name: stzJson
classes.brief: Holds a JSON document as a Ring list, as an object of keys or an array of items, and records its mistakes instead of raising them.
classes.description: Built from a JSON text or from a Ring list. An object is read and changed by key (HasKey, Value, SetValue, RemoveKey, TakeKey) and an array by position (At, Add, Insert, RemoveAt, TakeAt ...). A call that does not fit the kind of JSON held, or an index outside the array, leaves the object unchanged and records a message in LastError.
classes.example:
? o1.Value("name")
#--> John
? o1.ToString()
#--> {"name":"John","age":30}

methods.name: init
methods.brief: Builds the object from a JSON text or from a Ring list; an empty or invalid text leaves it empty and records an error.

parameters.name: p
parameters.role: a JSON text, or a Ring list (a list of [ key, value ] pairs gives an object, any other list gives an array)

notes: a text that is not valid JSON never raises: read LastError; an argument that is neither text nor list builds an empty object with no error

methods.name: IsArray
methods.brief: TRUE if the JSON held is an array, FALSE if it is an object.
notes: a list given to the constructor counts as an array unless it is a list of [ key, value ] pairs

methods.name: IsEmpty
methods.brief: TRUE if the object holds no key and no item, as after Clear or after a text that failed to parse.
notes: an empty object and an empty array are both empty

methods.name: IsNull
methods.brief: TRUE if the object is empty and an error has been recorded, as after a text that is not valid JSON.
notes: an empty object built from a valid text is not null

methods.name: Size
methods.brief: Returns how many keys the object holds, or how many items the array holds.
notes: Count gives the same answer

methods.name: ToString
methods.brief: Returns the content as JSON text on one line, without spaces after the colons and commas.
notes: an empty object writes as {} and an empty array as []; true and false held as 1 and 0 come out as numbers; ToStringXT gives the indented form

extensions.name: ToStringXT
extensions.adds: the extended form: more parameters than the base method

methods.name: HasKey
methods.brief: TRUE if the object has the key; on an array it answers FALSE and records an error.

parameters.name: cKey
parameters.role: the key to look for, as text

notes: the answer is FALSE and LastError reads "Cannot check key on array" when the JSON is an array

methods.name: Keys
methods.brief: Returns the keys of the object, in the order they have in the JSON text.
methods.returns: a list of text; [ ] for an array, with an error recorded

methods.name: Value
methods.brief: Returns the value stored under the key, or an empty text when the key is absent.

parameters.name: cKey
parameters.role: the key to read, as text

methods.returns: the value: a text, a number, or a list of [ key, value ] pairs for a nested object
notes: true and false in the JSON come back as 1 and 0; an absent key records no error; an array answers an empty text and records an error

methods.name: SetValue
methods.brief: Sets the key to the value, replacing the old value or adding the key at the end; returns the object itself.

parameters.name: cKey
parameters.role: the key to set, as text

parameters.name: value
parameters.role: the value to store: a text, a number or a list

methods.returns: the stzJson itself, so calls chain
notes: on an array nothing changes and LastError reads "Cannot set value by key on array"

methods.name: RemoveKey
methods.brief: Removes the key and its value from the object, in place; returns the object itself.

parameters.name: cKey
parameters.role: the key to remove, as text

methods.returns: the stzJson itself, so calls chain
notes: an absent key changes nothing and records no error; an array records an error and changes nothing

methods.name: TakeKey
methods.brief: Removes the key from the object, in place, and returns the value it held.

parameters.name: cKey
parameters.role: the key to take, as text

methods.returns: the value that was stored; an empty text when the key is absent
notes: an array answers an empty text and records an error

methods.name: At
methods.brief: Returns the item at position nIndex of the array, 1 being the first.

parameters.name: nIndex
parameters.role: the position of the item, from 1

methods.returns: the item; an empty text when nIndex is outside the array, with an error recorded
notes: an object answers an empty text and records the error "Cannot get index from object"

methods.name: First
methods.brief: Returns the first item of the array.
methods.returns: the item; an empty text for an empty array, with an error recorded
notes: an object answers an empty text and records an error

methods.name: Last
methods.brief: Returns the last item of the array.
methods.returns: the item; an empty text for an empty array, with an error recorded
notes: an object answers an empty text and records an error

methods.name: Add
methods.brief: Appends the value after the last item of the array, in place; returns the object itself.

parameters.name: value
parameters.role: the item to append

methods.returns: the stzJson itself, so calls chain
notes: on an object nothing changes and LastError reads "Cannot add to object"

methods.name: Prepend
methods.brief: Puts the value before the first item of the array, in place; returns the object itself.

parameters.name: value
parameters.role: the item to put first

methods.returns: the stzJson itself, so calls chain
notes: on an object nothing changes and an error is recorded

methods.name: Insert
methods.brief: Inserts the value at position nIndex of the array, in place, pushing the later items one place on; returns the object itself.

parameters.name: nIndex
parameters.role: the position the new item takes, from 1 to one past the last

parameters.name: value
parameters.role: the item to insert

methods.returns: the stzJson itself, so calls chain
notes: a position outside that range changes nothing and records "Index out of range"; an object records an error

methods.name: RemoveAt
methods.brief: Removes the item at position nIndex of the array, in place; returns the object itself.

parameters.name: nIndex
parameters.role: the position of the item to remove, from 1

methods.returns: the stzJson itself, so calls chain
notes: a position outside the array changes nothing and records "Index out of range"

methods.name: RemoveFirst
methods.brief: Removes the first item of the array, in place; returns the object itself.
methods.returns: the stzJson itself, so calls chain
notes: an empty array records the error "Array is empty"

methods.name: RemoveLast
methods.brief: Removes the last item of the array, in place; returns the object itself.
methods.returns: the stzJson itself, so calls chain
notes: an empty array records the error "Array is empty"

methods.name: TakeAt
methods.brief: Removes the item at position nIndex of the array, in place, and returns it.

parameters.name: nIndex
parameters.role: the position of the item to take, from 1

methods.returns: the item that was removed; an empty text when nIndex is outside the array
notes: a position outside the array records "Index out of range"

methods.name: Contains
methods.brief: TRUE if some item of the array equals the value.

parameters.name: value
parameters.role: the item to look for

notes: the comparison is Ring's loose equality, so 30 and "30" match; an object answers FALSE and records an error

methods.name: Replace
methods.brief: Puts the value in place of the item at position nIndex of the array, in place; returns the object itself.

parameters.name: nIndex
parameters.role: the position of the item to replace, from 1

parameters.name: value
parameters.role: the new item

methods.returns: the stzJson itself, so calls chain
notes: a position outside the array changes nothing and records "Index out of range"

methods.name: ToList
methods.brief: Returns the content as a Ring list: [ key, value ] pairs for an object, the items for an array.
notes: it is the held list itself, so it reads what the other methods changed

methods.name: Copy
methods.brief: Returns a new stzJson built from the text of this one, so changing the copy leaves the original alone.
notes: the recorded error is not copied

methods.name: Clear
methods.brief: Removes every key or item, in place; returns the object itself.
methods.returns: the stzJson itself, so calls chain
notes: the object stays an array or an object; an emptied object writes as {}; the recorded error is kept

methods.name: IsValid
methods.brief: TRUE if no error has been recorded since the object was built or since the last ClearError.
notes: misusing a method, for example At on an object, makes it FALSE

methods.name: LastError
methods.brief: Returns the message of the last error recorded, or an empty text when there is none.
notes: errors are recorded, never raised: a failed call returns an empty text or leaves the object unchanged

methods.name: HasError
methods.brief: TRUE if an error has been recorded and not cleared.
notes: it is the opposite of IsValid

methods.name: ClearError
methods.brief: Forgets the recorded error, in place; returns the object itself.
methods.returns: the stzJson itself, so calls chain

methods.name: FromString
methods.brief: Returns a new stzJson built from the JSON text; the receiver is not changed.

parameters.name: cJson
parameters.role: the JSON text to parse

notes: an invalid text gives an empty object with LastError set

methods.name: FromList
methods.brief: Returns a new stzJson built from the Ring list; the receiver is not changed.

parameters.name: aList
parameters.role: the Ring list to hold, as [ key, value ] pairs or as items

methods.name: EmptyObject
methods.brief: Returns a new stzJson holding an empty object.
notes: it writes as {} and IsArray answers FALSE

methods.name: EmptyArray
methods.brief: Returns a new stzJson holding an empty array.
notes: it writes as [] and IsArray answers TRUE

methods.name: Show

methods.name: Print

classes.name: stzJuliaCode
classes.brief: Runs a snippet of Julia from Ring and brings its answer back as a Ring value, through a result file.
classes.description: You set the code, which must assign its answer to a variable named res; Execute wraps it with a translator, runs it with the language's program in the current folder and writes the answer as Ring text, and Result reads that text back, so numbers, texts and nested lists cross the boundary. The files temp.<ext>, a run script, the result file and log.txt are written in the current folder. It is a thin face over stzExterCode, which has the full set of controls (runtime path, result variable, log file). The Julia program is the one configured in $aStzLibConfig[:JuliaPath], d:/julia/julia-1.11.7/bin/julia.exe by default. It was absent on the machine of this documentation run, so only the failure path was seen: Execute raised the not-created error.

methods.name: SetCode
methods.brief: Stores the Julia source text to run; nothing is written to disk until Execute.

parameters.name: pcJuliaCode
parameters.role: the Julia program text, which must assign its answer to a variable named res

methods.brief: Stores the Julia source text to run, as the call with the longer name does.

parameters.name: pcJuliaCode
parameters.role: the Julia program text, which must assign its answer to a variable named res

methods.name: Execute
methods.brief: Writes the source behind a translator, runs it with the Julia program and saves the answer for Result.
methods.returns: nothing; the answer is kept in a result file
notes: not run to completion: the Julia program is absent here, so only the failure path was seen
warnings: it runs real code with a real program and writes temp.jl, runjulia.bat and log.txt in the current folder; the Julia program configured by default is not installed on the machine of this run, so Execute raised the not-created error with a path-not-found log

methods.name: Run
methods.brief: Writes the source behind a translator and runs it with the Julia program, as the call with the other name does.
methods.returns: nothing; the answer is kept in a result file
warnings: same warning as Execute: it runs real code with a real program in the current folder

methods.name: Exec
methods.brief: Writes the source behind a translator and runs it with the Julia program, as the call with the other name does.
methods.returns: nothing; the answer is kept in a result file
warnings: same warning as Execute: it runs real code with a real program in the current folder

methods.name: Result
methods.brief: Reads the answer the Julia code saved and turns it into a Ring value: a number, a text or nested lists.
notes: not run: needs a successful Execute
warnings: evaluates the text of the result file as Ring code, so run only code you trust; reads the result file of the last run, which does not exist here because the run failed, so it raises an error that quotes the log

methods.name: Code
methods.brief: Returns the source text that was set, or, when none is set, the source file left on disk by an earlier run.
warnings: it returns your own code, not the wrapped source that is written to disk

methods.name: Duration
methods.brief: Returns how long the last run took, in seconds; 0 before any run.

methods.name: Log
methods.brief: Returns what the Julia program printed during the last run, errors included.
methods.returns: a text; empty when there is no log file
warnings: on a new object it can return the log of an earlier run left in the current folder

methods.name: Trace
methods.brief: Returns the history of runs of this object, oldest first, each a hashlist of language, timestamp, duration, log, exitcode and mode.
warnings: the exit code is always recorded as 0, even for a run that failed

classes.name: stzJwt
classes.brief: Reads one JSON Web Token: its header, its claims and its signature, and checks the signature against a public key.
classes.description: Use it on its own for any signed token with three parts. Reading a claim proves nothing: the token is only data until SignatureIsValidWith has passed against a key you hold, and a token meant for you must also carry your audience and an unexpired exp, which stzOidcClient checks. A malformed token is accepted at construction and simply reads as empty.
classes.example:
? o1.IsWellFormed()
#--> 1
? o1.Algorithm()
#--> ES256
? o1.Subject()
#--> alice
? o1.ClaimInt("exp")
#--> 1800003600
? o1.Audience()
#--> client-demo
? o1.SignatureIsValidWith([ [ "kty", "EC" ], [ "x", "t006lKtxiQpobDOpWwzGDVKazORGwZWNLbK206XQuHc" ], [ "y", "KGMvZoXXlU8YdR3KS-6Q6A8bqVqlwpoZy0Udq9TPUy4" ] ])
#--> 1

methods.name: init
methods.brief: Wraps one JSON Web Token given as text and cuts it at its dots into header, payload and signature.

parameters.name: pcToken
parameters.role: the token, three base64url parts joined by dots

warnings: nothing is checked at construction: a malformed token is accepted and reads as empty

methods.name: Token
methods.brief: Returns the token text this object wraps, trimmed.

methods.name: IsWellFormed
methods.brief: TRUE if the token has exactly three dot-separated parts and the first two are not empty.
notes: it checks the shape only, not that the parts decode

methods.name: SigningInput
methods.brief: Returns the text the signature covers, the header part and the payload part joined by a dot.
methods.returns: a text; the empty text when the token is not well formed

methods.name: SignatureB64
methods.brief: Returns the third part, the signature, still base64url encoded.
methods.returns: a text; the empty text when the token has fewer than three parts

methods.name: Header
methods.brief: Returns the decoded header of the token, normally a JSON text such as {"alg":"ES256","typ":"JWT","kid":"..."}.
methods.returns: a text; the empty text when there is no first part
notes: the part is decoded whatever it holds, so a part that is not base64url gives bytes that are not JSON

methods.name: Payload
methods.brief: Returns the decoded payload of the token, normally the JSON text of its claims.
methods.returns: a text; the empty text when there is no second part
notes: the claims are only data until SignatureIsValidWith has passed against a key you hold

methods.name: Algorithm
methods.brief: Returns the algorithm the header declares, such as ES256.
methods.returns: a text; the empty text when the header is missing or not JSON
notes: for information only: verify with the algorithm of the key you hold, never with this one

methods.name: KeyId
methods.brief: Returns the kid the header names, the key that signed the token.
methods.returns: a text; the empty text when there is none

methods.name: Claim
methods.brief: Returns the value of a claim of the payload as text.

parameters.name: pcName
parameters.role: the claim name, such as "sub" or "email"

methods.returns: a text; the empty text when the claim is absent or the payload is not JSON

methods.name: ClaimInt
methods.brief: Returns the value of a numeric claim of the payload, such as exp.

parameters.name: pcName
parameters.role: the claim name, such as "exp"

methods.returns: a number; 0 when the claim is absent or the payload is not JSON

methods.name: HasClaim
methods.brief: TRUE if the payload carries a claim of that name.

parameters.name: pcName
parameters.role: the claim name to look for

methods.returns: TRUE or FALSE; FALSE when the payload is not JSON

methods.name: Subject
methods.brief: Returns the sub claim, the identity the token is about.
methods.returns: a text; the empty text when absent

methods.name: Issuer
methods.brief: Returns the iss claim, the party that issued the token.
methods.returns: a text; the empty text when absent

methods.name: Audience
methods.brief: Returns the aud claim, the party the token was issued for.
methods.returns: a text; the empty text when absent

methods.name: SignatureIsValidWith
methods.brief: TRUE if the token's signature verifies against one public key given as a JWK, EC with ES256 or RSA with RS256.

parameters.name: paJwk
parameters.role: the public key as a list of [ name, value ] pairs: [ :kty, :x, :y ] for EC or [ :kty, :n, :e ] for RSA

methods.returns: TRUE or FALSE; FALSE for a malformed token, a foreign key, an unknown key type or a malformed key
notes: the key type picks the algorithm; the alg of the header is ignored
warnings: a TRUE proves only that the key's owner signed the token, not that it is meant for you, nor recent: check iss, aud and exp too, as VerifyIdToken does

methods.name: Show
methods.brief: Prints a one-line summary: the declared algorithm, the subject and the issuer.

classes.name: stzKernelMaker
classes.brief: Describes an elementwise GPU computation with vectors, scalars and one assignment, and has the engine generate and check the WGSL kernel.
classes.description: Declare the inputs with TakesVector, the parameters with TakesScalar, the output with ReturnsVector and the body with ForEachElement, an assignment such as { @C = alpha * @A + @B }. ToWGSL returns the generated kernel verbatim, nothing hidden, and needs no GPU, so kernels can be written and inspected on a machine without one. Anything outside the declared names and the allowed functions refuses at ToWGSL with a message naming it. Limits: up to 5 input vectors, 14 scalars and exactly one output; every value is f32 on the device. Hand the maker to stzGpu to run it.
classes.receiver: o1 = new stzKernelMaker o1.TakesVector(:A) o1.TakesVector(:B) o1.TakesScalar(:alpha) o1.ReturnsVector(:C) o1.ForEachElement("{ @C = alpha * @A + @B }")
classes.example:
? @@( o1.InputNames() )
#--> [ "a", "b" ]
? o1.OutputName()
#--> c
? len(o1.ToWGSL()) > 100
#--> 1

methods.name: init
methods.brief: Creates an empty kernel description, to be filled with the vectors, scalars, output and body of an elementwise computation.

methods.name: TakesVector
methods.brief: Declares an input vector by name; a kernel takes up to 5.

parameters.name: pcName
parameters.role: the vector's name, stored in lower case and used as @Name in the body

methods.returns: the maker itself, so calls chain
warnings: declaring a vector clears the cached kernel text

methods.name: TakesScalar
methods.brief: Declares a scalar parameter by name; a kernel takes up to 14.

parameters.name: pcName
parameters.role: the scalar's name, stored in lower case and used bare in the body

methods.returns: the maker itself, so calls chain
warnings: declaring a scalar clears the cached kernel text

methods.name: ReturnsVector
methods.brief: Declares the single output vector by name.

parameters.name: pcName
parameters.role: the output's name, stored in lower case and assigned as @Name in the body

methods.returns: the maker itself, so calls chain
warnings: a kernel without an output refuses at ToWGSL

methods.name: ForEachElement
methods.brief: Sets the body: one assignment from an expression over the declared vectors, scalars, numbers and a fixed set of functions.

parameters.name: pcW
parameters.role: the body in braces, such as '{ @C = alpha * @A + @B }'

methods.returns: the maker itself, so calls chain
warnings: the expression may call abs, min, max, sqrt, exp, log, sin, cos, tan, floor, ceil, pow, clamp, sign, fract and round; anything else refuses at ToWGSL naming the offender

methods.name: InputNames
methods.brief: Returns the declared input vectors, lower-cased, in the order declared.

methods.name: ScalarNames
methods.brief: Returns the declared scalars, lower-cased, in the order declared.

methods.name: OutputName
methods.brief: Returns the declared output vector, lower-cased; empty when none is declared.

methods.name: Spec
methods.brief: Returns the declarations in the engine's spec format: one in, scalar or out line each, then the body.
warnings: an empty maker gives an empty text

methods.name: ToWGSL
methods.brief: Returns the WGSL compute kernel the engine generates from the declarations, after checking them; needs no GPU.
notes: run: only the text transpiler of the engine, no device was opened
warnings: raises an error with the engine's message for a missing output, an unknown name or a function outside the list; the text is cached until a declaration changes

classes.name: stzKindConstraint
classes.brief: Declares what a kind of value must be, as a list of constraints kept for the whole process.
classes.description: ConstrainQ("score").ToBeQ(:Number).AndQ().ToBeQ(:Positive) declares that a score is a number and positive. A descriptor names a predicate: Number is checked by @isnumber, Positive by @ispositive. The declarations are read by stzCan, for possibility, and stzMust, for necessity. ConstraintsOn lists a kind's descriptors and DropConstraints forgets them.
classes.example:
o1.ToBeQ(:Number).AndQ().ToBeQ(:Positive)
? ConstraintsOn("scoreA")[2]
#--> positive
? o1.Kind()
#--> scorea

methods.name: init
methods.brief: Starts the declaration of constraints for a kind of value, such as score; the kind is trimmed and lowercased.

parameters.name: pcKind
parameters.role: the name of the kind to constrain

methods.name: ToBeQ
methods.brief: Declares that values of the kind must satisfy a descriptor, such as Number or Positive; declaring the same descriptor twice keeps one.

parameters.name: pcDesc
parameters.role: the descriptor, matched to a predicate named @is followed by it

methods.returns: the declaration itself, so calls chain
notes: the constraints of a kind are global to the process, read in the order declared
warnings: an unknown descriptor is not refused here: it raises Unknown constraint descriptor later, when a value is checked against it

methods.name: AndQ
methods.brief: Returns the declaration itself, so that ToBeQ can be chained after it for readability.

methods.name: Kind
methods.brief: Returns the kind this declaration constrains, trimmed and in lower case.

classes.name: stzKMeans
classes.brief: Groups numeric vectors into k clusters by Lloyd's k-means, deterministically, with the whole run done in the engine.
classes.description: Centroids are seeded from the first k distinct points, so two runs agree and nothing is random; shuffle the vectors upstream for randomised restarts. Each iteration assigns every point to its nearest centroid and moves the centroids, stopping when no assignment changes or the iteration limit is reached. An empty cluster keeps its centroid. Because the seeding is fixed, an unlucky order can settle in a poor local minimum, which Inertia shows.

methods.name: init
methods.brief: Builds a clusterer over a list of numeric vectors; the number of clusters defaults to 2.

parameters.name: paVectors
parameters.role: a list of lists of numbers

methods.name: SetK
methods.brief: Sets how many clusters to find.

parameters.name: n
parameters.role: the number of clusters, 1 or more

methods.returns: the clusterer itself, so calls chain
notes: a value below 1 is ignored without a message and the earlier value stays

methods.name: Run
methods.brief: Computes the clusters by Lloyd's k-means, seeding the centroids with the first k distinct points, and stops when no assignment changes.

parameters.name: nMaxIter
parameters.role: the most iterations allowed

methods.returns: the clusterer itself, so calls chain
notes: deterministic: two runs on the same data agree, and a point equidistant from two centroids goes to the lower-numbered one; with a poor seed the result can be a poor local minimum
warnings: raises an error when there are fewer vectors than clusters, when the vectors differ in width, or when there are fewer distinct points than clusters

methods.name: Clusters
methods.brief: Returns the members of each cluster, as positions in the input list.
methods.returns: a list with one list of numbers per cluster; empty lists before Run

methods.name: Centroids
methods.brief: Returns the centre of each cluster.
methods.returns: a list of vectors, one per cluster; empty before Run

methods.name: ClusterOf
methods.brief: Returns the number of the nearest cluster for a new vector, by Euclidean distance to the centroids.

parameters.name: paVector
parameters.role: the vector to place

notes: a vector shorter or longer than the centroids is compared over their common length
warnings: raises an error telling to call Run first

methods.name: Inertia
methods.brief: Returns the total squared distance of the points to their centroids, the quality number of the run.

methods.name: Iterations
methods.brief: Returns how many iterations the last Run took.

methods.name: Why
methods.brief: Returns a sentence saying how the last Run ended, with the iteration count and the inertia.

classes.name: stzKnn
classes.brief: Classifies a point by the majority label of its k nearest training examples, with no training step and a full explanation.
classes.description: The purest explainable classifier: nothing is fitted, and Why lists the neighbours that voted with their distances. The search is exact by default and runs in the engine; the resident index rebuilds when examples have been added through TrainingSetQ. Approximate search is an opt-in switch because the library cannot know how many queries will follow, and because it may change an answer; AgreementWithExact measures the cost on your own queries. Features are compared by Euclidean distance, so scale them first when their units differ.
classes.example:
o1.SetK(3)
? o1.Classify([5.0, 3.4])
#--> setosa
? o1.Classify([6.4, 3.0])
#--> virginica
? o1.Why()
#--> the 3 nearest examples were: #4 'virginica' (d=0.22), #6 'virginica' (d=0.30), #5 'virginica' (d=0.32) -- majority: 'virginica' (3/3)

methods.name: init
methods.brief: Builds a k-nearest-neighbours classifier over a training set; nothing is trained and k starts at 3.

parameters.name: poDataset
parameters.role: a stzTrainingSet

methods.name: TrainingSetQ
methods.brief: Returns the training set the classifier holds, the one to grow if more examples are wanted.
warnings: growing the set you passed to the constructor does not reach the classifier, because it keeps a copy; grow it here, and the next Classify sees it

methods.name: SetK
methods.brief: Sets how many nearest examples vote.

parameters.name: n
parameters.role: the number of neighbours, 1 or more

methods.returns: the classifier itself, so calls chain
notes: a value below 1 is ignored without a message and the earlier k stays

methods.name: SetApproximate
methods.brief: Switches between exact search and an approximate one through a projection forest in the engine.

parameters.name: bFlag
parameters.role: 1 for approximate search, 0 for exact

methods.returns: the classifier itself, so calls chain
notes: off by default: it pays only above a few thousand examples and many queries, and it can change an answer; AgreementWithExact measures that on your queries
warnings: raises an error unless the flag is exactly 1 or 0

methods.name: IsApproximate
methods.brief: TRUE if approximate search is on.
methods.returns: TRUE or FALSE; FALSE by default

methods.name: SetApproximateTrees
methods.brief: Sets how many trees the approximate index uses: more trees give better recall and a larger, slower index.

parameters.name: n
parameters.role: the number of trees, 1 or more

methods.returns: the classifier itself, so calls chain
notes: the default is 24
warnings: raises an error for a number below 1

methods.name: SetApproximateBudget
methods.brief: Sets how many candidates the approximate search examines per query before true distances decide.

parameters.name: n
parameters.role: the candidate count, 0 or more

methods.returns: the classifier itself, so calls chain
notes: it is the recall dial
warnings: raises an error for a negative number

methods.name: ApproximateTrees
methods.brief: Returns the number of trees set for the approximate index.

methods.name: ApproximateBudget
methods.brief: Returns the candidate budget set for the approximate search.
methods.returns: a number; 0 means the engine chooses

methods.name: AgreementWithExact
methods.brief: Returns the share of the given queries on which approximate and exact search give the same label.

parameters.name: paQueries
parameters.role: a non-empty list of feature lists, each as wide as the training examples

notes: the honest measure for a classifier: a vote often survives a swapped neighbour, so the label is compared and not the neighbour list
warnings: raises an error for an empty list or a query of the wrong width, naming it

methods.name: K
methods.brief: Returns how many neighbours vote.

methods.name: Classify
methods.brief: Returns the majority label among the k training examples nearest to a feature list, by Euclidean distance.

parameters.name: paFeatures
parameters.role: the numbers describing the thing to classify, as many as the training examples have

notes: the search runs in the engine and rebuilds when examples were added
warnings: raises an error for an empty training set and for a query of the wrong width; a tie goes to the label that appeared first in the training set

methods.name: Why
methods.brief: Returns the neighbours behind the last answer, each with its number and distance, and the vote.
methods.returns: a text such as the 3 nearest examples were: #3 'setosa' (d=0), ... -- majority: 'setosa' (3/3); empty before the first Classify

classes.name: stzKnowledgeGraph
classes.brief: Holds knowledge as facts, triples of subject, predicate and object, in a graph, with queries, laws, proofs and conversations.
classes.description: A stzKnowledgeGraph is a stzGraph of type semantic: each fact is an edge labelled with its predicate between two entity nodes, so every stzGraph method is also available. Facts are set-like (adding a known fact is a no-op), but only one fact can link a given ordered pair of entities. Laws (:unique, :symmetric, :transitive) are declared per relation with ConstrainRelation, and only :unique and :transitive are acted on here: Admit is the governed door that checks :unique and records a refusal as a named contradiction, and Prove follows :transitive; strict mode makes every fact carry provenance. Prove answers a goal with a replayable proof, and the space can hold stzConversation objects that elicit missing facts. Knowledge is saved and read as .zknw text. A number of methods carry a warning today.
classes.receiver: o1 = new stzKnowledgeGraph("zoo"); o1.AddFact("Dog", "is-a", "Animal"); o1.AddFact("Cat", "is-a", "Animal"); o1.AddFact("Dog", "eats", "Meat")
classes.example:
? @@( o1.Query([ "?x", "is-a", "Animal" ]) )
#--> [ "Dog", "Cat" ]

methods.name: init
methods.brief: Builds an empty knowledge graph of type semantic, with no fact, no law and no conversation; the id is folded to lowercase.

parameters.name: pcId
parameters.role: An identifier, as text.

notes: the id follows the rules of stzGraph: no space, no line break

methods.name: IsKnowledgeGraph
methods.brief: TRUE if the receiver is a knowledge graph, which a stzKnowledgeGraph always is.

methods.name: IsAKnowledgeGraph
methods.brief: TRUE if the receiver is a knowledge graph, spelled with an article; always TRUE here.

methods.name: AddFact
methods.brief: Adds a fact: entity nodes are created for the subject and the object when missing, and an edge labelled with the predicate links them.

parameters.name: pcSubject
parameters.role: The subject of the fact, as text.

parameters.name: pcPredicate
parameters.role: The predicate (the relation) of the fact, as text.

parameters.name: pcObject
parameters.role: The object of the fact, as text.

notes: AddFactXT adds a fact with provenance; AddTriple is another spelling
warnings: stating a known fact again does nothing, but a different predicate between the same two entities raises an error, and strict mode refuses any fact added this way

extensions.name: AddFactQ
extensions.adds: does what the method does, then returns the object, so the call can be chained

extensions.name: AddFactXT

classes.name: stzLanguage
classes.brief: Holds one human language, with its names, its codes, its default country and the scripts it is the default for, from the locale data.
classes.description: The identifier may be a language name (French), a short or long code (fr, fra), or the name of a country, which picks the first language of the data at home in that country, so it is a convenience and not a lookup of every language spoken there. The accessors read the locale tables: the English name in lower case, the native name in its own script, the number, the codes and the default country. The script accessors answer the scripts for which this language is the default language of the data, which is not the same as every script the language is written in. EngineField and EngineFieldByAbbr call functions that do not exist today and raise error R3.
classes.example:
? o1.Name()
#--> hausa
? o1.ShortAbbreviation()
#--> ha
? o1.LongAbbreviation()
#--> hau
? o1.DefaultCountry()
#--> nigeria
? o1.DefaultScript()
#--> boko

classes.name: stzLatencyHistogram
classes.brief: Tallies latency samples in an engine histogram and reads percentiles from it, such as the median and the 99th.
classes.description: Record samples in milliseconds, then ask for P50, P95, P99 or any Percentile. The histogram is bucketed: a percentile is answered as the upper bound of the bucket it falls in, so it is an approximation and never an interpolated value. Count and Sum are exact.

methods.brief: Makes this object read and write an engine histogram owned elsewhere, and frees the one it created itself.

parameters.name: pEngineHandle
parameters.role: the handle of an engine histogram, such as the one Handle returns

methods.brief: Tallies one latency sample, in milliseconds.

classes.name: stzLearner
classes.brief: Holds one learner's folder: the work they submitted and their progress, which only the checker writes, with its evidence.
classes.description: A learner is a folder: work/<exercise>.ring is what they submitted, as they wrote it, and progress.zknw is a plain text file of facts. A pass is recorded only by Submit or SubmitProject, after the checker has run the program, and it counts only while the sha256 of the work file (or of the project folder) still equals the evidence recorded then: a pass typed by hand, or a file changed afterwards, reads as not passed. A level is earned when every exercise of its chapters and its project have passed. The checker runs programs on the desktop with Softanza, never in a browser, and each submission takes seconds. The fr, ar and ha editions of the course are drafts, 0 of 35 units reviewed by a person, and no institution has adopted the system yet.
classes.example:
oC = StzProgramQ("../../education/program").CourseQ("elementary-introduction")
oEx = oC.ExerciseQ("ex-01-01")
? o1.ChapterOn(oC)
#--> find-then-apply
? o1.Submit(oEx, read(oEx.RightAnswers()[1])).Passed()
#--> 1
? o1.HasPassed("ex-01-01")
#--> 1
? o1.ChapterOn(oC)
#--> a-first-sentence

classes.name: stzLibDoc
classes.brief: Indexes the methods and doc blocks of many classes at once, so a plain-English question finds the method and the class that holds it.
classes.description: It harvests each named class with its inherited methods from the source, files every method under the class that defines it, and adds the intent recipes, small units that answer a how-do-I question with a runnable snippet. Ask ranks the entries by the meaning of the words: a lexical match first, with a loaded embedding or reranker model rescuing questions that share no word. Nothing is generated; the answer is always something the library already holds. Keep the class list short, since a large list costs index time when an embedding model is loaded.
classes.example:
? o1.NumberOfClasses()
#--> 2
? o1.NumberOfRecipes() > 0
#--> 1
? o1.BestMethodFor("remember a fact")
#--> stzAgentMemory.Fact
? o1.Ask("detect the language of a text")[1][1]
#--> (recipe)

classes.name: stzLinearSolver
classes.brief: Solves small linear programs written as text: variables with bounds, constraints such as x + y <= 5 and one objective to maximize or minimize.
classes.description: Declare the variables with addVariable, the constraints with addConstraint and the objective with maximize or minimize, then call solve with a solver name. The simplex solver (Big-M, run in the engine) gives the exact optimum and reports optimal, infeasible or unbounded in status. The greedy solver, the default, is a heuristic that raises every variable as far as allowed: it does not honour minimize and reads every constraint as a limit from above. The genetic solver raises an error as soon as the problem has a constraint, and branch_bound is not implemented, so it always raises. The integer and binary marks are recorded but no solver enforces them. The simplex pivot helpers (BuildSimplexTableau and its kin) are placeholders that answer constants. Pass an empty text to solve for the default solver, since the argument cannot be left out.
classes.example:
o1.addVariable("x", 0, 4).addVariable("y", 0, 6)
o1.addConstraint("x + y", "<=", 5).addConstraint("x + 3*y", "<=", 12)
o1.maximize("3*x + 2*y").solve("simplex")
? o1.solutionValue("x")
#--> 4
? o1.solutionValue("y")
#--> 1
? o1.objectiveValue()
#--> 14
? o1.status()
#--> optimal

methods.name: init
methods.brief: Builds an empty linear programming problem, with no variable, no constraint and no objective.

methods.name: clear
methods.brief: Empties the problem so a new one can be described: variables, constraints, objective, status and the last solution are dropped.
methods.returns: nothing; the problem is empty again

methods.name: addVariable
methods.brief: Adds a continuous variable with a lower and an upper bound, in declaration order.

parameters.name: varName
parameters.role: the variable's name, as text

parameters.name: _lowerBound_
parameters.role: the smallest value the variable may take

parameters.name: _upperBound_
parameters.role: the largest value it may take, never below the lower bound

methods.returns: the solver itself, so calls chain
notes: an empty text given for one bound copies the other bound (a, "" and 6 gives the range 6 to 6); expressions read names without regard to case
warnings: all three arguments must be given: calling with fewer raises R19 Calling function with less number of parameters, so the defaults coded for a missing bound are never reached; a name that is not text, bounds that are not numbers and an upper bound below the lower bound each raise an error

methods.name: addIntegerVariable
methods.brief: Adds a variable whose type is marked integer, with the same arguments and checks as a continuous one.

parameters.name: varName
parameters.role: the variable's name, as text

parameters.name: _lowerBound_
parameters.role: the smallest value the variable may take

parameters.name: _upperBound_
parameters.role: the largest value it may take

methods.returns: the solver itself, so calls chain
notes: all three arguments are needed, as for addVariable
warnings: the mark is only recorded in the variable list: the simplex solver ignores it (maximize n with 2*n <= 5 answers 2.5), the greedy solver floors every value, and branch and bound is not implemented

methods.name: addBinaryVariable
methods.brief: Adds a variable bounded between 0 and 1 and marked binary.

parameters.name: varName
parameters.role: the variable's name, as text

methods.returns: the solver itself, so calls chain
warnings: the mark is only recorded: the simplex solver ignores it (maximize b with 2*b <= 1 answers 0.5)

methods.name: variables
methods.brief: Returns the declared variables in order, each as a list of name, lowerbound, upperbound and type pairs.
methods.returns: a list with one list of [ key, value ] pairs per variable; [ ] when none is declared
notes: the keys are lower case

methods.name: variableNames
methods.brief: Returns the names of the declared variables, in declaration order.

methods.name: addConstraint
methods.brief: Adds one linear constraint: an expression such as "x + 3*y", a comparison and a number.

parameters.name: expression
parameters.role: the left side, as text, with terms like 2*x, x*2 or x

parameters.name: operator
parameters.role: the comparison: "<=", ">=" or "="

parameters.name: _value_
parameters.role: the number the expression is compared with

methods.returns: the solver itself, so calls chain
notes: constraints are stored as stzHashList objects
warnings: an expression that is not text, another operator, or a value that is neither a number nor text raise an error; a value given as text, such as "7" or "", is stored as 0 because the text is looked up in the variables list

methods.name: constraints
methods.brief: Returns the declared constraints in order, each as a stzHashList holding expression, operator and value.
methods.returns: a list of stzHashList objects; [ ] when none is declared

methods.name: maximize
methods.brief: Sets the objective to an expression to make as large as possible, replacing any earlier objective.

parameters.name: expression
parameters.role: the objective, as text, such as "3*x + 2*y"

methods.returns: the solver itself, so calls chain

methods.name: minimize
methods.brief: Sets the objective to an expression to make as small as possible, replacing any earlier objective.

parameters.name: expression
parameters.role: the objective, as text, such as "x + 2*y"

methods.returns: the solver itself, so calls chain
warnings: the greedy solver does not honour it (minimize x with x <= 4 answers 4); use the simplex solver

methods.name: objective
methods.brief: Returns the objective expression as text.
methods.returns: a text; "" before an objective is set

methods.name: objectiveType
methods.brief: Returns whether the objective is to be made larger or smaller.
methods.returns: the text "maximize" or "minimize"; "maximize" before any objective is set

methods.name: solve
methods.brief: Runs one of the built-in solvers and keeps its answer: "greedy" (the default), "simplex", "branch_bound" or "genetic".

parameters.name: _cSolver_
parameters.role: the solver's name, in lower case, an empty text selects greedy

methods.returns: the solver itself, so calls chain
notes: on maximize 3*x + 2*y with x + y <= 5 and x + 3*y <= 12, bounds 0..4 and 0..6, simplex and greedy both answer x = 4 and y = 1, value 14
warnings: the argument cannot be left out (R19), pass an empty text for the default; no variable, no objective or an unknown name raise an error; "branch_bound" always raises today and sets the status to unimplemented; "genetic" raises R5 as soon as the problem has a constraint; "greedy" is a heuristic and still reports the status optimal

methods.name: solveWithGreedy
methods.brief: Returns a solution that raises each variable, best objective per resource first, to the largest whole value its limits allow.
methods.returns: a list of [ name, value ] pairs, one per variable
notes: called directly it returns the pairs and sets the status and iterations but does not store the answer; solve does
warnings: a heuristic, reported with status optimal in every case: it raises variables as far as allowed even when minimizing (minimize x with x <= 4 answers 4, the simplex answers 0), it reads ">=" and "=" as "<=" so an equality can be violated (minimize x + 2*y with x + y >= 3 and x - y = -1 answers x = 0 and y = 3, value 6, where the simplex answers 1 and 2, value 5), and it floors values

methods.name: solveWithSimplex
methods.brief: Returns the optimum found by a Big-M simplex run in the engine, after shifting the variables to their lower bounds.
methods.returns: a list of [ name, value ] pairs, one per variable; the status is set to optimal, infeasible, unbounded or iteration_limit
notes: minimize x + 2*y with x + y >= 3 and x - y = -1, bounds 0..2 and 0..5, answers x = 1 and y = 2, which satisfies both rows
warnings: the integer and binary marks are ignored; a problem with no constraint and with every bound range at least 1000000000 wide raises 'the engine simplex returned an unusable result' (a single variable up to 1000000000000, and two such variables, both raised); an unbounded problem that has a constraint answers with the status unbounded instead of raising

methods.name: solveWithBranchAndBound
methods.brief: Raises error today instead of solving by branch and bound, which is not implemented yet.
methods.returns: nothing; always raises and sets the status to unimplemented
notes: the integer variables are therefore never enforced by any solver
warnings: an honesty guard stops the method on its first line, so the branching code after it never runs; use "greedy" or "simplex"

methods.name: solveWithGenetic
methods.brief: Returns a solution found by a genetic search of 50 candidates over 100 generations, scored by objective minus a constraint penalty.
methods.returns: a list of [ name, value ] pairs, one per variable
notes: the search draws random numbers from the engine
warnings: raises R5 Can't access the list item, Object is not list as soon as the problem has a constraint, because CalculatePenalty reads a variable oConst that does not exist (two problems, one and two constraints); a problem without constraints runs, and bounds 0..100 with maximize x + y answered x = 99 and y = 100, so the search is approximate

methods.name: parseObjectiveCoefficients
methods.brief: Returns the objective's coefficient for each declared variable, in declaration order.
methods.returns: a list of numbers; 0 for a variable the objective does not mention

methods.name: extractCoefficient

parameters.name: _cExpression_
parameters.role: the expression, as text, with terms like 2*x, x*2, -x or x

parameters.name: _cVarName_

methods.returns: a number; 0 when the variable does not appear

methods.name: calculateResourceCost

parameters.name: _cVarName_
parameters.role: the variable's name

methods.returns: a number; 0 when no constraint mentions the variable

methods.name: CalculateMaxPossibleValue

parameters.name: _cVarName_

parameters.name: _aSolution_

methods.returns: a whole number, never below 0; 999999 when no constraint with a positive coefficient limits it

parameters.name: _aSolution_

classes.name: stzListBounder
classes.brief: Answers questions about the ends of a list: its bounds, its middle, a section or range of it, and whether positions and values stay within limits.
classes.description: It is the bounds helper of stzList, which builds one over itself for its SectionXT, IsBoundedByCS, Bounds, BoundsUpToNItems and RemoveBoundsCS methods; build one with new stzListBounder when you only need the ends. It works on its own copy, so a stzList passed in is never changed, and you read the result of an in-place verb (RemoveBounds, ClampTo) with Content. Bounds are the first and last items: IsBoundedBy compares them with a pair [ open, close ], and BoundsRemoved returns the list without them when they match. Positions count from 1. Section raises when a position falls outside the list, where stzListGetter.Section clips; NFirstItems and NLastItems clip to the list. AreBoundsOf raises error R14 today, because the stzString method it calls does not exist. Hebrew, Arabic and emoji items work as bounds like any other value.

classes.name: stzListChecker
classes.brief: Answers yes or no questions about a list: what its items are made of, whether they are unique, ordered, equal or paired.
classes.description: Reach for it to validate a list before using it: AllItemsAreOfType and the IsListOf... family check the type of the items, IsMonotonic and the strict variants check their order, IsHashList and IsListOfPairs check the shape, and HasMoreNumberOfItems compares the length with another list. Most checks answer 1 or 0, a few answer TRUE or FALSE; both work in an if. A check made on the empty list is true for IsListOfNumbers, IsListOfStrings and AllItemsAreEqual, and false for IsListOfLists. ContainsItem, ContainsAllOfThese and ContainsOneOfThese look for numbers, texts and lists whole; ContainsW asks the engine's W language whether some item meets a condition.
classes.example:
? o1.IsListOfNumbers()
#--> 1
? o1.IsMonotonic()
#--> 0
? o1.IsEqualTo([3, 1, 2])
#--> 1
? o1.HasMoreNumberOfItems([1])
#--> 1

classes.name: stzListClassifier
classes.brief: Groups the items of a list by equality or by an expression, counts them, and answers the most and least frequent, plus halves and chunks.
classes.description: It is the grouping helper of stzList, which builds one over itself for its Classify, Classes, ClassifyBy, NumberOfClasses and Frequencies methods; build one with new stzListClassifier when you only need to group. It never changes the list, so a stzList passed in stays intact. Classify answers [ item, positions ] pairs with positions counted from 1, and Frequencies answers [ item, count ] pairs, both in order of first appearance. Two limits found today: Classify, Classes and NumberOfClasses answer nothing for a list made of numbers, and the counting methods (Classify, Frequencies, Mode, MostFrequent, ItemsAppearing...) fold capital and small ASCII letters together and give the numbers back as texts, while FrequencyOf compares with case and type. ItemsAppearingNTimes and its kin keep each item's own type. Partition, Chunks, Bisect, FirstHalf and SecondHalf only cut the list by position. Hebrew, Arabic and emoji items are classed like any other text.
classes.example:
? @@( o1.Classify() )
#--> [ [ "a", [ 1, 3, 5 ] ], [ "b", [ 2, 6 ] ], [ "c", [ 4 ] ] ]
? @@( o1.Frequencies() )
#--> [ [ "a", 3 ], [ "b", 2 ], [ "c", 1 ] ]
? o1.MostFrequent()
#--> a
? @@( o1.ItemsAppearingMoreThanNTimes(1) )
#--> [ "a", "b" ]
? @@( o1.Chunks(4) )
#--> [ [ "a", "b", "a", "c" ], [ "a", "b" ] ]
o2 = new stzListClassifier([ "apple", "bob", "kiwi", "fig", "plum" ])
? @@( o2.ClassifyBy("len(@item)") )
#--> [ [ "5", [ 1 ] ], [ "3", [ 2, 4 ] ], [ "4", [ 3, 5 ] ] ]
o3 = new stzListClassifier([ "שלום", "😀", "שלום" ])
? @@( o3.Frequencies() )
#--> [ [ "שלום", 2 ], [ "😀", 1 ] ]

classes.name: stzListComparator
classes.brief: Compares a list with another one: equality, subset and superset, common items, union, differences, prefix and suffix, and containment.
classes.description: It is the comparing helper of stzList, which builds one over itself for its ContainsAllOfTheseCS and ContainsOneOfTheseCS methods; build one with new stzListComparator when you only need to compare. It never changes the list, so a stzList passed in stays intact. Every test has a CS form taking 1 to compare with case and 0 to ignore it, and the plain form compares with case. IsEqualTo, IsNotEqualTo and IsPermutationOf compare sets: they ignore order and repeats, so [ 1, 1, 2 ] equals [ 1, 2, 2 ]; IsStrictlyEqualTo is the one that checks positions. Union, CommonItems and IsSubsetOf work on sets too. Found today: IsReverseOf raises error R3 (the function that reverses the other list does not exist), and IsSortedLike answers TRUE for any two lists of the same size. Hebrew, Arabic and emoji items compare like any other text.
classes.example:
? o1.IsStrictlyEqualTo([ 4, 3, 2, 1 ])
#--> 0
? o1.IsEqualTo([ 4, 3, 2, 1 ])
#--> 1
? @@( o1.CommonItems([ 3, 4, 5, 6 ]) )
#--> [ 3, 4 ]
? @@( o1.SymmetricDifference([ 3, 4, 5, 6 ]) )
#--> [ 1, 2, 5, 6 ]
? o1.IsSubsetOf([ 1, 2, 3, 4, 5 ])
#--> 1
? o1.StartsWith([ 1, 2 ])
#--> 1
o2 = new stzListComparator([ "a", "B", "c" ])
? o2.IsEqualToCS([ "A", "b", "C" ], 0)
#--> 1
o3 = new stzListComparator([ "שלום", "😀" ])
? o3.IsEqualTo([ "😀", "שלום" ])
#--> 1

classes.name: stzListCounter
classes.brief: Counts the items of a list: by condition, by type, by value, and empty or not, and inserts around the items that meet a condition.
classes.description: Build one with new stzListCounter(aList) or over a stzList object; it keeps its own copy, so what you passed in is never changed. A condition is written in the W notation, a text in braces where @item stands for the item under test, such as '{ @item > 5 }'. Count compares texts case- sensitively; CountCS takes a 0 or 1 flag. The insertion methods InsertAfterW and InsertBeforeW change the list the counter holds. The question forms HowManyItemsW, HowManyUniqueItemsW and the alias InsertAfterWhere raise error R24 today; see their warnings.
classes.example:
? o1.CountNumbers()
#--> 3
? o1.Count(12)
#--> 2
? o1.CountItemsW('{ isNumber(@item) and @item > 6 }')
#--> 2
? o1.CountEmptyItems()
#--> 1
