classes.name: stzListDuplicates
classes.brief: Finds, counts and removes the repeated items of a list: positions of the repeats, items that repeat, items that never do, and the most repeated one.
classes.description: It is the repeats helper of stzList, which builds one over itself for its ContainsDuplicatedItemsCS and DuplicatedItemsCS methods; build one with new stzListDuplicates when you need the rest. It works on its own copy, so a stzList passed in is never changed, and you read the result of an in-place verb (RemoveDuplicates) with Content. A repeat is an occurrence after the first one of its item, so the first occurrence is never a duplicate: on a b a c b a d the repeats sit at positions 3, 5 and 6, and NumberOfDuplicates is 3. Every question has a CS form taking 1 to compare with case and 0 to ignore it. ItemsDuplicatedNTimes and MostDuplicatedItem give the items back as texts, so the number 3 is "3". RemoveNthDuplicate does nothing today. Hebrew, Arabic and emoji items repeat like any other text.
classes.example:
? @@( o1.FindDuplicates() )
#--> [ 3, 5, 6 ]
? @@( o1.DuplicatedItems() )
#--> [ "a", "b" ]
? @@( o1.NonDuplicatedItems() )
#--> [ "c", "d" ]
? o1.MostDuplicatedItem()
#--> a
? @@( o1.WithoutDuplication() )
#--> [ "a", "b", "c", "d" ]
o2 = new stzListDuplicates([ "a", "A", "b", "a" ])
? @@( o2.FindDuplicatesCS(0) )
#--> [ 2, 4 ]
o3 = new stzListDuplicates([ "שלום", "😀", "שלום" ])
? @@( o3.FindDuplicates() )
#--> [ 3 ]

classes.name: stzListener
classes.brief: Recognises a sound against a closed list of accepted phrases, with a confidence, using the local speech recognizer.
classes.description: It does commands, not dictation, on purpose: free dictation measured 66.7 percent exact against 100 percent for a closed grammar, and every miss was a written form rather than a mishearing. A phrase outside the list is a no-match, which is a result and not an error. The text and its Confidence are separate calls so the confidence cannot be skipped. The recognizer runs in the process and reaches no network. Capability is per language and per direction: this machine hears only fr-FR. HearMicrophoneFor opens an input device, the library's consent boundary, and was not run in this reference. The examples feed the machine's own French voice to it; no person has been heard (UNPERCEIVED).
classes.example:
? o1.Accept([ "ouvrir le fichier", "enregistrer", "annuler" ])
#--> 1
? o1.PhraseCount()
#--> 3
? o1.HearSound(StzVoiceForQ("fr-FR").ToSoundOf("ouvrir le fichier"))
#--> 1
? o1.HeardText()
#--> ouvrir le fichier

methods.brief: Opens the machine's local speech recognizer for a listener that hears only a closed list of phrases.
notes: no microphone is opened here
warnings: a machine with no recognizer leaves the object unusable and LastError says why; the recognizer runs in the process and reaches no network

methods.name: Release
methods.brief: Frees the recognizer handle held by the listener.
warnings: afterwards the listener is not usable and every call is refused

methods.name: IsUsable
methods.brief: TRUE if the machine has a recognizer and the listener opened it.

methods.name: LastError
methods.brief: Returns the reason the last call failed, or the engine's last recognizer error when none was recorded here.
warnings: a successful call does not clear it, apart from Accept, which does

methods.name: Refusals
methods.brief: Returns how many calls the listener refused.
methods.returns: a number, a no-match not being counted

methods.name: RecognizerCount
methods.brief: Returns how many speech recognizers are installed.
methods.returns: a number; 0 when the speech tier is missing

methods.name: Languages
methods.brief: Returns the language tags the machine can hear, without repeats.
methods.returns: a list of text; fr-FR alone on this machine, which speaks en-US and fr-FR
warnings: hearing and speaking differ, so ask stzVoice for what can be spoken

methods.name: ToRecognizerList
methods.brief: Returns every installed recognizer with its language.
methods.returns: a list of [ name, language tag ] rows

methods.name: HasLanguage
methods.brief: TRUE if some recognizer hears the language, an exact tag or the same language with another region.

parameters.name: pcTag
parameters.role: a language tag such as fr-FR, or a bare language such as fr

warnings: the bare language fr matches fr-FR

methods.name: Accept
methods.brief: Declares the closed list of phrases the listener may hear; anything else will be a no-match.

parameters.name: paPhrases
parameters.role: the list of phrases that count as commands

methods.returns: TRUE if the grammar was set; FALSE with LastError set

extensions.name: AcceptQ

methods.name: AcceptedPhrases
methods.brief: Returns the phrases last accepted, as they were given.

methods.name: AcceptMeanings
methods.brief: Declares the phrases and the meaning each one carries in a single call.

parameters.name: paPairs
parameters.role: a list of [ phrase, meaning ] rows, each meaning one of danger, warning, info, success or muted

methods.returns: TRUE if the grammar was set; FALSE with LastError set
notes: the author declares each meaning; nothing is inferred from the words
warnings: an empty list, a row that is not a pair or a sixth meaning is refused at once, with LastError set and the refusal counted

extensions.name: AcceptMeaningsQ
extensions.adds: does what the method does, then returns the object, so the call can be chained

methods.name: MeaningHeard
methods.brief: Returns the meaning declared for the phrase just heard.
methods.returns: a text such as success or danger; an empty text for a no-match, which is a result and not an error
warnings: the phrase is matched without regard to case

methods.name: AcceptedMeanings
methods.brief: Returns the phrase and meaning pairs last declared.
methods.returns: a list of [ phrase in lower case, meaning in lower case ] rows; [ ] before AcceptMeanings

methods.name: PhraseCount
methods.brief: Returns how many phrases the grammar holds.
methods.returns: a number; 0 before Accept or when the listener is not usable

methods.name: HearSound
methods.brief: Recognises a sound against the accepted phrases, which needs no microphone.

parameters.name: poSound
parameters.role: the stzSound to listen to, such as one made by stzVoice

methods.returns: TRUE if a phrase was recognised; FALSE for a no-match or a refusal
notes: the recognizer ran on a phrase spoken by the machine's own voice, not on a person
warnings: a non-sound, an unusable listener and a sound with no WAV bytes are refused and counted; a no-match is not

methods.name: HearMicrophoneFor
methods.brief: Opens the microphone for a number of seconds and recognises what is said against the accepted phrases.

parameters.name: pnSeconds
parameters.role: how long to listen, in seconds

methods.returns: TRUE if a phrase was recognised; FALSE for a no-match or a refusal
notes: the operator should be told that the microphone is open; nothing leaves the machine
warnings: not run in this reference: it opens an input device, which is this library's consent boundary

methods.name: HeardText
methods.brief: Returns the text of the last recognised phrase.
methods.returns: a text; an empty text for a no-match and for a listener that is not usable
warnings: it is one of the accepted phrases, as declared

methods.name: Confidence
methods.brief: Returns how sure the recognizer was of the last phrase, from 0 to 1.
warnings: always read it with the text, since a phrase without its confidence is a guess dressed as a fact

methods.name: HeardSomething
methods.brief: TRUE if the last hearing recognised a phrase.

methods.name: WasNoMatch
methods.brief: TRUE if the last hearing found nothing in the grammar, which is a result and not an error.
methods.returns: TRUE or FALSE; FALSE before any hearing

classes.name: stzListex
classes.brief: Matches a list against a regex-like pattern of typed items, such as [@N, @S] for a number then a text.
classes.description: A pattern is a list of tokens: @N a number, @S a text, @L a list, @$ any item, each with an optional quantifier (+, *, ?, a count or a range such as 2-3), a set of allowed values written {a; b} with a trailing U for unique values, a negation @! and a case flag @cs:. Match answers 1 or 0 for the whole list, and Tokens, TokensInfo and Explain show how the pattern was read. Build one with StzListexQ, StzListRegexQ or Lx. Found today: the cache key of Match is the same for any reordering of a list, so on one matcher a reordered list gets the stale answer of the first (use ClearCache between them); the first alternative of a group never matches; sets written in single quotes never match, since their closing quote is kept; the unique flag U does not enforce uniqueness; a nested list with a quantifier fails for two sublists; and TokensInfo raises R41 for any token with a variable count. The cause of the quote, alternation and nested defects is the same as stzTimex: calls to @StzMid pass an end position where it now wants a length.

methods.name: init
methods.brief: Builds a list matcher from a pattern text such as [@N, @S], wrapping it in square brackets if needed.

parameters.name: _cPattern_
parameters.role: the pattern as text

notes: the pattern language: @N a number, @S a text, @L a list, @$ any item; + * ? 2 and 2-3 as quantifiers; {a; b} a set of allowed values and a trailing U for unique ones; @!N a negation; @cs:S case-sensitive; a bracketed group of tokens joined by a vertical bar for alternatives; [@N, @S] a nested list; build with StzListexQ, StzListRegexQ or Lx

methods.name: NormalizePattern
methods.brief: Returns the pattern text trimmed and wrapped in square brackets when it is not yet.

parameters.name: _cPattern_
parameters.role: the pattern as text

notes: @N, @S gives [@N, @S], and [@N] stays [@N]

methods.name: ParsePattern
methods.brief: Splits a bracketed pattern at its top-level commas and parses each piece into a token.

parameters.name: _cPattern_
parameters.role: the bracketed pattern

methods.returns: a list of tokens, each a list of [ name, value ] pairs
notes: [@N, @S, @L] gives 3 tokens; [@N2-3, @S?] gives a number token of 2 to 3 and a text token of 0 to 1

methods.name: ParseNestedPattern
methods.brief: Reads a nested list pattern such as [@N, @S]+ into one nested token holding the tokens of its inside.

parameters.name: cNestedPattern
parameters.role: the nested pattern with its quantifier, such as [@N, @S]+

parameters.name: _bNegated_
parameters.role: 1 if the token is negated

parameters.name: _bCaseSensitive_
parameters.role: the case flag the inner tokens inherit

methods.returns: a token with the keyword @NESTED and its nestedTokens
notes: the token has the type nested
warnings: a nested token with a quantifier of + or * did not match two sublists in checks (the pattern [[@N]+] answered FALSE for [[1],[2]] and TRUE for [[1]])

methods.name: ParseAlternationToken
methods.brief: Reads a bracketed group of alternatives, such as a number or a text, into one alternation token.

parameters.name: _cTokenStr_
parameters.role: the text of the group, its alternatives between round brackets and joined by vertical bars

parameters.name: _bNegated_
parameters.role: 1 if the token is negated

parameters.name: _bCaseSensitive_
parameters.role: the case flag the alternatives inherit

methods.returns: a token with the keyword @ALT and its alternatives
notes: the later alternatives are read correctly
warnings: the first alternative loses its keyword, type and pattern (in a group of @N and @S the @N becomes an empty token), so a matching list for the first alternative answers FALSE: a pattern with @N or @S in one group matches a but not 1

methods.name: ParseToken
methods.brief: Reads one piece of a pattern, such as @N2-3, @S{"a"; "b"}, @!N or @cs:S, into a token.

parameters.name: _cTokenStr_
parameters.role: the text of one piece

methods.returns: a token as a list of [ name, value ] pairs: keyword, type, pattern, min, max, quantifier, hasset, setvalues, requireunique, negated, casesensitive
notes: @N+ gives min 1 and a huge max, @N2-4 gives 2 and 4, @!N sets negated, @cs:S sets casesensitive
warnings: an unknown keyword such as @A returns a token with no keyword, type or pattern; set values written between single quotes keep their closing quote (the set of a and b read as a' and b'), so such sets never match

methods.name: SplitAtTopLevelCommas
methods.brief: Cuts a text at the commas that are outside square brackets.

parameters.name: cStr
parameters.role: the text to cut

methods.returns: a list of text, each piece trimmed
notes: @N, [@S, @N], @L gives @N, [@S, @N] and @L

methods.name: ParseSetValues
methods.brief: Reads the inside of a set such as {1; 2; 3} into a list of values of the given type.

parameters.name: _cSetContent_
parameters.role: the set text, with or without its braces, values separated by semicolons

parameters.name: _cType_
parameters.role: number, string, list or any

parameters.name: bCheckUnique
parameters.role: 1 to refuse repeated values

methods.returns: a list of values: numbers for number, double-quoted texts for string
notes: {1; 2; 3} gives 1, 2 and 3
warnings: raises Error: Duplicate value in unique set when bCheckUnique is 1 and a value repeats, and Error: Invalid number in set for a non-number; a value written between single quotes keeps its closing quote ('a' gives "a'")

methods.name: RemoveQuotes
methods.brief: Strips the quotes around a text, but keeps the closing one.

parameters.name: cStr
parameters.role: the text, possibly between single or double quotes

notes: a text without quotes comes back as it is
warnings: the closing quote stays: 'abc' gives abc' and "abc" gives abc"

methods.name: OptimizeTokens
methods.brief: Merges, in place, neighbouring tokens that have the same keyword, no set and a variable quantifier.
notes: it runs once when the matcher is built
warnings: [@N+, @N*] becomes one token whose minimum is 0, which is looser than the pattern says

methods.name: Match
methods.brief: TRUE if the whole list matches the pattern, element by element.

parameters.name: paList
parameters.role: the list to test

methods.returns: TRUE or FALSE, as 1 or 0; FALSE for a value that is not a list
notes: with a fresh matcher or after ClearCache the answers are right for [@N, @S]: [1, a] is TRUE, [a, 1] is FALSE; @S{"Hello"} accepts hello and @cs:S{"Hello"} does not
warnings: a repeated question returns a cached answer, and the cache key (the length and the sum of the characters) is the same for any reordering of a list: after [1, 2, a] matches [@N+, @S], the list [a, 2, 1] answers TRUE too on the same matcher, though a new matcher answers FALSE; a set U does not enforce uniqueness (the pattern [@N2{1; 2}U] accepts [2, 2]); a nested quantifier fails for two sublists; sets written in single quotes never match; the first of several alternatives never matches; Macth is a misspelled alias that works

methods.name: MatchTokensToElements
methods.brief: TRUE if the tokens match the elements from the start to the end.

parameters.name: _aTokens_
parameters.role: the list of tokens, from Tokens

parameters.name: _aElements_
parameters.role: the list of elements to test

notes: the tokens of [@N, @S] match [1, a]

methods.name: BacktrackMatch
methods.brief: TRUE if the tokens from one token on match the elements from one element on, trying alternatives by backtracking.

parameters.name: _aTokens_
parameters.role: the list of tokens

parameters.name: _aElements_
parameters.role: the list of elements

parameters.name: nTokenIndex
parameters.role: the 1-based index of the first token

parameters.name: nElementIndex
parameters.role: the 1-based index of the first element

parameters.name: aUsedValues
parameters.role: the values already used by unique sets, [ ] to start

notes: the tokens of [@N, @S] against [1, a] from 1 and 1 give TRUE, and against [a, 1] give FALSE

methods.name: CompareValues
methods.brief: TRUE if two values are equal under a type: numbers by value, texts with or without case, any by its kind.

parameters.name: xValue1
parameters.role: the first value

parameters.name: xValue2
parameters.role: the second value

parameters.name: _cType_
parameters.role: number, string, list or any

parameters.name: _bCaseSensitive_
parameters.role: 1 to compare with case, 0 to ignore it

notes: A against a is FALSE with 1 and TRUE with 0
warnings: the types list, and any when both values are lists, raise Calling Function without definition: @stzreplace (R3) through NormalizeListString

methods.name: NormalizeListString
methods.brief: Raises error R3 today instead of removing the spaces from the text of a list.

parameters.name: xList
parameters.role: the list, or its text

notes: strip the spaces yourself
warnings: raises Calling Function without definition: @stzreplace (R3), because it calls a function that does not exist

methods.name: ConvertToType
methods.brief: Returns a value read as the given type: a number for number, otherwise the text as it is.

parameters.name: _cValue_
parameters.role: the value as text

parameters.name: _cType_
parameters.role: number, string, list or any

notes: 12 with number gives the number 12

methods.name: ListSignature
methods.brief: Returns a short key made of a list's length and the sum of the characters of its text, used as the cache key.

parameters.name: aList
parameters.role: the list to describe

notes: an empty list gives 0:216
warnings: two lists with the same elements in another order get the same key ([1, 2, 3] and [3, 2, 1] both give 3:550), which is how Match returns a stale answer

methods.name: ClearCache
methods.brief: Empties the cache of past match answers.
methods.returns: the matcher itself, so calls chain
notes: call it before testing a list that is a reordering of one already tested

methods.name: SetCacheSize
methods.brief: Sets how many answers the cache may hold.

parameters.name: nSize
parameters.role: the largest number of cached answers

methods.returns: the matcher itself, so calls chain
notes: CacheInfo reads it back as maxsize, 100 on a new matcher

methods.name: CacheInfo
methods.brief: Returns how many answers the cache holds and its limit.
methods.returns: a list of [ entries, n ] and [ maxsize, n ] pairs

methods.name: DebugLog
methods.brief: Prints a titled debug message when the debug flag is on, and does nothing otherwise.

parameters.name: cMethod
parameters.role: the title

parameters.name: cMessage
parameters.role: the message

methods.name: EnableDebug
methods.brief: Turns on the debug printing of the parser and the matcher.
methods.returns: the matcher itself, so calls chain

methods.name: DisableDebug
methods.brief: Turns off the debug printing.
methods.returns: the matcher itself, so calls chain

methods.name: Tokens
methods.brief: Returns the tokens parsed from the pattern, after merging.
methods.returns: a list of tokens, each a list of [ name, value ] pairs
notes: TokensXT is the same call

extensions.name: TokensXT
extensions.adds: the extended form: more parameters than the base method

methods.name: TokensInfo
methods.brief: Returns one line of text per token: its number, keyword, quantifier and set.
methods.returns: a list of text such as Token #1: @N
notes: MatchInfo is the same call; @N{1;2} gives Token #1: @N {1; 2}
warnings: raises Invalid numeric string (R41) for every token whose minimum differs from its maximum (@N+, @N2-3 and @S? all raise), because it adds a number to a text; only tokens with a fixed count work

methods.name: JoinSetValues
methods.brief: Returns the set values joined as one text, separated by semicolons and a space.

parameters.name: _aValues_
parameters.role: the list of values

notes: 1, b and 3 give 1; b; 3

methods.name: Pattern
methods.brief: Returns the pattern text as stored, wrapped in square brackets.
notes: DomainPattern is the same call

methods.brief: Returns a summary of the pattern: its text, token count, cache entries and one record per token.
methods.returns: a list of [ name, value ] pairs
notes: each token record holds Index, Keyword, Type, Min, Max, HasSet, SetValues, Unique, Negated and CaseSensitive; ExplainXT is the same call

classes.name: stzListExtractor
classes.brief: Takes items out of a list and hands them back: by position, by section, by occurrence, the repeats, or all the texts, numbers or sublists.
classes.description: It is the extracting helper of stzList, which builds one over itself for its Extract, ExtractAll, ExtractNth, ExtractSection and ExtractRange methods; build one with new stzListExtractor when you only need to take things out. It works on its own copy, so a stzList passed in is never changed, and what is left is read with Content. Every Extract method does two things at once: it removes the items from the held list and returns them, the items that were taken out being the answer. Extract(pItem) removes every occurrence, while ExtractNthOccurrence, ExtractFirstOccurrence and ExtractLastOccurrence remove just one. A position outside the list raises (ExtractNth, ExtractFirst, ExtractLast, ExtractSection, ExtractRange, Take, TakeLast), except the occurrence methods, which answer an empty text when there is no such occurrence. Positions count from 1; the CS forms take 0 to ignore case. Hebrew, Arabic and emoji items are extracted like any other text.
classes.example:
? o1.ExtractNth(3)
#--> c
? @@( o1.Content() )
#--> [ "a", "b", "b", "d", "e" ]
? @@( o1.ExtractSection(2, 3) )
#--> [ "b", "b" ]
? @@( o1.Content() )
#--> [ "a", "d", "e" ]
o2 = new stzListExtractor([ "a", "b", "a", "c", "b", "a" ])
? @@( o2.ExtractDuplicates() )
#--> [ "a", "b", "a" ]
? @@( o2.Content() )
#--> [ "a", "b", "c" ]
o3 = new stzListExtractor([ 1, "a", [ 1, 2 ], 2, "שלום" ])
? @@( o3.ExtractStrings() )
#--> [ "a", "שלום" ]

methods.name: init
methods.brief: Builds an extractor over a list, given as a list or as a stzList object.

parameters.name: pListOrObj
parameters.role: the list to take items out of, or a stzList whose content is copied, any other value raises an error

notes: the extractor works on its own copy: taking items out never changes the list or the stzList you passed in, so read what is left with Content

methods.name: Content
methods.brief: Returns the items still in the list, after the extractions made so far.

methods.name: List
methods.brief: Returns the items still in the list, after the extractions made so far.
notes: the same answer as Content

methods.name: NumberOfItems
methods.brief: Returns how many items are still in the list.

methods.name: IsEmpty
methods.brief: TRUE if no item is left in the list.

methods.name: Extract
methods.brief: Takes an item out of the list and returns it, removing every occurrence of it.

parameters.name: pItem
parameters.role: the item to take out

methods.returns: the item that was taken out
notes: case counts: ExtractCS(pItem, 0) ignores case; ExtractMany(paItems) does the same for several items and returns the list it was given
warnings: an item that is absent raises Can't extract the item! It does not exist in the list; it removes all the occurrences and not just one: a b c b d e loses both b

extensions.name: ExtractManyCS
extensions.adds: works on a collection of items instead of one; takes a case-sensitivity flag

extensions.name: ExtractMany
extensions.adds: works on a collection of items instead of one

extensions.name: ExtractW
extensions.adds: selects by a condition

methods.name: ExtractAll
methods.brief: Takes every item out of the list and returns them, leaving it empty.
methods.returns: a list, the items that were in the list

methods.name: ExtractNth
methods.brief: Takes out the item at a position, counting from 1, and returns it.

parameters.name: n
parameters.role: the position of the item to take out

methods.returns: the item that was taken out
notes: the list closes up over the gap
warnings: a position outside the list raises Index outside the list! naming the position and the size

methods.name: ExtractFirst
methods.brief: Takes out the first item of the list and returns it.
methods.returns: the item that was taken out
notes: PopFirst is the same call
warnings: on an empty list it raises Index outside the list!

methods.name: ExtractLast
methods.brief: Takes out the last item of the list and returns it.
methods.returns: the item that was taken out
notes: Pop is the same call
warnings: on an empty list it raises Index outside the list!

methods.name: ExtractSection
methods.brief: Takes out the items from one position to another, both included, and returns them.

parameters.name: n1
parameters.role: the first position

parameters.name: n2

methods.returns: a list, the items that were taken out

methods.name: ExtractRange
methods.brief: Takes out a run of items given its first position and how many items it holds, and returns them.

parameters.name: pnStart

parameters.name: pnRange
parameters.role: how many items to take out

methods.returns: a list, the items that were taken out

methods.name: ExtractNthOccurrence
methods.brief: Takes out the nth occurrence of an item, leaving its other occurrences, and returns it.

parameters.name: n
parameters.role: which occurrence to take out, counting from 1

parameters.name: pItem
parameters.role: the item to look for

methods.returns: the item that was taken out, or an empty text when there is no nth occurrence
notes: an empty text from a missing occurrence cannot be told from an item that is an empty text; ExtractNthOccurrenceCS(n, pItem, 0) ignores case and returns the item as it is spelt in the list

extensions.name: ExtractNthOccurrenceCS
extensions.adds: takes a case-sensitivity flag

methods.name: ExtractFirstOccurrence
methods.brief: Takes out the first occurrence of an item, leaving the others, and returns it.

parameters.name: pItem
parameters.role: the item to look for

methods.returns: the item that was taken out, or an empty text when it is absent
notes: ExtractFirstOccurrenceCS(pItem, 0) ignores case and returns the item as it is spelt in the list

extensions.name: ExtractFirstOccurrenceCS
extensions.adds: takes a case-sensitivity flag

methods.name: ExtractLastOccurrence
methods.brief: Takes out the last occurrence of an item, leaving the others, and returns it.

classes.name: stzListexuter
classes.brief: Matches list-pattern triggers in a list, runs a piece of code on each match and keeps a log of what changed.
classes.description: The list counterpart of stzRegexuter. Register triggers (a name and a list pattern such as [@N, @S]), attach code that edits the match held in @list, then Process a list: every trigger is tried against the whole list and against every contiguous run of its items. Matches, Triggers and Results describe the last run and State logs the matches whose computed list differs. Build one with StzLxuter(), lxuter(), StzLxu() or lxu(). Edit the list in place in the code (@list[1] = @list[1] * 10): assigning @value has no effect and a whole-list assignment that mentions @list reads the new empty list. Found today: a whole list that matches is reported twice; GetDependencyChain overflows the stack once the log holds an entry; StateByPosition sorts by a field the entries do not have; and a single text given to AddTrigger raises R3.
classes.example:
o1.AddTrigger([ "pair", "[@N, @S]" ])
o1.AddCode("pair", "@list[1] = @list[1] * 10")
o1.Process([ 1, "a", 2, "b" ])
? @@( o1.Matches() )
#--> [ [ 1, "a" ], [ 2, "b" ] ]
? @@( o1.Results() )
#--> [ [ 10, "a" ], [ 20, "b" ] ]
o2 = StzLxuter()
o2.AddTrigger([ "word", "[@S]" ])
o2.Process([ "שלום", 5 ])
? @@( o2.Matches() )
#--> [ [ "שלום" ] ]

warnings: only the FIRST code attached to a trigger runs; only a change made to @list takes effect, and assigning @value changes nothing; edit the list in place: @list[1] = @list[1] * 10 works, whereas @list = [ @list[1] * 10 ] reads the new empty list and leaves the match as it was; a code that raises is silent

parameters.name: aList

classes.name: stzListFinder
classes.brief: Finds where an item occurs in a list, as positions: all, first, last, nth, the ones that differ, or those before or after a position.
classes.description: It is the search helper of stzList, which builds one over itself for its Find methods; build one with new stzListFinder when you only need to search. It never edits the list, so a stzList passed in stays intact. Positions are 1-based, and an absent item answers 0 for the single-position verbs and [ ] for the list verbs. Items are matched whole: a text, a number or a sublist, and Hebrew, Arabic and emoji texts match as one item each. Case counts unless you call the CS form with 0. The Next verbs look strictly after a position and count ranks forward; FindPreviousNthOccurrence counts ranks backward from the position, while FindPreviousNthOccurrences counts them forward from the start. Found today: AntiFind and AntiFindAsSections answer a wrong list for an empty list, and CountItemsW raises R14.
classes.example:
? @@( o1.Find("a") )
#--> [ 1, 3, 5 ]
? @@( o1.AntiFind("a") )
#--> [ 2, 4 ]
? o1.FindNextOccurrence("a", 1)
#--> 3
o2 = new stzListFinder([ "שלום", "مرحبا", "😀", "שלום", "😀" ])
? @@( o2.Find("😀") )
#--> [ 3, 5 ]

notes: it has no case-flag form
warnings: the ranks count forward from the start, while FindPreviousNthOccurrence counts backward from the position: a b a c a d A before 7 with ranks [ 1, 2 ] of a gives [ 1, 3 ], where FindPreviousNthOccurrence(2, a, 7) gives 3

classes.name: stzListFlattener
classes.brief: Reshapes a list: opens nested lists, pairs and chunks the items, finds repeated ends, and hands the list to the typed list classes.
classes.description: A flattener is built over a list with new stzListFlattener(aList) or StzListFlattenerQ(aList); stzList has its own Flatten methods and does not build one. It works on its own copy, so the list you passed is never changed. The verbs (Flatten, DeepFlatten, FlattenToDepth, AssociateWith) reshape the held list in place and return nothing, the Q form returning the flattener so calls chain; the past-tense forms (Flattened, DeepFlattened, FlattenedToDepth, AssociatedWith) return the new list and leave the flattener alone. Read the held list with Content. Flatten and DeepFlatten open every level; FlattenToDepth opens only n levels. Paired, Chunked, InterleavedWith, Stringify and Objectified return a new list and never change the held one. The ToStz methods hand the content to the typed class named: ToStzGrid needs a pair [ columns, rows ] and raises an error for other content. The repeated-items methods return the copies after the first item (or before the last), so a run of three gives two. Text items of any script (Hebrew, Arabic, emoji) are kept whole.
classes.example:
? @@( o1.Flattened() )
#--> [ 1, 2, 3, 4, "a" ]
? @@( o1.FlattenedToDepth(1) )
#--> [ 1, 2, [ 3, [ 4 ] ], "a" ]
o2 = new stzListFlattener([ 1, 2, 2, 3, 3, 3 ])
? @@( o2.Paired() )
#--> [ [ 1, 2 ], [ 2, 3 ], [ 3, 3 ] ]
? @@( o2.RepeatedTrailingItems() )
#--> [ 3, 3 ]
o3 = new stzListFlattener([ "שלום", [ "مرحبا", [ "😀" ] ] ])
? @@( o3.FlattenedToDepth(1) )
#--> [ "שלום", "مرحبا", [ "😀" ] ]

methods.brief: TRUE if the first item occurs again right after itself, comparing with or without case.

parameters.name: pCaseSensitive

methods.name: Paired

methods.returns: a list of pairs; the last may hold a single item

classes.name: stzListGetter
classes.brief: Reads items out of a list without changing it: by position, first or last, in sections, at random, by type, or in neighbouring runs.
classes.description: It is the reading helper of stzList, which builds one over itself for its UniqueItems, EveryNthItem, Head, Tail and ItemsBetween methods; build one with new stzListGetter when you only need to read. It works on its own copy, so a stzList passed in is never changed. Positions count from 1. NthItem, NFirstItems, NLastItems, Head, Tail and ItemsAtPositions raise error R2 when a position or a count goes past the list, while Section forgives it by clipping to the list and Range cuts a run that is too long. The Q forms (NFirstItemsQ, PairsQ, SlidingWindowQ ...) return the answer as a stzList to chain on. UniqueItemsCS takes the case flag (0 folds a and A). OnlyChars misses a single non-ASCII character today, and RandomItem and NRandomItems answer differently on every call.
classes.example:
? o1.NthItem(3)
#--> c
? @@( o1.Section(2, 4) )
#--> [ "b", "c", "d" ]
? @@( o1.EveryNthItem(3) )
#--> [ "c", "f" ]
? @@( o1.NLastItems(2) )
#--> [ "f", "g" ]
o2 = new stzListGetter([ 1, 2, 3, 4 ])
? @@( o2.SlidingWindow(2) )
#--> [ [ 1, 2 ], [ 2, 3 ], [ 3, 4 ] ]
o3 = new stzListGetter([ "שלום", "😀", "a", "שלום" ])
? @@( o3.UniqueItems() )
#--> [ "שלום", "😀", "a" ]

classes.name: stzListInserter
classes.brief: Inserts items into a list before or after a position, moves an item to another place and swaps two items.
classes.description: Build one with new stzListInserter(aList) or over a stzList object; it keeps its own copy, so the list you passed in is not changed, and Content gives the result. Positions count from 1. Insert, InsertBeforePosition and InsertAfterPosition accept the item as a plain value and the place as a number or a named pair such as [ :After, 2 ]. Out-of-range positions are not handled the same way by every method: most ignore them without a message, InsertAt raises, and a position two or more past the end kills the process through a missing method; see the warnings.

sections.title: inserting an item before a given position
inserting an item after a given position
moving item at position n1 to position n2
swapping items at two given positions

methods.name: init
methods.brief: Builds an inserter over a list or over a stzList object, working on its own copy, so the list passed in is never changed.

parameters.name: pListOrObj
parameters.role: a list, or a stzList object, in which items will be inserted, moved or swapped

warnings: any other kind of value raises "Can't create stzListInserter! Parameter must be a list or stzList object."

methods.name: Content
methods.brief: Returns the items the inserter holds, after the insertions made through it.

methods.name: NumberOfItems
methods.brief: Returns how many items the list holds now.

methods.name: IsEmpty
methods.brief: TRUE if the list holds no item.

methods.name: Insert
methods.section: inserting an item before a given position
methods.brief: Inserts an item before a position, or after one when the place is written [ :After, n ].

parameters.name: pItem
parameters.role: the item to insert

parameters.name: pWhere
parameters.role: a position (the item goes before it), or a named place such as [ :At, 2 ], [ :Before, 2 ] or [ :After, 2 ]

notes: a position one past the end appends
warnings: a position of 0, or a named place that is neither of those (such as [ :Foo, 1 ]), is ignored without a message; a position two or more past the end kills the process with R14 (ExtendToN), see InsertBeforePosition

extensions.name: InsertQ

parameters.name: pItem

parameters.name: pWhere

extensions.name: InsertBeforePositionQ

methods.section: inserting an item before a given position

methods.name: InsertAt
methods.section: inserting an item before a given position

parameters.role: the position the item takes, from 1

parameters.name: pItem

classes.name: stzListInString
classes.brief: Holds a list written as text, such as '[ "a", 2 ]', evaluates it, and gives the real list back.
classes.description: Build one with new stzListInString(cText) or StzListInStringQ(cText); StringIsListInString(cText) tells whether a text qualifies. It is a stzString, so the source text answers every string method, and the evaluated list is available as List, Content, Value and ToStzList. The text is evaluated as Ring code, which lets names stand for global variables. The analysis methods (Items, Values, VarNames, Types, VariablesAndTheirTypes) are broken today and the four Contains... methods are empty; see their warnings.
classes.example:
? @@( o1.List() )
#--> [ "a", 2, "שלום", 5 ]
? o1.ListInString()
#--> [ "a", 2, "שלום", 5 ]
? @@( o1.ToStzList().Content() )

classes.name: stzListLeadTrail
classes.brief: Examines and trims the repeated items at the beginning and at the end of a list, and tests what a list starts or ends with.
classes.description: A run is two or more equal items in a row at an end of the list; a single item is not a run. Build one with new stzListLeadTrail(aList) or over a stzList object; it keeps its own copy, so what you passed in is not changed, and Content gives the trimmed list. The remove methods keep one item of the run, never none. Every comparison is case-sensitive; the CS forms (RepeatedLeadingItemsCS, RemoveRepeatedTrailingItemsCS, StartsWithCS ...) take 0 to ignore case, and they honour it.

#--> [ "a", "a" ]
? o1.NumberOfRepeatedTrailingItems()
#--> 3
o1.RemoveRepeatedLeadingAndTrailingItems()
? @@( o1.Content() )
#--> [ "a", "b", "c" ]
? o1.StartsWith("a")
#--> 1

classes.name: stzListMerger
classes.brief: Combines lists: opens sublists, appends, prepends, interleaves, zips and unzips, and takes the union, the intersection or the difference of two lists.
classes.description: It is the combining helper of stzList, which builds one over itself for its MergeWith, AssociateWith, InterleaveWith, ZipWith and similar methods; build one with new stzListMerger when you only need to combine. It works on its own copy, so a stzList passed in is never changed. A verb (Merge, MergeWith, Flatten, InterleaveWith, PrependWith) changes the held list in place and returns nothing, its Q form returning the merger for chaining, while the past-tense form (Merged, MergedWith, Flattened, InterleavedWith, PrependedWith) returns the result and leaves the merger alone. Merge opens one level of sublists and Flatten opens them all. ZipWith stops at the shorter list, AssociateWith pads with an empty text. UnionWith, IntersectWith and DiffWith compare with case and take no case flag. Partition cuts into groups of the count divided by n, rounded up.

sections.title: zip -- pair items from two lists
unzip -- split pairs into two lists
diff -- items in this but not in other
union -- all unique items from both lists

classes.name: stzListMover
classes.brief: Reorders the items of a list: moves one item to another position, swaps two, reverses, rotates, shuffles, or brings an item to either end.
classes.description: It is the reordering helper of stzList, which builds one over itself for its Move, Swap, MoveToStart, MoveToEnd and SwapFirstAndLast methods; build one with new stzListMover when you only need to reorder. It works on its own copy, so a stzList passed in is never changed, and you read the result with Content. A verb (Move, Swap, Reverse, RotateLeft, Shuffle ...) reorders the held list in place and returns nothing, its Q form returning the mover for chaining; the past-tense forms (Reversed, RotatedLeft, RotatedRight, Shuffled) return a reordered copy and leave the mover alone. Positions count from 1, and a position outside the list moves nothing and says nothing. Move and Swap accept the pair forms [ :From, 2 ] and [ :To, 5 ], [ :Between, 2 ] and [ :And, 3 ]. A rotation count larger than the list wraps around, and a negative one kills the Ring process today. Shuffle gives a different order on every call.
classes.example:
? @@( o1.Reversed() )
#--> [ "e", "d", "c", "b", "a" ]
? @@( o1.RotatedLeft(2) )
#--> [ "c", "d", "e", "a", "b" ]
o1.Move(1, 4)
? @@( o1.Content() )
#--> [ "b", "c", "d", "a", "e" ]
o1.Swap(1, 5)
? @@( o1.Content() )
#--> [ "e", "c", "d", "a", "b" ]
o1.MoveItemToStart("d")
? @@( o1.Content() )
#--> [ "d", "e", "c", "a", "b" ]
o2 = new stzListMover([ "שלום", "😀", "x" ])
o2.MoveToStart(3)
? @@( o2.Content() )
#--> [ "x", "שלום", "😀" ]

classes.name: stzListNamedParams
classes.brief: Asks whether a list is a named parameter, a pair such as [ :At, 3 ] whose first item is a keyword of the library.
classes.description: The library lets a caller pass a value with a keyword, as in Insert(x, [ :After, 2 ]), and each method tells the pair apart with a test. This class holds a list and carries more than 1,300 such tests, one per keyword, named Is<Keyword>NamedParam; they are generated or hand-written one- liners, and only the dozen hand-written ones are described here. For a new test, prefer IsANamedParam (is it any known pair) or IsOneOfTheseNamedParams over adding another method. Build one with new stzListNamedParams(aList) or over a stzList object. Ring keeps symbols in lowercase, so [ :At, 3 ] is stored as [ "at", 3 ]; the comparison ignores case.
classes.example:
? o1.IsANamedParam()
#--> 1
? o1.IsOneOfTheseNamedParams([ "At", "Before" ])
#--> 1
? o1.IsNNamedParam()
#--> 0
? o1.IsHashList()
#--> 0

sections.title: each call does an o(1) hash lookup in the zig engine.

methods.name: init
methods.brief: Builds a checker over a list or over a stzList object, to ask whether that list is a named parameter such as [ :At, 3 ].

parameters.name: pListOrObj
parameters.role: a list, or a stzList object, to be tested

warnings: any other kind of value raises "Can't create stzListNamedParams! Parameter must be a list or stzList object."

methods.name: Content
methods.brief: Returns the list under test, as it is stored.
notes: Ring stores the keyword symbols in lowercase: [ :At, 3 ] reads back as [ "at", 3 ]

methods.name: NumberOfItems
methods.brief: Returns how many items the list under test holds.
notes: a named parameter has exactly 2

methods.name: IsEmpty
methods.brief: TRUE if the list under test holds no item.

methods.name: Item
methods.brief: Returns the item at a position of the list under test, counted from 1.

parameters.name: n
parameters.role: the position, from 1

methods.name: IsHashList
methods.brief: TRUE if the list under test is a hash list, a list of [ key, value ] pairs such as [ :Width = 3 ].
notes: a lone named parameter [ :At, 3 ] is a pair, not a hash list, and answers FALSE

methods.name: ToStzHashList
methods.brief: Returns the list under test as a stzHashList, when it is a well-formed hash list.
warnings: raises "Can't create the stzHashList object! You must provide a well formed hashlist." for a list that is not one, such as the pair [ :At, 3 ]

methods.name: IsANamedParam
methods.section: each call does an o(1) hash lookup in the zig engine.
methods.brief: TRUE if the list is a named parameter: two items, the first a keyword the library knows.
notes: one engine lookup, so it is the fast test to prefer to the many Is...NamedParam methods

methods.name: IsNamedParamWith
methods.section: each call does an o(1) hash lookup in the zig engine.
methods.brief: TRUE if the list is the named parameter with the given keyword, the case ignored.

parameters.name: cKeyword
parameters.role: the keyword to test for, such as "At"

methods.returns: nothing today: it raises error R20
notes: use IsThisNamedParam(aList, cKeyword) instead
warnings: Raises error R20 "Calling function with extra number of parameters" today instead of TRUE or FALSE, whatever the keyword; the global IsThisNamedParam(aList, cKeyword) it relies on answers 1 for [ :N, 5 ] and "N" outside the class

classes.name: stzListOfBytes
classes.brief: Holds a run of raw bytes in a Ring text, and reads, cuts and converts it byte by byte.
classes.description: Positions and sizes count bytes, never characters, so a character of several bytes is several items here (Chars and the per-character methods are the exception). The bytes can be read as numbers, as hexadecimal, as Base64 or with percent escapes, and written back from those forms. Methods that change the object say so with a verb such as Clear, Trim or Update; the others return a new text. The name stzBytes is the same class.
classes.example:
? @@( o1.Bytecodes() )
#--> [ 72, 105, 33 ]
? o1.ToHex()
#--> 0x486921
? o1.ToBase64()
#--> SGkh
? o1.LeftNBytes(2)
#--> Hi

methods.name: init
methods.brief: Builds a list of bytes from a text, or from another list of bytes, keeping the raw bytes of the text.

parameters.name: pValue
parameters.role: a text, whose bytes are kept as they are, or a stzListOfBytes, whose bytes are copied

warnings: any other value, a number for instance, raises the error Can't create the stzListOfBytes object!

methods.name: Content
methods.brief: Returns the bytes one by one, each as a one-byte text.
methods.returns: a list of one-byte texts; a character of several bytes is cut into several items
notes: Value, ListOfBytes and Bytes are the same call

methods.name: Value
methods.brief: Returns the bytes one by one, each as a one-byte text.

methods.name: Copy
methods.brief: Returns a new, independent list of bytes holding the same bytes.
methods.returns: a stzListOfBytes; changing it leaves this one as it is

methods.name: ToString
methods.brief: Returns all the bytes as one text.

methods.name: ToStzString
methods.brief: Returns the bytes as a stzString, to use the string methods on them.

methods.name: InsertNBytesOfSubstringAt
methods.brief: Inserts the first bytes of a text before a position, changing the object.

parameters.name: nPosition
parameters.role: the byte position the new bytes go before, 1 being the first

parameters.name: _nBytes_
parameters.role: how many bytes of pcSubstr to insert

parameters.name: pcSubstr
parameters.role: the text the bytes are taken from

methods.returns: nothing; read ToString for the result
notes: a position past the end appends; a position of 0 or less inserts at the start

methods.name: LeftNBytes
methods.brief: Returns the first n bytes as a text.

parameters.name: n
parameters.role: how many bytes to take

methods.returns: a text; the whole content when n is larger
notes: NLeftBytes is the same call; the cut is by bytes, so a character of several bytes can be cut in the middle

methods.name: 3LeftBytes
methods.brief: Returns the first three bytes as a text.
methods.returns: a text; the whole content when it has fewer than three bytes
notes: Left3Bytes is the same call

methods.name: RightNBytes
methods.brief: Returns the last n bytes as a text.

parameters.name: n
parameters.role: how many bytes to take

methods.returns: a text; the whole content when n is larger
notes: NRightBytes is the same call

methods.name: 3RightBytes
methods.brief: Returns the last three bytes as a text.
methods.returns: a text; the whole content when it has fewer than three bytes
notes: Right3Bytes is the same call

methods.name: Clear
methods.brief: Removes every byte, leaving the list empty.

extensions.name: ClearQ
extensions.adds: does what the method does, then returns the object, so the call can be chained

methods.name: IsEmpty
methods.brief: TRUE if the list holds no byte.

methods.name: RemoveNBytesStartingAt
methods.brief: Removes a number of bytes from a position, changing the object.

parameters.name: nPosition
parameters.role: the byte position of the first byte removed

parameters.name: _nBytes_
parameters.role: how many bytes to remove, fewer if the end comes first

notes: a position outside the content changes nothing

extensions.name: RemoveNBytesStartingAtQ
extensions.adds: does what the method does, then returns the object, so the call can be chained

methods.name: RemoveNBytesFromEnd
methods.brief: Removes the last n bytes, changing the object.

parameters.name: n
parameters.role: how many bytes to remove

extensions.name: RemoveNBytesFromEndQ
extensions.adds: does what the method does, then returns the object, so the call can be chained

methods.name: Section
methods.brief: Returns the bytes from one position to another, both included, as a text.

parameters.name: n1
parameters.role: the byte position to start at, 1 being the first

parameters.name: n2
parameters.role: the byte position to end at

methods.returns: a text; bytes beyond the end are left out, and an empty text when n2 is before n1
notes: Range takes a start and a count

methods.name: ReplaceNBytes
methods.brief: Replaces some bytes at a position by the first bytes of another text, changing the object.

parameters.name: nBytesFromMainStr
parameters.role: how many bytes of the list to remove

parameters.name: nStartingAtPosition
parameters.role: the byte position the replacement starts at

parameters.name: nWithNBytes
parameters.role: how many bytes of pcFromSubstr to put in

parameters.name: pcFromSubstr
parameters.role: the text the new bytes are taken from

extensions.name: ReplaceNBytesQ
extensions.adds: does what the method does, then returns the object, so the call can be chained

methods.name: UnicodeOfNthByte
methods.brief: Returns the value of one byte, a number from 0 to 255.

parameters.name: n
parameters.role: the byte position, 1 being the first

methods.returns: a number; -1 when n is outside the content
notes: the name says Unicode but the number is the raw byte, not a code point; BytecodeOfNthByte is the same call

methods.name: Bytecodes
methods.brief: Returns the value of every byte, each a number from 0 to 255.
notes: Unicodes is the same call, with the same raw bytes

extensions.name: BytecodesQ
extensions.adds: does what the method does, then returns the object, so the call can be chained

extensions.name: UnicodesQ
extensions.adds: does what the method does, then returns the object, so the call can be chained

methods.name: Chars
methods.brief: Returns the characters of the text, each as a text of one or more bytes.
notes: the cut is by character and not by byte

extensions.name: CharsQ
extensions.adds: does what the method does, then returns the object, so the call can be chained

methods.name: BytecodesPerChar
methods.brief: Returns every character with the values of its bytes.
methods.returns: a list of [ character, list of numbers ] pairs
notes: UnicodesPerChar is the same call

methods.name: BytesPerChar
methods.brief: Returns every character with its bytes as one-byte texts.
methods.returns: a list of [ character, list of one-byte texts ] pairs
notes: the one-byte texts of a multibyte character are not valid characters and print as garbage; use BytecodesPerChar to read them

methods.name: BytesOfChar
methods.brief: Returns the bytes of a character as one-byte texts, if the list contains that character.

parameters.name: pcChar
parameters.role: the character to look for, as text

methods.returns: a list of one-byte texts; an empty list when the character is not in the content

methods.name: BytesOfThisChar
methods.brief: Returns the bytes of a given character, as one-byte texts, when the list holds that character.

parameters.name: pcChar
parameters.role: the character to look for, as text

methods.returns: a list of one-byte texts, 1 to 4 of them for one character; an empty list when the character is not in the content
notes: the same answer as BytesOfChar, under the longer spelling
warnings: anything but a text of exactly one character raises the error Incorrect param type! pcChar must be a char.

methods.name: NumberOfBytesInCharNumber
methods.brief: Returns how many bytes the character at a position takes.

parameters.name: n
parameters.role: the character position, 1 being the first

notes: NumberOfBytesInCharN is the same call; a position beyond the last character raises an error

methods.name: BytesOfCharNumber
methods.brief: Returns the bytes of the character at a position, as one-byte texts.

parameters.name: n
parameters.role: the character position, 1 being the first

notes: BytesOfNthChar and BytesOfCharN are the same call
warnings: a position beyond the last character raises the error Array Access (Index out of range)

methods.name: NumberOfBytes
methods.brief: Returns how many bytes the list holds.
notes: Size and SizeInBytes are the same call; the count is of bytes, so é counts for 2

methods.name: NumberOfBytesPerChar
methods.brief: Returns every character with the number of bytes it takes.
methods.returns: a list of [ character, number ] pairs

methods.name: NumberOfBytesInNthChar
methods.brief: Returns how many bytes the character at a position takes.

parameters.name: n
parameters.role: the character position, 1 being the first

warnings: a position beyond the last character raises the error Array Access (Index out of range)

methods.name: NumberOfBytesInChar
methods.brief: Returns how many bytes a given character takes in this list.

parameters.name: pcCaract
parameters.role: the character to look for, as text

methods.returns: a number; an empty text when the character is not in the list

methods.name: FillWithAsciiChar
methods.brief: Replaces every byte by one ASCII character, keeping the same size.

parameters.name: pcChar
parameters.role: the ASCII character to fill with

methods.returns: the new content, as a text
notes: the size stays the number of bytes the list had
warnings: a character that is not ASCII raises an error

methods.name: FillWithAsciiCharUpToNBytes
methods.brief: Replaces the content by one ASCII character repeated for a number of bytes.

parameters.name: pcChar
parameters.role: the ASCII character to repeat

parameters.name: _nBytes_
parameters.role: how many bytes the new content has

methods.returns: nothing; read ToString for the result

methods.name: FillWithAsciiCharUpToNChars
methods.brief: Replaces the content by one ASCII character repeated for a number of characters.

parameters.name: pcChar
parameters.role: the ASCII character to repeat

parameters.name: nChars
parameters.role: how many characters the new content has; an ASCII character is one byte, so this is also its size in bytes

methods.returns: nothing; read ToString for the result
notes: zero or a negative number empties the content
warnings: a character that is not ASCII, a text of several characters and an empty text raise an error, and so does a nChars that is not a number

methods.name: Resize
methods.brief: Cuts the content to n bytes, or pads it with zero bytes up to n, changing the object.

parameters.name: n
parameters.role: the new size, in bytes

methods.returns: nothing; read ToString for the result
notes: the padding bytes have the value 0

methods.name: Reserve
methods.brief: Does nothing: the bytes are not pre-allocated in this class.

parameters.name: n
parameters.role: the size that would be reserved, which is ignored

notes: kept so that code written for a byte array can call it

methods.name: ReleaseUnusedMemory
methods.brief: Does nothing: the bytes are held in a Ring text with no spare room.
notes: Squeeze is the same call

methods.name: Squeeze
methods.brief: Does nothing: the bytes are held in a Ring text with no spare room.

methods.name: SetWithtNumberInBase
methods.brief: Replaces the content by the digits of a number written in a base.

parameters.name: nNumber
parameters.role: the whole number to write, a negative one gets a leading -

parameters.name: nBase
parameters.role: the base, 2 to 36

methods.returns: nothing; read ToString for the result
notes: digits above 9 are lower-case letters; the name has the typo Witht

methods.name: SwapWith
methods.brief: Exchanges the bytes of this list with those of another list of bytes.

parameters.name: oOtherListOfBytes
parameters.role: the other stzListOfBytes, which receives this list's bytes

warnings: a value that is not a list of bytes raises an error saying it can not swap

methods.name: ToBase64
methods.brief: Returns the bytes written in Base64.
methods.returns: a text; an empty text for an empty list

methods.name: FromBase64
methods.brief: Replaces the content by the bytes a Base64 text stands for.

parameters.name: pcBase64String
parameters.role: the Base64 text to decode

methods.returns: nothing; read ToString for the result

methods.name: ToPercentEncoding
methods.brief: Returns the bytes written with a % escape for every byte that is not a letter, a digit or one of - _ . ~.

parameters.name: pcExcludedFromEncoding
parameters.role: meant to name characters left unescaped

parameters.name: pcIncludedInEncoding
parameters.role: meant to name characters escaped too

parameters.name: pcPercentAsciiChar
parameters.role: meant to name the escape character

notes: the escapes use upper-case hex digits
warnings: the three arguments are accepted and ignored: with - given as excluded, a given as included and # as escape character the answers did not change (tried three times)

methods.name: FromPercentEncoding
methods.brief: Replaces the content by the bytes a %-escaped text stands for.

parameters.name: pcPercentEncodedString
parameters.role: the text to decode, such as "a%20b"

parameters.name: pcPercentAsciiChar
parameters.role: meant to name the escape character, which is not used

notes: the escape character is always %

methods.name: ToHex
methods.brief: Returns the bytes as hexadecimal digits behind the prefix 0x.

classes.name: stzListOfEntities
classes.brief: Holds a list of entities, each a name with a type, such as apple/fruit, and answers questions about them by name and by type.
classes.description: An entity is a hashlist with a :name and a :type. AddEntity lowercases both and refuses a duplicate, AppendEntity adds without any check, and the finders answer positions (FindEntityByName, FindEntitiesByType) or the entities themselves (EntitiesOfType, FilterByTypeQ). The shared world registry that WhatIs reads is one such list, reached by WorldEntities(). AddEntity refuses too much: a new entity whose name and whose type are both already in the list is refused even when no single entity has both.
classes.example:
o1.AddEntity([ :name = "Pear", :type = "Fruit" ])
? @@( o1.Names() )
#--> [ "apple", "tesla", "pear" ]
? @@( o1.UniqueTypes() )
#--> [ "fruit", "company" ]
? o1.CountByType("fruit")
#--> 2
? @@( o1.FilterByTypeQ("fruit").Names() )
#--> [ "apple", "pear" ]

classes.name: stzListOfLists
classes.brief: Holds a non-empty list of lists and answers questions about its rows and columns, sizes, padding, sorting and column edits.
classes.description: A stzListOfLists wraps a Ring list whose every item is a list, the lists being allowed to differ in size. Reach for it to treat the lists as rows of a table without the weight of stzTable: take a column (NthColumn), pad the short rows (Extend, AdjustWith), cut them (Shrink, ShrinkTo), sort the rows on a column (SortOn), find an item inside the rows (FindManyInLists) or edit a column (InsertCol, ReplaceCol). Active forms change the lists in place, passive forms (the ones ending in ed) return a changed copy as a plain list of lists. Item searches are case-sensitive. Merge and Flatten always raise an error on purpose: use their passive forms, Merged and Flattened.

classes.name: stzListOfNamedObjects
classes.brief: Is meant to hold named objects and fetch one by name or position; it can not be built with a list today.
classes.description: Building it with a list raises R14, because init calls IsListOfNamedObjects on a stzList and that method does not exist, so Copy raises as well. A holder built without parentheses is empty; Content and Value return its empty list. NamedObject looks a name up and raises for an unknown one; its number branch tests the wrong variable and raises. stzNamedObjects is another name of it.
classes.example:
? len(o1.Content())
#--> 0

warnings: the check calls IsListOfNamedObjects on a stzList, a method that does not exist, so every list raises R14 Calling Method without definition: islistofnamedobjects (tried with an empty list and with one object); a value that is not a list raises Incorrect param type

notes: the name lookup is the only branch that can answer

classes.name: stzListOfNumbers
classes.brief: Holds a list of numbers and finds, ranks, compares, edits and sorts them, and answers sums, means and differences.
classes.description: A stzListOfNumbers wraps a Ring list that holds only numbers; building it from anything else raises an error. Reach for it when the question is about the numbers as a series: the smallest and largest (Min, Top3), the nearest to a value (Nearest), the steps between neighbours (Diff, Steps), the totals (Sum, Mean, Median), arithmetic on every number at once (AddToEach, MultiplyEachBy), filters (NumbersBetween) and sorting. Active forms change the list in place, passive forms (the ones ending in ed, or beginning with Each) return a changed copy. Rank methods such as Bottom3 and Top3 work on distinct values and answer in ascending order. The random picks draw from the list itself, every position equally likely, and raise when nothing qualifies.

classes.name: stzListOfObjects
classes.brief: Is meant to hold a list of objects as a list of its own; it can not be built with a list today.
classes.description: Building it with a list of objects raises R14, because init calls IsListOfObjects on a stzList and that method does not exist; Content returns nothing; and Copy raises. Only the holder built without parentheses, as StzListOfObjectsQ() does, can be made, and it is empty. The class is a sketch whose file begins with a TODO. stzObjects is another name of it.
classes.example:
? classname(o1)
#--> stzlistofobjects
? isString(o1.Content())
#--> 1

methods.name: init
methods.brief: Raises error R14 today instead of building a list of objects from the given list.

parameters.name: paoObjects
parameters.role: the list of objects meant to be held

notes: new stzListOfObjects without parentheses skips init and builds an empty holder, which is what StzListOfObjectsQ() returns
warnings: the type check calls IsListOfObjects on a stzList, a method that does not exist, so every list raises R14 Calling Method without definition: islistofobjects (tried with one object and with two); a value that is not a list raises Incorrect param type

methods.name: Content
methods.brief: Returns an empty text today instead of the list of objects, because the method names the list and does not return it.
warnings: the body is the bare name @aContent with no return, so the list is never handed back, even for a holder built without init

methods.name: Copy
methods.brief: Raises error today instead of returning a copy of the list: it calls Content, which returns nothing, and init then refuses it.
warnings: raises Incorrect param type! paoObjects must be a list of objects

classes.name: stzListOfPairs
classes.brief: Holds a list whose every item is a pair [ first, second ], and answers questions about the first items, the second items and the order of the pairs.
classes.description: Reach for it when the data is naturally two-column: sections [ start, end ], key and value, name and score. It orders the pairs by the first or the second item (Sort, SortOn), exchanges the items of every pair (SwapItems), lists the first and the second items apart and checks their types. Most mutators change the object in place and return nothing; the Sorted, Swapped and Stringified forms return a copy. One method is broken today: ToStzSetOfSections, which cannot succeed until stzSetOfSections is repaired; see its warning. The Reverse and Inverse families exchange the two items of each pair, they do not reverse the order of the pairs.

classes.name: stzListOfSections
classes.brief: Holds a list of [ start, end ] sections of positions and merges them: the included ones, the overlapping ones, or the touching ones.
classes.description: A section is a pair of positions, [ 3, 7 ] meaning the third to the seventh. Build the list with new stzListOfSections(aSections), or with StzListOfSectionsQ or StzSectionsQ; the string module also builds one internally to merge the sections it finds, and stzListOfPairs hands one back through ToStzListOfSections. The verbs (Merge, MergeIncluded, MergeOverlapping, MergeContiguous) change the held sections in place, the Q form returning the object for chaining. Three things found today. Merge, MergeIncluded and MergeOverlapping sort the sections first and leave side-by- side neighbours apart ([ 1, 5 ] and [ 6, 8 ] stay two), while MergeContiguous joins neighbours but does not sort, so an unsorted input loses sections. And the past-tense forms (Merged, SectionsMerged, IncludedSectionsMerged, OverLappedSectionsMerged, ContiguousSectionsMerged) also change the object, because Copy returns the object itself. The pvt methods are the private helpers of the merges and cannot be called from outside.

classes.name: stzListOfTexts
classes.brief: Holds a list of sentences or documents and selects among them by meaning: closest to a query, ranked for a query, or by sentiment.
classes.description: A list of texts is a list of strings that carries meaning, so it inherits everything of stzStringList (Content, NthString, Joined, ThatContain, Longest) and adds the natural layer. Build one with new stzListOfTexts(aList) or StzListOfTextsQ(aList); the sentence splitters of stzText answer a plain stzList, so wrap their result. Without a neural model the meaning methods fall back to word overlap, and the sentiment scorer reads English only; a model loaded through StzNeuralModelQ upgrades the similarity and ranking.
classes.receiver: o1 = new stzListOfTexts([ "The cat sat on the mat.", "I love this wonderful sunny day!", "This is terrible and I hate it." ])
classes.example:
? o1.MostSimilarByMeaning("a cat on a mat")
#--> The cat sat on the mat.
? @@( o1.ThatAre("positive") )
#--> [ "I love this wonderful sunny day!" ]
? o1.MostRelevantTo("wonderful day")
#--> I love this wonderful sunny day!

methods.name: MostSimilarByMeaning
methods.brief: Returns the text of the list closest in meaning to a query: by neural sentence embeddings when a model is loaded, else by shared words.

parameters.name: pcQuery
parameters.role: the sentence or phrase to compare with

methods.returns: a text; "" when the list is empty or the query is not a text
notes: the word-overlap fallback knows nothing of synonyms: "a cat on a mat" finds the cat sentence and "feline" would not; ties go to the earlier text

extensions.name: MostSimilarByMeaningQ
extensions.adds: does what the method does, then returns the object, so the call can be chained

methods.name: ThatAre
methods.brief: Returns the texts of the list whose sentiment is the given polarity.

parameters.name: pcPolarity
parameters.role: the sentiment label to keep: "positive", "negative" or "neutral", in any case

methods.returns: a list of texts, in their order; [ ] when none match or the polarity is not a text
warnings: the sentiment scorer is English (VADER): clearly positive French, Arabic and German sentences all come out neutral, so ThatAre("positive") finds none of them

extensions.name: ThatAreQ
extensions.adds: does what the method does, then returns the object, so the call can be chained

methods.name: RankedForQuery
methods.brief: Returns every text with its relevance score to a query, the most relevant first.

parameters.name: pcQuery
parameters.role: the question or keywords the texts are ranked for

methods.returns: a list of [ text, score ] pairs; [ ] for an empty list
notes: a cross-encoder is used when a reranker model is loaded, else lexical similarity, where texts sharing no word with the query all score 0

extensions.name: RankedForQueryQ
extensions.adds: does what the method does, then returns the object, so the call can be chained

extensions.name: RankedForQueryQQ
extensions.adds: chains on the next, more specific type of object (the Q ladder)

methods.name: MostRelevantTo
methods.brief: Returns the single text of the list best ranked for a query.

parameters.name: pcQuery
parameters.role: the question or keywords to rank for

methods.returns: a text; "" when the list is empty

methods.name: Copy
methods.brief: Returns an independent copy of the list that is still a list of texts, so its meaning methods stay available.

classes.name: stzListOfTimeLines
classes.brief: Holds several named lanes of events on one shared time axis, to ask what happens when across all of them.
classes.description: Build one with new stzListOfTimeLines([ :Lanes = [ ... ], :Start = ..., :End = ... ]); it is also reached as stzTimeLines, TimeLines(p) and StzTimeLinesQ(p). Each lane is a stzTimeLine over the shared bounds. Lane names are stored in upper case and every lookup ignores case, and the dates are read as text, a bare date meaning midnight. The lane management (AddLane, RemoveLane, Lanes, HasLane), the adding calls (AddPointToLane and its alias AddMomentToLane, AddPointsToLane, AddSpanToLane, AddPeriodToLane, AddSpansToLane, AddBlockedSpanToLane, AddBlockedPointToLane), the editing calls (RemovePointFromLane, RenameLabelInLane, BlockSpanInLane, BlockPointInLane) and the reads (WhatsAt, HasOverlapsInLane, CrossLaneOverlaps, UncoveredPeriodsPerLane, ToTimeLine, Content) all work on the lanes stored in the set. Lane(name) returns a copy of a lane's timeline, so editing that copy changes nothing in the set. Copy gives an independent set that keeps the lanes, the bounds, the points, the spans and the blocks. Show, ShowShort, ShowUncovered, ShowXT and VizFind return a text drawing of every lane under its name; they print nothing. Lane names of any script (Hebrew, Arabic, emoji) work.
classes.example:
? @@( o1.Lanes() )
#--> [ "TEAM A", "TEAM B" ]
? o1.Duration()
#--> 31449600
o1.AddPointToLane("team a", "Kickoff", "2026-02-01")
? @@( o1.WhatsAt("2026-02-01") )
#--> [ [ [ "lane", "TEAM A" ], [ "events", [ [ "KICKOFF", "point" ] ] ] ] ]
o2 = new stzListOfTimeLines([ :Lanes = [ "צוות", "فريق", "😀" ], :Start = "2026-01-01 08:00:00", :End = "2026-01-01 18:00:00" ])
o2.AddPointToLane("فريق", "اجتماع", "2026-01-01 09:30:00")
? o2.NumberOfLanes()
#--> 3
? o2.Duration()
#--> 36000

methods.name: init
methods.brief: Builds a set of parallel timelines, one lane per name, all sharing a start and an end.

parameters.name: p
parameters.role: a hash list with :Lanes = a list of lane names, :Start = the first moment and :End = the last moment (:From and :To also work), any other value, or a missing key, raises an error

methods.returns: nothing; the object is built with every lane empty
notes: lane names are stored in upper case, so Team A is read back as TEAM A, and every lookup ignores case; Hebrew, Arabic and emoji names work; the class is also reached as stzTimeLines, TimeLines(p) and StzTimeLinesQ(p)
warnings: a start or end that is only a time, or not a date, raises an error; a date without a time becomes midnight

methods.name: Content
methods.brief: Returns the whole set as data: the start, the end, the lane names and each lane's content.
methods.returns: a hash list with the keys start, end, lanes and timelines
notes: each timeline entry holds the lane name and that lane's start, end, points and spans; the keys read back in lower case

methods.name: WhatsAt
methods.brief: Returns, lane by lane, what happens at a given moment; a lane with nothing is left out.

methods.name: HasOverlapsInLane
methods.brief: TRUE if two spans of a lane overlap.

parameters.name: pcLane
parameters.role: the lane name

notes: it answers FALSE for a lane with no span, or whose spans do not overlap

methods.name: CrossLaneOverlaps
methods.brief: Returns the overlaps between spans of different lanes: the two lanes, the two labels and the overlap in seconds.
methods.returns: a list of rows [ [ lane, lane ], label, label, seconds ]; empty when no spans of two lanes overlap

methods.name: UncoveredPeriodsPerLane

notes: it reads the spans stored in the lanes (see AddSpanToLane)
warnings: a lane with no span at all answers an empty list, although all of it is uncovered; this is how the lane's timeline answers (see stzTimeLine UncoveredPeriods)

methods.returns: a text, empty when the set has no lane

warnings: a lane with no span at all is answered by that same sentence, although nothing covers it (the timeline's own answer)

notes: a label that no point carries changes nothing and raises nothing; the other lanes are not touched

parameters.role: the label to change, without regard to case

parameters.name: pcNewLabel
parameters.role: the new label, stored in upper case

notes: a label that nothing carries changes nothing and raises nothing; the other lanes are not touched

parameters.name: pcStrategy
