classes.name: stzMBarPlot
classes.brief: Draws several series of numbers over the same categories as grouped bars, with a legend.
classes.description: The data is a hash list of series, each series a hash list of category = number pairs, such as :Sales = [ :Q1 = 25, :Q2 = 35 ]. Categories come from the first series. ToString draws one cluster of bars per category with a different character for each series and a legend line; ToSVG and ToPNG draw coloured bars and a legend, with no values above the bars. It inherits the axis, label and size settings of stzBarPlot. The average line raises an error in every form, SetLegendLayout is obeyed only by ToStringInRing, and AddValues draws nothing in the text picture; see the warnings. Gallery: doc/gallery/stzMBarPlot/quarters.png (three series over four quarters), seen right by stzlib-docs visual pass (a model reading the PNG), 2026-10-05, not a person; twoseries.png (two series over six months), seen uncertain by the same pass because the legend touches the last bar; terminal.txt is the text picture, read as text and judged right. The pixel labels are in lower case, the text ones capitalised.
classes.example:
? o1.SeriesCount()
#--> 2
? @@( o1.Categories() )
#--> [ "q1", "q2" ]

methods.name: init
methods.brief: Builds a grouped bar plot from series of category = number pairs; raises an error for any other data.

parameters.name: paMultiSeriesData
parameters.role: The series, such as [ :Sales = [ :Q1 = 25, :Q2 = 35 ], :Costs = [ :Q1 = 15, :Q2 = 20 ] ]

notes: a series that is not a hash list raises "Each series must be a hashlist of category:value pairs" and a negative or non-number value raises "All values must be positive numbers"
warnings: Categories come from the first series only, so a later series with other category names is drawn under the first series' names

methods.name: ToCanvasQ
methods.brief: Draws the series as grouped bars with a legend on a new canvas and answers it, so the plot can become SVG or PNG.

parameters.name: paOptions
parameters.role: A list of options [ :Width = , :Height = , :Title = , :Font = an stzFont, :Color = , :Background = , :Grid = , :ShowAverage = , :Min = , :Max = ]

notes: the legend is always drawn, no values are written above the bars, and :ShowAverage = 1 adds an average line that the text picture cannot
warnings: Only the series names, the categories and the values carry over to pixels, so the legend switch, the bar characters, the spacing and the sizes set on this object do not

methods.name: ToSVG
methods.brief: Returns the grouped bars as SVG text, with no graphics device needed.

parameters.name: paOptions
parameters.role: A list of options [ :Width = , :Height = , :Title = , :Font = an stzFont, ... ], as for ToCanvasQ

methods.returns: the SVG document as a string
notes: the default size is 900 by 500 and text needs a Font

methods.name: ToPNG
methods.brief: Draws the grouped bars on the graphics device and returns the PNG bytes, writing them to a file when a path is given.

parameters.name: pcPath
parameters.role: The file to write, or an empty text to write none

parameters.name: paOptions
parameters.role: A list of options [ :Width = , :Height = , :Title = , :Font = an stzFont, ... ], as for ToCanvasQ

methods.returns: the PNG bytes as a string, empty when no device is available

methods.name: SetSeriesChars
methods.brief: Sets the character each series is drawn with, in series order; a series whose entry is not a single character keeps its own.

parameters.name: acChars
parameters.role: A list of single characters, one per series, the extra ones being ignored

notes: the defaults are the block characters, cycling after eight series and a non-list is ignored

methods.name: SetBarsChars
methods.brief: Sets the character each series is drawn with, under another name.

parameters.name: acChars
parameters.role: A list of single characters, one per series

methods.name: SetSeriesSpace
methods.brief: Sets how many blank columns separate the bars of one category.

parameters.name: n
parameters.role: The number of blank columns, raised to 0 when negative

notes: with 0 the bars of a category touch and the default is 1

methods.name: SetBarInterSpace
methods.brief: Sets how many blank columns separate the bars of one category, under the bar name.

parameters.name: n
parameters.role: The number of blank columns, raised to 0 when negative

methods.name: SetBarSpace
methods.brief: Sets how many blank columns separate the bars of one category, under a shorter name.

parameters.name: n
parameters.role: The number of blank columns, raised to 0 when negative

methods.name: SetInterBarSpace
methods.brief: Sets how many blank columns separate the bars of one category, in the other word order.

parameters.name: n
parameters.role: The number of blank columns, raised to 0 when negative

methods.name: SetCategorySpace
methods.brief: Sets how many blank columns separate one category's group of bars from the next.

parameters.name: n
parameters.role: The number of blank columns, raised to 1 when smaller

notes: the default is 2

methods.name: SetCategoryInterSpace
methods.brief: Sets how many blank columns separate one category's group of bars from the next, under the longer name.

parameters.name: n
parameters.role: The number of blank columns, raised to 1 when smaller

methods.name: SetLegend
methods.brief: Shows or hides the legend line that pairs each series' character with its name under the plot.

parameters.name: bShow
parameters.role: 1 to show the legend, 0 to hide it

notes: it is shown by default

methods.name: AddLegend
methods.brief: Shows the legend line that pairs each series' character with its name.

methods.name: SetLegendLayout
methods.brief: Chooses whether the legend runs along one line or down one line per series, but only ToStringInRing obeys.

parameters.name: cLayout
parameters.role: The layout, in lower case: "horizontal", "vertical" or "h", "v" (or the symbols :Horizontal and :Vertical)

notes: any other value raises "Incorrect legend layout value! Must be 'horizontal' or 'vertical'."
warnings: ToString and the pixel output always draw the legend on one line, and "Horizontal" or "H" with a capital raise the layout error

methods.name: SetAverage
methods.brief: Raises the error "Unsupported feature in the current version." instead of drawing an average line.

parameters.name: bShow
parameters.role: Ignored, since the call raises before reading it

methods.returns: nothing; it always raises an error
notes: the single-series plot has a working average line
warnings: Raises an error for every argument: the average line was never built for grouped bars

methods.name: SetAverageLine
methods.brief: Raises the error "Unsupported feature in the current version." instead of drawing an average line, under the Line name.

parameters.name: bShow
parameters.role: Ignored, since the call raises before reading it

methods.returns: nothing; it always raises an error
warnings: Raises an error for every argument

methods.name: AddAverage
methods.brief: Raises the error "Unsupported feature in the current version." instead of drawing an average line.
methods.returns: nothing; it always raises an error
warnings: Raises an error whatever the data

methods.name: AddAverageLine
methods.brief: Raises the error "Unsupported feature in the current version." instead of drawing an average line, under the Line name.
methods.returns: nothing; it always raises an error
warnings: Raises an error whatever the data

methods.name: ToString
methods.brief: Returns the grouped bars as text, one cluster per category, with the category names under them and the legend below.
notes: values and percentages are not drawn here even after AddValues, and the legend is always on one line
warnings: Raises an error when the engine cannot render the plot

methods.name: ToStringInRing
methods.brief: Returns the grouped bars as text drawn by the Ring code the engine renderer was ported from.
notes: it obeys SetLegendLayout, which ToString does not

methods.name: SeriesNames
methods.brief: Returns the name of each series, in order, as the keys were stored.
notes: the names come back in lower case and the picture capitalises them

methods.name: Categories
methods.brief: Returns the name of each category, taken from the first series.
notes: the names come back in lower case and the picture capitalises them

methods.name: SeriesData
methods.brief: Returns one record per series holding its name, its categories, its values and its drawing character.
methods.returns: a list of hash lists with the keys seriesname, categories, values and char

methods.name: SeriesCount
methods.brief: Returns how many series the plot holds.

methods.name: CategoryCount
methods.brief: Returns how many categories the plot holds.

classes.name: stzMemoryBlobStore
classes.brief: Stores binary objects by key in memory, with the same four verbs as the file store; it is gone when the process ends.
classes.description: It is a real store for the length of the process, and the service registry reports it as ephemeral so that a production check can refuse it. Keys follow the same rules as the file store: exact comparison, 1024 bytes at most, never empty. Each instance keeps its own objects.
classes.example:
o1.Save("a/1", "abc")
o1.Save("a/2", "de")
o1.Save("b/1", "f")
? o1.TotalBytes()
#--> 6
? @@( o1.KeysWithPrefix("a/") )
#--> [ "a/1", "a/2" ]
? o1.IsEphemeral()
#--> 1

methods.name: init
methods.brief: Builds an empty store that holds its objects in memory, numbered so that each store keeps its own.
notes: two stores never see each other's objects

methods.name: IsLocalReal
methods.brief: TRUE if the store is a genuine local equivalent of a real object store rather than a fake.
methods.returns: TRUE or FALSE; always TRUE for this class

methods.name: IsEphemeral
methods.brief: TRUE if the stored objects vanish when the process ends.
methods.returns: TRUE or FALSE; always TRUE for this class, which is why a production check flags it

methods.name: Save
methods.brief: Stores bytes under an object key, replacing the object when the key already exists.

parameters.name: pcKey
parameters.role: the object key, any text up to 1024 bytes

parameters.name: pcBytes
parameters.role: the content to store, as text

notes: SaveQ is the same call and returns the store; keys are compared exactly: "photo.jpg" and "Photo.JPG" are two objects
warnings: an empty key and a key over 1024 bytes raise an error

extensions.name: SaveQ
extensions.adds: does what the method does, then returns the object, so the call can be chained

methods.name: Fetch
methods.brief: Returns the bytes stored under a key.

parameters.name: pcKey
parameters.role: the object key to read

methods.returns: a text; the empty text when the key is absent, which Exists tells apart from a stored empty object
warnings: an empty key raises an error

methods.name: Exists
methods.brief: TRUE if an object is stored under the key.

parameters.name: pcKey
parameters.role: the object key to look for

warnings: an empty key raises an error

methods.name: Remove
methods.brief: Deletes the object stored under a key; deleting an absent key also succeeds, as an S3 DELETE does.

parameters.name: pcKey
parameters.role: the object key to delete

warnings: an empty key raises an error

extensions.name: RemoveQ
extensions.adds: does what the method does, then returns the object, so the call can be chained

methods.name: Size
methods.brief: Returns the number of bytes stored under a key.

parameters.name: pcKey
parameters.role: the object key to measure

methods.returns: a number; 0 when the key is absent
warnings: an empty key raises an error

methods.name: Keys
methods.brief: Returns the keys of the stored objects.
methods.returns: a list of text, in the order saved

methods.name: KeysWithPrefix
methods.brief: Returns the keys that begin with a prefix, the way an S3 listing by prefix does.

parameters.name: pcPrefix
parameters.role: the beginning the keys must have, compared with case

methods.returns: a list of text, in the order saved; [ ] when none matches

methods.name: NumberOfBlobs
methods.brief: Returns how many objects the store holds.

methods.name: IsEmpty
methods.brief: TRUE if the store holds no object.

methods.name: TotalBytes
methods.brief: Returns the sum of the sizes of all stored objects, in bytes.

methods.name: Clear
methods.brief: Deletes every object of this store, leaving other stores alone.

extensions.name: ClearQ
extensions.adds: does what the method does, then returns the object, so the call can be chained

methods.name: Show
methods.brief: Prints a one-line summary: how many objects and how many bytes, marked EPHEMERAL.

classes.name: stzMesh
classes.brief: Holds a piece of 3D geometry in the engine, a primitive, an OBJ file or your own vertex layout, and reports its counts and format.
classes.description: A mesh knows its own attribute layout and the pipeline that draws it is derived from that layout, so a new attribute needs no change in the renderer; Format is that layout made visible. A cube is 24 vertices and not 8, because a shared corner cannot carry three face normals. The mesh lives in the engine and is released with Free; after that its counts answer -1. Building a mesh draws nothing and opens no window.
classes.example:
? o1.VertexCount()
#--> 24
? o1.TriangleCount()
#--> 12
? o1.Format()
#--> 3,3,2
? o1.Stride()
#--> 8
o2 = new stzMesh([ :Sphere, 1.0, 8, 4 ])
? o2.VertexCount()
#--> 45
? o2.TriangleCount()
#--> 64
o1.Free()
? o1.IsAlive()
#--> 0

methods.name: init
methods.brief: Builds a mesh in the engine from a primitive, an OBJ text or a custom vertex layout, and keeps its handle.

parameters.name: pWhat
parameters.role: a kind as a symbol, :Cube, :Sphere, :Torus or :Plane, or a list such as [ :Cube, nSize ], [ :Sphere, nRadius, nSegments, nRings ], [ :Torus, nRingRadius, nTubeRadius, nSegments, nSides ], [ :Plane, nSize ], [ :Obj, cObjText ] or [ :Custom, aComponentCounts, aVertices, aIndices ]

notes: omitted numbers take defaults: size 1, sphere 24 segments and 12 rings, torus 0.35 tube radius, 64 segments and 32 sides; StzMeshQ and StzMeshFromObjQ build the same object
warnings: an empty list raises error stzMesh: nothing to build; an unknown kind raises error stzMesh: unknown kind ... use :Cube, :Sphere, :Torus, :Plane, :Obj or :Custom; an OBJ text with no v and f lines, or a custom layout whose vertex count does not divide evenly or whose index is out of range, raises an error saying the engine refused it

methods.name: Id_
methods.brief: Returns the engine handle of the mesh.
methods.returns: a number above 0, or 0 after Free

methods.name: Kind
methods.brief: Returns the kind the mesh was built as, in lower case.
methods.returns: the kind as text, such as cube, sphere, obj or custom

methods.name: IsAlive
methods.brief: TRUE if the engine still holds the mesh.
methods.returns: TRUE or FALSE, as 1 or 0; 0 after Free

methods.name: VertexCount
methods.brief: Returns how many vertices the mesh holds.
notes: a cube has 24, not 8, because a shared corner cannot carry three face normals; a sphere of 8 segments and 4 rings has (8 + 1) x (4 + 1) = 45

methods.name: IndexCount
methods.brief: Returns how many indices the mesh holds, three per triangle.
notes: a cube has 36

methods.name: TriangleCount
methods.brief: Returns how many triangles the mesh draws.
methods.returns: a number, the index count divided by three; a negative fraction after Free
notes: a cube has 12 and a plane 2

methods.name: AttributeCount
methods.brief: Returns how many attributes each vertex carries.
methods.returns: a number such as 3 for position, normal and texture coordinates; -1 after Free
notes: a custom layout of [ 3 ] has one

methods.name: Stride
methods.brief: Returns how many floats make up one vertex.
methods.returns: a number such as 8; -1 after Free
notes: the sum of the components in Format

methods.name: Format
methods.brief: Returns the vertex layout as text, the components of each attribute, from which the pipeline is built.
methods.returns: text such as 3,3,2 for position, normal and texture coordinates; an empty text after Free
notes: extending the mesh with an attribute extends this text and nothing else

methods.name: Free
methods.brief: Releases the mesh in the engine and zeroes the handle.
notes: freeing twice does nothing the second time

classes.name: stzMetric
classes.brief: Holds one named series of measurements, a counter, a gauge or a timer, and answers the questions that its kind allows.
classes.description: The kind is fixed at birth. A counter counts events (Increment, IncrementBy, Value, RatePerSecond); a gauge holds a sampled level (Set, Mean, Min, Max, SlopePerMs); a timer records durations in milliseconds (Record, RecordWatch, then P50, P95 and P99 from a bucketed histogram, ExactPercentile over the recent samples, and an exact SumMs and MeanMs). A call that belongs to another kind raises an error that names the right kind. The samples are kept in the engine, so a copy of a metric is a second face on the same samples: recording through either is read through both. PromText and OtelMetricJson render the metric in the Prometheus and OpenTelemetry formats. Free a metric with Destroy when done. Readings that depend on the clock, such as RatePerSecond and SlopePerMs, should be tested with ranges and signs, not exact values.
classes.example:
o1.Record(5).Record(15).Record(25)
? o1.Count()
#--> 3
? o1.SumMs()
#--> 45
? o1.MeanMs()
#--> 15
? o1.ExactPercentile(50)
#--> 15
? o1.P50()
#--> 20
o2 = StzMetric("app.requests", :Counter)
o2.Increment().IncrementBy(4)
? o2.Value()
#--> 5
? o2.RatePerSecond() >= 0
#--> 1

methods.name: init
methods.brief: Builds a named metric of one kind, :Counter, :Gauge or :Timer, whose samples live in the engine; any other kind raises an error.

parameters.name: pcName
parameters.role: the metric's name, such as app.requests

parameters.name: pcKind
parameters.role: the kind: :Counter, :Gauge or :Timer, matched without regard to case

notes: StzMetric(name, kind) is the usual way to build one; a copy of a metric shares the same samples
warnings: a kind that is not one of the three raises stzMetric: kind must be :Counter, :Gauge or :Timer

methods.name: Name
methods.brief: Returns the metric's name as given.

methods.name: Kind
methods.brief: Returns the metric's kind, in lower case.
methods.returns: the text counter, gauge or timer

methods.name: IsCounter
methods.brief: TRUE if the metric counts events.

methods.name: IsGauge
methods.brief: TRUE if the metric holds a sampled level.

methods.name: IsTimer
methods.brief: TRUE if the metric records durations.

methods.name: SetHelp
methods.brief: Sets the description that the Prometheus and OpenTelemetry outputs carry, and returns the metric.

parameters.name: pcText
parameters.role: the description, as text

methods.returns: the metric itself, so calls chain

methods.name: Help
methods.brief: Returns the description set with SetHelp.
methods.returns: a text; empty until one is set

methods.name: LabelPairs
methods.brief: Returns the label pairs of a metric that is a child of a family.
methods.returns: a list of [ name, value ] pairs; an empty list for a metric made on its own

methods.name: Increment
methods.brief: Adds one to a counter and returns the metric.
methods.returns: the metric itself, so calls chain
notes: each call is one sample on the counter's timeline
warnings: a gauge or a timer raises an error saying the call belongs to the counter kind

methods.name: IncrementBy
methods.brief: Adds a number to a counter and returns the metric.

parameters.name: n
parameters.role: how much to add

methods.returns: the metric itself, so calls chain
warnings: a gauge or a timer raises an error saying the call belongs to the counter kind

methods.name: RatePerSecond
methods.brief: Returns the counter's events per second over the retained samples, read from the slope of its own timeline.
methods.returns: a number, 0 or more; it depends on the clock, so test it with a range
notes: the rate is measured, never configured
warnings: a gauge or a timer raises an error saying the call belongs to the counter kind

methods.name: Set
methods.brief: Records a level on a gauge and returns the metric.

parameters.name: nValue
parameters.role: the level to record

methods.returns: the metric itself, so calls chain
notes: RecordGauge is the same call
warnings: a counter or a timer raises an error saying the call belongs to the gauge kind

methods.name: SlopePerMs
methods.brief: Returns the trend of a gauge, in units per millisecond, over the retained samples.
methods.returns: a number; positive for a rising gauge, negative for a falling one
notes: it depends on the clock, so test its sign, not its value
warnings: a counter or a timer raises an error saying the call belongs to the gauge kind

methods.name: Mean
methods.brief: Returns the mean of the retained samples of a gauge or a timer.
notes: a timer's lifetime mean is MeanMs
warnings: a counter raises an error and points to RatePerSecond

methods.name: Min
methods.brief: Returns the smallest retained sample.

methods.name: Max
methods.brief: Returns the largest retained sample.

methods.name: Record
methods.brief: Records a duration on a timer in milliseconds and returns the metric; on a gauge it records a level, as Set does.

parameters.name: nMs
parameters.role: the duration in milliseconds

methods.returns: the metric itself, so calls chain
warnings: a counter raises an error saying the call belongs to the timer kind

methods.name: RecordWatch
methods.brief: Records the reading of a stopwatch, running or stopped, as one duration and returns the metric.

parameters.name: poStopwatch
parameters.role: a stzStopwatch, as StzStopwatch() builds it

methods.returns: the metric itself, so calls chain

methods.name: P50
methods.brief: Returns the median duration of a timer as the upper bound of its histogram bucket.
methods.returns: a number in milliseconds, rounded up to a bucket bound
notes: with the samples 5, 15 and 25 it gave 20; ExactPercentile gives 15
warnings: a counter or a gauge raises an error saying the call belongs to the timer kind

methods.name: P95
methods.brief: Returns the 95th percentile duration of a timer as the upper bound of its histogram bucket.
methods.returns: a number in milliseconds, rounded up to a bucket bound
warnings: a counter or a gauge raises an error saying the call belongs to the timer kind

methods.name: P99
methods.brief: Returns the 99th percentile duration of a timer as the upper bound of its histogram bucket.
methods.returns: a number in milliseconds, rounded up to a bucket bound
warnings: a counter or a gauge raises an error saying the call belongs to the timer kind

methods.name: ExactPercentile
methods.brief: Returns the percentile of the recent samples of a timer, computed by sorting them, with no bucket rounding.

parameters.name: nP
parameters.role: the percentile, from 0 to 100

notes: only the last 1024 samples are kept
warnings: a counter or a gauge raises an error saying the call belongs to the timer kind

methods.name: SumMs
methods.brief: Returns the total of all the durations recorded on a timer since it was built.
warnings: a counter or a gauge raises an error saying the call belongs to the timer kind

methods.name: MeanMs
methods.brief: Returns the exact mean of all the durations recorded on a timer, and 0 before any.
notes: the sum is kept exactly; only the buckets are rounded
warnings: a counter or a gauge raises an error saying the call belongs to the timer kind

methods.name: Value
methods.brief: Returns the metric's current reading: a counter's total, a gauge's level, or a timer's last duration.
notes: Last is the same call

methods.name: Count
methods.brief: Returns how many samples were recorded on the metric.

methods.name: SeriesQ
methods.brief: Returns the series object that holds the metric's recent samples.

methods.name: Percentile
methods.brief: Returns the percentile of the recent samples, whatever the kind.

parameters.name: nP
parameters.role: the percentile, from 0 to 100

warnings: for a timer it is the same as ExactPercentile

methods.name: PromName
methods.brief: Returns the name in the Prometheus vocabulary, with dots and dashes folded to underscores.

methods.name: PromText
methods.brief: Returns the metric in the Prometheus exposition format: help line, type line and samples; a counter gets _total.
notes: a timer gives the quantiles 0.5, 0.95 and 0.99, then _sum and _count

methods.name: OtelMetricJson
methods.brief: Returns one OpenTelemetry metric as JSON text: a sum for a counter, a gauge, or a summary for a timer.
notes: the time stamp in it is the wall clock, so compare the rest

methods.name: Explain
methods.brief: Returns the metric's state as a list of plain lines: its total or level, its rate or trend, and its percentiles.

methods.name: Show
methods.brief: Prints the lines that Explain returns.
methods.returns: nothing; it writes to the console

methods.name: Destroy
methods.brief: Frees the engine handles of the metric and returns it; a later call builds fresh, empty ones.
methods.returns: the metric itself, so calls chain
notes: free every metric when done, since the engine holds the samples

classes.name: stzMetricFamily
classes.brief: Holds one metric name over declared labels, with one child metric for every combination of label values and a bound on how many.
classes.description: A family such as http.checkout.ms with labels route and method gives each combination its own child with its own percentiles: Child(["/menu", "GET"]).Record(12.5). The registry of children lives in the engine, so a child created after the server copied its monitor is reached by every copy. Cardinality is bounded by design: when the family is full, new label sets are routed to a reserved overflow child whose labels are all _overflow, so data is never dropped and a growing overflow bucket shows in the exposition. The overflow child takes one of the slots from birth, so HasOverflowed answers 1 for a new family. A family has no single value, mean or percentile: ask a child. PromText and OtelMetricJson write one metric with every child.
classes.example:
? o1.ChildCount()
#--> 3
? o1.Child([ "/menu", "GET" ]).Count()
#--> 2
? o1.Child([ "/pay", "POST" ]).Value()
#--> 48
? o1.Keys()[2]
#--> /menu|GET
? o1.PromName()
#--> http_checkout_ms
? o1.Kind()
#--> timer
? left(o1.PromText(), 6)
#--> # TYPE

methods.name: init
methods.brief: Builds a family of one metric name over declared labels, with an engine registry for its children and a reserved overflow child.

parameters.name: pcName
parameters.role: the metric name, such as http.checkout.ms

parameters.name: pcKind
parameters.role: Counter, Gauge or Timer, in any letter case

parameters.name: paLabelNames
parameters.role: the label names, a non-empty list of text

parameters.name: pnWindow
parameters.role: how many samples each child keeps, 1 or more, otherwise 1024

parameters.name: pnMaxChildren
parameters.role: the most children, overflow included, 2 or more, otherwise 64

methods.returns: nothing; the engine registry and the overflow child exist when the object is made
notes: StzMetricFamily builds it with window 1024 and at most 64 children, StzMetricFamilyXT sets both; the reserved overflow child uses one of the slots, so a family of at most 3 holds 2 label sets of its own
warnings: a kind other than counter, gauge or timer raises error stzMetricFamily: kind must be :Counter, :Gauge or :Timer; an empty list of label names raises error ... a family WITHOUT labels is a plain stzMetric

methods.name: Name
methods.brief: Returns the metric name.
methods.returns: the name as text, as given

methods.name: Kind
methods.brief: Returns the kind of every child.
methods.returns: counter, gauge or timer, in lower case

methods.name: IsFamily
methods.brief: TRUE if the object is a family rather than one metric.
notes: a stzMetric answers 0

methods.name: LabelNames
methods.brief: Returns the declared label names.
methods.returns: a list of text, in declared order

methods.name: MaxChildren
methods.brief: Returns the bound on the number of children.

methods.name: SetHelp
methods.brief: Sets the help text written in the exposition.

parameters.name: pcText
parameters.role: the description

methods.returns: the family itself, so calls chain

methods.name: Help
methods.brief: Returns the help text.
methods.returns: the text; an empty text until SetHelp is called

methods.name: Child
methods.brief: Returns the child metric for one combination of label values, creating it on first sight.

parameters.name: paValues
parameters.role: the label values, a list with one value for each label in declared order

methods.returns: a stzMetric that records for those values; a full family returns the overflow child instead of dropping data
notes: every call with the same values reaches the same engine stores, even from a copy of the family; once the family is full, new label sets all land in the child whose labels are all _overflow
warnings: a list of another length raises error stzMetricFamily ...: Child() takes N value(s), one per label

methods.name: ChildCount
methods.brief: Returns how many children the family holds.
methods.returns: a number; a new family already holds 1, the reserved overflow child
notes: the count is the engine's, so every copy of the family agrees

methods.name: Keys
methods.brief: Returns the keys of the children, in the order they were created.
methods.returns: a list of text, each the label values joined with a bar; the first is always the overflow key
notes: for labels route and method the key of GET on /menu is the two values joined by a bar

methods.name: HasOverflowed
methods.brief: TRUE if the overflow child exists.
methods.returns: TRUE or FALSE, as 1 or 0; 1 from the moment the family is built
notes: the intended meaning, that some label set was routed to overflow, is not what it tests
warnings: the overflow child is created when the family is built, so this answers 1 for a new family that has never overflowed, whatever its children: on a family of 3 holding two children of its own it answered 1 before any label set was refused; whether overflow data exists has to be read from the overflow child's own count

methods.name: Value
methods.brief: Refuses with an error telling you to pick a child, since a family has no single value.
methods.returns: nothing; it always raises error stzMetricFamily ...: a family has no single Value() -- pick a Child([...]) and ask it
notes: by design: a family never impersonates one metric

methods.name: Mean
methods.brief: Refuses with an error telling you to pick a child, since a family has no single mean.
methods.returns: nothing; it always raises error ... a family has no single Mean()
notes: by design

methods.name: Percentile
methods.brief: Refuses with an error telling you to pick a child, since a family has no single percentile.

parameters.name: nP
parameters.role: the percentile that was asked for, ignored

methods.returns: nothing; it always raises error ... a family has no single Percentile()
notes: by design; ask a child, whose Percentile reads its own samples

methods.name: PromName
methods.brief: Returns the metric name in a form Prometheus accepts.
methods.returns: the name as text with dots and dashes replaced by underscores, such as http_checkout_ms

methods.name: PromText
methods.brief: Returns the family in the Prometheus text format: one header, then every child's sample lines with its labels.
methods.returns: a multi-line text; a counter is named with _total, a gauge as it is, and a timer is a summary with quantile 0.5, 0.95 and 0.99 lines, a sum and a count for each child
notes: the overflow child is listed like any other, so a growing overflow bucket shows in the exposition; a help line is written only when SetHelp was called

methods.name: OtelMetricJson
methods.brief: Returns the family as one OpenTelemetry metric with one data point for each child, the labels as attributes.
notes: a counter is a sum, a gauge a gauge and a timer a summary

methods.name: Explain
methods.brief: Returns the family as lines of text: a header with the counts, then each child with its value and its sample count.
notes: the header reads Metric family name (:kind) over [labels] -- N child(ren), max M

methods.name: Show
methods.brief: Prints the explanation to the console, one line per line.
notes: it prints with the ? statement

methods.name: Destroy
methods.brief: Frees the engine registry and every child.
methods.returns: the family itself, so calls chain
notes: after it ChildCount answers 0 and the family must not be used again

classes.name: stzMicrophone
classes.brief: Records from an input device and hands back the recording as an ordinary stzSound.
classes.description: RecordFor records for a number of seconds in one call; StartRecording, Collect and StopRecording let you drive it and watch the level as it goes. Collect is not optional: the device fills a ring of about 250 ms and, if nobody drains it, the newest frames are dropped and counted as overruns, never written over unread audio. A machine with no input or no device library is a supported configuration and IsAvailable answers 0. For this reference the microphone was never opened and no device was queried, so the example uses only what touches none: the settings, the counters at rest and the refusals. Nothing was recorded or heard (UNPERCEIVED).
classes.example:
? o1.IsRecording()
#--> 0
? o1.SecondsRecorded()
#--> 0
? o1.FramesRecorded()
#--> 0
? o1.Overruns()
#--> 0
? o1.Collect()
#--> 0
o1.SetChannels(2)
o1.SetSampleRate(44100)
oNone = o1.StopRecording()
? o1.LastError()
#--> not recording

methods.name: init
methods.brief: Builds a recorder with one channel at 48000 hertz, noting whether the sound engine is loaded.
methods.returns: nothing; the object is built and no device is opened
notes: StzMicrophoneQ builds the same object; without the sound engine LastError says stz_sound.dll is not loaded

methods.name: IsAvailable
methods.brief: TRUE if there is an input to record with.
methods.returns: TRUE or FALSE, as 1 or 0; 0 on a machine with no input or no device library, a supported configuration
notes: CI machines answer 0
warnings: not run: it asks the operating system for its capture devices

methods.name: DeviceCount
methods.brief: Returns how many capture devices the machine has.
methods.returns: a number; 0 when there is no device library
warnings: not run: it asks the operating system for its capture devices

methods.name: DeviceName
methods.brief: Returns the name of the default input.
methods.returns: the name as text, which may be UTF-8 and not ASCII; an empty text when there is none
notes: one machine of the plane reported a French name
warnings: not run: it asks the operating system for its capture devices

methods.name: IsRecording
methods.brief: TRUE if a recording is running.
notes: 0 for a recorder that never started

methods.name: SecondsRecorded
methods.brief: Returns how many seconds have been collected so far.
methods.returns: a number of seconds; 0 when no recording exists
notes: frames divided by the sample rate; it grows only when Collect moves frames in

methods.name: FramesRecorded
methods.brief: Returns how many frames have been collected so far.
methods.returns: a number; 0 when no recording exists

methods.name: Overruns
methods.brief: Returns how many frames the device had to drop because nobody collected in time.
methods.returns: a number; 0 is the answer you want, and 0 when no device is open
notes: the ring holds about 250 ms; when full, the newest frames are dropped and counted, never written over unread audio

methods.name: LastError
methods.brief: Returns the reason of the last failure.
methods.returns: the reason as text; an empty text when nothing went wrong
notes: after StopRecording with nothing running it reads not recording

methods.name: SetChannels
methods.brief: Sets how many channels the next recording has.

parameters.name: pnChannels
parameters.role: the number of channels, 1 by default

methods.returns: nothing; the number is stored. SetChannelsQ returns the microphone for chaining
notes: it is not checked; set it before StartRecording

extensions.name: SetChannelsQ
extensions.adds: does what the method does, then returns the object, so the call can be chained

methods.name: SetSampleRate
methods.brief: Sets the sample rate the next recording is made at.

parameters.name: pnRate
parameters.role: the rate in hertz, 48000 by default

methods.returns: nothing; the number is stored. SetSampleRateQ returns the microphone for chaining
notes: it is not checked; set it before StartRecording, and SecondsRecorded divides by it

extensions.name: SetSampleRateQ
extensions.adds: does what the method does, then returns the object, so the call can be chained

methods.name: RecordFor
methods.brief: Records for a number of seconds, collecting as it goes, and returns the sound.

parameters.name: pnSeconds
parameters.role: how long to record, in seconds

methods.returns: a stzSound of what was recorded; an empty text when no recording could start or nothing was captured
notes: it waits in steps of 50 ms and collects at each, so the ring does not overflow
warnings: not run: it opens the input device and records

methods.name: StartRecording
methods.brief: Opens the input and starts filling a recording of a fixed maximum length.

parameters.name: pnMaxSeconds
parameters.role: the longest the recording can be, in seconds, which sizes its buffer up front

methods.returns: 1 when recording began; 0 with the reason in LastError when it is already recording, there is no capture device or the device refused
notes: the buffer is sized at the start because growing it during capture is the pause that costs frames
warnings: not run: it opens the input device

methods.name: Collect
methods.brief: Moves what the device has delivered into the recording; to be called often while recording.
methods.returns: the number of frames moved; 0 when no recording exists. CollectQ returns the microphone for chaining
notes: it is not optional: an undrained ring drops the newest frames and counts them as overruns

extensions.name: CollectQ
extensions.adds: does what the method does, then returns the object, so the call can be chained

methods.name: StopRecording
methods.brief: Stops the input, collects the last frames and returns the recording as a sound.
methods.returns: a stzSound; an empty text, with the error not recording, when nothing is running or nothing was captured
notes: the consumer stops before the ring is freed; an empty recording is reported as a failure and not as a buffer of zeros

methods.name: CancelRecording
methods.brief: Gives up on a recording and discards what was captured.
methods.returns: nothing; the device is closed and the recording freed
notes: calling it with nothing running does nothing

classes.name: stzModelPlan
classes.brief: Holds what the registry decided for a requirement: the implementation chosen, those rejected, and why.
classes.description: A plan is the registry's answer made readable. Chosen and Kind say what would run, Rejected lists every implementation turned down with its reason, and Why writes the whole explanation one line per fact. A plan can be a refusal, with an empty chosen id and findings, when a pin cannot be honoured or the requirement forbids settling for the floor. Making a plan runs nothing.
classes.receiver: o1 = StzFacultyQ("planpos")  o1.SetInputType(:text)  o1.SetOutputType(:number) o1.SetFloor("last", "StzFindLast")  o1 = StzModelRegistryQ().ResolveQ("planpos")
classes.example:
? o1.Chosen()
#--> last
? o1.Kind()
#--> floor
? o1.IsFloor()
#--> 1
? @@( o1.Rejected() )
#--> [ ]

methods.name: init
methods.brief: Wraps a plan produced by the registry so it can be read by name and explained.

parameters.name: paPlan
parameters.role: a plan as the registry returns it: a list of [ key, value ] pairs faculty, chosen, kind, why, rejected, floor, refusal, findings, pinned

notes: the plan is kept as a copy, so changing the list afterwards does not change the object
warnings: the list is not checked: an empty list is accepted and the readers then return empty values

methods.name: Data
methods.brief: Returns the plan as the list of [ key, value ] pairs it was built from.
methods.returns: a list of pairs: faculty, chosen, kind, why, rejected, floor, refusal, findings, pinned and needle

methods.name: Faculty
methods.brief: Returns the name of the faculty the plan is for.

methods.name: Chosen
methods.brief: Returns the id of the implementation the plan picked.
methods.returns: a text; an empty text when the plan is a refusal

methods.name: Kind
methods.brief: Returns which kind of implementation the plan picked.
methods.returns: a text: floor, model, dlm or service; an empty text for a refusal
notes: the registry picks a service only when it was pinned by name

methods.name: Floor
methods.brief: Returns the id of the faculty's floor, the fallback the plan keeps.
methods.returns: a text; an empty text when the faculty is unknown
notes: this is the floor's id and not its row: Floor of the faculty returns the row

methods.name: IsRefusal
methods.brief: TRUE if the plan is a refusal: nothing can answer, or a pin cannot be honoured, or the requirement forbids the floor.
notes: a refusal plan has an empty chosen id and its findings say why

methods.name: IsFloor
methods.brief: TRUE if the plan picked the faculty's floor, whether the registry fell back to it or it was pinned.

methods.name: Rejected
methods.brief: Returns each implementation the plan turned down, with the reason.
methods.returns: a list of [ id, reason ] pairs; [ ] when nothing was rejected
notes: reasons name the filter: not installed, not permissive, memory, language, determinism, unmeasured, not beating the floor, a lower rank, a service

methods.name: Findings
methods.brief: Returns the findings of a refusal plan, in the house shape.
methods.returns: a list of findings, each [ rule, subject, where, severity, message ]; [ ] when the plan is not a refusal

methods.name: Why
methods.brief: Returns the whole explanation: the choice, one line per reason, then each rejection and each finding.
methods.returns: a text with one line per fact, starting with the faculty and the chosen implementation or REFUSED
notes: the scores it quotes are measured by the registry on the golden set and are not judged by a person

classes.name: stzModelRegistry
classes.brief: Resolves a requirement to the implementation of a faculty that should run, from what was measured, and stores the measurements.
classes.description: The registry trusts only measurements: an implementation with none is unknown and never chosen, and a model is chosen only when its score strictly beats the measured floor on the faculty's golden set and reaches the requested quality. RunGoldens records those scores, SaveMeasurements and LoadMeasurements keep them in a text file, and a pin always overrides the registry. It is a handle on process-wide tables, so every object sees the same measurements. StzModelPolicy(:deterministic), or the environment STZ_MODELS=off, puts every faculty on its floor. Scores are computed by the class from the goldens; no person has judged the output of any model.
classes.example:
o2 = StzFacultyQ("regpos")
o2.SetInputType(:text)
o2.SetOutputType(:number)
o2.SetFloor("last", "StzFindLast")
o2.AddGolden("b", 2)
o2.AddImplementation([ :id = "first", :kind = "model", :fn = "StzFindFirst", :licence = "mit" ])
? o1.Resolve("regpos")[:chosen]
#--> last
StzRecordMeasurement("regpos", "last", "v1", 0.5, 2, 1, "")
StzRecordMeasurement("regpos", "first", "v1", 1, 2, 1, "")
? o1.Resolve("regpos")[:chosen]
#--> first
? o1.MeasurementOf("regpos", "first")[:score]
#--> 1

methods.name: init
methods.brief: Builds a handle on the process-wide registry of measurements; it holds no state of its own.
notes: every handle reads the same measurements, the same model trace and the same policy, so there is one registry per process

methods.name: Resolve
methods.brief: Resolves a requirement to the implementation that should run and returns the plan as data.

parameters.name: pReq
parameters.role: a faculty name, an stzRequirement, or the list its Data returns

methods.returns: a plan: a list of [ key, value ] pairs faculty, chosen, kind, why, rejected, floor, refusal, findings, pinned and needle
notes: a model is chosen only when its measured score strictly beats the floor's and reaches the requested quality, and the floor stays as the fallback; under StzModelPolicy(:deterministic) or STZ_MODELS=off every faculty resolves to its floor; ResolveQ returns the same plan as an stzModelPlan, ready to explain
warnings: an unknown faculty, or one with no floor, gives a plan with refusal 1 and its findings, not an error; with no measurement the floor is chosen, because an unmeasured model is unknown and never good

extensions.name: ResolveQ
extensions.adds: does what the method does, then returns the object, so the call can be chained

methods.name: Measurements
methods.brief: Returns every measurement recorded in the process, in the order recorded.
methods.returns: a list of rows, each a list of [ key, value ] pairs: faculty, impl, golden, score, n, conformance, date, note
notes: a new measurement of the same implementation on the same golden version replaces the old row and goes to the end

methods.name: MeasurementOf
methods.brief: Returns the measurement recorded for one implementation under the faculty's current golden version.

parameters.name: pcFaculty
parameters.role: the faculty's name

parameters.name: pcImpl
parameters.role: the id of the implementation

methods.returns: a row of [ key, value ] pairs faculty, impl, golden, score, n, conformance, date, note; [ ] when none
notes: score is the share of golden inputs whose answer the checker accepted, and conformance the share the court accepted: both are computed by the class, not judged by a person
warnings: an unknown faculty gives [ ] and not an error; after SetGoldenVersion the earlier rows are not found

methods.name: RunGoldens
methods.brief: Runs the faculty's golden set through every installed implementation, the floor first, and records the scores.

parameters.name: pcFaculty
parameters.role: the name of the faculty to measure

methods.returns: the rows recorded: one measurement per implementation run
notes: the floor is run first because its score is the bar a model must strictly beat
warnings: raises an error for an unknown faculty; a model whose file is not in the models directory is skipped and a service is never run; an answer that stated a probability also enters the calibration ledger; the golden loop writes the merged defaults back into the list it passes, so a faculty whose default params are not [ key, value ] pairs is scored on grown params; not exercised with a real model: the answer shape is read from the code

methods.name: RunGoldensFor
methods.brief: Measures the floor and the named implementations on the golden set and records the scores.

parameters.name: pcFaculty
parameters.role: the name of the faculty to measure

parameters.name: pacImplIds
parameters.role: the ids of the non-floor implementations to measure

methods.returns: the rows recorded: the floor and each named implementation that is installed
notes: the floor is always measured, because it is the bar; implementations not named keep their earlier rows
warnings: raises an error for an unknown faculty; ids that are not installed, and services, are skipped; not exercised with a real model: the answer shape is read from the code

methods.name: SaveMeasurements
methods.brief: Writes every measurement to a text file, one line per row after a header, overwriting the file.

parameters.name: pcPath
parameters.role: the file to write

notes: each line holds faculty, impl, golden, score, n, conformance, date and note separated by vertical bars, so a note containing a bar would not read back whole

methods.name: LoadMeasurements
methods.brief: Reads a file written by SaveMeasurements back into the registry and returns how many rows it took.

parameters.name: pcPath
parameters.role: the file to read

methods.returns: a number: the rows loaded; 0 for a missing file
notes: a row for an implementation already measured on the same golden version replaces it, the saved date is kept, and lines with fewer than six fields are skipped

classes.name: stzMultiObjectiveSolver
classes.brief: Looks for trade-offs between several objectives at once: a front of solutions none of which beats another on every objective.
classes.description: Declare variables and bounds, add two or more objectives with maximize and minimize (each call appends one), then call solve with nsga_ii, a seeded genetic search, or epsilon_constraint, which bounds the secondary objectives and solves for the first. The search is deterministic: the same seed gives the same front, and SetSeed changes it. NSGA-II refuses a problem that has constraints, and the epsilon-constraint method is only a rough tool today: its greedy sub-solver reads a lower bound as an upper bound, so the front repeats the same few points. exportParetoFrontCSV raises R41. Objective values of a maximize goal are stored negated, so smaller is always better inside the individuals.
classes.example:
o1.addVariable("x", 0, 10)
o1.maximize("x")
o1.maximize("-x")
o1.setNSGAParameters(8, 3, 0.1, 0.9)
o1.solve("nsga_ii")
? len(o1.paretoSolutions())
#--> 8
? o1.status()
#--> optimal
? o1.dominates([ :objectives = [ -2, -2 ] ], [ :objectives = [ -1, -1 ] ])
#--> 1

methods.name: init
methods.brief: Builds an empty multi-objective problem, with no variable, constraint or objective and the generator seed set to 42.

methods.name: clear
methods.brief: Empties the problem: variables, constraints, objectives, the front found so far and the status are dropped, and the seed returns to 42.
methods.returns: nothing; the problem is empty again
notes: the NSGA-II settings made with setNSGAParameters are kept

methods.name: addVariable
methods.brief: Adds a continuous variable with a lower and an upper bound, in declaration order.

parameters.name: varName
parameters.role: the variable's name, as text

parameters.name: lowerBound
parameters.role: the smallest value the variable may take

parameters.name: upperBound
parameters.role: the largest value it may take, never below the lower bound

methods.returns: the solver itself, so calls chain
warnings: all three arguments must be given (R19 otherwise); a name that is not text, bounds that are not numbers and an upper bound below the lower bound each raise an error

methods.name: addIntegerVariable
methods.brief: Adds a variable marked integer, with the same arguments and checks as a continuous one.

parameters.name: varName
parameters.role: the variable's name, as text

parameters.name: lowerBound
parameters.role: the smallest value the variable may take

parameters.name: upperBound
parameters.role: the largest value it may take

methods.returns: the solver itself, so calls chain
warnings: the genetic search floors the values it draws for such a variable, but the epsilon-constraint method does not enforce the mark

methods.name: addBinaryVariable
methods.brief: Adds a variable bounded between 0 and 1 and marked binary.

parameters.name: varName
parameters.role: the variable's name, as text

methods.returns: the solver itself, so calls chain

methods.name: Variables
methods.brief: Returns the declared variables in order, each as a list of name, lowerbound, upperbound and type pairs.
methods.returns: a list with one list of [ key, value ] pairs per variable; [ ] when none is declared
notes: the keys are lower case

methods.name: Vars
methods.brief: Returns the same list of declared variables as the longer accessor does.
methods.returns: a list with one list of [ key, value ] pairs per variable

methods.name: VariableNames
methods.brief: Returns the names of the declared variables, in declaration order.

methods.name: addConstraint
methods.brief: Adds one linear constraint: an expression such as "x + y", a comparison and a number.

parameters.name: expression
parameters.role: the left side, as text

parameters.name: operator
parameters.role: the comparison: "<=", ">=" or "="

parameters.name: value
parameters.role: the number the expression is compared with

methods.returns: the solver itself, so calls chain
warnings: a value that is not a number, even the text "5", raises an error; the NSGA-II method refuses to run when any constraint exists

methods.name: constraints
methods.brief: Returns the declared constraints in order, each as a list of expression, operator and value pairs.
methods.returns: a list of lists of [ key, value ] pairs; [ ] when none is declared

methods.name: addObjective
methods.brief: Appends one objective: an expression and the goal to maximize or minimize it.

parameters.name: expression
parameters.role: the objective, as text, such as "3*x + 2*y"

parameters.name: type
parameters.role: the goal: "maximize" or "minimize"

methods.returns: the solver itself, so calls chain
warnings: an expression that is not text, or any other goal, raises an error

methods.name: maximize
methods.brief: Appends an objective to make as large as possible; earlier objectives are kept.

parameters.name: expression
parameters.role: the objective, as text

methods.returns: the solver itself, so calls chain
notes: unlike the single-objective solver, calling it twice gives two objectives

methods.name: minimize
methods.brief: Appends an objective to make as small as possible; earlier objectives are kept.

parameters.name: expression
parameters.role: the objective, as text

methods.returns: the solver itself, so calls chain

methods.name: objectives
methods.brief: Returns the declared objectives in order, each as a list of expression and type pairs.
methods.returns: a list of lists of [ key, value ] pairs; [ ] when none is declared

methods.name: setNSGAParameters
methods.brief: Sets the population size, the number of generations and the mutation and crossover rates of the genetic search.

parameters.name: populationSize
parameters.role: how many individuals each generation holds, 50 by default

parameters.name: generations
parameters.role: how many generations to breed, 100 by default

parameters.name: mutationRate
parameters.role: the chance, from 0 to 1, that a variable is redrawn, 0.1 by default

parameters.name: crossoverRate
parameters.role: the chance, from 0 to 1, that a child takes a variable from the first parent, 0.9 by default

methods.returns: the solver itself, so calls chain
warnings: nothing is checked: any value is stored

methods.name: solve
methods.brief: Finds a set of trade-off solutions with the named method, "nsga_ii" (the default) or "epsilon_constraint", and keeps it.

parameters.name: cMethod
parameters.role: the method's name, an empty text selects nsga_ii

methods.returns: the solver itself, so calls chain
notes: maximize x and maximize -x on 0..10 with 8 individuals and 3 generations gives a front of 8, since no point beats another
warnings: the argument cannot be left out (R19), pass an empty text for the default; no variable, no objective, a single objective or an unknown method raise an error; the status becomes optimal in every case

methods.name: solveWithNSGAII
methods.brief: Returns the non-dominated individuals of a genetic search that breeds a seeded population for the set number of generations.
methods.returns: a list of individuals, each a list of solution, objectives, rank, crowdingdistance, dominatedsolutions and dominationcount pairs
notes: the same seed gives the same front (three runs agreed), and another seed gives another; the objectives of a maximize goal are stored negated
warnings: raises an error when the problem has any constraint, because the search does not enforce them; the front can hold several copies of one point; it is approximate

methods.name: solveWithEpsilonConstraint
methods.brief: Returns one solution per combination of bounds on the secondary objectives, each found by the greedy solver on the first objective.
methods.returns: a list of individuals, each a list of solution, objectives and rank pairs
notes: the iteration count is set to 10 per objective
warnings: the front collapses: for maximize x and maximize y with x + y <= 10 all eleven solutions are x = 10 and y = 0 (the true trade-off is the line x + y = 10), and with minimize x + y and maximize x - y most solutions repeat, because the greedy solver reads ">=" bounds as "<=" and always raises a variable to its maximum; only the first two secondary objectives are used

methods.name: initializePopulation
methods.brief: Returns the starting population: one random solution per individual, with no objective values yet.
methods.returns: a list of individuals, each a list of solution, objectives, rank and crowdingdistance pairs
notes: rank starts at 0 and objectives is empty

methods.name: SetSeed
methods.brief: Sets the state of the pseudo-random generator that drives the genetic search.

parameters.name: n
parameters.role: the starting state, a positive whole number, zero or less is replaced by 42 when numbers are drawn

methods.returns: the solver itself, so calls chain

methods.name: Seed
methods.brief: Returns the state of the pseudo-random generator, 42 until it is set or numbers are drawn.
notes: the state moves each time a number is drawn, so it differs after a run

methods.name: generateRandomSolution
methods.brief: Returns one random solution within the bounds, whole numbers for integer and binary variables.
methods.returns: a list of [ name, value ] pairs, one per variable
notes: continuous values come in steps of 0.01

methods.name: evaluateObjectives
methods.brief: Returns the value of every objective for a solution, with maximize goals negated so that smaller is always better.

parameters.name: _aSolution_
parameters.role: a list of [ name, value ] pairs

methods.returns: a list of numbers, one per objective
notes: x = 3 and y = 4 under maximize x, minimize x + y and maximize y gives -3, 7 and -4

methods.name: calculateObjectiveValue
methods.brief: Returns the value of an expression for a solution.

parameters.name: cExpression
parameters.role: the expression, as text

parameters.name: _aSolution_
parameters.role: a list of [ name, value ] pairs

notes: 3*x + 2*y with x = 3 and y = 4 gives 17

methods.name: nonDominatedSort
methods.brief: Returns the fronts of a population as lists of positions, and writes each individual's rank and domination data into the population itself.

parameters.name: _aPopulation_
parameters.role: a list of individuals, each with an objectives list, it is changed in place

methods.returns: a list of fronts, each a list of positions in the population, the last one empty
notes: three individuals with objectives (-1,-1), (-2,-2) and (-3,0) give the fronts [ [ 2, 3 ], [ 1 ], [ ] ] and the ranks 2, 1 and 1

methods.name: dominates
methods.brief: TRUE if the first individual is no worse than the second on every objective and better on at least one.

parameters.name: _individual1_
parameters.role: an individual with an objectives list

parameters.name: _individual2_
parameters.role: an individual with an objectives list

notes: objectives are compared as smaller is better; an individual never dominates itself

methods.name: calculateCrowdingDistance
methods.brief: Returns the population with a crowding distance set on each individual: 999999 at the ends of a front, the spread of its neighbours inside.

parameters.name: _aFronts_
parameters.role: the fronts returned by nonDominatedSort

parameters.name: _aPopulation_
parameters.role: the population those fronts index

methods.returns: the population, a list of individuals

methods.name: sortFrontByObjective
methods.brief: Returns the positions of a front ordered from the smallest to the largest value of one objective.

parameters.name: _front_
parameters.role: a list of positions in the population

parameters.name: objIndex
parameters.role: the number of the objective to sort by

parameters.name: _aPopulation_
parameters.role: the population the positions index

notes: the sort is a bubble sort

methods.name: createNewPopulation
methods.brief: Returns the next generation: one child per individual of the population size, made by tournament selection, crossover and mutation.

parameters.name: _aPopulation_
parameters.role: the current population, each individual with solution and objectives

methods.returns: a list of individuals with no objective values yet
warnings: with fewer than two usable individuals it prints a warning line and returns a fresh random population

methods.name: tournamentSelection
methods.brief: Returns the better of two distinct usable individuals drawn at random: the lower rank, or on a tie the larger crowding distance.

parameters.name: _aPopulation_
parameters.role: a list of individuals

methods.returns: an individual; [ ] when fewer than two individuals have a solution and objectives
notes: the draw uses the seeded generator

methods.name: crossover
methods.brief: Returns a child that takes each variable from the first parent with the crossover rate and from the second otherwise.

classes.name: stzMusic
classes.brief: Makes sound in one line from a string of note names, a phrase of degrees in a tradition, lyrics or live loops.
classes.description: It owns no mechanism: each verb is a line over stzSoundScore, stzSoundScoreRenderer, stzSoundScheduler, stzSoundUniverse and stzSoundLive. Tempo, With and Swing apply to the note- string verbs (Play, ToSound, ScoreOf); the phrase verbs take their speed and instrument from the chosen universe. Play, PlayPhrase and the live loops on a sound card open an audio device and were not run in this reference; ToSound, ScoreOf, PhraseToSound and Sing render to memory. Live().CaptureInsteadOfDevice(seconds, FALSE) keeps the live verbs off the sound card. The sound has not been heard by a person (UNPERCEIVED): it is checked by frame count, sample rate and peak level, not by listening.
classes.example:
o1.Tempo(90).With(:Oud)
? o1.ScoreOf("d e f g a").Beats()
#--> 5
? o1.ToSound("d e f g a").SampleRate()
#--> 48000
? o1.With(:kazoo).Refusals()
#--> 1

classes.name: stzNaiveBayes
classes.brief: Classifies a text from the words of labelled texts, with Laplace smoothing and a score for every label.
classes.description: Your labelled texts train it: no download and no model file. The model is multinomial naive Bayes over word counts, kept in the engine, which tokenizes by Unicode word segmentation and folds case, so text in any script is counted the same way. Classify returns the label with the highest log- score, and Why lists the score of every label so that the decision can be read. A text made of words never seen is decided by the label proportions alone.
classes.example:
o1.Train("great food and lovely staff", "positive")
o1.Train("cold soup, rude waiter", "negative")
o1.Train("lovely evening and great dishes", "positive")
? o1.Classify("lovely evening, great dishes")
#--> positive
? o1.Classify("rude cold waiter")
#--> negative
? o1.NumberOfDocuments()
#--> 3

methods.brief: Adds one labelled text to the model, counting its words under the label.

parameters.role: the document

parameters.name: pcLabel
parameters.role: its class, trimmed and folded to lower case

methods.returns: the classifier itself, so calls chain
notes: words are found by Unicode word segmentation and folded to lower case, so Hebrew, Arabic and CJK text work; an empty label is accepted as a label of its own

methods.name: Labels

classes.name: stzNaturalEngine
classes.brief: Reads a narration written in plain words, turns it into Ring code on a text, list or number, runs it and keeps what it understood.
classes.description: Build it with Naturally("..."), NaturallyIn(lang, "...") or NaturallyXT(context, "..."): the narration runs when the engine is built, so Result, Answers and Understood are ready at once. A narration creates an object (Create a string with 'ring'), applies methods (Uppercase it), asks questions (Is it lowercase ?) and may name objects (called basket, Use basket) or keep values (Keep it as sep). Execution is permissive: a word the language does not know degrades to data and is listed by Unresolved; SetStrict(1) turns that into an error, and SetAllowedOperations limits what may be said. A narration that creates no object raises Unsupported object type!. Understood paraphrases the reading back, Analyze checks a narration without running it, and SuggestNext offers the next words. Most roots are the internal steps of Execute (tokenising, resolving words, writing the code); the reader methods are Result, Answers, Understood, Unresolved, Tokens and Values. Only the English pack covers the full lexicon: other languages (ha, ar and more) understand the words of their pack.
classes.receiver: o1 = Naturally("Create a string with 'ring' Uppercase it")
classes.example:
? o1.Result()
#--> RING
? o1.Understood()
#--> create a string with ring -> uppercase
? Naturally("Create a string with 'ring' Is it lowercase ? Does it contain 'g' ?").AllYes()
#--> 1
? @@( o1.Analyze("Create a string with 'abc' Flibber it") )
#--> [ [ "understood", 0 ], [ "unresolved", [ [ "Flibber", "" ] ] ] ]

classes.name: stzNetwork
classes.brief: Holds the connection state shared by the library's network clients: the last request, the last error and the timeout.
classes.description: It is the base of stzHttpClient, stzTcpClient, stzTcpServer and stzWebSocket and keeps no socket itself. Its state is plain attributes: the address and status of the last recorded request, the last error text and code, and a timeout in seconds. The engine HTTP client is request-scoped, so IsConnected only says that a request has run. Subclasses override IsConnected to report an open socket. The class makes no request by itself.
classes.example:
? o1.Timeout()
#--> 30
o1.SetTimeout(5)
? o1.Timeout()
#--> 5
? o1.IsConnected()
#--> 0
? o1.HasError()
#--> 0

methods.name: init
methods.brief: Builds the base state of a network object: no request yet, no error and a 30-second timeout.

methods.name: IsConnected
methods.brief: TRUE if a request has been recorded; the engine HTTP client keeps no connection open between requests.

methods.name: IsSecure
methods.brief: TRUE if the last recorded request used https.
methods.returns: TRUE or FALSE; FALSE before any request

methods.name: ConnectionInfo
methods.brief: Returns the last recorded request: its address, its status code and the timeout in force.
methods.returns: a hash list [ :url, :response_code, :timeout_seconds ]; an empty list before any request

methods.name: LastError
methods.brief: Returns the text of the last error, empty when there is none.

methods.name: HasError
methods.brief: TRUE if an error text is held.

methods.name: ClearErrors
methods.brief: Forgets the last error text and code.
methods.returns: the object itself, so calls chain

methods.name: SetTimeout
methods.brief: Sets the timeout, in seconds, that ConnectionInfo reports and requests use.

parameters.name: nSeconds
parameters.role: the timeout in seconds

methods.returns: the object itself, so calls chain
notes: the value is not checked, so a negative or non-number value is kept as given

methods.name: Timeout
methods.brief: Returns the timeout in seconds; 30 by default.

classes.name: stzNetworkDiagram
classes.brief: Holds a network topology of typed devices, links and subnets, draws it top-down and checks its rules about addresses and wiring.
classes.description: A device is a cloud, firewall, router, switch, accesspoint, server or host, drawn as the trade draws it; a link is an undirected line; a subnet is a cluster with an IPv4 range. Reading back answers who is wired to whom, how many hops apart two devices are and whether one reaches the other. Five rules judge the topology through GovernanceFindings: every device is linked, addresses are unique, an address lies in its subnet's range, switches form no loop, and the internet enters through a firewall. Addresses are checked and not drawn. VLANs, routes and link speeds are not here. ToCanvasXT draws the diagram.
classes.receiver: o1 = new stzNetworkDiagram("office") o1.AddDevice("net", "Internet", :cloud) o1.AddDeviceXT("fw", "Firewall", :firewall, "10.0.0.1") o1.AddDeviceXT("sw", "Switch", :switch, "10.0.1.2") o1.AddDeviceXT("pc", "Desk PC", :host, "10.0.1.10") o1.Link("net", "fw") o1.Link("fw", "sw") o1.Link("sw", "pc") o1.AddSubnet("lan", "LAN", "10.0.1.0/24", [ "sw", "pc" ])
classes.example:
? o1.HopsBetween("net", "pc")
#--> 3
? @@( o1.NeighboursOf("sw") )
#--> [ "fw", "pc" ]
? o1.SubnetOf("pc")
#--> lan
? o1.CidrOf("lan")
#--> 10.0.1.0/24
? @@( o1.GovernanceFindings() )
#--> [ ]
o1.AddDevice("lone", "Lonely", :host)
? o1.IsReachable("net", "lone")
#--> 0
? o1.GovernanceFindings()[1][:rule]
#--> every_device_is_linked

methods.name: init
methods.brief: Builds an empty network topology that draws top-down with the network notation, under a title.

parameters.name: pcTitle
parameters.role: the title of the diagram

methods.brief: Declares a device of one of the seven kinds, drawn as the trade draws it with its name beneath.

parameters.name: pcName

parameters.name: pcKind

parameters.name: pcName

parameters.name: pacMembers

methods.name: AsRuleGraph
methods.brief: Returns the network projected onto a plain stzGraph that the rules read, with kind, address and subnet as node properties.
methods.returns: a stzGraph with one node per device and note, and one edge per pair of linked devices
notes: a pair linked in both orders makes two edges

methods.name: GovernanceFindings
methods.brief: Returns every finding of the five network rules, such as a lone device or a duplicated address.
methods.returns: a list of findings, each a hash list with rule, subject, where, severity and message; [ ] when there is none

methods.name: GovernanceIsSound

classes.name: stzNetworkRule
classes.brief: Holds one rule about a network topology, a stzGraphRule that belongs to the network domain.
classes.description: The five built-in network rules are stzNetworkRule objects made by stzNetworkRuleSet: every_device_is_linked, addresses_are_unique, address_in_its_subnet, switches_form_no_loop and the_edge_is_guarded. Build one yourself with a name, set its severity, message and checker like any stzGraphRule, and add it to a stzNetworkRuleSet.
classes.example:
? o1.Name()
#--> every_switch_named
? o1.Domain()
#--> network

methods.brief: Builds a network rule with the given name, in the network domain.

parameters.name: pcName
parameters.role: the name of the rule, such as addresses_are_unique

classes.name: stzNetworkRuleSet
classes.brief: Holds the five rules a network topology must keep and judges a graph made from a network diagram.
classes.description: The set carries every_device_is_linked, addresses_are_unique and address_in_its_subnet as errors, and switches_form_no_loop and the_edge_is_guarded as warnings, in the network-governance set of the network domain. stzNetworkDiagram builds one for GovernanceFindings and hands it the graph from AsRuleGraph; use the set directly to add a rule of your own before checking.
classes.example:
? o1.Name()
#--> network-governance
? o1.Domain()
#--> network
? len(o1.Rules())
#--> 5

methods.name: init
methods.brief: Builds the set of the five network rules, in the network-governance set.

classes.brief: Is the common base of the neural classes, which carries what they share: access to the vendored ggml backend.
classes.description: It is not meant to be built for its own sake; stzNeuralEngine and stzNeuralModel derive from it. It answers two questions every neural class depends on: which ggml build is linked, and whether the backend computes. The data-returning shortcuts StzGgmlVersion() and StzGgmlReady() do the same without an object.
classes.example:
? o1.GgmlReady()
#--> 1

methods.brief: Returns the build version of the vendored ggml library, the same for every neural class.

methods.name: GgmlReady
methods.brief: TRUE if the ggml backend is compiled in and runs a small tensor computation end to end.

classes.name: stzNeuralChat
classes.brief: Holds a multi-turn conversation with a loaded decoder model, processing the transcript once and appending each new turn to the cache.
classes.description: The first Say fills the cache with the system prompt and the user turn; each later Say appends only the new turn instead of re-reading the transcript. Sampling knobs (temperature, top-p, top-k, seed, token budget) set before a turn carry across the following turns. Text from the user is made safe before it enters the prompt, so a control token typed by the user cannot open a turn of its own. It needs a generative model loaded in the engine: with none, Say gives an empty text and records nothing.
classes.example:
? o1.NumberOfTurns()
#--> 0
? len(o1.History())
#--> 0
? o1.CachedTokens()
#--> 0

methods.name: init
methods.brief: Builds a chat session with a system prompt, or a default brief-answer prompt when none is given.

parameters.name: pcSystem
parameters.role: the system prompt that frames every answer

methods.name: SetTemperature
methods.brief: Sets the sampling temperature that later turns use; 0 is greedy and deterministic.

parameters.name: n
parameters.role: the temperature, from 0 upward

notes: the knobs carry across turns

methods.name: SetTopP
methods.brief: Sets the nucleus-sampling mass that later turns use.

parameters.name: n
parameters.role: the cumulative probability to sample from, up to 1

notes: the default is 0.95

methods.name: SetTopK
methods.brief: Sets how many of the likeliest tokens later turns sample from.

parameters.name: n
parameters.role: the number of candidate tokens

notes: the default is 40

methods.name: SetSeed
methods.brief: Sets the random seed, so that the same turn with the same knobs gives the same text.

parameters.name: n
parameters.role: the seed number

notes: the default is 42

methods.name: SetMaxTokens
methods.brief: Sets the most tokens a reply may hold.

parameters.name: n
parameters.role: the token budget of one reply

notes: the default is 96

methods.brief: Sends a user turn and returns the assistant reply, adding only the new turn to the cached conversation.

classes.name: stzNeuralEngine
classes.brief: Reports which inference backend is linked and whether it is ready, as a facade with no state.
classes.description: It is the first thing to ask before loading a model: IsReady (also IsAvailable) says whether the ggml backend runs, Backend names it and Content gives all of it as data, which Show prints. It loads no model and downloads nothing.
classes.example:
? o1.Backend()
#--> ggml (CPU)
? o1.IsReady()
#--> 1

methods.brief: Builds the facade over the inference backend; it holds no state.

methods.name: Backend
methods.brief: Returns the name of the inference backend that runs the models.

methods.name: Content
methods.brief: Returns a snapshot of what the engine is: its backend, its ggml version and whether it is ready.
methods.returns: a list of [ key, value ] pairs for backend, version and ready

methods.brief: Prints one line that shows the engine's backend, version and readiness.
methods.returns: the engine itself, so calls chain; it prints

classes.name: stzNeuralModel
classes.brief: Loads a neural model from a GGUF file at runtime and exposes its architecture, embeddings, token ids and, for a decoder, generation.
classes.description: The model goes into the engine single active slot, so the text-meaning layer and the similarity operations upgrade from lexical to semantic while one is loaded. A file loads only when its SHA-256 digest was recorded as trusted (StzTrustModel, or StzExpectModelDigest for one process): otherwise LoadFrom answers FALSE and LoadStatus says why. With all-MiniLM-L6-v2 loaded it reports arch bert, embedding width 384, 6 layers, 12 heads and a vocabulary of 30522; EmbeddingOf then returns a unit-length 384-number vector, and SemanticSimilarityBetween is the dot product of two of them. An embedding model cannot generate: Generate and AnswerTo give an empty text unless a decoder model such as SmolLM2 is loaded. Everything answers empty or 0 while no model is loaded.
classes.example:
? o1.IsLoaded()
#--> 0
? @@(o1.EmbeddingOf("hello"))
#--> [ ]

classes.name: stzNeuralNetwork
classes.brief: Holds a small feed-forward network of dense layers, with seeded weights, forward prediction and a GGUF export.
classes.description: A network is declared by its input width and grown layer by layer, each layer with relu, sigmoid, tanh, linear or softmax activation. Training is the job of stzTrainer, which learns in the engine and writes the layers back through AdoptLayers into this same object. ExportToGguf writes the parameters to a file.

o1.AddDenseLayer(3, :Tanh)
o1.AddDenseLayer(1, :Sigmoid)
? o1.NumberOfLayers()
#--> 2
? o1.Layers()[1][1]
#--> 3
? len(o1.Predict([0.5, -0.5]))
