classes.name: stzNode
classes.brief: A node is an operating-system process that listens for STZM messages on a TCP port and dispatches each one to a handler by tag.
classes.description: It holds one bounded inbox with a declared overflow policy that the engine enforces and counts. On(tag, f) declares a handler; a handler's value is returned only when the sender asked for a reply. A message with no handler is counted, never silent; a handler that raises kills the node, on purpose, so that a supervisor sees the exit. stz.stop is the built-in clean shutdown and stz.info makes the node report its identity, binding and counters. Signing and capability gates reuse stzRequestSigner and stzSystemActor. Constructing a node opens a listening port, and Run blocks: none of the networked methods were run for this documentation.

methods.name: init
methods.brief: Starts a node: a reactor that listens for STZM messages on a TCP port, under a name, ready to dispatch each message to a handler.

parameters.name: pcName
parameters.role: the node's name

parameters.name: pnPort
parameters.role: the port to listen on, 0 for any free port

notes: not run: it opens a listening port, which this documentation pass does not do
warnings: binds a TCP port when it is built

methods.name: Name_
methods.brief: Returns the node's name, in lower case and without any @host part.

methods.name: Port
methods.brief: Returns the port the node is actually bound to, which differs from the one asked for when 0 was given.
warnings: not run: it needs a node that is listening

methods.name: SetInbox
methods.brief: Declares the bounded inbox: at most nCap queued messages, and what to do with the next one when it is full.

parameters.name: nCap
parameters.role: the most messages the inbox may hold

parameters.name: cPolicy
parameters.role: the overflow policy, :DropOldest, :DropNewest or :Refuse

methods.returns: the node itself, so calls chain
notes: not run: it needs a node that is listening
warnings: call it before Run; every overflow is counted by the engine and never silent

methods.name: On
methods.brief: Declares the handler for a message tag; a handler's return value is sent back only when the sender asked for a reply.

parameters.name: pcTag
parameters.role: the tag of the messages to handle, matched without regard to case

parameters.name: pfHandler
parameters.role: a function that takes the message list [ tag, args... ] and returns the reply

methods.returns: the node itself, so calls chain
notes: run on a node built without a reactor, so only the registration was exercised
warnings: a handler that raises is not caught: the node dies loudly, on purpose, and its exit is visible from outside; a message with no handler is counted in Unhandled

methods.name: SecureWith
methods.brief: Makes the node verify signed messages against a signer's keyring.

parameters.name: poSigner
parameters.role: a stzRequestSigner holding the shared keyring

methods.returns: the node itself, so calls chain
notes: read from the code, not run: it needs a signer and a live node
warnings: a message that fails verification (bad signature, stale, replayed) is refused and counted in Rejected

methods.name: RequireSigned
methods.brief: Makes the node refuse every message that is not signed.

parameters.name: bYes
parameters.role: 1 to refuse unsigned messages, 0 to accept them

methods.returns: the node itself, so calls chain
notes: run on a node built without a reactor, so only the flag was exercised
warnings: a refused message is counted in Rejected, and an Ask gets a [ stz.denied, unsigned ] reply

methods.name: AddActor
methods.brief: Registers an actor identity, so the verified key id of a signed message names the actor whose capabilities gate the admitted tags.

parameters.name: poActor
parameters.role: a stzSystemActor, whose Name() is matched to the key id of the sender

methods.returns: the node itself, so calls chain
warnings: read from the code, not run

methods.name: Admit
methods.brief: Requires the sender's actor to hold a capability kind before the node serves a tag.

parameters.name: pcTag
parameters.role: the tag to protect, matched without regard to case

parameters.name: pcKind
parameters.role: the capability kind the actor must hold: effectful, sensing, compute or inference

methods.returns: the node itself, so calls chain
notes: run on a node built without a reactor, so only the registration was exercised
warnings: an unsigned sender or an unknown actor is denied; each denial is counted in Denied and, on an Ask, answered with [ stz.denied, capability ]

methods.name: Rejected
methods.brief: Returns how many messages were refused for authentication: a bad signature, a replay, or unsigned when signing is required.

methods.name: Denied
methods.brief: Returns how many messages were refused for lack of capability.

methods.name: Processed
methods.brief: Returns how many messages were handled, including the built-in stz.stop and stz.info.

methods.name: Unhandled
methods.brief: Returns how many messages were dropped because no handler matched their tag or because they did not unpack.

methods.name: Overflow
methods.brief: Returns how many messages the engine's bounded inbox dropped or refused for lack of room.
warnings: not run: it needs a node that is listening

methods.name: Pending
methods.brief: Returns how much unread data the node's server holds.
warnings: not run: it needs a node that is listening

methods.name: Run
methods.brief: Serves messages until stz.stop arrives, Stop is called or the time limit elapses, then stops the server and destroys the reactor.

parameters.name: nTtlMs
parameters.role: how long to serve at most, in milliseconds

notes: not run: it blocks on a live port; read from the code
warnings: blocks the process while it serves, and the node cannot be reused afterwards

methods.name: Stop
methods.brief: Asks a running node to finish after its current wait.
notes: run on a node built without a reactor, so only the flag was set
warnings: takes effect at the next 100 ms wait inside Run; it does not return the node

classes.name: stzNodeApp
classes.brief: Declares a whole node topology as data, then runs it as real supervised processes on one machine or moves a node to another host.
classes.description: Node() makes a node current and the fluent calls On, Requires, Boot, AtHost, AtPort and InboxOf apply to it. A handler is a Ring code string, because code-as-data can cross an OS-process boundary where a closure cannot. Describe() returns the declaration as plain lists and StzNodeAppFromDescription rebuilds an identical app from it. RunLocal starts every node as a child process under a stzNodeSupervisor, all on loopback; Deploy moves a node by changing one host. The declaration methods are pure data and were run; RunLocal, StopAll and the running case of Deploy start processes and open ports, and were not run.
classes.receiver: o1 = new stzNodeApp("shop") o1.Node("indexer") o1.On("embed", "return aMsg[2]") o1.AtPort(47001)
classes.example:
? o1.Name_()
#--> shop
? @@( o1.Describe() )
#--> [ "app", "shop", [ [ "node", "indexer", "", 47001, [ [ "embed", "return aMsg[2]" ] ], [ ], 0, "none", "" ] ], [ ], [ 5, 30000 ] ]
? o1.RestartsOf("indexer")
#--> -1

classes.name: stzNodeRegistry
classes.brief: Resolves node names to addresses and carries location-transparent Send and Ask, so the caller's code is the same whether a node is local or remote.
classes.description: Register a name with a host and a port; Send then hands a message over without waiting and Ask waits for a reply, with a mandatory time limit (a limit of 0 or less is refused, never an infinite wait). Delivery is at most once, unreachable and dead are the same status, down, and links are cached by name and re-dialed after a close. LastStatus says which outcome the last call had. The plane the bare Send, Ask and NodeRegister functions ride is the one returned by StzNodePlane(). The documentation run exercised only the calls that do not dial: unknown names and refused time limits.
classes.example:
? o1.Send("ghost", [ "warm" ])
#--> 0
? o1.LastStatus()
#--> unknown
o1.Ask("ghost", [ "x" ], 0)
? o1.LastStatus()
#--> badtimeout

methods.name: init
methods.brief: Creates a registry of node addresses with one reactor that will carry every link to them.

methods.name: LastStatus
methods.brief: Returns the outcome of the last Send or Ask: ok, timeout, down, unknown, badtimeout or denied, in lower case.
warnings: it reads ok on a new registry

methods.name: SecureWith
methods.brief: Makes the registry sign every outgoing message as a given key, so receivers can verify and refuse it.

parameters.name: poSigner
parameters.role: a stzRequestSigner holding the shared keyring

parameters.name: pcKeyId
parameters.role: the key id the messages are signed as

methods.returns: the registry itself, so calls chain
notes: the signer was a stand-in during the run: only the storing was exercised
warnings: a receiver that refuses a signed Ask is reported as the status denied

methods.name: Register
methods.brief: Declares where a named node lives; registering a name again moves it, and the cached link is dropped so the next call dials the new place.

parameters.name: pcName
parameters.role: the node's name, matched without regard to case

parameters.name: pcHost
parameters.role: the node's host or interface address

parameters.name: pnPort
parameters.role: the node's port

methods.returns: the registry itself, so calls chain
warnings: nothing connects here: the link is dialed on the first Send or Ask

methods.name: Send
methods.brief: Hands a message to a node without waiting for an answer, and answers whether it reached the wire.

parameters.name: pcAddr
parameters.role: the node's name, or name@host to override the host

parameters.name: pMsg
parameters.role: the message, a list [ tag, args... ]

methods.returns: 1 if handed to the wire, 0 when the node is unknown or unreachable
notes: run only with a name that is not registered, so no link was dialed
warnings: at most once, with no retry; LastStatus tells unknown from down

methods.name: Ask
methods.brief: Sends a message to a node and waits up to a time limit for the reply, which it returns.

parameters.name: pcAddr
parameters.role: the node's name, or name@host to override the host

parameters.name: pMsg
parameters.role: the message, a list [ tag, args... ]

parameters.name: nTimeoutMs
parameters.role: how long to wait, in milliseconds, which must be above 0

methods.returns: the reply value; an empty text on timeout, down, unknown, badtimeout or denied
notes: run only with a name that is not registered and with a refused limit, so no link was dialed
warnings: the limit is mandatory: 0 or less is refused with the status badtimeout and nothing is sent; delivery is at most once, so a timed-out Ask may still have been handled, and its late reply is dropped by correlation id

methods.brief: Closes every cached link; the registered names stay and the next call dials again.
methods.returns: the registry itself, so calls chain

methods.name: Destroy
methods.brief: Closes every link and destroys the registry's reactor.
warnings: the registry cannot be used afterwards

classes.name: stzNodeSupervisor
classes.brief: Supervises node processes by declaration: it restarts the dead under a strategy and a budget, and escalates instead of looping.
classes.description: Declare children with Child, then the Strategy (:OneForOne or :AllForOne), the RestartBudget and optionally a Heartbeat and Monitor subscriptions. A death is a process exit or, with heartbeats on, a silent node. Each restart is counted per child and in a sliding window; beyond the budget the supervisor stops, reports through Escalated and EscalationReason, and leaves the child down. It keeps the house contract Name_() and Cycle(), so it can be hosted on an agent host. StartAll spawns real processes; the documentation run declared children and called the read methods only.

classes.example:
? o1.Escalated()
#--> 0
? o1.RestartsOf("indexer")
#--> 0
? o1.RestartsOf("nobody")
#--> -1
o1.Destroy()

parameters.name: pcChildName

parameters.name: pcSubscriberAddr
parameters.role: the node address that receives the notice

methods.returns: the supervisor itself, so calls chain

methods.name: EscalationReason

methods.brief: Returns how many times a child was restarted; -1 for an unknown name.

parameters.name: pcName

methods.name: TotalRestarts
methods.brief: Returns the restarts of all children added together.

methods.name: JobOf
methods.brief: Returns the spawn job number of a child's current process, 0 when it is not running or unknown.

parameters.name: pcName
parameters.role: the child's name, matched without regard to case

methods.name: StartAll
methods.brief: Spawns the process of every declared child and registers each name on the node plane.
methods.returns: the supervisor itself, so calls chain
notes: not run: it starts child processes
warnings: spawns operating-system processes and registers them on the node plane

methods.name: Cycle
methods.brief: Runs one supervision tick: finds dead children, notifies monitors, and restarts them under the strategy and the budget.
methods.returns: the supervisor itself, so calls chain
notes: run only while no child was started, where it does nothing
warnings: it never waits and never loops: past the budget it escalates and stops restarting

methods.name: StopAll
methods.brief: Kills every running child process and forgets their jobs.
methods.returns: the supervisor itself, so calls chain
notes: run only while no child was started, where it does nothing
warnings: kills processes

methods.name: Destroy
methods.brief: Stops every child and destroys the supervisor's reactor.
warnings: the supervisor cannot be used afterwards

classes.name: stzNotation
classes.brief: Declares a diagram domain as data: its node kinds and glyphs, its colours, its well-formedness rules and its layout grammar.
classes.description: A notation is a profile over the one diagram foundation, not a second renderer. It declares a vocabulary of kinds with a glyph, a fill and a scale each (AddKind, AddKindXT, AddKindXTT), closes it when unknown kinds must be findings (Close), adds rules by the name of a check (Forbid for SelfLink, SecondParent and Cycle, ForbidFor for Inbound and Outbound on one kind), and amends the grammar: direction, routing, arrowheads, one ink, layout mode, where names are written. Check sweeps a diagram against the rules in the house rule shape [ :rule, :subject, :where, :severity, :message ]; MayLink answers the same rules for one link, so an editor can refuse it at the gesture. StzRegisterNotation puts a profile in the registry, StzNotation(name) fetches it, and a diagram takes one with SetNotation. A name that is not registered gives the default profile, not an error. SetNameInside, SetNameOutside, SetPeerChildren and SetBranchSide return nothing, so a chain stops at them. A picture of a diagram under a notation needs a font passed to ToPNGXT; without one no label is drawn. Picture: a start, two states and an end drawn under a closed machine profile with LeftRight showed a small green start dot, two blue rounded boxes named Idle and Running, a small red end dot, and arrows left to right; the return arrow from Running to Idle had no arrowhead in the box glyphs (notation_machine.png).
classes.receiver: o1 = new stzNotation("machine"); o1.AddKindXT("state", "rounded", "Info.Solid"); o1.AddKind("start", "circle"); o1.AddKind("end", "circle"); o1.ForbidFor("end", :Outbound, "nothing leaves the end")
classes.example:
? @@( o1.Kinds() )
#--> [ "state", "start", "end" ]
? o1.GlyphOf("state")
#--> rounded
? @@( o1.SinkKinds() )
#--> [ "end" ]

methods.name: Forbid

parameters.name: pcWhat

parameters.name: pcMessage
parameters.role: the text reported as the finding and given as the reason for a refused link

methods.returns: the notation itself, so calls chain
notes: SelfLink forbids an edge from a node to itself, SecondParent a node with two incoming edges and Cycle an edge that closes a loop
warnings: a name that is not one of the three checks is stored and never used, with no error; the first rule of a name answers when it is repeated

extensions.name: ForbidQ
extensions.adds: does what the method does, then returns the object, so the call can be chained

methods.name: Rules

methods.name: ForbidFor
methods.brief: Adds a rule that belongs to one kind: nothing may enter a kind, or nothing may leave it.

parameters.name: pcKind
parameters.role: the node kind the rule is about

parameters.name: pcWhat
parameters.role: Inbound to forbid edges into the kind, or Outbound to forbid edges out of it

parameters.name: pcMessage
parameters.role: the text reported when the rule is broken

methods.returns: the notation itself, so calls chain

extensions.name: ForbidForQ
extensions.adds: does what the method does, then returns the object, so the call can be chained

methods.name: MayLink
methods.brief: TRUE if an edge from one node to another is allowed by the rules, so an editor can refuse the link before it is made.

parameters.role: the diagram the link would join, or an empty text to test the self-link rule alone

parameters.name: pcFrom
parameters.role: the id of the source node

parameters.name: pcTo
parameters.role: the id of the target node

methods.name: Check

parameters.name: poDiagram
parameters.role: the diagram to check

methods.returns: a list of rows [ :rule, :subject, :where, :severity, :message ]; empty when nothing is wrong or when the argument is not an object

classes.name: stzNullObject

classes.name: stzNumbrex
classes.brief: Tests whole numbers against a small pattern language that describes number structure, such as prime, three digits or a multiple of five.
classes.description: A pattern is written in braces and made of tokens: @Property(Prime), @Digit3 or @Digit(1..5)+, @Factor4, @Relation(Mod:5=0), @Approx(~3.14), @Part(Integer), @Divisor(3) and @Multiple(4). Tokens are joined by -> or & (all must hold) or by a vertical bar (any may hold), and @! negates one. Match answers TRUE or FALSE for a number and, on success, records its digits, factors and properties for Digits, Factors and Properties. MatchingNumberAfter, MatchingNumbersBetween and CountMatchingBetween search for numbers instead of testing one. A digit or factor token with no quantifier means exactly one digit or one factor, so write @Digit3, not @Digit. Several things do not work as the grammar suggests today: a pattern with no readable token matches every number, @Digit(7) can never match, and @Factor(prime) can never match; each is flagged in its entry. The parser steps (NormalizePattern, ParsePattern, the Parse and Check methods) are internal and are listed for completeness.
classes.example:
? o1.Match(17)
#--> 1
? o1.Match(18)
#--> 0
? @@( o1.MatchingNumbersBetween(1, 20) )
#--> [ 2, 3, 5, 7, 11, 13, 17, 19 ]
? o1.MatchingNumberAfter(14)
#--> 17

classes.name: stzNumBuffer
classes.brief: Holds numbers inside the engine so that bulk passes and reductions cross the Ring boundary once, not once per call.
classes.description: It is the number helper of stzListOfNumbers (ToStzNumBuffer brings a list in, ToStzListOfNumbers takes it back): the engine copy is the truth and Ring only holds a handle. Build one with StzNumBufferQ over a list, StzNumBufferOfSizeQ for zeros, or StzNumBufferRangeQ for a sequence. Writes (Scale, AddScalar, FillWith, RangeFrom, SetItem and the buffer-with-buffer verbs) change the buffer in place and return it, so calls chain; reductions (Sum, Mean, Min, Max, Dot, the variances) return a number and marshal nothing; ToList materialises a view when you want to look. Values are f64, Sum is compensated, and the variances name their convention (sample divides by n-1, population by n). Ring has no destructors: call Free on a large buffer when done. Found today: Item, SetItem and Resize with a negative number end the Ring process, an out-of-range positive Item answers 0, Dot of two lengths answers 0 where the other buffer verbs raise, and the reductions of an empty buffer answer 0.

methods.name: init
methods.brief: Builds a buffer of numbers held inside the engine, from a list of numbers or from a size.

parameters.name: pInput
parameters.role: a list of numbers, copied into the engine, or a number n for a buffer of n zeros

notes: stzListOfNumbers.ToStzNumBuffer brings a list in; StzNumBufferQ, StzNumBufferOfSizeQ and StzNumBufferRangeQ build one; the values are f64
warnings: the engine memory is held until Free is called: Ring has no destructors

methods.name: Handle
methods.brief: Returns the engine handle of the buffer, a number.
notes: other buffers read it for AddBuffer, SubtractBuffer, MultiplyBuffer and Dot

methods.name: Free
methods.brief: Releases the engine memory of the buffer.
notes: call it when done with a large buffer; calling it twice is harmless; do not read the buffer afterwards

methods.name: IsFreed
methods.brief: TRUE if the buffer has been freed.

methods.brief: Replaces the buffer by a new one of the given size filled with zeros, losing the numbers it held.

parameters.name: pnSize
parameters.role: the new number of items

methods.returns: the buffer itself, so calls chain
notes: the old memory is freed first
warnings: a negative size ends the Ring process: it panics inside stz_stats.dll with exit code 3

methods.name: NumberOfItems
methods.brief: Returns how many numbers the buffer holds.
notes: Size and Count are the same call

methods.name: IsEmpty
methods.brief: TRUE if the buffer holds no number.

classes.name: stzObject
classes.brief: Holds one value and gives every class of the library its common ground: naming, identity, kind tests, natural chains and constraints.
classes.description: stzObject is the ancestor of every class of the library. A stzString, a stzList, a stzNumber and every other class inherits from it, without writing a line, the questions about what an object is (IsA, Is, IsEitherA, IsOneOfTheseTypes), a variable name and a unique identifier (SetVarName, SetUuid), the self-description that answers plain-English questions about the class (Ask, ExplainMethod, HowTo, DoIntent), the grammar words of natural chains (Only, Exactly, AtLeast, AtMost, MoreThan, LessThan, About, IfSo, Otherwise, and the filler words such as Which or Their that change nothing), constraints that can be declared, verified and enforced at the update point (AddConstraint, EnforceConstraint), a recorded past that tense words can ask about (WasEver, UsedToBe, IsStill), and converters to the other classes (ToStzString, ToStzList, ToStzNumber). Several families here are overridden by the subclasses that know better, so for a stzString the answer to IsAString, Content, Repeat or IsEqualTo comes from stzString, and the version of this class is the one a bare stzObject, a stzNumber or a class with no override of its own runs. A bare stzObject wraps an object, or the global variable whose name is given as text. Some methods of the class raise today and are said so in their blocks: Values, AttributesAndValues, ToPointer, IsListOrString, WhichAreBoth, the time-value family, the OccursForThe...Time family and several of the Of... forms.
classes.example:
? o1.IsA(:String)
#--> 1
o1.SetVarName("oFruit")
? o1.VarName()
#--> oFruit
o1.AddConstraint("lower", :Lowercase)
? o1.VerifyConstraint("lower")
#--> 1
? Q("AnnIE").AtLeast(2).VowelNB()
#--> 1

methods.name: init

classes.name: stzObjectGuard
classes.brief: Answers a whole-object condition after a type guard such as IsAPairQ has passed.
classes.description: A passing type guard returns this guard instead of a true value, so that Where can test a condition against the whole object once: in o.IsAPairQ().Where('isString(@pair[1]) and isNumber(@pair[2])') the keyword @pair stands for the pair itself, not for each of its items. A failing guard returns a stzFalseObject whose Where answers 0. Content and Value give back the guarded object's content, and Object the object.
classes.example:
? o1.Where('isString(@pair[1]) and isNumber(@pair[2])')
#--> 1
? o1.Where('@pair[2] > 10')
#--> 0

methods.name: init
methods.brief: Wraps an object and the name of the whole-object keyword its condition may use.

parameters.name: poObj
parameters.role: the object to guard, such as a stzList

parameters.name: pcKeyword
parameters.role: the keyword name, such as @pair, kept for Keyword

methods.name: Content
methods.brief: Returns the content of the guarded object.
methods.returns: whatever the guarded object's Content returns

methods.name: Object
methods.brief: Returns the guarded object itself, not its content.

methods.name: Keyword
methods.brief: Returns the keyword the guard was built with, as the type guard wrote it.

methods.name: Where
methods.brief: Evaluates a condition once against the whole guarded object, with @pair, @list, @string, @number and @object each standing for that object.

parameters.name: pcCondition
parameters.role: a condition text written with a whole-object keyword, such as @pair[1] = "x"

notes: an IsAPairQ() that passes returns this guard, and one that fails returns a stzFalseObject
warnings: all five keywords are replaced, whichever one the guard was built with; the condition sees the object, so use an element access, @list[1], and not len(@list)

classes.name: stzObjective
classes.brief: Finds where a formula of named variables is smallest or largest, starting from a point, and reports how the search ended.
classes.description: Build one with new stzObjective("(x-1)^2 + (y-2)^2", [ "x", "y" ]). The search is L-BFGS on the exact gradient of the formula, with no constraints; for linear constraints use stzLinearSolver. MinimizeFrom and MaximizeFrom answer a record, not a bare point, because a bare point cannot say it did not converge: read :status and :why, and :evaluations for the real cost. The result is a local extremum, so different starts can end at different points. SetMaxIterations and SetGradientTolerance tune the stop. Status words are lowercase: converged, settled, maxiterations, linesearchfailed, notfinite.
classes.example:
aR = o1.MinimizeFrom([ -5, 8 ])
? @@( aR[:point] )
#--> [ 1, 2 ]
? aR[:status]
#--> converged
? o1.ValueAt([ 0, 0 ])
#--> 5

methods.name: init
methods.brief: Builds an objective from a formula of named variables, such as "(x-1)^2 + (y-2)^2", to be minimised or maximised.

parameters.name: pcExpression
parameters.role: the formula as text, in the syntax of stzMathFunction

parameters.name: pacVariables
parameters.role: the names of its variables, in the order points will be given

warnings: the formula is compiled at once, so a bad formula or variable list raises the error of stzMathFunction here

methods.name: Expression
methods.brief: Returns the formula text as it was given.

methods.name: Variables
methods.brief: Returns the variable names in declared order, which is the order of every point.

methods.name: MathFunctionQ
methods.brief: Returns the stzMathFunction that holds the compiled formula, to ask its derivatives directly.
notes: there is no plain form because it would return an object; the Q is the name

methods.name: ValueAt
methods.brief: Returns the value of the formula at a point.

parameters.name: paPoint
parameters.role: the values of the variables, one per variable in declared order

notes: the same as stzMathFunction.ValueAt; a point of the wrong length raises an error

methods.name: GradientAt
methods.brief: Returns the exact partial derivatives of the formula at a point, one per variable.

parameters.name: paPoint
parameters.role: the values of the variables, one per variable in declared order

methods.name: SetMaxIterations
methods.brief: Sets how many iterations the search may take before it gives up; the default is 500.

parameters.name: n
parameters.role: the limit, a number above 0

notes: a value of 0 or less is ignored without a message and the limit stays as it was

extensions.name: SetMaxIterationsQ
extensions.adds: does what the method does, then returns the object, so the call can be chained

methods.name: SetGradientTolerance
methods.brief: Sets how small the gradient must become for the search to call itself done; unset, the engine's default applies.

parameters.name: n
parameters.role: the tolerance, a number above 0

notes: a value of 0 or less is ignored without a message; a large tolerance stops the search early, away from the minimum

extensions.name: SetGradientToleranceQ
extensions.adds: does what the method does, then returns the object, so the call can be chained

methods.name: MinimizeFrom
methods.brief: Searches downhill from a starting point with L-BFGS and returns the point it reached with a record of how the search ended.

parameters.name: paStart
parameters.role: the starting values of the variables, one per variable in declared order

notes: check :status, which is "converged", "settled", "maxiterations", "linesearchfailed" or "notfinite" (lowercase, since Ring folds the case of symbols): a point is returned even when the search did not converge; it finds a local minimum, so the start matters

methods.name: MaximizeFrom

parameters.role: the starting values of the variables, one per variable in declared order

notes: a formula with no maximum ends with :status "linesearchfailed": maximising (x-1)^2 + (y-2)^2 from [ 0, 0 ] returns the start

classes.name: stzOccurrences
classes.brief: Carries the positions where a substring occurs in a string, and cuts, replaces or recases the text at them.
classes.description: The object holds three things: the positions (codepoint positions, counted from 1), the substring that was searched and the string it was searched in. Removed, ReplacedWithCS, Uppercased and Lowercased each answer a NEW text and leave the object unchanged. A position counts only where the text really holds the substring (a stale position is skipped, so nothing is cut at the wrong place), and positions that overlap are taken left to right without overlap, the way Remove and Replace of stzString treat "aa" in "aaaa". An empty substring has nothing to act on: the string comes back unchanged.
classes.example:
? o1.Removed()
#--> ba
? o1.Uppercased()
#--> bANANa

methods.name: init
methods.brief: Stores the positions where a substring occurs in a string, together with the substring and the string.

parameters.name: panOccurr
parameters.role: the positions found, as a list of numbers

parameters.name: pcSubStr
parameters.role: the substring that was searched, or the named form :Of = '...'

parameters.name: pcStr
parameters.role: the string that was searched, or the named form :In = '...'

notes: checked with plain texts and with the :Of and :In named forms; SubString and String answer the two texts afterwards

methods.name: Occurrences
methods.brief: Returns the list of positions given at construction, unchanged.

methods.name: Value
methods.brief: Returns the list of positions given at construction, as the call with the other name does.

methods.name: SubString
methods.brief: Returns the substring that was searched, as given at construction.
methods.returns: a text; the plain text even when the object was built with the named form :Of = '...'

extensions.name: SubStringQ
extensions.adds: does what the method does, then returns the object, so the call can be chained

methods.name: String
methods.brief: Returns the string that was searched, as given at construction.
methods.returns: a text; the plain text even when the object was built with the named form :In = '...'

extensions.name: StringQ
extensions.adds: does what the method does, then returns the object, so the call can be chained

methods.name: ValidOccurrencesCS
methods.brief: Returns the positions that really hold the substring, left to right and without overlap.

parameters.name: pCaseSensitive
parameters.role: 1 to compare the text at a position to the substring letter by letter, 0 to ignore case

methods.returns: a sorted list of positions: numbers inside the string, listed once, whose text equals the substring, each starting after the end of the previous one
notes: an empty substring has no hit; a position that does not fit is skipped

methods.name: RebuiltWith

parameters.name: paHits

parameters.name: pcMode
parameters.role: "remove", "replace", "upper" or "lower"

parameters.name: pcNew
parameters.role: the text put instead, used by the mode "replace" only

methods.returns: a text; the characters between the hits are copied as they are

methods.name: Removed
methods.brief: Returns the string with the substring cut out at every occurrence, matching letter by letter.
methods.returns: a new text; the object and its string are unchanged

extensions.name: RemovedCS

methods.name: ReplacedWith
methods.brief: Returns the string with the text at every occurrence put instead by another, matching letter by letter.

methods.returns: a new text; the object and its string are unchanged

extensions.name: ReplacedWithCS
extensions.adds: takes a case-sensitivity flag

methods.name: Uppercased
methods.brief: Returns the string with the text at every occurrence in capitals and the rest unchanged.
methods.returns: a new text; the object and its string are unchanged. The capitals follow the Unicode rules, so an accented letter is capitalised and a German sharp s becomes SS
notes: a position whose text differs from the substring only by case still counts

methods.name: Lowercased
methods.brief: Returns the string with the text at every occurrence in small letters and the rest unchanged.

classes.name: stzOctalNumber
classes.brief: Holds an octal number and writes it in decimal, binary and hexadecimal.
classes.description: Built from a text of the digits 0 to 7, with or without the 0o prefix, which is kept as given; the From... methods replace the number in place from a decimal, binary or hexadecimal value and store it with the 0o prefix. It inherits from stzString. Checked by hand: 0o377 is 255 (0b11111111, 0xFF); 0o755 is 493 (0b111101101, 0x1ED); 0o400000000000000000 is 9007199254740992. Found today: WithPrefix doubles a prefix that is already stored (0o0o377); ToDecimalForm gives 0 from 2 to the power 63 up; ToBaseNForm and ToScientificNotationForm raise R14; and a capital 0O17 is accepted and then converts to 0.
classes.example:
? o1.ToDecimalForm()
#--> 255
? o1.ToBinaryForm()
#--> 0b11111111
? o1.ToHexForm()
#--> 0xFF
o2 = new stzOctalNumber("755")
? o2.ToDecimalForm()
#--> 493
? o2.ToHexFormWithoutPrefix()
#--> 1ED
o2.FromDecimalForm(8)
? o2.Content()
#--> 0o10

methods.name: init
methods.brief: Builds an octal number from a text of octal digits, with or without the 0o prefix.

parameters.name: pNumber
parameters.role: a text of the digits 0 to 7, optionally written 0o..

notes: the class inherits from stzString; write the prefix in small letters: 0o377 and 755 are accepted
warnings: the text is kept exactly as given, prefix included, so Content of 0o377 is 0o377 and of 17 is 17; an empty text, 0o alone, a bare o prefix such as o17, a digit 8 or 9, a sign, a point and a number (17 without quotes) are all refused; a capital 0O17 is accepted but then ToDecimalForm gives 0

methods.name: Content
methods.brief: Returns the text the number was built or last set with, prefix included if it had one.
notes: 17 gives 17 and 0o377 gives 0o377; FromDecimalForm, FromBinaryForm and FromHexForm store the 0o prefix

methods.name: Value
methods.brief: Returns the text the number was built or last set with.

methods.name: WithPrefix
methods.brief: Returns the 0o prefix followed by the stored text.
notes: use Content when the number was built or set with the prefix
warnings: it adds the prefix to a text that may already have it, so 0o377 gives 0o0o377; only a number built without the prefix, such as 17, gives 0o17

methods.name: ToStzNumber
methods.brief: Returns the value as a stzNumber.
methods.returns: a stzNumber holding the decimal value
notes: 0o377 gives 255

methods.name: ToStzString
methods.brief: Returns the stored text as a stzString.

methods.name: ToDecimalForm
methods.brief: Returns the value in decimal.
notes: ToDecimal is the same call; 0o377 gives 255, 0o755 gives 493, 0o400000000000000000 gives 9007199254740992
warnings: a value from 2 to the power 63 up gives 0 instead of its value, and 0o777777777777777777777 (2 to the power 63 less 1) gives 9223372036854775808, rounded by the double it goes through; confirmed with three values

methods.name: OctalNumber
methods.brief: Returns the stored text.

methods.name: ToBinaryForm
methods.brief: Returns the value in binary with the 0b prefix.
notes: ToBinary is the same call; 0o377 gives 0b11111111; 17 gives 0b1111; 0 gives 0b0

methods.name: ToBinaryFormWithoutPrefix
methods.brief: Returns the value in binary, without a prefix.
notes: ToBinaryWithoutPrefix is the same call; 0o755 gives 111101101

methods.name: ToHexForm
methods.brief: Returns the value in hexadecimal with the 0x prefix, in capitals.
notes: ToHex is the same call; 0o377 gives 0xFF; 17 gives 0xF; 0 gives 0x0

methods.name: ToUnicodeHexForm
methods.brief: Returns the value as a U+ code point text, without padding to four digits.
notes: ToUnicodeHexFor is the same call; 0o377 gives U+FF; 101 gives U+41, where the usual written form is U+0041

methods.name: ToHexFormWithoutPrefix
methods.brief: Returns the value in hexadecimal, without a prefix, in capitals.
notes: ToHexmWithoutPrefix is the same call; 0o755 gives 1ED

methods.name: ToBaseNForm
methods.brief: Raises error R14 today instead of writing the value in another base.

parameters.name: n
parameters.role: the base meant, from 2 to 32

notes: toBaseN is the same call; use stzNumber.IntegerPartToBaseNForm on ToStzNumber() meanwhile
warnings: it forwards to ToBaseNForm on stzNumber, a method that does not exist there (stzNumber has IntegerPartToBaseNForm), so every base raises R14; confirmed with 0o377 and 17

methods.name: ToScientificNotationForm
methods.brief: Raises error R14 today instead of writing the value in scientific notation.
notes: ToScientificNotation is the same call
warnings: it forwards to ToScientificNotationForm on stzNumber, a method that does not exist there; stzNumber raises the same R14 on its own

methods.name: ToBytes
methods.brief: Returns eight raw bytes: the value stored as an IEEE 754 double, least significant byte first.
notes: these are not the bytes of the octal digits

methods.name: FromDecimalForm
methods.brief: Replaces the number with the octal form of a decimal value, in place.

parameters.name: n
parameters.role: the decimal value, an integer of 0 or more

notes: 255 gives 0o377, 8 gives 0o10, 0 gives 0o0
warnings: the stored text gets the 0o prefix, so WithPrefix doubles it afterwards; a negative value stores 0o-10 and a fraction 8.5 stores 0o10.4, which init would refuse

methods.name: FromDecimal
methods.brief: Replaces the number with the octal form of a decimal value, in place.

parameters.name: n
parameters.role: the decimal value, an integer of 0 or more

notes: 255 gives 0o377
warnings: same limits as FromDecimalForm

methods.name: FromBinaryForm
methods.brief: Replaces the number with the octal form of a binary value, in place.

parameters.name: cBinary
parameters.role: the binary text, which must carry the 0b prefix

warnings: a binary text without 0b raises Can't create binary number; the stored text gets the 0o prefix

methods.name: FromBinary
methods.brief: Replaces the number with the octal form of a binary value, in place.

parameters.name: cBinary
parameters.role: the binary text, which must carry the 0b prefix

notes: 0b1010 gives 0o12
warnings: a binary text without 0b raises Can't create binary number

methods.name: FromHexForm
methods.brief: Replaces the number with the octal form of a hexadecimal value, in place.

parameters.name: cHex
parameters.role: the hex text, with or without the 0x prefix

notes: 0xFF and FF both give 0o377; 0x10 gives 0o20
warnings: the stored text gets the 0o prefix

methods.name: FromHex
methods.brief: Replaces the number with the octal form of a hexadecimal value, in place.

parameters.name: cHex
parameters.role: the hex text, with or without the 0x prefix

notes: 0x10 gives 0o20
warnings: the stored text gets the 0o prefix

classes.name: stzOidcClient
classes.brief: Acts as the application side of a sign-in with an external identity provider: builds the sign-in address and decides whether the returned id-token may be believed.
classes.description: Give it the issuer, the client id and the provider's public keys (AddKey, or SetJwks with the provider's JWKS document). AuthorizationUrl sends the user to the provider with a state and a nonce, and PKCE when you pass a challenge. VerifyIdToken then checks, in order, the shape, the key, the signature, the issuer, the audience, the expiry, the not-before time and the nonce, and answers a list whose why names the first failure instead of a bare 0. The algorithm is taken from the key the client holds, never from the token. In tests, use stzOidcSandbox to mint tokens offline.
classes.example:
? o1.AuthorizationUrl("https://idp.invented.test/authorize", "s1", "n-1")
#--> https://idp.invented.test/authorize?response_type=code&client_id=client-demo&redirect_uri=https%3A%2F%2Fapp.invented.test%2Fcb&scope=openid%20profile%20email&state=s1&nonce=n-1
? o1.PkceChallengeOf("dBjftJeZ4CVP-mB92K27uhbUJU1p1r_wW1gFWFOEjXk")
#--> E9Melhoa2OwvFrEMTJguCHaoeK1t8URWbuGJSstw-cM
? o1.VerifyIdToken("junk", "n-1")[:ok]
#--> 0
? o1.Why()
#--> the token is not a well-formed JWT

methods.brief: Decides whether an id-token may be believed, at the present time: signature, issuer, audience, expiry, not-before and nonce.

parameters.name: pcToken
parameters.role: the id-token returned by the provider

parameters.name: pcExpectedNonce
parameters.role: the nonce this login sent

methods.returns: a list [ :ok, :subject, :email, :claims, :why ]: ok is 1 with the identity, or 0 with why naming the first check that failed
notes: the key is chosen by the token's kid (the only key when the token names none) and the algorithm comes from that key, never from the token
warnings: a refusal is returned, never raised, and each one is also noted in the security ledger by issuer and reason, never with the token

methods.name: VerifyIdTokenAt
methods.brief: Decides whether an id-token may be believed at a given time, so that expiry can be tested without waiting.

parameters.name: pcToken
parameters.role: the id-token to check

parameters.name: pcExpectedNonce
parameters.role: the nonce this login sent

parameters.name: pnNow
parameters.role: the time to judge by, in seconds since 1970

notes: the token is expired when pnNow is past exp plus the clock allowance
warnings: the checks run in order and stop at the first failure: shape, key, signature, issuer, audience, exp, nbf, nonce; a token with no exp is refused

methods.name: Why
methods.brief: Returns why the last verification was refused, or the empty text when it passed.

methods.name: Show
methods.brief: Prints a one-line summary: the issuer, the client id and the number of keys.

classes.name: stzOidcProvider
classes.brief: Makes an application the identity provider that other apps sign in through: it issues single-use codes and signed ID tokens.
classes.description: The authorization-code flow runs in two calls: Authorize hands a short-lived code to an exactly registered redirect URI, and ExchangeCode, a back-channel call that authenticates the client by its hashed secret, turns the code into a signed ID token and access token. A code is single-use and bound to its client, redirect URI, nonce and PKCE challenge. Tokens are signed ES256 with an engine key, or RS256 when you supply one, and RotateKey keeps the outgoing public key in the JWKS so tokens in flight keep verifying. Every refusal gives a reason and an OAuth error code. It runs inside the process: serving the endpoints over HTTP is the caller's job.
classes.example:
r = o1.Authorize([ :clientId = "app1", :redirectUri = "http://localhost:3000/cb" ], "alice")
t = o1.ExchangeCode("app1", "invented-client-secret", r[:code], "http://localhost:3000/cb", "")
? t[:subject]
#--> alice
t = o1.ExchangeCode("app1", "invented-client-secret", r[:code], "http://localhost:3000/cb", "")
? t[:error]
#--> invalid_grant

classes.name: stzOidcSandbox
classes.brief: Acts as a local OpenID Connect identity provider with a real signing key, so sign-in is developed without a provider account.
classes.description: It is not a stub that answers true. It holds an ES256 key pair, publishes the public half as a key set and a discovery document, and signs every token in the engine, so the relying party, stzOidcClient, runs its genuine signature check against a genuine key set. It also mints deliberately bad tokens, expired, forged, or with another audience, issuer or nonce, through IssueIdTokenXT, so the refusals can be tested, which a real provider will not do on request. The key comes from the engine's generator or from a seed for a reproducible suite, and is a sandbox key, never a real one. Token claims are joined into the JSON without escaping, so it must not be fed untrusted values.
classes.receiver: o1 = new stzOidcSandbox("https://idp.local", "my-app") o2 = new stzOidcClient("https://idp.local", "my-app")
classes.example:
o2.SetJwks(o1.JwksJson())
c1 = o1.IssueIdToken("dana", "nonce-1")
? o2.VerifyIdToken(c1, "nonce-1")[:ok]
#--> 1
? o2.VerifyIdToken(c1, "another-nonce")[:ok]
#--> 0
c2 = o1.IssueForgedIdTokenAt("dana", "n", floor(StzEngineTimeNowMs() / 1000))
? o2.VerifyIdToken(c2, "n")[:ok]
#--> 0
? o1.TokenEndpoint()
#--> https://idp.local/token

classes.name: stzOperatingSystem
classes.brief: Answers what machine and operating system the program runs on, with a predicate for each family and width.
classes.description: It reads the processor facts (architecture, pointer width, byte order) from the engine and the operating-system family from Ring, and offers one TRUE or FALSE question per family and per width, so a program branches on the machine instead of parsing a name. Name gives the family as a lower- case word, Info gathers the facts in a list of pairs, and PathSeparator, LineEnding, NormalizePath and ExecutableExtension answer what a path or a program file looks like here. It only reads: nothing is changed on the machine.
classes.example:
? o1.BitSize() = (o1.PointerSize() * 8)
#--> 1
? o1.NormalizePath("a/b/c.txt") = ("a" + o1.PathSeparator() + "b" + o1.PathSeparator() + "c.txt")
#--> 1
? len(o1.Info())
#--> 7

classes.name: stzOptimFile
classes.brief: Reads a .zopt optimization file and expands its indexed families into an ordinary stzOptimModel.
classes.description: A .zopt file declares sets, indexed parameters and variable families, an objective and constraints, with sum and forall over a set. Reading it checks the format and lists every fault in Findings; ToModel then expands the families into plain variables and constraint strings before the model ever sees them, so a file and a hand-built model of the same problem are the same model. ToZopt and Save write the expanded model back as a flat file. Adding a product is editing one list.
classes.receiver: o1 = new stzOptimFile("") o1.SetText("zopt: 1" + char(10) + "model: shop" + char(10) + "set Products: chairs, tables" + char(10) + "param profit[Products]: 30, 45" + char(10) + "var make[Products]: 0 .. 100 integer" + char(10) + "maximize: sum profit[p] * make[p] for p in Products" + char(10) + "subject to:" + char(10) + " forall p in Products: make[p] <= 60")
classes.example:
? o1.IsValid()
#--> 1
? o1.MembersOf("Products")[2]
#--> tables
? o1.ParamValue("profit", "tables")
#--> 45
? o1.ToModel().VarNames()[1]
#--> make_chairs

classes.name: stzOptimModel
classes.brief: Holds a linear or integer optimisation model that you write as variables, an objective and constraint texts, then solves it.
classes.description: Declare the variables with Vars or AddVar, set Maximize or Minimize, add constraints with SubjectTo, and Solve. A variable is bounded below (0 by default) and optionally above, and may be :integer or :binary. The built-in solver is a simplex with branch-and-bound; the :highs tier is refused because it is not vendored, so Why always names the engine that ran. Check IsOptimal before reading Solution: an infeasible or unbounded model leaves placeholder values. Violations re-checks the answer against the model. Known limit: a model with no constraint at all raises an error when solved, give it at least one constraint.
classes.receiver: o1 = new stzOptimModel() o1.Vars([ :x = [0, 40], :y = [0, :integer] ]) o1.Maximize("3*x + 2*y") o1.SubjectTo([ "x + y <= 50", "2*x + y <= 80" ])
classes.example:
o1.Solve()
? o1.IsOptimal()
#--> 1
? o1.Objective()
#--> 130
? @@( o1.Solution() )
#--> [ [ "x", 30 ], [ "y", 20 ] ]
? o1.Branched()
#--> 1
? o1.IsFeasibleAnswer()
#--> 1

methods.returns: the model itself, so calls chain
notes: an omitted upper bound means unbounded above; names are kept in lower case
warnings: a non-list, an entry that is not a pair, a name declared twice and an unknown qualifier raise an error

extensions.name: VarsQ
extensions.adds: does what the method does, then returns the object, so the call can be chained

methods.name: AddVar
methods.brief: Declares one variable with its bounds and whether it is whole-valued.

parameters.name: pcName
parameters.role: the variable's name, lower-cased, never empty

parameters.name: pSpec
parameters.role: a number (the lower bound) or a list as for Vars: bounds, then :integer or :binary

methods.returns: the model itself, so calls chain
notes: :binary means integer with bounds 0 and 1; a variable declared after the constraints widens the earlier rows with zeros
warnings: an empty name, a name declared twice and a qualifier other than :integer, :int, :binary or :bool raise an error

methods.name: HasVar
methods.brief: TRUE if a variable of that name is declared.

parameters.name: pcName
parameters.role: the variable's name, matched without regard to case

methods.name: NumberOfVars
methods.brief: Returns how many variables are declared.

methods.name: VarNames
methods.brief: Returns the names of the variables, in lower case, in declaration order.

methods.name: BoundsOf
methods.brief: Returns the declared bounds and kind of one variable.

parameters.name: pcName
parameters.role: the variable's name

methods.returns: a list [ :lb, :ub, :bounded, :integer ]; [ ] for an unknown name
notes: :ub is 0 and :bounded is 0 when the variable has no upper bound

methods.name: Maximize
methods.brief: Sets the objective to maximize, from a linear expression over the declared variables.

parameters.name: pcExpr
parameters.role: a linear expression such as "3*x + 2*y + 1"

methods.returns: the model itself, so calls chain
notes: a second call replaces the objective
warnings: raises an error when no variable is declared yet or when the expression names something that is not a variable

extensions.name: MaximizeQ
extensions.adds: does what the method does, then returns the object, so the call can be chained

methods.name: Minimize
methods.brief: Sets the objective to minimize, from a linear expression over the declared variables.

parameters.name: pcExpr
parameters.role: a linear expression such as "2*p + 3*q"

methods.returns: the model itself, so calls chain
notes: a second call replaces the objective
warnings: same errors as Maximize

extensions.name: MinimizeQ
extensions.adds: does what the method does, then returns the object, so the call can be chained

methods.name: Sense
methods.brief: Returns the direction of the objective.
methods.returns: a text: max, min, or the empty text before an objective is set

methods.name: ObjectiveCoefficients
methods.brief: Returns the coefficient of each variable in the objective.
methods.returns: a list of numbers, one per variable in declaration order; [ ] before an objective is set
notes: the constant of the expression is not in it; it is added to Objective after solving

methods.name: SubjectTo
methods.brief: Adds constraints from a list of relation texts, or one constraint from a single text.

parameters.name: paList
parameters.role: a list of relations such as [ "x + y <= 50", "2*x + y <= 80" ], or one relation as text

methods.returns: the model itself, so calls chain
notes: the constraints are named c1, c2 and so on, in order added
warnings: raises an error for anything else, when no variable is declared, and for a text with no <=, >= or =

extensions.name: SubjectToQ
extensions.adds: does what the method does, then returns the object, so the call can be chained

methods.name: AddConstraint
methods.brief: Adds one constraint from a relation text, named automatically.

parameters.name: pcText
parameters.role: a relation such as "x + y <= 50", with <=, >= or =

methods.returns: the model itself, so calls chain
notes: the name is c followed by the count of constraints added without a name
warnings: the same errors as SubjectTo

methods.name: AddNamedConstraint
methods.brief: Adds one constraint from a relation text under a name of your choice.

parameters.name: pcName
parameters.role: the constraint's name, kept in lower case

parameters.name: pcText
parameters.role: a relation such as "n <= 5"

methods.returns: the model itself, so calls chain
notes: the variables are moved to the left side, so "2 >= x" is stored as the row -1 against -2
warnings: the same errors as SubjectTo

methods.name: NumberOfConstraints
methods.brief: Returns how many constraints the model holds.

methods.name: ConstraintAt
methods.brief: Returns one stored constraint.

parameters.name: pnIndex
parameters.role: the position of the constraint, from 1

methods.returns: a list [ name, coefficients, operator, right side, text ]; the operator is -1 for <=, 1 for >= and 0 for =
notes: the coefficients are one per variable, in declaration order
warnings: an index outside 1 to NumberOfConstraints raises error R2, index out of range

methods.name: AST
methods.brief: Returns the model as a plain list that two descriptions can be compared by, rather than their answers.
methods.returns: a list [ :sense, :vars, :obj, :objconst, :cons ]; each var row is [ name, lb, ub, bounded, integer ] and each constraint row [ name, coefficients, operator, right side ]
notes: two different wrong models can give the same answer, so a guard compares the ASTs

methods.name: ASTCore
methods.brief: Returns the same list as AST with the constraint names dropped.
methods.returns: a list of the same shape; each constraint row is [ coefficients, operator, right side ]
notes: for comparing two descriptions that agree on the mathematics but label it differently

methods.name: ASTSignature
methods.brief: Returns the model, without constraint names, as one canonical text.
notes: exists because Ring's = does not compare nested lists structurally; the texts can be printed side by side

methods.name: Describe
methods.brief: Returns the model as it reads: the objective, the constraints and the bounds of the variables.

methods.name: Show
methods.brief: Prints the model as Describe returns it.

methods.name: SolveWith
methods.brief: Solves the model with a named tier of the solver and keeps the answer.

parameters.name: pcTier
parameters.role: :auto, :floor or the empty text for the built-in simplex and branch-and-bound

methods.returns: the model itself, so calls chain
notes: whole-valued variables make the solver branch; Why names the engine that ran
warnings: raises an error for :highs (not vendored), for any other tier, when no objective is set, and for a model with no constraint at all, which the engine refuses today although the code says it solves

extensions.name: SolveWithQ
extensions.adds: does what the method does, then returns the object, so the call can be chained

methods.name: Solve
methods.brief: Solves the model with the automatic tier.
methods.returns: the model itself, so calls chain
warnings: the same errors as SolveWith, including a model with no constraint

methods.name: IsSolved
methods.brief: TRUE if a solve has run, whatever it found.

methods.name: Status
methods.brief: Returns the solver's status code.
methods.returns: a number: 0 optimal, 1 unbounded, 2 infeasible, 3 iteration limit, 4 node limit; -1 before any solve

methods.name: StatusWord
methods.brief: Returns the status in words.
methods.returns: a text such as optimal, infeasible, unbounded or not solved

methods.name: IsOptimal
methods.brief: TRUE if a solve ran and found the optimum.

methods.name: Objective
methods.brief: Returns the value of the objective at the answer, constant included.
notes: meaningful only when IsOptimal is TRUE: for an unbounded or infeasible model it is the engine's placeholder

methods.name: Solution
methods.brief: Returns each variable with its value at the answer.
methods.returns: a list of [ name, value ] pairs in declaration order
notes: the values are placeholders when the model is infeasible or unbounded
warnings: before any solve it raises error R2, index out of range

methods.name: ValueOf
methods.brief: Returns the value of one variable at the answer.

parameters.name: pcName
parameters.role: the variable's name, matched without regard to case

warnings: raises an error for an unknown name and before any solve

methods.name: Nodes
methods.brief: Returns how many branch-and-bound nodes the last solve explored.

methods.name: Iterations
methods.brief: Returns how many simplex iterations the last solve took.

methods.name: Branched
methods.brief: Returns 1 when the solve used branch-and-bound, which it does when a variable is whole-valued.

methods.name: Engine
methods.brief: Returns the name of the engine that ran the last solve.
methods.returns: a text such as "engine floor (Zig simplex + branch-and-bound)"; the empty text before a solve

methods.name: Why
methods.brief: Returns the solver's account of itself: the tier chosen, the result, the objective and the point, and the work done.
methods.returns: a text; "nothing has been solved yet" before a solve
notes: for an infeasible or unbounded model it states the result and gives no point

methods.name: ShowWhy
methods.brief: Prints what Why returns.

methods.name: Violations
methods.brief: Checks the reported answer against every constraint, bound and whole-value requirement, to catch a confident wrong answer.
methods.returns: a list of [ name, left side, operator, right side ] rows, one per breach; [ ] when none, and also [ ] unless the status is optimal
notes: a tolerance of 0.000001 is allowed

methods.name: IsFeasibleAnswer
methods.brief: TRUE if Violations finds no breach.
notes: it is also TRUE when nothing has been solved or the model is infeasible, because Violations is empty then

classes.name: stzOptimSentence
classes.brief: Reads an optimization problem said as a sentence and builds the same stzOptimModel a hand-written model would give.
classes.description: The vocabulary is small and closed: maximize or minimize an expression, where a variable is between two numbers, at least or at most one, a whole number or binary, and keeping an expression under, over or at a number. An ambiguity is refused with a finding rather than guessed. The sentence calls the model's own methods, so there is one model class and one expression compiler. StzOptimNaturally(text) reads and builds in one call.
classes.receiver: o1 = new stzOptimSentence("maximize 3*x + 2*y" + char(10) + "where x is between 0 and 40" + char(10) + "and y is a whole number at least 0" + char(10) + "keeping x + y under 50")
classes.example:
? o1.IsValid()
#--> 1
? o1.ToModel().VarNames()[2]
#--> y
? o1.ToModel().ConstraintAt(1)[5]
#--> x + y <= 50

methods.name: init
methods.brief: Reads an optimization problem written as a short sentence of maximize or minimize, where and keeping clauses.

parameters.name: pcText
parameters.role: the sentence, one clause per line or clauses joined by and

warnings: a faulty sentence does not raise here: its faults are listed by Findings; a where clause written on the same line as the objective is not split off, so write it on its own line or after and; a bare relation placed after a where clause is read as one more variable, so use a keeping clause or put the relation first

methods.name: Findings
methods.brief: Returns the faults found in the sentence, one text each, empty when the sentence is understood.
methods.returns: a list of text; [ ] for a valid sentence

methods.name: IsValid
methods.brief: TRUE if the sentence has an objective, at least one variable and no clause the surface does not know.

methods.name: CiteFindings
methods.brief: Returns the faults as one text, each on its own line after a dash, ready to print.
methods.returns: a text; empty for a valid sentence

methods.name: ToModel
methods.brief: Builds the stzOptimModel the sentence says, through the same door a hand-written model uses; a faulty sentence is refused.
notes: a variable declared twice, which a bare relation after where can cause, raises AddVar: declared twice
warnings: raises stzOptimSentence: this sentence was REFUSED and the findings for a faulty sentence

classes.name: stzOrdinal
classes.brief: Turns a whole number into its ordinal form, such as 3rd in English, 3e in French or an Arabic ordinal word.
classes.description: The language comes from a global setting at the moment the object is built (SetOrdinalLanguage changes it for objects made afterwards) and SetLanguage changes it for one object. English, French and Arabic are supported. The function Ordinal(n) builds the object and answers the text in one step. Only the three public readers (ToString, Value, Language) are meant for callers; ToEnglish, ToFrench and ToArabic are private helpers of ToString.
classes.example:
? o1.ToString()
#--> 3rd
o1.SetLanguage("fr")
? o1.ToString()
#--> 3e
o1.SetLanguage("ar")
? o1.ToString()
#--> الثّالث

methods.brief: Builds an ordinal from a whole number, spelled in the language the library is set to when the object is made.

parameters.name: _n_
parameters.role: the number to turn into an ordinal

warnings: the language is read from the global $aOrdinalConfig at birth, so a later SetOrdinalLanguage does not reach an object already built

methods.name: SetLanguage
methods.brief: Switches this ordinal to English ("en"), French ("fr") or Arabic ("ar"), and ignores any other code.

parameters.name: lang
parameters.role: the language code, one of "en", "fr" or "ar"

methods.returns: nothing; an unknown code leaves the language as it was
warnings: an unknown code such as "xx" is silent: no error and no change

methods.name: Language
methods.brief: Returns the language code this ordinal speaks.

methods.name: ToString
methods.brief: Returns the ordinal as text in the language set on this object, such as 3rd, 3e or the Arabic word for third.
notes: English reads 11, 12 and 13 as th; French gives 1er and then e up to 9 and ème from 10; Arabic spells 1 to 5 as words and writes ال before any larger number; 0 and negatives get the th suffix in English and the ème suffix in French

methods.name: Value
methods.brief: Returns the number this ordinal was built from, unchanged.

methods.name: Number
methods.brief: Returns the plain number behind the ordinal, the same answer as Value.

methods.brief: Builds the English spelling of the number from the suffix table of the language, such as 21st or 12th.

parameters.name: _aConfig_
parameters.role: the English entry of $aOrdinalConfig: its :suffixes and :special_cases

warnings: private: ToString calls it, and a call from outside raises error R26

methods.name: ToFrench
methods.brief: Builds the French spelling of the number from the suffix table of the language, such as 1er, 2e or 12ème.

parameters.name: _aConfig_
parameters.role: the French entry of $aOrdinalConfig: its :suffixes

warnings: private: ToString calls it, and a call from outside raises error R26; the feminine form is never produced

methods.name: ToArabic
methods.brief: Builds the Arabic spelling of the number: the ordinal word for 1 to 5, and ال followed by the digits for any other.

parameters.name: _aConfig_
parameters.role: the Arabic entry of $aOrdinalConfig: its :suffixes list of ordinal words

warnings: private: ToString calls it, and a call from outside raises error R26

classes.name: stzOrgChart
classes.brief: Models an organisation as positions, people and departments, draws its reporting lines, and checks them against governance rules.
classes.description: An org chart is a diagram whose nodes are positions and whose edges run from supervisor to subordinate. Positions have a level (executive, management, staff), people are assigned to them, and the chart answers vacancy, span-of-control and succession questions, validates itself (BCEAO, segregation of duties, span, vacancy, succession), writes reports, highlights subsets with the View calls and saves to the .stzorg text format. Records are hash lists with lowercase keys. The limits of single calls are listed in their warnings; two View calls, ViewNodeWithProperties and ViewNodesWithTags, are placeholders that do nothing.
classes.receiver: o1 = new stzOrgChart("TechCo"); o1.AddExecutiveXT("ceo", "CEO"); o1.AddManagerXT("vp", "VP Sales"); o1.ReportsTo("vp", "ceo")
classes.example:
? @@( o1.DirectReports("ceo") )
#--> [ "vp" ]

classes.name: stzOtelBatch
classes.brief: Collects spans and writes them as the OpenTelemetry resourceSpans envelope that an OTLP collector takes at its traces endpoint.
classes.description: One stopwatch exports as one OTLP span; a real trace is many spans shipped together. The batch holds rendered JSON fragments, so copies of it are harmless, and writes the service identity once at the top, the way the performance monitor does for metrics. Spans that joined one another arrive sharing a traceId, so a collector reassembles the tree. Clear empties the batch for the next shipment. A service name that holds a double quote or a backslash is written unescaped today.
classes.receiver: o1 = StzOtelBatch("restolean") o2 = new stzStopwatch("checkout") o2.Start() o2.Stop() o1.AddSpan(o2) o1.AddSpanJson('{"name":"manual","kind":1}')
classes.example:
? o1.ServiceName()
#--> restolean
? o1.SpanCount()
#--> 2
? left(o1.ToJson(), 17)
#--> {"resourceSpans":
? right(o1.ToJson(), 15)
#--> "kind":1}]}]}]}
o1.Clear()
? o1.SpanCount()
#--> 0

methods.returns: a JSON text: the service identity once at the top, the scope softanza.perf, then the spans
notes: an empty batch gives the envelope with an empty list of spans; the spans keep the order they were added in

classes.name: stzOutputSchema
classes.brief: Declares the shape of an answer once, then judges raw or parsed values against it whole or not at all.
classes.description: A schema lists fields with a type (string, number, boolean, one of, list) and optional rules such as a numeric band. ParseOutput reads model text as JSON or as field: value lines and returns the validated value in declared order, or a refusal that names the rule and the field that failed. Partial credit is forbidden, a scalar that can be represented is coerced (the text 36 becomes the number 36), a closed enumeration must match exactly, and a required field that is present but empty counts as missing. Fields nobody declared are reported and dropped, unless RefuseUnknownFields closes the schema. ToGBNF compiles the shape into a grammar for the sampler, but a grammar fixes shape and never value, so this court still checks every band. Structure kills malformedness, not falsehood: a lie of the right shape validates.
classes.example:
? @@(o1.ParseOutput("name: Ana" + char(10) + "age: 36")[:value])
#--> [ [ "name", "Ana" ], [ "age", 36 ] ]
? o1.Accepts("name: Ana" + char(10) + "age: 900")
#--> 0
? o1.CiteFindings(o1.Check([ [ "name", "Ana" ], [ "age", 900 ] ]))
#--> [lessequal @ age] field 'age' must be at most '130', and the model answered '900'.

methods.name: init
methods.brief: Compiles a declaration of fields into a schema, judging it now so a faulty declaration never reaches a model.

parameters.name: paFields
parameters.role: the declaration, a list of field hash-lists with field, type (string, number, boolean, oneof, list or structure) and optional choices, of, must and optional

notes: the operators are equals, not-equals, contains, greaterthan, lessthan, greaterequal and lessequal, and symbols such as >= are normalized
warnings: raises an error for an unknown field type, a mistyped key or an unknown operator, naming it

methods.name: Name

methods.name: SetName

extensions.name: SetNameQ

methods.name: Fields

methods.brief: Returns how many top-level fields the schema declares.

parameters.name: pvValue
parameters.role: the value to judge, a list of [ field, value ] rows

methods.returns: a hash-list [ :ok, :value, :findings ]; :value holds the declared fields in declared order with scalars coerced, and is [ ] when :ok is 0

methods.name: Holds

parameters.name: pvValue

parameters.name: pvValue
parameters.role: the value to judge, a list of [ field, value ] rows

parameters.name: pcRaw

methods.name: DecodingStatus
methods.brief: Returns what constrained decoding does and what it does not do.

methods.brief: Returns the declaration read back as prose, one line per field, for a narrated test or a reader.

classes.name: stzOverlay
classes.brief: Describes an institution's adaptation of the core program, laid over it file by file, and judges it before it is used.
classes.description: An overlay is a folder with overlay.zknw (its name, the program it extends, the languages it speaks, its brand, the worlds it replaces) and optional worlds, courses and governance folders. It adds and shadows; it never forks the core: it may replace a world and add chapters and exercises, but a file that would replace a core chapter or a core exercise is refused. Check is its court and returns findings in the house shape; the overlay is valid when none is an error.
classes.example:
? o1.Name()
#--> bank
? @@( o1.Languages() )
#--> [ "fr", "en" ]
? o1.Brand()
#--> sahel-savings
? @@( o1.ReplacedWorlds() )
#--> [ "workplace" ]

methods.name: init
methods.brief: Opens an overlay folder and reads its overlay.zknw, whose is-a overlay fact gives the overlay its name.

parameters.name: pcFolder
parameters.role: the overlay's folder: its last segment is the overlay's id

notes: an overlay adds and shadows the core program file by file, and never forks it
warnings: a folder without overlay.zknw opens without error and has no name (HasManifest answers FALSE); a fact whose value holds a space, such as a brand of two words, raises the error Incorrect Id! pcNodeId must be one string without spaces nor new lines

methods.name: Folder
methods.brief: Returns the overlay's folder path, without a trailing slash.

methods.name: Id
methods.brief: Returns the overlay's identifier, which is the last segment of its folder's path.

methods.brief: Returns the name the manifest gives the overlay with its is-a overlay fact, or an empty text when there is none.

methods.name: HasManifest
methods.brief: TRUE if overlay.zknw names the overlay, which is the one thing an overlay cannot do without.

methods.name: Extends
methods.brief: Returns the ids of the programs the manifest says the overlay is laid over.
methods.returns: a list of text, such as softanza-education; [ ] when it says none
notes: Check demands that it names the id of the program it is judged against

methods.name: Languages
methods.brief: Returns the languages the overlay says it speaks, in the order the manifest gives them.
methods.returns: a list of language codes, such as fr and en
notes: each must be a language of the core program: a new language is added to the natural pack, not declared here

methods.name: Brand
methods.brief: Returns the brand the manifest gives the institution, or an empty text when there is none.
notes: the brand is one word, since a value with a space cannot be read

methods.name: ReplacedWorlds

methods.returns: a list of text, such as workplace

methods.brief: Judges the overlay against the program it is laid over and returns its findings, none of them an error when it is valid.

notes: the rules are overlay-manifest, overlay-extends, overlay-language, overlay- world, overlay-world-page, overlay-course, overlay-chapter, overlay-exercise, overlay-governance and overlay-no-fork: an overlay may replace a world and add chapters and exercises, but a file that would replace a core chapter or exercise is a fork and is refused; an overlay without a manifest gets that one finding only
warnings: it runs every added exercise and every world page to prove them, so the bank overlay takes about 45 seconds, and IsValid and CiteFindings each run it again; the runs happen on the desktop only

methods.brief: TRUE if Check finds no error in the overlay.

parameters.name: poProgram
parameters.role: the stzProgram the overlay is laid over

notes: it runs the whole court, which is slow

parameters.name: poProgram

notes: it runs the whole court, which is slow

classes.name: stzPair
classes.brief: Holds two values side by side and tells whether both are numbers, texts, lists or objects.
classes.description: Build one with new stzPair([ a, b ]) or StzPairQ([ a, b ]); the global IsPair(aList) tells whether a plain list has exactly two items. Item1 and Item2 read the two sides, and it is a stzList, so every list method also works. The list given to init is not checked for holding two items. Update, UpdateWith, Swap and Swapped raise error R24 today, so a pair cannot be changed or swapped through them.
classes.example:
? o1.Item1()
#--> שלום
? o1.Item2()
#--> 7
? o1.BothAreNumbers()
#--> 0
? IsPair([ 1, 2 ])
#--> 1

parameters.name: paList

warnings: Raises error R24 "Using uninitialized variable: panpair" today for every list, instead of replacing the items: the check reads panPair, a name that is not the parameter paPair

methods.brief: Replaces the items of the pair by those of another two-item list, the same as Update.

parameters.name: paPair
parameters.role: the list of two items that should replace the pair

methods.returns: nothing today: it raises error R24

Alternate is meant to interleave the two lists and raises error R24 today for any non-empty pair. The file marks the class as a candidate for generalisation into stzListOfLists.

classes.name: stzPairOfNumbers
classes.brief: Holds two numbers and compares them: least common multiple, greatest common divisor, speed-up factor and percentage gain.
classes.description: Build one with new stzPairOfNumbers([ a, b ]) or StzPairOfNumbersQ([ a, b ]); it is a stzPair, so Item1, Item2, Swap and the rest of the pair vocabulary are inherited. The measures are written for a before and an after, such as two timings: SpeedUp is a divided by b, GainFactor is b divided by a, PerfGain is the drop as a percentage of a, Gain is the rise as a percentage of b. Global functions of the same names (SpeedUp, PerfGain, GainFactor, RelativeGain, LeastCommonMuliple, GreatestCommonDividor) take the two numbers directly. BothAreBetween has a defect with a large first number.
classes.example:
? o1.GreatestCommonDividor()
#--> 6
? o1.LeastCommonMuliple()
#--> 36
? o1.PerfGain()
#--> -50
? SpeedUp(10, 2)
#--> 5

classes.brief: Is another name of stzListOfPairs: a list of pairs [ first, second ], with every method of it.

classes.name: stzPanel
classes.brief: Lays out an interface document with the RmlUi engine and hands the result over as triangles, text commands, boxes and events.
classes.description: A panel is neither a window nor a renderer: it computes where things go and leaves drawing to a canvas, so the same layout reaches an SVG on a machine with no graphics card. The markup is loaded as a text (LoadMarkup), never from a file, because it is meant to be emitted by a higher layer. After Layout the panel answers where an element sits (BoxOf), what lies under a point (ElementAt), which elements the keyboard reaches (TabRing) and what input produced (Events, drained by the caller and never dispatched back into Ring). SetTextOf and SetStyleOf change one element without loading the document again. RML has no default stylesheet, so give a div display: block and the body width: 100% to fill the panel. Pointer verbs act on the layout, so call Layout first. The event queue and the counters belong to the engine and are shared by every panel. Needs stz_gui.dll; ask StzGuiAvailable() first. Free the panel when done.
classes.example:
o1.LoadMarkup('<rml><head><style>body { width: 100%; height: 100%; } div { display: block; } #bar { height: 48px; background-color: #2b6cb0; } .b { width: 100px; height: 30px; tab-index: auto; }</style></head><body><div id="bar"/><div id="one" class="b"/><div id="two" class="b"/></body></rml>')
o1.Layout()
? @@( o1.BoxOf("bar") )
#--> [ 0, 0, 320, 48 ]
? @@( o1.TabRing() )
#--> [ "one", "two" ]
? o1.ElementAt(10, 10)
#--> bar
? o1.TriangleCount()
#--> 2
