classes.name: stzParcel
classes.brief: Carries a value between the stages of a flow together with its provenance, certainty, cost and content key.
classes.description: A parcel is the only thing that passes between stages. It has no public setter: the library fills its evidence, provenance and cost when a faculty runs, so it can be read and replayed but not edited. A stage yields either a parcel its court accepted or a refusal parcel whose value is the list of findings, which is why a refusal can travel through a flow like any other value. Certainty and probability are what the implementation stated, and unknown when it stated none; they are not a judgment made by a person.
classes.example:
? o1.Type()
#--> label
? o1.IsRefusal()
#--> 0
? o1.Certainty()
#--> unknown
o2 = StzRefusalParcelQ("stage x", "my-rule", "something failed")
? o2.Why()
#--> REFUSED: my-rule at stage x: something failed

methods.name: init
methods.brief: Builds a parcel of a payload type around a value, with a content key and no provenance yet.

parameters.name: pcType
parameters.role: the payload type of the value, such as text or label

parameters.name: pValue
parameters.role: the value the parcel carries

notes: the key is a SHA-256 of the type and the value, so two parcels of the same type and value share it until a run seals it over the chain
warnings: nothing judges the value here: the courts judge it when a faculty makes the parcel, and a parcel built by hand has certainty unknown, no probability and an empty chain

methods.name: Type
methods.brief: Returns the payload type of the parcel, or refusal when it is a refusal.
methods.returns: a text such as label, number or refusal

methods.name: Value
methods.brief: Returns the payload the parcel carries.
methods.returns: the value, whatever its type; for a refusal, the list of findings
notes: a parcel has no setter, so the value cannot change after it is built

methods.name: IsRefusal
methods.brief: TRUE if the parcel is a refusal: the court rejected the answer, or a stage or the registry could not answer.
notes: a refusal is a parcel too, so a flow can carry it without raising

methods.name: Findings
methods.brief: Returns the findings a refusal carries, in the house shape.
methods.returns: a list of findings, each [ rule, subject, where, severity, message ]; [ ] for a parcel that is not a refusal

methods.name: Certainty
methods.brief: Returns the evidential word the producer stated for the answer.
methods.returns: a text: unknown unless the implementation stated certain, probable or apparent
notes: the word is whatever the implementation declared and the class never invents one; it is not judged by a person, and a floor says unknown unless it states more

methods.name: P
methods.brief: Returns the probability the producer stated for the answer, or -1 when it stated none.
notes: it is the producer's own figure, kept as given; calibration is checked separately against the goldens, not by a person

methods.name: Provenance
methods.brief: Returns one row for every step that made the parcel, oldest first.
methods.returns: a list of rows, each a list of [ key, value ] pairs: faculty, implementation, version, kind, detail; [ ] for a parcel built by hand
notes: the detail of a floor that answered after a model failed says it fell back and why

methods.name: Chain
methods.brief: Returns the steps that made the parcel as faculty:implementation texts, oldest first.
methods.returns: a list of text such as clean:smart-clean
notes: a parcel from the last stage of a flow lists every stage before it

methods.name: Cost
methods.brief: Returns what producing the answer cost.
methods.returns: a list of [ key, value ] pairs: ms, tokens_in and tokens_out
notes: the token counts are whatever the implementation stated, and 0 when it stated none
warnings: the milliseconds are read from Ring's clock around the call, so a fast stand-in function reads 0

methods.name: Key
methods.brief: Returns the content key of the parcel: a SHA-256 in hexadecimal.
notes: once sealed by a run the key covers the type, the value and the chain, so the same value made by two implementations has two keys

methods.name: Trace
methods.brief: Returns the flow and stage that produced the parcel, set only by a flow run.
methods.returns: a text such as tidy-sort-loud:sort; an empty text outside a flow

methods.name: Why
methods.brief: Returns one sentence per step that made the parcel, with the certainty at the end; for a refusal, the findings.
methods.returns: a text such as conf -> m1 (model) [stand-in], ending with the certainty; for a refusal, REFUSED: followed by CiteFindings
notes: the certainty shown is the one the producer stated, not a judgment of quality

methods.name: CiteFindings
methods.brief: Returns the findings written as one line each part, rule then place then message.
methods.returns: a text such as my-rule at stage x: something failed, parts joined by a slash; an empty text when there are none

methods.name: Content
methods.brief: Returns a summary of what identifies the parcel, without its value.
methods.returns: a list of [ key, value ] pairs: type, refusal, certainty, chain and key

classes.name: stzParser
classes.brief: Keeps a value as the source to parse; the minimal base class that stzListParser is built on.
classes.description: In base/ this class is a stub: it stores whatever value it is built with and gives it back with Source. The full parser family lives elsewhere and is not loaded by the base library. Nothing else is defined here. stzListParser inherits from it but has its own init that does not call this one, so Source of a stzListParser answers an empty text; build a stzParser directly, or read the list of a stzListParser with List.
classes.example:
? o1.Source()
#--> some source
o2 = new stzParser([ 1, 2 ])
? @@( o2.Source() )
#--> [ 1, 2 ]

methods.name: init
methods.brief: Builds the minimal base parser around any value and keeps it as its source.

parameters.name: pSource
parameters.role: the value to keep as the source, of any type

notes: stzListParser inherits from it but does not call it: its own init takes a list and leaves Source empty

methods.name: Source
methods.brief: Returns the value the parser was built around.
methods.returns: the value given to init, of its own type
notes: on a stzListParser it answers an empty text, because that class stores its list elsewhere (see List)

classes.name: stzParseTree
classes.brief: Holds a constituency parse tree of a sentence: nested phrases (S, NP, VP, PP) over words tagged with their part of speech.
classes.description: Where the chunker of stzText gives flat phrases, this gives the nested structure. It is reached from a text, never built by hand in practice: ParseTreeQ() on a stzText returns the root, and ParseTreeWithQ takes your own phrase grammar. The tree answers its yield (Leaves, Text), its shape (Height, Children), the phrases of a kind (NounPhrases, VerbPhrases, PrepositionalPhrases, Phrases) and two renderings (ToBracket, ToTreeString). The tags come from the stzText tagger, so a Hebrew or Arabic sentence is tagged as plain nouns.
classes.receiver: o1 = Q("The quick brown fox jumps over the lazy dog").TextQ().ParseTreeQ()
classes.example:
? o1.Label()
#--> S
? @@( o1.Children() )
#--> [ "NP", "VP" ]
? @@( o1.NounPhrases() )
#--> [ "The quick brown fox", "the lazy dog" ]
? o1.Height()
#--> 5
? o1.Text()
#--> The quick brown fox jumps over the lazy dog

methods.name: init
methods.brief: Builds one node of a parse tree with a label: a phrase label such as NP, VP, PP or S, or the part-of-speech tag on a leaf.

parameters.name: pcLabel
parameters.role: the phrase label or, on a leaf, the part-of-speech tag, such as NN

methods.returns: nothing; the node is built, empty and without children
notes: a number is accepted and turned into its text; by hand, a leaf is made with a tag and SetWord, a phrase with a label and AddChild

methods.name: SetWord
methods.brief: Sets the word of a leaf node and returns the node, so calls chain.

parameters.name: pcWord
parameters.role: the token the leaf stands for

notes: the parser itself builds trees from the bottom up with it

methods.name: AddChild
methods.brief: Appends a node under this one as its last child and returns this node, so calls chain.

parameters.name: oNode
parameters.role: the stzParseTree to attach

notes: Ring copies the child on appending, so changes made to the child object afterwards do not reach the tree

methods.name: Label
methods.brief: Returns the label of the node: its phrase label, or the part-of-speech tag on a leaf.

methods.name: Word
methods.brief: Returns the word held by a leaf node; a phrase node holds none.
methods.returns: a text; "" on a phrase node

methods.name: IsLeaf
methods.brief: TRUE if the node has no child, which is how a word-bearing node ends the tree.
notes: a node just built with init is a leaf until a child is added

methods.name: Children
methods.brief: Returns the labels of the direct children, left to right.
notes: ChildrenQ answers the child nodes themselves, as objects

extensions.name: ChildrenQ
extensions.adds: does what the method does, then returns the object, so the call can be chained

methods.name: NumberOfChildren
methods.brief: Returns how many direct children the node has.

methods.name: Leaves
methods.brief: Returns the words at the ends of the tree, left to right, which is the sentence the tree spells.

methods.name: Text
methods.brief: Returns the words of the tree joined by single spaces.

methods.name: Height
methods.brief: Returns the number of levels from this node down to its deepest leaf, a lone leaf counting 1.

methods.name: Subtrees
methods.brief: Returns every node of the tree, this one included, whose label equals the given one.

parameters.name: pcLabel
parameters.role: the phrase label to search for, in any case and with spaces around it ignored

methods.returns: a list of stzParseTree nodes; [ ] when none match
notes: the answer holds objects, not text; Phrases gives their words

methods.name: Phrases
methods.brief: Returns the words of every phrase of one kind, as texts, in tree order.

parameters.name: pcLabel
parameters.role: the phrase label to collect, such as NP or VP, in any case

methods.returns: a list of texts; [ ] when the label is absent
notes: a phrase that contains another of the same kind is listed beside it

methods.name: NounPhrases
methods.brief: Returns the words of every noun phrase (NP) of the tree.

methods.name: VerbPhrases
methods.brief: Returns the words of every verb phrase (VP) of the tree.

methods.name: PrepositionalPhrases
methods.brief: Returns the words of every prepositional phrase (PP) of the tree.

methods.name: ToBracket
methods.brief: Returns the tree in Penn Treebank bracket notation, with each leaf written word/TAG.
notes: a node with no child and no word gives "/NP": only a leaf with a word prints as a leaf should

methods.name: ToTreeString
methods.brief: Returns the tree as indented lines, one node per line, two spaces per level.

methods.name: Show
methods.brief: Prints the indented tree on the console.

classes.name: stzPasskeySandbox
classes.brief: Acts as a virtual passkey authenticator in software, with real keys and real signatures, so passkey flows are tested with no hardware or browser.
classes.description: It is not a mock that answers ok. It generates a real P-256 key, emits a genuine attestation object with a COSE key inside, and produces real ECDSA signatures over the WebAuthn message, so the relying party runs its true parsing and verification. It also does what an attacker's device would do and no real authenticator will do on request: sign for the wrong origin, or write a counter that does not advance, so the refusals can be tested. The key comes from the engine's generator, or from a seed given to CreateCredentialXT for a reproducible suite. Its keys are sandbox keys and never real ones.
classes.example:
? o1.IsSandbox()
#--> 1
a1 = o1.CreateCredential("challenge-1", "https://example.com")
? len(a1[:credentialId]) > 0
#--> 1
a2 = o1.Assert("challenge-2", "https://example.com")
? o1.SignCount()
#--> 1
? len(a2[:signature]) > 0
#--> 1

methods.name: init
methods.brief: Builds a virtual authenticator for a domain, with no credential yet and its counter at 0.

parameters.name: pcRpId
parameters.role: the domain its credentials are bound to

methods.name: IsSandbox
methods.brief: TRUE if the object is a test double; here it always is, so it never passes for a real device.

methods.name: RpId
methods.brief: Returns the domain the authenticator is bound to, trimmed.

methods.name: CredentialId
methods.brief: Returns the id of the credential made last.

methods.name: SignCount
methods.brief: Returns the signature counter, which each Assert advances.
notes: an Assert that raises for lack of a credential has already advanced it

methods.name: CreateCredential
methods.brief: Makes a credential as a security key would, with a real P-256 key and attestation object, and returns what the browser passes on.

parameters.name: pcChallenge
parameters.role: the challenge the server issued

parameters.name: pcOrigin
parameters.role: the origin the browser would report

methods.returns: a hash list [ :attestationObject, :clientData, :credentialId ]; the first two are base64url
notes: a new key is generated each time unless the XT form is given a 32-byte hex seed; it replaces the earlier credential and resets the counter to 0; only invented sandbox keys, never real ones

extensions.name: CreateCredentialXT
extensions.adds: the extended form: more parameters than the base method

methods.name: Assert
methods.brief: Signs a challenge as the login ceremony does, advancing the counter by one.

parameters.name: pcChallenge
parameters.role: the challenge the server issued

parameters.name: pcOrigin
parameters.role: the origin the browser would report

warnings: raises an error telling to call CreateCredential first when there is no credential

methods.name: AssertAtCount
methods.brief: Signs a challenge with a chosen counter value, which is how a cloned authenticator behaves when it does not advance.

parameters.name: pcChallenge
parameters.role: the challenge the server issued

parameters.name: pcOrigin
parameters.role: the origin to report

parameters.name: pnCount
parameters.role: the counter to write into the authenticator data

notes: the stored counter is not changed
warnings: raises the no-credential error when there is no credential

methods.name: AssertForOrigin
methods.brief: Signs for another origin, as a phishing site would obtain, and advances the counter.

parameters.name: pcChallenge
parameters.role: the challenge the server issued

parameters.name: pcPhishingOrigin
parameters.role: the origin to report in its place

notes: the relying party's origin check must refuse the result
warnings: raises the no-credential error when there is no credential

methods.name: ClientData
methods.brief: Builds the client data JSON a browser would build, base64url-encoded.

parameters.name: pcType
parameters.role: webauthn.create or webauthn.get

parameters.name: pcChallenge
parameters.role: the challenge

parameters.name: pcOrigin
parameters.role: the origin

notes: it is a test double: real client data comes from the browser
warnings: the challenge and the origin are written into the JSON without escaping, so a value holding a quote can add keys or break the JSON, which is useful for testing and wrong for real input

methods.name: Show
methods.brief: Prints one line with the domain, the credential id and the counter.

classes.name: stzPasskeyServer
classes.brief: Judges passkey registrations and logins as the relying party: the ceremony, the challenge, the origin, the signature, user presence and the counter.
classes.description: A passkey replaces the password with a key pair that the user's device holds. The cryptography and the parsing of the binary formats are the engine's; this class makes the relying party's decisions, which is where implementations fail. Registration and login both check the browser's client data: the ceremony type, the challenge this server issued and the origin, which is what makes a passkey unphishable. Login then verifies the signature under the stored key, requires user presence, and refuses a signature counter that did not advance, noted as a suspected clone. Two settings fail open and must never be empty: an empty expected challenge and an empty server origin each switch their check off. Every refusal returns a reason and is noted. Use stzPasskeySandbox as the virtual authenticator for development.
classes.receiver: o1 = new stzPasskeyServer("example.com", "https://example.com") o2 = new stzPasskeySandbox("example.com")
classes.example:
c1 = o1.NewChallenge()
a1 = o2.CreateCredential(c1, "https://example.com")
a2 = o1.RegisterCredential(a1[:attestationObject], a1[:clientData], c1)
? a2[:ok]
#--> 1
c2 = o1.NewChallenge()
a3 = o2.Assert(c2, "https://example.com")
a4 = [ :keyType = a2[:keyType], :key1 = a2[:key1], :key2 = a2[:key2], :signCount = 0 ]
? o1.VerifyAssertion(a4, a3[:authenticatorData], a3[:clientData], a3[:signature], c2)[:ok]
#--> 1
a5 = o2.AssertForOrigin(c2, "https://evil.example")
a6 = o1.VerifyAssertion(a4, a5[:authenticatorData], a5[:clientData], a5[:signature], c2)
? a6[:ok]
#--> 0

methods.name: init
methods.brief: Builds the relying party for passkeys, bound to a domain and to the exact origin a browser will report.

parameters.name: pcRpId
parameters.role: the registrable domain the credentials are bound to, such as example.com

parameters.name: pcOrigin
parameters.role: the exact origin, such as https://example.com

warnings: an empty origin switches the origin check off, so any site's response is accepted: always give one

methods.name: RpId
methods.brief: Returns the domain the credentials are bound to, trimmed.

methods.name: Origin
methods.brief: Returns the origin the server demands from the browser, trimmed.

methods.name: SetOrigin
methods.brief: Replaces the origin the server demands.

parameters.name: pcOrigin
parameters.role: the exact origin, such as https://example.com

notes: the text is kept as given, without trimming
warnings: setting an empty origin switches the origin check off

extensions.name: SetOriginQ
extensions.adds: does what the method does, then returns the object, so the call can be chained

methods.name: Why
methods.brief: Returns the reason for the last refusal, or an empty text after a success.
warnings: the reason can quote the origin the browser reported, without escaping, so show it as text and never as markup

methods.name: NewChallenge
methods.brief: Returns a fresh random challenge of 64 hexadecimal characters from the engine's secure generator.
notes: keep it for the one exchange it belongs to and refuse a second use: that is what stops a replay

methods.name: RegisterCredential
methods.brief: Judges the response of a device that creates a credential, and returns the credential to store.

parameters.name: pcAttObjB64
parameters.role: the attestation object, base64url

parameters.name: pcClientDataB64
parameters.role: the client data JSON, base64url

parameters.name: pcExpectedChallenge
parameters.role: the challenge this server issued for this exchange

methods.returns: a hash list [ :ok, :credentialId, :keyType, :key1, :key2, :signCount, :why ]; :ok is 1 only when every check passed, and :why says what failed
notes: the checks are the ceremony type webauthn.create, the challenge, the origin and the user-presence flag
warnings: an empty expected challenge skips the challenge check, so a response to any earlier challenge is accepted; an empty server origin skips the origin check; it never raises, a refusal is returned

methods.name: VerifyAssertion
methods.brief: Judges a login response against a stored credential: client data, signature, user presence and the signature counter.

parameters.name: paCredential
parameters.role: the stored credential as a hash list [ :keyType, :key1, :key2, :signCount ]

parameters.name: pcAuthDataB64
parameters.role: the authenticator data, base64url

parameters.name: pcClientDataB64
parameters.role: the client data JSON, base64url

parameters.name: pcSigB64
parameters.role: the signature, base64url

parameters.name: pcExpectedChallenge
parameters.role: the challenge issued for this login

methods.returns: a hash list [ :ok, :signCount, :why ]; :signCount is the new counter to store
notes: every refusal is noted as auth.passkey.failed; a refusal returns, it never raises
warnings: an empty expected challenge skips the challenge check, so a captured assertion could be replayed; an empty server origin skips the origin check; a counter that does not advance past the stored one is refused and noted as a suspected clone, while a counter of 0 is allowed

methods.name: Show
methods.brief: Prints one line with the domain and the origin.

classes.name: stzPassword
classes.brief: Holds a password as a secret that you hash and compare rather than reveal, both steps governed by the actor gate.
classes.description: It is a stzSecret of kind password. HashedBy gives a salted Argon2id hash that is safe to store, and Matches compares a candidate with the held password. Both read the plaintext, so both need an effectful, non-sandboxed actor and raise an error for any other.
classes.example:
? o1.Matches("invented-pw", HumanActor("alice"))
#--> 1
? o1.Matches("other", HumanActor("alice"))
#--> 0
? left(o1.HashedBy(HumanActor("alice")), 10)
#--> $argon2id$

methods.name: init
methods.brief: Builds a password secret with a name, of kind password and no source yet.

parameters.name: pcName
parameters.role: the password name, which appears in its descriptor

methods.name: HashedBy
methods.brief: Returns a salted Argon2id hash of the password, safe to store.

parameters.name: poActor
parameters.role: the actor asking, which must be effectful and not sandboxed

methods.returns: a text beginning $argon2id$; each call salts afresh, so two hashes of the same password differ
notes: StzVerifyPassword checks a candidate against the hash
warnings: raises an error for a refused actor, as Reveal does

methods.name: Matches
methods.brief: TRUE if the candidate equals the password; the comparison reads the plaintext.

parameters.name: pcCandidate
parameters.role: the text to compare with the password

parameters.name: poActor
parameters.role: the actor asking, which must be effectful and not sandboxed

notes: the comparison is a plain equality, not a constant-time one
warnings: raises an error for a refused actor, rather than answering FALSE

classes.name: stzPattern
classes.brief: A pattern is a function of time: it tells which events happen in cycle 0, cycle 1, and so on, written in a small mini-notation.
classes.description: The notation is that of TidalCycles: words in a sequence share the cycle equally, ~ is a rest, [a b] a group, <a b c> alternates one step per cycle, a*2 and a/2 speed a step up or down, a? plays about half the cycles. Fast, Slow, Rev, Every and Off build a new pattern out of the old one, in place, and return the pattern so they chain. The class knows no domain: what a word means belongs to a subclass such as stzSoundPattern. A text that does not parse never raises: IsValid says so and LastError tells why.

methods.name: init
methods.brief: Parses a pattern written in mini-notation, such as 'red ~ blue [green green]', into a tree of steps.

parameters.name: pcText
parameters.role: the pattern in mini-notation: words, ~ for a rest, [ ] groups, < > alternation, * and / for speed, ? ! @

warnings: a text that does not parse leaves the object invalid instead of raising: read IsValid and LastError

methods.name: IsValid
methods.brief: TRUE if the text parsed into a pattern.

methods.name: Text
methods.brief: Returns the mini-notation the pattern was built from, as given.

methods.name: LastError
methods.brief: Returns the message of the last parse error or refused verb, empty when there was none.
warnings: the message of a refused verb (Fast with 1.5, Off with 2) replaces the parse message

methods.name: Refusals
methods.brief: Returns how many times a verb refused its argument since the pattern was built.
warnings: a refused verb leaves the pattern unchanged and does not raise

methods.name: Tree
methods.brief: Returns the parsed pattern as nested lists, each node tagged seq, atom, rest, fast, slow, rev, every or off.
methods.returns: a list; NULL when the text did not parse

methods.name: CycleEvents
methods.brief: Returns the events of one cycle, each as [ onset, length, kind, value ], sorted by onset; onset and length are fractions of the cycle.

parameters.name: pnCycle
parameters.role: the cycle number, counted from 0

methods.returns: a list of lists; empty when the pattern is invalid
warnings: rests give no event; the events of a cycle are computed from its number, so cycle 100000 costs the same as cycle 0

methods.name: DistinctValues
methods.brief: Returns the distinct [ kind, value, length ] triples that occur over the first pnCycles cycles.

parameters.name: pnCycles
parameters.role: how many cycles to scan, starting at cycle 0

methods.name: Period
methods.brief: Returns after how many cycles the pattern repeats exactly, at most 64; 1 for an invalid pattern.
warnings: '<a b c>' has period 3, a plain sequence has period 1

methods.name: Fast
methods.brief: Plays the pattern pnFactor times faster, in place, so its events squeeze into 1/pnFactor of a cycle and repeat.

parameters.name: pnFactor
parameters.role: a whole number of 1 or more

methods.returns: the pattern itself, so calls chain
notes: the pattern is changed in place
warnings: a fractional factor is refused and counted in Refusals

methods.name: Slow
methods.brief: Plays the pattern pnFactor times slower, in place, so one cycle shows 1/pnFactor of it.

parameters.name: pnFactor
parameters.role: a whole number of 1 or more

methods.returns: the pattern itself, so calls chain
notes: the pattern is changed in place
warnings: a fractional factor is refused and counted in Refusals

methods.name: Rev
methods.brief: Reverses the order of the events inside each cycle, in place.
methods.returns: the pattern itself, so calls chain
warnings: the pattern is changed in place

methods.name: Every
methods.brief: Applies a transformation to the pattern on every pnN-th cycle, in place, and plays it unchanged on the others.

parameters.name: pnN
parameters.role: a whole number of cycles, 1 or more

parameters.name: pXform
parameters.role: :Rev, [ :Fast, n ] or [ :Slow, n ]

methods.returns: the pattern itself, so calls chain
notes: the transformed cycle is the first of each group: Every(2, :Rev) reverses cycles 0, 2, 4
warnings: an unknown transformation or a pnN below 1 is refused and counted in Refusals

methods.name: Off
methods.brief: Layers a copy of the pattern shifted later by a fraction of a cycle on top of it, in place.

parameters.name: pnCycles
parameters.role: the shift, strictly between 0 and 1

parameters.name: pArg
parameters.role: a value the subclass uses to alter the shifted copy, NULL for none

methods.returns: the pattern itself, so calls chain
notes: the pattern is changed in place
warnings: a shift of 0 or of 1 and more is refused and counted in Refusals

classes.name: stzPaymentBatch
classes.brief: Gathers many payment orders, or many requests to pay, under one instructionId so that they travel as a single bulk.
classes.description: Give it an instructionId, the platform's own alias (FromAlias for payments, ToAlias for requests) and its items with Add, then hand it to PayInBulk or RequestPaymentsInBulk of stzPaymentsPort. Each item keeps its own txId, and the platform's alias and the confirmation belong to the batch. TotalAmount is the sum that a payout plan has to authorise for a bulk payment. Building a batch sends nothing.
classes.example:
? o1.NumberOfItems()
#--> 2
? o1.TotalAmount()
#--> 3500

methods.name: init
methods.brief: Builds an empty batch, to which orders or requests are added under one instructionId.

methods.name: WithInstructionId
methods.brief: Sets the one identifier of the whole batch, the key that makes a retry safe.

parameters.name: pcId
parameters.role: the platform's instructionId, unique for the batch

methods.returns: the batch itself, so calls chain
notes: each item still carries its own txId

methods.name: FromAlias
methods.brief: Sets the platform's alias that is debited, for a batch of payments.

parameters.name: pcAlias
parameters.role: the platform's PI-SPI alias, a UUID

methods.returns: the batch itself, so calls chain
notes: a batch of requests uses ToAlias instead

methods.name: ToAlias
methods.brief: Sets the platform's alias that is paid, for a batch of requests to pay.

parameters.name: pcAlias
parameters.role: the platform's PI-SPI alias, a UUID

methods.returns: the batch itself, so calls chain
notes: a batch of payments uses FromAlias instead

methods.name: InCategory
methods.brief: Sets the category of a batch of requests to pay; a batch starts at 401, an invoice.

parameters.name: pcCategory
parameters.role: the category code as text: 500, 521 or 401

methods.returns: the batch itself, so calls chain
notes: a batch of payments does not send it

methods.name: Motive
methods.brief: Sets the free text the other side sees on the whole batch.

parameters.name: pcMotif
parameters.role: the text shown with the batch

methods.returns: the batch itself, so calls chain

methods.name: WithConfirmation
methods.brief: Makes the hub hold the batch until the platform confirms it.
methods.returns: the batch itself, so calls chain
notes: the batch then starts as INITIE

methods.name: WithoutConfirmation
methods.brief: Makes the hub send the batch at once, which is how a batch starts.

methods.name: Add
methods.brief: Adds one payment order or one request to pay to the batch, as the item the hub expects.

parameters.name: poItem
parameters.role: a stzPaymentOrder for a batch of payments, or a stzPaymentRequest for a batch of requests

methods.returns: the batch itself, so calls chain
notes: the item is copied in at once, so changing the order afterwards does not reach the batch
warnings: raises an error when the item lacks what an item needs: its txId, its amount, and its payee or payer

methods.brief: Returns the instructionId set on the batch.
methods.returns: a text; an empty text when none was set

methods.name: NumberOfItems
methods.brief: Returns how many items the batch holds.

methods.name: TotalAmount
methods.brief: Returns the sum of the items' amounts in whole francs, the figure a payout plan must authorise for the batch.

methods.returns: a list of [ key, value ] pairs: instructionId, payeurAlias, confirmation, motif when set, then transactions
notes: stzPaymentsPort PayInBulk calls it for you
warnings: raises an error when the instructionId, the payer's alias or the items are missing

methods.name: AsRequestBody
methods.brief: Returns the batch as the message body for a bulk of requests to pay, a list of pairs, once it is complete.
methods.returns: a list of [ key, value ] pairs: instructionId, payeAlias, confirmation, motif when set, categorie, then transactions
notes: stzPaymentsPort RequestPaymentsInBulk calls it for you
warnings: raises an error when the instructionId, the platform's alias (ToAlias) or the items are missing

classes.name: stzPaymentOrder
classes.brief: Describes one payment to send, who is paid, how much and under which id, in the words the hub expects.
classes.description: Build it with its chained setters, then hand it to Pay of stzPaymentsPort. The txId is yours and unique, and a retry reuses it. The amount comes from StzAmountQ and only XOF is accepted. The payee is named by alias, by IBAN or by account, and one of WithConfirmation or WithoutConfirmation must be chosen. Building an order sends nothing: AsBody shows what would be sent.

methods.name: init
methods.brief: Builds an empty order, which is then told who pays whom, how much and under which id.

methods.name: WithTxId
methods.brief: Sets the platform's own unique identifier of the payment, the key that makes a retry safe.

parameters.name: pcTx
parameters.role: the platform's id, unique, kept to at most 35 characters by the hub

methods.returns: the order itself, so calls chain
notes: a retry reuses this id: a new id is a new payment

methods.name: FromAlias
methods.brief: Sets the platform's own alias, the account that is debited.

parameters.name: pcAlias
parameters.role: the platform's PI-SPI alias, a UUID

methods.returns: the order itself, so calls chain
notes: stzPaymentsPort Pay refuses an order without it

methods.name: ToAlias
methods.brief: Sets the payee by PI-SPI alias, the usual route to a customer.

parameters.name: pcAlias
parameters.role: the payee's PI-SPI alias, a UUID

methods.returns: the order itself, so calls chain
notes: if several routes are set the alias wins, then the IBAN, then the account

methods.name: ToIban
methods.brief: Sets the payee by IBAN and by the participant that holds the account.

parameters.name: pcIban
parameters.role: the payee's IBAN

parameters.name: pcParticipant
parameters.role: the code of the payee's participant, as Participants lists it

methods.returns: the order itself, so calls chain

methods.name: ToAccount
methods.brief: Sets the payee by account number and by the participant that holds the account.

parameters.name: pcCompte
parameters.role: the payee's account number

parameters.name: pcParticipant
parameters.role: the code of the payee's participant, as Participants lists it

methods.returns: the order itself, so calls chain
notes: in a bulk item the account number travels as payeOther, the hub's other name for it

methods.name: WithAmount
methods.brief: Sets the amount from an amount built with its currency, kept in whole francs.

parameters.name: poAmount
parameters.role: an amount built with StzAmountQ, in XOF

methods.returns: the order itself, so calls chain
notes: 25000 francs is stored as 25000
warnings: raises an error for a bare number, which carries no currency, and for any currency but XOF, before a request exists

methods.name: Motive
methods.brief: Sets the free text the payee sees on the payment, such as an invoice number.

parameters.name: pcMotif
parameters.role: the text shown to the payee, at most 140 characters

methods.returns: the order itself, so calls chain
notes: the hub shows it to the payee

methods.name: Documented
methods.brief: Attaches a reference document to the payment: its number and its type.

parameters.name: pcNumber
parameters.role: the document's number, such as an invoice number

parameters.name: pcType

methods.returns: the order itself, so calls chain

methods.name: WithConfirmation
methods.brief: Makes the hub hold the payment until the platform confirms it.
methods.returns: the order itself, so calls chain
notes: the payment then starts as INITIE, not ENVOYE; either this or WithoutConfirmation must be set

methods.name: WithoutConfirmation
methods.brief: Makes the hub send the payment at once, with no confirmation step.
methods.returns: the order itself, so calls chain

methods.name: TxId
methods.brief: Returns the txId set on the order.

methods.name: Amount
methods.brief: Returns the amount set on the order, in whole francs.

methods.brief: Returns the order as the message body the hub expects, a list of pairs, once every required part is set.

notes: stzPaymentsPort Pay calls it for you

classes.name: stzPaymentRequest
classes.brief: Describes one request to pay, who is asked, how much and for what, in the words the hub expects.
classes.description: Build it with its chained setters, then hand it to RequestPayment of stzPaymentsPort. The txId is yours and unique, and a retry reuses it. One of WithConfirmation or WithoutConfirmation must be chosen. Asking for money moves none, and building a request sends nothing.

? o1.TxId()
#--> APP-RTP-1
? @@(o1.AsBody()[6])
#--> [ "categorie", "401" ]
? @@(o1.AsBody()[7])
#--> [ "dateLimitePaiement", "2026-10-31" ]

classes.name: stzPaymentsPort
classes.brief: Speaks the BCEAO's PI-SPI payment verbs to a hub: sends money, asks for it, verifies webhooks and raises refusals as problems.
classes.description: An application sends money with Pay, asks for it with RequestPayment, hears about payments with RegisterWebhook and ReceiveWebhook, and reads a refusal with StzLastPaymentsProblem. The port speaks the verbs of the BCEAO's API Business to any backend that has a Request method, so the code tested against the twin (StzPiSpiSandboxQ) is the code that talks to a participant. WHERE THIS STANDS: behind the twin every verb runs and is tested; behind the live adapter (stzPispiHttpAdapter) the port has been proven against the twin served over real HTTP and has NOT been run against the BCEAO's sandbox, so treat that path as unperceived. WHAT THE PORT ADDS: a txId is an idempotency key, since sending it again answers the current state and sends nothing (replayed is 1); money out (Pay, PayInBulk, ReturnFunds, accepting a request or a cancellation) needs a committed plan on a governed port, which is how a port starts; an amount carries its currency and only XOF is spoken; a status of 400 or more raises, and StzLastPaymentsProblem reads it; a webhook is verified before it is believed. The amount is forwarded as built and nothing is added to it. The journal, the webhook secrets and the events already seen are kept per port in shared tables, so copies of a port agree. The card verbs (Authorize, Capture, Refund) are not here: they belong to stzCardPaymentsAdapter. The practical guide is docs/payments-guide.md.
classes.example:
oOrder = StzPaymentOrderQ().WithTxId("APP-2026-000001").FromAlias(oHub.BusinessAlias()).ToAlias(oHub.Alias("fatou")).WithAmount(StzAmountQ("25000", "XOF")).WithoutConfirmation()
aR = o1.Pay(oOrder)
? aR[:statut]
#--> ENVOYE
oHub.AdvanceSeconds(25)
? o1.StatusOf(aR[:end2endId])[:statut]
#--> IRREVOCABLE
o1.RegisterWebhook(StzWebhookQ().CallingBack("https://app.example/pispi").OnEvents([ "PAIEMENT_RECU" ]))
oHub.SimulateIncomingPayment("fatou", 18500, "APP-2026-000002")
aEv = o1.ReceiveWebhook(oHub.LastCallbackBody(), oHub.LastCallbackSignature())
? aEv[:accepted]
#--> 1
? aEv[:events][1][:motif]
#--> APP-2026-000002

methods.name: init
methods.brief: Builds a port in front of a hub, the one object an application calls to send money, ask for it and hear about it.

parameters.name: poBackend
parameters.role: the hub to talk to: the twin (StzPiSpiSandboxQ), a live adapter, or any object with Request(method, path, query, body) answering [ status, body ]

notes: the port keeps its journal, its webhook secrets and its plan authorisations per port, so two ports on one hub do not share them
warnings: raises an error when poBackend is not an object with a Request method

methods.name: IsSandbox
methods.brief: TRUE if the backend is the in-process twin, which moves no money; a registry reads it to refuse the twin in production.
methods.returns: TRUE or FALSE; FALSE when the backend does not say so
notes: the port only asks its backend

methods.name: IsConformance
methods.brief: TRUE if the backend talks to the BCEAO's sandbox, which speaks the real protocol with virtual money; a registry refuses it in production.
methods.returns: TRUE or FALSE; FALSE when the backend does not say so
notes: UNPERCEIVED: the adapter that answers TRUE here has been proven against the twin over real HTTP and has not been run against the BCEAO's sandbox

methods.name: RequiresCertificate
methods.brief: TRUE if the backend presents a mutual-TLS client certificate, which a registry then expects to find in a secret store.
methods.returns: TRUE or FALSE; FALSE when the backend does not say so
notes: UNPERCEIVED: only a live adapter answers TRUE, and no live adapter has been run against the BCEAO's sandbox

methods.name: CertificateSecretName
methods.brief: Returns the name of the secret that holds the backend's client certificate, so a registry can check it exists and has not expired.
methods.returns: a text; an empty text when the backend has none
notes: UNPERCEIVED: only a live adapter names one, and none has been run against the BCEAO's sandbox

methods.name: Backend

methods.returns: TRUE or FALSE; the opposite of AllowsUngovernedPayouts
notes: asking for money, refusing a request and moving money between the platform's own accounts need no plan on a governed port

methods.name: Pay
methods.brief: Sends money to a payee from an order and returns the payment as the hub states it, ENVOYE until it is final.

parameters.name: poOrder
parameters.role: a stzPaymentOrder with its txId, payer, payee, amount and confirmation set

methods.returns: a record with the hub's fields (statut, end2endId, montant, payeNom...) plus replayed, 1 when the txId had already been sent
notes: UNPERCEIVED behind a live adapter: that adapter has been proven against the twin over real HTTP and has not been run against the BCEAO's sandbox. ENVOYE is pending, not done: only IRREVOCABLE and REJETE are final. Sending the same txId again answers the current state and sends nothing, whatever the second order says. The amount is forwarded as built and nothing is added to it

methods.name: SentPayment

methods.brief: Returns the payments the platform sent, filtered, as a list; the hub gives 20 per page unless asked otherwise.

notes: pass [ ] for no filter; the paging data is dropped, SentPaymentsPage keeps it

parameters.role: the hub's id for the payment, found in the answer of Pay

methods.returns: a payment record whose statut is ENVOYE while pending, then IRREVOCABLE or REJETE; statutRaison holds the ISO code of a rejection
notes: a payment the payee's bank refuses is not an exception: it is a payment whose statut became REJETE. The twin's clock moves by hand with AdvanceSeconds
warnings: raises stzPaymentsProblem 404 for an unknown id

methods.name: ReturnFunds
methods.brief: Sends back a payment received, as a new movement of the same amount; the hub allows it within 90 days.

parameters.name: pcEnd2EndId
parameters.role: the end2endId of the payment received

methods.returns: the received payment's record, with retourStatut set (INITIE just after)

parameters.name: pcEnd2EndId
parameters.role: the end2endId of the payment the request concerns

parameters.name: pbAccept
parameters.role: TRUE to accept, FALSE to refuse

methods.returns: the payment record, with annulationStatut ACCEPTE after an accept

methods.name: RequestPayment
methods.brief: Asks a payer for money with a request to pay and returns it as the hub states it, ENVOYE or INITIE until it is final.

parameters.name: poRequest
parameters.role: a stzPaymentRequest with its txId, payer, payee, amount and category set

methods.returns: a record with the hub's fields (statut, end2endId, montant...) plus replayed, 1 when the txId had already been sent
notes: asking for money is not money out, so it needs no plan on a governed port. Sending the same txId again answers the current state and sends nothing. UNPERCEIVED behind a live adapter, which has not been run against the BCEAO's sandbox
warnings: the twin refuses an invoice or e-commerce request that lacks PayableBy, with a 400 problem naming dateLimitePaiement

methods.name: ConfirmRequest
methods.brief: Answers the confirmation step of a request to pay made with confirmation: yes sends it, no cancels it.

parameters.name: pcTxId
parameters.role: the txId of the request waiting for confirmation

parameters.name: pbYes

parameters.name: pcEnd2EndId

parameters.role: TRUE to pay it, FALSE to refuse

parameters.name: pcReason
parameters.role: the reason code sent when refusing, such as AM09 for a wrong amount, unused when accepting

methods.returns: the request record; statut is REJETE after a refusal and IRREVOCABLE after an accept

methods.name: Requests
methods.brief: Returns the requests to pay the platform sent, filtered, as a list.

parameters.name: paFilter

methods.brief: Returns one request to pay the platform sent, found by its txId, with its current status.

methods.brief: Returns the requests to pay that others sent to the platform: what is waiting for an answer.

parameters.name: paFilter

methods.brief: Sends many payments as one batch under one instructionId and returns the batch status with its counts.

methods.name: ReceiveWebhook

classes.name: stzPaymentsProblem
classes.brief: Holds the refusal a hub returned, as the RFC 7807 fields: a status, a title, a detail and the fields found wrong.
classes.description: When a hub answers 400 or more, stzPaymentsPort raises an error and keeps the problem; StzLastPaymentsProblem hands it over. Read Status to decide what to do, Detail to log what the hub said, and InvalidParams to see which field of the message was refused. A payment that the payee's bank refuses is not a problem: it is a payment whose statut became REJETE.
classes.receiver: oHub = StzPiSpiSandboxQ(); oPay = StzPaymentsPortQ(oHub); oPay.AllowUngovernedPayouts(); try oPay.Pay(StzPaymentOrderQ().WithTxId("BIG- 1").FromAlias(oHub.BusinessAlias()).ToAlias(oHub.Alias("fatou")).WithAmount(StzAmount Q("20000000", "XOF")).WithoutConfirmation()) catch o1 = StzLastPaymentsProblem() done
classes.example:
? o1.Status()
#--> 403
? o1.Detail()
#--> Plafond de paiement depasse
? o1.InvalidParams()[1][1][2]
#--> montant

methods.name: init
methods.brief: Builds a problem from the body the hub returned with a refusal, a list of pairs in the RFC 7807 shape.

parameters.name: paBody
parameters.role: the problem as a list of [ key, value ] pairs

notes: an application rarely builds one: StzLastPaymentsProblem hands over the one the port just recorded

methods.name: Status
methods.brief: Returns the HTTP status the hub gave the refusal, such as 403 or 404.
methods.returns: a number; 0 when the problem is empty

methods.name: Title
methods.brief: Returns the short, general name of the refusal, such as Forbidden.
methods.returns: a text; an empty text when the hub gave none

methods.name: Detail
methods.brief: Returns the hub's sentence about this refusal, the one to log or show a developer, such as Plafond de paiement depasse.
methods.returns: a text; an empty text when the hub gave none
notes: the twin writes it in French

methods.name: Type
methods.brief: Returns the problem's type address, which is about:blank when the hub gave none.

methods.name: InvalidParams
methods.brief: Returns the fields the hub found wrong, each with the reason, for a refusal of a malformed message.
methods.returns: a list of records [ name, reason ]; an empty list when the hub named none

methods.name: Content
methods.brief: Returns the whole problem as a list of pairs, exactly as the hub returned it.
methods.returns: a list of [ key, value ] pairs; an empty list when the problem is empty

classes.name: stzPaymentsSandbox
classes.brief: Names the card-gateway double under its historical name, with no behaviour of its own beyond stzCardPaymentsAdapter.
classes.description: The class was renamed when the card verbs were moved out of the payments port, and this name stays because the payments checks and the registry's examples use it. It adds nothing: every method is that of stzCardPaymentsAdapter. Build it with parentheses or with StzPaymentsSandboxQ(), because a paren-less new skips init and every object built that way shares one gateway.
classes.example:
o1.DeclineToken("tok_chargeback")
? o1.Authorize(4200, "tok_chargeback")[:status]
#--> declined
? o1.NumberOfDeclines()
#--> 1

classes.name: stzPayoutDesk
classes.brief: Takes a payout plan from proposal to release: rehearse it, judge it, and let a person commit it, with a journal of every attempt.
classes.description: Money out is a plan a human commits, and the desk is where that happens. Rehearse writes the plan into a workbench, a twin of the disk, so nothing real moves. Judge reads the rehearsed document and applies the policy. Commit checks the policy, that the rehearsed document is the plan that will be paid, and that the actor may change reality; a language-model actor and a sandboxed actor are refused. Only then does the plan cross into a real file, the durable record of what was authorised, visas included, and the port is told exactly which payouts to allow and for how much before each is released. A refusal never raises: it is a journal row and an event. One plan, one workbench. Everything here was run against the in-process twin, which moves no money.
classes.example:
? o1.PathOf("SUP-1")
#--> payouts/SUP-1.plan.json
? len(o1.Journal())
#--> 0

methods.name: init
methods.brief: Builds a desk that rehearses, judges and commits payout plans for one port under one policy, keeping its journal in a folder.

parameters.name: poPort
parameters.role: the stzPaymentsPort that will be told what to allow and then release

parameters.name: poPolicy
parameters.role: the stzPayoutPolicy that judges every plan

parameters.name: pcDir
parameters.role: the folder where a committed plan is written as its journal file

notes: each desk has its own journal, and a plan is known only to the desk it was rehearsed on

methods.name: PathOf
methods.brief: Returns where a plan is written, in the desk's folder: the rehearsed document in a workbench and the journal file once committed.

parameters.name: pcPlanId
parameters.role: the plan's identifier

methods.name: Rehearse
methods.brief: Writes a plan's document into a workbench, a twin of the disk, so it can be judged without anything real moving.

parameters.name: poPlan
parameters.role: the stzPayoutPlan to rehearse

parameters.name: pnBench
parameters.role: the workbench number returned by StzOpenAgentWorkbench

methods.returns: the desk itself, so calls chain
notes: the proposer acts in the workbench under the plan's proposer name, and no real file exists yet
warnings: the desk keeps the plan as it is now: visas added to the plan afterwards are not seen until it is rehearsed again, and rehearsing again overwrites the document; one plan, one workbench

methods.name: Judge
methods.brief: Returns the verdict of the policy on the plan document held in the workbench, in the house rule report.

parameters.name: pnBench
parameters.role: the workbench the plan was rehearsed into

parameters.name: pcPlanId
parameters.role: the identifier of the plan to judge

methods.returns: a stzRuleReport: IsSound is 1 when no rule fails and Errors lists the failing ones, each naming its rule
notes: a verdict is not a payment: a sound plan still pays nothing until a person commits it

methods.name: Commit
methods.brief: Lets an actor who may change reality release a judged plan: its journal file is written, then each item is paid through the port.

parameters.name: pnBench
parameters.role: the workbench the plan was rehearsed into

parameters.name: pcPlanId
parameters.role: the identifier of the plan to commit

parameters.name: poActor
parameters.role: the actor committing it, such as HumanActor("tresorier")

methods.returns: a list [ committed, reason, detail, results, file ]: committed is 1 or 0, results holds one answer per item, file is the journal path
notes: money out is a plan that a human commits: a refusal is a journal row and a payout.refused event, a commit is a journal row, a payout.committed event and a real file
warnings: a refusal never raises: committed is 0 and reason is unknown-plan, already- committed, policy, rehearsal-differs, actor or crossing, with the cause in detail; a language-model actor, a sandboxed actor and a value that is not an object are all refused for actor; the checks run in that order and the policy is judged before the actor; a plan commits once; an item the port refuses is that item's error in results while the others still go

methods.name: Journal
methods.brief: Returns the desk's record of every commit attempt, oldest first, whether it was refused or went through.
methods.returns: a list of records [ seq, plan, outcome, reason, actor, total, visas ] where outcome is committed or refused
notes: a second desk has its own empty journal

classes.name: stzPayoutPlan
classes.brief: Holds a proposed payout as a plan to be judged and committed by a person, since money out is never a method call.
classes.description: Money out is a PLAN a human commits. A plan names what it pays, whether one payment, a bulk, the return of a payment received, or the acceptance of a request to pay or of a cancellation, and carries the visas of the people who approve it. Building a plan moves nothing: a stzPayoutDesk rehearses it into a workbench, a policy judges the rehearsed document, and only an actor who may change reality, never a language model, can commit it, after which the port releases exactly what the plan names. The weight of a plan is the sum of what it pays, so a payroll cannot be cut into small lines to slip under a threshold. The policy that judges it is the platform's own data. The whole path was run against the in-process twin, which moves no money.
classes.example:
o1.WithId("SUP-2026-10").ProposedBy("treasury-agent")
o1.Returning("E2E-0001", 40000)
o1.Visa("comptable", "A. Issoufou")
o1.Visa("DAF", "M. Garba")
? o1.TotalAmount()
#--> 40000
? o1.NumberOfDistinctVisas()
#--> 2

methods.name: init
methods.brief: Builds an empty plan that pays nothing yet, to be filled by naming what it pays and who gives a visa.
notes: a plan is a proposal: building it, filling it and rehearsing it move no money, and only a person's commit through a stzPayoutDesk releases it

methods.name: WithId
methods.brief: Sets the identifier of the plan, which names its rehearsed document and the file written when it is committed.

parameters.name: pcId
parameters.role: the plan's identifier, as text

methods.returns: the plan itself, so calls chain
notes: the rehearsed document lives at <folder>/<id>.plan.json, so the id is also a file name

methods.name: Id
methods.brief: Returns the identifier of the plan.
methods.returns: a text; empty until WithId is called

methods.name: ProposedBy
methods.brief: Sets the name of whoever proposes the plan, an agent or a person.

parameters.name: pcName
parameters.role: the proposer's name, as text

methods.returns: the plan itself, so calls chain
notes: a policy built with ProposerCannotVisa refuses a plan whose proposer is among its visas

methods.name: Proposer
methods.brief: Returns the name of whoever proposed the plan.
methods.returns: a text; empty until ProposedBy is called

methods.name: Paying
methods.brief: Adds one payment to the plan, kept with the order behind it so that the commit can release exactly that order.

parameters.name: poOrder
parameters.role: the stzPaymentOrder to pay, whose id and amount are read

methods.returns: the plan itself, so calls chain
notes: the item is recorded as kind pay, keyed by the order's transaction id
warnings: a value that is not an object raises error R13 at once

methods.name: PayingBulk
methods.brief: Adds a whole bulk of payments to the plan as one item whose amount is the sum of the batch.

parameters.name: poBatch
parameters.role: the stzPaymentBatch to pay, whose instruction id and total are read

methods.returns: the plan itself, so calls chain
notes: the item is recorded as kind bulk, keyed by the batch's instruction id
