methods.name: Returning
methods.brief: Adds the return of a payment that was received, by its end-to-end id and the amount the hub holds for it.

parameters.name: pcEnd2EndId
parameters.role: the end-to-end id of the payment received

parameters.name: pnAmount
parameters.role: the amount the hub holds for it, in francs

methods.returns: the plan itself, so calls chain
notes: the port refuses the movement at the commit if this amount differs from the hub's (payout-amount-differs); the plan still commits and the refusal is that item's result

methods.name: AcceptingRequest
methods.brief: Adds the acceptance of a request to pay somebody sent us, which is money out, by its end-to-end id and amount.

parameters.name: pcEnd2EndId
parameters.role: the end-to-end id of the request received

parameters.name: pnAmount
parameters.role: the amount of the request, in francs

methods.returns: the plan itself, so calls chain
notes: at the commit the desk answers the request with acceptance through the port

methods.name: AcceptingCancellation
methods.brief: Adds the acceptance of a cancellation request, which returns funds, by its end-to-end id and amount.

parameters.name: pcEnd2EndId
parameters.role: the end-to-end id of the payment to cancel

parameters.name: pnAmount
parameters.role: the amount to return, in francs

methods.returns: the plan itself, so calls chain
notes: refusing a cancellation is not money out and needs no plan

methods.name: Items
methods.brief: Returns what the plan pays, one record per item, in the order they were added.
methods.returns: a list of [ kind, key, amount ] where kind is pay, bulk, return, answer-request or answer-cancellation

methods.name: Objects
methods.brief: Returns the order or batch behind each item, in the same order as Items.
methods.returns: a list with the stzPaymentOrder or stzPaymentBatch for a pay or bulk item, and an empty text for the other kinds

methods.name: NumberOfItems
methods.brief: Returns how many items the plan pays.

methods.name: TotalAmount
methods.brief: Returns the weight of the plan: the sum of every item it pays.
notes: a policy judges this sum, so a payroll cannot be cut into small lines to slip under a threshold

methods.name: Visa
methods.brief: Records the role and the name of a person who approves the plan; the same person signing twice counts once.

parameters.name: pcRole
parameters.role: the role of the signer, such as comptable or DG

parameters.name: pcName
parameters.role: the signer's name

methods.returns: the plan itself, so calls chain
notes: visas added after a rehearsal do not reach the desk until the plan is rehearsed again

methods.name: Visas
methods.brief: Returns every visa recorded, in the order given.

methods.name: NumberOfVisas
methods.brief: Returns how many visas were recorded, signatures and not people.

methods.name: NumberOfDistinctVisas
methods.brief: Returns how many different people gave a visa; the same name in another case is one person and an empty name counts for none.

methods.name: Document
methods.brief: Returns the plan as one JSON text: its id, proposer, items and visas, which is what is rehearsed, judged and committed.
notes: the document holds no credential, and the object behind a pay or bulk item is not in it

classes.name: stzPayoutPolicy
classes.brief: Holds the rules of who must approve a payout plan, as data a platform writes, and judges a plan against them.
classes.description: The rule of which people must approve what is a platform's, so it is data in a policy and never a constant in the port. A policy counts people, not signatures: a person who signs twice, in any case, is one visa. The first rule says above, so a total exactly equal to the threshold needs none. A verdict is a list of findings in the house shape [ rule, subject, where, severity, message ], which joins stzRuleReport, the one CI gate. A policy only judges: it moves nothing and commits nothing. StzDikoPayoutPolicyQ builds one platform's policy, four visas above 100 000 FCFA.
classes.example:
o1.RequireVisasAbove(100000, 4).ProposerCannotVisa()
oPlan = StzPayoutPlanQ().WithId("P1").ProposedBy("agent").Returning("E2E-0001", 250000)
oPlan.Visa("DAF", "M. Garba")
? o1.JudgePlan(oPlan)[1][:rule]
#--> payout-over-100000-needs-4-visas

methods.name: init
methods.brief: Builds a named policy with no rule, which finds fault only with a plan that pays nothing.

parameters.name: pcName
parameters.role: the policy's name, as text

notes: the rule of who must approve what is a platform's data, never a constant of the port: add yours with RequireVisasAbove and ProposerCannotVisa

methods.name: Name
methods.brief: Returns the title the policy was given when it was built.

methods.name: RequireVisasAbove
methods.brief: Adds a rule: a plan whose total is strictly above an amount needs a number of visas from distinct people.

parameters.name: pnAmount
parameters.role: the threshold in francs, a total exactly equal to it needs no visa

parameters.name: pnVisas
parameters.role: how many distinct people must have given a visa

methods.returns: the policy itself, so calls chain
notes: several rules may be added and each one that fails gives its own finding named payout-over-<amount>-needs-<visas>-visas

methods.name: ProposerCannotVisa
methods.brief: Adds separation of duties: the person who proposed a plan may not be one of its visas.
methods.returns: the policy itself, so calls chain
notes: the names are compared without regard to case, and a plan with no proposer is never refused by this rule

methods.name: JudgePlan
methods.brief: Returns the findings of this policy on a plan object, by judging the document the plan would write.

parameters.name: poPlan
parameters.role: the stzPayoutPlan to judge

methods.returns: a list of findings, each [ rule, subject, where, severity, message ]; an empty list means the plan is sound
notes: a desk judges the rehearsed document and not the plan object, so this is for a quick look before rehearsing

methods.name: JudgeDocument
methods.brief: Returns the findings of this policy on a rehearsed plan document, which is what a desk judges and commits.

parameters.name: pcDocument
parameters.role: the plan's JSON text, as Document of the plan returns it

methods.returns: a list of findings, each [ rule, subject, where, severity, message ]; an empty list means the plan is sound
notes: the findings join stzRuleReport, the one CI gate; where is the plan's id
warnings: a plan with no item gives the finding payout-plan-empty whatever the rules

classes.name: stzPCA
classes.brief: Finds the directions along which a table of samples varies most, by singular value decomposition of the centered data.
classes.description: It is the PCA engine behind stzEmbedding; build one with new stzPCA over a list of samples, each a list of feature values (rows are samples, columns are features). You must choose how to prepare the data before Fit: Center keeps the units (covariance PCA, for comparable features) and Standardize divides each feature by its standard deviation (correlation PCA, for features in different units); Fit refuses until you have said which. The variance convention is the library's one authority: the sample one (n-1) by default, UsePopulationVariance for n. After Fit, Components are the directions (a column per component), Scores the samples in those coordinates, ExplainedVariance and its ratio say how much spread each accounts for, Transform projects new rows with the fit's mean and scale, and Inverse sends scores back, with an error equal to the variance of the dropped components. Checked by hand on four samples, [[2,0],[-2,0],[0,1],[0,-1]] under Center: singular values the square roots of 8 and 2, variances 8/3 and 2/3, ratios 0.8 and 0.2.
classes.example:
o1.Center()
o1.Fit()
? @@( o1.ExplainedVarianceRatio() )
#--> [ 0.80, 0.20 ]
? o1.NumberOfComponentsFor(0.9)
#--> 2
? o1.Why()
#--> fitted covariance PCA on 4 sample(s) x 2 feature(s): 2 component(s), the first explaining 80% of the variance

methods.name: init
methods.brief: Builds a principal component analysis over a table of samples, each a list of feature values.

parameters.name: paData
parameters.role: the list of samples (rows), each a list of the same number of numbers (columns are features)

notes: nothing is computed yet: choose Center or Standardize, then Fit

methods.name: NumberOfSamples
methods.brief: Returns how many samples, rows, the data holds.

methods.name: NumberOfFeatures
methods.brief: Returns how many features, columns, each sample holds.

methods.name: Center
methods.brief: Chooses to subtract each feature's mean and keep its units, which gives a covariance PCA.
methods.returns: nothing; CenterQ returns the analysis for chaining
notes: for features of comparable units; Fit refuses to run until Center or Standardize has been called

extensions.name: CenterQ
extensions.adds: does what the method does, then returns the object, so the call can be chained

methods.name: Standardize
methods.brief: Chooses to subtract each feature's mean and divide by its standard deviation, which gives a correlation PCA.
methods.returns: nothing; StandardizeQ returns the analysis for chaining
notes: for features in different units; a constant column is left as zeros and does not break the fit

extensions.name: StandardizeQ
extensions.adds: does what the method does, then returns the object, so the call can be chained

methods.name: Centered
methods.brief: Returns the data with every feature's mean subtracted, leaving the analysis unchanged.
notes: [[2,0],[-2,0],[0,1],[0,-1]] is already centered and comes back as it is

methods.name: Standardized
methods.brief: Returns the data centered and divided by each feature's standard deviation, leaving the analysis unchanged.
notes: the divisor follows the variance convention chosen: [[2,0],[-2,0],[0,1],[0,-1]] gives 1.2247 where the entries were 2, with the sample convention; a constant column becomes zeros

methods.name: IsStandardized
methods.brief: TRUE if Standardize was chosen, FALSE after Center or before any choice.

methods.name: UseSampleVariance
methods.brief: Chooses the sample convention, dividing by n minus 1, which is the default.
methods.returns: nothing; UseSampleVarianceQ returns the analysis for chaining
notes: call it before Fit

extensions.name: UseSampleVarianceQ
extensions.adds: does what the method does, then returns the object, so the call can be chained

methods.name: UsePopulationVariance
methods.brief: Chooses the population convention, dividing by n.
methods.returns: nothing; UsePopulationVarianceQ returns the analysis for chaining
notes: call it before Fit; it changes the variances, not the ratios

extensions.name: UsePopulationVarianceQ
extensions.adds: does what the method does, then returns the object, so the call can be chained

methods.name: UsesSampleVariance
methods.brief: TRUE if the sample convention, dividing by n minus 1, is in force.
notes: 1 on a new analysis

methods.name: Fit
methods.brief: Computes the analysis by singular value decomposition of the prepared data.
methods.returns: nothing; FitQ returns the analysis for chaining
notes: the other reads (Components, Scores...) raise Fit() me first until it has run
warnings: raises an error until Center or Standardize has been called, and another with fewer than two samples

extensions.name: FitQ
extensions.adds: does what the method does, then returns the object, so the call can be chained

methods.name: IsFitted
methods.brief: TRUE if Fit has run.

methods.name: NumberOfComponents
methods.brief: Returns how many components the analysis kept, the smaller of the samples and the features.
notes: 2 for two features
warnings: raises Fit() me first before Fit

methods.name: Components
methods.brief: Returns the directions, one column per component, one row per feature.
methods.returns: a list of rows: row i, column j is how much feature i contributes to component j
notes: Loadings is the same call; the sign is fixed so the largest loading of each component is positive; two features that move together give 0.71 and 0.71 for the first component
warnings: raises Fit() me first before Fit

methods.name: Scores
methods.brief: Returns the samples in component coordinates, one row per sample.
methods.returns: a list of rows, one column per component
notes: each column averages zero; the training rows [[2,0],[-2,0],[0,1],[0,-1]] under Center give themselves back
warnings: raises Fit() me first before Fit

methods.name: SingularValues
methods.brief: Returns the singular value of each component, largest first.
notes: the square of each, divided by n minus 1, is the explained variance: 2.83 and 1.41 for the sample above, whose hand computation is the square roots of 8 and 2
warnings: raises Fit() me first before Fit

methods.name: ExplainedVariance
methods.brief: Returns the variance each component accounts for, largest first.
methods.returns: a list of numbers that add up to TotalVariance
notes: for the sample [[2,0],[-2,0],[0,1],[0,-1]] it gives 8/3 and 2/3 (2.67 and 0.67) with the sample convention and 2 and 0.5 with the population one
warnings: raises Fit() me first before Fit

methods.name: TotalVariance
methods.brief: Returns the total variance of the prepared data, the sum over the components.
notes: 10/3 (3.33) for the sample above with the sample convention, and the number of features when standardized with the sample convention
warnings: raises Fit() me first before Fit

methods.name: ExplainedVarianceRatio
methods.brief: Returns the fraction of the total variance each component accounts for.
methods.returns: a list of numbers that add up to 1
notes: 0.8 and 0.2 for the sample above, by hand 8 over 10 and 2 over 10; a fraction of the spread, not of any cause
warnings: raises Fit() me first before Fit

methods.name: CumulativeVarianceRatio
methods.brief: Returns the running total of the variance ratios, component by component.
methods.returns: a list of numbers ending at 1
notes: 0.8 then 1 for the sample above
warnings: raises Fit() me first before Fit

methods.name: NumberOfComponentsFor
methods.brief: Returns how many leading components are needed to keep a given fraction of the variance.

parameters.name: nWanted
parameters.role: the fraction to keep, above 0 and at most 1

notes: 0.8 needs 1 component and 0.9 needs 2 for the sample above
warnings: raises Fit() me first before Fit

methods.name: Mean
methods.brief: Returns the mean of each feature that Fit subtracted.
methods.returns: a list of numbers, one per feature
notes: new data must be centered with the same means; Transform does it
warnings: raises Fit() me first before Fit

methods.name: Scale
methods.brief: Returns the divisor of each feature that Fit applied: the standard deviations when standardized, 1 otherwise.
methods.returns: a list of numbers, one per feature
notes: 1 and 1 under Center
warnings: raises Fit() me first before Fit

methods.name: Inverse
methods.brief: Returns score rows sent back to feature space, undoing the projection, scale and mean.

parameters.name: paScores
parameters.role: the list of score rows to send back

methods.returns: a list of rows, one column per feature
notes: scores 2, 0 come back as 2, 0 and a single score 2 as 2, 0; the error left is the variance of the dropped components
warnings: raises Fit() me first before Fit; a row longer than the kept components raises an error

methods.name: Reconstructed
methods.brief: Returns the training samples rebuilt from their scores, which shows what the kept components retain.
notes: with every component kept the data comes back, to rounding
warnings: raises Fit() me first before Fit

methods.name: Transform
methods.brief: Projects new rows into the component space with the mean and scale of the fit.

parameters.name: paRows
parameters.role: the list of rows to project, each as long as the fitted features

methods.returns: a list of rows, one column per component
notes: rows unseen by the fit land in the same space as Scores; [[2,0],[0,1],[1,1]] gives 2,0 and 0,1 and 1,1 for the sample above
warnings: raises Fit() me first before Fit

methods.name: Why
methods.brief: Returns one sentence naming the kind of analysis, its shape and the share the first component explains.
notes: fitted covariance PCA on 4 sample(s) x 2 feature(s): 2 component(s), the first explaining 80% of the variance
warnings: raises Fit() me first before Fit

classes.name: stzPCIDSSRuleBase
classes.brief: Holds the PCI-DSS compliance rules for an org chart, ready to pass to CheckCompliance.
classes.description: Holds the four universal org rules and no rule of its own yet: only the name tells it from the other regimes.
classes.example:
? o1.NumberOfRules()
#--> 4

methods.name: init
methods.brief: Builds the PCI-DSS rule base: the four universal org rules under the name PCI-DSS; it adds no rule of its own.
methods.returns: nothing; the rule base is built
warnings: only the name tells the regimes apart today

classes.name: stzPerfMonitor
classes.brief: Samples the process senses into gauges on a cadence, holds your own counters, gauges and timers, and renders them for Prometheus or OpenTelemetry.
classes.description: Declare what to watch (WatchMemory, WatchCpu, WatchSystemMemory), then sample in one of three ways: call Sample yourself, call Tick from any loop (it samples only when the Every interval has passed), or host the monitor on an agent host through Name_ and Cycle. Register your own metrics with NewCounter, NewGauge and NewTimer and read any metric back with MetricQ. Prometheus and OtelJson render all of them, Explain and Show describe them in text, and EnableTracing keeps the last request traces. The numbers are engine-side, so copies of the monitor agree; call Destroy when done. Live values change on every run: test them as ranges and signs, never as exact numbers.
classes.example:
o1.WatchMemory().WatchCpu().Every(250)
? o1.Sample()
#--> 2
? o1.Sample()
#--> 3
? o1.MetricQ("process.memory.rss").Value() > 0
#--> 1
o1.NewCounter("orders").Increment()
? o1.MetricQ("orders").Value()
#--> 1
? @@( o1.Metrics()[4] )
#--> [ "orders", "counter" ]
? o1.SampleCount()
#--> 2
? o1.EveryMs()
#--> 250
o1.Destroy()

methods.name: init
methods.brief: Builds a monitor with the given name, watching nothing yet, sampling every 1000 ms and with tracing off.

parameters.name: pcName
parameters.role: the monitor's name, which becomes the service name in the OpenTelemetry output

methods.name: Name
methods.brief: Returns the monitor's name.

methods.name: Name_
methods.brief: Returns the monitor's name under the spelling the agent-host contract expects.

methods.name: WatchMemory
methods.brief: Declares that every sample reads the process memory, and registers the gauges process.memory.rss and process.memory.peak.
methods.returns: the monitor itself, so calls chain
notes: calling it twice registers nothing more

methods.name: WatchCpu
methods.brief: Declares that every sample reads the CPU use of the process, and registers the gauge process.cpu.utilization.
methods.returns: the monitor itself, so calls chain
notes: the first sample only sets the baseline, so the gauge is written from the second sample on

methods.name: WatchSystemMemory
methods.brief: Declares that every sample reads the free physical memory of the machine, and registers the gauge system.memory.free.
methods.returns: the monitor itself, so calls chain

methods.name: Every
methods.brief: Sets the interval, in milliseconds, that Tick and RunFor wait between two samples.

parameters.name: pnMs
parameters.role: the interval in milliseconds, 1 or more

methods.returns: the monitor itself, so calls chain
warnings: a value below 1 or one that is not a number is ignored and the old interval stays

methods.name: EveryMs
methods.brief: Returns the sampling interval in milliseconds.
methods.returns: a number; 1000 on a new monitor

methods.name: EnableTracing
methods.brief: Starts keeping the last requests' traces in an engine ring, and does nothing if tracing is already on.

parameters.name: pnCapacity
parameters.role: how many traces the ring keeps

methods.returns: the monitor itself, so calls chain
notes: turn it on before handing the monitor to a server, which stores a copy at that moment

methods.name: IsTracing
methods.brief: TRUE if tracing was turned on and not yet destroyed.

methods.name: RecordTrace
methods.brief: Adds one request trace to the ring, stamped with the wall clock; ignored when tracing is off.

parameters.name: pcTraceId
parameters.role: the identifier of the trace

parameters.name: pcPath
parameters.role: the request path

parameters.name: pnStatus
parameters.role: the response status such as 200

parameters.name: pnDurMs
parameters.role: how long the request took in milliseconds

methods.returns: the monitor itself, so calls chain

methods.name: TraceCount
methods.brief: Returns how many traces were recorded since tracing started, or 0 when tracing is off.
notes: it counts every trace ever recorded, so it can exceed the ring's capacity; RecentTraces returns at most the capacity

methods.name: RecentTraces
methods.brief: Returns the newest traces, oldest of them first, up to the number asked for.

parameters.name: pnHowMany
parameters.role: how many of the newest traces to return

methods.returns: a list of hash-lists with traceId, path, status, durMs and wallMs; [ ] when tracing is off

methods.name: NewCounter
methods.brief: Registers a counter of your own and returns it, ready to count up.

parameters.name: pcName
parameters.role: the metric's name, unique in this monitor

warnings: raises an error when a metric of that name is already registered

extensions.name: NewCounterXT
extensions.adds: the extended form: more parameters than the base method

methods.name: NewGauge
methods.brief: Registers a gauge of your own and returns it, ready to hold a value that goes up and down.

parameters.name: pcName
parameters.role: the metric's name, unique in this monitor

warnings: raises an error when a metric of that name is already registered

extensions.name: NewGaugeXT
extensions.adds: the extended form: more parameters than the base method

methods.name: NewTimer
methods.brief: Registers a timer of your own and returns it, ready to record durations in milliseconds.

parameters.name: pcName
parameters.role: the metric's name, unique in this monitor

warnings: raises an error when a metric of that name is already registered

extensions.name: NewTimerXT
extensions.adds: the extended form: more parameters than the base method

methods.name: HasMetric
methods.brief: TRUE if a metric of this name is registered, among the watched ones or your own.

parameters.name: pcName
parameters.role: the metric's name

methods.name: MetricQ
methods.brief: Returns the registered metric of this name, a chainable object that shares its numbers with the registry.

parameters.name: pcName
parameters.role: the metric's name

warnings: raises an error naming the metric when none is registered

methods.name: Metrics
methods.brief: Returns the registry as data, one pair of name and kind for each metric, in registration order.
methods.returns: a list of pairs such as [ "queue", "gauge" ]

methods.name: NumberOfMetrics
methods.brief: Returns how many metrics are registered.

methods.name: Sample
methods.brief: Reads every declared sense now, whether due or not, and writes the gauges.
methods.returns: the number of gauge writes made, a number; 0 when nothing is watched
notes: the first sample with the CPU watched writes one gauge fewer, as it only sets the baseline

methods.name: SampleCount
methods.brief: Returns how many samples have been taken.

methods.name: SelfCost
methods.brief: Returns what the sampling itself has cost, measured on the monotonic clock.
methods.returns: a hash-list with samples, totalMs and perSampleMs
notes: totalMs and perSampleMs vary from run to run, so test them as ranges

methods.name: Tick
methods.brief: Takes a sample only when the interval has passed since the last one, so any loop can call it freely.
methods.returns: 1 if it sampled, 0 if not yet due; the first call always samples

methods.name: RunFor
methods.brief: Keeps ticking for the given time, sleeping between samples, and blocks until it ends.

parameters.name: pnMs
parameters.role: how long to run, in milliseconds

methods.returns: the monitor itself, so calls chain
warnings: meant for scripts and guards; a server should host the monitor instead

methods.name: Prometheus
methods.brief: Renders every metric in the Prometheus text format served at /metrics.
methods.returns: a text of HELP and TYPE lines followed by the values; empty text with no metric
notes: a labeled family with no child yet prints one line with the label value _overflow

methods.name: OtelJson
methods.brief: Renders every metric as one OpenTelemetry metrics envelope in JSON.
methods.returns: a text holding the JSON, with the monitor's name as service name

methods.name: Explain
methods.brief: Describes the monitor and each metric in plain lines of text.
methods.returns: a list of text, the first line giving the metric count, interval and sample count

methods.name: Show
methods.brief: Prints the lines of the explanation on the console.

methods.name: Destroy
methods.brief: Frees the engine handles of every metric and of the trace ring, and empties the registry.
methods.returns: the monitor itself, so calls chain
notes: call it when done, as engine handles are not freed by Ring

classes.name: stzPerfPlan
classes.brief: Holds a performance tuning plan as proposed actions that only an effectful actor may commit, with every outcome audited.
classes.description: Optimization crosses reality: scaling a fleet, draining workers, healing the dead. Expression is free and admission is governed. The plan's catalog is closed: ScaleUp, ScaleDown and RestartDead, each mapping to one verb on the target. An actor whose effects are empty, such as an inference- only LLMActor, can build the plan, explain it and hand it over, but ExecuteOn refuses it wholesale and audits each refusal; a HumanActor commits. MayCommit answers admissibility before any attempt. The audit trail holds [ n, verdict, action, tag, actor, why ] for every outcome, so refusals are never silent.
classes.receiver: o1 = StzPerfPlan("relieve-nlp") o1.Propose(:ScaleUp, "nlp", "measured load 0.92 > high-water 0.75") o1.Propose(:RestartDead, "nlp", "2 dead workers") oAdvisor = LLMActor("advisor") oChief = HumanActor("mansour")
classes.example:
? o1.NumberOfActions()
#--> 2
? o1.Actions()[1][1]
#--> scaleup
? o1.MayCommit(oAdvisor)
#--> 0
? o1.MayCommit(oChief)
#--> 1
? o1.WasExecuted()
#--> 0
? o1.Explain()[1]
#--> Perf plan relieve-nlp -- 2 proposed action(s).

methods.name: init
methods.brief: Builds an empty plan of tuning actions under a name.

parameters.name: pcName
parameters.role: the name of the plan

notes: StzPerfPlan builds the same object; building and explaining a plan is free, only committing it is governed

methods.name: Name
methods.brief: Returns the name the plan was built with.

methods.name: Propose
methods.brief: Adds one action to the plan, with the reason for it; nothing is executed.

parameters.name: pcAction
parameters.role: ScaleUp, ScaleDown or RestartDead, in any letter case

parameters.name: pcTag
parameters.role: the tag of the part of the fleet it concerns, kept in lower case

parameters.name: pcRationale
parameters.role: why, as a sentence, kept in the audit

methods.returns: the plan itself, so calls chain
notes: the action is stored in lower case, such as scaleup
warnings: an action outside the closed catalog, such as Reboot, raises error stzPerfPlan: unknown action ... The catalog is closed

methods.name: Actions
methods.brief: Returns the proposed actions in order.
methods.returns: a list of [ action, tag, rationale ]

methods.name: NumberOfActions
methods.brief: Returns how many actions the plan holds.

methods.name: MayCommit
methods.brief: TRUE if an actor is admitted to commit the plan, asked before any attempt.

parameters.name: poActor
parameters.role: the actor, such as LLMActor or HumanActor

notes: an actor that is not effectful, or whose posture is sandboxed, is refused, so an inference-only advisor may build and explain a plan but never commit it

methods.name: ExecuteOn
methods.brief: Applies the plan to a target when the actor may commit it, and audits every action as committed or refused.

parameters.name: poTarget
parameters.role: a stzAppCluster or any object answering ScaleUp(tag), ScaleDown(tag) and RestartDead()

parameters.name: poActor
parameters.role: the actor asking to commit

methods.returns: the number of actions committed; 0 when the actor was refused, with one refused line for each action in the audit
notes: a RestartDead heals every dead worker in one call, and a second RestartDead in the same plan is counted as committed without calling the target again; refused attempts stay in the trail beside later committed ones

methods.name: WasExecuted
methods.brief: TRUE if the plan was committed at least once.
notes: a refusal does not set it

methods.name: AuditTrail
methods.brief: Returns every outcome so far, refusals included.
methods.returns: a list of [ n, verdict, action, tag, actor name, why ], verdict being committed or refused, n the action's position in the plan; [ ] before any attempt
notes: a refusal says the actor is not effectful or sandboxed and that expression is free while admission is governed

methods.name: RefusedCount
methods.brief: Returns how many audit lines are refusals.
notes: an attempt by a refused actor adds one for each action in the plan

methods.name: CommittedCount
methods.brief: Returns how many audit lines are commits.

methods.name: Explain
methods.brief: Returns the plan as lines of text: a header, each proposed action with its reason, then the audit if there is one.

methods.name: Show
methods.brief: Prints the explanation to the console, one line per line.
notes: it prints with the ? statement

classes.name: stzPerfProfile
classes.brief: Turns a monitor's measured numbers into operational analysis: throughput, utilization, service demand and response time over an interval.
classes.description: The instruments measure and the profile understands. It speaks the vocabulary of operational analysis: U utilization, R response time, X throughput and D, the CPU milliseconds each request consumed. It applies the laws that bind them (the utilization law and Little's law, each checked against a second, independent measurement), splits a request's time into computing and waiting, and forecasts memory growth. A profile is interval-based: it anchors at birth and every answer covers the time since; Mark starts a fresh interval. Assert ranges and signs on live readings, never exact values, and profile over many requests, because Windows accounts CPU in 15.625 ms ticks.
classes.example:
? o1.Requests()
#--> 0
? o1.ServiceDemandMs()
#--> 0
? o1.Bottleneck()[:kind]
#--> cpu
? o1.UtilizationCheck()[:sampled]
#--> -1
? o1.HoursToMemoryCeiling(1000)
#--> -1

methods.name: init
methods.brief: Builds a profile of a performance monitor and anchors it there, so every answer covers the time since.

parameters.name: poMonitor
parameters.role: the stzPerfMonitor whose request timer and CPU numbers are analysed

methods.name: Mark
methods.brief: Moves the anchor to now, so the next answers cover a fresh interval and forget the earlier one.
methods.returns: the profile itself, so calls chain

methods.name: MonitorQ
methods.brief: Returns the monitor this profile reads.

methods.name: IntervalMs
methods.brief: Returns how many milliseconds have passed since the anchor, on the monotonic clock.

methods.name: Requests
methods.brief: Returns how many requests the monitor counted since the anchor.
methods.returns: a number; 0 when the monitor has no http.requests counter

methods.name: Throughput
methods.brief: Returns X, the requests completed per second over the interval.
methods.returns: a number; 0 when no time has passed

methods.name: CpuMsUsed
methods.brief: Returns the CPU time the whole process consumed since the anchor, in milliseconds, all threads together.
notes: Windows counts CPU in 15.625 ms ticks, so a short interval reads 0 or one tick: average over many ticks

methods.name: Utilization
methods.brief: Returns U, the fraction of the whole machine's CPU this process used over the interval.
methods.returns: a number from 0 to 1; 0 when no time has passed

methods.name: ServiceDemandMs
methods.brief: Returns D, the CPU milliseconds each request consumed, the profile's most diagnostic number.
methods.returns: a number; 0 when no request completed
notes: D counts the whole process, so a quiet interval with few requests is quantized by the CPU tick

methods.name: MaxThroughput
methods.brief: Returns the requests per second at which this machine saturates if the CPU is the constraint.

methods.name: LoadRatio
methods.brief: Returns how close the workload is to its CPU ceiling, throughput over maximum throughput, capped at 1.
methods.returns: a number from 0 to 1; 0 when nothing is measurable yet

methods.name: Headroom
methods.brief: Returns how much of the CPU ceiling remains, 1 minus throughput over maximum throughput.
methods.returns: a number from 0 to 1; 0 when nothing is measurable yet

methods.name: UtilizationCheck
methods.brief: Compares the utilization computed from the anchors with the monitor's independently sampled CPU gauge.
methods.returns: a hashlist with the keys computed, sampled, consistent and message; sampled is -1 and consistent 0 when the monitor does not watch the CPU
notes: the two agree when within a factor of 3; a disagreement means the measurement is broken, not the machine

methods.name: LittleN
methods.brief: Returns N, the average requests in flight that Little's law implies from throughput and mean response time.

methods.name: LittleCheckAgainst
methods.brief: Compares the implied requests in flight with a concurrency you measured elsewhere, for example a worker pool's.

parameters.name: pnMeasured
parameters.role: the concurrency you counted, as a number

methods.returns: a hashlist with the keys implied, measured, consistent and message
notes: consistent means within a factor of 3, with both sides floored at 0.05 so tiny numbers agree

methods.name: ResponseTimeMeanMs
methods.brief: Returns R, the mean response time in milliseconds of the requests completed since the anchor.
methods.returns: a number; 0 when none completed or the monitor has no http.request.ms timer

methods.name: ResponseTimeP50
methods.brief: Returns the median response time in milliseconds, over the timer's retained window.
methods.returns: a number; 0 when the monitor has no http.request.ms timer
notes: a window percentile, not an interval one: it can include requests from before the anchor

methods.name: ResponseTimeP95
methods.brief: Returns the response time in milliseconds under which 95 percent of requests fall, over the timer's window.
methods.returns: a number; 0 when the monitor has no http.request.ms timer

methods.name: ResponseTimeP99
methods.brief: Returns the response time in milliseconds under which 99 percent of requests fall, over the timer's window.
methods.returns: a number; 0 when the monitor has no http.request.ms timer

methods.name: WaitMsPerRequest
methods.brief: Returns the part of each request's mean response time that was not computation: waiting on IO, locks or queues.
methods.returns: a number of milliseconds, never below 0

methods.name: Bottleneck
methods.brief: Answers whether the app is busy or blocked, by splitting each request's time into CPU computed and time waited.
methods.returns: a hashlist with the keys kind (cpu or waiting, whichever share is larger), cpuMsPerRequest, waitMsPerRequest and maxThroughput
notes: with no requests it answers cpu and zeros

methods.name: MemoryTrendPerHour
methods.brief: Returns the bytes per hour by which the monitor's resident memory gauge is trending, positive when growing.
methods.returns: a number; 0 when the monitor does not watch memory

methods.name: HoursToMemoryCeiling
methods.brief: Returns the hours until resident memory reaches a ceiling at the current trend.

parameters.name: pnCeilingBytes
parameters.role: the memory ceiling, in bytes

methods.returns: a number of hours; 0 when memory is already at or past the ceiling, -1 when it is not growing or is not watched

methods.name: Snapshot
methods.brief: Records one point of the response-time-versus-throughput curve for the current interval and returns it.
methods.returns: a list [ atMs, X, U, D, Rp95 ]
notes: only the newest 128 points are kept

methods.name: Curve
methods.brief: Returns the points recorded by Snapshot, in recording order.
methods.returns: a list of [ atMs, X, U, D, Rp95 ] rows

methods.name: Explain
methods.brief: Returns a narration of the interval in lines: work done, CPU, service demand, response time, Little's law and the constraint.
notes: a monitor with no request instruments gets only the CPU line

methods.name: Show
methods.brief: Prints the narration of the interval, one line per row.

classes.name: stzPerfSentinel
classes.brief: Judges an SLA on a cadence and turns changes of verdict into alerts, one when a breach appears and one when it clears.
classes.description: An SLA judges when asked; the sentinel judges on a cadence and is edge-triggered, which is the honest flap suppression: a breach fires once when it appears and a recovery once when it clears, so an invariant that stays broken does not page you four hundred times. Run it three ways: Check whenever you like, Every and Tick from any loop, or hosted by an agent host through Name_ and Cycle. Every alert also goes out on the engine event bus, perf.breach and perf.clear, and a new breach takes a black-box snapshot of the process. The ledger keeps the newest 256 alerts. Explain and Show raise error R41 today while a rule is breached.
classes.receiver: oMon = StzPerfMonitor("api") oDepth = oMon.NewGauge("queue.depth") oDepth.Set(50) oSla = StzSla("api") oSla.ExpectValue("queue.depth").AtMost(100) o1 = StzPerfSentinel(oSla, oMon)
classes.example:
? o1.Check()
#--> 0
oDepth.Set(150)
? o1.Check()
#--> 1
? o1.IsBreached()
#--> 1
? @@( o1.ActiveBreaches() )
#--> [ "value-queue.depth-under-100" ]
? o1.Check()
#--> 0
? o1.LastAlert()[2]
#--> breach
? o1.LastBlackBox()[:metrics][1][3]
#--> 150
oDepth.Set(10)
? o1.Check()
#--> 0
? o1.LastAlert()[2]
#--> clear
? o1.CheckCount()
#--> 4

methods.name: init
methods.brief: Builds a sentinel that judges an SLA against a monitor on a cadence and turns verdict changes into alerts.

parameters.name: poSla
parameters.role: the stzSla to judge

parameters.name: poMonitor
parameters.role: the stzPerfMonitor whose metrics it reads

methods.returns: nothing; the object is built with its own event bus and no breach
notes: StzPerfSentinel builds the same object; the SLA is copied at birth, the monitor copy shares the engine-backed metrics, and the sentinel's own transition state lives in Ring, so one copy should drive Check and Tick

methods.name: Name
methods.brief: Returns the sentinel's name.
methods.returns: the name as text, perf-sentinel until SetName changes it

methods.name: Name_
methods.brief: Returns the sentinel's name, the form an agent host asks for.
methods.returns: the name as text, the same as Name

methods.name: SetName
methods.brief: Sets the sentinel's name.

parameters.name: pcName
parameters.role: the new name, a non-empty text

methods.returns: the sentinel itself, so calls chain

methods.name: OnBreach
methods.brief: Sets the function called once when a rule newly breaches.

parameters.name: pfCallback
parameters.role: a function taking the finding, a hash list with rule, subject, where, severity and message

methods.returns: the sentinel itself, so calls chain
notes: it is edge-triggered: a rule that stays broken does not call it again

methods.name: OnClear
methods.brief: Sets the function called once when a breached rule recovers.

parameters.name: pfCallback
parameters.role: a function taking the name of the rule that recovered

methods.returns: the sentinel itself, so calls chain

methods.name: SetChannels
methods.brief: Sets the names of the process-wide event channels the alerts are also published on.

parameters.name: pcBreach
parameters.role: the channel for breaches

parameters.name: pcClear
parameters.role: the channel for recoveries

methods.returns: the sentinel itself, so calls chain
notes: the defaults are perf.breach and perf.clear, so an agent supervised on a channel wakes when the SLA breaks

methods.name: BreachChannel
methods.brief: Returns the channel breaches are published on.
methods.returns: the channel name as text, perf.breach by default

methods.name: ClearChannel
methods.brief: Returns the channel recoveries are published on.
methods.returns: the channel name as text, perf.clear by default

methods.name: Every
methods.brief: Sets the cadence of Tick.

parameters.name: pnMs
parameters.role: the interval in milliseconds, 1 or more

methods.returns: the sentinel itself, so calls chain
notes: the default is 1000

methods.name: Check
methods.brief: Judges the SLA once and fires alerts for the changes since the last judgment only.
methods.returns: the number of new breaches in this pass
notes: a new breach logs, photographs the process in the black box, publishes on the breach channel and calls OnBreach; a recovery logs, publishes on the clear channel and calls OnClear; a breach that persists does nothing, which is the flap suppression; an unmeasured expectation counts as a breach

methods.name: CheckCount
methods.brief: Returns how many judgments have been made.

methods.name: Tick
methods.brief: Judges the SLA if the cadence says it is due, for any loop to call.
methods.returns: the number of new breaches; 0 when it was not due
notes: the first call is always due, then the next one waits for Every milliseconds on the monotonic clock; Cycle is the same call, which makes the sentinel hostable by a stzAgentHost

methods.name: ActiveBreaches
methods.brief: Returns the rules in breach as of the last judgment.

methods.name: IsBreached
methods.brief: TRUE if any rule is in breach as of the last judgment.

methods.name: AlertLog
methods.brief: Returns the alerts so far, breaches and recoveries, oldest first.
methods.returns: a list of [ time in milliseconds, breach or clear, rule, message ]; at most the newest 256
notes: the time is on the monotonic clock; a recovery's message is recovered

methods.name: LastAlert
methods.brief: Returns the newest alert.
methods.returns: a list [ time, breach or clear, rule, message ]; [ ] when there is none

methods.name: Explain
methods.brief: Returns the state as lines of text: the name, the number of checks and whether expectations are met, then each breached rule.
notes: with no breach the single line reads Sentinel name -- N check(s), all expectations met.
warnings: raises error R41 Invalid numeric string whenever a rule is in breach, because the state text adds the number of breaches to a text; it answers well only while nothing is breached

methods.name: Show
methods.brief: Prints the explanation to the console, one line per line.
notes: it prints with the ? statement
warnings: raises the same error R41 as Explain while a rule is in breach

methods.name: BlackBox
methods.brief: Returns the flight-recorder snapshots, one taken at each new breach.
methods.returns: a list of hash lists, the newest 16
notes: each holds at, rule, message, rssBytes, peakBytes, cpuMs, sysFreeBytes, the current value of every metric and the recent trace ids; the values are live, so assert ranges and signs

methods.name: LastBlackBox
methods.brief: Returns the newest flight-recorder snapshot.
methods.returns: a hash list with the keys at, rule, message, rssBytes, peakBytes, cpuMs, sysFreeBytes, metrics and traces; [ ] when there is none
notes: metrics is a list of [ name, kind, value ]; traces is [ ] when the monitor does not trace

classes.name: stzPerfSeries
classes.brief: Keeps the latest samples of a metric in a fixed-size window held by the engine, and answers statistics over it.
classes.description: Recording is constant-time and the memory is fixed at creation: a series left running for a month costs what one left for an hour does. Past its capacity the oldest samples are overwritten, so Count says how many were ever recorded and Size how many are kept; every statistic answers over the kept window only. Percentile is exact (nearest rank), unlike the bucketed latency histogram: choose the histogram for an unbounded stream and the series for a windowed gauge. SlopePerMs is the leak detector. Call Destroy when done, because the samples live in the engine.
classes.example:
for i = 1 to 6 o1.RecordAt(i * 1000, i * 10) next
? o1.Size()
#--> 4
? o1.Count()
#--> 6
? @@( o1.Values() )
#--> [ 30, 40, 50, 60 ]
? o1.Percentile(50)
#--> 40
? o1.SlopePerMs()
#--> 0.01

methods.name: init
methods.brief: Builds a series that keeps the latest samples of a metric in a fixed-size window held by the engine.

parameters.name: pnCapacity
parameters.role: how many samples the window retains

methods.name: Handle
methods.brief: Returns the engine pointer that holds the samples, to share the series with other engine calls.

methods.name: AdoptHandle
methods.brief: Makes the series read and write a window owned elsewhere, freeing the one it made for itself.

parameters.name: pEngineHandle
parameters.role: the engine pointer of the series to adopt, for example the Handle of another series

methods.returns: the series itself, so calls chain
notes: Destroy on the adopter leaves the owner's samples untouched
warnings: an adopted window is never freed by this object: freeing it stays with its owner

methods.name: Capacity
methods.brief: Returns how many samples the window can hold at most.

methods.name: Record
methods.brief: Adds a value to the window, stamped with the engine's monotonic clock in milliseconds.

parameters.name: nValue
parameters.role: the number to record

methods.returns: the series itself, so calls chain

methods.name: RecordAt
methods.brief: Adds a value to the window against a time you supply, in milliseconds of your own clock.

parameters.name: nTimeMs
parameters.role: the time of the sample, in the unit of the clock you chose

parameters.name: nValue
parameters.role: the number to record

methods.returns: the series itself, so calls chain

methods.name: Count
methods.brief: Returns how many samples were ever recorded, including those the window has already overwritten.

methods.name: Size
methods.brief: Returns how many samples the window holds now, never more than its capacity.

methods.name: Last
methods.brief: Returns the most recent value recorded.
methods.returns: a number; 0 for an empty series

methods.name: Min
methods.brief: Returns the smallest value in the window.
methods.returns: a number; 0 for an empty series

methods.name: Max
methods.brief: Returns the largest value in the window.
methods.returns: a number; 0 for an empty series

methods.name: Mean
methods.brief: Returns the average of the values in the window.
methods.returns: a number; 0 for an empty series

methods.name: SlopePerMs
methods.brief: Returns the least-squares slope of the values over time, per millisecond: near 0 is stable, positive is growing.
methods.returns: a number; 0 for an empty series
notes: with a clock in milliseconds, a rise of 10 over 2000 ms is 0.005; use it to spot a leak

methods.name: Percentile
methods.brief: Returns the value at a rank, as the exact nearest-rank percentile over the window.

parameters.name: nP
parameters.role: the percentage from 0 to 100, such as 95

methods.returns: a number; 0 for an empty series
notes: 0 gives the smallest value and 100 the largest

methods.name: P50
methods.brief: Returns the median value of the window.
methods.returns: a number; 0 for an empty series

methods.name: P95
methods.brief: Returns the value under which 95 percent of the window lies.
methods.returns: a number; 0 for an empty series

methods.name: P99
methods.brief: Returns the value under which 99 percent of the window lies.
methods.returns: a number; 0 for an empty series

methods.name: TimeAt
methods.brief: Returns the time of the nth sample in the window, oldest first.

parameters.name: n
parameters.role: the position in the window, from 1 for the oldest sample

methods.returns: a number; -1 when n is 0 or beyond the window

methods.name: ValueAt
methods.brief: Returns the value of the nth sample in the window, oldest first.

parameters.name: n
parameters.role: the position in the window, from 1 for the oldest sample

methods.returns: a number; -1 when n is 0 or beyond the window
notes: -1 is also a legal sample value: check Size before reading

methods.name: Values
methods.brief: Returns the whole window as a list of numbers, oldest first.
methods.returns: a list of numbers; empty for an empty series
notes: it crosses the engine bridge once per sample, so keep it for display and small windows

methods.name: Times
methods.brief: Returns the times of the whole window as a list of numbers, oldest first.
methods.returns: a list of numbers; empty for an empty series

methods.name: Reset
methods.brief: Empties the window and the count and keeps the capacity.
methods.returns: the series itself, so calls chain

methods.name: Destroy
methods.brief: Frees the engine memory of the series; any later call builds a fresh, empty window.
methods.returns: the series itself, so calls chain

classes.name: stzPetriNet
classes.brief: Draws a Petri net whose state is on the picture, and plays the token game: transitions fire only when their input places hold enough tokens.
classes.description: A place holds tokens, a transition moves them, and the same drawing read twice a moment apart shows two different facts. Places and transitions are typed nodes, arcs are directed edges with a weight, and the net is meant to be bipartite: an arc joins a place to a transition or a transition to a place, which the first of five rules reports when it does not. The token game is Tokens, SetTokens, Marking, IsEnabled, Enabled and Fire; a refused firing says which place is short and by how much, and a net never goes negative. Tokens are drawn inside the place, one to four as dots and more as the number, and published by RenderTokens. Not computed: reachability, boundedness and liveness in the full sense. Not here: inhibitor arcs, coloured tokens, timed transitions and priorities.
classes.example:
o1.AddPlaceXT("idle", "Idle", 3)
o1.AddPlace("busy", "Busy")
o1.AddTransition("start", "Start")
o1.ArcXT("idle", "start", 2)
o1.Arc("start", "busy")
? o1.IsEnabled("start")
#--> 1
o1.Fire("start")
? @@( o1.Marking() )
#--> [ [ "idle", 1 ], [ "busy", 1 ] ]
? o1.WhyNotEnabled("start")
#--> place 'Idle' holds 1 and the arc wants 2
? len(o1.Enabled())
#--> 0

methods.name: init
methods.brief: Builds an empty Petri net that draws left to right with the Petri notation, with a title.

parameters.name: pcTitle
parameters.role: the title of the diagram

methods.name: AddPlace

parameters.name: pcId

methods.returns: the net itself, so calls chain

extensions.name: AddPlaceXT
extensions.adds: the extended form: more parameters than the base method

extensions.name: AddPlaceXTQ
extensions.adds: the extended form: more parameters than the base method; does what the method does, then returns the object, so the call can be chained

methods.brief: Declares a transition, the bar across the flow that moves tokens when it fires.

parameters.name: pcId
parameters.role: the transition's identifier, which must be new in the net

parameters.name: pcName
parameters.role: the transition's name, shown beside its bar

methods.returns: the net itself, so calls chain
notes: AddTransitionQ is the same call

extensions.name: AddTransitionQ
extensions.adds: does what the method does, then returns the object, so the call can be chained

methods.name: AddNote

parameters.name: pcId

parameters.name: pcText

methods.returns: the net itself, so calls chain

methods.name: Arc
methods.brief: Draws a token path from one node to another with weight 1; ArcXT gives the weight.

parameters.name: pcFrom

parameters.name: pcTo
parameters.role: the identifier of the place or transition it enters

extensions.name: ArcXT
extensions.adds: the extended form: more parameters than the base method

extensions.name: ArcQ
extensions.adds: does what the method does, then returns the object, so the call can be chained

extensions.name: ArcXTQ
extensions.adds: the extended form: more parameters than the base method; does what the method does, then returns the object, so the call can be chained

methods.name: Places
methods.brief: Returns the places, in the order they were added, with their current tokens.

methods.name: Transitions
methods.brief: Returns the transitions, in the order they were added.
methods.returns: a list of hashlists with the keys id and name

methods.name: Arcs
methods.brief: Returns the arcs, in the order they were added.

methods.name: Tokens
methods.brief: Returns how many tokens a place holds now.

parameters.name: pcPlace

parameters.name: pnTokens

methods.returns: the net itself, so calls chain

methods.name: Marking
methods.brief: Returns the marking: every place with its current tokens, the state of the net.

warnings: an identifier that is not a transition raises an error

methods.name: IsEnabled
