methods.returns: the net itself, so calls chain
notes: FireQ is the same call
warnings: a transition that is not enabled raises an error naming the short place and the numbers, and changes nothing, so a net never goes negative

extensions.name: FireQ
extensions.adds: does what the method does, then returns the object, so the call can be chained

methods.name: AsRuleGraph
methods.brief: Returns the net as a plain graph that the five Petri rules read.
methods.returns: a stzGraph with the places, transitions and notes as nodes and the arcs as edges

methods.name: GovernanceFindings
methods.brief: Returns what the five Petri rules find wrong with the net, warnings included.
methods.returns: a list of findings, each a hashlist with the keys rule, where, severity and message; empty when the net is sound
notes: CheckRules is the same call
warnings: the rules are arc_joins_place_and_transition, transition_has_input, transition_has_output, place_can_be_marked and transition_can_fire

methods.name: GovernanceIsSound
methods.brief: TRUE if the rules found no error; warnings do not count against it.
warnings: RulesAreSound is the same call

methods.name: RenderTokens
methods.brief: Returns what the last drawing wrote inside each place.
methods.returns: a list of [ place, count, x, y ] rows; empty before the first drawing
warnings: one to four tokens are drawn as dots, five or more as the number

classes.name: stzPetriRule
classes.brief: Holds one named check of the Petri-net governance, run over the rule graph of a net.
classes.description: It is a graph rule filed under the petri domain. The five rules the library ships are built by stzPetriRuleSet and applied through the net's GovernanceFindings; a rule of your own can be added to a set the same way.
classes.example:
? o1.Name()
#--> my_rule
? o1.Domain()
#--> petri

methods.name: init
methods.brief: Builds a named rule of the Petri-net governance, filed under the petri domain.

parameters.name: pcName
parameters.role: the rule's name, such as place_can_be_marked

classes.name: stzPetriRuleSet
classes.brief: Holds the five rules a Petri net is judged by: arcs join a place and a transition, transitions have inputs and outputs, places can be marked, transitions can fire.
classes.description: Check takes the rule graph of a net (AsRuleGraph) and answers the findings. A net asks for this through its own GovernanceFindings, so a rule set is built by hand only to add a rule of your own or to run the rules on a graph. The last two rules are structural: a place empty forever and a transition starved at birth, not liveness in the full sense.
classes.example:
? o1.Name()
#--> petri-governance
? o1.NumberOfRules()
#--> 5
? o1.RuleNames()[1]
#--> arc_joins_place_and_transition

methods.name: init
methods.brief: Builds the Petri-net governance, the set of five rules a net is judged by.
warnings: the rules are arc_joins_place_and_transition, transition_has_input, transition_has_output, place_can_be_marked and transition_can_fire, in that order

classes.name: stzPIAgent
classes.brief: Holds an agent that perceives its memory, decides under governance, acts through verified skills and can say why.
classes.description: A stzPIAgent is assembled from parts that already exist: a stzAgentMemory over a knowledge graph, stzAgentSkill objects (precondition, action, check) and a stzGovernance record. Cycle runs one pass over the skills: a skill whose precondition does not hold is skipped, a governed skill asks MayProceed first and is refused if it does not pass, and an admitted skill is applied and verified. Pursue repeats Cycle to a fixpoint, bounded at 20 rounds. It is deterministic and offline. GiveWorkbench binds the safe world: the agent's ring functions then rehearse file writes in memory, and GenerateUpdatePlan is the one export toward reality.
classes.receiver: o1 = new stzPIAgent("kitchen-bot") o2 = new stzAgentSkill("restock")
classes.example:
o2.SetWhen(func m { return m.Fact("stock", "level", "low") })
o2.SetDoes(func m { m.Learn("stock", "level", "ordered") return 1 })
o1.AddSkill(o2)
o1.MemoryQ().Learn("stock", "level", "low")
? o1.Cycle()
#--> 1
? o1.MemoryQ().Fact("stock", "level", "ordered")
#--> 1
? o1.Trace()[1][:decision]
#--> ran

methods.name: init
methods.brief: Builds an agent with a name, an empty memory, a governance record and no skills.

parameters.name: pcName
parameters.role: the agent's name, also the actor named in governance decisions

methods.name: Name_
methods.brief: Returns the name the agent was built with.

methods.name: MemoryQ
methods.brief: Returns the agent's memory, where the skills perceive and learn.

methods.name: GovernanceQ
methods.brief: Returns the agent's governance record: risks, permissions, authority and decisions.

methods.name: Trace
methods.brief: Returns what happened to each skill on every cycle so far, in order.
methods.returns: a list of hash lists [ :skill, :decision, :verified, :why ]; decision is skipped, refused or ran
notes: the trace grows with every cycle and is never cleared

methods.name: Why
methods.brief: Returns the sentence that sums up the last Pursue.
methods.returns: a text; empty before the first Pursue

methods.name: GiveWorkbench
methods.brief: Opens a rehearsal workbench for the agent, if it has none, so that its file writes land in memory.
notes: during Cycle the workbench is the ambient one, reached by a ring function through StzActiveWorkbenchQ; calling it again keeps the same workbench

extensions.name: GiveWorkbenchQ
extensions.adds: does what the method does, then returns the object, so the call can be chained

methods.name: HasWorkbench
methods.brief: TRUE if the agent was given a workbench.

methods.name: WorkbenchQ
methods.brief: Returns a face onto the agent's workbench.
notes: the face reaches the one live workbench, so changes through it are the agent's own
warnings: raises an error naming the agent when it holds no workbench

methods.name: GenerateUpdatePlan
methods.brief: Returns the agent's rehearsed file changes as an update plan, its only export toward reality.
notes: the plan is executed by a committing actor, never by the agent
warnings: raises the no-workbench error when the agent holds none

methods.name: AddSkill
methods.brief: Adds a skill that runs whenever its precondition holds, without asking governance.

parameters.name: poSkill
parameters.role: a stzAgentSkill

extensions.name: AddSkillQ
extensions.adds: does what the method does, then returns the object, so the call can be chained

methods.name: AddGovernedSkill
methods.brief: Adds a skill whose action must first pass the governance gate, which asks about the action by its lower-case name.

parameters.name: poSkill
parameters.role: a stzAgentSkill

parameters.name: pcAction
parameters.role: the governed action the skill performs

notes: the gate refuses an action with no declared risk tier, and each refusal is traced

extensions.name: AddGovernedSkillQ
extensions.adds: does what the method does, then returns the object, so the call can be chained

methods.name: NumberOfSkills
methods.brief: Returns how many skills the agent holds.

methods.name: Cycle
methods.brief: Runs one pass over all skills: tests each precondition, asks governance for governed ones, then applies and verifies.
methods.returns: a number, how many skills ran and were verified
notes: a skill whose precondition stays true fires again on every cycle

methods.name: Pursue
methods.brief: Repeats Cycle until a cycle verifies nothing or 20 rounds are done.
methods.returns: a number, the total of skill-firings that were verified
notes: a skill that leaves its own precondition true runs to the 20-round limit; the sentence for it is kept for Why

methods.name: DecisionLog
methods.brief: Returns the governed decisions taken so far: every trace row that ran or was refused.
notes: skipped rows, where a precondition did not hold, are left out

classes.name: stzPispiHttpAdapter
classes.brief: Carries the payments contract over HTTP to a participant's API Business, with OAuth2, an API key and optional mutual TLS.
classes.description: UNPERCEIVED. This adapter is proven against the twin served over real HTTP (stzPiSpiHttpFront), plain and with mutual TLS, and has NOT been run against the BCEAO's sandbox. No payment made through it has been watched landing in a real dashboard by a named person, and until one has it stays unperceived: built, not yet proven in the world. It is the live backend of the payments port, answering the same Request(method, path, query, body) as the twin, which is why the port cannot tell the two apart. Before each call it takes an OAuth token with the client credentials read from a secret store, reuses it until a minute before it lapses, retries once on a 401, and sends the API key; it presents a client certificate on an https address when the participant requires one. A hub's problem comes back as the same [ status, problem ] the twin gives, while a transport failure raises. The base address is configuration, nothing in the adapter names a bank, and it promises no homologation. The payments guide, docs/payments-guide.md, is the desk's own account.
classes.example:
o1.WithParticipant("bia")
o1.AsLive()
? o1.CertificateSecretName()
#--> pispi-bia-mtls-cert
? o1.RequiresCertificate()
#--> 1

methods.name: init
methods.brief: Builds an adapter that asks for every scope the contract names, with no endpoint, no credentials and no posture yet.
notes: every setter answers the adapter, so the calls chain
warnings: an adapter that is never told AsLive or AsConformance answers no to RequiresCertificate and to IsConformance, so a registry binds it as live without asking for a certificate

methods.name: WithParticipant
methods.brief: Sets the participant's short name and derives from it the four secret names the adapter looks up in the store.

parameters.name: pcParticipant
parameters.role: the participant's short name, kept in lower case, such as bia

methods.returns: the adapter itself, so calls chain
notes: nothing in the adapter names a bank, the participant is configuration
warnings: the names are pispi-<participant>-client, -api-key, -mtls-cert and -mtls- key; until this is called all four are empty

methods.name: WithBaseUrl
methods.brief: Sets the participant's API Business address, version included, to which every contract path is added.

parameters.name: pcUrl
parameters.role: the base address such as https://host/piz/v1, trailing slashes are removed and an https address selects the engine's TLS client

methods.returns: the adapter itself, so calls chain
notes: UNPERCEIVED: pointed at the twin served over real HTTP this has been run, pointed at the BCEAO's sandbox or at any participant it has NOT, and no payment through it has been watched landing in a real dashboard
warnings: the address is configuration, the contract is the BCEAO's

methods.name: WithTokenUrl
methods.brief: Sets the address of the OAuth token endpoint when it is not the one derived from the base address.

parameters.name: pcUrl
parameters.role: the full token address

methods.returns: the adapter itself, so calls chain

methods.name: WithScopes
methods.brief: Narrows or sets the list of scopes the token asks for, so that fewer scopes make a narrower adapter.

parameters.name: paScopes
parameters.role: a list of the contract's scope names such as paiement.read, without the prefix, which is added from WithScopePrefix

methods.returns: the adapter itself, so calls chain
notes: the default is all 23 scopes of the contract
warnings: a call whose operation needs a scope outside the list is refused by the hub with a 401 problem naming that scope; the token already cached is not replaced until ForgetToken

methods.name: WithScopePrefix
methods.brief: Sets the text put before every scope, which is piz/ in the BCEAO's sandbox.

parameters.name: pcPrefix
parameters.role: the text such as piz/, an empty text for none

methods.returns: the adapter itself, so calls chain
warnings: a hub that expects the prefix answers every call of an adapter without it with a 401 problem, while the token is still issued; the twin front refused the calls this way

methods.name: WithSecretsFrom
methods.brief: Gives the adapter the secret store and the actor through which it reads the OAuth client and the API key.

parameters.name: poStore
parameters.role: the stzSecretStore holding pispi-<participant>-client as clientId:clientSecret and pispi-<participant>-api-key

parameters.name: poActor
parameters.role: the effectful actor that may reveal them, a language-model actor is refused

methods.returns: the adapter itself, so calls chain
notes: UNPERCEIVED: the credentials read here were only ever the test values of the twin, never a participant's sandbox or production ones
warnings: the store is copied when handed over, so hand it again after a rotation; without a store and an actor the first call raises an error saying no credentials were given; the client secret is revealed again at each token fetch and the API key at each call

methods.name: WithCertificateFrom
methods.brief: Gives the adapter the store whose file-sourced certificate and key secrets name the mutual TLS PEM files.

parameters.name: poStore
parameters.role: the stzSecretStore holding pispi-<participant>-mtls-cert and -mtls-key as secrets with a file source, whose path is the PEM file

methods.returns: the adapter itself, so calls chain
notes: UNPERCEIVED: mutual TLS is proven only against the twin front with the engine's throwaway test certificates, never against a participant
warnings: it keeps the same store as WithSecretsFrom, so a different store passed here replaces that one, which is read from the code and not run; the private key stays in its file and never enters Ring

methods.name: WithCertificateFiles
methods.brief: Sets the client certificate and private key as PEM file paths, used when the store names no file-sourced secret for them.

parameters.name: pcCert
parameters.role: the path of the client certificate PEM file

parameters.name: pcKey
parameters.role: the path of the private key PEM file

methods.returns: the adapter itself, so calls chain
notes: UNPERCEIVED: mutual TLS has not been run against a participant or the BCEAO's sandbox
warnings: a path found in the store takes the place of these two, which is read from the code and not run, as is the method itself

methods.name: WithCaFile
methods.brief: Sets the PEM file of the authority that signs the participant's server certificate.

parameters.name: pcCa
parameters.role: the path of the CA PEM file, an empty text meaning the operating system's roots

methods.returns: the adapter itself, so calls chain
notes: UNPERCEIVED: no participant's real server certificate chain has been checked with it
warnings: it is read only on an https address, a plain http address ignores it

methods.name: AsConformance
methods.brief: Declares the adapter to be talking to the BCEAO's sandbox, genuine protocol over virtual money, where no client certificate is required.
methods.returns: the adapter itself, so calls chain
notes: UNPERCEIVED: this is the posture of the conformance run that has NOT been done. Against the BCEAO's sandbox under the platform's own account the adapter has not been run, and it stays unperceived until a named person has watched a payment land in the sandbox dashboard
warnings: the last of AsConformance and AsLive wins; a registry refuses a conformance binding in a production phase

methods.name: AsLive
methods.brief: Declares the adapter to be talking to a participant in production, where a client certificate is required.
methods.returns: the adapter itself, so calls chain
notes: UNPERCEIVED: the adapter is proven against the twin served over real HTTP and has NOT been run against the BCEAO's sandbox, let alone a participant in production, and no payment through it has been watched landing in a real dashboard
warnings: after this call RequiresCertificate answers TRUE, so a registry bound to the adapter judges the certificate secret and reports live-without-certificate while the store has none

methods.name: IsSandbox
methods.brief: Answers FALSE always, because the adapter is never a fake.
warnings: the registry asks this first, so an adapter is never taken for a fake

methods.name: IsConformance
methods.brief: TRUE if the adapter was declared to talk to the BCEAO's sandbox.
notes: UNPERCEIVED: see AsConformance, the conformance run has not been done
warnings: the registry reads it as the conformance posture

methods.name: RequiresCertificate
methods.brief: TRUE if the adapter was declared live, because a live participant demands a client certificate and the BCEAO's sandbox does not.
warnings: the registry asks it to decide whether to judge the certificate secret

methods.name: CertificateSecretName
methods.brief: Returns the name of the store secret that holds the mutual TLS client certificate.
methods.returns: a text such as pispi-bia-mtls-cert, empty before WithParticipant

methods.name: ClientSecretName
methods.brief: Returns the name of the store secret that holds clientId:clientSecret.
methods.returns: a text such as pispi-bia-client, empty before WithParticipant

methods.name: ApiKeySecretName
methods.brief: Returns the name of the store secret that holds the API key.
methods.returns: a text such as pispi-bia-api-key, empty before WithParticipant

methods.name: Participant
methods.brief: Returns the participant's short name in lower case.

methods.name: DropNextResponse
methods.brief: Makes the next call go out and its answer be lost, as a dropped connection loses it, so a test can meet doubt about money.
methods.returns: the adapter itself, so calls chain
notes: a test hook, used with the twin only; the payments port journals the transaction id so that a retry reads the payment before it sends it again
warnings: the next call raises a transport error saying the response was lost and the request may have been processed, and the call after it works; the hub did process the request

methods.name: TokensFetched
methods.brief: Returns how many tokens this adapter has taken from the token endpoint.
warnings: a token is reused until a minute before it lapses, so a count of one after several calls shows the cache working

methods.name: ForgetToken
methods.brief: Drops the cached token so that the next call asks for a fresh one.
methods.returns: the adapter itself, so calls chain
warnings: a 401 on a call already does this once by itself

methods.name: Request
methods.brief: Sends one call of the hub contract to the participant and answers [ status, body ], taking or reusing an OAuth token.

parameters.name: pcMethod
parameters.role: GET, POST, PUT or DELETE

parameters.name: pcPath
parameters.role: the contract path after the base address, such as /paiements-envoyes

parameters.name: paQuery
parameters.role: a list of [ key, value ] pairs such as [ "montant[gte]", "4000" ], percent- encoded except brackets

parameters.name: paBody
parameters.role: the body as a list, written as JSON, a non-list meaning no body

methods.returns: a list of two items, the HTTP status and the body as a list, or an empty text for a 204 or an empty answer
notes: UNPERCEIVED: run only against the twin served over real HTTP, plain and with mutual TLS, and NOT against the BCEAO's sandbox or any participant, so no payment sent here has been watched landing in a real dashboard. The base address decides what it reaches
warnings: a 401 drops the token and retries once with a fresh one; a transport failure raises an error; a token endpoint that does not answer 200 raises an error naming the status; two behaviours are read from the code and not run, an answer that is not JSON comes back as a problem record titled Not JSON, and over plain http a method other than the four goes as GET

classes.name: stzPiSpiHttpFront
classes.brief: Serves the twin of the PI-SPI hub over HTTP, with a token endpoint, an API key and scopes, so a live adapter has a real server to talk to.
classes.description: UNPERCEIVED, the live adapter this front exists to test. stzPispiHttpAdapter is proven against this twin over real HTTP, plain and with mutual TLS, and has NOT been run against the BCEAO's sandbox: a green run against the front says the adapter and the twin agree, not that a participant's hub agrees, and no payment made through the adapter has been watched landing in a real dashboard. The front puts the twin's single Request() behind an application server and adds what a participant puts in front of the contract: an OAuth2 client-credentials token endpoint, an x-api-key, a scope for each operation, and optional mutual TLS. It moves no money, the twin holds virtual francs. The token is not bound to the certificate it was taken under, which the real hub's is, because the engine does not show the peer certificate to a handler. EnableControl adds /_twin/ routes for a test, with no credential asked. All its state is process-wide, so run one front per process, and run it in a process of its own since RunFor blocks its caller.
classes.example:
? o1.Hub().Balance()
#--> 50000000
? o1.Hub().IsSandbox()
#--> 1

methods.name: init
methods.brief: Builds a front over a new twin hub, with an application server that routes every GET, POST, PUT and DELETE path to the contract handler.
notes: it moves no money, the twin holds virtual francs
warnings: the front keeps its settings and its tokens in process-wide tables, so a second front in the same process shares the first one's credentials and counters and only takes over the hub; run one front per process, which is read from the code and not run

methods.name: WithCredentials
methods.brief: Sets the OAuth client and the API key the front demands before it serves a call.

parameters.name: pcClientId
parameters.role: the client id the token endpoint accepts

parameters.name: pcClientSecret
parameters.role: the client secret it accepts

parameters.name: pcApiKey
parameters.role: the key every API call must send in x-api-key

methods.returns: the front itself, so calls chain
notes: the values are test values the caller generates, never a participant's credentials
warnings: with no API key set every API call is refused with a 401 problem

methods.name: WithScopePrefix
methods.brief: Sets the text that every scope of a token must carry, which is piz/ in the BCEAO's sandbox.

parameters.name: pcPrefix
parameters.role: the text such as piz/, an empty text for none

methods.returns: the front itself, so calls chain
warnings: a call whose token lacks the prefixed scope its operation needs is refused with a 401 problem naming the scope

methods.name: WithBasePath
methods.brief: Sets the path under which the contract is served, /piz/v1 unless changed.

parameters.name: pcBase
parameters.role: the path prefix such as /piz/v1

methods.returns: the front itself, so calls chain
warnings: any other path, apart from the token endpoint and the control routes, answers a 404 problem

methods.name: WithTokenLifetime
methods.brief: Sets how many seconds a token issued from now on stays valid, 3600 unless changed.

parameters.name: pnSeconds
parameters.role: the lifetime in seconds, which the token response reports as expires_in

methods.returns: the front itself, so calls chain
warnings: the adapter refreshes a token a minute before it lapses, so a lifetime under a minute makes it fetch one for every call

methods.name: EnableControl
methods.brief: Turns on the /_twin/ routes with which a test drives the twin behind the wire.
methods.returns: the front itself, so calls chain
notes: they advance the clock, settle what is pending, make a customer pay, ask or cancel, change how a customer answers, read the queued webhooks and the counters; a server that holds real money never enables them
warnings: those routes ask for no credential at all, so anyone who can reach the port can advance the clock, make the twin pay or ask, and revoke tokens, and loopback only is a matter of the host given to Start and is not enforced here

methods.name: Hub
methods.brief: Returns a face onto the twin the front serves, for a caller in the same process.
methods.returns: an stzPiSpiSandbox on the same hub
warnings: the face shares its state with the served twin, so a payment made through it is seen over HTTP

methods.name: Start
methods.brief: Binds the front to a port and an address and returns 1, without serving anything until RunFor is called.

parameters.name: pnPort
parameters.role: the port to listen on, 0 for any free one

parameters.name: pcHost
parameters.role: the address to bind, an empty text meaning 127.0.0.1

notes: UNPERCEIVED, for the live adapter this front is built to serve: stzPispiHttpAdapter is proven against this twin over real HTTP and has NOT been run against the BCEAO's sandbox, so a green run here says the adapter and the twin agree, not that a participant's hub agrees
warnings: raises an error when the port cannot be bound or the front already runs

methods.name: StartTls
methods.brief: Binds the front to a port and an address behind TLS, with mutual TLS when a CA is given, and returns 1.
usage: StartTls(pnPort, pcHost, pcCert, pcKey, pcCa, pbRequireClient)

parameters.name: pnPort
parameters.role: the port to listen on, 0 for any free one

parameters.name: pcHost
parameters.role: the address to bind, an empty text meaning 127.0.0.1

parameters.name: pcCert
parameters.role: the server certificate PEM file

parameters.name: pcKey
parameters.role: the server private key PEM file

parameters.name: pcCa
parameters.role: the CA PEM file that checks client certificates, an empty text for none

parameters.name: pbRequireClient
parameters.role: TRUE to demand a client certificate, so that a client without one gets no response at all

notes: UNPERCEIVED: mutual TLS is proven only between the adapter and this twin with the engine's throwaway test certificates, never against the BCEAO's sandbox or a participant
warnings: raises an error for a certificate, key or CA file that cannot be used, naming the code -13, -14 or -17; the token is not bound to the certificate it was fetched under, as the real hub's is, because the engine does not show the peer certificate to a handler

methods.name: Port
methods.brief: Returns the port the front listens on, the real one when 0 was asked for.
methods.returns: a number, 0 before the first start

methods.name: RunFor
methods.brief: Serves requests for the given time and then returns, the call that makes the front answer.

parameters.name: pnMs
parameters.role: how long to serve, in milliseconds

methods.returns: the front itself, so calls chain
warnings: it blocks its caller, so an adapter running in the same process cannot be served: run the front in a process of its own, as the library's live-adapter guard does

methods.name: Stop
methods.brief: Closes the listener and keeps the routes for a later start.
methods.returns: the front itself, so calls chain
warnings: a front that is not running is left as it is

classes.name: stzPispiQr
classes.brief: Builds the PI-SPI interoperable QR payload, the short text a camera reads, and refuses to build one that would print wrong.
classes.description: The library builds the QR STRING and does not draw the picture, and no QR it made has been scanned by any wallet or bank app: the black and white matrix a phone's camera reads is a second step this library does not do, so hand the string to a QR-drawing component of your front end. The string follows the BCEAO's published merchant-presented format: the receiver's PI-SPI alias, the currency XOF, an optional whole-franc amount, a country of the union, a reference label of at most 25 characters and a checksum. A static code serves many payments and a dynamic code one sale. The builder refuses a bad alias, country, label or amount when the payload is asked for, and StzPispiQrParse reads a string back without raising and says what is wrong. It is a builder, not a payment: the payer's banking application makes an ordinary payment to the alias. The checksum matches an independent implementation, which proves the string is well formed and nothing about a scan.
classes.example:
o1.WithAlias("9b1b3499-3e50-435b-b757-ac7a83d8aa96").InCountry("NE").AsDynamic()
o1.WithReference("APP-2026-000002").WithAmount(StzAmountQ("18500", "XOF"))
cQr = o1.Payload()
? StzPispiQrParse(cQr)[:valid]
#--> 1
? StzPispiQrParse(cQr)[:data][:amount]
#--> 18500
? StzPispiQrParse("0002010102126304BEEF")[:valid]
#--> 0

methods.name: WithAlias
methods.brief: Sets the PI-SPI alias of the receiver, the one account the code pays.

parameters.name: pcAlias
parameters.role: the receiver's PI-SPI alias, a UUID of 36 characters such as the twin's BusinessAlias()

methods.returns: the builder itself, so calls chain
notes: the UUID shape is checked, not the version
warnings: an alias that is not in the shape of a UUID is not refused here but when Payload is asked for

methods.name: InCountry
methods.brief: Sets the country of the receiver, in capitals whatever case is given.

parameters.name: pcCountry
parameters.role: the country code, one of BJ BF CI GW ML NE SN TG

methods.returns: the builder itself, so calls chain
warnings: a country outside the union is not refused here but when Payload is asked for

methods.name: AsStatic
methods.brief: Makes the code a static one, printed once and read for many payments, with channel 000.
methods.returns: the builder itself, so calls chain
notes: in a static code the payer types the amount unless WithAmount fixes it; the last of AsStatic and AsDynamic called wins

methods.name: AsDynamic
methods.brief: Makes the code a dynamic one, made for one sale, with channel 400.
methods.returns: the builder itself, so calls chain
notes: the last of AsStatic and AsDynamic called wins

methods.name: WithReference
methods.brief: Sets the label the payer's application shows and the receiver reconciles the payment on.

parameters.name: pcLabel
parameters.role: the reference label, 1 to 25 printable ASCII characters

methods.returns: the builder itself, so calls chain
notes: the payment received carries it as its motif
warnings: a label that is empty, over 25 characters or outside printable ASCII is not refused here but when Payload is asked for

methods.name: WithAmount
methods.brief: Fixes the amount the payer is asked for, which must be whole francs in XOF.

parameters.name: poAmount
parameters.role: the stzAmount to ask for, in XOF, above zero and of at most 13 digits

methods.returns: the builder itself, so calls chain
warnings: raises an error at once for an amount in another currency or an amount that is not above zero; without it the payer types the amount

methods.name: WithPurpose
methods.brief: Sets the optional purpose text carried in the additional data of the code.

parameters.name: pcPurpose
parameters.role: the purpose, in printable ASCII

methods.returns: the builder itself, so calls chain

methods.brief: Adds an additional-data tag of the receiver's own to the code.

parameters.name: pcTag
parameters.role: the tag, exactly two characters, digits or capital letters

parameters.name: pcValue
parameters.role: the tag's value, as text

classes.name: stzPiSpiSandbox
classes.brief: Answers the PI-SPI hub contract in process as a twin, with virtual francs and a clock moved by hand, so a platform can be tested without a bank.
classes.description: The twin implements the REST contract of the hub in one method, Request(method, path, query, body), which the payments port and the live adapter both speak. It enforces what the reference enforces, so code that pays twice, sends a field the schema refuses or exceeds the quota fails in a test: a txId replayed is answered REJETE with reason DU03, a payment is pending and becomes final 20 seconds later on the twin's own clock, and the hub's webhooks are signed. It declares itself a fake, so a registry refuses it in a production phase. It holds virtual francs and takes no fee, montantFrais is absent because the participant's fee is the participant's contract. It is a model of the contract, not the hub: the live adapter has not been run against the BCEAO's sandbox, so how closely the twin matches that hub is unperceived. The live adapter that talks to a real hub is UNPERCEIVED for the same reason. The state lives in process-wide tables, so a copy of the object is the same hub.
classes.example:
? o1.Balance()
#--> 50000000
o1.SimulateIncomingPayment("fatou", 40000, "facture 12")
? o1.Balance()
#--> 50040000

methods.name: init

notes: the state lives in process-wide tables and the object carries only the hub number, so a copy of the object is the same hub
warnings: the twin holds virtual francs and takes no fee, montantFrais is absent because the participant's fee is the participant's contract

methods.name: Request
methods.brief: Answers one call of the hub contract in process, as [ status, body ], the method the port and the live adapter both speak.

parameters.name: pcPath

parameters.name: paQuery

parameters.name: paBody
parameters.role: the body as a list, a non-list meaning none

notes: the twin enforces what the reference enforces, so that code which pays twice or sends an unknown field fails in a test, but it is a model of the contract and not the hub: the live adapter has not been run against the BCEAO's sandbox, so how closely the two agree is unperceived

classes.name: stzPispiSecret
classes.brief: Describes one of the five secrets a live payment needs, by name and kind, as a token that can expire.
classes.description: The five parts are the OAuth client, the API key, the mTLS private key, its certificate and a webhook secret. A descriptor is a stzToken underneath, because a token is the one kind of secret the store already knows how to expire, and its kind says which part it is. It carries no value until a source is given: the value comes from an environment variable, a file outside the repository or a vault, and is shown by no output. Use invented values in a test and never write a real one in a source file, a memo or an example. A descriptor that is only a name is refused by the registry in production, as is one whose certificate has lapsed.
classes.example:
o1.FromEnv("INVENTED_MTLS_CERT_PATH")
? o1.Kind()
#--> pispi-mtls-cert
? o1.Part()
#--> mtls-cert
? o1.Descriptor()
#--> <secret 'pispi-bia-mtls-cert' (pispi-mtls-cert) from env:INVENTED_MTLS_CERT_PATH>

methods.name: init
methods.brief: Builds an unset descriptor for one of the five parts of a live payment: a name and a kind, and no value.

parameters.name: pcName
parameters.role: the name the descriptor is registered under in the store

parameters.name: pcPart
parameters.role: one of client, api-key, mtls-key, mtls-cert or webhook-secret, in any case

notes: a descriptor with no value is a name, not a credential: give it a source with FromEnv, FromFile or FromVault, and its kind becomes pispi- followed by the part
warnings: raises an error naming the five parts when pcPart is anything else, an empty text included

methods.name: Part
methods.brief: Returns which of the five elements of a live payment this descriptor stands for, in lower case.
methods.returns: a text: client, api-key, mtls-key, mtls-cert or webhook-secret

classes.name: stzPivotTable
classes.brief: Cross-tabulates a table: groups its rows by one or two label columns against a column of labels, and aggregates a value column in each cell.
classes.description: Give it a source table, then name the row labels, the column labels and the value column, with SetRowLabels, SetColumnLabels and SetValues (or By and Analyze). Value, RowTotal, ColumnTotal and GrandTotal read the cells, ToTable returns the result as a table and Show prints it. The pivot is generated again whenever a setting changes. Use the supported shape: one column label, one or two row labels, one value column; that shape runs in the engine. Known limits, all reproduced: the totals of every function but SUM and COUNT are sums of the cells; any other shape runs in a Ring fallback that drops the first source record; Show raises for two column labels; SaveToFile writes an empty file.
classes.receiver: o1 = new stzPivotTable([ [ "CITY", "YEAR", "SALES" ], [ "Tunis", 2023, 10 ], [ "Tunis", 2024, 5 ], [ "Sfax", 2023, 20 ], [ "Gabes", 2024, 3 ] ]) o1.SetRowLabels(:CITY) o1.SetColumnLabels(:YEAR) o1.SetValues(:SALES)
classes.example:
? o1.Value("Tunis", 2023)
#--> 10
? o1.RowTotal("Tunis")
#--> 15
? o1.ColumnTotal(2023)
#--> 30
? o1.GrandTotal()
#--> 38
o1.SetNullValue("-")
? o1.Value("Sfax", 2024)
#--> -

classes.name: stzPlanComparison
classes.brief: Compares two executed plans: their routes, costs and lengths, which is cheaper and what each gains.
classes.description: It is built by stzGraphPlanner.CompareToQ and is the object behind CompareTo, Tradeoffs, WhichIsCheaper and CostSaving. The route length is counted in nodes.
classes.receiver: g1 = new stzGraph("g1"); g1.AddNodeXTT("a", "A", [ :x = 0 ]); g1.AddNodeXTT("b", "B", [ :x = 1 ]); g1.AddNodeXTT("c", "C", [ :x = 2 ]); g1.AddEdgeXTT("a", "b", "r", [ :distance = 5, :cost = 1 ]); g1.AddEdgeXTT("b", "c", "r", [ :distance = 5, :cost = 9 ]); g1.AddEdgeXTT("a", "c", "r", [ :distance = 20, :cost = 2 ]); o1 = new stzGraphPlanner(g1); o1.AddPlan("short"); o1.Walk("a", "c"); o1.Minimize("distance"); o1.Execute(); o1.AddPlan("cheap"); o1.Walk("a", "c"); o1.Minimize("cost"); o1.Execute(); o2 = o1.CompareToQ("short")
classes.example:
? o2.WhichIsCheaper()
#--> cheap

methods.brief: Builds a comparison of two executed plans from their names and their results, which the planner supplies.

parameters.name: paResult1

classes.name: stzPlatform
classes.brief: Wraps a stzApp world in what makes it operable: build and deploy of its parts, governed capabilities, a Commons of identities and messages, and a world registry.
classes.description: A stzApp models the world and lacks the operational envelope; the platform is that envelope, in five duties. It owns a deployment profile whose parts Build and then Deploy (Build records the compiler command of each part and Deploy lowers it to an artifact text, neither runs anything). SetWorld takes a world, and Generate writes a shell file for each of its reaches. A capability such as the camera is requested with AddCapability and decided by Granted against a governance regime. OpenCommonsOn turns an open database into identities (salted PBKDF2 hashes, never the secret), sessions, messages and a key-value store. ServeBody serves the world and the Commons over HTTP on 127.0.0.1. PushWorld, Bond and CallAcross keep a registry in which a call between worlds goes through only if both are active, a bond names the action and governance agrees. The runs behind this reference were in memory only: no shell file was written and no port was opened.
classes.example:
o1.PushWorld("resto", "1.0")
? o1.IsActiveWorld("resto")
#--> 1
o1.RetireWorld("resto")
? o1.IsActiveWorld("resto")
#--> 0
? o1.KdfRounds()
#--> 100000

classes.name: stzPlatformProfile
classes.brief: Describes a whole solution: its development system and its parts, each with the system it deploys to.
classes.description: The architect's common ground. Declare the solution with DevelopedOn and WithApp, WithServer, WithSuperApp or WithPart, then check it with Validate. Feature code is authored per part (ReadPinIn, SpawnIn, ConnectIn and the others) and checked at once against that part's target: an operation the target forbids raises an error, one the live machine cannot perform is rehearsed and recorded for deploy-time lowering. The profile only describes: it builds and deploys nothing, and it is saved as a small .stzplatform text. A part obtained with App and assigned to a variable is a copy; chain the calls instead.

#--> 2
? o1.App(:firmware).DeploymentOSName()
#--> espidf
? o1.HasApp("BACKEND")
#--> 1
? o1.IsSound()
#--> 1
? @@( o1.Validate() )
#--> [ ]

warnings: it adds the parts to those already declared; comment lines and lines it does not understand are skipped

methods.name: Show
methods.brief: Prints the solution: its name, development system and one line per part.

classes.name: stzPolynomial
classes.brief: Holds a polynomial in one variable, evaluates and differentiates it, adds and multiplies, and finds its real and complex roots.
classes.description: Coefficients are written highest degree first, the way the polynomial is written: [1, -6, 11, -6] is x^3 - 6x^2 + 11x - 6, and leading zeros are dropped. The roots are the eigenvalues of the companion matrix, computed by the engine, so a root repeated m times comes back as a small cluster rather than exactly (the tolerance of RealRoots and RealRootsWithin is how that is surfaced). Plus, Minus, Times and the Derivative return coefficient lists and the Q forms return a new stzPolynomial; none of them changes the object. Checked by hand: x^3 - 6x^2 + 11x - 6 has the roots 1, 2, 3, value 6 at 4, derivative 3x^2 - 12x + 11 and, times x - 1, the product x^4 - 7x^3 + 17x^2 - 17x + 6; x^2 + 1 has the roots i and -i.

methods.name: init
methods.brief: Builds a polynomial in one variable from its coefficients, highest degree first, dropping leading zeros.

parameters.name: paCoefficients
parameters.role: the coefficient list, highest degree first, numbers or numbers written as text

notes: [1, -6, 11, -6] is x^3 - 6x^2 + 11x - 6; [0, 0, 1, -3] is x - 3; all zeros give the zero polynomial [ 0 ]; build one with StzPolynomialQ(list)

methods.name: Coefficients
methods.brief: Returns the coefficients, highest degree first, with leading zeros removed.
notes: Coeffs is the same call; [0, 0, 1, -3] gives [ 1, -3 ]

methods.name: Degree
methods.brief: Returns the highest power of x with a non-zero coefficient.
methods.returns: a number; 0 for a constant and for the zero polynomial
notes: x^3 - 6x^2 + 11x - 6 gives 3; the constant 5 gives 0

methods.name: LeadingCoefficient
methods.brief: Returns the coefficient of the highest power.
notes: Leading is the same call; 2x^2 - 8x + 8 gives 2

methods.name: IsMonic
methods.brief: TRUE if the leading coefficient is exactly 1.
notes: x^3 - 6x^2 + 11x - 6 gives 1; 2x^2 - 8x + 8 gives 0

methods.name: IsZeroPolynomial
methods.brief: TRUE if every coefficient is zero.
notes: [0, 0] gives 1; the constant 5 gives 0

methods.name: Monic
methods.brief: Returns the coefficients divided by the leading one, so that the leading coefficient is 1.
methods.returns: a list of numbers; the object is not changed
notes: MonicQ returns a stzPolynomial; 2x^2 - 8x + 8 gives [ 1, -4, 4 ]
warnings: the zero polynomial raises Monic: the zero polynomial cannot be made monic

extensions.name: MonicQ
extensions.adds: does what the method does, then returns the object, so the call can be chained

methods.name: ValueAt
methods.brief: Returns the value of the polynomial at a number, by Horner's rule.

parameters.name: pnX
parameters.role: the number to evaluate at

notes: At and Eval are the same call; x^3 - 6x^2 + 11x - 6 gives 6 at 4, 0 at 1 and -6 at 0

methods.name: Derivative
methods.brief: Returns the coefficients of the derivative, by the power rule.
methods.returns: a list of numbers; [ 0 ] for a constant
notes: DerivativeQ returns a stzPolynomial; x^3 - 6x^2 + 11x - 6 gives [ 3, -12, 11 ]

extensions.name: DerivativeQ
extensions.adds: does what the method does, then returns the object, so the call can be chained

methods.name: CompanionMatrix
methods.brief: Returns the companion matrix of the monic form, whose eigenvalues are the roots.
methods.returns: a list of rows, each a list of numbers
notes: CompanionMatrixQ returns a stzMatrix; x^3 - 6x^2 + 11x - 6 gives [6, -11, 6], [1, 0, 0], [0, 1, 0]; x^2 + 1 gives [0, -1], [1, 0]
warnings: a constant, of degree 0, raises CompanionMatrix: this needs a polynomial of degree 1 or more

extensions.name: CompanionMatrixQ
extensions.adds: does what the method does, then returns the object, so the call can be chained

methods.name: ComplexRoots
methods.brief: Returns every root, real or complex, as a list of stzComplex, found as the eigenvalues of the companion matrix.
methods.returns: a list of stzComplex, one per degree; [ ] for a constant or the zero polynomial
notes: Roots is the same call; x^2 + 1 gives i and -i, x^2 + 2x + 5 gives -1 plus or minus 2i
warnings: a root repeated m times comes back as a cluster of nearby roots, not exactly: (x-2)^3 gives 2.00001 plus or minus 0.0000166i and 1.99998

methods.name: RealRootsWithin
methods.brief: Returns the real roots in ascending order, counting a root as real when its imaginary part is at most a tolerance.

parameters.name: pnTolerance
parameters.role: the largest absolute imaginary part still counted as real

notes: x^3 - 6x^2 + 11x - 6 gives 1, 2, 3 up to rounding
warnings: a repeated root only comes back whole with a loose tolerance: (x-2)^3 gives 2, 2, 2 with 0.001 and a single 2 with 0

methods.name: RealRoots
methods.brief: Returns the real roots in ascending order, with a tolerance of 0.000001.
methods.returns: a list of numbers; [ ] when all roots are complex
notes: x^3 - 6x^2 + 11x - 6 gives 1, 2, 3; x^2 + 1 gives [ ]; 2x^2 - 8x + 8 gives 2, 2; x^6 - 1 gives -1 and 1
warnings: a root repeated three times loses two of its copies, since their imaginary parts exceed the tolerance: (x-2)^3 gives a single 2

methods.name: NumberOfRealRoots
methods.brief: Returns how many real roots there are, counted with the tolerance of RealRoots.
notes: x^3 - 6x^2 + 11x - 6 gives 3; x^2 + 1 gives 0

methods.name: HasRealRoot
methods.brief: TRUE if the polynomial has at least one real root.
notes: x^2 + 1 gives 0; the constant 5 gives 0

methods.name: HasComplexRoot
methods.brief: TRUE if the polynomial has more roots than real ones, so some root has a non-negligible imaginary part.
notes: x^2 + 1 gives 1; x^3 - 6x^2 + 11x - 6 gives 0
warnings: a real polynomial with a repeated real root can answer TRUE: (x-2)^3 gives 1

methods.name: Plus
methods.brief: Returns the coefficients of the sum with another polynomial, aligned at the lowest degree.

parameters.name: paOther
parameters.role: a stzPolynomial or a coefficient list

methods.returns: a list of numbers; the object is not changed
notes: PlusQ returns a stzPolynomial and trims; adding [1, 1] gives [ 1, -6, 12, -5 ]; adding x^2 + 1 gives [ 1, -5, 11, -5 ]
warnings: the result keeps leading zeros: x^3 - 6x^2 + 11x - 6 minus itself gives [ 0, 0, 0, 0 ], which init would trim; any other value raises I need a polynomial or a coefficient list

extensions.name: PlusQ
extensions.adds: does what the method does, then returns the object, so the call can be chained

methods.name: Minus
methods.brief: Returns the coefficients of the difference with another polynomial, aligned at the lowest degree.

parameters.name: paOther
parameters.role: a stzPolynomial or a coefficient list

methods.returns: a list of numbers; the object is not changed
notes: MinusQ returns a stzPolynomial and trims; subtracting [1, 0, 0, 0] gives [ 0, -6, 11, -6 ], written -6x^2 + 11x - 6 by MinusQ
warnings: the result keeps leading zeros, as Plus does

extensions.name: MinusQ
extensions.adds: does what the method does, then returns the object, so the call can be chained

methods.name: Times
methods.brief: Returns the coefficients of the product with another polynomial, by convolution.

parameters.name: paOther
parameters.role: a stzPolynomial or a coefficient list

methods.returns: a list of numbers; the object is not changed
notes: TimesQ returns a stzPolynomial; exact for whole coefficients; x^3 - 6x^2 + 11x - 6 times x - 1 gives [ 1, -7, 17, -17, 6 ] and times x^2 + 1 gives [ 1, -6, 12, -12, 11, -6 ]; above 4096 coefficient pairs it switches to the transform

extensions.name: TimesQ
extensions.adds: does what the method does, then returns the object, so the call can be chained

methods.name: TimesViaTransform
methods.brief: Returns the same product by the frequency domain, so the two routes can be compared.

parameters.name: paOther
parameters.role: a stzPolynomial or a coefficient list

methods.returns: a list of numbers, which may carry rounding errors
notes: TimesViaTransformQ returns a stzPolynomial; x + 1 times 1, 2, 3 gives [ 1, 3, 5, 3 ]

extensions.name: TimesViaTransformQ
extensions.adds: does what the method does, then returns the object, so the call can be chained

methods.name: Content
methods.brief: Returns the coefficients, highest degree first.

methods.name: Show
methods.brief: Prints the polynomial as text on the console.
notes: x^3 - 6x^2 + 11x - 6 prints as that line

methods.name: ToString
methods.brief: Returns the polynomial written in the usual form, such as x^2 - 3x + 2.
methods.returns: a text; 0 for the zero polynomial
notes: zero terms are left out, a coefficient of 1 is not written, and signs sit between terms: -x^2 + 4, 0.50x^2 - 1.50x + 1 and x - 3

classes.name: stzPredicateSet
classes.brief: Holds a declared set of governance predicates, house code rules and agent-graph invariants, that can be saved with a seal and enforced.
classes.description: The mechanism, not any particular constitution: a set names which code rules and which graph invariants apply, EnforceOnCode and EnforceOnGraph run only those, and Save writes the set as readable lines ending with a SHA-256 seal that Verify checks after LoadFrom. Names are checked against the library's lists when added or loaded, so a file cannot add a rule that does not exist. The seal is an unkeyed digest: it catches a silent edit of the rules but proves nothing about authorship, which a reviewer's signature must supply outside the file.
classes.example:
o1.AddRule("no-len-method")
o1.AddInvariant("no-llm-effectful")
? @@( o1.Rules() )
#--> [ "no-len-method" ]
o2 = "class Foo" + nl + "def Len()" + nl + "  return 5" + nl
? o1.EnforceOnCode(o2)[1][:rule]
#--> no-len-method
? len(o1.Seal())
#--> 64

methods.name: init
methods.brief: Builds an empty named set of governance predicates: code rules and agent-graph invariants.

parameters.name: pcName
parameters.role: the set's name, written into a saved file

methods.name: SetName
methods.brief: Changes the name under which the set is saved, replacing the one it was built with.

parameters.name: pcName
parameters.role: the new name

methods.returns: the set itself, so calls chain
notes: LoadFrom also replaces the name with the one in the file

methods.name: Name_
methods.brief: Returns the name of the set.

methods.name: AddRule
methods.brief: Adds a code rule to the set by name; adding one already held changes nothing.

parameters.name: pcRule
parameters.role: the name of a house code rule, in any case, as StzCodeRuleNames lists them

notes: names are stored in lower case
warnings: raises an error naming StzCodeRuleNames for a rule it does not know

extensions.name: AddRuleQ
extensions.adds: does what the method does, then returns the object, so the call can be chained

methods.name: AddInvariant
methods.brief: Adds an agent-graph invariant to the set by name; adding one already held changes nothing.

parameters.name: pcInv
parameters.role: the name of a governance invariant, in any case, as StzGovernanceInvariantNames lists them

notes: names are stored in lower case
warnings: raises an error naming StzGovernanceInvariantNames for an invariant it does not know

extensions.name: AddInvariantQ
extensions.adds: does what the method does, then returns the object, so the call can be chained

methods.name: Rules
methods.brief: Returns the code rules in the set, in the order added.

methods.name: Invariants
methods.brief: Returns the agent-graph invariants in the set, in the order added.

methods.name: Seal
methods.brief: Returns the SHA-256 digest of the set's body: its name, its rules and its invariants.
notes: a reviewer's signature has to be added outside the file
warnings: the seal is a plain unkeyed digest: it shows that a file was edited without its seal line being redone, and it does not authenticate who wrote the file, since anyone who edits the body can recompute the seal

methods.name: LoadFrom
methods.brief: Reads a saved .zrlz file into this set: the name, the rules, the invariants and the seal recorded in it.

parameters.name: pcFile
parameters.role: the full path of the file, extension included

methods.returns: the set itself, so calls chain
notes: rules and invariants are added to those already held, not substituted for them
warnings: raises the file error when the file is missing, and the unknown-rule error when it names a rule or invariant that does not exist, so a file cannot add a rule the library lacks

methods.name: Save
methods.brief: Writes the set to a .zrlz file as readable lines ending with its seal, adding the extension when it is missing.

parameters.name: pcFile
parameters.role: the path of the file to write

notes: LoadFrom does not add the extension, so pass it the returned path

methods.name: Verify
methods.brief: TRUE if a seal was loaded and it matches the body now held.
methods.returns: TRUE or FALSE; FALSE for a set built in memory, which has loaded no seal
notes: it checks integrity, not authorship
warnings: a file whose rules were edited without redoing the seal answers FALSE, and one edited with the seal recomputed answers TRUE

methods.name: EnforceOnCode
methods.brief: Runs the house code checks on a source text and keeps only the findings of this set's rules.

parameters.name: pcSource
parameters.role: the Ring source text to check

methods.returns: a list of hash lists [ :rule, :line, :severity, :message ]; empty when the set holds no rules
notes: a source that breaks a rule the set does not hold gives no finding

methods.name: EnforceOnGraph
methods.brief: Runs the agent-graph checks on a graph and keeps only the findings of this set's invariants.

parameters.name: poGraph
parameters.role: the agent graph to check, such as the graph an stzAgentGraph holds

notes: an invariant the set does not hold gives no finding

classes.name: stzProcess
classes.brief: Tells the facts of the running program (identity, uptime, memory, machine) and manages one child process: spawn, stream, wait, kill.
classes.description: Without a child, an object reads the running program: its id, uptime on a monotonic clock, memory, processor time, architecture, operating system and byte order, all delegated to the engine. Spawn starts a child through the platform shell and SpawnIn starts one from an argument list with no shell; both are effectful and start a real program. The usage contract avoids a pipe deadlock: read the child's output to its end, then Wait, then Free. Kill ends the child whose handle the object holds and never looks a process up by name. WaitFor, IsRunning and SpawnIn need an engine built from the current source; an older stz_system.dll lacks them and raises R3.
classes.example:
? o1.HasChild()
#--> 0
? o1.BitSize()
#--> 64
o2 = SpawnProcess("echo hello")
? trim(o2.ReadOutputAll())
#--> hello
? o2.Wait()
#--> 0
o2.Free()

methods.name: init
methods.brief: Creates a handle on the running program, with no child attached; a child comes only from Spawn or SpawnIn.
notes: the identity methods work at once; the child methods raise until a child is attached

methods.name: Spawn
methods.brief: Starts a child process from a command line run by the platform shell (cmd.exe /c on Windows), with its output piped back.

parameters.name: pcCommand
parameters.role: the command line to run, a non-empty text

methods.returns: nothing; the object now manages the child
notes: run only with echo and an invented word, and with exit 3; the child was waited for each time
warnings: effectful: it starts a real program; an empty or non-text command raises an error; the shell parses the command, so never build it from untrusted text

extensions.name: SpawnQ
extensions.adds: does what the method does, then returns the object, so the call can be chained

methods.name: SpawnIn
methods.brief: Starts a program from its argument list with no shell between, in a folder of your choosing.

parameters.name: pcDir
parameters.role: the folder the child works in, an empty text to inherit

parameters.name: pacArgv
parameters.role: the program followed by its arguments, a non-empty list of texts

methods.returns: the process itself, so calls chain
notes: run with cmd /c echo and with ring on a scratch script, against the newer engine build of a sibling worktree
warnings: effectful: it starts a real program; an argument with a space or a quote reaches the program unparsed, and Kill reaches the program itself; a program that cannot start raises Failed to spawn; needs an engine built from the current source: the stz_system.dll of this worktree is older than the source and lacks the entry point, so there the call raises R3 Calling Function without definition

extensions.name: SpawnInQ
extensions.adds: does what the method does, then returns the object, so the call can be chained

methods.name: HasChild
methods.brief: TRUE if this object is managing a spawned child.

methods.name: ChildPid
methods.brief: Returns the operating-system process id of the child.
notes: run on a child that had just printed one word
warnings: raises an error when no child was spawned

methods.name: ReadOutput
methods.brief: Reads the next chunk of the child's standard output, waiting for it; an empty text means the stream ended.
warnings: raises an error when no child was spawned; read the output to the end before Wait, or a child with much output can block on a full pipe

methods.name: ReadOutputAll
methods.brief: Reads the child's standard output to its end and returns all of it.
notes: echo output came back with its trailing newline
warnings: raises an error when no child was spawned; it blocks until the child closes its output

methods.name: ReadError
methods.brief: Reads the next chunk of the child's error output, waiting for it; an empty text means the stream ended.
warnings: raises an error when no child was spawned

methods.name: ReadErrorAll
methods.brief: Reads the child's error output to its end and returns all of it.
notes: tested with a command that wrote one word to the error stream
warnings: raises an error when no child was spawned; it blocks until the child closes its error output

methods.name: ReadAvailable
methods.brief: Reads what the child has printed so far without waiting; an empty text when there is nothing yet or the stream has ended.
notes: run on a child that printed two lines over three seconds
warnings: raises an error when no child was spawned; the end of the stream is signalled only through StdoutEnded, so poll until it is TRUE

methods.name: StdoutEnded
methods.brief: TRUE if ReadAvailable has seen the end of the child's output.
warnings: it stays FALSE if you read with ReadOutput or ReadOutputAll only, because only ReadAvailable sets it

methods.name: WaitFor
methods.brief: Waits up to a number of milliseconds for the child to exit and returns its exit code, or -2 while it still runs.

parameters.name: pnMs
parameters.role: how long to wait at most, in milliseconds, 0 to only look

methods.returns: a number: the exit code, or -2 if still running
notes: run against the newer engine build of a sibling worktree: -2 after 100 ms on a running child, 0 on a finished one
warnings: raises an error when no child was spawned; after a Kill the exit code reads -1; needs an engine built from the current source: the stz_system.dll of this worktree is older than the source and lacks the entry point, so there the call raises R3 Calling Function without definition

methods.name: IsRunning
methods.brief: TRUE if the child has been spawned and has not exited.
notes: run against the newer engine build of a sibling worktree
warnings: FALSE when no child was spawned, instead of an error; needs an engine built from the current source: the stz_system.dll of this worktree is older than the source and lacks the entry point, so there the call raises R3 Calling Function without definition

methods.name: Wait
methods.brief: Waits until the child exits and returns its exit code.
notes: exit code 0 for echo and 3 for exit 3
warnings: raises an error when no child was spawned; read the output to the end first

methods.name: ExitCode
methods.brief: Returns the child's exit code, waiting for the child first if it has not been waited for.
notes: exit 3 gave 3
warnings: a child that was killed reads -1

methods.name: Succeeded
methods.brief: TRUE if the child exited with code 0.
warnings: it waits for the child if needed

methods.name: Failed
methods.brief: TRUE if the child did not exit with code 0, which includes a killed child.
warnings: it waits for the child if needed

methods.name: Kill
methods.brief: Ends the child's process by force and returns whether the engine did it.
methods.returns: TRUE if the child was killed
notes: run on a child of this session that was busy for three seconds
warnings: effectful; raises an error when no child was spawned; kills the process whose handle this object holds, never one found by name; the exit code then reads -1

methods.name: Close
methods.brief: Frees the child handle.
methods.detail: If the child is still running it is killed first, so a dropped handle never leaks a process. Ring has no destructors -- call this when done with a child.

extensions.name: CloseQ
extensions.adds: does what the method does, then returns the object, so the call can be chained

methods.name: Free
methods.brief: Releases the child handle so the engine can reap it; the object can then spawn again.
warnings: call it after Wait; it does not kill a running child

methods.name: Id
methods.brief: Returns the id of the running program itself.

methods.name: Uptime
methods.brief: Returns how many seconds the running program has been up.
notes: measured on a monotonic clock fixed when the engine was loaded

methods.name: UptimeInMilliseconds
methods.brief: Returns how many milliseconds the running program has been up.

methods.name: UptimeInNanoseconds
methods.brief: Returns how many nanoseconds the running program has been up.

methods.name: MemoryBytes
methods.brief: Returns the resident memory of the running program, in bytes.
notes: never above the peak

methods.name: PeakMemoryBytes
methods.brief: Returns the highest resident memory the running program has reached, in bytes.

methods.name: CpuTimeNs
methods.brief: Returns the processor time the running program has used, in nanoseconds.
warnings: Windows counts processor time in ticks of 15.6 ms, so a short interval is one tick, not a measurement

methods.name: CpuTimeMs
methods.brief: Returns the processor time the running program has used, in milliseconds.
warnings: same tick size as CpuTimeNs

methods.name: EngineArchitecture
methods.brief: Returns the architecture tag as the engine spells it, such as x86_64 or aarch64.

methods.name: Architecture
methods.brief: Returns the canonical architecture name: x64, arm64, x86 or arm.
warnings: an unrecognised tag is returned as the engine gave it

methods.name: OperatingSystem
methods.brief: Returns the name of the operating system, such as windows, linux or macos, in lower case.

methods.name: IsLittleEndian
methods.brief: TRUE if the machine stores the low byte of a number first.

methods.name: IsBigEndian
methods.brief: TRUE if the machine stores the high byte of a number first.

methods.name: Endianness
methods.brief: Returns little or big, the byte order of the machine.

methods.name: PointerSize
methods.brief: Returns the size of a pointer on this machine in bytes, 8 on a 64-bit one.

methods.name: BitSize
methods.brief: Returns the width of the machine word in bits, 64 on a 64-bit machine.

methods.name: Is64Bit
methods.brief: TRUE if the object is 64 bit.

methods.name: Is32Bit
methods.brief: TRUE if the object is 32 bit.

methods.name: Info
methods.brief: Returns the facts about the running program as a list of [ name, value ] pairs: pid, uptime_s, architecture, os, endianness and more.

methods.name: Show
methods.brief: Prints the facts of Info, one name = value line each.

classes.name: stzProfiler
classes.brief: Answers where the time goes by recording the frames you bracket as a call tree with calls, total and self time, and by sampling.
classes.description: Mark frames around the work you care about with Enter and Leave; the profiler keeps, for each path such as checkout;charge, the number of calls, the total time and the self time, which is the total minus the children. StartSampling starts an engine thread that photographs the active path at a fixed cadence, a statistical view with constant cost. Instrumented numbers are exact for what you bracketed; sampled numbers are statistical. Folded writes the folded-stacks format that flamegraph.pl and speedscope read. The frame stack lives in the engine, bounded by the maximum number of paths, and frames are cooperative: only what you bracket is seen. Times depend on the clock, so assert ranges and signs.
classes.receiver: o1 = StzProfiler(16) o1.Enter("checkout") o1.Enter("validate") StzEngineTimeSleepMs(20) o1.Leave() o1.Enter("charge") StzEngineTimeSleepMs(40) o1.Leave() o1.Leave()
classes.example:
? o1.Depth()
#--> 0
? o1.PathCount()
#--> 3
? o1.Paths()[1][:path]
#--> checkout;validate
? o1.Paths()[3][:calls]
#--> 1
? o1.HotSpots(1)[1][:path]
#--> checkout;charge
? o1.Paths()[3][:totalMs] > o1.Paths()[2][:totalMs]
#--> 1
? o1.Paths()[3][:selfMs] < o1.Paths()[3][:totalMs]
#--> 1
? o1.IsSampling()
#--> 0

methods.name: init
methods.brief: Builds a frame profiler whose frame stack and path table live in the engine, bounded to a number of distinct paths.

parameters.name: pnMaxPaths
parameters.role: the most distinct paths kept, 2 or more, otherwise 256

methods.returns: nothing; the engine handle is made when the object is built
notes: StzProfiler builds the same object; beyond the bound, paths fold into an _overflow path that stays visible, so with a bound of 2 only one path of its own fits; frames deeper than 32 fold into their parent

methods.name: Enter
methods.brief: Opens a frame, a named piece of work whose time is measured until the matching Leave.

parameters.name: pcFrameName
parameters.role: the name of the frame

methods.returns: the profiler itself, so calls chain
notes: frames nest, and a frame's path is its name joined to its parents' with semicolons; a call costs one engine call; a destroyed profiler is made again by it

methods.name: Leave
methods.brief: Closes the innermost open frame and adds its time to its path.
methods.returns: the profiler itself, so calls chain
notes: leaving with no frame open does nothing and leaves the depth at 0; a path is recorded when its frame is left, so a child path is listed before its parent

methods.name: Depth
methods.brief: Returns how many frames are open now.

methods.name: StartSampling
methods.brief: Starts the engine's sampler thread, which photographs the active frame path at a fixed interval.

parameters.name: pnIntervalMs
parameters.role: the interval between photographs, in milliseconds

methods.returns: the profiler itself, so calls chain
notes: the cost is constant and does not depend on how often frames are entered; without a running reactor Windows rounds a short interval up to about 15.6 ms, so there are fewer samples with the same statistics

methods.name: StopSampling
methods.brief: Stops the sampler thread.
methods.returns: the profiler itself, so calls chain

methods.name: IsSampling
methods.brief: TRUE if the sampler thread is running.

methods.name: Ticks
methods.brief: Returns how many times the sampler woke up, in a frame or idle.
notes: the samples of the paths add up to no more than the ticks; the count is live, so assert ranges and signs

methods.name: PathCount
methods.brief: Returns how many distinct paths have been recorded.

methods.name: Paths
methods.brief: Returns every recorded path with its instrumented and sampled numbers.
methods.returns: a list of hash lists with the keys path, calls, totalms, selfms and samples, in the order the frames were left; times are in milliseconds
notes: total includes the children and self does not; instrumented numbers are exact for what was bracketed and sampled numbers are statistical

methods.name: HotSpots
methods.brief: Returns the paths that spent the most time in themselves, children excluded.

parameters.name: pnHowMany
parameters.role: how many paths to return

methods.returns: a list of the same hash lists as Paths, longest self time first, at most pnHowMany
notes: asking for more than exist returns them all

methods.name: Folded
methods.brief: Returns the paths in the folded-stacks format that flame-graph tools read, one line per path as the path then a weight.
methods.returns: a text of lines such as checkout;charge 42
notes: the weight is the sample count when sampling ran and otherwise the self time in milliseconds rounded up; a path of weight 0 is left out

methods.name: WriteFoldedTo
methods.brief: Writes the folded stacks to a file, ready for flamegraph.pl or speedscope.

parameters.name: pcPath
parameters.role: the path of the file to write

classes.name: stzProgram
classes.brief: Opens a learning program, a folder of courses, skills, levels and teaching worlds, and lets an institution lay its own overlay over it.
classes.description: A learner or a teacher starts here: CourseQ takes a course by its slug, WithWorld chooses the world the chapters reason over, and the Review methods say how far each translation has been checked by a person. The program is a folder read through its .zknw manifests; every file is looked up in the overlay first and the core after, so an institution replaces a world or adds an exercise and never writes into the core. Set the overlay and the world BEFORE CourseQ: Ring copies the program into the course, so a later WithOverlay does not reach it. WithOverlay, WithoutOverlay and WithWorld change the program and have a Q twin that returns it for chaining. LIMITS, stated where you meet them: the translations (fr, ar, ha) are drafts, 0 of 35 units of each reviewed by a person when this was written, and only ReviewCoverage gives the live figure; the cells of the chapters run on the desktop only, not in a browser, and the Run methods start Ring processes whose executable path must not contain a space; no institution has adopted the system, and the two overlays shipped, bank and university, are references.
classes.example:
? o1.Id()
#--> softanza-education
? @@( o1.Languages() )
#--> [ "en", "fr", "ar", "ha" ]
? @@( o1.LevelIds() )
#--> [ "s0", "s1", "s2", "s3", "s4" ]
? @@( o1.ChaptersForLevel(o1.CourseQ("elementary-introduction"), "s0") )
#--> [ "find-then-apply", "a-first-sentence", "read-the-name-as-a-sentence", "say-it-in-your-language" ]

classes.name: stzProject
classes.brief: Holds a level project: a brief, and a guard that judges a learner's folder by running it.
classes.description: A level is earned by a project that passes, never by a score. The project is a folder with a brief in each language, guard.ring (the court, run in a fresh process with the library loaded, exactly like an exercise's harness), promise.ring (the lines the guard must print for a pass) and wrong/ and right/ sample folders that must be refused and accepted. The guard runs on the desktop only. The fr, ar and ha briefs are drafts, 0 of 35 units reviewed by a person.
classes.example:
? o1.Id()
#--> project-s0
? o1.HasGuard()
#--> 1
? @@( o1.Promises() )
#--> [ "cells five or more: yes", "every cell has a promise: yes", "every promise kept: yes", "stored output: no" ]
? o1.Check(o1.RightSamples()[1]).Passed()
#--> 1

methods.name: init
methods.brief: Opens a level project's folder, reading its guard and the promises the guard must keep when they are there.

parameters.name: pcFolder

classes.name: stzPrologCode
classes.brief: Runs a snippet of Prolog from Ring and brings its answer back as a Ring value, through a result file.
classes.description: You set the code, which must assign its answer to a variable named res; Execute wraps it with a translator, runs it with the language's program in the current folder and writes the answer as Ring text, and Result reads that text back, so numbers, texts and nested lists cross the boundary. The files temp.<ext>, a run script, the result file and log.txt are written in the current folder. It is a thin face over stzExterCode, which has the full set of controls (runtime path, result variable, log file). The Prolog program is the one configured in $aStzLibConfig[:PrologPath], d:/prolog/swipl-9.9.9/bin/swipl.exe by default. It was absent on the machine of this documentation run, so only the failure path was seen: Execute raised the not-created error.

parameters.role: the Prolog program text, which must assign its answer to a variable named res

methods.brief: Stores the Prolog source text to run, as the call with the longer name does.

parameters.name: pcPrologCode
parameters.role: the Prolog program text, which must assign its answer to a variable named res

methods.name: Execute
methods.brief: Writes the source behind a translator, runs it with the Prolog program and saves the answer for Result.
methods.returns: nothing; the answer is kept in a result file
notes: not run to completion: the Prolog program is absent here, so only the failure path was seen
warnings: it runs real code with a real program and writes temp.pl, runprolog.bat and log.txt in the current folder; the Prolog program configured by default is not installed on the machine of this run, so Execute raised the not-created error with a path-not-found log

methods.name: Run
methods.brief: Writes the source behind a translator and runs it with the Prolog program, as the call with the other name does.
methods.returns: nothing; the answer is kept in a result file
warnings: same warning as Execute: it runs real code with a real program in the current folder

methods.name: Exec
methods.brief: Writes the source behind a translator and runs it with the Prolog program, as the call with the other name does.
methods.returns: nothing; the answer is kept in a result file
warnings: same warning as Execute: it runs real code with a real program in the current folder

methods.name: Result
methods.brief: Reads the answer the Prolog code saved and turns it into a Ring value: a number, a text or nested lists.

classes.name: stzPyCodeGraph
classes.brief: Holds Python source as a code graph: its classes, methods with multiple inheritance, functions and imports.
classes.description: A sibling of stzJsCodeGraph under stzCodeGraph, which gives it the whole query surface (owners, ancestry, impact, cascade, call edges, dead code, cyclic calls). It adds Python's own identity and three ways to read source: the indentation floor, a structural scan with no dependency that finds declarations only; tree-sitter in the engine, through StzPyCodeGraphFromSourceTS, which is the preferred real parse with call edges; and Python's own ast, through a spawned interpreter, as a fallback where the grammar is not built.
classes.receiver: o1 = StzPyCodeGraphFromSource("class Animal:" + nl + "    def speak(self):" + nl + " return 1" + nl + "class Puppy(Animal):" + nl + "    def fetch(self):" + nl + " return 2" + nl)
classes.example:
? o1.Language()
#--> python
? @@( o1.Classes() )
#--> [ "Animal", "Puppy" ]
? @@( o1.AncestryOf("Puppy") )
#--> [ "Puppy", "Animal" ]
? @@( o1.OwnersOf("fetch") )
#--> [ "Puppy" ]
