classes.name: stzQmlCode
classes.brief: Shells a piece of QML out to Qt's standalone qml runtime as a child process, and captures its output and duration.
classes.description: Write the QML with SetCode, run it with Execute (which writes temp/temp.qml and starts the runtime) and read what it printed with Result. It keeps the library free of any Qt binding: the runtime is found by the name qml, by $aStzLibConfig[:QmlPath] or by SetQmlPath. It does not read an exit code, and IsRuntimeAvailable only checks that a path is configured. Use new stzQmlCode() with parentheses so that Init creates the temp folder. A QML view opens a window: the qml runtime is not installed on the machine of this documentation run, so Execute was exercised only against a path that does not exist.
classes.example:
o1.SetCode("import QtQuick 2.0" + char(10) + "Item { }")
? o1.WasExecuted()
#--> 0
? o1.TempSourcePath()
#--> temp/temp.qml

methods.name: Init
methods.brief: Creates the temp folder in the current folder where the QML source and log will be written, if it is not there.
warnings: a paren-less new (the factories StzQmlCodeQ and XQml use it) skips Init, so the folder is then created only by Execute and EnsureDirectories, and WriteSource alone raises R35 when it is missing

methods.name: SetCode
methods.brief: Stores the QML source text to run; nothing is written to disk until WriteSource or Execute.

parameters.name: pcQml
parameters.role: the QML markup, a text

warnings: a value that is not text raises an error

methods.brief: Stores the QML source text to run, as the call with the longer name does.

parameters.name: pcQml
parameters.role: the QML markup, a text

warnings: a value that is not text raises an error

methods.name: Code
methods.brief: Stores the QML source text to run, as SetCode does; it does not return the code.

parameters.name: pcQml
parameters.role: the QML markup, a text

warnings: unlike the Code of the other external-code classes, this one is a setter: read the text with Source

methods.name: Source
methods.brief: Returns the QML source text that was set; empty before SetCode.

methods.name: SetQmlPath
methods.brief: Sets the program that runs the QML, in place of the one found by the name qml or by $aStzLibConfig[:QmlPath].

parameters.name: pcPath
parameters.role: the path of the qml runtime, a non-empty text

warnings: the path is not checked: a wrong one shows only in the log of Execute; an empty or non-text path raises an error

methods.name: QmlPath
methods.brief: Returns the program that will run the QML.

methods.name: IsRuntimeAvailable
methods.brief: TRUE if a runtime path is configured.
warnings: it never looks for the program: it answered TRUE for the path C:/nowhere/qml.exe, which does not exist

methods.name: EnsureDirectories
methods.brief: Creates the temp folder in the current folder if it is missing.
warnings: starts the mkdir command through the system call

methods.name: TempSourcePath
methods.brief: Returns where the QML source is written, temp/temp.qml in the current folder.

methods.name: LogPath
methods.brief: Returns where the runtime's output is captured, temp/qmllog.txt in the current folder.

methods.name: WriteSource
methods.brief: Writes the QML source to the temp file, replacing what was there.
warnings: raises R35 when the temp folder does not exist; the file is deleted by CleanupTemp

methods.name: Execute
methods.brief: Writes the QML source, starts the qml runtime on it and captures the output and the time taken.
methods.returns: nothing; read the output with Result
notes: not run with a real runtime: the qml runtime is not installed here, so it was run with the path C:/nowhere/qml.exe, which only produced a path-not-found log
warnings: it starts a real program, which for a view opens a window and for a plain script runs until it ends; the exit code is not read, so a failure shows only as text in the log; raises an error when no source is set

methods.name: Run
methods.brief: Writes the QML source and starts the runtime, as the call with the other name does.
methods.returns: nothing; read the output with Result
notes: not run with a real runtime
warnings: same warning as Execute

methods.name: Exec
methods.brief: Writes the QML source and starts the runtime, as the call with the other name does.
methods.returns: nothing; read the output with Result
notes: not run with a real runtime
warnings: same warning as Execute

methods.name: Result
methods.brief: Returns what the runtime printed during the last run, errors included; empty before a run.
warnings: the same text as Log and Trace

methods.name: Log
methods.brief: Returns what the runtime printed during the last run, errors included.
warnings: the same text as Result and Trace

methods.name: Trace
methods.brief: Returns what the runtime printed during the last run, errors included.
warnings: not a history of runs, unlike Trace in the other external-code classes: it is the same text as Result

methods.name: Duration
methods.brief: Returns how long the last run took, in seconds; 0 before any run.

methods.name: WasExecuted
methods.brief: TRUE if Execute has run at least once.

methods.name: CleanupTemp
methods.brief: Deletes the temp source file and the log file when they exist.
warnings: the temp folder itself stays

classes.name: stzQuestion
classes.brief: Builds a question word by word and returns its answer as data when the first plain-form word closes it.
classes.description: A question is a frame: a force word opens it (WhatQ, HowManyQ, IsQ), articles and nouns fill its slots, and the first closer without a Q (Of, Is, OrNot) computes the answer. A comparison opens the right-hand side with TheSameAsQ, DifferentFromQ, MoreThanQ or LessThanQ. Nouns such as FirstCharQ, VowelsQ or LengthQ are generated from the semantic lexicon and only record the aspect; the computation happens at the closer, through the accountable dispatcher. Every answer is certain, records its reason in Why() and joins the session ask-record. The frame has no stzObject parent on purpose.
classes.example:
? o1.TheQ().FirstCharQ().Of("Ring")
#--> R
? HowManyQ().VowelsQ().Of("Ring")
#--> 1
? IsQ().TheQ().LengthQ().OfQ("Ringo").MoreThanQ().TheQ().LengthQ().Of("Ruby")
#--> 1
? Why()
#--> yes: 5 is more than 4

sections.title: grammar particles -- one word each, written once
comparators -- open the right constituent slot
closers -- plain form: answer as data (the q-convention)
hand-written aspect nouns (not lexicon op names)

methods.name: init
methods.brief: Opens a question frame with its illocutionary force: what, howmany or is; the force is not validated.

parameters.name: pcForce
parameters.role: the force word: what for a wh-question, howmany for a count, is for a polar comparison

methods.name: TheQ
methods.section: grammar particles -- one word each, written once
methods.brief: Adds the article the to the sentence and changes nothing, so a chain reads as English.
methods.returns: the question itself, so the chain goes on

methods.name: AQ
methods.section: grammar particles -- one word each, written once
methods.brief: Adds the article a to the sentence and changes nothing, so a chain reads as English.
methods.returns: the question itself, so the chain goes on

methods.name: AnQ
methods.section: grammar particles -- one word each, written once
methods.brief: Adds the article an to the sentence and changes nothing, so a chain reads as English.
methods.returns: the question itself, so the chain goes on

methods.name: NumberOfQ
methods.section: grammar particles -- one word each, written once
methods.brief: Puts the current side of the question in count mode, as in the number of letters in ring.
methods.returns: the question itself, so the chain goes on

methods.name: TheSameAsQ
methods.section: comparators -- open the right constituent slot
methods.brief: Opens the right-hand side of a comparison that asks whether the two aspects are equal.
methods.returns: the question itself, so the chain goes on

methods.name: DifferentFromQ
methods.section: comparators -- open the right constituent slot
methods.brief: Opens the right-hand side of a comparison that asks whether the two aspects differ, the way English negates a comparison.
methods.returns: the question itself, so the chain goes on

methods.name: MoreThanQ
methods.section: comparators -- open the right constituent slot
methods.brief: Opens the right-hand side of a comparison that asks whether the left aspect is greater than the right.
methods.returns: the question itself, so the chain goes on

methods.name: LessThanQ
methods.section: comparators -- open the right constituent slot
methods.brief: Opens the right-hand side of a comparison that asks whether the left aspect is smaller than the right.
methods.returns: the question itself, so the chain goes on

methods.name: Of
methods.section: closers -- plain form: answer as data (the q-convention)
methods.brief: Closes the question with its last host and returns the answer as data; OfQ and InQ record the host and keep the frame open.

parameters.name: pHost
parameters.role: the value the aspect is taken of, such as Ring

methods.returns: the answer: the value asked for, a count, or 1 or 0 for a comparison
notes: on the right-hand side it supplies the second host; In and InQ are the locative spelling
warnings: raises when no aspect was named, such as FirstCharQ

extensions.name: OfQ
extensions.adds: does what the method does, then returns the object, so the call can be chained

extensions.name: InQ
extensions.adds: does what the method does, then returns the object, so the call can be chained

methods.name: OrNot
methods.section: closers -- plain form: answer as data (the q-convention)
methods.brief: Closes a polar question with the tag or not; it does not negate, it answers the question already asked.
methods.returns: the answer, 1 or 0 for a comparison, the value for a wh-question
warnings: raises when no host was given at all

methods.name: Is
methods.section: closers -- plain form: answer as data (the q-convention)
methods.brief: Closes a question whose host is already given, as in what the first char of Ring is.
methods.returns: the answer: the value asked for, a count, or 1 or 0
warnings: raises when no host was given

methods.name: Why
methods.section: closers -- plain form: answer as data (the q-convention)
methods.brief: Returns the reason of the last answer this question gave, such as yes: 4 is the same as 4.
methods.returns: a text; empty until the question has been answered

methods.name: LengthQ
methods.section: hand-written aspect nouns (not lexicon op names)
methods.brief: Sets the noun length on the current side of the question and returns the question.
methods.detail: 'length' is not an operation name (the op is NumberOfChars); the dispatcher resolves it through the lexicon bags, so the noun only needs to exist as a WORD here.

classes.name: stzRateLimiter
classes.brief: Admits or refuses requests per key with one engine token bucket each, so short bursts pass and the sustained rate stays capped.
classes.description: Give each key a rate and a burst with SetLimit, then ask Allow before serving a request. A key with no limit is unlimited. Block and BlockFor shut a key out whatever its bucket holds; refusals are noted in the refusal ledger. Where stzRetryBudget caps the retries of one workload, this class caps the request rate of many independent keys. Destroy frees the engine buckets.
classes.example:
? o1.Allow("alice")
#--> 1
? o1.AllowN("alice", 2)
#--> 1
? o1.Allow("alice")
#--> 0
? o1.RejectedCount("alice")
#--> 1
? o1.Allow("bob")
#--> 1
o1.Destroy()

methods.name: init
methods.brief: Creates an empty rate limiter with a name, ready to receive one limit per key.

parameters.name: pcName
parameters.role: the limiter's name, used in reports and refusal notes

methods.name: Block
methods.brief: Blocks a key until it is unblocked, whatever its bucket holds, and notes the refusal reason.

parameters.name: pcKey
parameters.role: the key to block, matched without regard to case

parameters.name: pcReason
parameters.role: why it is blocked, kept for BlockOf and the refusal note

methods.returns: the limiter itself, so calls chain
warnings: blocking a key again replaces the earlier block and resets its refused count

methods.name: BlockFor
methods.brief: Blocks a key for a number of milliseconds, after which the block lifts by itself; 0 or less blocks it without end.

parameters.name: pcKey
parameters.role: the key to block, matched without regard to case

parameters.name: pcReason
parameters.role: why it is blocked

parameters.name: pnMs
parameters.role: how long the block lasts, in milliseconds

methods.returns: the limiter itself, so calls chain
warnings: the end of the block is stored as wall-clock epoch milliseconds

methods.name: Unblock
methods.brief: Lifts the block on a key; a key that is not blocked changes nothing.

parameters.name: pcKey
parameters.role: the key to unblock, matched without regard to case

methods.returns: the limiter itself, so calls chain
warnings: the bucket keeps whatever it held, so a key blocked for a long time may be refused right after

methods.name: IsBlocked
methods.brief: TRUE if the key is blocked now.

parameters.name: pcKey
parameters.role: the key to test, matched without regard to case

methods.name: BlockOf
methods.brief: Returns the block on a key as [ :reason, :until, :refused ], or an empty list when it is not blocked.

parameters.name: pcKey
parameters.role: the key to look up, matched without regard to case

warnings: :until is 0 for a block without end, else epoch milliseconds; :refused counts the Allow calls the block turned away

methods.name: BlockedKeys
methods.brief: Returns the keys that are blocked now, lower-cased, after dropping the blocks whose time has run out.

methods.name: Name_
methods.brief: Returns the name the limiter was created with.

methods.name: SetLimit
methods.brief: Gives a key its own token bucket: it holds nBurst tokens and refills at nRatePerSec tokens a second.

parameters.name: pcKey
parameters.role: the key to limit, matched without regard to case

parameters.name: nRatePerSec
parameters.role: the sustained rate, in tokens a second

parameters.name: nBurst
parameters.role: the bucket size, the most tokens that can be spent at once

methods.returns: the limiter itself, so calls chain
notes: a key with no limit is unlimited
warnings: a rate or burst below 1 is raised to 1; setting a key again replaces its bucket, which starts full

methods.name: HasLimit
methods.brief: TRUE if the key has a bucket.

parameters.name: pcKey
parameters.role: the key to test, matched without regard to case

methods.name: Keys
methods.brief: Returns the keys that have a bucket, lower-cased, in the order they were set.

methods.name: Allow
methods.brief: Takes one token from the key's bucket and answers whether the request may go ahead.

parameters.name: pcKey
parameters.role: the key making the request, matched without regard to case

warnings: a key with no limit is always allowed; a blocked key is always refused, and its refusal is counted on the block and not in RejectedCount

methods.name: AllowN
methods.brief: Takes n tokens from the key's bucket at once and answers whether the request may go ahead.

parameters.name: pcKey
parameters.role: the key making the request, matched without regard to case

parameters.name: n
parameters.role: how many tokens the request costs

warnings: n of 0 is always allowed; a refused request takes nothing from the bucket

methods.name: Available
methods.brief: Returns how many tokens are left in the key's bucket, as a decimal, or -1 for a key with no limit.

parameters.name: pcKey
parameters.role: the key to read, matched without regard to case

warnings: the bucket refills continuously, so a reading just after a spend is already a little above the exact remainder

methods.name: AllowedCount
methods.brief: Returns how many tokens were granted to the key so far; 0 for an unknown key.

parameters.name: pcKey
parameters.role: the key to read, matched without regard to case

warnings: it counts tokens, not calls: AllowN(key, 2) adds 2

methods.name: RejectedCount
methods.brief: Returns how many requests the key's bucket refused so far; 0 for an unknown key.

parameters.name: pcKey
parameters.role: the key to read, matched without regard to case

warnings: requests turned away by a block are not counted here

methods.name: RateOf
methods.brief: Returns the key's sustained rate in tokens a second; 0 for a key with no limit.

parameters.name: pcKey
parameters.role: the key to read, matched without regard to case

methods.name: BurstOf
methods.brief: Returns the key's bucket size; 0 for a key with no limit.

parameters.name: pcKey
parameters.role: the key to read, matched without regard to case

methods.name: Narrate
methods.brief: Returns a few lines of text that describe each limited key with its rate, burst and counts.

methods.name: Destroy
methods.brief: Frees the engine buckets of every key and forgets the limits.
methods.returns: the limiter itself, so calls chain
warnings: the blocks are kept

classes.name: stzRateLimiterResponder
classes.brief: Carries out the ShedSource action of a response plan by blocking a source in a rate limiter.
classes.description: A response plan proposes containment as data; a responder performs one verb for real once a committing actor approves. This one answers ShedSource only, by calling BlockFor on the limiter it holds, so the source is refused by Allow whether or not it had a limit. A duration of 0 blocks until the limiter's Unblock. Every other verb raises an error that names the responder to wire, rather than pretending. It holds the limiter by reference.
classes.receiver: oRL = new stzRateLimiter("front") o1 = new stzRateLimiterResponder(oRL, 0)
classes.example:
o1.ShedSource("Flood-Source")
? oRL.IsBlocked("flood-source")
#--> 1
? oRL.Allow("flood-source")
#--> 0
oRL.Destroy()

methods.name: init
methods.brief: Builds a responder that performs the ShedSource action of a response plan by blocking a source in a rate limiter.

parameters.name: poLimiter
parameters.role: the stzRateLimiter in which sources are blocked, held by reference

parameters.name: pnBlockMs
parameters.role: how long a block lasts in milliseconds, or 0 to block until Unblock

notes: keep the limiter alive as long as the responder is used

methods.name: Owns
methods.brief: TRUE if the verb is ShedSource, the only one this responder answers.

parameters.name: pcVerb
parameters.role: the verb, matched without regard to case

methods.name: ShedSource
methods.brief: Blocks the named source in the limiter, so every request from it is refused for the configured time.

parameters.name: pcTarget
parameters.role: the source to block, such as a client address, kept in lower case

methods.returns: nothing; the limiter then answers IsBlocked and BlockOf
notes: the block carries the reason shed by a containment plan, and the limiter notes the block in the security refusal record; with a duration of 0 the block holds until the limiter's Unblock

methods.name: LockAccount
methods.brief: Refuses by raising an error that names the responder to wire, because this responder does not lock accounts.

parameters.name: pcTarget
parameters.role: the account the plan named

notes: wire an auth responder for this verb
warnings: raises an error whatever the target

methods.name: RevokeSession
methods.brief: Refuses by raising an error that names the responder to wire, because this responder does not end sessions.

parameters.name: pcTarget
parameters.role: the actor the plan named

warnings: raises an error whatever the target

methods.name: RotateSecret
methods.brief: Refuses by raising an error that names the responder to wire, because this responder does not rotate secrets.

parameters.name: pcTarget
parameters.role: the secret the plan named

warnings: raises an error whatever the target

methods.name: RevokeCapability
methods.brief: Refuses by raising an error that names the responder to wire, because this responder does not revoke capabilities.

parameters.name: pcTarget
parameters.role: the actor the plan named

warnings: raises an error whatever the target

methods.name: QuarantinePart
methods.brief: Refuses by raising an error that names the responder to wire, because this responder does not quarantine parts.

parameters.name: pcTarget
parameters.role: the part the plan named

warnings: raises an error whatever the target

classes.name: stzRCode
classes.brief: Meant to run a snippet of R from Ring and bring its answer back as a Ring value, but Execute always raises today.
classes.description: You set the code, which must assign its answer to a variable named res; Execute wraps it with a translator, runs it with the language's program in the current folder and writes the answer as Ring text, and Result reads that text back, so numbers, texts and nested lists cross the boundary. The files temp.<ext>, a run script, the result file and log.txt are written in the current folder. It is a thin face over stzExterCode, which has the full set of controls (runtime path, result variable, log file). WARNING: with R 4.5.1 the translator that Execute puts in front of your code is rejected by R (unexpected symbol at the identifier _items_), so every run raises the not- created error with that message in its log. The R program is the one configured in $aStzLibConfig[:RPath], d:/r/r-4.5.1/bin/rscript.exe by default, which exists on this machine.

methods.name: SetCode
methods.brief: Stores the R source text to run; nothing is written to disk until Execute.

parameters.name: pcRCode
parameters.role: the R program text, which must assign its answer to a variable named res

methods.brief: Stores the R source text to run, as the call with the longer name does.

parameters.name: pcRCode
parameters.role: the R program text, which must assign its answer to a variable named res

methods.name: Execute
methods.brief: Writes the source behind a translator, runs it with the R program and saves the answer for Result.
methods.returns: nothing; the answer is kept in a result file
notes: run with a snippet that sets res: the run failed with the translator error, in a scratch folder
warnings: it runs real code with a real program and writes temp.R, runr.bat and log.txt in the current folder; with R 4.5.1 it always raises today, because the R translator that Execute adds in front of your code is rejected by R (unexpected symbol at the identifier _items_)

methods.name: Run
methods.brief: Writes the source behind a translator and runs it with the R program, as the call with the other name does.
methods.returns: nothing; the answer is kept in a result file
warnings: same warning as Execute: it runs real code with a real program in the current folder

methods.name: Exec
methods.brief: Writes the source behind a translator and runs it with the R program, as the call with the other name does.
methods.returns: nothing; the answer is kept in a result file
warnings: same warning as Execute: it runs real code with a real program in the current folder

methods.name: Result
methods.brief: Reads the answer the R code saved and turns it into a Ring value: a number, a text or nested lists.
notes: not run: needs a successful Execute
warnings: evaluates the text of the result file as Ring code, so run only code you trust; reads the result file of the last run, which does not exist here because the run failed, so it raises an error that quotes the log

methods.name: Code
methods.brief: Returns the source text that was set, or, when none is set, the source file left on disk by an earlier run.
warnings: it returns your own code, not the wrapped source that is written to disk

methods.name: Duration
methods.brief: Returns how long the last run took, in seconds; 0 before any run.

methods.name: Log
methods.brief: Returns what the R program printed during the last run, errors included.
methods.returns: a text; empty when there is no log file
warnings: on a new object it can return the log of an earlier run left in the current folder

methods.name: Trace
methods.brief: Returns the history of runs of this object, oldest first, each a hashlist of language, timestamp, duration, log, exitcode and mode.
warnings: the exit code is always recorded as 0, even for a run that failed

classes.name: stzReactive
classes.brief: Is the short name of stzReactiveSystem, so every method and every form is the same.
classes.description: Use whichever name reads better at the call site; the class adds nothing of its own.
classes.example:
? isObject( o1.ReactorQ() )
#--> 1

classes.name: stzReactiveFunc
classes.brief: Wraps a function so that each call is a task recording its status, result and error, with optional handlers.
classes.description: Call_ calls the wrapped function now with a list of up to ten parameters and answers the executed task. CallAsync takes handlers for success and failure; despite its name it runs the task at once on the calling thread and the handlers run before it returns. A failure inside the function is recorded on the task with its real reason and passed to the error handler. The wrapper keeps its engine as a copy, so tasks added to the engine are not seen by the original. It is not Ring's call function.
classes.receiver: oEngine = new stzReactive() o1 = new stzReactiveFunc(func a, b { return a + b }, oEngine)
classes.example:
oTask = o1.Call_([ 2, 3 ])
? oTask.Result()
#--> 5
? oTask.Status()
#--> completed
oBad = o1.Call_(7)
? oBad.Status()
#--> error
? oBad.Error()
#--> Reactive call params must be a list

methods.name: Init
methods.brief: Wraps a function so it can be called as a task that records its outcome.

parameters.name: f
parameters.role: the function to wrap

parameters.name: engine
parameters.role: the reactive engine the tasks are registered with

notes: the engine is kept as a copy, so a task added to it is not seen by the original engine

methods.name: Call_
methods.brief: Calls the wrapped function now with a list of parameters and returns the task holding the outcome.

parameters.name: params
parameters.role: the arguments, a list of up to 10 values

methods.returns: a stzFunctionTask already executed: read its Status, Result and Error
notes: the call is synchronous and is not run by the engine later: the task is executed here, which is what makes the result real; it is not Ring's call function
warnings: a params value that is not a list, or more than 10, leaves a task in error with the reason Reactive call params must be a list or Reactive call has too many params

methods.name: CallAsync
methods.brief: Calls the wrapped function with handlers for success and for failure, and returns the task.

parameters.name: params
parameters.role: the arguments, a list of up to 10 values

parameters.name: onComplete
parameters.role: a function taking the result

parameters.name: onError
parameters.role: a function taking the error text

notes: despite the name it runs the task at once on the calling thread, as Call_ does; the handlers run before it returns
warnings: a failure inside the function is passed to onError with its real reason, such as Error (R1) : Can't divide by zero, and the task is left in error

classes.name: stzReactiveHttp
classes.brief: Sends HTTP requests for a reactive engine, asynchronously through a reactor when it has one and blocking otherwise.
classes.description: Get_, Post, Put_ and Delete take the address, the body where there is one, and a function for success and one for failure. With a reactor set by SetReactor, http and https requests are submitted as jobs and return a job number at once; the run loop calls DrainPending, which delivers each finished job to its callback, a 2xx status to onSuccess with the body and anything else to onError. Without a reactor, or for another kind of address, each verb runs a blocking stzHttpTask and returns it. None of the four verbs was run for this reference because they reach the network; the example uses what makes no request.
classes.receiver: oEngine = new stzReactive() o1 = new stzReactiveHttp(oEngine)
classes.example:
? o1.PendingCount()
#--> 0
? o1.DrainPending()
#--> 0
o1.SetReactor(NULL)
? o1.PendingCount()
#--> 0

methods.name: Init
methods.brief: Builds an HTTP client for a reactive engine, with no reactor, so its requests are blocking until SetReactor gives one.

parameters.name: engine
parameters.role: the reactive engine the blocking tasks are registered with

methods.name: SetReactor
methods.brief: Sets the reactor that makes requests asynchronous, or removes it.

parameters.name: poReactor
parameters.role: a stzReactor, or NULL to go back to blocking requests

methods.returns: the client itself, so calls chain
notes: with a reactor, http and https requests are submitted as jobs and return at once; without one, or for any other address, each verb runs a blocking task

methods.name: PendingCount
methods.brief: Returns how many asynchronous requests have not been drained yet.
methods.returns: a number; 0 for a new client

methods.name: Get_
methods.brief: Sends a GET request and calls onSuccess with the body or onError with the failure text.

parameters.name: url
parameters.role: the address

parameters.name: onSuccess
parameters.role: a function taking the response body

parameters.name: onError
parameters.role: a function taking the failure text

methods.returns: a stzHttpTask, already executed, on the blocking path; the job number on the asynchronous path, -1 when the reactor refused it
notes: on the asynchronous path the callbacks run later, from DrainPending in the run loop; the failure text is HTTP request failed, with the status in parentheses when there is one
warnings: not run: it reaches the network

methods.name: Post
methods.brief: Sends a POST request with a body and calls onSuccess with the response body or onError with the failure text.

parameters.name: url
parameters.role: the address

parameters.name: data
parameters.role: the body to send

parameters.name: onSuccess
parameters.role: a function taking the response body

parameters.name: onError
parameters.role: a function taking the failure text

methods.returns: a stzHttpTask on the blocking path; the job number on the asynchronous path
notes: success is a status from 200 to 299
warnings: not run: it reaches the network

methods.name: Put_
methods.brief: Sends a PUT request with a body and calls onSuccess with the response body or onError with the failure text.

parameters.name: url
parameters.role: the address

parameters.name: data
parameters.role: the body to send

parameters.name: onSuccess
parameters.role: a function taking the response body

parameters.name: onError
parameters.role: a function taking the failure text

methods.returns: a stzHttpTask on the blocking path; the job number on the asynchronous path
warnings: not run: it reaches the network

methods.name: Delete
methods.brief: Sends a DELETE request and calls onSuccess with the response body or onError with the failure text.

parameters.name: url
parameters.role: the address

parameters.name: onSuccess
parameters.role: a function taking the response body

parameters.name: onError
parameters.role: a function taking the failure text

methods.returns: a stzHttpTask on the blocking path; the job number on the asynchronous path
notes: on the blocking path a delete answered with no body counts as a failure
warnings: not run: it reaches the network

methods.name: DrainPending
methods.brief: Delivers every finished asynchronous request to its callback, for the run loop to call each tick.
methods.returns: the number of requests delivered; 0 when none was pending or none had finished
notes: a 2xx status calls onSuccess with the body, any other status or a failed job calls onError; a job still in flight stays pending; run with nothing pending it answered 0

classes.name: stzReactiveObject
classes.brief: Turns attributes into values that notify: a change runs watchers, recalculates dependent attributes and updates bindings.
classes.description: A reactive object holds named attributes, made from nothing or wrapped around an existing object. SetAttribute stores a value and, when it changed, calls the functions registered with Watch, recomputes the attributes declared with Computed from the attributes they depend on, and writes to the targets given to BindTo. WaitForAttributetoSettle calls a function once an attribute stops changing, and Batch notifies a group of changes together afterwards. An error inside a watcher, a calculated attribute or a batch does not stop the caller: it is recorded (Errors, LastError, ErrorCount) and passed to the OnError handler, or printed when there is none. Names are not case sensitive. Two members do not work as intended today: a binding reaches its target only once, when it is made, and StreamAttribute never emits.
classes.example:
gLog = []
o1.Watch(:name, func(oSelf, attr, oldV, newV) { gLog + [ oldV, newV ] })
o1.SetAttribute(:name, "Ann")
o1.SetAttribute(:name, "Bob")
? @@( gLog )
#--> [ [ "", "Ann" ], [ "Ann", "Bob" ] ]
o1.Computed(:greeting, func oSelf { return "Hello " + oSelf.GetAttribute(:name) }, [ :name ])
o1.SetAttribute(:name, "Cy")
? o1.GetAttribute(:greeting)
#--> Hello Cy
o1.OnError(func(w, m) { })
o1.Watch(:age, "not a function")
? o1.LastError()
#--> Watch callback is not a function

methods.name: OnError
methods.brief: Sets the handler that receives each error the object catches instead of printing it, and returns the object.

parameters.name: fCallback
parameters.role: a function taking two arguments, the place that failed and the message

methods.returns: the object itself, so calls chain
notes: without a handler the error is printed as [stzReactiveObject.place] message, and recorded either way

methods.name: Errors
methods.brief: Returns the errors recorded so far, as pairs of the place that failed and its message, oldest first.
methods.returns: a list of [ place, message ] pairs; at most 50 are kept
notes: the places look like Watch:name, Watcher:name, Computed:name, Binding:name->target or Batch

methods.name: LastError
methods.brief: Returns the message of the newest recorded error.
methods.returns: a text; empty when nothing was recorded

methods.name: LastErrorWhere
methods.brief: Returns the place of the newest recorded error, such as Watch:age or Batch.
methods.returns: a text; empty when nothing was recorded

methods.name: ErrorCount
methods.brief: Returns how many errors were seen, including the ones dropped once 50 were kept.

methods.name: ErrorsDropped
methods.brief: Returns how many errors were counted but not kept, because the record holds 50.

methods.name: HasErrors
methods.brief: TRUE if at least one error was recorded since the last ClearErrors.

methods.name: ClearErrors
methods.brief: Empties the error record and its counters, then returns the object.
methods.returns: the object itself, so calls chain

methods.name: Init
methods.brief: Builds the reactive object around an existing object, or around nothing when given an empty text, and keeps the engine that serves it.

parameters.name: existingObject
parameters.role: the object to wrap, or an empty text for an object made of attributes only

parameters.name: reactiveEngine
parameters.role: the stzReactive system that serves timers and streams

notes: the attributes of a wrapped object are read into the storage and the cache when it is built
warnings: the wrapped object is stored as a copy: changing the original afterwards does not reach the reactive object, and setting through the reactive object does not change the original

methods.name: BraceStart
methods.brief: Runs when Ring opens a brace block on the object, and does nothing today.

methods.name: BraceEnd
methods.brief: Runs when Ring closes a brace block on the object, and notifies the changes queued during the block.

methods.name: BraceError
methods.brief: Runs when a call in a brace block fails, and hands the error text to the failure function of every SetAsync made so far.
warnings: the SetAsync records are never removed, so a later failed brace call reaches the failure handlers of earlier, finished SetAsync calls as well

methods.name: SetAttribute
methods.brief: Sets an attribute, creating it when new, and on a real change runs its watchers, dependent attributes and bindings.

parameters.name: _cAttribute_
parameters.role: the attribute's name, which is lowercased

parameters.name: _newValue_
parameters.role: the value to store

methods.returns: the object itself, so calls chain
notes: the name is lowercased, so :Name and :name are one attribute
warnings: inside Batch the notifications are queued and the value is stored at once; an equal value triggers nothing

methods.brief: Sets an attribute from a pair of its name and its value, so that a set reads like an assignment.

parameters.name: paAttr
parameters.role: a list of two items, the attribute's name and its value

notes: it calls SetAttribute and, unlike it, does not return the object

methods.name: GetAttribute
methods.brief: Returns the current value of an attribute, matched without regard to case.

parameters.name: _cAttribute_
parameters.role: the attribute's name

methods.returns: the value; an empty text when the attribute is unknown

methods.name: GetAttributeValue
methods.brief: Returns the value of an attribute, reading the cache first, then the wrapped object, then the storage.

parameters.name: _cAttribute_
parameters.role: the attribute's name

methods.returns: the value; an empty text when the attribute is unknown
warnings: a value written with SetAttributeValue is not read back while the cache holds an older one

methods.name: SetAttributeValue
methods.brief: Writes a value into the storage, the wrapped object and the object's own attribute, without any notification and without touching the cache.

parameters.name: _cAttribute_
parameters.role: the attribute's name

parameters.name: _value_
parameters.role: the value to write

notes: it is the call a binding makes on its target
warnings: GetAttribute keeps answering the older value for an attribute already in the cache; use SetAttribute to set and notify

methods.name: Watch
methods.brief: Registers a function called as f(object, name, oldValue, newValue) each time the attribute changes, and returns the object.

parameters.name: _cAttribute_
parameters.role: the attribute to watch

parameters.name: fCallback
parameters.role: a function taking four arguments: the reactive object, the attribute's name, the old value and the new value

methods.returns: the object itself, so calls chain
notes: the function runs on every real change, in order of registration; an error inside it is recorded as Watcher:name
warnings: a value that is not a function is refused: nothing is stored and the error Watch callback is not a function is recorded

methods.name: Computed
methods.brief: Creates an attribute whose value is calculated by a function from other attributes, now and again each time one of them changes.

parameters.name: _cAttribute_
parameters.role: the name of the calculated attribute

parameters.name: _fnComputer_
parameters.role: a function taking the reactive object and returning the value

parameters.name: _aDependencies_
parameters.role: the names of the attributes it depends on, as a list

methods.returns: the object itself, so calls chain
notes: a watcher on the calculated attribute also fires when it is recomputed
warnings: a function that is not one, or dependencies that are not a list, are refused and recorded, and nothing is created

methods.name: BindTo
methods.brief: Binds an attribute to an attribute of another reactive object, copying its current value to the target at once.

parameters.name: oTargetObject
parameters.role: the reactive object that receives the value

parameters.name: _cSourceAttribute_
parameters.role: the attribute of this object to follow

parameters.name: _cTargetAttribute_
parameters.role: the attribute to write in the target, or an empty text for the same name

methods.returns: the object itself, so calls chain
notes: the starting value is written to the object you passed
warnings: a later change of the source does not reach the target object you passed, because the binding keeps a copy of the target: the target holds the value of the moment of binding; a target that is not an object is refused and recorded

methods.name: SetAsync
methods.brief: Sets an attribute at once, completes a task with the value, calls the success function, and returns the task.

parameters.name: _cAttribute_
parameters.role: the attribute's name

parameters.name: _newValue_
parameters.role: the value to set

parameters.name: fnSuccess
parameters.role: a function taking the value, or an empty text

parameters.name: fnError
parameters.role: a function taking the error text, or an empty text

methods.returns: a stzReactiveTask, already completed or failed
notes: the error is also recorded as SetAsync:name
warnings: the name suggests a deferred update, but nothing waits: the value is set before the call returns

methods.name: Batch
methods.brief: Runs a function in which attribute changes are stored at once but notified together afterwards, then returns the object.

parameters.name: fnUpdates
parameters.role: the function with no argument that makes the changes

methods.returns: the object itself, so calls chain
notes: each changed attribute is notified once
warnings: the watcher receives the first change of an attribute, with its old value and the value it had then, not the last: after sets of 1, 2 and 3 on an attribute that held 10 it is told 10 and 1 while the attribute holds 3; an error in the function is recorded as Batch and the changes already made stay

methods.name: StreamAttribute
methods.brief: Returns a stream that never emits, because the watcher behind it fails at every change; the failure is recorded, not raised.

parameters.name: _cAttribute_
parameters.role: the attribute to follow

methods.returns: a stream object; it stays empty
warnings: the watcher raises error R24 Using uninitialized variable: _stream_, because the function it registers reads a local of the method; the error is recorded as Watcher:name and nothing reaches the stream

methods.name: WaitForAttributetoSettle
methods.brief: Calls a function once an attribute has stopped changing for the given delay, with the last change, and returns the object.

parameters.name: _cAttribute_
parameters.role: the attribute to watch

parameters.name: nDelay
parameters.role: the quiet time in milliseconds

parameters.name: fCallback
parameters.role: a function taking three arguments: the name, the old value and the new value

methods.returns: the object itself, so calls chain
notes: after three quick sets, the function ran once, with the second value as old and the last as new; DebounceAttribute is the same call
warnings: the timer is run by the reactive loop, so nothing fires until the loop runs

methods.name: OnSettleChange
methods.brief: Restarts the settle timer of an attribute each time it changes, so that the function fires only when the changes stop.

parameters.name: cAttr
parameters.role: the attribute that changed

parameters.name: oldVal
parameters.role: its old value

parameters.name: newVal
parameters.role: its new value

warnings: internal: the object registers it for you

methods.name: Reactivate
methods.brief: Returns a new reactive object wrapping an object, which is copied.

parameters.name: existingObject
parameters.role: the object to wrap, or an empty text

warnings: the new object is given this reactive object as its engine, not the stzReactive system, so StreamAttribute on it raises error R14 Calling Method without definition: createstream

methods.name: GetAttributeFromStorage
methods.brief: Returns the value of an attribute from the storage only, ignoring the cache and the wrapped object.

parameters.name: _cAttribute_
parameters.role: the attribute's name

methods.returns: the value; an empty text when absent

methods.name: SetAttributeInStorage
methods.brief: Writes a value into the storage only, adding the attribute when absent.

parameters.name: _cAttribute_
parameters.role: the attribute's name

parameters.name: _value_
parameters.role: the value to store

methods.name: UpdateAttributeCache
methods.brief: Writes a value into the cache that GetAttribute reads first, adding the attribute when absent.

parameters.name: _cAttribute_
parameters.role: the attribute's name

parameters.name: _value_
parameters.role: the value to cache

methods.name: FindAttributeInCache
methods.brief: Returns the position of an attribute in the cache, or 0 when it is not cached.

parameters.name: _cAttribute_
parameters.role: the attribute's name

methods.name: ProcessAttributeChange
methods.brief: Notifies one change: runs the watchers, recomputes the calculated attributes that depend on it, and updates the bound targets.

parameters.name: _cAttribute_
parameters.role: the attribute that changed

parameters.name: oldValue
parameters.role: its previous value

parameters.name: _newValue_
parameters.role: its new value

warnings: calling it directly notifies without changing any value

methods.name: ProcessPendingReactions
methods.brief: Notifies the changes queued by Batch, if any.

methods.name: ProcessBatchChanges
methods.brief: Notifies each attribute queued by Batch once, using its first queued change, then empties the queue.

methods.name: TriggerAttributeWatchers
methods.brief: Calls every watcher of an attribute as f(object, name, oldValue, newValue); an error in one is recorded and the others still run.

parameters.name: _cAttribute_
parameters.role: the attribute whose watchers to call

parameters.name: oldValue
parameters.role: the old value to pass

parameters.name: _newValue_
parameters.role: the new value to pass

methods.name: UpdateDependentComputedAttributes
methods.brief: Recomputes each calculated attribute that lists the changed attribute among its dependencies.

parameters.name: _cChangedAttribute_
parameters.role: the attribute that changed

methods.name: UpdateBoundAttributes
methods.brief: Writes a new value to the target of each binding that follows the attribute.

parameters.name: _cAttribute_
parameters.role: the source attribute

parameters.name: _newValue_
parameters.role: the value to write

warnings: the targets written are the copies kept by BindTo, so the object you passed to BindTo does not see the value

methods.name: ComputeAttribute
methods.brief: Recomputes one calculated attribute with its function, stores the result and runs the watchers of the attribute.

parameters.name: _cAttribute_
parameters.role: the name of a calculated attribute

warnings: an error in the function is recorded as Computed:name and the old value stays

classes.name: stzReactiveStream
classes.brief: Carries values one by one through steps (transform, filter, accumulate) to the functions that subscribed to it.
classes.description: Values enter with Recieve (spelt Receive, Feed, Emit or Send as well) and leave through the functions given to OnPassed, after the steps added with Transform and Filter, in the order they were added. Accumulate replaces the per-value output with one final result, handed to the subscribers when the stream concludes: by Conclude, or by itself after a quiet delay once the loop runs. SetOverflowStrategy bounds the buffer and decides what is lost when it is full; OverflowStats counts what was lost. A stream made with new is inactive and ignores values until Start is called, and one made by stzReactive.CreateStream is already started. Known faults: OnBufferFull functions are never called, and a stream that concluded at once through RecieveMany can conclude a second time when its pending timer fires.
classes.example:
gOut = []
o1.Transform(func p { return p * 2 })
o1.Filter(func p { return p >= 100 })
o1.OnPassed(func v { gOut + v })
o1.SetAutoConclude(0)
o1.Recieve(30)
o1.Recieve(60)
o1.Recieve(80)
? @@( gOut )
#--> [ 120, 160 ]
o2 = oRs.CreateStream("sum")
gSum = []
o2.Accumulate(func(t, x) { return t + x }, 0)
o2.OnPassed(func t { gSum + t })
o2.SetAutoConclude(0)
o2.Recieve(5)
o2.Recieve(7)
? @@( gSum )
#--> [ ]
o2.Conclude()
? @@( gSum )
#--> [ 12 ]

methods.name: Init
methods.brief: Builds a stream with an id, a kind of source and the system that serves it; an unknown source kind becomes manual.

parameters.name: id
parameters.role: the stream's name, as text

parameters.name: sourceType
parameters.role: the kind of source: manual, libuv, timer, file, network or sensor

parameters.name: engine
parameters.role: the stzReactive system that created it

notes: the kind of source only labels the stream
warnings: a stream built with new is inactive and ignores every value until Start is called; CreateStream of stzReactive starts it for you

methods.name: Transform
methods.brief: Adds a step that replaces each value by the result of a function, then returns the stream; steps run in the order they were added.

parameters.name: mapFunction
parameters.role: a function taking one value and returning the new value

methods.returns: the stream itself, so calls chain
notes: Map is the same call

methods.name: Filter
methods.brief: Adds a step that lets a value go on only when a function answers true for it, then returns the stream.

parameters.name: filterFunction
parameters.role: a function taking one value and returning TRUE to keep it

methods.returns: the stream itself, so calls chain
notes: Where is the same call

methods.name: Accumulate
methods.brief: Adds a step that folds all the values into one running result, which the subscribers receive only when the stream concludes.

parameters.name: reduceFunction
parameters.role: a function taking the running result and the new value and returning the new result

parameters.name: initialValue
parameters.role: the result before the first value

methods.returns: the stream itself, so calls chain
notes: Reduce is the same call
warnings: with this step the subscribers get nothing per value; they get the final result once, at Conclude

methods.name: OnPassed
methods.brief: Registers a function called with each value that comes out of the steps, then returns the stream.

parameters.name: _Rf_
parameters.role: a function taking one value

methods.returns: the stream itself, so calls chain
notes: OnRecieved, OnReceived, Subscribe, OnNext and OnPass are the same call

methods.name: OnRecieved
methods.brief: Registers a function called with each value that comes out of the steps, then returns the stream.

parameters.name: _Rf_
parameters.role: a function taking one value

methods.returns: the stream itself, so calls chain
notes: the same call as OnPassed

methods.name: OnReceived
methods.brief: Registers a function called with each value that comes out of the steps, then returns the stream.

parameters.name: _Rf_
parameters.role: a function taking one value

methods.returns: the stream itself, so calls chain
notes: the same call as OnPassed

methods.name: Subscribe
methods.brief: Registers a function called with each value that comes out of the steps, then returns the stream.

parameters.name: _Rf_
parameters.role: a function taking one value

methods.returns: the stream itself, so calls chain
notes: the same call as OnPassed

methods.name: OnNext
methods.brief: Registers a function called with each value that comes out of the steps, then returns the stream.

parameters.name: _Rf_
parameters.role: a function taking one value

methods.returns: the stream itself, so calls chain
notes: the same call as OnPassed

methods.name: OnPass
methods.brief: Registers a function called with each value that comes out of the steps, then returns the stream.

parameters.name: _Rf_
parameters.role: a function taking one value

methods.returns: the stream itself, so calls chain
notes: the same call as OnPassed

methods.name: OnError
methods.brief: Registers a function called with the error text when CheckErrorHandling reports one, then returns the stream.

parameters.name: errorHandler
parameters.role: a function taking the error

methods.returns: the stream itself, so calls chain
warnings: an error raised inside a step or a subscriber is not routed here: it reaches the caller of Recieve

methods.name: OnNoMore
methods.brief: Registers a function called, with no argument, when the stream concludes, then returns the stream.

parameters.name: concludeHandler
parameters.role: a function taking no argument

methods.returns: the stream itself, so calls chain
notes: OnComplete is the same call

methods.name: Recieve
methods.brief: Takes one value into the stream and, when no overflow strategy is set, runs it through the steps and the subscribers at once.

parameters.name: data
parameters.role: the value to take in, of any type

notes: Feed, FeedWith, Emit, Send and Receive are the same call
warnings: ignored without any error when the stream is stopped or concluded; with an overflow strategy set, the value is only buffered until ProcessAnItemFromBuffer or ProcessAllInBuffer runs

extensions.name: RecieveMany
extensions.adds: works on a collection of items instead of one

extensions.name: FeedMany
extensions.adds: works on a collection of items instead of one

extensions.name: FeedWithMany
extensions.adds: works on a collection of items instead of one

extensions.name: SendMany
extensions.adds: works on a collection of items instead of one

extensions.name: ReceiveMany
extensions.adds: works on a collection of items instead of one

extensions.name: EmitMany
extensions.adds: works on a collection of items instead of one

methods.name: SetAutoConclude
methods.brief: Turns automatic conclusion on or off and returns the stream; turning it off cancels a pending timer.

parameters.name: enabled
parameters.role: 1 to conclude by itself after a quiet delay, 0 to conclude only by Conclude

methods.returns: the stream itself, so calls chain
notes: on by default; SetAutoComplete is the same call

extensions.name: SetAutoConcludeXT
extensions.adds: the extended form: more parameters than the base method

methods.name: SetAutoConcludeDelay
methods.brief: Sets the quiet time, in milliseconds, that precedes automatic conclusion, and returns the stream.

parameters.name: pnMilliseconds
parameters.role: the delay, a number not below 0

methods.returns: the stream itself, so calls chain
notes: the default is 100
warnings: a value that is not a number or is negative is ignored and the old delay stays

methods.name: ScheduleAutoConclude
methods.brief: Starts, or restarts, the timer that concludes the stream when no value is pending after the quiet delay.
notes: Recieve calls it after every value
warnings: the timer is run by the reactive loop, so nothing happens until the loop runs; it acts on a copy of the stream taken now

methods.name: PendingDataCount
methods.brief: Returns how many values were received and not yet processed.

methods.name: AutoConcludeEnabled
methods.brief: TRUE if the stream concludes by itself after a quiet delay.

methods.name: ClearAutoConcludeTimer
methods.brief: Forgets the pending timer's id without cancelling it, and returns the stream.
methods.returns: the stream itself, so calls chain
notes: the timer calls it when it fires

methods.name: ScheduleAutoComplete
methods.brief: Starts, or restarts, the timer that concludes the stream when no value is pending after the quiet delay.
notes: the same call as ScheduleAutoConclude

methods.name: AutoConclude
methods.brief: Concludes the stream if it has an accumulating step or a conclude function and is not already concluded; otherwise does nothing.
notes: AutoComplete is the same call

methods.name: AutoComplete
methods.brief: Concludes the stream if it has an accumulating step or a conclude function and is not already concluded; otherwise does nothing.
notes: the same call as AutoConclude

methods.name: Conclude
methods.brief: Ends the stream once: hands the final accumulated result to the subscribers, calls the conclude functions and stops the stream.
notes: Complete is the same call
warnings: a second call does nothing; the stream accepts no value afterwards until Start is called

methods.name: Start
methods.brief: Makes the stream accept values, clears its concluded state, and returns it.
methods.returns: the stream itself, so calls chain
notes: CreateStream of stzReactive has already called it

methods.name: Stop
methods.brief: Makes the stream ignore values until Start is called, and returns it.
methods.returns: the stream itself, so calls chain

methods.name: Cleanup
methods.brief: Stops the stream and releases its libuv handle, if it has one.

methods.name: CheckErrorHandling
methods.brief: Calls every error function with the error and stops the stream; ignored when the stream is stopped or concluded.

parameters.name: error
parameters.role: the error to report, usually a text

classes.name: stzReactiveSystem
classes.brief: Declarative reactive programming: schedules timers and tasks, makes functions and objects reactive, makes streams and non-blocking HTTP calls, and runs them all in one loop.
classes.description: Create one system, register what should happen (RunAfter, RunEvery, CreateTimer, CreateTask, HttpGet, the stream makers), then call Start: the loop runs the pending tasks, ticks the timers and drains the HTTP answers until nothing is left, the patience runs out or a callback calls Stop. The system sits on a stzReactor when the engine library is present, and falls back to a polling loop when it is not. Callbacks always run on the Ring thread. Timers are named by the id that RunAfter and RunEvery answer; StopTimer and StopAllTimers end them. Reactivate wraps a function or an object so that calls take success and error handlers. StopSafe and its five spellings ask the loop to end at the close of the pass that is running, from inside a callback. BindObjects binds the reactive objects you pass, once: the target takes the source value of the moment of binding.
classes.example:
? isObject( o1.ReactorQ() )
#--> 1

classes.name: stzReactiveTask
classes.brief: Holds one piece of asynchronous work, a function with a status, a result, an error and handlers, as the base of every reactive task.
classes.description: A task is pending until Execute runs its function once; it then records completed with the result, or error with the real reason, for example Error (R1) : Can't divide by zero. Then_ sets the handler for success and Catch_ the one for failure. The error mode decides what a failure does: ERROR_LOG prints it, ERROR_THROW raises it again, ERROR_CALLBACK calls the Catch_ function and ERROR_IGNORE stays silent, and the reason is on the task in every mode, readable with Error. Complete and Fail let a caller that did the work itself report through the same surface. The class is the base of stzHttpTask and stzFunctionTask and is not meant for the final programmer.
classes.receiver: oEngine = new stzReactive() o1 = new stzReactiveTask("t1", func { return 6 * 7 }, oEngine, "") o2 = new stzReactiveTask("t2", func { return 1 / 0 }, oEngine, ERROR_IGNORE)
classes.example:
? o1.Status()
#--> pending
o1.Execute()
? o1.Status()
#--> completed
? o1.Result()
#--> 42
o2.Execute()
? o2.HasFailed()
#--> 1
? o2.Error()
#--> Error (R1) : Can't divide by zero
? o2.WasReported()
#--> 0
o3 = new stzReactiveTask("t3", "", oEngine, "")
o3.Complete("from outside")
? o3.Result()
#--> from outside

parameters.name: engine
parameters.role: the reactive engine, kept for subclasses

parameters.name: errorMode
parameters.role: how a failure is reported: ERROR_LOG, ERROR_THROW, ERROR_CALLBACK or ERROR_IGNORE, or an empty text for the default ERROR_LOG

methods.returns: nothing; the task is built and not run
notes: the class is meant for subclasses such as stzHttpTask and stzFunctionTask and not for the final programmer

classes.name: stzReactiveTimer
classes.brief: Holds a timer that calls a function every interval, or once, advanced by a timer manager's loop on the engine's clock.
classes.description: The timer does not run by itself: a stzTimerManager loop calls CheckAndTick, which fires the function when the interval has passed since the last firing, on the engine's monotonic clock in milliseconds, and answers whether the timer is still active so the manager can prune finished one- shots. A one-shot timer stops itself after firing. Start takes the time now as the starting point; Tick calls the function at once whatever the clock says.
classes.receiver: $nFired = 0 o1 = new stzReactiveTimer("beat", 30, func { $nFired++ }, new stzReactive(), 0)
classes.example:
? o1.CheckAndTick()
#--> 0
o1.Tick()
? $nFired
#--> 1
o1.Start()
? o1.CheckAndTick()
#--> 1
? $nFired
#--> 1
StzEngineTimeSleepMs(60)
? o1.CheckAndTick()
#--> 1
? $nFired
#--> 2
o1.Stop()
? o1.CheckAndTick()
#--> 0

classes.name: stzReactor
classes.brief: Runs timers, TCP and HTTP clients, child programs and servers on a libuv event loop that lives on a thread of its own, and hands the results to Ring by polling.
classes.description: Ring stays synchronous: you submit work and get a job id back at once, then Poll, Await or JobState that id, and no callback ever crosses into Ring. The calls come in families: Submit, Await, Poll and a LastStatus reader for timers, TCP, spawned programs and HTTP, plus one-call forms (TcpRequest, Spawn, HttpGet, HttpPost). A listener (Listen, ListenHttp, ListenStzm and the TLS forms) queues events that ServerPoll or ServerAwait drain as [ :accept, nConn, "" ], [ :data, nConn, cBytes ] or [ :closed, nConn, "" ]; ServerWrite and ServerCloseConn answer on a connection, and the Connect calls dial out and give a channel that is used the same way. A job id is spent once it is drained. The last-status readers (TcpLastStatus, SpawnLastStatus, HttpLastStatus, TlsClientStatus) hold one value for the whole process. The loop starts at the first call and Destroy stops it. Known gap today: Spawn and SubmitSpawn raise error R21 when given a plain text instead of a list.
classes.example:
? o1.AwaitTimer( o1.SubmitTimer(20), 2000 )
#--> 0

classes.name: stzReactorHttpClient
classes.brief: Sends real HTTP requests through the reactor's curl client and reports only a body, with status 200 or 0.
classes.description: It is the live side of the HTTP port, with the same Request(method, url, body) shape as stzHttpSandbox. The reactor's client returns a body and no status line, so the adapter answers status 200 when content came back and 0 when nothing did; headers, redirects and non-2xx bodies are not seen. It was run only against a listener started on 127.0.0.1 in the same process, which never answers, and against a closed port: both gave status 0. The 200 path was read from the code and not run.
classes.example:
o1.SetTimeout(500)
? o1.Timeout()
#--> 500
? o1.GetFrom("http://127.0.0.1:1/x")[:status]
#--> 0

classes.name: stzReactorPool
classes.brief: Holds several reactors, each an event loop on its own thread, and sends a batch of TCP requests across them at once.
classes.description: A pool is libuv's multi-loop scaling model: work is round-robined across the loops, each loop multiplexes many connections, and Ring stays synchronous, submitting a batch and then awaiting the answers in order. A handful of loops is plenty for most uses. FetchAll takes a list of [ host, port, payload ] and answers the response texts in the same order. The requests reach the network and were not run for this reference.
classes.example:
? o1.Count()
#--> 3
? @@( o1.FetchAll([ ], 100) )
#--> [ ]
o1.Destroy()
? o1.Count()
#--> 0
? StzReactorPool(0).Count()
#--> 1

classes.name: stzRecursiveRegexMaker
classes.brief: Describes a pattern as named levels nested inside one another, each with its own piece of pattern and quantifier.
classes.description: A level has a name, a pattern text, a parent, children and a quantifier. AddLevel adds a top level, AddChildLevel adds one inside an existing level, and AddQuantifier gives a level its repeat suffix. The tree can be read back with LevelNames, LevelParent, LevelChildren and Info. With named recursion on, which is the state at birth, each level becomes a named capture group. Pattern joins the top levels into one regular expression, each level nesting its children inside its own group, and SubPattern does the same for one level. stzNestedRegexMaker is another name for this class.
classes.example:
o1.AddLevel("open", "\(")
o1.AddChildLevel("open", "inner", "[^()]*")
o1.AddLevel("close", "\)")
? @@( o1.LevelNames() )
#--> [ "open", "inner", "close" ]
? @@( o1.LevelChildren("open") )
#--> [ "inner" ]
? o1.LevelParent("inner")
#--> open
? o1.Pattern()
#--> (?P<open>\((?P<inner>[^()]*))\)
o1.AddQuantifier("inner", "+")
? o1.Info()[2][:quantifier]
#--> +

methods.name: init
methods.brief: Builds an empty maker of levelled patterns, with named recursion switched on.
notes: named recursion is on at birth and off after Reset

methods.name: AddLevel
methods.brief: Adds a top level, a named piece of pattern with no parent, after the levels already added.

parameters.name: cName
parameters.role: the level's name

parameters.name: _cPattern_
parameters.role: the pattern text of the level

warnings: a name that already exists is added again; the name is matched with case, and the first one is found by the other calls

methods.name: AddChildLevel
methods.brief: Adds a level inside an existing level, which becomes its parent.

parameters.name: cParentName
parameters.role: the name of an existing level

parameters.name: cChildName
parameters.role: the name of the new level

parameters.name: _cPattern_
parameters.role: the pattern text of the new level

warnings: an unknown parent raises Parent level 'name' not found!

methods.name: AddQuantifier
methods.brief: Sets the repeat suffix of a level, such as + or *, replacing the one it had.

parameters.name: cLevelName
parameters.role: the name of an existing level

parameters.name: cQuant
parameters.role: the suffix text, such as + or {2,3}

warnings: an unknown level raises Level 'name' not found!

methods.name: EnableNamedRecursion
methods.brief: Makes each level a named capture group when the pattern is built.

methods.name: DisableNamedRecursion
methods.brief: Stops wrapping each level in a named capture group when the pattern is built.

methods.name: Pattern
methods.brief: Returns the regular expression joined from the top levels, each with its children nested inside it.
methods.returns: a text; empty when no level was added
notes: with named recursion on, which is the state at birth, each level becomes a named group (?P<name>pattern) holding its own pattern followed by its children, then its quantifier; a child is written inside the group of its parent, not after it; a level named close is the exception and is written as its bare pattern, with no group, no children and no quantifier; a pattern text can refer to a group with (?P>name), which is how a recursive pattern is made
warnings: levels added with the same name are all written, and the other calls find the first

methods.name: SubPattern
methods.brief: Returns the regular expression of one level, with its children nested inside it; empty for an unknown level.

parameters.name: cLevelName
parameters.role: the name of a level, matched with case

notes: it is the part of the Pattern text that the level writes, so a child level gives its own group and a level named close gives its bare pattern

methods.name: LevelNames
methods.brief: Returns the names of all the levels, in the order they were added.

methods.name: NumberOfLevels
methods.brief: Returns how many levels were added.

methods.name: HasLevel
methods.brief: TRUE if a level of that name exists.

parameters.name: cName
parameters.role: the level's name, matched with case

methods.name: LevelParent
methods.brief: Returns the name of the level a level sits inside; an empty text for a top level or an unknown level.

parameters.name: cName
parameters.role: the level's name

methods.name: LevelChildren
methods.brief: Returns the names of the levels added inside a level, in order; an empty list for an unknown or childless level.

parameters.name: cName
parameters.role: the level's name

methods.name: Info
methods.brief: Returns one hashlist per level, with its name, pattern, parent, children and quantifier.
methods.returns: a list of hashlists; the parent and the children are positions in the list, and the parent is an empty text for a top level

classes.name: stzRefinableCode
classes.brief: Treats tagged values in source code as typed, reversible knobs: a change is a proposal that passes a gate, never a diff.
classes.description: Mark the adjustable values of a piece of code with tags such as <R:PARAM name="vat" value="0.20" min="0" max="0.9"> or <R:ALGO name="sort" value="quick" options="quick|merge|heap">. RefinementPoints lists them and Cascade previews what a change touches. Refine(name).To(value) sends the proposal through the gate: the point must exist, the value must respect min and max or the options, then governance (when wired), the trust floor and the derivation rules decide. The answer is a hash-list with admitted and why, and a refused change never alters the source. Every admitted change goes on a timeline that Revert, RevertTo, Checkpoint and Redo walk, and Rendered returns the refined source. Refine only code you own: Save writes a file with the extension zrfn.
classes.receiver: o1 = new stzRefinableCode('vat = <R:PARAM name="vat" value="0.20" min="0" max="0.9">' + char(10) + 'engine = <R:ALGO name="sort" value="quick" options="quick|merge|heap">')
classes.example:
? @@( o1.RefinementPoints() )
#--> [ [ "vat", "param", "0.20" ], [ "sort", "algo", "quick" ] ]
? o1.Refine("vat").To("0.22")[:admitted]
#--> 1
? o1.Refine("vat").To("0.95")[:admitted]
#--> 0
? @@( o1.Why() )
#--> "constraint: 0.95 above max 0.9"
? @@( o1.ValueOf("vat") )
#--> "0.22"
o1.Refine("sort").To("heap")
? o1.NumberOfSteps()
#--> 2
o1.Revert()
? @@( o1.ValueOf("sort") )
#--> "quick"
? o1.CanRedo()
#--> 1

classes.name: stzRegex
classes.brief: Holds a regular expression compiled by the PCRE2 engine and answers whether, where and how a text matches it, including partial and recursive matches.
classes.description: Build it with a pattern, then call a match method with a text: the text and the outcome of the last call are kept in the object, and the readers (Matches, FindMatches, CaptureGroups, NamedGroups, CaptureByName, the partial and recursive readers) work on that last call. Match asks whether the pattern covers the whole text; MatchFirst and MatchAt search inside it. MatchAsYouType and the partial family serve form validation while a person is still typing, and MatchRecursive handles nested brackets through (?R). A pattern that does not compile does not raise: IsValid answers FALSE and every match call answers FALSE. Known gaps today, each carried as a warning on its method: LastError and PatternErrorOffset are placeholders (the engine keeps no compile error), Explain answers an empty text for a pattern the library does not know by name, MatchWordsIn stacks word boundaries on the pattern each time it is called, and positions count bytes, not characters.

classes.name: stzRegexLookaroundMaker
classes.brief: Builds a look-around regular expression: a main pattern that must, or must not, come before or after another pattern.
classes.description: One look-around is held at a time: MustBeFollowedBy and CantBeFollowedBy build a look-ahead, MustBePrecededBy and CantBePrecededBy a look-behind, and the Word, Number and Space forms fill in the common patterns. A second call replaces the first. ThenMatch sets the main pattern, which Pattern writes after the look-around, so a look-behind reads correctly: (?<=\$)\d+ finds the digits that follow a dollar sign. A look-ahead followed by a main pattern does not read as the name says: (?=ing)[a-z]+ tests what the main pattern starts on, so it finds ing in walking and not walk. A look-behind of variable length, such as the Number and Space forms, finds nothing in the engine.
classes.example:
o1.MustBePrecededBy("\$").ThenMatch("\d+")
? o1.Pattern()
#--> (?<=\$)\d+
o2 = new stzRegex(o1.Pattern())
o2.MatchFirst("cost $42 now")
? @@( o2.Matches() )
#--> [ "42" ]

classes.name: stzRegexMaker
classes.brief: Builds a regular expression piece by piece from calls, then hands it over as one text with Pattern.
classes.description: Each Add call appends a fragment: a class such as [abc] or [a-z] with a repeat suffix (AddRange, AddAmongChars, AddCharsRange and their digit forms), a literal, a shorthand class, a group, a flag or an assertion. Pattern joins the fragments in order. The calls that add ranges also record a sequence, the same call in data form, so Sequences and Fragments are two views of one pattern; literals and groups add a fragment and no sequence, so the two lists have different lengths, and the maker remembers which fragment each sequence made (Sequence, SequenceXT and RepeatSequence follow that link, not the position). Groups made with DefineGroup are remembered and can be reused or referred back to. The text is not escaped or validated: a literal goes in as given. Quantifiers and QuantifiersCommands are placeholders that answer an empty text. For ready-made patterns by name use AddCommonPattern or StzRxp.
classes.example:
o1.AddAmongChars("abc", :repeatedExactly, 3, 0)
o1.AddLiteral("-")
o1.AddCharsRange("a-z", :repeatedAtLeast, 1, 0)
? o1.Pattern()
#--> [abc]{3}-[a-z]{1,}
? o1.NumberOfFragements()
#--> 3

methods.name: AddRange

parameters.name: _nTimes2_

classes.name: stzRegexuter
classes.brief: Matches regular-expression triggers in a text, runs a piece of code on each match and keeps a log of what changed.
classes.description: Register triggers (a name and a regular expression), attach code to them that works on the match held in @value, then Process a text. Matches, Triggers, Positions and Results describe the last run, trigger by trigger, and State is a log of the matches whose computed value differs, with timestamp, order, pattern, position, dependson and affects. Build one with StzRxuter(), rxuter() or StzRxu(). Positions count characters and the Hebrew class [א-ת] and emoji patterns work. Found today: GetDependencyChain overflows the stack once the log holds an entry; Positions gives the first occurrence for every copy of a repeated match; only the first code attached to a trigger runs; and a code that raises is silently ignored.
classes.example:
o1.AddTrigger([ "num", "[0-9]+" ])
o1.AddCode("num", "@value = @value * 2")
o1.Process("abc 12 de 5")
? @@( o1.Matches() )
#--> [ "12", "5" ]
? @@( o1.Results() )
#--> [ 24, 10 ]
? @@( o1.Positions() )
#--> [ 5, 11 ]
o2 = StzRxuter()
o2.AddTrigger([ "he", "[א-ת]+" ])
o2.Process("שלום 12 עולם")
? @@( o2.Positions() )
#--> [ 1, 9 ]

parameters.role: the name of a registered trigger, or a pair [ :when, name ]

parameters.role: the code as text, or a pair [ :do, code ], which must mention @value and may be wrapped in braces

methods.brief: Returns the names of the triggers whose log entries depend on a given trigger.

parameters.name: _cTriggerName_
parameters.role: the trigger whose dependants are wanted

methods.returns: a list of trigger names, repeats removed
notes: num after a run that changed numbers gives [ "num" ]; an unknown name gives [ ]
warnings: because an entry always depends on its own trigger, the answer for a trigger that has logged an entry is that trigger itself

methods.brief: Returns the state log sorted by the position of the match in the text, ascending.
methods.returns: a list of entries, each a list of [ key, value ] pairs
notes: the log is not changed; entries at the same position keep their order

methods.name: StateByComputationOrder
methods.brief: Returns a copy of the state log in the order the computations ran.
methods.returns: a list of entries, each a list of [ key, value ] pairs

methods.brief: Raises a stack overflow today instead of returning the triggers a trigger depends on.

parameters.name: _cTriggerName_

methods.returns: nothing; the call raises R4 Stack Overflow
notes: an unknown trigger or an empty log gives [ ]

methods.brief: Returns the state log: one entry per match whose computed value differs from the match.
methods.returns: a list of entries, each a list of [ key, value ] pairs; [ ] after ResetState

methods.name: Triggers

methods.returns: a list of texts, parallel to Matches

methods.name: Matches
methods.brief: Returns the text of each match of the last run, trigger by trigger.

methods.name: Positions
methods.brief: Returns the 1-based position of each match of the last run, counted in characters.

classes.name: stzRelation
classes.brief: Keeps weighted subject-relation-object triples in the engine, such as alice knows bob with weight 0.5, and reads them back by position.
classes.description: The store is held by the engine and shared by every stzRelation object of the process, so call Clear() first for a fresh one. Positions count from 0 in the order of adding, and Remove leaves a hole instead of shifting the others. There is no lookup by subject: read the triples by position.
classes.receiver: o1 = new stzRelation() o1.Clear() o1.Add("alice", "knows", "bob", 0.5) o1.AddSimple("bob", "knows", "carol")
classes.example:
? o1.Count()
#--> 2
? o1.Subject(0) + " " + o1.RelationType(0) + " " + o1.Object(0)
#--> alice knows bob
? o1.Weight(0)
#--> 0.50
? o1.Weight(1)
#--> 1
o1.Clear()

classes.name: stzRequestClassifier
classes.brief: Maps an incoming request to a facet, the routing target, in three tiers: operator rules, capability-lexical scoring and an optional model.
classes.description: Rules on content type, path prefix and method are tried first and win; then the lexical tier scores the request against each facet's own capability vocabulary and a synonym lexicon; then an optional model function, installed with SetModelClassifier, is asked. It only routes to facets the bound catalog knows. Why() says which tier decided. The lexical tier is deterministic and offline.
classes.example:
? o1.Classify("POST", "/api/analyze", "application/pdf", "review this NDA")
#--> vision
? o1.Why()
#--> rule: content-type 'application/pdf' -> vision
? o1.ClassifyText("find the shortest path between two nodes")
#--> graph
? o1.ClassifyPath("/api/risk/score")
#--> math

classes.name: stzRequestSigner
classes.brief: Signs and verifies requests between nodes and webhook bodies with HMAC-SHA256, refusing forged, stale and replayed ones.
classes.description: Governance decides whether a caller may proceed; signing proves the request is from that caller and was not altered. Each caller key id shares a secret with the receiver. Sign computes an HMAC- SHA256 over a length-prefixed canonical form of the method, path, body, timestamp and nonce; Verify recomputes it and also demands a fresh timestamp and a nonce not used before, remembered for the freshness window. The comparison is constant-time through a double HMAC. A second form, SignBody, VerifyBody and VerifyWebhook, covers a webhook that signs only its raw body, and tries every held key so that an old and a new secret can overlap. Every refusal returns a reason and is noted in the process security ledger when one is open, with the caveats written on Verify. Secrets in examples here are invented.
classes.example:
a1 = o1.Sign("web-host", "GET", "/work?q=x", "", 1000000, "n-1")
? len(a1[:sig])
#--> 64
? o1.Verify("web-host", "GET", "/work?q=x", "", 1000000, "n-1", a1[:sig], 30000, 1010000)
#--> 1
? o1.Verify("web-host", "GET", "/work?q=x", "", 1000000, "n-1", a1[:sig], 30000, 1010000)
#--> 0
? o1.Why()
#--> replay detected (nonce already used for this key)
