methods.name: Verify
methods.brief: Judges a signed request against an explicit current time: known key, fresh timestamp, matching signature, and a nonce not seen before.
usage: Verify(pcKeyId, pcMethod, pcPath, pcBody, pnTs, pcNonce, pcSig, pnMaxSkewMs, pnNowMs)

parameters.name: pcKeyId
parameters.role: the caller's key id

parameters.name: pcMethod
parameters.role: the HTTP method

parameters.name: pcPath
parameters.role: the path with its query

parameters.name: pcBody
parameters.role: the body text

parameters.name: pnTs
parameters.role: the signed time

parameters.name: pcNonce
parameters.role: the signed nonce

parameters.name: pcSig
parameters.role: the signature received

parameters.name: pnMaxSkewMs
parameters.role: the freshness window in milliseconds, both ways

parameters.name: pnNowMs
parameters.role: the current time in milliseconds

notes: a valid request is accepted once: its nonce is remembered for the window; the signature is compared in constant time
warnings: every refusal is noted in the process security ledger when one is open, as sig.key.unknown, sig.timestamp.stale, sig.signature.forged or sig.nonce.replayed; the note holds the path with its query string, so a token placed in a query string reaches the ledger, and an unknown key id is written as received, line breaks included, which a text view of the ledger shows as a forged extra line

methods.name: VerifyNow
methods.brief: Judges a signed request as Verify does, taking the current time from the engine clock.

parameters.name: pcMethod

parameters.name: pcNonce

parameters.name: pcSig
parameters.role: the signature received

parameters.name: pnMaxSkewMs
parameters.role: the freshness window in milliseconds

methods.returns: TRUE or FALSE, with the reason in Why
warnings: the notes written to the ledger are those of Verify

methods.name: VerifyEnvelope
methods.brief: Judges a request together with the envelope that Sign or SignNow made for it, against the engine clock.

parameters.name: pcMethod
parameters.role: the HTTP method

parameters.name: pcPath

parameters.name: pcBody
parameters.role: the body text

parameters.name: paEnvelope

parameters.name: pnMaxSkewMs

methods.returns: TRUE or FALSE, with the reason in Why

methods.brief: Signs the raw body of a webhook delivery alone, with no method, path, time or nonce.

parameters.name: pcKeyId
parameters.role: the key id whose secret signs

parameters.name: pcBody
parameters.role: the body text

methods.returns: a text, the HMAC-SHA256 in 64 hexadecimal characters

methods.name: VerifyBody
methods.brief: Judges a webhook body against the signature a given key would give it, with no replay check.

parameters.name: pcKeyId
parameters.role: the key id to verify with

parameters.name: pcBody
parameters.role: the body text

parameters.name: pcSig
parameters.role: the signature received

methods.returns: TRUE or FALSE, with the reason in Why

parameters.name: pcBody

parameters.name: pcSig
parameters.role: the signature received

parameters.name: pnNowMs
parameters.role: the current time in milliseconds

parameters.name: pnWindowMs
parameters.role: how long a believed body counts as a replay

classes.name: stzRequirement
classes.brief: States what a faculty is needed for, in quality, memory, languages, licence and determinism, and never which model.
classes.description: The registry resolves a requirement to an implementation and explains its choice. The requirement is a plain record read through Data. Quality, memory, languages, licence and determinism filter the models; the floor is never filtered. Latency and locality are recorded but the registry does not read them yet. A quality bar is checked against the score the registry measured on the golden set, a figure computed by the class and not judged by a person.
classes.example:
o1.RequireQualityQ(:good).RequireMemoryQ(500)
? o1.Data()[:quality]
#--> 0.70
? o1.Data()[:memory]
#--> 500
? o1.Faculty()
#--> position

parameters.name: pcFaculty
parameters.role: the name of the faculty the requirement is for, folded to lower case

methods.name: Data
methods.brief: Returns the whole requirement as data, the form the registry resolves.
methods.returns: a list of [ key, value ] pairs: faculty, quality, latency, memory, languages, locality, licence, deterministic, refusebelow
notes: defaults: quality 0, latency interactive, memory 0 (no budget), no languages, locality local, licence permissive, deterministic 0, refusebelow 0

methods.brief: Sets the quality an implementation must have measured on the golden set to be chosen.

parameters.name: pQuality
parameters.role: any (0), good (0.7), best (0.9) or a number

notes: the bar is checked against the measured score, a figure computed by the class from the goldens, not judged by a person; the floor is never filtered by it
warnings: any other word raises an error, but a number is not checked against the range 0 to 1, so 1.5 is stored and no implementation can reach it

classes.name: stzResourceSpec
classes.brief: Holds an amount of resources, memory, virtual processors, disk and a GPU, either as the need of a part or as the capacity of a host.
classes.description: The same class plays two roles. As a requirement it says what a part needs, including a GPU that is required or optional. As a capacity it says what a host offers, including whether a GPU is present. Meets asks whether a capacity covers a requirement; Plus adds requirements, as for several parts on one host. Nothing is validated: set numbers.
classes.receiver: o1 = new stzResourceSpec() o1.SetMemory(2048) o1.SetCompute(2) o1.SetStorage(20)
classes.example:
? o1.Text()
#--> 2048MB / 2 vCPU / 20GB
oNeed = new stzResourceSpec()
oNeed.SetMemory(1024)
oNeed.SetCompute(1)
? o1.Meets(oNeed)
#--> 1
oNeed.SetGpuRequired()
? o1.Meets(oNeed)
#--> 0
o1.SetGpuPresent(1)
? o1.Meets(oNeed)
#--> 1

classes.name: stzResponderSet
classes.brief: Routes each verb of a response plan to the first responder in the set that owns it, so one plan can have several owners.
classes.description: A plan may lock an account and rotate a secret, and no single object owns both. The set asks each member Owns for the verb and passes the call to the first that says yes; a verb no member owns raises an error, and a plan that holds such an action is refused whole by ExecuteOn before anything is performed. The list given to the constructor copies its objects, which is harmless for a responder that holds its target by reference and wrong for one you want to read afterwards; build the set with Add to keep the object itself.
classes.receiver: oAuth = new stzAuth(); oAuth.Register("mallory", "pw-invented-1"); o1 = new stzResponderSet([ ])
classes.example:
o1.Add(StzAuthResponder(oAuth))
? o1.Owns("lockaccount")
#--> 1
? o1.Owns("rotatesecret")
#--> 0
o1.LockAccount("mallory")
? oAuth.IsAccountLocked("mallory")
#--> 1

classes.name: stzResponsePlan
classes.brief: Holds a containment plan: a list of actions anyone may propose and only an effectful, non-sandboxed actor may commit.
classes.description: Containment is the only step that touches reality, so it is a plan. Expression is free: any actor, a language-model agent included, may compose it with Propose or derive it from an incident with ProposeForIncident. Admission is governed: ExecuteOn performs the actions on a responder only for an actor MayCommit admits, and audits every outcome, committed or refused, in the plan and in the security ledger. The catalog is closed to RevokeSession, LockAccount, RotateSecret, RevokeCapability, ShedSource and QuarantinePart. The responder is any object that answers those verbs: rehearse on a double, or on a responder over in-memory objects. Never point a plan at the real machine to try it.
classes.example:
o1.Propose(:LockAccount, "mallory", "stolen credentials")
o1.Propose(:RotateSecret, "signing-key", "read by the intruder")
? o1.NumberOfActions()
#--> 2
? o1.MayCommit(LLMActor("advisor"))
#--> 0
? o1.MayCommit(HumanActor("oncall"))
#--> 1

methods.name: init
methods.brief: Builds an empty containment plan with a name, to be proposed into and committed by an effectful actor.

parameters.name: pcName
parameters.role: the name of the plan, such as the incident it answers

methods.name: Name
methods.brief: Returns the name the plan was built with.

methods.name: Propose
methods.brief: Adds one containment action to the plan; the action is only recorded, nothing is performed.

parameters.name: pcAction
parameters.role: the kind of action, one of :RevokeSession, :LockAccount, :RotateSecret, :RevokeCapability, :ShedSource, :QuarantinePart

parameters.name: pcTarget
parameters.role: what the action is about, such as an account, a secret name or an address

parameters.name: pcRationale
parameters.role: the reason, kept with the action in the audit

methods.returns: the plan itself, so calls chain
notes: the kind is folded to lower case
warnings: an action outside the closed catalog raises an error that lists the catalog

methods.name: ProposeForIncident
methods.brief: Adds the actions an incident calls for: lock and revoke for its actor, a rotation per secret it implicates.

parameters.name: poIncident
parameters.role: the stzIncident to read

methods.returns: the plan itself, so calls chain
notes: it only proposes; the actions are performed by ExecuteOn

methods.name: Actions
methods.brief: Returns the proposed actions, in the order proposed.
methods.returns: a list of [ kind, target, rationale ] rows, the kind in lower case

methods.name: NumberOfActions
methods.brief: Returns how many actions the plan holds.

methods.name: MayCommit
methods.brief: TRUE if the actor may commit a plan: it must be effectful and not sandboxed.

parameters.name: poActor
parameters.role: the actor asking to commit

methods.returns: TRUE or FALSE; always FALSE for a language-model actor
notes: answered before any attempt, and nothing is audited

methods.name: WhyNot
methods.brief: Returns the reason an actor may not commit, in words.

parameters.name: poActor
parameters.role: the actor to explain

methods.returns: a text; an empty text when the actor may commit

methods.name: ExecuteOn
methods.brief: Performs the actions on a responder when the actor may commit, auditing each; otherwise performs none and audits refusals.

parameters.name: poResponder
parameters.role: the object that answers the six verbs, a rehearsal double or a responder over in-memory objects

parameters.name: poActor
parameters.role: the actor committing, effectful and not sandboxed

methods.returns: the number of actions committed; 0 when the actor may not, or when no responder owns an action
notes: each outcome also reaches the security ledger as response.action.committed or response.action.refused
warnings: a responder that answers Owns is asked about every action first, and one action nobody owns refuses the whole plan before any is performed; a plan executed twice performs its actions twice

methods.name: WasExecuted
methods.brief: TRUE if a commit has gone through for this plan.
notes: a refused attempt does not set it

methods.name: AuditTrail
methods.brief: Returns every outcome recorded, committed and refused alike, in the order they happened.
methods.returns: a list of [ number, verdict, kind, target, actor, why ] rows

methods.name: CommittedCount
methods.brief: Returns how many actions were committed over the life of the plan.

methods.name: RefusedCount
methods.brief: Returns how many actions were refused over the life of the plan, a signal worth watching.

methods.name: Explain
methods.brief: Returns the plan as lines of text: each proposed action with its reason, then the audit.

methods.name: Show
methods.brief: Prints the lines of the plan.

classes.name: stzRetryBudget
classes.brief: Caps the retries of a whole workload with an engine token bucket, so a storm of failures cannot turn into a retry storm.
classes.description: A budget of N retries refills over a window of W seconds, at floor(N / W) retries a second and never less than one. Ask Allow before every retry; when it answers FALSE, fail instead of retrying. One budget guards one workload; for many independent keys use stzRateLimiter.
classes.example:
? o1.Allow()
#--> 1
? o1.AllowN(5)
#--> 0
? o1.RefillPerSecond()
#--> 1
o1.Destroy()

methods.name: init
methods.brief: Creates a retry budget: a token bucket of pnBudget retries that refills over a window of pnWindowSeconds.

parameters.name: pnBudget
parameters.role: how many retries the bucket holds

parameters.name: pnWindowSeconds
parameters.role: the seconds over which the budget refills, raised to 1 if smaller

warnings: the refill rate is floor(pnBudget / pnWindowSeconds) tokens a second, with a minimum of 1

methods.name: Allow
methods.brief: Takes one retry from the budget and answers whether the retry may go ahead.
warnings: refuses once the budget is spent and recovers as the window refills

methods.name: Spend
methods.brief: Takes one retry from the budget and answers whether it may go ahead, as the call with the other name does.

methods.name: AllowN
methods.brief: Takes n retries from the budget at once and answers whether they may all go ahead.

parameters.name: n
parameters.role: how many retries to take

warnings: a refused request takes nothing; n of 0 is allowed

methods.name: Available
methods.brief: Returns how many retries are left in the budget, as a decimal.
warnings: the budget refills continuously, so a reading just after a spend is slightly above the exact remainder

methods.name: Budget
methods.brief: Returns the size of the budget, as given at construction.

methods.name: Window
methods.brief: Returns the refill window in seconds, with a minimum of 1.

methods.name: RefillPerSecond
methods.brief: Returns how many retries the budget regains each second.
warnings: floor(budget / window), never below 1

methods.name: Destroy
methods.brief: Frees the engine bucket and marks the object unusable.
methods.returns: the budget itself, so calls chain
warnings: a later call builds a new full bucket

classes.name: stzRingCodeGraph
classes.brief: Holds Ring source as a code graph: classes with their parent, methods and a name-based graph of the calls between them.
classes.description: Its parser reads the Ring source itself: class headers with a single parent, def lines, and the calls in method bodies, found as an identifier before an open parenthesis once string literals and comments are stripped. A call is an edge only when some class defines a method of that name, so the graph is name-based and honest about it. DeadCode is scoped to private helpers that nothing references, and CyclicCalls to two methods of one class that call each other, the signals a name- based graph can assert without guessing. The query surface of the family (classes, owners, ancestry, impact, cascade) is inherited from stzCodeGraph. Build one from a folder with new stzRingCodeGraph(path) or from text with StzRingCodeGraphFromSource.
classes.receiver: o1 = StzRingCodeGraphFromSource("class Animal" + nl + "def Speak()" + nl + "return This._Sound()" + nl + "def _Sound()" + nl + "return 1" + nl + "def _Unused()" + nl + "return 2" + nl + "class Dog from Animal" + nl + "def Fetch()" + nl + "return This.Speak()" + nl)
classes.example:
? @@( o1.AncestryOf("Dog") )
#--> [ "Dog", "Animal" ]
? @@( o1.CallEdges() )
#--> [ [ "Animal", "Speak", "_Sound" ], [ "Dog", "Fetch", "Speak" ] ]
? @@( o1.CalleesOf("Dog", "Fetch") )
#--> [ "Speak" ]
? o1.DeadCode()[1][:method]
#--> _Unused

methods.name: init
methods.brief: Builds a Ring code graph, scanning every .ring file of a folder, or an empty graph when the path is empty.

parameters.name: pcRootPath
parameters.role: the folder to scan, below which every sub-folder is scanned too

warnings: a path that is not a folder raises the file-system error of dir

methods.name: Language
methods.brief: Returns the name of the language this graph models.

methods.name: FileExtension
methods.brief: Returns the file extension of the source files it scans, with the dot.

methods.name: ScanSource
methods.brief: Scans one Ring source text: class headers with their parent, methods, and the calls found in method bodies.

parameters.name: pcContent
parameters.role: the Ring source text

parameters.name: pcFile
parameters.role: the file name recorded for what it finds

notes: call edges appear only after BuildGraph and the private resolve step that StzRingCodeGraphFromSource and the folder constructor run, so a graph filled by hand through ScanSource shows none

methods.name: CallEdges
methods.brief: Returns the resolved calls between defined methods, as the class, the calling method and the name called.
methods.returns: a list of [ class, method, callee ] triples, without repeats
notes: a call to something no class defines, such as a builtin, is not an edge

methods.name: NumberOfCallEdges
methods.brief: Returns how many call edges were resolved.

methods.name: RawCallEntries
methods.brief: Returns every call found in a method body, defined or not, builtins included, with the line of the call.
methods.returns: a list of [ class, method, callee, line ] rows
notes: strings and comments are stripped first, so a name in a message is not a call; a definition is not a call

methods.name: CallersOf
methods.brief: Returns the methods whose body calls the named method, by name.

parameters.name: pcMethod
parameters.role: the name of the method that is called

methods.returns: a list of hash lists [ :class, :method ], without repeats
notes: the name is matched without regard to case

methods.name: CalleesOf
methods.brief: Returns the names of the defined methods that one method calls.

parameters.name: pcClass
parameters.role: the class of the calling method

parameters.name: pcMethod
parameters.role: the calling method

notes: the class and method are matched without regard to case; an unknown pair answers an empty list

methods.name: DeadCode
methods.brief: Returns the private helpers, whose names start with an underscore, that no call in the scanned tree reaches.
notes: public methods are never reported, since they may be entry points called from outside the tree; calls through a variable are invisible to a name-based graph

methods.name: CyclicCalls
methods.brief: Returns pairs of methods of one class that call each other, a mutual recursion.
methods.returns: a list of hash lists [ :class, :cycle = [ a, b ] ]
notes: a method calling itself is legitimate and not reported

methods.name: Stats
methods.brief: Returns the size of the graph: root, language, classes, methods, inheritance edges and call edges.
methods.returns: a hash list; its keys come back in lower case, such as inheritsedges and calledges

classes.name: stzRingTimer
classes.brief: Holds a timer in pure Ring that calls a function every interval, or once, advanced by a timer manager's loop.
classes.description: The same contract as stzReactiveTimer, with an owner object kept for the caller: CheckAndTick fires the function when the interval has passed since the last firing on the engine's clock, answers 1 while the timer stays active and 0 when it is stopped or has just fired as a one-shot. It decides whether to stop a one-shot before it calls the function, because the function may stop the whole timer system.
classes.receiver: $nFired = 0 o1 = new stzRingTimer("once", 20, func { $nFired++ }, new stzReactive(), 1, "")
classes.example:
o1.Start()
? o1.CheckAndTick()
#--> 1
? $nFired
#--> 0
StzEngineTimeSleepMs(50)
? o1.CheckAndTick()
#--> 0
? $nFired
#--> 1
? o1.CheckAndTick()
#--> 0
? $nFired
#--> 1

methods.name: init
methods.brief: Builds a timer in pure Ring that calls a function every interval, or once, when driven by a timer manager.
usage: init(id, intervalMs, f, engine, oneTime, obj)

parameters.name: id
parameters.role: the timer's identifier

parameters.name: intervalMs
parameters.role: the time between calls in milliseconds

parameters.name: f
parameters.role: the function to call

parameters.name: engine
parameters.role: the reactive engine it belongs to

parameters.name: oneTime
parameters.role: 1 for a timer that fires once, 0 or an empty text for one that repeats

parameters.name: obj
parameters.role: the object the timer belongs to, kept for the owner

methods.returns: nothing; the timer is built stopped
notes: it does not run by itself: a stzTimerManager loop calls CheckAndTick

methods.name: Start
methods.brief: Starts the timer, taking the time now as its starting point.
notes: starting an active timer does nothing

methods.name: Stop
methods.brief: Stops the timer, so CheckAndTick no longer fires it.

methods.name: CheckAndTick
methods.brief: Calls the function if the interval has passed since the last call, for a manager's loop to call.
methods.returns: 1 while the timer stays active, 0 when it is stopped or has just fired as a one- shot
notes: a call before the interval has passed does nothing and answers 1; it decides whether to stop a one-shot before calling the function, because the function may stop the whole timer system

methods.name: Cleanup
methods.brief: Stops the timer when its owner lets go of it.

classes.name: stzRuleBase
classes.brief: Holds a named set of org-chart compliance rules, starting with the four universal ones, ready to check a chart.
classes.description: It is a stzGraphRuleSet in the orgchart domain: self-report, reporting cycle, orphan position and span of control. The regime classes below it (SOX, GDPR, PCI-DSS, HIPAA, ISO 27001, Basel III, BCEAO) differ by name today, and only SOX adds a rule of its own. Pass one to stzOrgChart.CheckCompliance.
classes.example:
? o1.NumberOfRules()
#--> 4

methods.name: init
methods.brief: Builds a compliance rule base named for a regime, in the orgchart domain, with the four universal org rules; a non-text name gives "".

parameters.name: pcName
parameters.role: The rule base name, as text

methods.returns: nothing; the rule base is built
warnings: the rules are self-report, reporting cycle, orphan position and span of control

classes.name: stzRuleGovernance
classes.brief: Judges a set of scoped rules two ways, against the cases they govern and against the questions a rule cannot ask of itself.
classes.description: Running a rule set asks whether the claim holds where the rule looked, never whether the rule looked in the right place. CheckRules asks that over a corpus of cases: a scope that selects nothing (scope_empty), a scope that selects every subject everywhere (scope_vacuous), a counter no case contains (boundary_unwitnessed), a rule with no claim (claim_unstated), two rules reaching for one subject with no declared precedence (subject_contested) and a rule reading a quantity that a later rule writes (read_is_stale). CheckCases is the ordinary half, the rules over the cases; CheckAll does both. A case is any object the scopes understand, a rendered diagram, a code graph, an org chart. StzPlasticGovernance is the graph plane's spelling.
classes.receiver: o1 = new stzRuleGovernance("numbers") o2 = new stzScopedRule("all_small") o2.SetClaim("every number is below 10") o2.SetScope(func oL { return oL }) o2.SetClaimCheck(func oL, n { if n < 10  return [ 1, "" ]  ok  return [ 0, "it is " + n ] }) o1.AddRule(o2) o1.AddCase("one", [ 1, 2, 3, 12 ]) o1.AddCase("two", [ 4, 6, 7 ])
classes.example:
? @@( o1.ScopeTable() )
#--> [ [ "all_small", 7, 0, 2, 2 ] ]
? o1.CheckCases()[1][:where]
#--> one / 12
? o1.CheckRules()[1][:rule]
#--> scope_vacuous
? o1.IsSound()
#--> 1
? len(o1.CheckAll())
#--> 3

methods.name: init
methods.brief: Builds a governance with a name, no rules and no cases.

parameters.name: pcName
parameters.role: the name of the governance

notes: StzRuleGovernanceQ and StzPlasticGovernance build the same object

methods.name: Name_
methods.brief: Returns the name the governance was built with.

methods.name: Rules
methods.brief: Returns the rules added so far, in the order they were added.

methods.name: Findings
methods.brief: Returns the findings of the last CheckRules or CheckAll.
methods.returns: a list of findings; [ ] before either has run
notes: CheckCases does not store its findings here

methods.name: AddRule
methods.brief: Adds a rule to judge, in the order it will be listed.

parameters.name: poRule
parameters.role: a stzScopedRule

methods.returns: the governance itself, so calls chain

methods.name: AddCase
methods.brief: Adds a case the rules are judged against, under a name, whatever kind of object it is.

parameters.name: pcName
parameters.role: the name of the case, shown in findings

parameters.name: poSubject
parameters.role: the case, such as a rendered diagram, a code graph or any object the scopes understand

methods.returns: the governance itself, so calls chain
notes: the case must already be in the state the scopes read: nothing is solved or rendered for it

methods.name: AddPicture
methods.brief: Adds a diagram as a case after solving its layout in place, so copies of it carry the solution.

parameters.name: pcName
parameters.role: the name of the case

parameters.name: poDg
parameters.role: the diagram

methods.returns: the governance itself, so calls chain
notes: solving before the copy avoids a second layout when the first scope asks

methods.name: DeclarePrecedence
methods.brief: Declares which of two rules wins where both govern one subject, with the reason.

parameters.name: pcWins
parameters.role: the name of the rule that wins

parameters.name: pcYields
parameters.role: the name of the rule that yields

parameters.name: pcWhy
parameters.role: the reason, kept with the declaration

methods.returns: the governance itself, so calls chain
notes: it silences subject_contested for that pair in either order; a pair that write nothing in common is never reported as contested

methods.name: CheckCases
methods.brief: Judges every case against every rule and returns the findings of the rules.
methods.returns: a list of findings, each a hash list with rule, subject, where, severity and message; [ ] when all hold
notes: where reads case name, a slash, then the subject; CheckPictures is the same call

methods.name: CheckRules
methods.brief: Asks the questions a rule cannot ask of itself, over the cases, and returns the findings about the rules.
methods.returns: a list of findings whose rule is scope_empty, scope_vacuous, boundary_unwitnessed, claim_unstated, subject_contested or read_is_stale
notes: the findings are kept for Findings and IsSound; where is the rule's name; scope_empty and claim_unstated are errors, the rest warnings except read_is_stale, an error

methods.name: CheckAll
methods.brief: Runs the questions about the rules, then the rules over the cases, and returns every finding.
methods.returns: a list of findings, those about the rules first
notes: the whole list is kept for Findings and IsSound

methods.name: IsSound
methods.brief: TRUE if the last CheckRules or CheckAll found nothing of severity error.
methods.returns: TRUE or FALSE, as 1 or 0; 1 before either has run
notes: warnings do not make it false

methods.name: ScopeTable
methods.brief: Returns for each rule how much it governs and how much it excludes over the cases.
methods.returns: a list of rows [ name, subjects governed, subjects excluded, cases where it governs something, number of cases ]
notes: it calls every scope and counter again, so it costs a pass over the cases

classes.name: stzRuleReport
classes.brief: Collects the findings of every rule domain into one list and gives one verdict, the single gate a build can fail on.
classes.description: Rule sets of different domains, code, agents, security, schemas, networks, all report findings in one shape: a hash list with rule, subject, where, severity and message, the subject being the domain. A report gathers them with Run for a rule set and a graph, Collect for an object that checks itself, Ingest for findings already in that shape and IngestLegacy for the older checkers' shapes. IsSound is true when no finding of severity error was collected; warnings advise. Explain returns the report as text lines grouped by subject and Report prints them.
classes.receiver: o1 = new stzRuleReport("ci") o1.Ingest([ [ :rule = "entity_has_key", :subject = "er", :where = "b", :severity = "error", :message = "entity B has no key" ] ]) o1.IngestLegacy([ [ :invariant = "unguarded", :node = "api", :severity = "warning", :message = "no check" ] ], "agentic")
classes.example:
? o1.NumberOfFindings()
#--> 2
? @@( o1.Subjects() )
#--> [ "er", "agentic" ]
? o1.IsSound()
#--> 0
? len(o1.Warnings())
#--> 1
? o1.Explain()[1]
#--> Rule report 'ci': 2 finding(s), 1 error(s), 1 warning(s) -> UNSOUND (errors present)

methods.name: init
methods.brief: Builds an empty report under a name, ready to collect findings from any domain.

parameters.name: pcName
parameters.role: the name of the report, shown in its first line

notes: StzRuleReportQ builds the same object

methods.brief: Runs a rule set over a graph and adds the findings it produces to the report.

methods.returns: the report itself, so calls chain
notes: each finding keeps the subject of its rule's domain, so domains coexist in one list

methods.name: Collect
methods.brief: Asks a graph to check itself and adds its findings to the report.

parameters.name: poGraph
parameters.role: any object that answers CheckRules, such as a stzErDiagram, a stzGraph or an org chart

methods.returns: the report itself, so calls chain
notes: an object with no CheckRules raises error R14

methods.name: Ingest
methods.brief: Adds findings that are already in the unified shape to the report.

parameters.name: paFindings
parameters.role: a list of hash lists with rule, subject, where, severity and message

methods.returns: the report itself, so calls chain
notes: the findings are kept as given and nothing is checked

methods.name: IngestLegacy
methods.brief: Adds findings from an older checker, turning invariant and node or line into rule and where.

parameters.name: paFindings
parameters.role: a list of hash lists that carry rule or invariant, and where, node or line

parameters.name: pcSubject
parameters.role: the subject to give every finding

methods.returns: the report itself, so calls chain
notes: a missing severity becomes error and a missing message an empty text

methods.name: Name
methods.brief: Returns the name the report was built with.

methods.name: Findings
methods.brief: Returns every finding collected so far, in the order they arrived.
methods.returns: a list of hash lists with rule, subject, where, severity and message

methods.name: NumberOfFindings
methods.brief: Returns how many findings the report holds.

methods.name: FindingsOfSeverity
methods.brief: Returns the collected findings that carry a given level, such as error or warning.

parameters.name: pcSeverity
parameters.role: the severity to keep, such as error or warning, in any letter case, with spaces ignored

methods.returns: a list of findings; [ ] when none match

methods.name: FindingsOfSubject
methods.brief: Returns the findings of one subject, that is one domain.

parameters.name: pcSubject
parameters.role: the subject to keep, such as er or code, in any letter case

methods.returns: a list of findings; [ ] when none match

methods.name: Errors
methods.brief: Returns the findings of severity error.

methods.name: Warnings
methods.brief: Returns the findings of severity warning.

methods.name: Subjects
methods.brief: Returns the subjects that produced at least one finding, in the order they first appear.

methods.name: IsSound
methods.brief: TRUE if no finding of severity error has been collected.
methods.returns: TRUE or FALSE, as 1 or 0; 1 for an empty report
notes: warnings advise and do not make it false; this is the CI gate

methods.name: Explain
methods.brief: Returns the report as lines of text: a verdict line, then each subject with its findings.
notes: the verdict line gives the counts and SOUND or UNSOUND (errors present); subjects come in the order they first appeared, not errors first

methods.name: Report
methods.brief: Prints the lines of the explanation to the console, one per line.
methods.returns: the report itself, so calls chain
notes: it prints with the ? statement

classes.name: stzSamlIdentityProvider
classes.brief: Issues signed SAML assertions for registered services, so a service provider can be developed and tested without an external identity provider.
classes.description: Assertions are signed by the engine with ECDSA-SHA256 over a P-256 key (random, or derived from a seed for repeatable tests) or with RSA-SHA256 over a key you supply or generate. Only a registered service can be the audience: an identity provider that vouches for any service that asks is an open redirect for identity. Subject and audience are escaped for & < and > before they enter the XML, so a subject holding markup cannot inject elements (checked with a quote, angle brackets and an ampersand); the issuer entity id, set by the operator, is written as given. The private key never leaves the object: PublicKey and TrustMeOn hand over only what a service provider needs. Use invented identities and keys in tests.
classes.example:
o1.RegisterServiceProvider("https://sp.invented.test", "https://sp.invented.test/acs")
? o1.SigningAlgorithm()
#--> ES256
? o1.ServiceProviderIds()[1]
#--> https://sp.invented.test
cXml = o1.UnsignedAssertion("a<b", "https://sp.invented.test", 1790000000, 300)
? len(StzFind("<saml:NameID>a<b</saml:NameID>", cXml)) > 0
#--> 1

methods.name: init
methods.brief: Builds an identity provider with a fresh random P-256 signing key.

parameters.name: pcEntityId
parameters.role: this provider's entity id, written as the issuer of every assertion

notes: the issuer is written into the assertion as given, without XML escaping
warnings: raises an error when pcEntityId is empty or only spaces

methods.name: EntityId
methods.brief: Returns this provider's entity id, the issuer of its assertions.

methods.name: UseSeed
methods.brief: Replaces the signing key with an ES256 key derived from a seed, so assertions can be reproduced in a test.

parameters.name: pcSeedHex
parameters.role: the 32-byte seed as 64 hex characters, or an empty text for a random key

notes: the same seed always gives the same public key
warnings: raises an error when the seed is not valid hex

extensions.name: UseSeedQ
extensions.adds: does what the method does, then returns the object, so the call can be chained

methods.name: SigningAlgorithm
methods.brief: Returns the signature algorithm in use.
methods.returns: the text ES256, or RS256 after an RSA key was set

methods.brief: Signs assertions RSA-SHA256 with a private key you supply, for service providers that accept RSA only.

parameters.name: pcPem
parameters.role: the RSA private key as PEM text

notes: the EC key material is cleared, so KeyX and KeyY answer an empty text afterwards
warnings: raises an error when the PEM cannot be read

extensions.name: UseRsaKeyQ
extensions.adds: does what the method does, then returns the object, so the call can be chained

methods.brief: Generates a fresh RSA key and signs with it from now on.

notes: for development and first runs

extensions.name: UseNewRsaKeyQ
extensions.adds: does what the method does, then returns the object, so the call can be chained

methods.name: PublicKey
methods.brief: Returns the public half of the signing key, which is all a service provider needs to verify.
methods.returns: a hash list with kty EC and crv, x, y, or kty RSA and n, e

methods.name: KeyX
methods.brief: Returns the x coordinate of the public EC key in base64url, or an empty text under RSA.

methods.name: KeyY
methods.brief: Returns the y coordinate of the public EC key in base64url, or an empty text under RSA.

methods.brief: Makes a service provider trust this identity provider, passing it the entity id and the public key.

parameters.name: poServiceProvider
parameters.role: the stzSamlServiceProvider that is to trust this issuer

methods.returns: the identity provider itself, so calls chain
notes: the key handed over is the one in use at the call: change the key and call it again to follow; the service provider's earlier trust is replaced

methods.name: SetLifetime
methods.brief: Sets, in seconds, how long a new assertion stays valid.

parameters.name: pnSecs
parameters.role: the validity of each assertion in seconds

notes: the default is 300 seconds

extensions.name: SetLifetimeQ

methods.name: Lifetime
methods.brief: Returns how long a new assertion stays valid, in seconds.

parameters.role: its assertion consumer URL

methods.returns: the identity provider itself, so calls chain

methods.brief: Returns a signed assertion XML vouching for a subject to a registered service, valid from now.

methods.brief: Returns a signed assertion XML whose validity starts at a given moment.

methods.brief: Returns a signed assertion in base64url whose validity starts at a given moment.

parameters.name: pcSubject
parameters.role: the subject name

classes.name: stzSamlServiceProvider
classes.brief: Decides whether to believe a SAML assertion posted back by a single trusted identity provider, and says why when it refuses.
classes.description: The signature check and the anti-wrapping guarantee belong to the engine, which returns claims read only from the signed bytes. This class adds the judgement that depends on your configuration: the issuer must be the trusted identity provider, the audience must be this provider's entity id, the validity window must contain the moment of judgement (with a clock-skew allowance, 120 seconds by default), and an assertion already accepted is refused as a replay. Every refusal returns a reason and is noted in the refusal record. Trust is set with raw key parts, a certificate, or the identity provider's metadata document. Known limits today: the sign-in request (AuthnRequest, AuthnRequestAt) writes its values into attributes without XML escaping and stamps IssueInstant with the clock in milliseconds, and a consumed subject comes back still XML-escaped.
classes.example:
oIdp = new stzSamlIdentityProvider("https://idp.invented.test")
oIdp.RegisterServiceProvider(o1.EntityId(), o1.AcsUrl())
oIdp.TrustMeOn(o1)
? o1.TrustsAnIdp()
#--> 1
cXml = oIdp.IssueAssertionAt("dana@x.test", o1.EntityId(), 1790000000)
aR = o1.ConsumeXmlAt(cXml, 1790000005)
? aR[:nameid]
#--> dana@x.test
aR = o1.ConsumeXmlAt(cXml, 1790000006)
? aR[:why]
#--> this assertion has already been consumed (replay)

classes.name: stzScatterPlot
classes.brief: Draws points given as [ h, v ] pairs on two axes: as text for a terminal, as SVG, or as a PNG picture.
classes.description: The points come as pairs, as two lists named H and V (or X and Y), or as labelled points. ToString draws a circle per point on ticked axes with the letters X and Y at the axis ends, and switches to the Ring renderer when the dashed grid or the point labels are on; ToSVG and ToPNG draw one circle per point and carry the coordinates and nothing else, so the grid, labels, letters, axis switches and point character do not reach pixels. The axis letters read the opposite of the usual way (X on the vertical axis), the text picture writes one x tick label per point so many points make them collide, and the pixel picture draws no x tick labels at all; see the warnings. Gallery: doc/gallery/stzScatterPlot/clusters.png (two clusters of 40 points) and negative.png (points around the origin), each with its script, seen wrong by stzlib-docs visual pass (a model reading the PNG), 2026-10-05, not a person because the horizontal axis carries no numbers; terminal.txt is the text picture of the clusters, read as text and judged wrong because the x tick labels run together.

classes.name: stzScene
classes.brief: Holds a 3D scene, a camera, a light and meshes placed in space, and renders it to a picture.
classes.description: Add meshes with AddMesh, which places one instance each; every instance has a position, a rotation and a scale kept apart from its mesh, so moving, rotating or scaling re-sends matrices and never geometry (Stats makes that checkable). All the instances of a mesh are drawn in one call. Set the eye and target with SetCamera, the lens with SetLens, the light with SetLight and the colour of each instance with SetColor. SetParent makes a chain, and WorldPosition says where an instance really ended up. Project turns a point of the scene into a pixel, for putting a 2D label on a 3D thing. ToPNG renders on the graphics device and returns empty text when there is none: a scene has no vector fallback. The plain forms act and return nothing, and the Q twins return the scene so calls chain.
classes.receiver: oCube = new stzMesh([ :Cube, 1 ]); o1 = new stzScene(400, 300)
classes.example:
o1.SetCamera(6, 4, 8, 0, 0, 0)
o1.AddMesh(oCube, 0, 0, 0)
o1.AddMeshQ(oCube, 2, 0, 0).ColorQ("#30a0e0")
? o1.InstanceCount()
#--> 2
? o1.LastIndex()
#--> 2
o1.SetParent(2, 1)
o1.MoveTo(1, 0, 3, 0)
? @@( o1.WorldPosition(2) )
#--> [ 2, 3, 0 ]
? o1.HierarchyDepth()
#--> 1
? @@( o1.Camera() )
#--> [ 6, 4, 8, 0, 0, 0, 45, 0.10, 200 ]
? o1.Width()
#--> 400

classes.name: stzScenePanel
classes.brief: Hangs an interface panel as a quad in a 3D scene and turns a click on the screen into a click on the panel.
classes.description: Two conversions in opposite directions. Out: the panel is drawn to pixels, uploaded as a texture and worn by a quad lying flat at the origin. In: a screen pixel becomes a ray from the camera, the ray meets the quad's plane, the hit becomes a texture point and the texture point becomes panel pixels, so the panel itself knows nothing of a scene. The camera is copied in and not shared, so call LooksThrough beside Refresh when the camera moves. VerifyAgainstProjection checks the ray against the engine's own projection. The mapping is arithmetic and needs no device; Mount and Refresh upload a texture and need one, but no window is opened.
classes.receiver: oDoc = new stzUiDocument('DEFINE PANEL console ( SIZE [400, 300], DIRECTION column, BACKGROUND "#101820", PADDING 40, CHILDREN [row] ) RATIONALE "A control surface."' + char(10) + 'DEFINE BOX row ( DIRECTION row, HEIGHT 90, GAP 20, CHILDREN [fire, abort] ) RATIONALE "The two commands."' + char(10) + 'DEFINE BOX fire ( WIDTH 140, BACKGROUND "#b03030", FOCUSABLE yes, ROLE button, LABEL "Fire" ) RATIONALE "The one that does the thing."' + char(10) + 'DEFINE BOX abort ( WIDTH 140, BACKGROUND "#3a4450", FOCUSABLE yes, ROLE button, LABEL "Abort" ) RATIONALE "The one that does not."') oPanel = oDoc.ToPanel() oScene = new stzScene(800, 600) oScene.SetCamera(0, 3, 4, 0, 0, 0) oScene.SetLens(60, 0.1, 100) o1 = new stzScenePanel(oPanel, oScene, 2.0)
classes.example:
? @@( o1.UvAtScreen(400, 300) )
#--> [ 0.50, 0.50 ]
? @@( o1.PanelPointAtScreen(400, 300) )
#--> [ 200, 150 ]
? @@( o1.UvAtScreen(5, 5) )
#--> [ ]
? o1.ClickAtScreen(5, 5)
#--> 0
? o1.VerifyAgainstProjection(5) < 0.000001
#--> 1
? o1.IsMounted()
#--> 0
? @@( o1.ViewportInUse() )
#--> [ 800, 600 ]

classes.name: stzScopedRule
classes.brief: Holds a rule as a triple, the subjects it governs, the claim it makes about them and the subjects it must not govern.
classes.description: Most rules are one function that both selects its subjects and judges them, so a rule that selects the wrong subjects and judges them correctly reports a pass. A scoped rule separates the two: SetScope says which subjects, SetClaimCheck says what must hold of one, SetCounter says which subjects it must leave alone, and SetClaim writes the sentence in words. SetReads, SetWrites and SetOrder let a governance find a stale read from declarations. A subject key is any text or number the scope returns. Check judges one case and returns findings in the house shape; stzRuleGovernance judges a set of rules over many cases. StzPlasticRule is the graph plane's spelling of the same class.
classes.receiver: o1 = new stzScopedRule("evens_small") o1.SetClaim("an even number is below 10") o1.SetScope(func oL { _a_ = []  for i = 1 to len(oL)  if oL[i] % 2 = 0  _a_ + oL[i] ok  next  return _a_ }) o1.SetCounter(func oL { _a_ = []  for i = 1 to len(oL)  if oL[i] % 2 = 1  _a_ + oL[i]  ok  next  return _a_ }) o1.SetClaimCheck(func oL, n { if n < 10  return [ 1, "" ]  ok  return [ 0, "it is " + n ] })
classes.example:
? @@( o1.SubjectsIn([ 1, 2, 3, 12 ]) )
#--> [ 2, 12 ]
? @@( o1.CounterSubjectsIn([ 1, 2, 3, 12 ]) )
#--> [ 1, 3 ]
? o1.Check([ 1, 2, 3, 12 ], "list one")[1][:message]
#--> an even number is below 10 -- it is 12
? o1.Check([ 1, 2, 3, 12 ], "list one")[1][:where]
#--> list one / 12
? len(o1.Check([ 4, 6 ], "list two"))
#--> 0

classes.name: stzScreenReaderBridge
classes.brief: Hands the accessibility tree of a window to the operating system's screen-reader service and counts whether anything read it.
classes.description: The class carries no accessibility knowledge: the tree is built and judged by stzAccessibilityTree, and its JSON crosses unchanged. The bridge owns a platform connection through AccessKit and a lifetime. A machine with no runtime, or a window with no platform handle, is not an error, the bridge is simply not live and LastError says why. TimesAnnounced counts what the program did and TimesRead counts the times an assistive technology asked, which stays 0 on a quiet machine. Attaching to a window hides and re-shows it. The live path needs a real window and was not run for this reference: the example uses an object with no platform handle.

classes.example:
? o1.IsLive()
#--> 0
? o1.LastError()
#--> the window has no platform handle
? o1.Announce("{}")
#--> 0
? o1.TimesAnnounced()
#--> 0
? @@( o1.Stats() )
#--> [ ]

classes.name: stzScript
classes.brief: Holds one writing system, with its name, its four-letter code, its default language and the languages written in it.
classes.description: The identifier may be a script name (Arabic), a code (Arab, Latn), or a text whose first character decides, so a Han ideograph gives han. The accessors read the locale tables: the name, the number, the code, the default language and its country, and the list of languages written in the script. A script has one default language in the data, so Latin answers english, and the matching Languages list is a separate table that does not always contain it.
classes.example:
? o1.Abbreviation()
#--> Arab
? o1.DefaultLanguage()
#--> arabic
? o1.DefaultCountry()
#--> egypt
o2 = new stzScript("Latn")
? o2.Name()
#--> latin

parameters.name: pcScriptIdentifier
parameters.role: a name such as Arabic, a code such as Arab, or a text whose first character is taken to find the script

notes: case is free; a character such as a Han ideograph gives han, with the code Hant

methods.brief: Returns the script's name in lower case.

methods.name: Abbreviation
methods.brief: Returns the four-letter code of the script.

classes.name: stzSecret
classes.brief: Holds a credential you use but never show: it redacts itself everywhere, and only an effectful actor can read the value.
classes.description: A secret has a name, a kind and a source: an inline literal for development, an environment variable, a file, or a vault reference. The value is resolved lazily, at reveal time. Show, Descriptor and any configuration it lands in print only the redacted descriptor. Reveal is the one door to the plaintext and it is governed: an effectful actor such as HumanActor passes, while an inference-only LLMActor can reference the secret in a plan but is refused, and the refusal is noted to the security ledger. stzApiKey, stzPassword, stzDeployKey and stzToken specialise it by kind.
classes.example:
? o1.Descriptor()
#--> <secret 'db-pass' (secret) from literal>
? o1.IsRevealableBy(HumanActor("alice"))
#--> 1
? o1.IsRevealableBy(LLMActor("bot"))
#--> 0

notes: a refused read never touches the value
warnings: raises an error for a refused actor (an inference-only LLMActor or a value that is not an actor), and the refusal is noted to the security ledger as secret.reveal.refused; raises an error for a vault source or when no source is set

methods.brief: Returns the plaintext as Reveal does, fetching a vault-sourced secret through a resolver.

classes.name: stzSecretExpiryWatch
classes.brief: Reads a store of secrets on a tick and tells the security ledger, once, which are about to expire or have.
classes.description: Expiry is a detection, not a check at call time: the port never looks at a date. Each cycle compares every expiring secret in the store with the clock and writes secret.expiring or secret.expired once per change of state, naming the secret and never its value. The default window is thirty days. The watch holds the store as it was handed over, so a host that runs it periodically hands it the current store each cycle. It is a periodic thing with a name and a Cycle, hostable on any agent host. Use invented secrets in a test.
classes.example:
oCert = StzPispiSecretQ("bia", "mtls-cert")
oCert.FromEnv("INVENTED_MTLS_CERT_PATH")
oCert.SetExpiry(1800000000 + 10 * 86400)
oStore = StzSecretStoreQ("billing")
oStore.Register(oCert)
o1.Watch(oStore)
o1.AsOf(1800000000)
? o1.Cycle()
#--> 1
? o1.Cycle()
#--> 0

methods.name: init
methods.brief: Builds a watch over the secrets of a store, to announce in the security ledger those about to expire or already expired.

parameters.name: poStore
parameters.role: the stzSecretStore to read

notes: a secret registered after this call is not seen: hand the watch the current store with Watch before each cycle

methods.name: Name_
methods.brief: Returns the name under which a host schedules this watch on its tick.

methods.name: Watch
methods.brief: Replaces the store this object reads with the current one, keeping what it has already announced.

parameters.name: poStore
parameters.role: the stzSecretStore to read from now on

methods.returns: the watch itself, so calls chain
notes: Ring copies an object on assignment, which is why a host calls this each cycle

methods.name: WarnWithinDays
methods.brief: Sets how many days before its end a secret counts as expiring; thirty days when never set.

parameters.name: pnDays
parameters.role: the length of the warning window, in days

methods.returns: the watch itself, so calls chain

methods.name: AsOf
methods.brief: Fixes the moment the watch judges against, so a test does not depend on the clock; 0 returns to the engine clock.

parameters.name: pnEpoch
parameters.role: the moment as epoch seconds, 0 for the engine clock

methods.returns: the watch itself, so calls chain

methods.name: Cycle
methods.brief: Writes one security-ledger event for each secret whose state changed since the last run, and answers how many it wrote.
notes: an expiring secret goes in the ledger as secret.expiring, a lapsed one as secret.expired, by the secret's name and never its value; a renewed secret is forgotten, so its next lapse is announced afresh
warnings: a secret with no expiry date, or of a kind that has none, is never judged; the state changes are expiring then expired, and the second cycle on an unchanged store writes nothing

classes.name: stzSecretStore
classes.brief: Holds a project's secrets in one registry, with one governed and audited door through which a value can leave.
classes.description: Secrets are registered once by name, so the whole credential surface is enumerable and every entry is self-redacting. Reveal applies the actor gate (only an effectful, non-sandboxed actor passes; a language-model actor is refused) and records the attempt in the access log and in the security ledger, by the secret's name and never its value. RotateToFresh renews a value the store owns, and refuses a secret that lives in an environment variable, a file or a vault, naming where to rotate it. SaveSealedTo writes the store as one authenticated-encryption blob, and StzSecretStoreFromSealedFile reads it back. The store keeps a copy of what it registers.
classes.example:
o1.Register(StzApiKeyQ("stripe").FromEnvQ("INVENTED_STRIPE_ENV"))
? o1.DescriptorOf("stripe")
#--> <secret 'stripe' (apikey) from env:INVENTED_STRIPE_ENV>

methods.name: init
methods.brief: Builds an empty store, the one registry in which a project governs its secrets.

parameters.name: pcName
parameters.role: the store's name, bound into sealed files as their authenticated context

methods.name: Name
methods.brief: Returns the store's name.

methods.name: Register
methods.brief: Adds a secret under its own name, in lower case; a name already registered is replaced, which is rotation.

parameters.name: poSecret
parameters.role: the stzSecret, or a kind of one such as stzApiKey, to register

methods.returns: the store itself, so calls chain
notes: secrets are enumerable by Names and show only their descriptor
warnings: a non-object raises an error; the store keeps a COPY of the secret, so changing the original afterwards does not reach it; replacing a name leaves no entry in the access log and none in the ledger

methods.name: Rotate
methods.brief: Replaces the secret registered under the new secret's name, or adds it when the name is new.

parameters.name: poNewSecret
parameters.role: the stzSecret that takes the place of the registered one

notes: RotateQ is the same call and returns the store
warnings: the replacement leaves no entry in the access log and none in the ledger

extensions.name: RotateQ
extensions.adds: does what the method does, then returns the object, so the call can be chained

methods.name: RotateToFresh
methods.brief: Replaces the value of a secret the store owns with 32 fresh random bytes as 64 hex characters, keeping its kind and name.

parameters.name: pcName
parameters.role: the name of the registered secret to renew

parameters.name: poActor
parameters.role: the actor that performs the rotation, which must be effectful and not sandboxed

methods.returns: the store itself, so calls chain
notes: the access log gets a rotated entry and the ledger a secret.rotated grant; a token's expiry is cleared (rotate_secret_narrated)
warnings: raises an error for an unknown name, for a refused actor and for a secret whose source is an environment variable, a file or a vault, naming where to rotate it; an actor that is not an object also fails closed, but with R13 Object is required and no refusal is recorded

methods.name: Revoke
methods.brief: Removes a secret by name; an unknown name changes nothing.

parameters.name: pcName
parameters.role: the name of the secret to remove

methods.returns: the store itself, so calls chain
notes: the name is matched without regard to case
warnings: the removal leaves no entry in the access log and none in the ledger

methods.name: Has
methods.brief: TRUE if a secret of that name is registered.

parameters.name: pcName
parameters.role: the secret's name, matched without regard to case

methods.name: NumberOfSecrets
methods.brief: Returns how many secrets are registered.

methods.name: Names
methods.brief: Returns the names of the registered secrets, in lower case, in the order registered: the project's whole credential surface.
notes: safe to show or log, because no value is in it

methods.name: Secret
methods.brief: Returns the stored secret object, which is still self-redacting.

parameters.name: pcName
parameters.role: the secret's name, matched without regard to case

methods.returns: a stzSecret, or an empty text when the name is unknown
notes: holding it reveals nothing, and it is a copy: changing it does not change the store

methods.name: DescriptorOf
methods.brief: Returns the redacted descriptor of a registered secret, never its value.

parameters.name: pcName
parameters.role: the secret's name, matched without regard to case

methods.returns: a text such as <secret 'stripe' (apikey) from env:STRIPE_KEY>, or <no secret 'name'> when unknown

methods.name: Reveal
methods.brief: Returns a secret's plaintext through the store's governed door: only an effectful, non-sandboxed actor passes, and each try is audited.

parameters.name: pcName
parameters.role: the name of the secret to read

parameters.name: poActor
parameters.role: the actor asking, an object that must be effectful and not sandboxed

notes: a granted read is logged and recorded as secret.reveal.granted, with the secret's name and never its value
warnings: raises an error for an unknown name, which is not logged, and for a refused actor, which is logged as refused and recorded in the ledger as secret.reveal.refused

methods.name: RevealVia
methods.brief: Reveals a secret through a vault resolver for a vault-sourced secret, still gated and audited; for any other secret the resolver is ignored.

parameters.name: pcName
parameters.role: the name of the secret to read

parameters.name: poResolver
parameters.role: the vault resolver object, or an empty text when the secret is not vault- sourced

parameters.name: poActor
parameters.role: the actor asking, an object that must be effectful and not sandboxed

notes: a superset of Reveal, which calls it with no resolver
warnings: an unknown name and a refused actor raise errors, as for Reveal

methods.name: IsRevealableBy
methods.brief: TRUE if the actor could reveal that secret; asking changes nothing and leaves no audit entry.

parameters.name: pcName
parameters.role: the secret's name

parameters.name: poActor
parameters.role: the actor to test

methods.returns: TRUE or FALSE; FALSE for an unknown name or an actor that is not an object

methods.name: SaveSealedTo
methods.brief: Writes the whole store to a file as one encrypted blob keyed by a key secret; literal values are sealed, other sources by pointer only.

parameters.name: pcPath
parameters.role: the file to write, overwritten

parameters.name: poKeySecret
parameters.role: the stzSecret whose 64-hex value keys the seal

parameters.name: poActor
parameters.role: the actor performing the seal, effectful and not sandboxed

methods.returns: the store itself, so calls chain
notes: an environment, file or vault secret is saved as its pointer, so its plaintext never leaves its source; the store's name is bound as context, so a file cannot pass for another store's
warnings: a refused actor raises an error and is recorded; an actor that is not an object also fails closed, but with R13 Object is required and no refusal is recorded

methods.name: SaveSealedToVia
methods.brief: Writes the sealed store as SaveSealedTo does, with the key secret fetched through a vault resolver.

parameters.role: the stzSecret that keys the seal

parameters.name: poResolver
parameters.role: the vault resolver object, or an empty text

parameters.name: poActor
parameters.role: the actor performing the seal, effectful and not sandboxed

methods.returns: the store itself, so calls chain
notes: the file reads back with StzSecretStoreFromSealedFile
warnings: same as SaveSealedTo

methods.name: AccessLog
methods.brief: Returns the audit trail: who read, or was refused, which secret, in order.
methods.returns: a list of [ number, actor, secret, outcome ] rows, outcome granted, refused or rotated
notes: an unknown name is not logged; the log lives in the object and dies with it, which is why each entry also reaches the ledger

methods.name: NumberOfAccesses
methods.brief: Returns how many entries the audit trail holds.

methods.name: RefusedAccesses
methods.brief: Returns how many reveals were refused, a misuse signal worth watching.

methods.name: Show
methods.brief: Prints a summary line of the store, then the redacted descriptor of each secret.
notes: no value is printed

classes.name: stzSecretStoreResponder
classes.brief: Performs the :RotateSecret action of a response plan by replacing a secret of a stzSecretStore with fresh random bytes.
classes.description: It holds the store by reference, not a copy, so the caller's store sees the new value, and it rotates as the service identity it is given, which must be effectful and not sandboxed. Only a secret the store owns can be rotated; one read from an environment variable, a file or a vault raises an error naming where to rotate it. It answers no other verb: each of those raises an error that names the responder to wire. A value is never printed.
classes.receiver: oStore = StzSecretStoreQ("billing"); oStore.Register(StzApiKeyQ("signing- key").FromLiteralQ("old-invented-value")); o1 = new stzSecretStoreResponder(oStore, HumanActor("secrets-service"))
classes.example:
o1.RotateSecret("signing-key")
? oStore.Reveal("signing-key", HumanActor("oncall")) != "old-invented-value"
#--> 1
? o1.Owns("lockaccount")
#--> 0
