classes.name: stzSection
classes.brief: Holds a section, the start and end positions of a stretch of a list or a string, checked against the size of that host.
classes.description: Build one with new stzSection(n1, n2, nSize) or StzSectionQ(n1, n2, nSize); the global Section(n1, n2, nSize) answers just the [ start, end ] list and IsSection(n1, n2, nSize) tells whether the three numbers make a valid section. The positions may be keywords (:First, :Last) or named places ([ :From, 3 ], [ :To, 6 ]). Positions count from 1 and negative ones are refused. The check is incomplete: a start past the size is accepted when the end is inside, and nothing orders the two positions.
classes.example:
? @@( o1.Content() )
#--> [ 2, 5 ]
? o1.StartPosition()
#--> 2
? o1.EndPosition()
#--> 5
? IsSection(1, 11, 10)
#--> 0

methods.name: init
methods.brief: Builds a section, a pair of start and end positions, checked against the size of the list or string it is meant for.

parameters.name: _n1_
parameters.role: the start position, from 1, or a keyword such as :First, :Start or a named place such as [ :From, 3 ]

parameters.name: _n2_
parameters.role: the end position, from 1, or :Last, :End or [ :To, 6 ]

parameters.name: _nSize_
parameters.role: the number of items or chars of the host, or [ :Size, 10 ]

notes: negative positions that count from the end are refused here, unlike stzList.Section
warnings: A start or end of 0, or not a number, raises "Incorrect params! n1 and n2 must be numbers different from zero"; an end past the size, or a negative position, raises "Out of range! nSize must between n1 and n2"; a start past the size is accepted when the end is inside it: new stzSection(12, 3, 10) answers [ 12, 3 ], and a start after the end is kept as given

methods.name: Content
methods.brief: Returns the section as a list of its start and end positions.
methods.returns: a list of two numbers, [ start, end ]

methods.name: StartPosition
methods.brief: Returns the first position of the section, as given.
notes: a section built as (5, 2, 10) is not reordered: its start is 5

methods.name: StartPos
methods.brief: Returns the first position of the section, the same as StartPosition.

methods.name: EndPosition
methods.brief: Returns the last position of the section, as given.

methods.name: EndPos
methods.brief: Returns the last position of the section, the same as EndPosition.

methods.name: StzType
methods.brief: Returns the kind of object this is, in lowercase.

classes.name: stzSecurityAttestation
classes.brief: Exports a security ledger to a sealed file under an actor's name and states who exported what, when and how to verify it.
classes.description: The ledger's hash chain makes the file tamper-evident; the attestation adds the custody statement an auditor needs: the attestor, the time, the number of entries, the head of the chain and the key kind. Exporting is governed by the sensing capability, so an inference-only actor may analyse an incident in the process and may not write the evidence out. Both a refusal and an export are recorded as events, so the ledger carries its own custody history. A keyed seal needs the same key to verify with StzVerifyAttestation. Use invented keys in examples; real ones belong in a secret store.
classes.example:
? o1.WasWritten()
#--> 0
? o1.MayAttest(HumanActor("alice"))
#--> 1
? o1.MayAttest(LLMActor("bot"))
#--> 0
? o1.Statement()
#--> Attestation nightly-evidence: nothing written yet.

methods.name: init
methods.brief: Builds a custody statement for exported evidence, with a name and nothing attested yet.

parameters.name: pcName
parameters.role: the attestation's name, quoted in its statement

methods.name: Name
methods.brief: Returns the name the attestation was built with.

methods.name: Of
methods.brief: Chooses the security ledger whose events will be exported.

parameters.name: poLedger
parameters.role: a stzSecurityLedger, such as the process ledger

methods.returns: the attestation itself, so calls chain
notes: the ledger is read when WriteTo runs

methods.name: SealedWith
methods.brief: Sets the key that seals the exported file with a keyed HMAC-SHA256 over the chain head and the count.

parameters.name: pcKey
parameters.role: the sealing key, held as given

methods.returns: the attestation itself, so calls chain
notes: the same key is needed to verify the file
warnings: without a key, or with an empty one, the export is sealed with no key: the chain still detects a changed entry, but anyone can recompute the seal, and Statement says so

methods.name: MayAttest
methods.brief: TRUE if the actor holds the sensing capability that reading the evidence out requires.

parameters.name: poActor
parameters.role: the actor asking

notes: an inference-only actor, such as an LLM actor, is refused

methods.name: WhyNot
methods.brief: Returns the reason an actor may not export the evidence, an empty text when it may.

parameters.name: poActor
parameters.role: the actor asking

notes: the reason names the actor

methods.name: WriteTo
methods.brief: Seals the ledger to a file under this actor's name and records the export as an event; a refused actor writes nothing.

parameters.name: pcPath
parameters.role: the file to write

parameters.name: poActor
parameters.role: the actor exporting, which needs the sensing capability

methods.returns: TRUE when the file was written, FALSE when the actor is refused
notes: the ledger names actors, subjects and refusals, so the file is sensitive: store it with care
warnings: raises an error telling to say Of first when no ledger was chosen; a refusal is noted as evidence.export_refused, a success as evidence.exported

methods.name: WasWritten
methods.brief: TRUE if a successful export has been made.

methods.name: Path
methods.brief: Returns the file the last export was written to.
methods.returns: a text; empty before an export

methods.name: Attestor
methods.brief: Returns the name of the actor who made the last export.
methods.returns: a text; empty before an export

methods.name: AttestedAt
methods.brief: Returns when the last export was made.
methods.returns: a number, epoch milliseconds on the wall clock; 0 before an export

methods.name: HeadDigest
methods.brief: Returns the digest of the last event exported, the head of the hash chain.
methods.returns: a text of 64 hexadecimal characters; empty before an export

methods.name: EntryCount
methods.brief: Returns how many events the exported file holds.

methods.name: Statement
methods.brief: Returns the custody statement a person reads beside the file, as one text with a line per fact.
methods.returns: a multi-line text, or a sentence saying nothing is written yet

methods.name: Explain
methods.brief: Returns the custody statement as a list of lines: file, attestor, time, entries, chain head, seal and how to verify.
notes: it states that entries are descriptors with no secret value, which holds only for the values a caller put in an event: a path with a query string, or an actor name, is recorded as received

methods.name: Show
methods.brief: Prints the custody statement, one line per fact.

classes.name: stzSecurityDrill
classes.brief: Rehearses an attack on a spawned target application and reports whether the detections fired, from sealed and verified evidence.
classes.description: A drill spawns a target (its own ledger, auth and signed-request gate), attacks it with credential stuffing, a forged signature and a replayed request, and then learns what happened only from the ledger the target sealed to a file and the drill verified. Contain then derives a plan from that evidence, commits it as an operator, and ContainmentHolds proves from outside that the account is locked. Timings are measured: TimeToDetectMs and TimeToContainMs. SpawnTarget starts a second process and opens a port on 127.0.0.1, so a drill belongs on a machine set aside for it; the methods that only read state work without a target.
classes.example:
? o1.Name()
#--> nightly
? o1.Passed()
#--> 0
? o1.TimeToDetectMs()
#--> -1
? o1.AcquisitionWhy() = ""
#--> 1

methods.name: init
methods.brief: Builds a named drill with a default evidence file path in the current folder; nothing is started or contacted yet.

parameters.name: pcName
parameters.role: the drill's name

notes: the evidence path is absolute, built from the current folder at construction
warnings: nothing is spawned or contacted until SpawnTarget

methods.name: Name
methods.brief: Returns the drill's name.

methods.name: SetKey
methods.brief: Sets the shared secret of the target's signed-request gate, which FireReplay also signs with.

parameters.name: pcKey
parameters.role: the secret, as text

methods.returns: the drill itself, so calls chain
notes: an invented key only: it is a rehearsal secret, never a real one
warnings: the key is handed to the target at SpawnTarget, so set it before

methods.name: SetEvidencePath
methods.brief: Sets the file where the target seals its ledger and from which the drill reads it back.

parameters.name: pcPath
parameters.role: the evidence file path, absolute because the target resolves paths in its own folder

methods.returns: the drill itself, so calls chain
warnings: Destroy deletes this file if it exists

methods.name: EvidencePath
methods.brief: Returns the path of the evidence file.

methods.name: Port
methods.brief: Returns the port the target listens on, 0 before SpawnTarget.

methods.name: SpawnTarget
methods.brief: Starts the application under attack as a child ring process on 127.0.0.1 and waits for it to answer.

parameters.name: pnPort
parameters.role: the port to listen on

methods.returns: 1 (TRUE) when the target answered within 20 seconds, else 0
notes: the target has its own ledger, auth, signed-request gate and /seal route, and ends by itself after 60000 ms
warnings: not run here: it starts a second process, opens a port and writes a generated script .stzdrilltarget_gen.ring beside the security sources; a drill is for a machine set aside for it, and Destroy stops the child

methods.name: WaitReady
methods.brief: Polls the target's /health route until it answers 200 OK or the time is up.

parameters.name: pnTimeoutMs
parameters.role: how long to wait, in milliseconds

methods.returns: 1 (TRUE) when the target answered; 0 on timeout
warnings: not run here: it sends requests to the target's port; on a drill that never spawned a target it can only time out

methods.name: FireCredentialStuffing
methods.brief: Sends a number of login requests with wrong passwords for one account and expects the credential-stuffing detection to fire.

parameters.name: pcUser
parameters.role: the account to attack

parameters.name: pnTimes
parameters.role: how many wrong passwords to send, one request each

methods.returns: the drill itself, so calls chain
notes: the first attack sent stamps the start of TimeToDetectMs
warnings: the passwords are wrong-1, wrong-2 and so on; the expectation is recorded whether or not the target answered

methods.name: FireForgery
methods.brief: Sends one signed request whose signature does not verify and expects the forged-request detection to fire.
methods.returns: the drill itself, so calls chain
notes: the request carries the current time and the nonce forge-1

methods.name: FireReplay
methods.brief: Sends one validly signed request twice, so the second is a replay, and expects the replayed-request detection.
methods.returns: the drill itself, so calls chain
notes: it signs with the drill's key (SetKey) and assigns the global $oDrillServer, a stzRequestSigner, in the calling process

methods.name: Expectations
methods.brief: Returns what the attacks fired so far expect to see detected.
methods.returns: a list of [ detection name, attack label ] rows, in the order fired; [ ] before any attack

methods.name: CollectEvidence
methods.brief: Asks the target to seal its ledger, verifies the sealed file, rebuilds a working ledger from it and notes which detections fired in it.
methods.returns: 1 (TRUE) when the evidence was verified and acquired; 0 when the file is missing or fails verification, and AcquisitionWhy says why
notes: when every expectation is met, the time of detection is stamped; the rebuilt ledger recomputes its own chain
warnings: the drill believes only the sealed and verified file, never the target's memory

methods.name: OpenVictimSession
methods.brief: Logs the victim in for real before the attack, so containment has a live session to end.

parameters.name: pcUser
parameters.role: the account to log in

parameters.name: pcPassword
parameters.role: its password

methods.returns: TRUE if the target returned a session token; FALSE when it refused
warnings: the token is kept inside the drill for ContainmentHolds

methods.name: Contain
methods.brief: Turns the acquired evidence into a response plan and performs on the target what the operator may commit.

parameters.name: poOperator
parameters.role: the actor who commits, for example HumanActor("oncall")

methods.returns: the number of actions committed, 0 when the operator is refused
notes: the plan holds one incident per credential-stuffing finding; when something was committed and ContainmentHolds is TRUE, the time of containment is stamped
warnings: raises an error when no evidence was acquired yet; a refused operator commits nothing and the plan records the refusal

methods.name: ContainmentHolds
methods.brief: TRUE if the right password is refused and the pre-attack session is dead, checked from outside the target.
methods.returns: TRUE or FALSE; FALSE before containment
notes: it sends two requests to the target for the account named victim

methods.name: TimeToDetectMs
methods.brief: Returns the milliseconds from the first attack sent to the evidence showing every expected detection.
methods.returns: a number; -1 when that point was not reached

methods.name: TimeToContainMs
methods.brief: Returns the milliseconds from the detection to a containment that was applied and verified.
methods.returns: a number; -1 when that point was not reached

methods.name: Containment
methods.brief: Returns what Contain did: how many actions were planned, committed and refused.
methods.returns: a list of [ :planned, :committed, :refused ] rows, one list per Contain call; [ ] before any

methods.name: AcquiredLedger
methods.brief: Returns the ledger rebuilt from the verified evidence.
methods.returns: a ledger object; the empty text before a successful CollectEvidence

methods.name: Attestor
methods.brief: Returns who attested the sealed evidence.
methods.returns: a text, such as target-process; the empty text before a successful CollectEvidence

methods.name: AcquisitionWhy
methods.brief: Returns the verdict of the last evidence acquisition, in words.
methods.returns: a text such as "acquired 9 verified entr(ies)", or the reason it was refused, such as a missing file; empty before CollectEvidence

methods.name: FiredDetections
methods.brief: Returns the names of the detections found in the acquired evidence.
methods.returns: a list of text; [ ] before CollectEvidence

methods.name: Passed
methods.brief: TRUE if at least one attack was fired and every expected detection fired in the evidence.

methods.name: MissedDetections
methods.brief: Returns the expected detections that did not fire.
methods.returns: a list of text; [ ] when none missed

methods.name: Explain
methods.brief: Returns the drill's report as lines: verdict, evidence, one line per expected detection, and the timings.
warnings: one line per expected detection is marked fired or MISSED, and the two timings follow when known; with an acquired ledger but no attack fired, the verdict reads "MISSED: ." with nothing after it

methods.name: Show
methods.brief: Prints the lines of Explain.

methods.name: Destroy
methods.brief: Kills the child target if one was spawned and deletes the evidence file if it exists.
methods.returns: the drill itself, so calls chain
notes: on a drill that spawned nothing it only deletes the evidence file

classes.name: stzSecurityEvent
classes.brief: Holds one typed security record: what happened, who did it, to which thing, how it ended, why, and when.
classes.description: The kind comes from a closed catalog of dotted names (auth.login.failed, secret.reveal.refused ...), and an unknown kind raises. The setters return the event, so calls chain. An event never carries a secret value: About takes the descriptor of an object, never its value. Both clocks are stamped when the event is built, the wall clock for the forensic when and the monotonic clock for ordering, together with the active trace id. An event is recorded in a stzSecurityLedger, and CanonicalString, ToOcsfJson and AsLine are its three serial forms.
classes.example:
o1.ByActorNamed("bob", "external")
o1.About("user:bob")
o1.Refused("bad password")
? o1.AsLine()
#--> REFUSED auth.login.failed by bob (external) on user:bob -- bad password

methods.name: init
methods.brief: Builds an event of one kind from the closed catalog, stamping both clocks and the active trace id at the moment of detection.

parameters.name: pcKind
parameters.role: the event kind, a dotted catalog name such as auth.login.failed, matched without regard to case

notes: the outcome starts as refused; severity and technique start at the catalog values for the kind
warnings: an unknown kind raises an error that lists every known kind: the catalog is closed

methods.name: Kind
methods.brief: Returns the catalog name of the event, in lower case.

methods.name: Severity
methods.brief: Returns the severity of the event: info, warning or error.
notes: it starts at the catalog default of the kind and the As calls override it

methods.name: Technique
methods.brief: Returns the MITRE ATT&CK technique id of the kind, or an empty text where no honest mapping exists.

methods.name: Meaning
methods.brief: Returns the catalog's one-line sentence saying what the kind stands for.

methods.name: Actor
methods.brief: Returns the name of the actor that did it.
methods.returns: a text; empty until an actor is given

methods.name: Posture
methods.brief: Returns the actor's posture in lower case, such as trusted, sandboxed or external.
methods.returns: a text; empty until an actor is given

methods.name: ActorKinds
methods.brief: Returns the capability kinds the actor object held, as ByActor read them.
methods.returns: a list of text; [ ] for an actor given by name

methods.name: Action
methods.brief: Returns the act that was attempted, trimmed and in lower case.
methods.returns: a text; empty until Doing sets it

methods.name: Risk
methods.brief: Returns the risk tier of the act that was attempted.
methods.returns: a number, 0 until AtRisk sets one

methods.name: Subject
methods.brief: Returns the descriptor of the thing acted on; the value of a secret is never in it.
methods.returns: a text; empty until About sets it

methods.name: Origin
methods.brief: Returns where the event came from, such as an address, a host or an endpoint.
methods.returns: a text; empty until FromOrigin sets it

methods.name: Outcome
methods.brief: Returns how the attempt ended: granted, refused, failed or observed.
methods.returns: a text, refused for a new event

methods.name: Reason
methods.brief: Returns the gate's own words for a refused, failed or observed event.
methods.returns: a text; empty for a grant

methods.name: AtWall
methods.brief: Returns the wall-clock time of the event, in epoch milliseconds.
notes: stamped when the event was built, which is the moment of detection and not of recording

methods.name: AtMono
methods.brief: Returns the monotonic-clock stamp of the event, in milliseconds, which keeps its ordering across a clock correction.
methods.returns: a number, which may have a fraction
notes: it orders the events of this process only and is not part of the canonical line

methods.name: TraceId
methods.brief: Returns the id of the trace scope that was active when the event was built.
methods.returns: a text; empty outside a trace scope

methods.name: IsRefusal
methods.brief: TRUE if the outcome is refused or failed; a granted or an observed event is not a refusal.

methods.name: ByActor
methods.brief: Takes the actor's name, posture and capability kinds from an actor object, or only the name from a text.

parameters.name: poActor
parameters.role: an actor object such as HumanActor, or the actor's name as text

methods.returns: the event itself, so calls chain
notes: a text sets only the name, so a posture and kinds set earlier stay as they were; an object without Name records its class name

methods.name: ByActorNamed
methods.brief: Sets the actor from a name and a posture, for a caller with no actor object yet, such as a login door.

parameters.name: pcName
parameters.role: the actor name, as text

parameters.name: pcPosture
parameters.role: the actor's posture, stored in lower case, such as external

methods.returns: the event itself, so calls chain

methods.name: About
methods.brief: Sets the subject: a text is taken as already safe, an object contributes its redacted descriptor and never its value.

parameters.name: pSubject
parameters.role: a descriptor text such as user:admin, or an object such as a secret

methods.returns: the event itself, so calls chain
notes: an object that has neither a descriptor nor a name records its class name
warnings: the redaction law lives here: given a secret it records the descriptor and never reveals it

methods.name: Doing
methods.brief: Sets the act that was attempted, trimmed and put in lower case.

parameters.name: pcAction
parameters.role: the verb, such as reveal or login

methods.returns: the event itself, so calls chain

methods.name: AtRisk
methods.brief: Sets the risk tier of the act that was attempted; a value that is not a number is ignored.

parameters.name: pnTier
parameters.role: the risk tier, as a number

methods.returns: the event itself, so calls chain

methods.name: FromOrigin
methods.brief: Sets where the event came from.

parameters.name: pcOrigin
parameters.role: an address, a host or an endpoint, as text

methods.returns: the event itself, so calls chain

methods.name: OccurredAt
methods.brief: Sets the wall time of an event that did not happen now, such as an imported one or a guard needing exact windows.

parameters.name: pnWallMs
parameters.role: the event time, in epoch milliseconds

methods.returns: the event itself, so calls chain
notes: a value that is not a number is ignored; the monotonic stamp is left alone, because it cannot be borrowed

methods.name: Granted
methods.brief: Sets the outcome to granted.
methods.returns: the event itself, so calls chain
notes: the reason is left as it was

methods.name: Refused
methods.brief: Sets the outcome to refused, with the gate's own words as the reason.

parameters.name: pcReason
parameters.role: the gate's own words, as text

methods.returns: the event itself, so calls chain

methods.name: Failed
methods.brief: Sets the outcome to failed: the gate admitted the act and it still did not complete.

parameters.name: pcReason
parameters.role: why it did not complete, as text

methods.returns: the event itself, so calls chain

methods.name: Observed
methods.brief: Sets the outcome to observed, a fact that carries no verdict, such as a session reaching its expiry.

parameters.name: pcReason
parameters.role: what was seen, as text

methods.returns: the event itself, so calls chain
notes: an observed event is not a refusal, so no pivot that counts refusals counts it

methods.name: AsInfo
methods.brief: Sets the severity of the event to info, overriding the catalog default.
methods.returns: the event itself, so calls chain
notes: OcsfSeverityId and ToOcsfJson on the event itself do use the override
warnings: the ledger keeps the override, but the OCSF exports of the ledger read the catalog default again

methods.name: AsWarning
methods.brief: Sets the severity of the event to warning, overriding the catalog default.
methods.returns: the event itself, so calls chain
notes: OcsfSeverityId and ToOcsfJson on the event itself do use the override
warnings: the ledger keeps the override, but the OCSF exports of the ledger read the catalog default again

methods.name: AsError
methods.brief: Sets the severity of the event to error, overriding the catalog default.
methods.returns: the event itself, so calls chain
notes: OcsfSeverityId and ToOcsfJson on the event itself do use the override
warnings: the ledger keeps the override, but the OCSF exports of the ledger read the catalog default again

methods.name: Record
methods.brief: Returns the event as its native record, every field including the actor's kinds and the monotonic stamp.
methods.returns: a list of [ key, value ] pairs: kind, severity, technique, actor, posture, actorKinds, action, risk, subject, origin, outcome, reason, atWall, atMono, traceId

methods.name: CanonicalString
methods.brief: Returns the event as one fixed-order line of twelve fields, the form the ledger hashes into its chain.
notes: a vertical bar inside a field is folded to a slash so the line splits back cleanly; two events with the same facts give the same line; the technique, the actor kinds and the monotonic stamp are not in it

methods.name: OcsfSeverityId
methods.brief: Returns the OCSF severity id: 1 informational, 3 medium for a warning, 4 high for an error.

methods.name: OcsfStatusId
methods.brief: Returns the OCSF status id: 1 for a granted event, 2 for every other outcome.
notes: refused and failed both read 2 as well
warnings: an observed event also reads 2, so a fact with no verdict reaches a SIEM as a failure

methods.name: OcsfClassUid
methods.brief: Returns the OCSF class uid chosen from the kind: 3002 for auth, sso and oauth kinds, 4002 for http kinds, 6003 for the rest.
notes: a best-effort mapping: facts that map no field travel under unmapped

methods.name: OcsfCategoryUid
methods.brief: Returns the OCSF category uid of the event's class: 3, 4 or 6.

methods.name: ToOcsfJson
methods.brief: Returns the event as one OCSF JSON object, with the facts that map no field riding under unmapped.
notes: the trace id appears as metadata_trace_id and the technique under unmapped; backslashes and quotes in the text are escaped

methods.name: AsLine
methods.brief: Returns the event as one readable line: outcome, kind, actor with posture, subject, origin and reason.
methods.returns: a text, for example REFUSED auth.login.failed by bob (external) on route:/pay -- bad password

methods.name: Explain
methods.brief: Returns the event told as lines of text: kind and severity, meaning, the readable line, both times and the ATT&CK id.

methods.name: Show
methods.brief: Prints the lines Explain returns, one per line.

classes.name: stzSecurityGraph
classes.brief: Holds the security surface as a graph of actors, tools, capabilities, secrets, stores and sites, so that escalation is a path query.
classes.description: A flag check sees one object at a time and misses a sandboxed actor that reaches an effect through a tool or a delegation, because that is a path. This graph makes the paths explicit: Uses, Grants, Holds, Delegates, References and StoredIn add labelled edges, and ReachesEffectful, PathToEffectful and AuditEscalations ask whether, and how, a sandboxed node gets to the effectful capability. AttachSecret refuses a live secret for a sandboxed actor, BlastRadius lists who can reach a secret, and CutCapability removes an actor's routes to a capability. Node ids are lower- cased. The postures that gates decide on are also recorded out of reach of GraphQ, and Tampering reports any that were edited around the doors.
classes.receiver: o1 = new stzSecurityGraph("resto"); o1.AddActor("llm", "sandboxed"); o1.AddTool("shell") o1.Uses("llm", "shell"); o1.Grants("shell", "effectful")
classes.example:
? o1.ReachesEffectful("llm")
#--> 1
? @@(o1.PathToEffectful("llm"))
#--> [ "llm", "shell", "effectful" ]
? o1.IsSound()
#--> 0

methods.name: init
methods.brief: Builds an empty security graph with a name, ready for actors, tools, secrets and the edges between them.

parameters.name: pcName
parameters.role: the graph name

methods.name: GraphQ
methods.brief: Returns the underlying stzGraph, to draw or query directly.
methods.returns: the stzGraph object that holds the nodes and edges
warnings: the graph can be edited through it around the governed doors; Tampering reports a changed posture

methods.name: Name
methods.brief: Returns the name the graph was built with.

methods.name: AddActor
methods.brief: Declares an actor node with a trust posture, and records the posture where gates read it.

parameters.name: pcId
parameters.role: the actor name, lower-cased and trimmed to make the node id

parameters.name: pcPosture
parameters.role: the posture, trusted, external or sandboxed

methods.returns: the graph itself, so calls chain
notes: declaring the same id again replaces its posture; the posture record is kept out of reach of GraphQ

methods.name: Tampering
methods.brief: Returns the actors whose posture in the graph no longer equals the one AddActor recorded.
methods.returns: a list of [ actor, recorded, found ] rows; found is (removed) for a deleted node
notes: [ ] when nothing was edited around the governed doors

methods.name: AddTool
methods.brief: Declares a tool node, something an actor can use and that can grant a capability.

parameters.name: pcId
parameters.role: the tool name, lower-cased and trimmed to make the node id

methods.returns: the graph itself, so calls chain

methods.name: AddSecret
methods.brief: Declares a secret node, by descriptor and never by value.

parameters.name: pcId
parameters.role: the secret name, lower-cased and trimmed to make the node id

methods.returns: the graph itself, so calls chain

methods.name: AddStore
methods.brief: Declares a store node, a place where secrets live.

parameters.name: pcId
parameters.role: the store name, lower-cased and trimmed to make the node id

methods.returns: the graph itself, so calls chain

methods.name: AddSite
methods.brief: Declares a site node, an application surface that can reference secrets.

parameters.name: pcId
parameters.role: the site name, lower-cased and trimmed to make the node id

methods.returns: the graph itself, so calls chain

methods.name: AddCapability
methods.brief: Declares a capability node, such as effectful, ahead of its first use.

parameters.name: pcId
parameters.role: the capability name, lower-cased and trimmed to make the node id

methods.returns: the graph itself, so calls chain
notes: Holds and Grants create the node themselves when it is missing

methods.name: Holds
methods.brief: Adds the edge by which an actor directly holds a capability.

parameters.name: pcActor
parameters.role: the declared actor

parameters.name: pcCapability
parameters.role: the capability, created if missing

methods.returns: the graph itself, so calls chain
notes: an existing edge between the same two nodes is kept, so no second edge is added
warnings: raises an error when the actor was not declared first

methods.name: Uses
methods.brief: Adds the edge by which an actor uses a tool.

parameters.name: pcActor
parameters.role: the declared actor

parameters.name: pcTool
parameters.role: the declared tool

methods.returns: the graph itself, so calls chain
warnings: raises an error when either node was not declared first

methods.name: Grants
methods.brief: Adds the edge by which a tool confers a capability on whoever uses it.

parameters.name: pcTool
parameters.role: the declared tool

parameters.name: pcCapability
parameters.role: the capability, created if missing

methods.returns: the graph itself, so calls chain
warnings: raises an error when the tool was not declared first

methods.name: Delegates
methods.brief: Adds the edge by which one actor may act as another, so trust passes along it.

parameters.name: pcFrom
parameters.role: the declared actor that delegates

parameters.name: pcTo
parameters.role: the declared actor that it may act as

methods.returns: the graph itself, so calls chain
warnings: raises an error when either node was not declared first

methods.name: References
methods.brief: Adds the edge by which a site refers to a secret.

parameters.name: pcSite
parameters.role: the declared site

parameters.name: pcSecret
parameters.role: the declared secret

methods.returns: the graph itself, so calls chain
warnings: raises an error when either node was not declared first

methods.name: StoredIn
methods.brief: Adds the edge by which a secret lives in a store.

parameters.name: pcSecret
parameters.role: the declared secret

parameters.name: pcStore
parameters.role: the declared store

methods.returns: the graph itself, so calls chain
warnings: raises an error when either node was not declared first

methods.name: MayAttach
methods.brief: TRUE if attaching a secret to that actor keeps the surface sound: the actor exists and was not declared sandboxed.

parameters.name: pcActor
parameters.role: the actor name

parameters.name: pcSecret
parameters.role: the secret name, which is not looked at

methods.returns: TRUE or FALSE; FALSE for an actor that is not in the graph
notes: it reads the recorded posture, so editing the graph through GraphQ does not change the answer

methods.name: AttachSecret
methods.brief: Adds the edge by which a live secret is attached to an actor, refusing it for a sandboxed actor.

parameters.name: pcActor
parameters.role: the declared actor

parameters.name: pcSecret
parameters.role: the declared secret

methods.returns: the graph itself, so calls chain
notes: the escalation never enters the graph through this door
warnings: raises an error for a sandboxed actor, and the refusal is noted to the security ledger as posture.refused; also raises when either node was not declared

methods.name: ReachesEffectful
methods.brief: TRUE if the actor can reach the effectful capability by any path: held, through a tool, or through a delegation.

parameters.name: pcActor
parameters.role: the actor name

methods.returns: TRUE or FALSE; FALSE for an actor that is not in the graph
notes: a flag check on the actor alone cannot see a path through a tool

methods.name: ReachesCapability
methods.brief: TRUE if the actor can reach the named capability by any path.

parameters.name: pcActor
parameters.role: the actor name

parameters.name: pcCapability
parameters.role: the capability name

methods.returns: TRUE or FALSE; FALSE when the actor or the capability is not in the graph

methods.name: PathToCapability
methods.brief: Returns the route by which the actor reaches a capability, shortest first, not just whether one exists.

parameters.name: pcActor
parameters.role: the actor name

parameters.name: pcCapability
parameters.role: the capability name

methods.returns: a list of node names from the actor to the capability; [ ] when there is no route or a node is unknown

methods.name: PathToEffectful
methods.brief: Returns the route by which the actor reaches the effectful capability.

parameters.name: pcActor
parameters.role: the actor name

methods.returns: a list of node names from the actor to effectful; [ ] when there is none

methods.name: CutCapability
methods.brief: Removes every path by which the actor reaches a capability, by deleting the actor own first-hop edges that lead there.

parameters.name: pcActor
parameters.role: the actor name

parameters.name: pcCapability
parameters.role: the capability name

methods.returns: a list of [ from, label, to ] rows, the edges removed; [ ] when there was nothing to cut
notes: other actors keep their own routes; a cut is noted to the ledger as capability.revoked

methods.name: BlastRadius
methods.brief: Returns every node that can reach the secret, which tells what a leak of it exposes.

parameters.name: pcSecret
parameters.role: the secret name

methods.returns: a list of node names, the secret itself excluded; [ ] for an unknown secret
notes: use it to plan a rotation

methods.name: AuditEscalations
methods.brief: Returns every sandboxed actor that can reach the effectful capability with its route, and records each one in the ledger.
methods.returns: a list of [ actor, [ path ] ] rows
notes: a deliberate audit, unlike the query methods, each finding is noted as graph.escalation_path_found

methods.name: NumberOfEscalations
methods.brief: Returns how many sandboxed actors can reach the effectful capability.
notes: it runs the audit, so each finding is noted to the ledger

methods.name: Violations
methods.brief: Returns the rule findings of the security surface, plus one for each posture changed around the gate.
methods.returns: a list of rows [ :rule, :subject, :where, :severity, :message ]; [ ] when sound

methods.name: IsSound
methods.brief: TRUE if the graph breaks no security rule and no posture was changed around the gate.

classes.name: stzSecurityLedger
classes.brief: Keeps security events as evidence: a bounded, hash-chained ring in the engine that can be made durable, anchored off the machine and sealed.
classes.description: Each entry's digest is the SHA-256 of the previous digest and the entry, computed in the engine and never handed in, so an edit to any entry breaks every digest after it and Verify names the first broken link. The ring forgets: past its capacity the oldest events give way, Count keeps counting and Size is what remains. PersistTo writes every event to an insert-only SQLite file and verifies it from the first entry on restart; an anchor sent off the machine shows a cut tail, which a chain alone cannot; SealTo exports a keyed file. A refused kind writes at most a budgeted number of lines per window, so a stranger cannot flush the evidence. The chain detects retroactive edits only, and protects nothing against an attacker already running code in the process. The pivots (OfActor, OfKind, Refusals, Since ...) return records rebuilt from the stored canonical line.
classes.example:
o1.Record(StzSecurityRefusal("auth.login.failed", "alice", "user:alice", "bad password"))
? o1.Count()
#--> 1
? o1.Verify()[:intact]
#--> 1

methods.name: init
methods.brief: Builds an empty ring ledger that keeps the newest pnCapacity events; a missing, non-numeric or sub-1 capacity gives 1024.

parameters.name: pnCapacity
parameters.role: how many events the ring keeps, at least 1

notes: the ring lives in the engine and is created at birth, so every copy of the ledger object reads and writes the same events

methods.name: Handle
methods.brief: Returns the engine handle of the ring, creating the ring again first if Destroy had freed it.
notes: StzOpenSecurityLedger passes this handle to the engine as the process ledger

methods.name: AdoptHandle
methods.brief: Binds this object to a ledger owned elsewhere, such as the process ledger, so both read and write the same events.

parameters.name: pEngineHandle
parameters.role: an engine ledger handle, as Handle gives

methods.returns: the ledger itself, so calls chain
notes: the ring this object made first is destroyed; Destroy later leaves an adopted handle alone, because its owner frees it

methods.name: Capacity
methods.brief: Returns how many events the ring can keep, as the engine reports it, even for an object bound to the process ledger.

methods.name: Record
methods.brief: Appends an event to the ring; the engine chains its digest to the previous one, so the caller never supplies a digest.

parameters.name: poEvent
parameters.role: the stzSecurityEvent to append

methods.returns: the ledger itself, so calls chain
notes: a refused kind is subject to the refusal budget and grants never are; past capacity the oldest event is evicted while Count keeps counting
warnings: raises an error when the ledger is durable and the disk write fails: the event is then in memory only

methods.name: AppendCanonical
methods.brief: Appends a canonical line as it is, with the wall time and severity code given, without building an event first.

parameters.name: pcCanonical
parameters.role: the twelve-field line as CanonicalString gives it

parameters.name: pnWallMs
parameters.role: the event time, in epoch milliseconds

parameters.name: pnSeverityCode
parameters.role: 0 for info, 1 for warning, 2 for error

methods.returns: the ledger itself, so calls chain
notes: the path that rebuilds a working ledger from a verified sealed file
warnings: the chain is recomputed here and does not carry the digests of the file the line came from; a line that is not canonical is accepted and reads back with empty fields

methods.name: PersistTo
methods.brief: Makes the ledger durable: later events are also written, in chain order, to an insert-only SQLite file that is checked first.

parameters.name: pcPath
parameters.role: the SQLite file to create or to resume

notes: call it before recording; after a restart the ring shows the newest window while Count carries the whole history (durable_ledger_narrated)
warnings: a ledger that already holds events, one that is already durable, an unreadable path and a stored history with an edited or missing row are all refused with :ok 0 and nothing is attached

methods.name: IsDurable
methods.brief: TRUE if PersistTo succeeded, so that every event is also written to a file.

methods.name: VerifyDurable
methods.brief: Checks the whole stored chain from the first entry, where Verify can only speak for the retained window.
notes: an edited or removed row shows; a cut tail does not, which is what Anchor is for
warnings: a ledger that is not durable answers :intact 0 with :brokenAt 0 and that message, so ask IsDurable first

methods.name: Count
methods.brief: Returns how many events were ever recorded, including those the ring has already evicted.

methods.name: Size
methods.brief: Returns how many events the ring still holds.
methods.returns: a number, never above the capacity

methods.name: Anchor
methods.brief: Returns the count and head digest of the ledger at this moment, with a one-line text to send off the machine.
notes: the line reads stzledger-anchor:v1: then the count, a colon and the 64-character digest (threat model R5)
warnings: an anchor kept only on the machine that holds the file proves nothing; an empty ledger gives count 0 and 64 zeros, which VerifyAgainstAnchor rejects as malformed in the list form

methods.name: VerifyAgainstAnchor
methods.brief: Checks the durable history against an anchor taken earlier: does the stored file still reach that count with that digest.

parameters.name: pAnchor
parameters.role: the list Anchor returned, or its :line text

notes: :state is holds, truncated, diverged, broken, not-durable, unreadable or malformed; truncated means the tail was cut and diverged means the history was rewritten (ledger_anchor_narrated); only a durable ledger can be checked

methods.name: SetRefusalBudget
methods.brief: Sets how many lines per time window each refused kind may write; past it the engine counts the refusals, writes one marker, then a summary.

parameters.name: pnMax
parameters.role: the lines each refused kind may write per window, 0 turns the budget off

parameters.name: pnWindowMs
parameters.role: the window length, in milliseconds

methods.returns: the ledger itself, so calls chain
notes: the default is 64 per 60000 ms; grants are never budgeted; the budget is counted per kind, so a flood of one kind cannot evict other evidence (ledger_flood_narrated)
warnings: a negative pnMax acts as 0 and turns the budget off, a negative window becomes 1 ms, and neither raises an error

methods.name: RefusalBudget
methods.brief: Returns the refusal budget now in force.
warnings: 64 and 60000 by default

methods.name: Suppressed
methods.brief: Returns how many refusals were counted instead of written, since the ledger was made.
warnings: a flush does not reset it

methods.name: FlushRefusalCounts
methods.brief: Closes every open budget window now and writes each count of suppressed refusals into the chain as one summary line.
methods.returns: the ledger itself, so calls chain
notes: the summary has the outcome observed and the actor ledger, and reads N further refusal(s) of this kind were counted; without a flush a window closes only when the next refusal of that kind arrives after it

methods.name: At
methods.brief: Returns the retained record at a 1-based position, oldest retained first, with its chain digest.

parameters.name: pnIndex
parameters.role: the position among the retained events, 1 is the oldest

methods.returns: a list of [ key, value ] pairs, or [ ] when the position is out of range
notes: the keys are kind, severity, actor, posture, action, risk, subject, origin, outcome, reason, atWall, traceId and digest; atMono, technique and actorKinds are not stored

methods.name: All
methods.brief: Returns every retained record, oldest first, each in the shape At gives.
methods.returns: a list of records; [ ] when the ledger is empty
notes: every call rebuilds the records from the stored lines, so on a large ledger keep the result instead of calling it in a loop

methods.name: Recent
methods.brief: Returns the newest records, the oldest of them first.

parameters.name: pnHowMany
parameters.role: how many records to take from the end

methods.returns: a list of records; all of them when pnHowMany exceeds the size, [ ] for 0 or less

methods.name: OfActor
methods.brief: Returns the retained records made by one actor.

parameters.name: pcActor
parameters.role: the actor name

notes: the match is exact and case-sensitive: ALICE does not find alice

methods.name: OfSubject
methods.brief: Returns the retained records about one subject descriptor.

parameters.name: pcSubject
parameters.role: the subject text the event stored, such as user:bob

methods.name: OfKind
methods.brief: Returns the retained records of one event kind.

parameters.name: pcKind
parameters.role: the event kind, a dotted catalog name

methods.name: OfTrace
methods.brief: Returns the retained records stamped with one trace id, which ties events to the log lines and spans of one request.

parameters.name: pcTraceId
parameters.role: the trace id, as text

notes: events recorded outside a trace scope carry an empty trace id, which this pivot finds when given an empty text

methods.name: OfOutcome
methods.brief: Returns the retained records that ended one way.

parameters.name: pcOutcome
parameters.role: granted, refused, failed or observed

notes: the match is exact and case-sensitive

methods.name: OfSeverity
methods.brief: Returns the retained records of one severity.

parameters.name: pcSeverity
parameters.role: info, warning or error

notes: the severity is the one stored with the event, which may be an override of the catalog default

methods.name: OfOrigin
methods.brief: Returns the retained records that came from one origin.

parameters.name: pcOrigin
parameters.role: the address, host or endpoint the event stored

notes: an empty text finds the events that carry no origin

methods.name: Refusals
methods.brief: Returns the retained records whose outcome is refused or failed, the signal to watch.
notes: granted and observed records are left out, so an expired session is never counted as a refusal

methods.name: Since
methods.brief: Returns the retained records at or after a wall time.

parameters.name: pnWallMs
parameters.role: the earliest event time, in epoch milliseconds, included

methods.name: Between
methods.brief: Returns the retained records inside a time range, both ends included.

parameters.name: pnFromMs
parameters.role: the start of the range, in epoch milliseconds

parameters.name: pnToMs
parameters.role: the end of the range, in epoch milliseconds

methods.returns: a list of records; [ ] when the start is after the end

methods.name: Digest
methods.brief: Returns the head digest, 64 hex characters, that commits to every event ever recorded, evicted ones included.
notes: an empty ledger answers 64 zeros

methods.name: DigestAt
methods.brief: Returns the chain digest stored with the retained entry at a position.

parameters.name: pnIndex
parameters.role: the position among the retained events, 1 is the oldest

methods.returns: a text; empty when the position is out of range

methods.name: Verify
methods.brief: Recomputes the chain over the retained window and names the first entry whose stored digest disagrees with it.
notes: it speaks for the retained window only: after eviction the first retained entry's predecessor is gone; chaining shows a retroactive edit and protects nothing against code already running in this process

methods.name: SealAttestedTo
methods.brief: Writes the retained window as a sealed file like SealTo, with a custody header that names who attested it and when.

parameters.name: pcPath
parameters.role: the file to write, overwritten

parameters.name: pcKey
parameters.role: the secret that keys the seal

parameters.name: pcAttestor
parameters.role: who vouches for the export, as text

methods.returns: the ledger itself, so calls chain
notes: the verifier reads the two lines back as attestor and attestedAt (I7)
warnings: the attestor and time lines sit outside the seal: editing them breaks nothing, so the verifier accepts a file whose attestor was changed after sealing

methods.name: SealTo
methods.brief: Writes the retained window to a file, one digest and canonical line per event, under a header holding the count and a keyed seal.

parameters.name: pcPath
parameters.role: the file to write, overwritten

parameters.name: pcKey
parameters.role: the secret that keys the HMAC seal, an empty text writes no seal

methods.returns: the ledger itself, so calls chain
notes: evidence-grade means exported: editing any line breaks the chain, and the seal needs the key to be made
warnings: StzVerifySealedLedger skips the seal check when the seal line is missing, so a tail cut that also deletes the seal line still verifies with the key

methods.name: ToOcsfNdJson
methods.brief: Returns the retained events as OCSF JSON objects, one per line, the stream form a collector ingests.
notes: each line is the stzSecurityEvent.ToOcsfJson of one record
warnings: the events are rebuilt from the stored record, so a severity override reads as the catalog default and an observed fact is exported as refused with status_id 2

methods.name: ToOcsfJson
methods.brief: Returns the retained events as one OCSF JSON array, the batch form.
notes: an empty ledger gives []
warnings: the events are rebuilt from the stored record, so a severity override reads as the catalog default and an observed fact is exported as refused with status_id 2

methods.name: ToOtelLogsJson
methods.brief: Returns the retained events as one OTLP logs envelope, the shape stzLog ships, so events and log lines reach one collector.
notes: the severity and outcome come from the stored record; trace ids are carried when present; the service name is softanza.security

methods.name: Explain
methods.brief: Returns the ledger told as lines of text: a header with the counts and the chain state, then one line per retained event.
notes: the header reads N event(s) recorded, M retained of C, chain intact or BROKEN at K

methods.name: Show
methods.brief: Prints the lines Explain returns, one per line.

methods.name: Reset
methods.brief: Empties the ring and restarts the chain, as a ledger made fresh.
methods.returns: the ledger itself, so calls chain
notes: the count and the digest start again from zero
warnings: raises an error for a durable ledger, whose chain continues on disk

methods.name: Destroy
methods.brief: Frees the engine ring; an object bound to the process ledger by AdoptHandle leaves it open.
methods.returns: the ledger itself, so calls chain
notes: the next call that needs the ring creates a fresh empty one, so a destroyed ledger is not a closed one

classes.name: stzSecurityPosture
classes.brief: Runs the security invariants over a project's surface, its secret store, its sites, its actors and its services, and reports findings.
classes.description: It turns the principle that expression is free and admission is governed into a check. The invariants are no-sandboxed-effectful (an error: a sandboxed actor that holds the effectful capability), inline-key, no-central-store and refused-accesses (warnings), and the findings of an attached service registry. Findings are [ :invariant, :severity, :where, :message ] with the severity written error or warn. IsSound means no error; IsClean means nothing flagged at all. The posture keeps a copy of everything handed to it, so describe the surface completely first and ask last.
classes.example:
o1.AddActor(LLMActor("planner"))
? o1.IsSound()
#--> 1

methods.name: init
methods.brief: Builds an empty posture audit of a project's security surface, with no store, no sites, no actors and no service registry.

parameters.name: pcName
parameters.role: the project's name, shown in the report and in findings

methods.name: SetStore
methods.brief: Sets the project's central secret store, so the audit can see its refused reveals and tell a store-backed site from an inline key.

parameters.name: poStore
parameters.role: the stzSecretStore of the project

methods.returns: the posture itself, so calls chain
notes: without a store, secret-bearing sites raise the no-central-store warning
warnings: the posture keeps a COPY of the store: reveals refused after this call are not seen, so set the store last, just before asking

methods.name: AddSite
methods.brief: Adds a deployment site to audit for a secret it holds inline instead of through the store.

parameters.name: poSite
parameters.role: the stzDeploymentSite to audit

methods.returns: the posture itself, so calls chain
notes: an inline secret raises the inline-key warning
warnings: the posture keeps a COPY of the site

methods.name: AddActor
methods.brief: Adds an actor to audit for the load-bearing rule that a sandboxed actor must never hold the effectful capability.

parameters.name: poActor
parameters.role: the actor to audit, such as HumanActor or LLMActor

methods.returns: the posture itself, so calls chain
notes: a sandboxed actor that holds effectful is an ERROR finding
warnings: the posture keeps a COPY of the actor: a posture or capability changed after this call is not seen

methods.name: SetServices
methods.brief: Attaches the project's service registry, so findings about fakes and unbound services join the same audit.

parameters.name: poReg
parameters.role: the stzServiceRegistry of the project

methods.returns: the posture itself, so calls chain
notes: the audit asks the registry in the production frame and restores its phase, so a sandbox still bound is reported while there is time to act

methods.name: ServicesQ
methods.brief: Returns the attached service registry.
methods.returns: the stzServiceRegistry, or an empty text when none was attached

methods.name: HasServices
methods.brief: TRUE if a service registry was attached with SetServices.

methods.name: Findings
methods.brief: Runs every invariant over the described surface and returns the findings as one flat list.
methods.returns: a list of [ :invariant, :severity, :where, :message ] findings; [ ] when nothing is flagged
notes: the severity is the symbol error or warn, not the word warning that stzDetection uses; the findings are recomputed at each call

methods.name: IsSound
methods.brief: TRUE if no finding is an error; warnings are advisory and do not block.

methods.name: IsClean
methods.brief: TRUE if nothing at all is flagged, neither an error nor a warning.

methods.name: NumberOfFindings
methods.brief: Returns how many findings the audit raises, errors and warnings together.

methods.name: NumberOf
methods.brief: Returns how many findings have one severity.

parameters.name: pcSeverity
parameters.role: error or warn, as the findings spell it

notes: NumberOf(:error) and NumberOf(:warn) are the two that count
warnings: warning does not match: the findings say warn, so NumberOf with the word warning answers 0, and the match is case-sensitive

methods.name: Report
methods.brief: Prints a verdict line for the project, then one line per finding with its severity, invariant, place and message.
notes: the verdict reads SOUND or UNSOUND (errors present)

classes.name: stzSecurityRule
classes.brief: Holds one security invariant over a security graph as a declared rule, in the security domain.
classes.description: A security rule is a stzGraphRule whose domain is security. Unlike the posture checks, which look at one node, these rules run over a whole stzSecurityGraph and see paths, such as an actor that can reach a capability through a tool or a delegate. The library's rules are declared in stzSecurityRuleSet.
classes.example:
? o1.Name()
#--> sandboxed-reaches-effectful
? o1.Domain()
#--> security

methods.name: init
methods.brief: Builds a security rule of that name in the security domain; it is a graph rule over a security graph.

parameters.name: pcName
parameters.role: the rule's name

classes.name: stzSecurityRuleSet
classes.brief: Holds the security invariants that see paths in a security graph, so an escalation by any route is caught, not only a direct grant.
classes.description: Three rules are loaded. sandboxed-reaches-effectful finds a sandboxed actor that can reach the effectful capability by any path, though it holds none itself. sandboxed-holds-secret finds a sandboxed actor attached to a live secret. unstored-secret finds a secret that a site references but that lives in no store, so its reveals are unaudited. Each rule governs only the nodes it is about, so a clean report can tell no sandboxed actor can reach an effect from there is no sandboxed actor.
classes.example:
? o1.Name()
#--> security-invariants
? o1.NumberOfRules()
#--> 3
? o1.RuleNames()[1]
#--> sandboxed-reaches-effectful

methods.name: init
methods.brief: Builds the security-invariants rule set, already loaded with its three rules.
notes: the rules are sandboxed-reaches-effectful, sandboxed-holds-secret and unstored- secret

classes.name: stzSecuritySentinel
classes.brief: Watches a security ledger on a cadence and raises an alert only when a detection starts or stops firing.
classes.description: A detection set judges when asked; the sentinel asks and turns the change of verdict into alerts. A detection is identified by its where text, so one account still under attack is not a new alert at each pass, and a returning attack, after a real clear, fires again. Each start records a case, a snapshot holding the finding, the ledger's head digest and the events nearest the firing; each start and clear is logged in the sentinel's own bounded log and announced on two process-wide event-bus channels. It runs three ways: Check on demand, Tick from any loop, or Cycle under an agent host. It reads the ledger and never writes into it. Test it on an in-memory ledger with invented events.
classes.example:
oLed = StzSecurityLedger(64)
o1.Watching(oLed)
? o1.Check()
#--> 0
for i = 1 to 5
	oE = StzSecurityEvent("auth.login.failed")
	oE.ByActorNamed("victim", "external")
	oE.About("user:victim")
	oE.Refused("scripted")
	oE.OccurredAt(1785600000000 + (i * 3000))
	oLed.Record(oE)
next
? o1.Check()
#--> 1
? o1.ActiveDetections()[1]
#--> credential-stuffing/victim
? o1.Check()
#--> 0
oLed.Destroy()

methods.name: init
methods.brief: Builds a sentinel that judges the ledger with the given detection set.

parameters.name: poDetectionSet
parameters.role: the detection set whose findings the sentinel turns into alerts, such as the one StzDefaultDetectionSet returns

notes: without Watching, the process-wide ledger is the one watched

methods.name: Name
methods.brief: Returns the sentinel's name, security-sentinel until it is renamed.

methods.name: Name_
methods.brief: Returns the sentinel's name, the way an agent host asks for it.

methods.name: SetName
methods.brief: Gives the sentinel a name, which an agent host uses to tell its agents apart.

parameters.name: pcName
parameters.role: the new name

methods.returns: the sentinel itself, so calls chain

methods.name: Watching
methods.brief: Points the sentinel at a given ledger instead of the process-wide one.

parameters.name: poLedger
parameters.role: the ledger to judge on every check

methods.returns: the sentinel itself, so calls chain

methods.name: OnDetection
methods.brief: Sets the function called once for each detection that starts firing.

parameters.name: pfCallback
parameters.role: a function that receives the finding, a hash list with the keys rule, severity, where and message

methods.returns: the sentinel itself, so calls chain
notes: a detection already firing does not call it again until it has cleared

methods.name: OnClear
methods.brief: Sets the function called once for each detection that stops firing.

parameters.name: pfCallback
parameters.role: a function that receives the where text of the detection that cleared

methods.returns: the sentinel itself, so calls chain

methods.name: SetChannels
methods.brief: Sets the two event-bus channels on which firings and clearings are announced.

parameters.name: pcDetection
parameters.role: the channel name for a detection that starts

parameters.name: pcClear
parameters.role: the channel name for one that clears

methods.returns: the sentinel itself, so calls chain
notes: the defaults are sec.detection and sec.clear; the channels are process-wide, so other code can wait on them

methods.name: DetectionChannel
methods.brief: Returns the event-bus channel on which new detections are announced.

methods.name: ClearChannel
methods.brief: Returns the event-bus channel on which cleared detections are announced.

methods.name: Every
methods.brief: Sets the cadence of Tick, in milliseconds.

parameters.name: pnMs
parameters.role: the minimum time between two ticks that check

methods.returns: the sentinel itself, so calls chain
notes: the default is 1000

methods.name: Check
methods.brief: Judges the ledger once and fires only what changed since the last pass: new detections start, ended ones clear.
methods.returns: a number, how many detections started firing in this pass
notes: the identity of a detection is its where text, such as credential- stuffing/victim, so two accounts under attack are two alerts and one account still under attack is not a new alert; each start also records a case

methods.name: Tick
methods.brief: Checks the ledger when the cadence says it is due, and does nothing before.
methods.returns: a number, how many detections started firing, or 0 when the tick was not due
notes: the clock is monotonic, so a change of the wall clock does not disturb it

methods.name: CheckCount
methods.brief: Returns how many passes have judged the ledger.

methods.name: ActiveDetections
methods.brief: Returns the where text of every detection that is firing now.
methods.returns: a list of texts, empty when quiet

methods.name: IsFiring
methods.brief: TRUE if at least one detection is firing.

methods.name: AlertLog
methods.brief: Returns the sentinel's own log of starts and clears, oldest first.
methods.returns: a list of entries, each a list of the monotonic time in milliseconds, the kind detection or clear, the where text and the message
notes: the log keeps the newest 256 entries; it is not written to the ledger, so detections over detections cannot feed back

methods.name: LastAlert
methods.brief: Returns the newest entry of the alert log, or an empty list when nothing has fired.
methods.returns: a list of time, kind, where and message

methods.name: Cases
methods.brief: Returns the snapshots taken when detections started firing, oldest first.
methods.returns: a list of hash lists, each with the keys at, where, rule, severity, message, ledgercount, headdigest and recent
notes: only the newest 16 are kept; the keys are lower case: ledgercount, headdigest

methods.name: LastCase
methods.brief: Returns the newest case snapshot, or an empty list when nothing has fired.
methods.returns: a hash list with the keys at, where, rule, severity, message, ledgercount, headdigest and recent
notes: headdigest is a 64-character digest committing to the whole ledger history at that moment, and recent holds the events nearest the firing

methods.name: Explain
methods.brief: Returns the sentinel's state as lines of text: its name, its check count and one line for each firing detection.

methods.name: Show
methods.brief: Prints the lines of Explain.

classes.name: stzSelfDoc
classes.brief: Lets a class describe itself: it reads the methods and doc blocks from the source, then answers plain-English questions and explains each method.
classes.description: The knowledge already lives in the library; this indexes it. A class is read by name, with every method it inherits, or by the path of its source file. ExplainMethod and RecordOf say only what the author wrote in the doc block and what the tests show. Ask ranks the methods by meaning, a word match first with a loaded embedding or reranker model as a rescue, deterministic and with no generation. HowTo goes from an intent to a call template. Retrieval is by shared words, so check the answer when two methods share the question's words.
classes.example:
? o1.NumberOfMethods()
#--> 9
? o1.HasMethod("apply")
#--> 1
? o1.DefiningClassOf("Apply")
#--> stzAgentSkill
? o1.BestMethodFor("run the action only when the precondition holds")
#--> Apply
? o1.RecordOf("Kind")[:returns]
#--> the text pi or llm

methods.name: init
methods.brief: Reads a class's methods and doc blocks from its source, including the ones it inherits, so it can answer questions about them.

parameters.name: pcTarget
parameters.role: a class name, or the path of a .ring file for the class it names

notes: a path harvests only that file's class, with no inherited methods
warnings: anything that is not a text raises an error; an unknown class name builds an object with no methods

methods.name: ClassName
methods.brief: Returns the class the object describes.

methods.name: Source
methods.brief: Returns the path of the source file the class was found in.
methods.returns: a text; empty when the class is unknown

methods.name: NumberOfMethods
methods.brief: Returns how many methods were harvested, own and inherited.

methods.name: MethodNames
methods.brief: Returns the names of the harvested methods, in source order.

methods.name: HasMethod
methods.brief: TRUE if the class has a method of that name, own or inherited; case is ignored.

parameters.name: pcName
parameters.role: the method name

methods.name: DescriptionOf
methods.brief: Returns the brief written above a method.

parameters.name: pcName
parameters.role: the method name, in any case

methods.returns: a text; empty for an unknown method or an undocumented one

methods.name: DefiningClassOf
methods.brief: Returns the class that defines a method: this class or an ancestor it inherits from.

parameters.name: pcName
parameters.role: the method name

methods.returns: a text; empty for an unknown method

methods.name: NumberOfInheritedMethods
methods.brief: Returns how many harvested methods are defined by an ancestor and not by the class itself.

methods.name: ExplainMethod
methods.brief: Explains a method in plain words: its brief, parameter roles, return, notes, see-also, example and the form its name implies.

parameters.name: pcName
parameters.role: the method name

methods.returns: a multi-line text; a sentence saying the method is absent for an unknown name
notes: everything is read from what the author wrote and from the tests; nothing is invented or generated

methods.name: RecordOf
methods.brief: Returns what the author wrote in a method's doc block, field by field.

parameters.name: pcName
parameters.role: the method name

classes.name: stzSemanticIndex
classes.brief: Searches texts by meaning: each text is stored with an embedding and a query returns the closest ones by cosine score.
classes.description: Texts are embedded when they are added, with whatever sentence-embedding model the engine holds (AddText), or the caller brings the vectors (AddEmbedded). Vectors are kept resident in the engine so a search crosses only the query. The search is exact, not approximate, and the reported score is the cosine for unit vectors. SearchByVectorXT needs no model at all; Search and Closest embed the query text, so they need one. Call Close when done.
classes.example:
? o1.Count()
#--> 2
? o1.SearchByVectorXT([ 0, 1, 0 ], 1)[1][1]
#--> north
? o1.EmbeddingDim()
#--> 3

methods.name: init
methods.brief: Builds an index, embedding and adding each text of the list when one is given.

parameters.name: paTexts
parameters.role: a list of texts to index now, or an empty list

warnings: a non-empty list needs a loaded embedding model, and raises AddText: no embedding model is loaded without one

methods.brief: Embeds a text with the model the engine holds and stores both; the model must be loaded already.

parameters.name: pcText
parameters.role: the text to index, not empty

methods.returns: the index itself, so calls chain

methods.brief: Stores a text with an embedding the caller already has, so no model is needed; the vector must have unit length.

parameters.name: pcText
parameters.role: the text to index

parameters.name: paVec
parameters.role: its embedding, a list of numbers of the index's size and of norm 1

methods.returns: the index itself, so calls chain
notes: the norm is not checked, and the score is only a cosine for unit vectors
warnings: raises for an empty text, an empty vector and a size different from the first one

methods.name: AddTexts
methods.brief: Adds each text of a list with AddText.

parameters.name: paTexts
parameters.role: the list of texts

methods.returns: the index itself, so calls chain

methods.brief: Returns how many texts the index holds.

methods.brief: Returns the indexed texts in the order they were added.

methods.name: SearchByVectorXT
methods.brief: Returns the n texts closest in meaning to a query embedding, best first, each with its cosine score and position.

parameters.name: paQ
parameters.role: the query embedding, of the index's size

parameters.name: n
parameters.role: how many hits to return, 1 or more

methods.returns: a list of [ text, cosine, position ] rows; [ ] for an empty index

notes: the score is 1 for the same meaning, near 0 for unrelated texts

classes.name: stzSequence
classes.brief: Generates numbers one by one from a start and a step, counting on, repeating between bounds or bouncing between them.
classes.description: Build one with new stzSequence(name, start, step, mode); the counter lives in the engine under its name, so give each sequence its own name and call Destroy when finished. Modes are 0 (count on without end), 1 (repeat between the bounds set by SetBounds) and 2 (bounce between them). NextValue answers the value it stands on and then moves, so the first call gives the start. Values are whole numbers: a fraction in the start or the step is cut silently.
classes.example:
? o1.NextValue()
#--> 10
? o1.Current()
#--> 15
? @@( o1.NextNValues(3) )
#--> [ 15, 20, 25 ]
o1.Reset()
? o1.Iteration()
#--> 0
o1.Destroy()

methods.name: init
methods.brief: Creates a named number sequence in the engine, from a start value, a step and a mode: 0 counts on, 1 repeats, 2 bounces.

parameters.name: cName
parameters.role: the unique name of the sequence, a non-empty text

parameters.name: nStart
parameters.role: the first value

parameters.name: nStep
parameters.role: the amount added each time

parameters.name: nMode
parameters.role: 0 for step, 1 for repeat, 2 for bounce

methods.returns: nothing; the sequence now exists in the engine under its name
notes: the engine keeps the sequence until Destroy; a second object built with a name already in use shares that counter and its own start and step are ignored (start 100 on a counter standing at 20 still answers 20)
warnings: A start or a step that has a fraction is silently cut to a whole number: start 2.5 gives 2, step 0.5 gives 0 so the value never moves, step 1.5 gives 1; a name that is empty or a value that is not a number raises an error

methods.name: Name
methods.brief: Returns the name the sequence was created with.

methods.name: SetBounds
methods.brief: Sets the lowest and highest values a repeating or bouncing sequence moves between.

parameters.name: nMin
parameters.role: the lowest value

parameters.name: nMax
parameters.role: the highest value

notes: bounds act in modes 1 and 2 only: a mode-0 sequence given bounds 2 and 4 from 1 still counts 1 to 5; mode 1 with bounds 1 to 3 gives 1 2 3 1 2 3 and mode 2 gives 1 2 3 2 1 2 3 2

extensions.name: SetBoundsQ
extensions.adds: does what the method does, then returns the object, so the call can be chained

methods.name: NextValue
methods.brief: Returns the value the sequence stands on and then moves it by one step, so the first call answers the start.
notes: Advance is the same method; Current shows the value the next call will return

methods.name: Current
methods.brief: Returns the value the next NextValue will return, without moving the sequence.
notes: Value is the same method; after Destroy it answers 0

methods.name: Iteration
methods.brief: Returns how many times the sequence has been moved since its creation or last Reset.
notes: IterationNumber is the same method

methods.name: NextNValues
methods.brief: Returns the next n values in order and moves the sequence n steps.

parameters.name: n
parameters.role: how many values to take, at least 1

notes: n below 1 raises "Incorrect param! n must be a positive number."

methods.name: Reset
methods.brief: Puts the sequence back at its start value and its iteration count at 0, keeping its bounds.

extensions.name: ResetQ
extensions.adds: does what the method does, then returns the object, so the call can be chained

methods.name: Destroy
methods.brief: Removes the sequence from the engine, which Ring cannot do by itself.
notes: afterwards Current and NextValue answer 0 and SetBounds is silent: do not use the object again

classes.name: stzServiceRegistry
classes.brief: Holds the services a solution depends on and what serves each, so that a fake can be refused when the solution ships.
classes.description: Application code asks the registry for a service by name, never for an implementation, and the phase decides what is in place: a sandbox that captures mail or a local database while programming, a hosted adapter at deploy. Because the whole outside surface is declared in one place it can be listed and judged: Findings names what is unbound, what is still a fake in a production phase, what is a local source that vanishes on restart, and what is live without its credential in the secret store, and IsSound says whether any of that is an error. Each binding carries a posture read off the object itself (sandbox, local, live or conformance), and an object that says nothing is taken as live so that production does not excuse it. The registry holds the NAME of a credential, never the credential. The payments binding comes second. The library ships one live adapter for a payment hub, stzPispiHttpAdapter, and it is UNPERCEIVED: it is proven against the twin served over real HTTP, plain and with mutual TLS, and has NOT been run against the BCEAO's sandbox. No payment made through it has been watched landing in a real dashboard, so a registry that judges it sound has judged the declared surface and not the service. BindLive, BindConformance and BindLiveWithCertificate carry the same status in their notes. The twin and the BCEAO's sandbox are refused in production (sandbox-in-production, conformance-in-production), and so is a payments port told to skip the payout plan. The payments guide, docs/payments-guide.md, is the desk's own account.
classes.example:
o1.Declare(:mail)
o1.Bind(:mail, new stzMailSandbox())
? o1.PostureOf(:mail)
#--> sandbox
? o1.SetPhaseQ(:production).IsSound()
#--> 0

classes.brief: Holds one rule about the services a solution depends on, as a declared graph rule in the services domain.
classes.description: A service rule is a stzGraphRule whose domain is services. It runs over a graph that joins the delivery model (parts and their destinations) with the service registry (services and their postures), so it can ask which part of the solution depends on a fake. The rules are declared in stzServiceRuleSet.

? o1.Name()
#--> production-part-uses-sandbox
? o1.Domain()
#--> services

classes.name: stzServiceRuleSet
classes.brief: Holds the rules that ask which part of a solution would ship on a fake service, read from each part's destination.
classes.description: Four rules are loaded, deliberately few, since the registry already checks its own invariants and restating them would let two copies drift. The first three are errors: a part bound to a real site that depends on a sandbox double, on a store that lasts only until the next restart, or on a protocol conformance double. The fourth, a warning, finds a part that declares a need the registry has never heard of. They read a part's destination, so they fire while the phase is still development, as a rehearsal of if I shipped this today.
classes.example:
? o1.Name()
#--> service-invariants
? o1.NumberOfRules()
#--> 4
? o1.RuleNames()[4]
#--> part-uses-undeclared-service

classes.name: stzSet
classes.brief: Holds a list without repeats, a mathematical set, and gives its union, intersection and difference with other lists.
classes.description: A set is built with new stzSet(aList) or StzSetQ(aList) and drops every repeated item on the way in, keeping the first of each; case counts, so a and A are two elements. It is a stzList underneath, so the stzList methods are available on it, and stzListFlattener.ToStzSet hands one back. UnionWith, IntersectionWith and DifferenceWith return a plain list and leave the set as it was, their Q form wrapping the answer in a new stzSet; UnifyWith and the Update family change the set in place. A bad argument raises the class's own message (stzSetError). Subsets and SubSetsOfNElements list the subsets by size, then by the position of their items, and NumberOfSubsets counts them without listing them; listing is refused beyond 65536 subsets. AddElement only accepts a list element; Includes and Contains take a list of elements and cannot test one item; Updated simply returns its argument. Hebrew, Arabic and emoji elements are kept like any other text.
classes.example:
? @@( o1.Content() )
#--> [ 3, 1, 2 ]
? @@( o1.UnionWith([ 5, 4 ]) )
#--> [ 3, 1, 2, 5, 4 ]
? @@( o1.IntersectionWith([ 2, 3, 9 ]) )
#--> [ 3, 2 ]
? @@( o1.DifferenceWith([ 2, 9 ]) )
#--> [ 3, 1 ]
? o1.Includes([ 1, 2 ])
#--> 1
? o1.IsIncludedIn([ 1, 2, 3, 4 ])
#--> 1
o2 = new stzSet([ "שלום", "😀", "שלום" ])
? o2.NumberOfElements()
#--> 2
