methods.name: Subsets
methods.brief: Returns every subset of the set, the empty one and the set itself included, smallest first.
notes: a set of n items has 2^n subsets. They come by size, 0 items first, and within one size in the order of the positions of their items, [ 1, 2 ] before [ 1, 3 ] before [ 2, 3 ]; each subset keeps the order of the set and holds the items themselves, unchanged. The empty set answers [ [ ] ]
warnings: more than 65536 subsets, which means a set of more than 16 items, raises the message "Can't list the subsets!"; NumberOfSubsets counts them without listing

methods.name: SubSetsOfNElements
methods.brief: Returns the subsets of the set that hold exactly n items, in the order of their positions.

parameters.name: n
parameters.role: how many items each subset holds, a whole number from 0

notes: the order is the one of Subsets: [ 1, 2 ] before [ 1, 3 ] before [ 2, 3 ]. A size of 0 answers [ [ ] ], and a size larger than the set answers [ ]
warnings: a negative or fractional size, or a value that is not a number, raises the message "Can't list the subsets of a given size!"; more than 65536 subsets raise the message of Subsets

methods.name: NumberOfSubsets
methods.brief: Returns how many subsets the set has, counted without listing them.
methods.returns: a number, 2 to the power of the number of items
notes: the empty set has 1, and a set of 3 items has 8; the answer is exact, because a power of 2 is held exactly, and it equals the length of what Subsets lists
warnings: a set of more than 1023 items raises the message "Can't count the subsets!"

classes.name: stzSimilarity
classes.brief: Measures how alike two vectors are: cosine similarity, Euclidean and Manhattan distance, dot product, and the length and unit form of one vector.
classes.description: Build one with new stzSimilarity() or StzSimilarityQ(); it holds nothing, so it is a bundle of calculations done in the Zig engine. The methods ending in 3 take six numbers, for two 3-component vectors; the ones ending in FromLists, and their short names Cosine, Euclidean, Manhattan and Dot, take two lists of any length, 1,536 for a sentence embedding included, and refuse lists of different lengths. The global functions CosineSimilarity3, EuclideanDistance3, ManhattanDistance3 and DotProduct3 do the 3-component case without an object. Cosine is 1 for the same direction, 0 for perpendicular, -1 for opposite.
classes.example:
? o1.CosineFromLists([ 1, 0 ], [ 0, 1 ])
#--> 0
? o1.EuclideanFromLists([ 0, 0 ], [ 3, 4 ])
#--> 5
? o1.DotProductFromLists([ 1, 2 ], [ 3, 4 ])
#--> 11
? o1.MagnitudeOf([ 3, 4 ])
#--> 5

classes.name: stzSla
classes.brief: Holds the expectations a service must meet, stated in operational terms, and judges them against measured numbers.
classes.description: An SLA is part of the design and not a dashboard threshold added after an incident. Expect names a well-known subject, response time percentiles, throughput, error rate, availability, CPU, memory, and a closer, Under, AtMost, AtLeast or Over, gives the bound; ExpectP95, ExpectMean, ExpectValue, ExpectRate and ExpectStable do the same for a metric of your own. CheckAgainst judges them against a stzPerfMonitor and returns the breaches as findings in the unified shape, subject perf, ready for stzRuleReport. An expectation over a metric the monitor does not carry is an error finding, never a silent pass. AsWarning softens the last expectation to advice. Judged values that depend on the clock, rates and CPU, should be asserted by range.
classes.receiver: oMon = StzPerfMonitor("api") oT = oMon.NewTimer("http.request.ms") oT.Record(20) oT.Record(40) oT.Record(60) oT.Record(80) oT.Record(400) oReq = oMon.NewCounter("http.requests") oReq.IncrementBy(200) oErr = oMon.NewCounter("http.errors") oErr.IncrementBy(1) oDepth = oMon.NewGauge("queue.depth") oDepth.Set(120) o1 = StzSla("restolean-api") o1.Expect(:ResponseTimeP95).Under(200) o1.Expect(:ResponseTimeP50).AtMost(100) o1.Expect(:Availability).AtLeast(99.9) o1.ExpectValue("queue.depth").AtMost(100)
classes.example:
? o1.NumberOfExpectations()
#--> 4
aF = o1.CheckAgainst(oMon)
? len(aF)
#--> 3
? aF[1][:rule]
#--> response-time-p95-under-200
? aF[1][:message]
#--> response-time-p95-under-200: measured 400 (must be <= 200)
? o1.Verdicts()[2][:ok]
#--> 1
? o1.Passed()
#--> 0
? o1.BreachCount()
#--> 3

notes: the rule is named from the subject, the closer and the bound, such as response- time-p95-under-200; AtMost is the same call
warnings: closing when nothing is open raises error stzSla: no open expectation to close -- say Expect(...) first

methods.name: AtMost
methods.brief: Closes the open expectation: it passes when the measured value is at most the bound.

parameters.name: pnBound
parameters.role: the largest value that passes

methods.returns: the SLA itself, so calls chain
notes: the same call as Under
warnings: closing when nothing is open raises error stzSla: no open expectation to close

methods.name: AtLeast
methods.brief: Closes the open expectation: it passes when the measured value is at least the bound.

parameters.name: pnBound
parameters.role: the smallest value that passes, such as 99.9 for an availability in percent

methods.returns: the SLA itself, so calls chain
notes: the rule name carries atleast; Over is the same call
warnings: closing when nothing is open raises error stzSla: no open expectation to close

methods.name: Over
methods.brief: Closes the open expectation: it passes when the measured value is at least the bound.

parameters.name: pnBound
parameters.role: the smallest value that passes

methods.returns: the SLA itself, so calls chain
notes: the same call as AtLeast, so the bound itself passes
warnings: closing when nothing is open raises error stzSla: no open expectation to close

methods.name: AsWarning
methods.brief: Softens the last closed expectation to an advisory one, which does not fail the gate.
methods.returns: the SLA itself, so calls chain
notes: its findings carry the severity warning, which stzRuleReport.IsSound ignores; Passed and BreachCount still count them
warnings: calling it before any expectation is closed raises error stzSla.AsWarning: no expectation closed yet

methods.name: NumberOfExpectations
methods.brief: Returns how many expectations have been closed.
methods.returns: a number; an expectation still open is not counted

methods.name: CheckAgainst
methods.brief: Judges every expectation against the monitor's measured numbers and returns the breaches.

parameters.name: poMonitor
parameters.role: the stzPerfMonitor whose metrics are read

methods.returns: a list of findings in the unified shape, each a hash list with rule, subject perf, where, severity and message; [ ] when everything is met
notes: the finding is ready for stzRuleReport.Ingest; where reads the SLA name, a slash, and the metric; a call replaces the verdicts of the call before
warnings: an expectation over a metric the monitor does not carry is an error finding whose message says NOT MEASURED and what to watch, never a pass

methods.name: Findings
methods.brief: Returns the breaches of the last check again, in the unified shape, without measuring anything.
methods.returns: a list of findings; [ ] before any check or when all were met

methods.name: Verdicts
methods.brief: Returns the verdict of every expectation from the last check, the passes too.
methods.returns: a list of hash lists with the keys rule, ok, actual, bound and message
notes: an unmeasured expectation has ok 0 and actual 0

methods.name: Passed
methods.brief: TRUE if the last check found no breach, of any severity.
methods.returns: TRUE or FALSE, as 1 or 0; 1 before any check
notes: an advisory breach makes it 0 though the gate stays sound: with only a warning it answered 0 while stzRuleReport.IsSound answered 1

methods.name: BreachCount
methods.brief: Returns how many expectations breached in the last check.
methods.returns: a number, the advisory ones and the not-measured ones included

methods.name: Explain
methods.brief: Returns the last check as lines of text: a verdict line, then each expectation marked MET or BREACH with its message.
notes: the first line gives the number of expectations and MET or BREACHED with the count

methods.name: Show
methods.brief: Prints the explanation to the console, one line per line.
notes: it prints with the ? statement

classes.name: stzSLARuleBase
classes.brief: Holds the two service-level rules of a business process and judges a workflow against them.
classes.description: The set, named SLA Compliance in the sla domain, carries sla_defined, which wants a step marked critical to have an sla above 0, and sla_compliance, which flags a step whose duration exceeds its sla. A step with no sla is outside the second rule. Check(oWorkflow) answers the findings in the house shape.
classes.receiver: oWf = new stzWorkflow("order") oWf.AddStepXT("pack", "Pack") oWf.SetStepDuration("pack", 30) oWf.SetStepSLA("pack", 20) o1 = new stzSLARuleBase()
classes.example:
? o1.Name()
#--> SLA Compliance
? len(o1.Rules())
#--> 2
? o1.Check(oWf)[1][:rule]
#--> sla_compliance
? o1.Check(oWf)[1][:message]
#--> duration 30 exceeds SLA 20: pack

methods.name: init
methods.brief: Builds the set of two service-level rules, in the SLA Compliance set.
notes: the rules are sla_defined, which wants a critical step to have an sla above 0, and sla_compliance, which flags a step whose duration exceeds its sla; Check(oWorkflow) answers the findings

classes.name: stzSmsSandbox
classes.brief: Captures text messages instead of sending them, validates the number, and counts the billable segments a carrier would charge.
classes.description: A capture sink with the shape of stzMailSandbox, whose point is the bill. SMS is charged per segment, and the segment count depends on the alphabet: text within the GSM 7-bit alphabet takes 160 characters in one segment and 153 per part, and one character outside it, such as an Arabic letter or an emoji, makes the whole message UCS-2 with 70 and 67; nine characters of the extension table cost two septets each. Send names the encoding and the segments, and TotalSegments lets a test assert the cost. Numbers must be E.164. An outage is refused and recorded nowhere, while a bad number is rejected, so retrying and fixing the data are told apart. The honest limit: a sink shows what you would have sent, not that a carrier would accept it. The outbox is shared by copies of the object.
classes.example:
? o1.Send("+22790123456", "Your code is 482910")[:segments]
#--> 1
? o1.LastEncoding()
#--> gsm7
? o1.Send("+22790123456", "Salut, code 482910 😀")[:encoding]
#--> ucs2
? o1.Send("0612345678", "hi")[:status]
#--> rejected
? o1.TotalSegments()
#--> 2
? o1.WasSentTo("+22790123456")
#--> 1

classes.name: stzSortedList
classes.brief: Holds a list that stays sorted: it sorts at creation and every item added goes to its place.
classes.description: Build one with new stzSortedList(aList) or StzSortedListQ(aList); it is a stzList, so every list method also works on the sorted content (Content, NumberOfItems, Contains ...). Numbers sort before texts; texts sort by character code, so "Apple" comes before "apple", which comes before "banana". Add, Append and the + operator insert one item at its place. The Q forms AddQ and AppendQ do not insert today.
classes.example:
? @@( o1.Content() )
#--> [ 1, 2, 5, 9 ]
o1.Add(4)
? @@( o1.Content() )
#--> [ 1, 2, 4, 5, 9 ]
o2 = new stzSortedList([ "pear", "Apple", "שלום" ])
? @@( o2.Content() )
#--> [ "Apple", "pear", "שלום" ]

classes.name: stzSound
classes.brief: Holds a buffer of audio samples that you can load, inspect, change, analyse and save as a WAV file.
classes.description: The buffer lives in the sound engine and carries its own sample rate and channel count, so a saved file and a reloaded file keep the rate they were made at. The plain form of a verb acts and returns nothing; the Q twin does the same and returns the sound, so a chain never leaves it. Readers such as Duration, Peak and Rms return data, and the To... analysis methods return stzSoundGrid objects of numbers, never pictures. Play and PlayFor open an audio device and block until the sound ends; they are the only methods here that do. The sound has not been heard by a person (UNPERCEIVED): the examples are checked by frame count, sample rate, peak level and duration, not by listening.
classes.example:
? o1.Frames()
#--> 24000
? o1.SampleRate()
#--> 48000
? o1.Duration()
#--> 0.50
o1.SetSampleAt(10, 1, 0.5)
? o1.Peak()
#--> 0.50

classes.name: stzSoundFormantVoice
classes.brief: Sings the five vowels at a pitch with a formant voice built in the engine, a glottal pulse through five resonators.
classes.description: The voice is a Rosenberg glottal pulse through formant resonators taken from the Csound tenor and soprano tables, and holds a pitch to a fraction of a cent. Vowel gives one vowel at a note, VowelGlide a gliding pitch, VowelsQ a line of vowels at a tempo. It sings vowels only: a consonant needs a model or the neural tier. Sing is present and gated by StzSoundSingingVerdict, and refuses while the formant voice is recorded as UNPERCEIVED. Everything is rendered to memory and checked by frame count, sample rate, peak and measured pitch; no audio device is opened. It has not been heard by a person (UNPERCEIVED), so whether it reads as a voice is not claimed.
classes.example:
? oV.SampleRate()
#--> 48000
? oV.Frames()
#--> 79200
? oV.Peak() > 0.1 and oV.Peak() <= 1
#--> 1
? abs(StzEngineSoundPitchOf(oV.BufferId(), 24001, 4096, 50, 2000) - 220) < 2
#--> 1
? @@( o1.FormantsOf("a", 220) )
#--> [ 650, 1080 ]
oBad = o1.Vowel("y", "A3", 1)
? o1.LastError()
#--> 'y' is not one of the five vowels a e i o u
oS = o1.Sing("la la", "c4 e4")
? o1.Refusals()
#--> 2

parameters.name: pcVowel
parameters.role: one of a, e, i, o or u

parameters.name: pnHz
parameters.role: the pitch in hertz

methods.returns: a list of two numbers; [ ] for a name that is not one of the five vowels
notes: for the vowel a at 220 hertz they are 650 and 1080, and for i 290 and 1870, from the Csound formant tables

methods.name: Vowel
methods.brief: Renders one sung vowel at a pitch as a sound.

parameters.name: pcVowel
parameters.role: one of a, e, i, o or u

parameters.name: pNote
parameters.role: a note name such as A3 or a frequency in hertz

parameters.name: pnSeconds
parameters.role: how long to hold it, in seconds

methods.returns: a mono stzSound at 48000 hertz; an empty text when the vowel or the pitch is refused, with the reason in LastError
notes: the sound runs 0.15 s longer than asked, a release: 1.5 s gave 79200 frames; A3 read back at 219.73 hertz by the engine's pitch reader, against 220; the peak was 0.56
warnings: a vowel that is not one of the five, such as y, gives an empty text and the error ... is not one of the five vowels a e i o u; a pitch that is neither a note name nor a number gives the error a pitch is a note name (A3, C#4) or Hz

methods.name: VowelGlide
methods.brief: Renders one sung vowel whose pitch glides from one note to another.

parameters.name: pcVowel
parameters.role: one of a, e, i, o or u

parameters.name: pFrom
parameters.role: the note or frequency it starts on

parameters.name: pTo
parameters.role: the note or frequency it ends on

parameters.name: pnSeconds
parameters.role: how long the glide lasts, in seconds

methods.returns: a mono stzSound at 48000 hertz; an empty text when refused, with the reason in LastError
notes: the pitch rises or falls through the sound: from A3 to A4 over 1 s it read about 233 hertz early on and 400 hertz near the end; the tail adds 0.15 s as in Vowel
warnings: the same refusals as Vowel

methods.name: Sing
methods.brief: Sings lyrics, each syllable as its first vowel, if the voice has been ruled to sing.

parameters.name: pcLyrics
parameters.role: the syllables, separated by spaces

parameters.name: pcNotes
parameters.role: the notes, separated by spaces

methods.returns: a sound, as VowelsQ gives, one vowel for each note at 90 beats a minute; an empty text while the ruling is not SINGING
notes: it sings vowels only: a consonant model does not exist, so la is sung as a; Vowel and VowelsQ are what the voice honestly does
warnings: refused today: StzSoundSingingVerdict records the formant voice as UNPERCEIVED, so it returns an empty text and the error Sing is not available YET: the formant voice has not been heard by the author

methods.name: LastError
methods.brief: Returns the reason of the last refusal.
methods.returns: the reason as text; an empty text when the last call went well

methods.name: Refusals
methods.brief: Returns how many calls were refused.
notes: it counts a bad vowel, a bad pitch, a refused Sing and a bad breath or vibrato

classes.name: stzSoundGraph
classes.brief: Describes a sound once as nodes joined by name, then renders it to memory or a file, or plays it.
classes.description: A node is something the graph does, not an object you hold: Add... calls add a node and make it the output, NameIt labels the last one, and the ...On calls take a label and build after that node. A node may only take inputs that already exist, so a graph cannot loop. Once Prepare, ToSound, ToFile or PlayFor has frozen the graph, no node can be added: the Add... calls then do nothing and LastError says so. The plain form acts and returns nothing; the Q twin returns the graph. ToSound and ToFile render with no audio device; PlayFor is the only method that opens one. The sound has not been heard by a person (UNPERCEIVED): it is checked by frame count, sample rate and peak level, not by listening.
classes.example:
o1.AddOscillator(:Sine, 440, 0.5)
? o1.NodeCount()
#--> 1
? o1.ToSound(0.5).Frames()
#--> 11025
? o1.ToSound(0.5).SampleRate()
#--> 22050

methods.name: init
methods.brief: Builds an empty sound graph, stereo at 48000 Hz, to which nodes are added by name.
warnings: a library without the sound engine leaves it empty and sets LastError

methods.name: Reshape
methods.brief: Frees the graph and starts a new empty one with a different channel count and sample rate.

parameters.name: pnChannels
parameters.role: the number of channels, 1 for mono and 2 for stereo

parameters.name: pnRate
parameters.role: the sample rate in hertz

warnings: only legal before anything is added, since every node and name is forgotten

extensions.name: ReshapeQ
extensions.adds: does what the method does, then returns the object, so the call can be chained

methods.name: Release
methods.brief: Frees the engine graph and leaves the object empty.
warnings: afterwards GraphId and NodeCount answer 0

methods.name: LastError
methods.brief: Returns the reason the last call failed, or the engine's last graph error when the face has recorded none.
warnings: once the face has recorded an error it keeps returning that one, and a later success does not clear it

methods.name: NodeCount
methods.brief: Returns how many nodes the graph holds.
warnings: 0 for a released graph

methods.name: GraphId
methods.brief: Returns the engine's id of the graph, to hand to a transport or a stream.
methods.returns: a number; 0 for a released graph

methods.name: SampleRate
methods.brief: Returns the sample rate of the graph, in hertz.
methods.returns: a number, 48000 until Reshape changes it

methods.name: Channels
methods.brief: Returns the number of channels of the graph.
methods.returns: a number, 2 until Reshape changes it

methods.name: OutputNode
methods.brief: Returns the index of the node the graph hands to the world.
methods.returns: a number; 0 when nothing has been added
warnings: a node added after the graph was prepared can reset this to 0, see the defects file

methods.name: AddMasterGain
methods.brief: Adds a gain node after the current output and makes it the output, so a pause can fade everything with one ramp.
methods.returns: the index of the new node; 0 when the graph has no output yet or is already prepared
notes: a refusal sets LastError
warnings: the node is named master; a transport adds it by itself when built, before the graph is prepared

methods.name: NameIt
methods.brief: Labels the last node added so that later calls can refer to it by name.

parameters.name: pcName
parameters.role: the label, kept in lower case

warnings: with nothing added it sets LastError and labels nothing

extensions.name: NameItQ
extensions.adds: does what the method does, then returns the object, so the call can be chained

methods.name: NodeNamed
methods.brief: Resolves a label or a raw node number to a node index.

parameters.name: pName
parameters.role: the label given to NameIt, matched without regard to case, or a node number

methods.returns: a number; 0 and a LastError for an unknown label; a number is returned as it is, existing or not

methods.name: HasNode
methods.brief: TRUE if a label resolves to a node.

parameters.name: pName
parameters.role: the label to look for, or a node number

warnings: a number is always TRUE, whether or not that node exists; an unknown label also sets LastError

methods.name: AddOscillator
methods.brief: Adds a tone generator as a source and makes it the last node and the output.

parameters.name: pWave
parameters.role: the waveform: Sine, Triangle, Square or Saw

parameters.name: pnHz
parameters.role: the frequency in hertz

parameters.name: pnAmplitude
parameters.role: the peak level, 1 being full scale

notes: after the graph is prepared nothing is added, LastError says so, and the output index becomes 0
warnings: an unknown waveform name sets LastError but still adds a sine

extensions.name: AddOscillatorQ
extensions.adds: does what the method does, then returns the object, so the call can be chained

methods.name: AddSound
methods.brief: Adds an existing sound as a source that plays once, and makes it the last node and the output.

parameters.name: poSound
parameters.role: a stzSound, or an engine buffer id

warnings: a refusal sets LastError

extensions.name: AddSoundQ
extensions.adds: does what the method does, then returns the object, so the call can be chained

methods.name: AddLoopingSound
methods.brief: Adds an existing sound as a source that repeats for as long as the graph is rendered.

parameters.name: poSound
parameters.role: a stzSound, or an engine buffer id

warnings: the loop makes a 0.1 s sound fill any length asked of ToSound

extensions.name: AddLoopingSoundQ
extensions.adds: does what the method does, then returns the object, so the call can be chained

methods.name: AddTimeline
methods.brief: Adds a node whose output is the notes placed on it, each at the frame asked, and makes it the output.
methods.returns: the index of the timeline node; 0 with LastError set when refused
warnings: the node has no input; the scheduler and live loops place notes on it through engine calls

methods.name: AddGainOn
methods.brief: Adds a gain stage after a node and makes it the output.

parameters.name: pName
parameters.role: the label or number of the node to act on

parameters.name: pnGain
parameters.role: the multiplier, 1 leaving the level unchanged

notes: it acts on the node the label names, not on the last one added: two calls on the same label branch from it, so label each new node with NameIt to chain them
warnings: an unknown node sets LastError and adds nothing

extensions.name: AddGainOnQ
extensions.adds: does what the method does, then returns the object, so the call can be chained

methods.name: AddFilterOn
methods.brief: Adds a filter after a node and makes it the output.

parameters.name: pName
parameters.role: the label or number of the node to act on

parameters.name: pKind
parameters.role: the filter type: LowPass, HighPass or BandPass

parameters.name: pnCutoff
parameters.role: the cut-off or centre frequency in hertz

parameters.name: pnQ
parameters.role: the resonance, above 0, 0.7 being a gentle slope

notes: a low-pass at 300 Hz brought a 2000 Hz sine down to a peak of 0.01
warnings: an unknown filter name sets LastError but still adds a low-pass; a cut-off of 0 or at and above half the rate is refused by the engine and adds nothing

extensions.name: AddFilterOnQ
extensions.adds: does what the method does, then returns the object, so the call can be chained

methods.name: AddEnvelopeOn
methods.brief: Adds a loudness envelope after a node and makes it the output.
usage: AddEnvelopeOn(pName, pnAttack, pnDecay, pnSustain, pnRelease, pnHold)
AddEnvelopeOnQ(pName, pnAttack, pnDecay, pnSustain, pnRelease, pnHold)

parameters.name: pName
parameters.role: the label or number of the node to act on

parameters.name: pnAttack
parameters.role: the rise time in seconds

parameters.name: pnDecay
parameters.role: the fall time in seconds from the peak to the sustain level

parameters.name: pnSustain
parameters.role: the held level from 0 to 1

parameters.name: pnRelease
parameters.role: the final fall time in seconds

parameters.name: pnHold
parameters.role: the time in seconds, counted from the start, at which the release begins

notes: measured: with attack 0.1, decay 0.2, sustain 0.5, release 0.2 and hold 0.5 the level is 0.5 from 0.3 s to 0.5 s and silent after 0.7 s
warnings: an unknown node sets LastError and adds nothing; a sustain above 1 or a negative time is refused by the engine and adds nothing

extensions.name: AddEnvelopeOnQ
extensions.adds: does what the method does, then returns the object, so the call can be chained

methods.name: AddEnvelopeOnAt
methods.brief: Adds a loudness envelope that starts a number of seconds into the sound, so a voice knows when it sounds.
usage: AddEnvelopeOnAt(pName, pnAttack, pnDecay, pnSustain, pnRelease, pnHold, pnStart)
AddEnvelopeOnAtQ(pName, pnAttack, pnDecay, pnSustain, pnRelease, pnHold, pnStart)

parameters.name: pName
parameters.role: the label or number of the node to act on

parameters.name: pnAttack
parameters.role: the rise time in seconds

parameters.name: pnDecay
parameters.role: the fall time in seconds from the peak to the sustain level

parameters.name: pnSustain
parameters.role: the held level from 0 to 1

parameters.name: pnRelease
parameters.role: the final fall time in seconds

parameters.name: pnHold
parameters.role: the time in seconds, counted from the start, at which the release begins

parameters.name: pnStart
parameters.role: the time in seconds at which the envelope begins

warnings: an unknown node sets LastError and adds nothing

extensions.name: AddEnvelopeOnAtQ
extensions.adds: does what the method does, then returns the object, so the call can be chained

methods.name: AddEchoOn
methods.brief: Adds a single feedback delay after a node and makes it the output.

parameters.name: pName
parameters.role: the label or number of the node to act on

parameters.name: pnSeconds
parameters.role: the delay time in seconds

parameters.name: pnFeedback
parameters.role: the share of each echo fed back into the line, from 0 to below 1

parameters.name: pnWet
parameters.role: the share of the echoes in the output, 0 for none and 1 for echoes only, the dry sound being scaled by 1 minus pnWet

warnings: a feedback of 1 or more, a delay over 60 s or a delay of 0 is refused by the engine and adds nothing; named an echo and not a reverb because one fading repeat is not a room

extensions.name: AddEchoOnQ
extensions.adds: does what the method does, then returns the object, so the call can be chained

methods.name: AddPanOn
methods.brief: Adds a stereo pan after a node and makes it the output.

parameters.name: pName
parameters.role: the label or number of the node to act on

parameters.name: pnPan
parameters.role: the position from 0 for left to 1 for right, 0.5 being the centre

notes: the pan is not -1 to 1: -0.5 plays left only and 2 plays right only
warnings: an unknown node sets LastError and adds nothing

extensions.name: AddPanOnQ
extensions.adds: does what the method does, then returns the object, so the call can be chained

methods.name: AddMixOf
methods.brief: Adds a mixer that sums several named nodes and makes it the output.

parameters.name: paNames
parameters.role: the labels or numbers of the nodes to mix

warnings: a name that is not a node is skipped and named in LastError, and the mixer is still added with the others

extensions.name: AddMixOfQ
extensions.adds: does what the method does, then returns the object, so the call can be chained

methods.name: SetOutputTo
methods.brief: Chooses which node the graph hands to the world, instead of the last one added.

parameters.name: pName
parameters.role: the label or number of the node to use as output

warnings: an unknown label changes nothing and sets LastError

extensions.name: SetOutputToQ
extensions.adds: does what the method does, then returns the object, so the call can be chained

methods.name: Prepare
methods.brief: Freezes the graph with the chosen output so it can be rendered.
methods.returns: 1 if the graph is ready, 0 if not; an empty graph answers 0 and LastError says it has no nodes
warnings: once prepared no node can be added, whatever the call; ToSound, ToFile and PlayFor call it themselves

methods.name: ToSound
methods.brief: Renders a number of seconds of the graph into memory as a sound.

parameters.name: pnSeconds
parameters.role: how many seconds to render

methods.returns: a stzSound at the graph's rate and channel count; an empty text with LastError set when the graph cannot be prepared
warnings: no audio device is opened; rendering again carries on from where the last render stopped, so a spent envelope stays silent, unless Rewind is called first; the sound has not been heard by a person

methods.name: ToFile
methods.brief: Renders a number of seconds of the graph into a 16-bit WAV file.

parameters.name: pcPath
parameters.role: the file to write, overwritten

parameters.name: pnSeconds
parameters.role: how many seconds to render

warnings: the rate and channel count are stored in the file; a failure sets LastError

extensions.name: ToFileQ
extensions.adds: does what the method does, then returns the object, so the call can be chained

methods.name: Rewind
methods.brief: Takes every stateful node back to its start so the next render begins from the top.
warnings: a prepared graph stays prepared

extensions.name: RewindQ
extensions.adds: does what the method does, then returns the object, so the call can be chained

methods.name: PlayFor
methods.brief: Plays the graph on the audio device for a number of seconds, then closes the device.

parameters.name: pnSeconds
parameters.role: how long to play

notes: it blocks the calling thread for the whole time
warnings: not run in this reference: it opens an audio device; with no device it sets LastError and returns

extensions.name: PlayForQ
extensions.adds: does what the method does, then returns the object, so the call can be chained

methods.name: Underruns
methods.brief: Returns how many frames the last PlayFor could not supply.
methods.returns: a number; 0 is the answer to want, and 0 before any PlayFor

classes.name: stzSoundGrid
classes.brief: Holds what a sound analysis returns, a table of numbers whose axes mean seconds and hertz, never a picture.
classes.description: A spectrum is one row, a spectrogram has one row for each window and an onset list is one row of seconds, all the same handle and the same table, with 1-based rows and columns. The axes carry their meaning: SecondsPerRow and HertzPerColumn come from the analysis, and are 0 where a row is not a moment or a column not a frequency. Because the output is data it is assertable: a 1000 hertz sine lies in the bin that contains 1000. ToCanvas hands the grid to the graphics plane as a heat map, low frequencies at the bottom, loudest value under each cell, decibels not amplitude; ToSVG needs no device and ToPNG uses the graphics device without a window. Release frees the grid. Sounds here are rendered to memory and not heard by a person (UNPERCEIVED).
classes.receiver: oScore = StzSoundScoreQ() oScore.Note(1000, 1) oScore.Tempo(120) oSound = oScore.ToSound() o1 = oSound.ToSpectrum()
classes.example:
? o1.Rows()
#--> 1
? o1.Columns()
#--> 2049
? o1.HertzPerColumn()
#--> 11.72
? o1.PeakColumnOfRow(1)
#--> 86
? o1.PeakFrequencyOfRow(1)
#--> 996.09
? o1.At(1, 86) = o1.Max()
#--> 1
oSg = oSound.ToSpectrogram()
? oSg.Rows()
#--> 81
? left(oSg.ToSVG(300, 120), 4)
#--> <svg
o1.Release()
? o1.IsEmpty()
#--> 1

methods.name: init
methods.brief: Wraps the engine's table of analysis numbers, taking its handle.

parameters.name: pnGridId
parameters.role: the engine's number for the grid, as a sound's ToSpectrum, ToSpectrogram or ToOnsets makes it

notes: you rarely build one yourself; a spectrum is one row, a spectrogram has a row for each window, and an onset list is one row of seconds

methods.name: GridId
methods.brief: Returns the engine's number for the grid.

methods.name: Release
methods.brief: Frees the grid in the engine.
methods.returns: nothing; every question answers its empty value afterwards
notes: releasing twice does nothing the second time; the sound's own buffer is not touched

methods.name: IsEmpty
methods.brief: TRUE if the grid holds no rows.
notes: it is TRUE after Release

methods.name: Rows
methods.brief: Returns how many rows the grid has.
notes: 1 for a spectrum, one for each window for a spectrogram, and 1 for onsets; a 0.9 second sound at 48000 hertz gave 81 windows of 2048 frames moving 512

methods.name: Columns
methods.brief: Returns how many columns the grid has.
notes: 2049 for a spectrum of 4096 frames, 1025 for a spectrogram, and one for each onset in an onset list

methods.name: SecondsPerRow
methods.brief: Returns what one row step means in time.
methods.returns: a number of seconds; 0 when a row is not a moment
notes: 512 over 48000, about 0.0107, for a default spectrogram; 0 for a spectrum and for onsets, whose numbers are already seconds

methods.name: HertzPerColumn
methods.brief: Returns what one column means in frequency.
methods.returns: a number of hertz; 0 when a column is not a frequency
notes: 11.72 for a default spectrum and 23.44 for a default spectrogram at 48000 hertz; 0 for onsets

methods.name: At
methods.brief: Returns the value in one cell.

parameters.name: pnRow
parameters.role: the row, counted from 1

parameters.name: pnColumn
parameters.role: the column, counted from 1

methods.returns: a number, 0 for a cell outside the grid or after Release
notes: the values of a spectrum are magnitudes

methods.name: Max
methods.brief: Returns the largest value in the whole grid.

methods.name: PeakColumnOfRow
methods.brief: Returns which column holds the largest value of a row, which frequency won.

parameters.name: pnRow
parameters.role: the row, counted from 1

methods.returns: the column, counted from 1; -1 for a row outside the grid or after Release
notes: for a rendered 1000 hertz note it was column 86

methods.name: PeakFrequencyOfRow
methods.brief: Returns the frequency of the strongest column of a row, in hertz.

parameters.name: pnRow
parameters.role: the row, counted from 1

methods.returns: a number of hertz, the start of the bin; -1 for a row outside the grid or after Release
notes: it is (column - 1) times HertzPerColumn, so a 1000 hertz note reads 996.09, the bin containing it, and in a spectrogram row 1007.81, since a bin is 23.44 wide and 1000 divided by it is 42.7

methods.name: ToList
methods.brief: Returns one row as a plain Ring list.

parameters.name: pnRow
parameters.role: the row, counted from 1

methods.returns: a list of numbers, one for each column; [ ] after Release
notes: it crosses into the engine once for each value, so use it to look at a row, not at a whole spectrogram

methods.name: ToTimesList
methods.brief: Returns the first row, which for an onset list is the list of times.
methods.returns: a list of numbers, in seconds for an onset grid
notes: the onset times come from a detector with a window of 2048 frames and are not exact to the frame

methods.name: ToCanvas
methods.brief: Draws the grid as a heat map on a stzCanvas of a given size, with low frequencies at the bottom.

parameters.name: pnWidth
parameters.role: the width in pixels

parameters.name: pnHeight
parameters.role: the height in pixels

methods.returns: a stzCanvas of rectangles, one for each cell of 3 by 3 pixels
notes: the grid is reduced to the cells that fit, each taking the loudest value beneath it; colour runs from dark blue through cyan and yellow to white over 60 decibels below the peak; only the first 120 columns are drawn; a canvas that is background alone for an empty or silent grid

methods.name: ToCanvasOf
methods.brief: Draws the grid as a heat map like ToCanvas, with a chosen number of frequency columns.

parameters.name: pnWidth
parameters.role: the width in pixels

parameters.name: pnHeight
parameters.role: the height in pixels

parameters.name: pnMaxBins
parameters.role: how many columns, from the lowest frequency up, to draw, or 0 for all

methods.returns: a stzCanvas of rectangles, one for each cell of 3 by 3 pixels
notes: most musical energy sits in the lowest fraction of the range, so the default of 120 columns covers about 2.8 kilohertz at 48000 hertz

methods.name: ToSVG
methods.brief: Draws the heat map as SVG text; no graphics device is needed.

parameters.name: pnWidth
parameters.role: the width in pixels

parameters.name: pnHeight
parameters.role: the height in pixels

notes: the temporary canvas is freed

methods.name: ToSVGFile
methods.brief: Draws the heat map and writes it to an SVG file.

parameters.name: pcPath
parameters.role: the path of the file

parameters.name: pnWidth
parameters.role: the width in pixels

parameters.name: pnHeight
parameters.role: the height in pixels

notes: it works on a machine with no graphics device; an existing file is overwritten

methods.name: ToPNG
methods.brief: Draws the heat map and writes it to a PNG file through the graphics device.

parameters.name: pcPath
parameters.role: the path of the file

parameters.name: pnWidth
parameters.role: the width in pixels

parameters.name: pnHeight
parameters.role: the height in pixels

notes: it needs a graphics device but opens no window; the picture of a 1000 hertz note showed a bright line at 1000 hertz and its second harmonic, ending where the note ends

classes.name: stzSoundInstrument
classes.brief: Renders one note of any of twenty instruments as a stzSound, in tune to the cent, from a note name, a frequency, a glide or a stroke.
classes.description: A note is data: a stzSound rendered offline by the engine, so every verb of the sound plane applies to it, loudness, onsets, filters, a WAV. Nothing here plays. Strings, bows and winds tune themselves: each plays a probe, measures the pitch it made and corrects, and RawCents and TuningCents report what that took. FM and membrane instruments are in tune by construction. Each instrument has an honest fallback name decided before anyone listened. Strokes belong to membranes, hand drums and the drum kit, and a plucked or FM voice cannot glide. An unknown instrument does not raise: it is not usable and LastError lists the twenty. Rendered notes are checked by frame count, sample rate, peak and measured pitch and have not been heard by a person (UNPERCEIVED).
classes.example:
? o1.IsUsable()
#--> 1
? o1.HonestName()
#--> darkpluck
? o1.Engine()
#--> pluck
? @@( o1.Range() )
#--> [ 70, 700 ]
? oNote.SampleRate()
#--> 48000
? oNote.Frames()
#--> 60000
? abs(StzEngineSoundPitchOf(oNote.BufferId(), 12001, 4096, 50, 2000) - 293.66) < 1
#--> 1
oBad = o1.ToSoundOfStroke("tak", 180, 0.5)
? o1.LastError()
#--> ToSoundOfStroke: oud is not struck -- it has no strokes
? StzSoundInstrumentQ("kazoo").IsUsable()
#--> 0

methods.name: init
methods.brief: Looks one of the twenty instruments up by name and makes it ready to render notes.

parameters.name: pName
parameters.role: the instrument name in any letter case, such as :Oud, one of piano, guitar, harp, bell, epiano, brass, flute, oud, koto, kora, metallophone, drumkit, mezwed, zokra, darbouka, bendir, kakaki, sarewa, imzad or kalangu

methods.returns: nothing; the instrument is usable only if the name was found and the sound engine is loaded
notes: StzSoundInstrumentQ builds the same object
warnings: an unknown name does not raise: the instrument is not usable, a refusal is counted and LastError lists the twenty names

methods.name: IsUsable
methods.brief: TRUE if the instrument was found and can render.

methods.name: Name
methods.brief: Returns the instrument name as the engine spells it.
methods.returns: the name as text in lower case, such as oud; an empty text when it is not usable

methods.name: HonestName
methods.brief: Returns the name the instrument ships under if the ear says the real one is a lie.
methods.returns: the fallback name as text, such as darkpluck for the oud, talkingdrum for the kalangu or fmbell for the bell; an empty text when not usable
notes: decided in the engine table before anyone listened

methods.name: Engine
methods.brief: Returns how the instrument makes its sound.
methods.returns: pluck, bow, wind, fm or membrane, as text; an empty text when not usable
notes: the oud is a pluck and the kalangu and the drum kit are membranes

methods.name: PitchClass
methods.brief: Returns how well the instrument has a pitch.
methods.returns: harmonic, inharmonic or none, as text; an empty text when not usable
notes: harmonic is held to 2 cents, inharmonic is a bar, a bell or a drum whose partials are not multiples, and none is a hi-hat or a snare; the oud is harmonic, the kalangu and the bell inharmonic, the drum kit none

methods.name: Range
methods.brief: Returns the lowest and highest frequency the instrument plays, in hertz.
methods.returns: a list of two numbers; [ ] when not usable
notes: the oud plays 70 to 700 hertz and the kalangu 70 to 400

methods.name: Velocity
methods.brief: Returns the strength the notes are struck with.
methods.returns: a number above 0 and at most 1, 0.8 by default

methods.name: SetVelocity
methods.brief: Sets the strength the notes are struck with.

parameters.name: pnVelocity
parameters.role: the strength, above 0 and at most 1

methods.returns: nothing; the velocity is stored. SetVelocityQ returns the instrument for chaining
notes: the next notes use it
warnings: a value of 0 or less, above 1, or not a number counts a refusal, sets LastError to SetVelocity: a velocity is above 0 and at most 1 and leaves the old value

extensions.name: SetVelocityQ
extensions.adds: does what the method does, then returns the object, so the call can be chained

methods.name: ToSoundOf
methods.brief: Renders one note at a frequency as a mono sound at 48000 hertz.

parameters.name: pnHz
parameters.role: the frequency in hertz

parameters.name: pnSeconds
parameters.role: how long the note is written for, in seconds

methods.returns: a stzSound; an empty text when the instrument is not usable or the engine refused
notes: the note may ring past its written length: an oud of 0.5 s gave 36000 frames, 0.75 s; the engine tunes each plucked, bowed and wind model by measuring a probe
warnings: an unusable instrument gives an empty text and LastError says so

methods.name: ToSoundOfNote
methods.brief: Renders one note, given by name, as a mono sound at 48000 hertz.

parameters.name: pcNote
parameters.role: a note name such as A4, C#3, Bb2, D4+50 for a quarter tone above or E4-50 for one below

parameters.name: pnSeconds
parameters.role: how long the note is written for, in seconds

methods.returns: a stzSound; an empty text when the name is not a note or the instrument cannot render
notes: an oud D4 of 1 s gave 60000 frames, 1.25 s, a peak of 0.56 and a pitch read back as 293.67 hertz, against 293.66; E4-50 read back as 320.26, against 320.24
warnings: a name that is not a note, such as H9, gives an empty text and the error ToSoundOfNote: ... is not a note name

methods.name: ToSoundOfGlide
methods.brief: Renders one note whose pitch moves from one frequency to another while it sounds.

parameters.name: pnFromHz
parameters.role: the frequency it starts on

parameters.name: pnToHz
parameters.role: the frequency it ends on

parameters.name: pnSeconds
parameters.role: how long the glide lasts, in seconds

methods.returns: a stzSound; an empty text when the instrument cannot glide, with the reason in LastError
notes: a kalangu glide of 0.8 s gave exactly 38400 frames
warnings: a pluck and an FM voice hold one pitch and refuse: an oud gave an empty text and the error this instrument cannot glide

methods.name: ToSoundOfStroke
methods.brief: Renders one stroke of a drum, where it is struck, as a sound.

parameters.name: pStroke
parameters.role: dum, tak or ka on a hand drum, or kick, snare, hihat, openhat, crash, ride, hightom, midtom or floortom on the kit, as a symbol or text

parameters.name: pnHz
parameters.role: the pitch of the drum in hertz

parameters.name: pnSeconds
parameters.role: how long it is written for, in seconds

methods.returns: a stzSound; an empty text when the instrument is not struck, the stroke is unknown or this drum has not got it
notes: cymbals ring past the length written: a crash is at least 2 seconds, a ride at least 1.2 and an open hi-hat at least 0.6, which the drum kit gave exactly as 96000, 57600 and 28800 frames
warnings: an instrument that is not a membrane, such as the oud, gives the error ... is not struck; an unknown stroke such as boom gives the error ... is not a stroke; a stroke the instrument does not have, such as crash on a darbouka, gives the error that stroke is not one this instrument has

methods.name: RawCents
methods.brief: Returns how far off pitch the untuned model of the last note was, in cents.
methods.returns: a number; 0 for an FM or membrane instrument, which is in tune by construction
notes: measured by the engine from a probe

methods.name: TuningCents
methods.brief: Returns the correction the tuner applied to the last note, in cents.
methods.returns: a number; 0 when none was needed
notes: the oud D4 needed none

methods.name: LastError
methods.brief: Returns the reason of the last refusal.
methods.returns: the reason as text; an empty text when the last call went well

methods.name: Refusals
methods.brief: Returns how many calls were refused.
notes: it counts an unknown instrument, a bad velocity, a bad note and a refused stroke or glide

classes.name: stzSoundLadder
classes.brief: Draws a mode as a ladder, one rung for each degree, spaced by cents, so where the notes sit is visible and not only named.
classes.description: A mode is shown when the question is where its notes sit and not what the melody is. Each degree is a rung whose height is its pitch and whose distance from the next is the step, so on the ladder a half-flat third sits half way between the minor and the major third, which a staff cannot show. Everything drawn is declared by the universe: a degree lowered going down is a dashed rung, a degree the sources disagree on is dotted with its source named, ajnas are brackets beside the rails. Rungs gives the numbers, ToText a text, ToSVG and SaveAs the picture. A mode name the universe does not declare falls back to its default mode without an error. No sound is played; the SVG was rendered by a headless browser and read by a model, not by a person (UNPERCEIVED).
classes.example:
? o1.IsUsable()
#--> 1
? o1.ModeName()
#--> dhil
? len(o1.Rungs())
#--> 8
? o1.Rungs()[3][2]
#--> e-half-flat
? o1.Rungs()[3][3]
#--> 350
? o1.Rungs()[3][4]
#--> 320.24
? @@( o1.Steps() )
#--> [ 200, 150, 150, 200, 200, 150, 150 ]
? o1.Ajnas()[2][1]
#--> rast
? left(o1.ToSVG(), 4)
#--> <svg
? StzSoundLadderQ(:nowhere, :x).IsUsable()
#--> 0

methods.name: init
methods.brief: Reads one mode of a declared universe and prepares to show its degrees as a ladder.

parameters.name: pUniverse
parameters.role: the universe name or object, such as :tunisian or :maqam

parameters.name: pMode
parameters.role: the name of a mode of that universe, or an empty text for its first

methods.returns: nothing; the ladder is usable if the universe and a mode with degrees were found
notes: StzSoundLadderQ builds the same object
warnings: an unknown universe is not raised: the ladder is not usable and LastError lists the declared universes; a mode name the universe does not declare is not refused either: the ladder shows the universe default mode instead, without any error, so :tunisian with :rast and :maqam with :zzz gave the modes dhil and rast with IsUsable 1

methods.name: Tonic
methods.brief: Sets the note the ladder is built on.

parameters.name: pcNote
parameters.role: a note name such as D4

methods.returns: the ladder itself, so calls chain
notes: the cents stay the same and the hertz of every rung move with the tonic: for the dhil mode on D4 the first rung is 293.66 hertz

methods.name: IsUsable
methods.brief: TRUE if the ladder has a mode with degrees to show.

methods.name: LastError
methods.brief: Returns why the ladder is not usable.
methods.returns: the reason as text; an empty text when it is usable

methods.name: ModeName
methods.brief: Returns the name of the mode on show.
methods.returns: the mode name as text, in lower case
notes: it is the default mode of the universe when the requested name was not found

methods.name: TonicName
methods.brief: Returns the note the ladder is built on.
methods.returns: the note as text, such as C4
notes: C4 until Tonic or the mode sets another

methods.name: Rungs
methods.brief: Returns every degree of the mode as a rung, the octave included, with its pitch and the step to the next rung.
methods.returns: a list of [ degree, name, cents above the tonic, hertz, step to the next rung in cents ]; the last, octave rung has a step of 0
notes: rungs are spaced by cents, so a half-flat third sits half way between the minor and the major third; for the dhil mode on C4 the degrees are at 0, 200, 350, 500, 700, 900 and 1050 cents and the third is 320.24 hertz, checked by hand as 261.63 times 2 to the power of 350 over 1200; a mode that declares no names shows its degree numbers

methods.name: DescendingRungs
methods.brief: Returns the degrees of the descending form of the mode, when it differs from the ascending one.
methods.returns: the same rows as Rungs; [ ] when the mode declares no descending form or it equals the ascending one
notes: in the maqam rast the seventh degree is 1050 cents going up and 1000 coming down

methods.name: Steps
methods.brief: Returns the distances between neighbouring rungs, in cents.
methods.returns: a list of numbers, one fewer than the rungs

methods.name: Ajnas
methods.brief: Returns the ajnas, the small scales a mode is built from, with the cents each spans.
methods.returns: a list of [ name, lowest cents, highest cents, the list of its cents above the tonic ]
notes: a jins counts its cents from its own first degree, unless they begin below zero, when the declaration counted them from the tonic; the dhil mode has a rast on the tonic, 0 to 500, and one below it, minus 500 to 0

methods.name: ToText
methods.brief: Returns the ladder as plain text, the highest rung first, with the cents, the hertz and the steps.
notes: a step is named when it falls on the quarter-tone grid, such as 150 (3/4 tone), and a step off the grid has no name; descending forms and ajnas are listed after the rungs

methods.name: SaveAs
methods.brief: Writes the ladder to a file: SVG when the name ends in .svg, an HTML page otherwise.

parameters.name: pcPath
parameters.role: the path of the file

notes: an existing file is overwritten

methods.name: ToHTML
methods.brief: Returns the ladder as a complete HTML page with the SVG inside.
methods.returns: the HTML text, starting with the doctype

methods.name: ToSVG
methods.brief: Returns the ladder as SVG text: rails, rungs spaced by cents, a faint quarter-tone grid, steps, and brackets for the ajnas.
notes: a degree the mode lowers going down is a dashed rung, a degree the sources disagree on is dotted with its source named, and a degree left out going down is marked; seen in a rendered picture of the dhil mode on D4: eight rungs from 0 to 1200 cents, the half-flat third between two dotted variants at 300 and 400, the steps beside the rails and the rast bracket

classes.name: stzSoundLive
classes.brief: Runs named live loops that can be redefined while they play, each change landing on the next cycle boundary.
classes.description: A cycle is one bar of 4 beats. A loop's notes are posted a whole cycle at a time, well ahead of the render; a redefinition withdraws the loop's notes from the first cycle the producer has not reached and posts the new pattern from there, and the call returns that cycle. The console reports what was heard, not what was posted. Without CaptureInsteadOfDevice the session plays on a sound card through a transport, which was not run in this reference; with it, a producer thread renders into a ring that this session drains into a buffer, so no device is opened. In capture mode WaitCycles for longer than the buffer never returns. The sound has not been heard by a person (UNPERCEIVED): it is checked by frame count, sample rate and peak level, not by listening.
classes.example:
o1.CaptureInsteadOfDevice(6, FALSE)
? o1.OnDevice()
#--> 0
? o1.LiveLoopOn(:tune, "c5 e5 g5 e5", :Harp)
#--> 0
o1.WaitCycles(1)
? o1.HeardCycle()
#--> 1
? o1.ConsoleLog()[1][3]
#--> cycle 0 | tune v1
o1.Stop()

methods.name: init
methods.brief: Builds a live session at 120 beats per minute with no loops, started on a sound card unless capture is chosen.
warnings: build it with StzSoundLiveQ to set the speed in the same call; a cycle is one bar of 4 beats

methods.name: SetTempo
methods.brief: Sets the speed of the session in beats per minute.

parameters.name: pnBpm
parameters.role: the speed in beats per minute, from 20 to 400

methods.returns: the session itself, so calls chain
notes: it builds a new renderer, because the notes of a loop are rendered at the speed in force
warnings: refused, with LastError set and the refusal counted, once the session runs, once any loop is defined, or for a value outside the range

methods.name: Tempo
methods.brief: Returns the speed of the session in beats per minute.

methods.name: SetDefaultInstrument
methods.brief: Sets the instrument given to loops that name none and are made of pitched notes.

parameters.name: pcName
parameters.role: the instrument name, such as piano or harp, kept in lower case

methods.returns: the session itself, so calls chain
notes: an unknown name is refused later, when a loop is defined with it
warnings: a loop of strokes ignores it and takes the drum kit, or the darbouka for dum, tak and ka

methods.name: CaptureInsteadOfDevice
methods.brief: Chooses to drain the sound into a buffer instead of a sound card, for at most a number of seconds.

parameters.name: pnSeconds
parameters.role: the length of the buffer that keeps what came out

parameters.name: pbPaced
parameters.role: TRUE to drain at the pace of the wall clock, FALSE to drain as fast as WaitCycles asks

methods.returns: the session itself, so calls chain
notes: this is the only way to run the session without opening an audio device; a device drains on its own thread, so a render in capture mode stalls the drain and proves nothing about late notes
warnings: refused once the loops have started; the buffer is silent beyond what was heard; WaitCycles for longer than pnSeconds never returns, see the defects file

methods.name: Capture
methods.brief: Returns the buffer that capture mode fills with what has been heard.
methods.returns: a stzSound of the length given to CaptureInsteadOfDevice, with the same rate and channels as the session; an empty text before the loops start or when capture was not chosen
warnings: read it after WaitCycles; the sound has not been heard by a person

methods.name: OnCycle
methods.brief: Sets the function called each time a cycle boundary is heard, with the console line of that cycle.

parameters.name: f
parameters.role: the function, or its name, to call with one text argument

methods.returns: the session itself, so calls chain
warnings: it fires when the frames consumed cross a cycle boundary, not when the cycle is posted, so the console never runs ahead of the sound

methods.name: LiveLoop
methods.brief: Defines or redefines a loop from a pattern, naming the instrument itself.

parameters.name: pName
parameters.role: the loop's name, kept in lower case

parameters.name: pcPattern
parameters.role: a pattern of note names and strokes, such as c5 e5 g5 e5 or bd hh sn hh

methods.returns: the cycle the loop lands on, counted from 0; -1 when refused
notes: a redefinition lands on the first cycle boundary the producer has not reached
warnings: a bad pattern, an unknown instrument, strokes on an instrument that is not struck or notes on a drum are refused with LastError set and the old version goes on playing; before the loops start a redefinition replaces and lands on cycle 0

methods.name: LiveLoopOn
methods.brief: Defines or redefines a loop from a pattern, played on a chosen instrument.

parameters.name: pName
parameters.role: the loop's name, kept in lower case

parameters.name: pcPattern
parameters.role: a pattern of note names and strokes

parameters.name: pInstrument
parameters.role: the instrument name, or an empty text for the session's default

methods.returns: the cycle the loop lands on, counted from 0; -1 when refused
notes: while running, the notes of the loop from the landing cycle on are withdrawn and posted again
warnings: refused like LiveLoop; every distinct note is rendered before anything already posted is touched

methods.name: LiveLoopOf
methods.brief: Defines or redefines a loop from a pattern object that has already been transformed.

parameters.name: pName
parameters.role: the loop's name, kept in lower case

parameters.name: poPattern
parameters.role: a valid stzSoundPattern

parameters.name: pInstrument
parameters.role: the instrument name, or an empty text for the default

methods.returns: the cycle the loop lands on, counted from 0; -1 when refused
warnings: anything but a valid stzSoundPattern is refused, with LastError set

methods.name: Every
methods.brief: Redefines a loop as itself transformed every so many cycles.

parameters.name: pnN
parameters.role: the period of the transform in cycles

parameters.name: pName
parameters.role: the name of an existing loop

parameters.name: pXform
parameters.role: the transform to apply, such as rev

methods.returns: the cycle the loop lands on; -1 when refused
notes: the change lands on a cycle boundary like any redefinition
warnings: an unknown loop, a silenced loop or a transform the pattern refuses is refused with LastError set; the playing version is not touched

methods.name: Silence
methods.brief: Stops one loop from the first cycle boundary it can land on.

parameters.name: pName
parameters.role: the name of the loop to silence

methods.returns: the cycle on which the loop falls silent; -1 for an unknown loop
warnings: the loop stays defined and can be redefined later

methods.name: Hush
methods.brief: Silences every loop at the first cycle boundary each can land on.
methods.returns: the cycle of the last loop's landing; -1 when there are no loops

methods.name: Start
methods.brief: Posts the first window of notes and starts the performance, on a sound card or into the capture buffer.
methods.returns: TRUE if running; FALSE with LastError set when there are no loops or the engine refused
notes: asking again while running answers TRUE
warnings: without CaptureInsteadOfDevice it opens an audio device through a transport, which was not run in this reference

methods.name: Tick
methods.brief: Posts what is due, drains the ring in paced capture mode and reports the cycles heard.
methods.returns: the session itself, so calls chain
notes: a reactive loop calls it every 20 ms for a driven session
warnings: does nothing unless the session runs

methods.name: WaitCycles
methods.brief: Lets the session run for a number of heard cycles, starting it first when needed, and then returns.

parameters.name: pnCycles
parameters.role: how many cycles of heard time to wait

methods.returns: the session itself, so calls chain
notes: the wait counts heard frames, not posted ones
warnings: in capture mode it never returns when the wait is longer than the capture buffer, see the defects file; without capture it plays on a device, which was not run in this reference

methods.name: DriveWith
methods.brief: Starts the session when needed and registers it so that a reactive loop steps it every 20 ms.

parameters.name: poReactive
parameters.role: the stzReactive whose loop should call the session

methods.returns: the session itself, so calls chain
notes: the session is registered by pointer in a global list and Stop removes it
warnings: anything but a stzReactive is refused, with LastError set; the reactive loop itself was not run in this reference

methods.name: Stop
methods.brief: Takes the session out of any reactive loop and stops the performance, keeping the loops and the logs.
methods.returns: the session itself, so calls chain
warnings: does nothing to a session that is not running

methods.name: Release
methods.brief: Stops the session, then frees the graph and the rendered notes.
warnings: call it once nothing is playing, since the timeline reads the note samples directly

methods.name: IsRunning
methods.brief: TRUE if the performance has started and not been stopped.

methods.name: CycleFrames
methods.brief: Returns how many frames one cycle of 4 beats lasts at the session's speed.
methods.returns: a number of frames; 96000 at 120 beats per minute and 48000 Hz

methods.name: FrameOfCycle
methods.brief: Returns the frame at which a cycle begins.

parameters.name: pnCycle
parameters.role: the cycle number, counted from 0

methods.returns: a number of frames, counted from 0
warnings: computed with the same function the offline render uses

methods.name: HeardFrames
methods.brief: Returns the frames the listener has been given: those the device consumed, or those capture mode drained.
methods.returns: a number of frames; 0 before the loops start
warnings: it can pass a cycle boundary by a few hundred frames, since draining is done in chunks

methods.name: HeardCycle
methods.brief: Returns the number of the last cycle whose boundary has been heard.
methods.returns: a number counted from 0; -1 before any

methods.name: RenderFrames
methods.brief: Returns how far the producer has rendered the timeline, in frames.
methods.returns: a number of frames; 0 before the loops start
warnings: it runs ahead of HeardFrames by about a ring, a cycle and half a second

methods.name: ConsoleLog
methods.brief: Returns one row per cycle as it was heard.
methods.returns: a list of [ cycle, heardFrame, text ] rows, the text such as cycle 1 and each loop with its version
warnings: the text reports what was posted for that cycle, not the latest definition

methods.name: Ledger
methods.brief: Returns what was posted for each cycle.
methods.returns: a list of [ cycle, loop name, version ] rows
warnings: rows for cycles from a landing cycle on are dropped when a loop is redefined and posted again

methods.name: Landings
methods.brief: Returns where each definition of a loop took effect.
methods.returns: a list of [ loop name, version, landing cycle, cycle heard when it was asked ] rows
warnings: before the loops start every landing is cycle 0 and the heard cycle is -1; a loop redefined twice before the start and once while running is numbered v3 and then v2, so version numbers can go back, see the defects file

methods.name: Late
methods.brief: Returns how many notes reached the timeline after the producer had rendered their frame.
methods.returns: a number; 0 is the answer to want
warnings: 0 before the loops start

methods.name: Cancelled
methods.brief: Returns how many notes were withdrawn before they sounded, by a redefinition.
warnings: measured: redefining a four-note loop at heard cycle 1 withdrew 4 notes

methods.name: MidCycleChanges
methods.brief: Returns the withdrawals the engine refused because the note was already sounding, which would be a change in the middle of a cycle.
warnings: it is the kill criterion of the live design

methods.name: NotesRenderedLive
methods.brief: Returns how many notes were rendered while the session was playing, because a pattern ran past its first period.

methods.name: SecondsRendering
methods.brief: Returns the wall time spent rendering the notes of the loops, in seconds.

methods.name: DrainShortfall
methods.brief: Returns the frames that paced capture was due to drain and the ring did not yet hold.

methods.name: Underruns
methods.brief: Returns the frames the sound card asked for and did not get, as of the last step.

methods.name: OnDevice
methods.brief: TRUE if the session plays on a sound card, FALSE if capture was chosen.
methods.returns: TRUE or FALSE; TRUE for a new session

methods.name: Renderer
methods.brief: Returns the renderer that holds the notes of the loops.

methods.name: LastError
methods.brief: Returns the reason the last call was refused, or an empty text.

methods.name: Refusals
methods.brief: Returns how many calls the session has refused.

classes.name: stzSoundNotation
classes.brief: Writes a score as notation and as a MIDI file, and says what each format could not carry.
classes.description: Notation is a rendering of the score and never its source: ABC 2.1 text, MusicXML and a Standard MIDI File, type 1, are written from the same stzSoundScore. Quarter tones are written in each format's own terms, ^/ and _/ in ABC and decimal alterations in MusicXML; a pitch further than 5 cents from the nearest quarter tone, and a duration rounded by more than a hundredth of a beat, are counted in Losses. MIDI has no quarter tones, so every pitched note gets a pitch bend on a channel of its own, and strokes go to the drum channel. Everything is text or bytes: no audio device is opened and nothing is played. The files have not been heard or read by a musician (UNPERCEIVED): they are checked by their bytes and text.
classes.receiver: oS = StzSoundScoreOfQ("C4 D4 E4 C4") oS.Tempo(90) o1 = StzSoundNotationQ(oS)
classes.example:
? left(o1.ToABC("Tiny study"), 3)
#--> X:1
? StzFindFirst("Q:1/4=90", o1.ToABC("Tiny study")) > 0
#--> 1
? StzFindFirst("C4 D4 E4 C4", o1.ToABC("Tiny study")) > 0
#--> 1
? StzFindFirst("<step>E</step>", o1.ToMusicXML("Tiny study")) > 0
#--> 1
? left(o1.ToMidiBytes(), 4)
#--> MThd
? len(o1.ToMidiBytes())
#--> 569
? @@( o1.Losses() )
#--> [ ]

methods.name: init
methods.brief: Builds a notation writer over a score; the formats are written from the score, which stays the source.

parameters.name: poScore
parameters.role: the stzSoundScore to write out

notes: StzSoundNotationQ builds the same object

methods.name: Losses
methods.brief: Returns what the last format written could not carry.
methods.returns: a list of sentences; [ ] when nothing was lost
notes: each ToABC and ToMusicXML starts the list afresh; strokes are not written in ABC or MusicXML, so a score with a stroke leaves strokes are not written in ABC or MusicXML here (MIDI carries them); a pitch more than 5 cents from the nearest quarter tone, and a rounding of more than a hundredth of a beat, are counted too

methods.name: ToABC
methods.brief: Writes the score as ABC 2.1 text, one voice per instrument.

parameters.name: pcTitle
parameters.role: the title written on the T line

methods.returns: the ABC text, with header lines X, T, M, L, Q and K, a V line naming each voice and one line of notes per voice
notes: a note is its letter, an octave mark and a length in sixteenths of a beat, so C4 is middle C lasting one beat; a quarter tone is written ^/A or _/B; a rest is z; long notes are tied across barlines; for a four-note piano score at 90 beats a minute it gives Q:1/4=90 and the line [V:1] C4 D4 E4 C4 followed by a closing bar

methods.name: ToMusicXML
methods.brief: Writes the score as MusicXML text, with quarter tones as decimal alterations.

parameters.name: pcTitle
parameters.role: the title written in the document

methods.returns: the MusicXML text, with one part for each instrument
notes: durations use four divisions to the quarter note; a quarter tone is an alter of 0.5 or -0.5; strokes are not written

methods.name: ToMidiFile
methods.brief: Writes the score as a Standard MIDI File, type 1, to a file.

parameters.name: pcPath
parameters.role: the path of the file to write

notes: the same bytes as ToMidiBytes; an existing file is overwritten

methods.name: ToMidiBytes
methods.brief: Returns the score as the bytes of a Standard MIDI File, type 1, with 480 ticks to the quarter note.
methods.returns: the bytes as text, starting with MThd; for a four-note piano score 3 tracks and 569 bytes
notes: every pitched note gets its own channel and a pitch bend, because MIDI has no quarter tones, with the bend range set to plus or minus 12 semitones; channels rotate and a note needing a channel when all fifteen are busy is counted in Losses; strokes go to the drum channel with General MIDI numbers; the note events for C4 D4 E4 C4 at velocity 0.8 were checked by hand: 60, 62, 64 and 60 at velocity 102

classes.name: stzSoundNotationReader
classes.brief: Reads ABC, MIDI and MusicXML back into the stzSoundScore every transform already reads, and counts what it dropped.
classes.description: The other direction from stzSoundNotation: a MIDI file, an ABC tune or a MusicXML score becomes a stzSoundScore, which can be played, transcribed against, analysed for its modes or written out in another format. The reader counts what a score cannot keep, a tempo change, an ornament, a lyric, in Losses and refuses a file it cannot read honestly, with the reason in LastError: a SMPTE-timed or format 2 MIDI file, an ABC tune with no K: line, a MusicXML score-timewise or one that is not well-formed. Pitch in MIDI is the key plus the bend, so quarter tones come back as the frequency they were. Repeats are played out, since a score is what is performed. Reading opens no audio device and plays nothing; what comes back has not been heard by a person (UNPERCEIVED).
classes.receiver: o1 = StzSoundNotationReaderQ() cAbc = "X:1" + char(10) + "T:Tiny study" + char(10) + "M:4/4" + char(10) + "L:1/16" + char(10) + "Q:1/4=90" + char(10) + "K:C" + char(10) + "[V:1] C4 D4 E4 C4" + char(10) oS = o1.FromAbcQ(cAbc)
classes.example:
? oS.NumberOfEvents()
#--> 4
? oS.TempoInBpm()
#--> 90
? oS.Events()[3][3]
#--> 329.63
? o1.Title()
#--> Tiny study
? @@( o1.Losses() )
#--> [ ]
oBad = o1.FromAbcQ("X:1" + char(10) + "C D E")
? o1.LastError()
#--> ABC: music before the K: line -- a tune's header ends with K:, and this one has none
oM = o1.FromMidiBytesQ("not midi")
? o1.LastError()
#--> MIDI: not a Standard MIDI File -- 8 bytes, and a header alone is 14

methods.name: init
methods.brief: Builds a notation reader with no losses, no error and no title.
notes: StzSoundNotationReaderQ builds the same object, and StzSoundScoreFromAbcQ, StzSoundScoreFromMidiQ and StzSoundScoreFromMusicXMLQ read in one call when the losses do not matter

methods.name: Losses
methods.brief: Returns what the last read could not keep of the notation.
methods.returns: a list of sentences; [ ] when nothing was dropped
notes: each read starts the list afresh; an ABC tune with an ornament and a lyric line gave ABC: decorations (ornaments, dynamics, articulations) are not read and ABC: lyrics (w:, W:) are not read

methods.name: LastError
methods.brief: Returns why the last read was refused.
methods.returns: the reason as text; an empty text when the last read was accepted
notes: examples are an ABC tune with music before its K: line, a MIDI file shorter than a header, a MusicXML score-timewise and a text that is not well-formed XML

methods.name: Title
methods.brief: Returns the title of the last tune or score read.
methods.returns: the title as text; an empty text when none
notes: it is set from the header before a refusal, so a refused ABC tune can still leave its T: line here

methods.name: Voices
methods.brief: Returns the voices of the last ABC tune.
methods.returns: a list of [ voice id, instrument ] pairs, such as [ "1", "piano" ]
notes: only ABC sets it

methods.name: FromMidiFileQ
methods.brief: Reads a Standard MIDI File from disk, formats 0 and 1, into a stzSoundScore.

parameters.name: pcPath
parameters.role: the path of the file

methods.returns: a stzSoundScore; an empty text when the file is missing or refused, with the reason in LastError
notes: the file is read and handed to FromMidiBytesQ
warnings: a path that does not exist gives an empty text and the error FromMidiFileQ: no file at ...

methods.name: FromMidiBytesQ
methods.brief: Reads the bytes of a Standard MIDI File, formats 0 and 1, into a stzSoundScore.

parameters.name: pcBytes
parameters.role: the bytes of the file, as text

methods.returns: a stzSoundScore with one event for each note or stroke; an empty text when refused, with the reason in LastError
notes: pitch is the key plus the pitch bend, read against each channel's bend range, so a quarter tone written as a bend comes back as its frequency; a bend that moves during a note makes a glide; channel 10 is drums and a key with no stroke here is dropped and counted in Losses; for the file written by ToMidiBytes from C4 D4 E4 C4 at 90 beats a minute it returned the same four notes at 261.63, 293.66, 329.63 and 261.63 hertz
warnings: text that is not a MIDI file, a SMPTE-timed file or format 2 is refused with the reason in LastError; 8 bytes of text gave MIDI: not a Standard MIDI File

methods.name: FromAbcQ
methods.brief: Reads ABC 2.1 text into a stzSoundScore, with voices, repeats played out and the key signature applied.

parameters.name: pcAbc
parameters.role: the ABC text, a header ending with a K: line and then the music

methods.returns: a stzSoundScore with the instrument named by each voice; an empty text when refused, with the reason in LastError
notes: beats are quarter notes, so Q:3/8=100 is 150 beats a minute and a 6/8 bar is three beats, checked by hand; repeats such as a repeated pair of notes between repeat bars are played out, so the score holds what is performed; lengths, ties, broken rhythm, tuplets, chords, rests and bar accidentals are read; decorations and lyrics are dropped and counted in Losses
warnings: an empty text, or music before the K: line, gives an empty text and the error ABC: the text is empty or ABC: music before the K: line

methods.name: FromMusicXMLFileQ
methods.brief: Reads an uncompressed MusicXML file from disk into a stzSoundScore.

parameters.name: pcPath
parameters.role: the path of the file

methods.returns: a stzSoundScore; an empty text when the file is missing or refused, with the reason in LastError
notes: a compressed .mxl is refused: unzip it first
warnings: a path that does not exist gives an empty text and the error FromMusicXMLFileQ: no file at ...

methods.name: FromMusicXMLQ
methods.brief: Reads MusicXML text, score-partwise, into a stzSoundScore: what sounds, with decimal alterations as quarter tones.

parameters.name: pcXml
parameters.role: the MusicXML text

methods.returns: a stzSoundScore; an empty text when refused, with the reason in LastError
notes: a transposing part is read at its sounding pitch; repeats are played out; the key signature is not needed because every alteration is on its note; the score written by ToMusicXML from C4 D4 E4 C4 came back as the same four notes
warnings: score-timewise, a text that is not well-formed XML and a duration before any divisions are refused with the reason in LastError

classes.name: stzSoundPattern
classes.brief: Holds rhythm written as a string, Tidal's mini-notation, as a function of time that answers the events of any cycle.
classes.description: A pattern is not a list of notes but a function from a cycle number to the events in that cycle, so the verbs compose. In the string a b c is a sequence sharing the cycle, ~ a rest, [a b] a group sharing one step, [a, b] a stack, <a b> an alternation by cycle, a*2 twice as fast, a/2 half as fast, a? sometimes, a!3 three times and a@3 three steps long. A word is a note name or a stroke, with bd, sn and hh stored as kick, snare and hihat. ToScoreQ turns cycles into a stzSoundScore, four beats a cycle, which is data a player can render; nothing here opens an audio device or plays. Not here: euclidean rhythms, fractional factors, sample banks and jux. The output has not been heard by a person (UNPERCEIVED): it is checked by the events it holds.
classes.example:
? o1.IsAllStrokes()
#--> 1
? o1.HasStroke("kick")
#--> 1
? o1.HasStroke("crash")
#--> 0
oS = o1.ToScoreQ(2)
? oS.NumberOfEvents()
#--> 8
? oS.Beats()
#--> 8
? oS.Events()[3][1]
#--> 3
? oS.Events()[3][6]
#--> hihat

methods.name: IsAllStrokes
methods.brief: TRUE if every event of the first cycle is a drum stroke, so the pattern names its own drum.
notes: a pattern of notes answers 0 and an empty pattern answers 0; only the first cycle is read, so an alternation that has notes in a later cycle can still answer 1

methods.name: HasStroke
methods.brief: TRUE if some event in any cycle of the pattern is the named stroke.

parameters.name: pcName
parameters.role: the stroke's canonical name, kick, snare, hihat, dum, tak, ka, crash, ride, hightom, midtom, floortom or openhat

notes: the words bd, sn and hh are spellings: they are stored as kick, snare and hihat, so HasStroke("bd") answers 0 and HasStroke("kick") answers 1; all the cycles of the pattern's period are searched

methods.name: ToScoreQ
methods.brief: Renders a number of cycles of the pattern as a stzSoundScore, a cycle being four beats.

parameters.name: pnCycles
parameters.role: how many cycles to render, from cycle 0

methods.returns: a stzSoundScore holding one event for each event of each cycle, of length 4 beats per cycle
notes: the pivot from a function of time to data: for bd ~ sn [hh hh] one cycle gives a kick at beat 0, a snare at 2 and hi-hats at 3 and 3.5, checked by hand; c e g gives three notes 1.33 beats long at 261.63, 329.63 and 392 hertz; an alternation such as <c e> gives c in cycle 0 and e in cycle 1; nothing is played

classes.name: stzSoundPlot
classes.brief: Draws a sound's analysis, a spectrogram, spectra or a waveform, as a readable picture on a dark plate, in SVG or PNG.
classes.description: Create the plate with a width and a height, set the title and the note, call one Draw method with the analysis it needs, add markers, then ToSVG, SaveAsSVG or SaveAsPNG. The title and the note are read when the Draw method runs, so they must be set before it. The spectrogram uses the inferno colour ramp, the spectra a fixed order of hues with a legend, and every magnitude axis is in decibels. Reach for it when a number about a sound is not enough: it needs the sound engine for the analysis grids, and the PNG needs the graphics device while the SVG does not. Only the first two lines of the note are drawn, and DrawSpectra raises for a starting frequency of 0; see the warnings. Gallery: doc/gallery/stzSoundPlot/spectrogram.png (a sweep), spectra.png (two tones with a marker) and wave.png (beats, with a marker), each with its script, seen right by stzlib-docs visual pass (a model reading the PNG), 2026-10-05, not a person; wave.png carries thin dark hairlines inside the filled band.
classes.example:
o1.SetNote("A short note.")
? @@( o1.ToNoteLines() )
#--> [ "A short note." ]

methods.name: init
methods.brief: Builds an empty dark plate of a width and a height in pixels, ready for one of the Draw methods, and looks for a system font.

parameters.name: pnWidth
parameters.role: The width of the plate, in pixels

parameters.name: pnHeight
