parameters.role: The height of the plate, in pixels

notes: the plot area leaves 64 pixels at the left, 22 at the right, 74 at the top and 62 at the bottom
warnings: A non-number or a size outside 1 to 16384 raises the stzCanvas error, and with no font found the plate is drawn without any text

methods.name: Canvas
methods.brief: Returns the stzCanvas the plate is drawn on, so extra shapes can be added to the picture.
notes: a shape added through it shows in the plot only after the canvas's Flush has posted it

methods.name: SetTitle
methods.brief: Sets the title and the subtitle written at the top left of the next picture drawn; one called after a Draw method changes nothing.

parameters.name: pcTitle
parameters.role: The title, drawn at 17 pixels in white

parameters.name: pcSubtitle
parameters.role: The subtitle under it, drawn at 12 pixels in grey

notes: call it before the Draw method and SetTitleQ answers the plot for chaining

extensions.name: SetTitleQ
extensions.adds: does what the method does, then returns the object, so the call can be chained

methods.name: SetNote
methods.brief: Sets the sentence written under the plot to say what the picture means; one called after a Draw method changes nothing.

parameters.name: pcNote
parameters.role: The sentence, wrapped to the plate width

notes: call it before the Draw method and SetNoteQ answers the plot for chaining
warnings: Only the first two wrapped lines are drawn, the rest are dropped without a message

extensions.name: SetNoteQ
extensions.adds: does what the method does, then returns the object, so the call can be chained

methods.name: ToNoteLines
methods.brief: Returns the note cut into the lines it will be laid out in, ready to be checked without reading the picture.
methods.returns: a list of text, empty when there is no note
notes: the line length follows the plate width at about 5.6 pixels a character
warnings: The plot draws only the first two lines of the list

methods.name: SetDynamicRange
methods.brief: Sets how many decibels below the loudest cell of a spectrogram still get ink; a value of zero or less is ignored.

parameters.name: pnDb
parameters.role: The range in decibels

notes: the default is 70, and a tighter range hides a broadband floor
warnings: Only DrawSpectrogram reads it, since DrawSpectra always spans 72 dB

extensions.name: SetDynamicRangeQ
extensions.adds: does what the method does, then returns the object, so the call can be chained

methods.name: SaveAsPNG
methods.brief: Draws the picture on the graphics device and writes it to a PNG file.

parameters.name: pcPath
parameters.role: The file to write

notes: use SaveAsSVG on a machine without a GPU
warnings: With no graphics device no file is written, and the answer is empty either way

methods.name: SaveAsSVG
methods.brief: Writes the picture to an SVG file, with no graphics device needed.

parameters.name: pcPath
parameters.role: The file to write

notes: text reaches the file as glyph outlines, not as characters

methods.name: ToSVG
methods.brief: Returns the picture as SVG text, with no graphics device needed.
methods.returns: the SVG document as a string
notes: an undrawn plate gives a bare background of about 160 characters

methods.name: DrawSpectrogram
methods.brief: Draws a spectrogram from an analysis grid, with time across, frequency up and loudness as brightness, in the inferno colour ramp.

parameters.name: poGrid
parameters.role: The analysis grid of a sound, from its ToSpectrogram

parameters.name: pnMaxHz
parameters.role: The highest frequency to show, or 0 to show them all

notes: the time axis ends at the grid's own span (0.96 s for a one second sound), so give MarkTimeAt that span
warnings: A silent or empty grid draws only the title, with no axes

methods.name: DrawSpectra
methods.brief: Draws one or more spectra as lines on a log frequency axis in decibels, all measured against the loudest point of any of them.

parameters.name: paSeries
parameters.role: The spectra, as pairs [ label, one-row grid ] where the grid comes from a sound's ToSpectrumOf

parameters.name: pnFromHz
parameters.role: The lowest frequency shown, which must be above 0

parameters.name: pnToHz
parameters.role: The highest frequency shown

notes: the first series is drawn on top, a legend appears from two series and the hues cycle after five
warnings: A starting frequency of 0 raises R51 because its logarithm is undefined

methods.name: DrawWave
methods.brief: Draws the waveform of a sound's first channel as a band between its lowest and highest sample in each pixel column.

parameters.name: poSound
parameters.role: The sound to draw, any object answering Frames, SampleAt and Duration

notes: the axis shows the time from 0 to the sound's duration and the amplitude from -1 to 1
warnings: A sound of fewer than two frames draws only the title

methods.name: MarkTimeAt
methods.brief: Draws a red vertical line with a label at a moment of the picture, to point at where something happens.

parameters.name: pnSeconds
parameters.role: The moment to mark, in seconds

parameters.name: pnTotalSeconds
parameters.role: The time span the horizontal axis shows

parameters.name: pcLabel
parameters.role: The text written beside the line

notes: call it after the Draw method
warnings: A moment past the span is drawn outside the plot area without an error

methods.name: MarkFrequencyAt
methods.brief: Draws a red vertical line with a label at a frequency on the log axis of DrawSpectra, to point at a corner or a fundamental.

parameters.name: pnHz
parameters.role: The frequency to mark

parameters.name: pnFromHz
parameters.role: The lowest frequency of the axis, as given to DrawSpectra

parameters.name: pnToHz
parameters.role: The highest frequency of the axis, as given to DrawSpectra

parameters.name: pcLabel
parameters.role: The text written beside the line

notes: call it after the Draw method with the same two limits
warnings: A frequency outside the axis is skipped without a message

classes.name: stzSoundRetunedVoice
classes.brief: Holds a spoken syllable on a note: the speech voice's own timbre with its pitch replaced by the engine's period-synchronous retuner.
classes.description: SAPI says the syllable slowly into memory and the engine's PSOLA lays its glottal periods back at the note's period, so the timbre is the speech voice's and the pitch is the engine's, held. Large shifts from the voice's own pitch, about 166 hertz for Zira, sound processed. Syllable holds one syllable, LineQ lays syllables on notes a beat each, and Sing does the same at 90 beats a minute when StzSoundSingingVerdict records the retuned voice as SINGING, which it does, ruled by the Principal on 2026-09-27. Everything is rendered to memory and checked by frame count, sample rate and peak; no audio device is opened. This run was not heard by a person (UNPERCEIVED).
classes.example:
? o1.IsUsable()
#--> 1
? oS.SampleRate()
#--> 48000
? oS.Frames() > 57600 and oS.Frames() < 66000
#--> 1
? oS.Peak() > 0.1 and oS.Peak() <= 1
#--> 1
? o1.Marks() > 50
#--> 1
oL = o1.LineQ("la la la", "c4 e4 g4", 90)
? oL.Frames()
#--> 124800
oBad = o1.Syllable("la", "Zzz9", 1)
? o1.LastError()
#--> a pitch is a note name (A3, C#4) or Hz

methods.name: init
methods.brief: Builds a retuned voice over the machine's speech voices, taking the last one installed.
methods.returns: nothing; the object is built, and not usable when the machine has no speech voice
notes: StzSoundRetunedVoiceQ builds the same object; with no voice it counts a refusal and LastError says no SAPI voice

methods.name: IsUsable
methods.brief: TRUE if a speech voice is available to retune.

methods.name: VoiceName
methods.brief: Returns the name of the speech voice in use.
methods.returns: the name as text, such as Microsoft Zira Desktop - English (United States); an empty text when the voice is not usable

methods.name: SetVibrato
methods.brief: Sets the depth of the vibrato laid on a held syllable.

parameters.name: pnCents
parameters.role: the depth in cents, from 0 to 100

methods.returns: the voice itself, so calls chain
notes: the default is 20 cents
warnings: a value outside 0 to 100 or not a number is refused: it counts a refusal, sets LastError to SetVibrato: 0 to 100 cents, and the old depth stays

methods.name: FromHz
methods.brief: Returns the pitch the last syllable had as the speech voice spoke it.
methods.returns: a number in hertz; 0 before any syllable
notes: for the syllable la of the voice here it was 187.11, so a note far from it is a large shift and sounds processed

methods.name: Marks
methods.brief: Returns how many glottal periods the last retune found in the spoken syllable.
notes: 139 for the syllable la of the voice here

methods.name: Spoken
methods.brief: Returns a syllable as the speech voice says it, slowly and mono, before any retuning.

parameters.name: pcSyllable
parameters.role: the text to speak

methods.returns: a stzSound at the voice's own rate, 22050 hertz here, mono; an empty text when the voice is not usable or refused
notes: the sound is rendered to memory; the syllable la gave 75398 frames and a peak of 0.77; release it with Release when done

methods.name: Syllable
methods.brief: Holds a spoken syllable on a note: the voice's own timbre with the pitch laid down by the engine's period-synchronous retuner.

parameters.name: pcSyllable
parameters.role: the text to speak

parameters.name: pNote
parameters.role: a note name such as A3 or C#4, or a frequency in hertz

parameters.name: pnSeconds
parameters.role: how long to hold it, in seconds

methods.returns: a mono stzSound at 48000 hertz; an empty text when the pitch is bad or the voice failed, with the reason in LastError
notes: the sound runs about 0.05 s longer than asked: 1.2 s gave 60001 frames and 1.0 s gave 50401; the peak was 0.56; the vibrato is the one set by SetVibrato
warnings: a pitch that is neither a note name nor a number, such as Zzz9, gives an empty text and the error a pitch is a note name (A3, C#4) or Hz

methods.name: LineQ
methods.brief: Sings syllables on notes, one beat each, laid end to end into one sound.

parameters.name: pcSyllables
parameters.role: the syllables, separated by spaces

parameters.name: pcNotes
parameters.role: the notes, separated by spaces, one for each syllable

parameters.name: pnBpm
parameters.role: the tempo in beats a minute

methods.returns: a mono stzSound at 48000 hertz as long as the notes plus 0.6 s; an empty text when the counts differ or a syllable failed
notes: each syllable is held for 95 percent of a beat; three syllables at 90 beats a minute gave 124800 frames, which is 2.6 seconds
warnings: a different number of syllables and notes gives an empty text and the error LineQ: as many syllables as notes

methods.name: Sing
methods.brief: Sings lyrics on notes through LineQ at 90 beats a minute, if the voice has been ruled to sing.

parameters.name: pcLyrics
parameters.role: the syllables, separated by spaces

parameters.name: pcNotes
parameters.role: the notes, separated by spaces

methods.returns: the same sound as LineQ; an empty text when the ruling is not SINGING
notes: the tempo is fixed at 90; the formant voice, by contrast, is still recorded as UNPERCEIVED
warnings: the class header still says Sing is refused until the author rules, which is out of date: StzSoundSingingVerdict records the retuned voice as SINGING, ruled by the Principal on 2026-09-27, and Sing returned a sound

methods.name: LastError
methods.brief: Returns the reason of the last refusal.
methods.returns: the reason as text; an empty text when the last call went well

methods.name: Refusals
methods.brief: Returns how many calls were refused.
notes: it counts a bad pitch, a count mismatch, a bad vibrato and a missing voice

classes.name: stzSoundScheduler
classes.brief: Plays a score live, posting each note to an engine timeline just before its frame.
classes.description: The notes are rendered first, all of them, so no instrument tunes itself while the performance runs. Notes are then posted a ring plus half a second ahead of the producer, and the engine counts any that still arrive after their frame in Late. Play and RunToEnd use a sound card through a transport and were not run in this reference. RenderThroughRing runs the same real-time path with this thread draining the ring instead of a card, so it opens no device, and its output matched the offline render of the same score at every 97th sample. The sound has not been heard by a person (UNPERCEIVED): it is checked by frame count, sample rate and peak level, not by listening.
classes.example:
? o1.Lookahead()
#--> 40384
? o1.Prepare()
#--> 1
? len(o1.Plan())
#--> 4
? o1.RenderThroughRing().Frames()
#--> 115200
? o1.Late()
#--> 0

methods.name: init
methods.brief: Builds a scheduler over a score, with a renderer for its notes and nothing started.

parameters.name: poScore
parameters.role: the stzSoundScore to perform

warnings: anything but an object is refused, with LastError set, and the scheduler then holds no score; a library without the sound engine does the same

methods.name: SetLookahead
methods.brief: Sets how many frames ahead of the producer each note must be posted.

parameters.name: pnFrames
parameters.role: the lookahead in frames

methods.returns: the scheduler itself, so calls chain
warnings: a very small value is meant to prove that the engine counts notes that arrive after their frame

methods.name: Lookahead
methods.brief: Returns how many frames ahead of the producer notes are posted.
methods.returns: a number of frames; the ring size plus half a second, 40384 at 48000 Hz, until SetLookahead changes it

methods.name: SetGain
methods.brief: Sets the factor applied to every note when it is placed on the timeline.

parameters.name: pnGain
parameters.role: the gain per note, 0.6 by default

methods.returns: the scheduler itself, so calls chain
warnings: it changes the renderer's gain, which is read each time a note is posted

methods.name: Prepare
methods.brief: Renders every note of the score and builds the graph with its timeline, once.
methods.returns: TRUE if the scheduler is ready; FALSE for a score with no renderable note
notes: the notes are rendered first so that no instrument tunes itself while the performance runs
warnings: asking again answers TRUE without rendering again; a score of no notes is refused, with LastError set

methods.name: NotesRendered
methods.brief: Returns how many distinct notes the instruments have rendered.
warnings: a note that recurs counts once, but only after Prepare has run

methods.name: SecondsRendering
methods.brief: Returns the wall time spent rendering the notes, in seconds.

methods.name: Play
methods.brief: Posts the first window of notes, starts the score on the audio device and returns at once.
notes: RunToEnd or Tick must follow to keep posting notes
warnings: not run in this reference: it opens an audio device through a transport; a refusal by the transport is copied into LastError and counted

extensions.name: PlayQ
extensions.adds: does what the method does, then returns the object, so the call can be chained

methods.name: Tick
methods.brief: Posts the notes that have come due, keeps the transport's clock and stops it after the last note has played out.
notes: cheap enough to call as often as you like
warnings: does nothing unless Play has started a transport; its device path was not run in this reference

methods.name: IsPlaying
methods.brief: TRUE if a transport started by Play is still running.
methods.returns: TRUE or FALSE; FALSE before Play

methods.name: RunToEnd
methods.brief: Ticks every 20 ms until the transport has stopped.
notes: blocks the calling thread until the last note has played out
warnings: returns at once when nothing is running, which is the only case run in this reference

methods.name: RenderThroughRing
methods.brief: Performs the score through the real-time path with no sound card and returns what came out as a sound.
methods.returns: a stzSound as long as the score's last note; NULL for a score with no renderable note
notes: it runs faster than a device would, which is harder for the scheduler; the sound has not been heard by a person
warnings: a producer thread renders the graph into a ring while this thread posts notes ahead of it and drains the ring, so no audio device is opened; the result matched the offline render at every 97th sample

methods.name: Placed
methods.brief: Returns how many notes have been posted to the timeline.
methods.returns: a number; 0 before anything is posted
warnings: read from the engine's timeline counters

methods.name: Late
methods.brief: Returns how many notes reached the timeline after the producer had rendered their frame.
methods.returns: a number; 0 is the answer to want
warnings: read from the engine's timeline counters

methods.name: LateMaxInMs
methods.brief: Returns the worst lateness of any note, in milliseconds.
methods.returns: a number of milliseconds; 0 when no note was late

methods.name: PostsRefused
methods.brief: Returns how many times the timeline refused a note because all its 512 slots were busy.
warnings: a refused note is retried on the next tick, not dropped

methods.name: Underruns
methods.brief: Returns the frames the device asked for and the ring could not supply, as of the last Tick.
methods.returns: a number; 0 when nothing has played on a device
warnings: the producer falling behind, counted apart from a note posted late

methods.name: Plan
methods.brief: Returns one row per event giving the frame it starts at and the buffer that holds its note.
methods.returns: a list of [ frame, bufferId ] rows in start order; [ ] for an empty score
warnings: the rows come from the renderer, which renders on first use

methods.name: Renderer
methods.brief: Returns the renderer that holds the score's notes.
warnings: it is the one the scheduler uses, not a copy to configure separately

methods.name: LastError
methods.brief: Returns the reason the last failure gave, or an empty text.

methods.name: Refusals
methods.brief: Returns how many times the scheduler refused to go on.

methods.name: Release
methods.brief: Stops any transport, frees the graph and frees the notes.
warnings: call it only once nothing is playing, because the timeline reads the note samples directly

classes.name: stzSoundScore
classes.brief: Holds music as data: a flat list of timed notes, rests and drum strokes, measured in beats rather than seconds.
classes.description: Everything from one note to a whole piece is the same type, so Then, Together, Repeat, On and Transpose work on all of it. An event is [ startBeat, beats, hz, instrument, velocity, stroke, glideEndHz ]. The performance settings Tempo, Quantize and Swing turn beats into frames only when a sound is made, in FrameOf, so one score can be rendered at two speeds or swung and straight without being rewritten. A refused call leaves the score unchanged, counts in Refusals and explains itself in LastError. ToSound renders to memory with no audio device; Play goes live through the scheduler. The result has not been heard by a person (UNPERCEIVED): it is checked by frame count, sample rate and peak level.
classes.receiver: o1 = new stzSoundScore("c e g c5")
classes.example:
? o1.Beats()
#--> 4
? o1.Seconds()
#--> 2
? o1.Contour()
#--> U U U
? o1.ToSound().SampleRate()
#--> 48000

methods.name: init
methods.brief: Builds a score, empty or filled from space-separated note names of one beat each.

parameters.name: pcNotes
parameters.role: space-separated note names, ~ for a rest, or an empty text for an empty score

notes: the octave carries from one name to the next
warnings: a name that is not a note is skipped and counted in Refusals

methods.name: Note
methods.brief: Appends one pitched note after everything already in the score.

parameters.name: pNote
parameters.role: a note name such as A4, C#3, Bb2 or D4+50, or a frequency in hertz

parameters.name: pnBeats
parameters.role: the length of the note in beats

methods.returns: the score itself, so calls chain
notes: the note takes the instrument named by On and the velocity set by SetVelocity
warnings: a name or length that is refused leaves the score unchanged, counts in Refusals and sets LastError

extensions.name: NoteQ
extensions.adds: does what the method does, then returns the object, so the call can be chained

methods.name: GlideAt
methods.brief: Adds a note whose pitch slides from one pitch to another over its whole length, at an explicit beat.

parameters.name: pnBeat
parameters.role: the beat where the glide starts, 0 or later

parameters.name: pFrom
parameters.role: the starting pitch, a note name or a frequency

parameters.name: pTo
parameters.role: the ending pitch, a note name or a frequency

parameters.name: pnBeats

classes.name: stzSoundScoreRenderer
classes.brief: Renders the events of a score once each into sound buffers that the offline render and the live scheduler share.
classes.description: Every event is rendered by its instrument, and the same note (same instrument, pitch, length, velocity and stroke) is rendered only once however often it recurs, because a wind instrument tunes itself by listening and that is slow. Plan lists a start frame and a buffer id per event; Offline mixes the plan into one stereo sound at 48000 Hz. An instrument that refuses a note, such as a glide on a pluck, is counted in Refusals and the note is missing from the plan. Nothing here opens an audio device. The sound has not been heard by a person (UNPERCEIVED): it is checked by frame count, sample rate and peak level.
classes.receiver: o1 = new stzSoundScoreRenderer(StzSoundScoreOfQ("c e c e"))
classes.example:
? len(o1.Plan())
#--> 4
? o1.NotesRendered()
#--> 2
? o1.Offline().Frames()
#--> 115200

classes.name: stzSoundStaff
classes.brief: Draws a score on the staff as musicians write it, as a list of marks first and an SVG picture second.
classes.description: The layout is computed as data, with each notehead, accidental, rest, tie, beam, ledger line and barline as a row of Model, and only then written as SVG, so a guard can hold the model to the rules of notation without reading pixels. It draws one staff per instrument with a clef chosen by range, bar splitting with ties, beaming by the beat, key signatures read from the music or set (quarter tones included), key and metre changes at barlines, and percussion staves. The readers Meters, KeyChanges, Key, KeyName, Losses, Model, Bars, Systems and Clefs are filled by ToSVG, ToHTML or SaveAs. A pitch more than 5 cents from the nearest quarter tone is drawn there and listed in Losses. The drawings have not been seen by a musician (UNPERCEIVED).

o1.ToSVG("Eight notes")
? o1.Bars()
#--> 2
? o1.KeyName()
#--> C major (no sharps or flats)
? o1.Clefs()[1][2]
#--> treble

classes.name: stzSoundTranscriber
classes.brief: Turns a sound into a score by finding the onsets, reading the pitch of each, and keeping how clear each pitch was.
classes.description: Onsets are found in the sample domain, a jump in the energy of the first difference in 5 ms hops, and refined to the sample. The pitch is read at each onset, past its attack, by the engine's unguided reader (McLeod, 50 to 2000 Hz) and its clarity becomes the note's confidence. What comes back is an ordinary stzSoundScore. It is monophonic and cannot say which stroke a drum hit was: an onset with no pitch is kept in Unpitched with its time. It works on a sound in memory and opens no audio device or microphone. The results have not been heard by a person (UNPERCEIVED): they are checked by pitch against the known notes.
classes.receiver: oScore = StzSoundScoreOfQ("C4 E4 G4 C5") oScore.Tempo(96) oSound = oScore.ToSound() o1 = StzSoundTranscriberQ() oBack = o1.TranscribeQ(oSound, 96)
classes.example:
? oBack.NumberOfEvents()
#--> 4
? oBack.Events()[1][1]
#--> 0.00
? oBack.Events()[2][1]
#--> 1
? floor(oBack.Events()[3][3] + 0.5)
#--> 392
? len(o1.Confidences())
#--> 4
? min(o1.Confidences()) > 0.9
#--> 1
? @@( o1.Unpitched() )
#--> [ ]
o2 = StzSoundTranscriberQ()
oNone = o2.TranscribeQ(0, 96)
? o2.LastError()
#--> TranscribeQ: nothing to transcribe

parameters.role: the tempo, in beats a minute, that turns seconds into beats

methods.returns: a stzSoundScore at the given tempo with one note for each onset that had a clear pitch; an empty score when the sound is missing or empty, with the reason in LastError
notes: it is monophonic: two notes at once are not separated; a rendered C4 E4 G4 C5 at 96 beats a minute came back as notes starting at beats 0, 1, 2 and 3 at 261.63, 329.56, 391.83 and 523.19 hertz, against the true 261.63, 329.63, 392.00 and 523.25; the length of a note runs to the next onset, so the last one includes its ring-out; the sound is read in a mono copy made by the engine

classes.name: stzSoundTransport
classes.brief: Plays, pauses, resumes and stops a sound graph on the audio device, and keeps a clock the rest of the library can read.
classes.description: The legal moves are declared once in a state machine: stopped to playing, playing to paused, paused to playing, and playing or paused to stopped. Any other move is refused and counted, never obeyed. The position comes from the frames the device has consumed, not from a wall clock, so it cannot drift from what is heard. Pause and Stop fade the master gain over 10 ms first, because cutting the device is an audible click. There is no seek, only Rewind to the top. Play, PlayFor, Resume and RunFor open an audio device and were not run in this reference; the examples use only the refused moves of a stopped transport. Nobody has heard the fades (UNPERCEIVED).
classes.example:
? o1.State()
#--> stopped
o1.Pause()
? o1.LastError()
#--> cannot pause while stopped
? o1.Refusals()
#--> 1

methods.name: init
methods.brief: Builds a transport over a graph, with a master gain added for fades and a state machine that starts stopped.

parameters.name: poGraph
parameters.role: the stzSoundGraph to start, pause and stop

notes: nothing starts and no device is opened here
warnings: a non-graph is refused, with LastError set; the master gain is added to the graph before it is prepared, which is why the graph gains a node

methods.name: State
methods.brief: Returns what the transport is doing now.
methods.returns: a text: stopped, playing or paused
warnings: stopped for a transport that was built without a graph

methods.name: IsPlaying
methods.brief: TRUE if the transport is in the playing state.

methods.name: IsPaused
methods.brief: TRUE if the transport is in the paused state.

methods.name: IsStopped
methods.brief: TRUE if the transport is in the stopped state, as it is when built.

methods.name: LastError
methods.brief: Returns the reason the last move was refused or failed, or an empty text.
methods.returns: a text such as cannot pause while stopped
warnings: a successful move clears it

methods.name: Refusals
methods.brief: Returns how many moves the state machine refused.
warnings: a transport that is driven wrongly says so in this number instead of misbehaving

methods.name: PositionInFrames
methods.brief: Returns the frames the device has consumed, not the frames the graph has produced.
methods.returns: a number of frames; 0 before any play
warnings: the producer runs a ring ahead of the device, so the device's count is what has been heard

methods.name: PositionInSeconds
methods.brief: Returns the device's position in seconds, from its frames and the graph's rate.

methods.name: SampleRate
methods.brief: Returns the sample rate of the graph the transport drives, in hertz.
methods.returns: a number; 48000 when the transport was built without a graph

methods.name: Underruns
methods.brief: Returns the frames the producer could not supply in time.
methods.returns: a number; 0 is the answer to want, and 0 when nothing is playing

methods.name: Play
methods.brief: Starts the graph on the audio device from the top and returns at once.
methods.returns: the transport itself, so calls chain
notes: with no device the move is undone and LastError says there is no audio device
warnings: not run in this reference: it opens an audio device; from any state but stopped it is refused by the state machine, counted, and LastError names the state

extensions.name: PlayQ
extensions.adds: does what the method does, then returns the object, so the call can be chained

methods.name: PlayFor
methods.brief: Starts the graph on the audio device and arranges for it to stop by itself after a number of seconds.

parameters.name: pnSeconds
parameters.role: how long to play before stopping

methods.returns: the transport itself, so calls chain
notes: a value of 0 or less means play until stopped
warnings: not run in this reference: it opens an audio device; the stop happens in Tick, so something must be ticking

extensions.name: PlayForQ
extensions.adds: does what the method does, then returns the object, so the call can be chained

methods.name: Pause
methods.brief: Fades the master gain to silence over 10 ms, closes the device and remembers the position.
methods.returns: the transport itself, so calls chain
notes: the fade comes first, because cutting the device dead is an audible click
warnings: the move is refused and counted when the transport is not playing, which is the only case run in this reference

extensions.name: PauseQ
extensions.adds: does what the method does, then returns the object, so the call can be chained

methods.name: Resume
methods.brief: Reopens the device after a pause, fades the master gain back up and goes on from where the graph was.
methods.returns: the transport itself, so calls chain
notes: the graph is not rewound, so an envelope half way through its decay goes on
warnings: refused and counted unless the transport is paused, which is the only case run in this reference; its device path was not run

extensions.name: ResumeQ
extensions.adds: does what the method does, then returns the object, so the call can be chained

methods.name: Stop
methods.brief: Fades the master gain to silence, closes the device, takes the transport out of any reactive loop and calls the finished handler.
methods.returns: the transport itself, so calls chain
notes: a stopped transport that was driven is no longer ticked
warnings: refused and counted when already stopped, which is the only case run in this reference

extensions.name: StopQ
extensions.adds: does what the method does, then returns the object, so the call can be chained

methods.name: Rewind
methods.brief: Takes the graph back to its top and the position back to 0, only while stopped.
methods.returns: the transport itself, so calls chain
notes: there is no seek: the engine can only rewind to the start
warnings: refused and counted when not stopped, since rewinding under a running device is a jump

extensions.name: RewindQ
extensions.adds: does what the method does, then returns the object, so the call can be chained

methods.name: Tick
methods.brief: Reads the device position, calls the tick handler and stops the transport once the stop time passed to PlayFor is reached.
methods.returns: the transport itself, so calls chain
notes: cheap enough to call as often as you like
warnings: does nothing unless the transport is playing, which is the only case run in this reference

methods.name: RunToEnd
methods.brief: Ticks every 20 ms until the transport is no longer playing.
methods.returns: the transport itself, so calls chain
notes: blocks the calling thread while it plays
warnings: returns at once when the transport is not playing

methods.name: RunFor
methods.brief: Plays for a number of seconds and waits, ticking, until the transport has stopped.

parameters.name: pnSeconds
parameters.role: how long to play

methods.returns: the transport itself, so calls chain
notes: it occupies the thread, like RunToEnd
warnings: not run in this reference: it opens an audio device

methods.name: DriveWith
methods.brief: Registers the transport so that a reactive loop steps it every 20 ms, alongside its other timers.

parameters.name: poReactive
parameters.role: the stzReactive whose loop should call the transport

methods.returns: the transport itself, so calls chain
notes: the transport is registered by pointer in a global list, and Stop or Release removes it
warnings: a non-reactive argument is refused, with LastError set and the refusal counted; registering twice adds it once; the loop was not run in this reference

extensions.name: DriveWithQ
extensions.adds: does what the method does, then returns the object, so the call can be chained

methods.name: OnStarted
methods.brief: Sets the function to call when the transport has started.

parameters.name: f
parameters.role: the function to call, with no arguments

methods.returns: the transport itself, so calls chain
warnings: a function that raises is swallowed silently

methods.name: OnFinished
methods.brief: Sets the function to call when the transport has stopped.

parameters.name: f
parameters.role: the function to call, with no arguments

methods.returns: the transport itself, so calls chain
warnings: a function that raises is swallowed silently

methods.name: OnTick
methods.brief: Sets the function to call at every step of a playing transport.

parameters.name: f
parameters.role: the function to call, with no arguments

methods.returns: the transport itself, so calls chain
warnings: a function that raises is swallowed silently

methods.name: Release
methods.brief: Takes the transport out of any reactive loop, closes the device and discards the state machine.
warnings: afterwards State answers stopped

classes.name: stzSoundUniverse
classes.brief: Holds a musical tradition declared as data, and plays a phrase of degrees inside it as a score.
classes.description: A universe declares a tuning, a pitch vocabulary with movement rules, a rhythmic cycle with accents, ornaments and an instrument set, as a list with no logic; the class reads the declaration and knows no tradition by name. A phrase is written in degrees, so one phrase means something in every universe: 5_ is a degree an octave down and a degree past the mode's size wraps up an octave. Eight traditions ship: western, maqam, tunisian, niger, raga, gamelan, westafrican and flamenco. Every declaration carries its sources and the line listener, UNPERCEIVED until a person from the tradition has heard it, and none has. Nothing here opens an audio device.
classes.example:
o1.Mode(:Hijaz).Tonic("D4")
? o1.CentsOf("3", FALSE)
#--> 400
? o1.HzOf("5", FALSE)
#--> 440
? len(o1.Check("1 2 3 4 5"))
#--> 0
? o1.PerformQ("1 2 3 4 5 4 3 2", 2).Beats()
#--> 16

methods.name: init
methods.brief: Loads one of the shipped musical traditions, declared as data, and chooses its default mode and rhythmic cycle.

parameters.name: pName
parameters.role: the tradition: western, maqam, tunisian, niger, raga, gamelan, westafrican or flamenco, in any case

notes: the universe's own speed and instrument are taken first, so a rhythm-only universe keeps its speed
warnings: an unknown tradition leaves the object unusable, with LastError listing those declared

methods.name: IsUsable
methods.brief: TRUE if a declaration was loaded.

methods.name: Name
methods.brief: Returns the short identifier of the loaded tradition, in lower case.
methods.returns: a text such as maqam; an empty text when unusable

methods.name: Title
methods.brief: Returns the declaration's full heading.
methods.returns: a text such as Arabic maqam

methods.name: Declaration
methods.brief: Returns the whole declaration as a list of key and value pairs.
warnings: the data a tradition's theorists wrote down; nothing in it is logic

methods.name: Listener
methods.brief: Returns who has heard this universe, or UNPERCEIVED.
methods.returns: a text; UNPERCEIVED until a person from the tradition has heard it, then their verdict
warnings: none of the shipped universes has a listener's verdict yet

methods.name: Sources
methods.brief: Returns where the declaration comes from.
methods.returns: a list of text, the references of the declaration

methods.name: ModeNames
methods.brief: Returns the modes the tradition declares.
methods.returns: a list of text in lower case; [ ] for a rhythm-only tradition

methods.name: CycleNames
methods.brief: Returns the rhythmic cycles the tradition declares.
methods.returns: a list of text in lower case

methods.name: Mode
methods.brief: Chooses a mode, taking its tonic, instrument and speed from the declaration.

parameters.name: pName
parameters.role: the mode's name, in any case

methods.returns: the universe itself, so calls chain
notes: it overrides a Tonic, Tempo or On given before
warnings: an unknown mode is refused, with LastError listing those declared

methods.name: Cycle
methods.brief: Chooses a rhythmic cycle.

parameters.name: pName
parameters.role: the cycle's name, in any case

methods.returns: the universe itself, so calls chain
warnings: an unknown cycle is refused, with LastError listing those declared

methods.name: NoCycle
methods.brief: Replaces the rhythmic cycle by a bare one with no layers and no accents, to hear a mode without its rhythm.

parameters.name: pnBeats
parameters.role: the length of the bare cycle in beats

methods.returns: the universe itself, so calls chain
warnings: the cycle is then called none

methods.name: Tonic
methods.brief: Sets the note from which the degrees are counted.

parameters.name: pcNote
parameters.role: a note name with its octave, such as D4

methods.returns: the universe itself, so calls chain
warnings: anything that is not a note name is refused, with LastError set, and the old note stays

methods.name: Tempo
methods.brief: Sets the speed of the performance, in beats per minute.

parameters.name: pnBpm
parameters.role: the speed in beats per minute

methods.returns: the universe itself, so calls chain
warnings: the value is stored without a check, and a score refuses a bad one when it is made

methods.name: On
methods.brief: Sets the instrument that plays the melody.

parameters.name: pInstrument
parameters.role: the instrument name, kept in lower case

methods.returns: the universe itself, so calls chain
warnings: an unknown instrument is refused only later, when the notes are rendered

methods.name: ModeName
methods.brief: Returns the chosen mode.
methods.returns: a text in lower case; an empty text for a rhythm-only tradition

methods.name: CycleName
methods.brief: Returns the chosen rhythmic cycle.

methods.name: TonicName
methods.brief: Returns the note from which degrees are counted.

methods.name: Melody
methods.brief: Returns the instrument that plays the melody.
methods.returns: a text in lower case; an empty text for a rhythm-only tradition

methods.name: HasScale
methods.brief: TRUE if the chosen mode declares degrees, so phrases can be written in it.
warnings: FALSE for a rhythm-only tradition such as westafrican

methods.name: LadderQ
methods.brief: Returns the chosen mode drawn as a ladder with a rung per degree, spaced by cents.
methods.returns: a stzSoundLadder at the current tonic
warnings: the ladder has not been seen by a person from the tradition

methods.name: CentsOf
methods.brief: Returns the distance of a degree above the tonic, in cents, going up or coming down.

parameters.name: pcDegree
parameters.role: the degree as text: 5, 5_ for the octave below, 9 for the next octave up

parameters.name: pbDown
parameters.role: TRUE to take the descending form of the mode where it declares one

methods.returns: a number of cents; -1 when the mode declares no scale
notes: measured in maqam hijaz: degree 3 is 400 cents, 5 is 700, 8 is 1200 and 5_ is -500
warnings: a degree past the mode's size wraps up an octave; 5_ is 1200 cents lower

methods.name: HzOf
methods.brief: Returns the frequency of a degree, from the tonic and the declared cents.

parameters.name: pcDegree
parameters.role: the degree as text, such as 5 or 5_

parameters.name: pbDown
parameters.role: TRUE to take the descending form of the mode where it declares one

methods.returns: a number of hertz; 0 when the mode declares no scale
warnings: measured: with the tonic D4, degree 1 is 293.66 Hz, degree 5 is 440 and degree 8 is 587.33

methods.name: Check
methods.brief: Holds a phrase of degrees against the movement rules of the chosen mode and lists what breaks them.

parameters.name: pcPhrase
parameters.role: the phrase in degrees, such as 1 2 3 4 5

methods.returns: a list of text, one per broken rule; [ ] for a phrase the declaration allows
warnings: a phrase that is not made of degrees gives one text, the parser's reason; an empty list is not a verdict by a musician of the tradition

methods.name: PerformQ
methods.brief: Plays a phrase of degrees through the rhythmic cycle, for a number of cycles, as a score.

parameters.name: pcPhrase
parameters.role: the phrase in degrees, such as 1 2 3 4 5 4 3 2, where 5_ is an octave down

parameters.name: pnCycles
parameters.role: how many times the phrase is repeated

methods.returns: a stzSoundScore with the universe's speed; an empty score with LastError set when the mode has no scale or the phrase is bad
notes: no audio device is opened; the score has not been heard by a person from the tradition
warnings: the cycle's accents raise the velocity, the mode's ornaments become slides and graces, and the cycle's own layers play beneath; for a rhythm-only tradition the rhythm is still returned, with the refusal recorded

methods.name: Sentences
methods.brief: Returns the sentences the tradition declares for its talking drum.
methods.returns: a list of text; [ ] when it declares none

methods.name: SentenceQ
methods.brief: Returns a declared sentence as a score of drum notes, each syllable at the pitch of its tone.

parameters.name: pcText
parameters.role: the sentence, as listed by Sentences

methods.returns: a stzSoundScore; an empty score with LastError set for an unknown sentence
notes: no audio device is opened; the drum has not been heard by a Hausa speaker
warnings: a high tone, a low tone or a falling glide per syllable, a long vowel lasting two units

methods.name: SonifyQ
methods.brief: Turns a series of numbers into a melody in the chosen mode, the lowest value on degree 1 and the highest two octaves up.

parameters.name: paValues
parameters.role: the numbers to turn into notes

methods.returns: a stzSoundScore; an empty score with LastError set when the mode has no scale, the series is shorter than two, holds a non-number or does not move
notes: no audio device is opened
warnings: the top degree is lowered when the melody instrument cannot play it

methods.name: SonifiedDegrees
methods.brief: Returns the degrees the last SonifyQ chose, one per value.
methods.returns: a list of numbers; [ ] before SonifyQ

methods.name: SonifiedTop
methods.brief: Returns the highest degree the last SonifyQ allowed.
methods.returns: a number: twice the mode's size, or fewer when the instrument's range is short; 0 before SonifyQ

methods.name: SonifiedPhrase
methods.brief: Returns the degree phrase the last SonifyQ built, one bracket per cycle.
methods.returns: a text such as <[3 7 5 9] [1 8 ~ ~]>; an empty text before SonifyQ

methods.name: ToneSyllables
methods.brief: Reads Hausa text with tone marks into syllables, each with its tone and length.

parameters.name: pcText
parameters.role: Hausa text in UTF-8 with Newman's tone marks: no mark is high, a grave low, a circumflex falling

methods.returns: a list of [ syllable, tone, units ] rows, the tone H, L or F; [ ] when refused
notes: LastError keeps that reason after a later successful call, which does not clear it
warnings: text with no tone mark at all is refused, with LastError set, since reading it as all high would be a confident lie

methods.name: DrumTonesQ
methods.brief: Returns marked Hausa text as a score of drum notes, each syllable at the pitch of its tone.

parameters.name: pcText
parameters.role: Hausa text in UTF-8 with tone marks

methods.returns: a stzSoundScore; an empty score with LastError set when the text has no tone marks or the tradition has no talking drum
notes: the drum has not been heard by a Hausa speaker
warnings: no audio device is opened; it draws the contour of the tones and does not claim to be speech

methods.name: SayOnDrum
methods.brief: Gives marked Hausa text on the talking drum, once a Hausa speaker has confirmed that the drum speaks.

parameters.name: pcText
parameters.role: Hausa text in UTF-8 with tone marks

methods.returns: a stzSoundScore when the declaration's verdict is SPEAKS; an empty text otherwise
notes: the gate is the declaration's talking drum verdict, not a flag in code
warnings: refused today, with LastError naming the missing verdict, because the verdict is UNPERCEIVED

methods.name: ToSound
methods.brief: Renders a phrase of degrees through the rhythmic cycle to a sound in memory.

parameters.name: pcPhrase
parameters.role: the phrase in degrees, such as 1 2 3

parameters.name: pnCycles
parameters.role: how many times the phrase is repeated

methods.returns: a stzSound at 48000 Hz, two channels
notes: the sound has not been heard by a person from the tradition
warnings: no audio device is opened; a bad phrase gives a sound of one frame, with LastError set

methods.name: PlayedNotes

classes.name: stzSplitter
classes.brief: Holds a number of positions, 1 to N, and answers where a string or a list would be cut, as sections [ first, last ] and never as parts.
classes.description: A splitter knows only a size. It never sees the items: every Split method returns a list of sections that a stzString or a stzList then hands to its own Sections method to get the parts. The family has three axes. The cut can fall AT a position or section (the cut-out positions are left out), BEFORE it (the position starts a new section) or AFTER it (the position ends a section); each exists for one position, for several positions, for one section and for several sections, plus SplitToNParts and SplitToPartsOfNItems for even cuts. The IB forms (inclusive bounds, such as SplitAtSectionIB) grow the sections by one part width so the cut positions are kept. Known gaps today, each carried as a warning on its method: SplitAround with a flat pair raises R19, SplitAroundSection raises R14, SplitAroundPosition raises R21 for the last position, SplitAtSections reads its first and last cuts before sorting, and the named forms of SplitAt (:ToNParts, :ToPartsOfNItems) raise R14.

classes.name: stzSqliteDataSource
classes.brief: Holds a local SQLite database as the data port of the service plane: a real database in a file you own, not a fake.
classes.description: A data port is any object with Exec, Rows and Value, the surface stzDatabase already has. This source is local-real: SQLite is not a pretend database, so it may ship, and registering it with BindLocal says so. The one dangerous case is the :memory: path, a genuine database that loses every row at restart and is one character away from a file path, so IsEphemeral reports it and the registry treats it as an error in a production phase. The three port methods run the SQL text as written; the small conveniences, TableExists, Tables and RowCount, build their own SQL. At deploy a hosted client such as Postgres is bound behind the same three methods.
classes.example:
o1.Exec("CREATE TABLE people (id INTEGER, name TEXT)")
? o1.Exec("INSERT INTO people VALUES (1, 'Aicha'), (2, 'Zin')")
#--> 2
? o1.Value("SELECT name FROM people WHERE id = 2")
#--> Zin
? o1.RowCount("people")
#--> 2
? @@( o1.Tables() )
#--> [ "people" ]
? o1.IsEphemeral()
#--> 1

classes.name: stzStateMachine
classes.brief: A finite state machine kept in the engine: add states and transitions, send events, and read the state the machine is in.
classes.description: Declare the states, then the transitions as [ from, event, to ]. Send follows the matching transition and answers the new state. The first state added is the starting state. Mistakes are not reported by the machine: an event that matches no transition, a SetState to an unknown state and a transition naming an unknown state are all ignored without an error, so check CurrentState after the call that matters.
classes.example:
? o1.CurrentState()
#--> closed
? o1.Send("open")
#--> open
? o1.Send("lock")
#--> open
? o1.NumberOfTransitions()
#--> 3

classes.name: stzStochasticSolver
classes.brief: Describes one optimisation problem under several scenarios, each with a probability, and checks and scores a plan against all of them.
classes.description: Declare variables, constraints and an objective as for stzLinearSolver, then add scenarios: each has a name, a description, parameters such as [ "d", 4 ] that are replaced as text inside the expressions and the constraint values, and a probability. The probabilities must add up to 1 when the problem is solved. setSolverType chooses expected, robust, chance or montecarlo. WHAT WORKS TODAY: the description of the problem, the scenario parameters, evaluateConstraintValue, checkScenarioFeasibility, calculateScenarioObjectiveValue, analyzeScenarios and expectedObjectiveValue for a plan you supply. WHAT DOES NOT: solve gives wrong answers. The expected, robust and chance solvers leave every variable at its lower bound, because they update a copy of each solution pair, and calculateScenarioMaxValue answers 999999 (no limit) for every constraint, because its switch label on "=" or "<=" matches no operator, so the Monte Carlo solver returns upper bounds that break the constraints. The status is optimal in every case. See the defect list of wave 10.
classes.example:
o1.addVariable("x", 0, 10).addVariable("y", 0, 10)
o1.addScenario("low", "Low demand", [ [ "d", 4 ] ], 0.4).addScenario("high", "High demand", [ [ "d", 8 ] ], 0.6)
o1.addConstraint("x + y", "<=", "d").maximize("3*x + 2*y")
? o1.checkScenarioFeasibility([ [ "x", 3 ], [ "y", 1 ] ], o1.scenarios()[1])
#--> 1
? o1.checkScenarioFeasibility([ [ "x", 3 ], [ "y", 3 ] ], o1.scenarios()[1])
#--> 0
? o1.calculateScenarioObjectiveValue([ [ "x", 3 ], [ "y", 1 ] ], o1.scenarios()[2])
#--> 11
