methods.brief: Adds a constraint that must hold with a given probability, to be read when the solver type is chance.

parameters.name: expression
parameters.role: the left side, as text

parameters.name: operator
parameters.role: the comparison: "<=", ">=" or "="

parameters.name: value
parameters.role: a number or a text to evaluate

parameters.name: confidenceLevel
parameters.role: the probability, from 0 to 1, with which it must hold

methods.returns: the solver itself, so calls chain
warnings: a confidence level outside 0 to 1, or not a number, raises an error; the expression and the operator are not checked

methods.name: constraints
methods.brief: Returns the declared constraints in order, each as a list of expression, operator, value, scenario and chance pairs.
methods.returns: a list of lists of [ key, value ] pairs; [ ] when none is declared

methods.name: maximize
methods.brief: Sets the objective to an expression to make as large as possible, replacing any earlier objective.

parameters.name: expression
parameters.role: the objective, as text, which may name scenario parameters

methods.returns: the solver itself, so calls chain

methods.name: minimize
methods.brief: Sets the objective to an expression to make as small as possible, replacing any earlier objective.

parameters.name: expression
parameters.role: the objective, as text, which may name scenario parameters

methods.returns: the solver itself, so calls chain

methods.name: objective
methods.brief: Returns the objective expression as text.
methods.returns: a text; "" before an objective is set

methods.name: objectiveType
methods.brief: Returns whether the objective is to be made larger or smaller.
methods.returns: the text "maximize" or "minimize"; "maximize" before any objective is set

methods.name: setSolverType
methods.brief: Chooses how solve treats the uncertainty: expected, robust, chance or montecarlo.

parameters.name: cType
parameters.role: one of "expected", "robust", "chance" or "montecarlo", in lower case

methods.returns: the solver itself, so calls chain
warnings: any other name raises an error

methods.name: setRobustnessFactor
methods.brief: Sets the fraction, from 0 to 1, by which the robust solver shrinks every scenario limit; 0.1 by default.

parameters.name: nFactor
parameters.role: a number from 0 to 1

methods.returns: the solver itself, so calls chain
warnings: a value outside 0 to 1, or not a number, raises an error

methods.name: setConfidenceLevel
methods.brief: Sets the probability, from 0 to 1, that the chance solver aims to cover; 0.95 by default.

parameters.name: nLevel
parameters.role: a number from 0 to 1

methods.returns: the solver itself, so calls chain
warnings: a value outside 0 to 1, or not a number, raises an error

methods.name: evaluateConstraintValue
methods.brief: Returns a constraint's right side for one scenario: a number as it is, a text after its parameters are replaced and evaluated.

parameters.name: value
parameters.role: a number or a text such as "d * 2"

parameters.name: _scenario_
parameters.role: a scenario, as returned by scenarios

notes: with d = 4 the text "d * 2" gives 8 and "d + 3" gives 7

methods.name: evaluateExpression
methods.brief: Returns the value of a text holding a single number or one operation between two numbers: *, /, + or -.

parameters.name: cExpression
parameters.role: the text, such as "6 / 3"

notes: 6 / 3 gives 2, 7 - 2 gives 5, 2 + 3 gives 5
warnings: a text with two operations, such as "2 * 3 + 1", raises R41 Invalid numeric string, and a division by zero raises an error

methods.name: solve
methods.brief: Validates the problem and runs the solver chosen with setSolverType, then stores its solution.
methods.returns: the solver itself, so calls chain
warnings: no variable, no objective, no scenario, or probabilities that do not add up to 1 raise an error; the solvers expected, robust and chance leave every variable at its lower bound today, and no solver respects the constraints (see solveExpectedValue and calculateScenarioMaxValue); the status is set to optimal in every case

methods.name: solveExpectedValue
methods.brief: Returns a solution from the probability-weighted objective, giving each variable in turn the largest value its limits allow.
methods.returns: a list of [ name, value ] pairs, one per variable
warnings: it answers every variable at its lower bound: the update writes to a copy of the pair (_sol_ is a copy of the list item), so the solution never changes; with one variable x in 0..3, x <= 2 and maximize x it answers 0, and in a two-variable problem it answers 0 and 0; its limits are also broken, see calculateScenarioMaxValue

methods.name: solveRobust
methods.brief: Returns a solution built from the first scenario's objective, with each limit shrunk by the robustness factor.
methods.returns: a list of [ name, value ] pairs, one per variable
warnings: it answers every variable at its lower bound, for the same reason as solveExpectedValue (a copy of the pair is updated), on two problems

methods.name: solveChanceConstrained
methods.brief: Returns a solution built from the expected objective, with limits read at the confidence level.
methods.returns: a list of [ name, value ] pairs, one per variable
warnings: it answers every variable at its lower bound, for the same reason as solveExpectedValue (a copy of the pair is updated), on two problems

methods.name: solveMonteCarlo
methods.brief: Returns the best of 100 per-scenario solutions, each for a scenario drawn at random by probability.
methods.returns: a list of [ name, value ] pairs, one per variable
warnings: the draws are random; the constraints do not limit anything today, so every variable comes back at its upper bound (with x in 0..3 and x <= 2 it answered 3; with x + y <= d it answered 10 and 10)

methods.name: applyScenarioParameters
methods.brief: Returns the expression with every parameter name replaced by its value, as text.

parameters.name: cExpression
parameters.role: the expression, as text

parameters.name: aParameters
parameters.role: a list of [ name, value ] pairs

notes: the replacement is plain text: 2*d + x with d = 4 gives 2*4 + x, and dd + 2*d gives 44 + 2*4

methods.name: extractCoefficient
methods.brief: Returns the coefficient of one variable in an expression.

parameters.name: cExpression
parameters.role: the expression, as text

parameters.name: _cVarName_
parameters.role: the variable's name

methods.returns: a number; 0 when the variable does not appear
notes: in 3*x + 2*y the coefficient of y is 2

methods.name: parseObjectiveCoefficients
methods.brief: Returns the coefficient of each declared variable in an expression, in declaration order.

parameters.name: cExpression
parameters.role: the expression, as text

notes: 3*x + 2*y gives [ 3, 2 ]

methods.name: calculateExpectedResourceCost
methods.brief: Returns the probability-weighted sum, over the scenarios, of the absolute coefficients of a variable in the constraints that apply.

parameters.name: _cVarName_
parameters.role: the variable's name

methods.name: calculateWorstCaseResourceCost
methods.brief: Returns the largest, over the scenarios, of the summed absolute coefficients of a variable in the constraints that apply.

parameters.name: _cVarName_
parameters.role: the variable's name

methods.name: calculateChanceResourceCost
methods.brief: Returns the probability-weighted resource cost of a variable, each constraint weighted by its chance against the confidence level.

parameters.name: _cVarName_
parameters.role: the variable's name

methods.name: calculateExpectedMaxValue
methods.brief: Returns the smallest probability-weighted scenario limit on a variable, never below 0.

parameters.name: _cVarName_
parameters.role: the variable's name

parameters.name: _aSolution_
parameters.role: a list of [ name, value ] pairs for the other variables

notes: the weighting by probability makes the limit smaller than any single scenario allows
warnings: built on calculateScenarioMaxValue, so it answers 399999.6 for a variable whose scenario limit is really 4 and 6: the weighting multiplies the 999999 that means no limit

methods.name: calculateRobustMaxValue
methods.brief: Returns the smallest scenario limit on a variable, reduced by the robustness factor, never below 0.

parameters.name: _cVarName_
parameters.role: the variable's name

parameters.name: _aSolution_
parameters.role: a list of [ name, value ] pairs for the other variables

warnings: built on calculateScenarioMaxValue, so it answers 899999.1 where the limit is really 4 and 6

methods.name: calculateChanceMaxValue
methods.brief: Returns the scenario limit on a variable at which the cumulated probability, from the smallest limit up, reaches the confidence level.

parameters.name: _cVarName_
parameters.role: the variable's name

parameters.name: _aSolution_
parameters.role: a list of [ name, value ] pairs for the other variables

warnings: built on calculateScenarioMaxValue, so it answers 999999 where the limit is really 4 and 6

methods.name: calculateScenarioMaxValue
methods.brief: Returns the largest value a variable can take in one scenario, given the values of the others, from the constraints that apply.

parameters.name: _cVarName_
parameters.role: the variable's name

parameters.name: _aSolution_
parameters.role: a list of [ name, value ] pairs for the other variables

parameters.name: _scenario_
parameters.role: a scenario, as returned by scenarios

warnings: it answers 999999, meaning no limit, for every constraint with "<=", ">=" or "=": the switch labelled on "=" or "<=" matches none of the operators; one variable x with x <= 6, x >= 6 or x = 6 gives 999999 each time

methods.name: getWorstCaseObjective
methods.brief: Returns the objective expression of the first scenario, with its parameters replaced.
warnings: it does not look for a worst case: it keeps the first scenario's objective, as its comment says

methods.name: solveForScenario
methods.brief: Returns a solution for one scenario, filling the variables in declaration order with the largest value the limits and the upper bound allow.

parameters.name: _scenario_
parameters.role: a scenario, as returned by scenarios

methods.returns: a list of [ name, value ] pairs, one per variable
warnings: the constraints do not limit anything today (calculateScenarioMaxValue), so every variable comes back at its upper bound: with x + y <= d it answered 10 and 10

methods.name: calculateScenarioObjectiveValue
methods.brief: Returns the objective's value for a solution under one scenario's parameters.

parameters.name: _aSolution_
parameters.role: a list of [ name, value ] pairs

parameters.name: _scenario_
parameters.role: a scenario, as returned by scenarios

notes: 3*x + 2*y with x = 1 and y = 2 gives 7

methods.name: getSolutionValue
methods.brief: Returns the value of one variable in a list of [ name, value ] pairs.

parameters.name: _aSolution_
parameters.role: a list of [ name, value ] pairs

parameters.name: _cVarName_
parameters.role: the variable's name

methods.returns: a number; 0 when the name is not in the list

methods.name: analyzeScenarios
methods.brief: Returns, for each scenario, the objective value and the feasibility of the stored solution.
methods.returns: a list of lists of scenario, probability, objectivevalue and feasible pairs
warnings: raises an error when no solution is stored, so call solve first

methods.name: checkScenarioFeasibility
methods.brief: TRUE if a solution satisfies every constraint that applies in one scenario, within 0.001.

parameters.name: _aSolution_
parameters.role: a list of [ name, value ] pairs

parameters.name: _scenario_
parameters.role: a scenario, as returned by scenarios

notes: with 2*x + y <= d, d = 4, x = 1 and y = 2 it is TRUE and with x = 2 and y = 2 it is FALSE

methods.name: expectedObjectiveValue
methods.brief: Returns the probability-weighted objective value of the stored solution over all scenarios.

methods.name: solution
methods.brief: Returns the solution stored by the last solve.
methods.returns: a list of [ name, value ] pairs; [ ] before any solve

methods.name: status
methods.brief: Returns how the last solve ended.
methods.returns: the text optimal after a solve; "" before

methods.name: iterations
methods.brief: Returns the work counted by the last solve: the number of variables, set by the expected solver only.
methods.returns: a number; 0 before any solve or for the other solver types

methods.name: solveTime
methods.brief: Returns the time the last solve took, in seconds.

methods.name: solverType
methods.brief: Returns the solver type in force.
methods.returns: the text expected, robust, chance or montecarlo; expected by default

methods.name: show
methods.brief: Prints the problem, its scenarios and, once solved, the solution, the expected objective and the analysis of every scenario.
methods.returns: nothing; it prints to the console

methods.name: exportToCSV
methods.brief: Writes the stored solution to a file, one Variable,Value line per variable.

parameters.name: cFileName
parameters.role: the path of the file to write

methods.name: exportScenarioAnalysis
methods.brief: Writes the objective value and feasibility of the stored solution for each scenario to a file.

parameters.name: cFileName
parameters.role: the path of the file to write

notes: the first line is Scenario,Probability,ObjectiveValue,Feasible; it raises when nothing is solved

classes.name: stzStopwatch
classes.brief: Measures elapsed time on the monotonic engine clock, with pause, laps, and export as an OpenTelemetry span.
classes.description: A stopwatch starts running when it is made. Pause leaves the paused time out, Resume carries on, Stop also stamps the end of the span, and Start throws everything away and begins again. Elapsed time is a number in the unit named by the method, taken from a clock that wall-clock changes cannot move. A stopped stopwatch is exportable as an OpenTelemetry span with real W3C trace and span ids, its laps as events, so a program can hand its timings to any OTLP backend. Assert ranges and signs on live readings, never exact values.
classes.example:
? o1.IsRunning()
#--> 1
o1.Lap("first")
o1.Stop()
? o1.NumberOfLaps()
#--> 1
? o1.IsRunning()
#--> 0
? o1.Record()[:name]
#--> job
? o1.ElapsedNs() > 0
#--> 1

methods.name: init
methods.brief: Builds a stopwatch that starts running at once, under a name that labels its span.

parameters.name: pcName
parameters.role: the span's name, kept as given

methods.name: Name
methods.brief: Returns the name that labels this stopwatch's span.
methods.returns: a text; empty when none was given

methods.name: SetName
methods.brief: Sets the name of the span; a value that is not a text is ignored and the old name is kept.

parameters.name: pcName
parameters.role: the new name, as text

methods.returns: the stopwatch itself, so calls chain

methods.name: Start
methods.brief: Restarts the stopwatch from zero, with no laps and a fresh start time, and leaves it running.
methods.returns: the stopwatch itself, so calls chain
notes: it throws away the time already counted; use Resume to carry on after a pause

methods.name: Pause
methods.brief: Stops counting without discarding what was counted, so the time spent paused is left out.
methods.returns: the stopwatch itself, so calls chain; pausing twice changes nothing

methods.name: Resume
methods.brief: Starts counting again after a pause or a stop and clears the span's end time, keeping the time already counted.
methods.returns: the stopwatch itself, so calls chain

methods.name: Stop
methods.brief: Pauses the stopwatch and stamps the span's end time, so the record and the export carry a closed interval.
methods.returns: the stopwatch itself, so calls chain

methods.name: Reset
methods.brief: Sets the elapsed time to zero, empties the laps and leaves the stopwatch paused, not running.
methods.returns: the stopwatch itself, so calls chain

methods.name: IsRunning
methods.brief: TRUE if the stopwatch is counting, FALSE once it is paused, stopped or reset.

methods.name: ElapsedNs
methods.brief: Returns the time counted so far in nanoseconds, from the monotonic engine clock.

methods.name: ElapsedUs
methods.brief: Returns the time counted so far in microseconds, as a number with a fraction.

methods.name: ElapsedMs
methods.brief: Returns the time counted so far in milliseconds, as a number with a fraction; the library's house unit.

methods.name: ElapsedS
methods.brief: Returns the time counted so far in seconds, as a number with a fraction.

methods.name: Lap
methods.brief: Records a split reading with a label and the elapsed milliseconds, without stopping the watch.

parameters.name: pcLabel
parameters.role: the split's label

methods.returns: the stopwatch itself, so calls chain

methods.name: Laps
methods.brief: Returns the splits recorded so far, oldest first.
methods.returns: a list of hashlists with the keys label, atMs and wallMs

methods.name: NumberOfLaps
methods.brief: Returns how many splits have been recorded since the last start or reset.

methods.name: Record
methods.brief: Returns the stopwatch as one hashlist, the library's own serialization of a span.
methods.returns: a hashlist with the keys name, startWallMs, stopWallMs, durationMs, running and laps; stopWallMs is 0 while the span is open
notes: the wall times are epoch milliseconds; durationMs comes from the monotonic clock

methods.name: TraceContextQ
methods.brief: Returns the W3C trace context object of this span, created on first use.

methods.name: TraceId
methods.brief: Returns the 32-hex-digit trace identity of the span.
methods.returns: a text of 32 hexadecimal digits; empty after JoinTrace with a header that is not valid

methods.name: SpanId
methods.brief: Returns the 16-hex-digit identity of this span inside its trace.
methods.returns: a text of 16 hexadecimal digits; empty after JoinTrace with a header that is not valid

methods.name: TraceParent
methods.brief: Returns the W3C traceparent header value to hand to a downstream call so both join one trace.
methods.returns: a text such as 00-<trace id>-<span id>-01

methods.name: JoinTrace
methods.brief: Adopts the identity carried by an incoming traceparent header, so this span joins an existing trace.

parameters.name: pcTraceParent
parameters.role: the traceparent header text received from the caller

methods.returns: the stopwatch itself, so calls chain
notes: a valid header gives its trace and span ids back unchanged
warnings: the header is not checked: garbage, a short header such as 00-abc-def-01 and an empty text leave TraceId and SpanId empty, TraceParent echoes the text as given, and the OTLP export then carries an empty traceId and spanId

methods.name: ToOtelSpan
methods.brief: Returns the span in OpenTelemetry vocabulary, with its laps as events and its exact duration as an attribute.
methods.returns: a hashlist with the keys name, traceId, spanId, kind, startTimeUnixNano, endTimeUnixNano, attributes and events
notes: the absolute times are epoch nanoseconds written as text (milliseconds followed by 000000), because a number cannot hold them; a running watch is exported with the current time as its end

methods.name: ToOtelJson
methods.brief: Returns the span as one OTLP-style JSON text, ready for a backend that speaks OpenTelemetry.
methods.returns: a text holding one JSON object

methods.name: Explain
methods.brief: Returns a short narration of the stopwatch: its name, state, elapsed milliseconds and one line per lap.

methods.name: Show
methods.brief: Prints the narration of the stopwatch, one line per row.

classes.name: stzStoryboard
classes.brief: Tells a story over one picture as an ordered list of frames, each with a caption whose numbers are read from the picture's facts.
classes.description: A frame is opened with Frame, changed with marks (Emphasis, Callout, Measure, Show, Region), a window (WindowOn, SetWindow) or an action (Act), and closed by opening the next frame or by asking any question about the frames. The caption carries holes, written {name}, never numbers: Bind ties a hole to a fact read from the picture when the frame closes, and BindFact takes a fact from another plane. Closing a frame draws the picture to a PNG file named after the storyboard, in the folio, and puts it through the picture gate, which prints a line. Judge then checks every frame against the gate and every hole against its fact, and Render writes the HTML page that shows the frames in order. A frame about a picture that is meant to be unlawful says so with ExpectFindings. Marks stay on the picture from frame to frame until ClearMarks. The storyboard keeps its own copy of the picture, so every change goes through it. ToNarration writes the same story as a .narration document, and RenditionAs gives it as markup or text.
classes.receiver: oS = new stzMathSubstance(StzSetTheoryDomain()); oS.DeclareAll("Set", [ "A", "B" ]); oS.Assert("Subset", [ "B", "A" ]); oS.AutoLabelAll(); oP = new stzMathDiagram(StzSetTheoryDomain(), oS, StzEulerStyle()); oP.SetFont(new stzFont("C:/Windows/Fonts/segoeui.ttf"), 28); oP.SetVariation("twosets"); StzEngineDirCreatePath("t_story_doc"); o1 = new stzStoryboard("sets", oP, "t_story_doc")
classes.example:
o1.Frame("B has radius {r} px and A has {ra} px.")
o1.Bind("r", :value, [ "B.icon.r" ])
o1.Bind("ra", :value, [ "A.icon.r" ])
o1.Emphasis("B.icon", :ring)
? o1.Caption(1)
#--> B has radius 46.40 px and A has 155.32 px.
? o1.FileOf(1)
#--> sets_01.png
? o1.NumberOfHoles()
#--> 2
? o1.IsClean()
#--> 1
o1.Frame("A frame that expects something to be wrong.")
o1.ExpectFindings()
? o1.Judge()[1][:rule]
#--> expected_a_finding_and_got_none

methods.name: init
methods.brief: Builds a storyboard of frames about one picture, named so that its frame files are named after it.

parameters.name: pcName
parameters.role: the storyboard's name, which starts the name of every frame file

parameters.name: poPicture
parameters.role: the picture the frames are about, such as a stzMathDiagram

parameters.name: pcFolio
parameters.role: the folder that receives the frame files and the page, or an empty text for the current folder

notes: the storyboard keeps its own copy of the picture, so changes must go through the storyboard
warnings: an empty name raises stzStoryboard: a storyboard needs a name, and a picture that is not an object raises give the picture the frames are about; the folder must already exist

methods.name: Frame
methods.brief: Closes the frame being built, if any, and opens a new one with its caption, whose {holes} are filled when it closes.

parameters.name: pcCaption
parameters.role: the sentence of the frame, with a hole written {name} wherever a number from a fact goes

methods.returns: the storyboard itself, so calls chain
notes: FrameQ is the same call; a frame closes by itself when another is opened or any question about the frames is asked
warnings: the marks of earlier frames stay on the picture: use ClearMarks to start a frame clean; closing a frame draws the picture to a PNG file and prints the gate's line pictures judged

extensions.name: FrameQ
extensions.adds: does what the method does, then returns the object, so the call can be chained

methods.name: FrameOf
methods.brief: Closes the frame being built and opens a new one on a different picture, which becomes the picture of the storyboard.

parameters.name: poPicture
parameters.role: the picture this frame and the next ones are about

parameters.name: pcCaption
parameters.role: the sentence of the frame, with its holes

methods.returns: the storyboard itself, so calls chain
notes: FrameOfQ is the same call
warnings: a picture that is not an object raises give the picture this frame is about

extensions.name: FrameOfQ
extensions.adds: does what the method does, then returns the object, so the call can be chained

methods.name: ExpectFindings
methods.brief: Says the open frame is about a picture the gate finds fault with, so the findings are its subject and not its failure.
methods.returns: the storyboard itself, so calls chain
warnings: a frame that expects findings and gets none is itself reported by Judge, as expected_a_finding_and_got_none; with no frame open it raises open a frame first

methods.name: Bind
methods.brief: Ties a hole of the open frame to a fact read from the picture when the frame closes, and returns the storyboard.

parameters.name: pcHole
parameters.role: the hole's name, as written between braces in the caption

parameters.name: pcKind
parameters.role: the kind of fact, such as :value or :distance

parameters.name: paArgs
parameters.role: the list of arguments of that fact, such as [ "B.icon.r" ]

methods.returns: the storyboard itself, so calls chain
notes: BindQ is the same call; the number is read at close, so a later action in the same frame still moves it
warnings: with no frame open it raises open a frame first; a hole the caption never quotes is reported by Judge as fact_bound_but_never_shown

extensions.name: BindQ
extensions.adds: does what the method does, then returns the object, so the call can be chained

methods.name: BindFact
methods.brief: Ties a hole to a fact handed in whole, from another plane, and returns the storyboard.

parameters.name: pcHole
parameters.role: the hole's name, as written between braces in the caption

parameters.name: paFact
parameters.role: a fact, as Fact() answered it or StzFact() built it, with at least a value and a message

methods.returns: the storyboard itself, so calls chain
notes: BindFactQ is the same call; {name.message} and {name.unit} show the fact's sentence and unit
warnings: a list that is not a fact raises that is not a fact; with no frame open it raises open a frame first

extensions.name: BindFactQ
extensions.adds: does what the method does, then returns the object, so the call can be chained

methods.name: Show
methods.brief: Draws on the picture the boundary a rule states, such as the circle of a leash, for the open frame.

parameters.name: pcRule
parameters.role: words that appear in the rule's own line, such as disjoint or lessthan v111

methods.returns: the storyboard itself, so calls chain
notes: tested on a sets picture: a thin circle appeared around the smaller set
warnings: with no frame open it raises open a frame first; words that match no rule raise an error saying a rule is addressed by words from its own line

methods.name: Region
methods.brief: Tints on the picture the area a clearance rule forbids, for the open frame.

parameters.name: pcRule
parameters.role: words that appear in the rule's own line, such as disjoint

methods.returns: the storyboard itself, so calls chain
notes: tested on a sets picture: a pink disc appeared around the smaller set
warnings: with no frame open it raises open a frame first; words that match no rule raise the same error as Show

methods.name: Measure
methods.brief: Draws on the picture a line between two things, with its length written beside it, for the open frame.

parameters.name: pcA
parameters.role: the first thing, such as A.icon

parameters.name: pcB
parameters.role: the second thing, such as B.icon

parameters.name: paOpts
parameters.role: the options list, or an empty list

methods.returns: the storyboard itself, so calls chain
notes: the length is read from the picture; in the test the label was drawn far from the line, at the bottom of the larger set
warnings: with no frame open it raises open a frame first

methods.name: Callout
methods.brief: Writes a short text with a leader line pointing at a thing on the picture, for the open frame.

parameters.name: pcTarget
parameters.role: the thing pointed at, such as B.icon

parameters.name: pcText
parameters.role: the text to write

parameters.name: paOpts
parameters.role: the options list, or an empty list

methods.returns: the storyboard itself, so calls chain
warnings: with no frame open it raises open a frame first; the gate may find the text overlapping a name, as it did in the test, and Judge then reports it

methods.name: Emphasis
methods.brief: Marks a thing on the picture for the open frame, as a ring around it, a stronger stroke or a dimmed one.

parameters.name: pcTarget
parameters.role: the thing to mark, such as B.icon

parameters.name: pcMode
parameters.role: :ring, :focus or :dim

methods.returns: the storyboard itself, so calls chain
notes: the ring was drawn in orange around the smaller set
warnings: with no frame open it raises open a frame first; any other mode raises an error naming the three

methods.name: ClearMarks
methods.brief: Removes every mark the picture carries, so the open frame starts clean.
methods.returns: the storyboard itself, so calls chain
notes: marks stay from frame to frame until this call
warnings: with no frame open it raises open a frame first

methods.name: WindowOn
methods.brief: Shows only a part of the picture for the open frame: the window centred on a thing, with some reach around it.

parameters.name: pcPath
parameters.role: the thing to centre on, such as B.icon

parameters.name: pnReach
parameters.role: how far around it to show, in pixels

methods.returns: the storyboard itself, so calls chain
notes: in the test the window was scaled up to the whole canvas
warnings: with no frame open it raises open a frame first; a mark outside the window is reported by Judge as mark_inside_the_window

methods.name: SetWindow
methods.brief: Shows only a part of the picture for the open frame: a window given by its centre and its size.

parameters.name: pnCx
parameters.role: the x of the window's centre, in pixels

parameters.name: pnCy
parameters.role: the y of its centre

parameters.name: pnW
parameters.role: its width

parameters.name: pnH
parameters.role: its height

methods.returns: the storyboard itself, so calls chain
warnings: with no frame open it raises open a frame first; a width or height that is not positive raises an error

methods.name: ClearWindow
methods.brief: Shows the whole picture again for the open frame.
methods.returns: the storyboard itself, so calls chain

classes.name: stzString
classes.brief: Holds a text and finds, cuts, edits, splits and compares it, character by character, in Unicode.
classes.description: A stzString counts characters, not bytes: positions, lengths and sections are in Unicode codepoints, so Hebrew, Arabic, Chinese and emoji behave like Latin letters. Active forms change the text in place (Remove, Uppercase), passive forms return a changed copy (Uppercased), and the Q forms return the object so calls chain. Reach for it before writing a loop over a text.

classes.name: stzStringAligner
classes.brief: Aligns a text in a field of a given width: pads it on the left, on the right or on both sides with a chosen character.
classes.description: It is the alignment helper behind the padding methods of stzString. Build one with new stzStringAligner("abc") over a text. Each in-place verb (AlignLeft, AlignRight, AlignCenter, PadLeft, PadRight, PadBoth) changes the text it holds and has a passive twin that returns the padded text (AlignedLeft, AlignedRight, AlignedCenter, PaddedLeft ...). Widths count characters, not bytes, so Hebrew, Arabic and emoji align like any other text, and a width smaller than the text changes nothing. Do not pass a stzString object you still need: the first in-place edit empties it.
classes.example:
? o1.AlignedLeft(6, ".")
#--> abc...
? o1.AlignedRight(6, ".")
#--> ...abc
? o1.AlignedCenter(7, "-")
#--> --abc--
o2 = new stzStringAligner("שלום")
? o2.AlignedLeft(6, "😀")
#--> שלום😀😀

classes.name: stzStringBounder
classes.brief: Cuts a text by position or by its surroundings: sections, ranges, the text between two bounds, and tests of what bounds what.
classes.description: It is the cutting helper behind the Section, Between and IsBoundedBy methods of stzString, which builds one over itself; reach for it directly with new stzStringBounder(cText) or StzStringBounderQ(cText) when you only need the cutting. The reads (Section, Range, Between, FirstBetween, SectionBounds, IsBoundedBy...) return a text, a list or TRUE or FALSE and leave the held text alone; the ReplaceBetween and RemoveBetween verbs change the held text in place and keep the bounds, and the variants ending in IB (ReplaceBetweenIB, RemoveBetweenIB) take the bounds with them. Read the result with Content. Positions count characters from 1, not bytes, so Hebrew, Arabic and emoji text is cut where you expect. The rank of the Nth forms starts at 1. Pass a plain text, not a stzString object: an in-place edit through a bounder empties the stzString that was passed in. At the edges of a text, trust SectionBounds and FindSectionBoundsZZ over their IB forms.
classes.example:
? o1.Section(5, 9)
#--> [two]
? @@( o1.Between("[", "]") )
#--> [ "two", "four" ]
? o1.NthBetween(2, "[", "]")
#--> four
o1.RemoveBetween("[", "]")
? o1.Content()
#--> one [] three [] five
o2 = new stzStringBounder("שלום [עולם] יפה")
? o2.FirstBetween("[", "]") = "עולם"
#--> 1
o3 = new stzStringBounder("a😀b😀c")

classes.name: stzStringBoxed
classes.brief: Draws a text inside a box made of Unicode line characters, the whole text in one box or each character in its own cell.
classes.description: Build one with new stzStringBoxed("hello"); Boxed and BoxedChars return the drawing as a text and print nothing, and the text held never changes. The global function StzBoxedString(text) (also BoxedString) is the one-call form of Boxed. Several lines of text give several rows in the box, padded to the longest. BoxedChars draws a single row and its borders are mis-sized today, see its warning.

classes.name: stzStringCaseChanger
classes.brief: Changes the case of a text: capitals, small letters, first letter only, each word, or swapped, with Unicode rules.
classes.description: It is the case helper behind the case methods of stzString. Build one with new stzStringCaseChanger("text"). Each in-place verb (Uppercase, Lowercase, Capitalize, CapitalizeEachWord, ToggleCase, DecapitalizeFirst, SetCase) changes the text it holds and has a passive twin that returns the changed text (Uppercased, Lowercased, Capitalized, EachWordCapitalized, CaseToggled, FirstDecapitalized). Accents follow the letter, the German ß uppercases to SS, and scripts without case (Hebrew, Arabic, emoji) are left alone. Do not pass a stzString object you still need: the first in-place edit empties it. IsCapitalized only checks the first character.
classes.example:
? o1.Uppercased()
#--> ÇA VA ÉTÉ
? o1.Capitalized()
#--> Ça va été
? o1.EachWordCapitalized()
#--> Ça Va Été
? o1.CaseToggled()
#--> ÇA VA été
o2 = new stzStringCaseChanger("שלום")
? o2.Uppercased()
#--> שלום

notes: a control char and a private-use char count as named: their name is a label such as <control>

methods.name: Name
methods.brief: Returns the official Unicode name, such as LATIN SMALL LETTER A, and raises when the database has none.
notes: a control char answers <control>; the first char of a range answers a range label such as <Private Use, First>; an unassigned code such as U+0378 raises

methods.name: NameIs
methods.brief: TRUE if the char carries the given Unicode name; the comparison ignores case.

parameters.name: pcName
parameters.role: A name, as text.

notes: NameIs("latin small letter a") is TRUE for a

methods.name: AsciiCode
methods.brief: Returns the ASCII code of the char, 0 to 127, and raises a clear error for a char above 127.
notes: a non-ASCII char raises "Can't get ASCII code for this character!" and names its U+ code; IsAscii tells beforehand, and Unicode answers for any char

methods.name: Orientation
methods.brief: Returns "ltr" or "rtl", the writing direction of the char as the string layer judges it.
notes: judged by script block: a char of the Arabic range, even the shaddah or U+FEFF, answers rtl where UnicodeDirection says nonspacingmark or boundaryneutral

methods.name: UnicodeDirection
methods.brief: Returns the name of the char's Unicode bidi class, such as lefttoright, europeannumber or whitespace.
notes: other names seen: righttoleft, righttoleftarabic, arabicnumber, otherneutrals, nonspacingmark

methods.name: UnicodeDirectionNumber
methods.brief: Returns the bidi class as a number written as text, in Qt numbering: 0 left-to-right, 1 right-to-left, 2 European number, 9 whitespace.
notes: the other values: 3 separator, 4 terminator, 5 Arabic number, 6 common separator, 7 paragraph, 8 section, 10 neutral, 13 Arabic letter, 17 nonspacing mark, 18 boundary neutral

methods.name: IsVowel
methods.brief: TRUE if the char is one of the ASCII vowels a, e, i, o, u in either case; an accented vowel answers FALSE.

methods.name: IsLeftToRight
methods.brief: TRUE if the bidi class is left-to-right, or a left-to-right embedding, override or isolate mark.
notes: a digit answers FALSE: its class is European number

methods.name: IsRightToLeft
methods.brief: TRUE if the bidi class is right-to-left, as for Hebrew and Arabic letters, or the char is an RLE, RLO or RLI mark.

methods.name: IsArabicFraction
methods.brief: TRUE if the char is in the library's list of fraction chars, such as the vulgar half U+00BD or U+2153.

methods.name: IsEuropeanNumber
methods.brief: TRUE if the bidi class is European number, as for the ASCII digits and the Extended Arabic-Indic digits.
notes: the Arabic-Indic digits U+0660 to 0669 are class Arabic number and answer FALSE

methods.name: IsEuropeanNumberSeparator
methods.brief: TRUE if the bidi class is European number separator, as for the plus sign and the hyphen-minus.

methods.name: IsEuropeanNumberTerminator
methods.brief: TRUE if the bidi class is European number terminator, as for the dollar and percent signs.

methods.name: IsIndianDigit
methods.brief: TRUE if the char is one of the library's Indian digits: the Arabic-Indic digits U+0660 to 0669 and most Persian ones.
notes: Devanagari digits answer FALSE, and so do the Persian U+06F4 to 06F7

methods.name: IsCommonNumberSeparator
methods.brief: TRUE if the bidi class is common number separator, as for the comma, the full stop and the fraction slash.

methods.name: IsParagraphSeparator
methods.brief: TRUE if the bidi class is paragraph separator, as for the newline and U+2029.

methods.name: IsSectionSeparator
methods.brief: TRUE if the bidi class is segment separator, which is the tab char.

methods.name: IsWhitespace
methods.brief: TRUE if the bidi class is whitespace, as for the plain space and U+2028; a tab, a newline and a no-break space answer FALSE.

methods.name: IsOrientationNeutral
methods.brief: TRUE if the bidi class is other neutral, as for parentheses, or if the char is a digit.
notes: the digit clause makes 7 answer TRUE although its class is European number

methods.name: IsLeftToRightEmbedding
methods.brief: TRUE if the char is the left-to-right embedding mark, U+202A.

methods.name: IsLeftToRightOverride
methods.brief: TRUE if the char is the left-to-right override mark, U+202D.

methods.name: IsLeftToRightIsolate
methods.brief: TRUE if the char is the left-to-right isolate mark, U+2066.
notes: the first strong isolate U+2068 and the pop directional isolate U+2069 answer FALSE

methods.name: IsRightToLeftIsolate
methods.brief: TRUE if the char is the right-to-left isolate mark, U+2067.
notes: the first strong isolate U+2068 and the pop directional isolate U+2069 answer FALSE

methods.name: IsRightToLeftArabic
methods.brief: TRUE if the bidi class is right-to-left Arabic, as for Arabic letters and Arabic presentation forms.

methods.name: IsRightToLeftEmbedding
methods.brief: TRUE if the char is the right-to-left embedding mark, U+202B.

methods.name: IsRightToLeftOverride
methods.brief: TRUE if the char is the right-to-left override mark, U+202E.

methods.name: IsPopDirectionalFormat
methods.brief: TRUE if the char is the pop directional formatting mark, U+202C, which ends an embedding or override.

methods.name: IsNonSpacingMark
methods.brief: TRUE if the bidi class is nonspacing mark, as for combining accents and the Arabic shaddah.

methods.name: IsBoundaryNeutral
methods.brief: TRUE if the bidi class is boundary neutral, as for control chars, the soft hyphen and U+FEFF.

methods.name: UnicodeCategoryNumber
methods.brief: Returns the Unicode general-category code of the char, from the engine: 1 Lu, 2 Ll, 5 Lo, 9 Nd, 18 Po, 23 Zs, 26 Cc.

methods.name: UnicodeCategory
methods.brief: Returns the name of the Unicode general category, such as letter_lowercase, number_decimaldigit or punctuation_dash.

extensions.name: CharTypeQ
extensions.adds: does what the method does, then returns the object, so the call can be chained

extensions.name: CategoryQ
extensions.adds: does what the method does, then returns the object, so the call can be chained

methods.name: TypeUnicodeQ
methods.brief: Returns the category name wrapped in a stzString object, so that calls can chain.

methods.name: IsArabicShaddah
methods.brief: TRUE if the char is U+0651, the Arabic shaddah.

methods.name: IsLetter
methods.brief: TRUE if the engine counts the char as a letter, or if it is the Arabic shaddah, which the library treats as a letter.

methods.name: IsNotLetter
methods.brief: TRUE if the char is not a letter, so for digits, spaces, punctuation and accents; the shaddah answers FALSE.

methods.name: IsLetterOrSpaceOrChar
methods.brief: TRUE if the char is a letter, a Unicode space, or equal to the given char.

parameters.name: c
parameters.role: the extra char that also qualifies

methods.name: IsTheLetter
methods.brief: TRUE if the char equals the given char once both are uppercased, so the test ignores case.

parameters.name: c
parameters.role: the char to compare with

notes: any char works, not only letters

methods.name: IsLetterOrNumber
methods.brief: TRUE if the char is a letter or a digit char, in any script, or a circled digit.
notes: a Roman numeral answers FALSE

methods.name: IsLetterOrSpace
methods.brief: TRUE if the char is a letter or a Unicode space, a newline included.

methods.name: IsLetterOrSpaceOrThisChar
methods.brief: TRUE if the char is a letter, a Unicode space, or equal to the given char.

parameters.name: pcChar
parameters.role: A single character.

methods.name: IsEuropean
methods.brief: TRUE if the bidi class is European number, European separator or European terminator.
notes: a digit, the plus and hyphen-minus signs and the dollar and percent signs answer TRUE; the comma and the full stop are common separators and answer FALSE

methods.name: IsSpace
methods.brief: TRUE if the engine counts the char as a space: the plain space, a tab, a newline or the no-break space.
notes: U+2028 and U+2029 answer FALSE

methods.name: IsUnicodeNumber
methods.brief: TRUE if the char is in a Unicode number category (digit, letter number such as a Roman numeral, other number).
notes: the library's Mandarin and Indian numerals also answer TRUE

methods.name: IsNotNumber
methods.brief: TRUE if the char is neither a decimal digit nor a circled digit.
notes: a Roman numeral answers TRUE

methods.name: IsDigit
methods.brief: TRUE if the engine counts the char as a decimal digit, in any script: 7, the Arabic-Indic three, the Devanagari one.
notes: a circled digit answers FALSE

methods.name: IsArabicNumber
methods.brief: TRUE if the char is one of the Arabic digits 0 to 9, U+0030 to U+0039.
notes: the Arabic-Indic digits answer FALSE here; IsIndianNumber covers them

methods.name: IsANumber
methods.brief: TRUE if the char is a decimal digit in any script or a circled digit.

methods.name: IsIndianNumber
methods.brief: TRUE if the char is in the library's list of Indian digits, the Arabic-Indic and most Persian digits.

methods.name: IsRomanNumber
methods.brief: TRUE if the char is a Roman numeral char, such as U+2160 or U+2171, from the library's list.

methods.name: IsMandarinNumber
methods.brief: TRUE if the char is a Mandarin numeral from the library's list: 〇, 一 to 十, 百, 千 or 万.

methods.name: IsAscii
methods.brief: TRUE if the codepoint is below 128, control chars included.

methods.name: IsAsciiLetter
methods.brief: TRUE if the char is an unaccented ASCII letter, A to Z or a to z.

methods.name: IsPunctuation
methods.brief: TRUE if the engine counts the char as punctuation, such as ( ) - or !.
notes: the dollar sign and the infinity sign are symbols and answer FALSE

methods.name: IsGeneralPunctuation
methods.brief: TRUE if the char lies in the Unicode General Punctuation block, U+2000 to U+206F.
notes: the comma and the exclamation mark are not in this block

methods.name: IsSupplementalPunctuation
methods.brief: TRUE if the char lies in the library's Supplemental Punctuation range, U+2DF6 to U+2E7F.

methods.name: IsSymbol
methods.brief: TRUE if the engine counts the char as a symbol, such as $, the infinity sign or an emoji.

methods.name: IsNonChar
methods.brief: TRUE if the codepoint is a Unicode noncharacter: U+FDD0 to U+FDEF, or a codepoint ending in FFFE or FFFF.

methods.name: IsMark
methods.brief: TRUE if the engine counts the char as a combining mark, such as an accent or the Arabic shaddah.

methods.name: IsSeparator
methods.brief: TRUE if the engine counts the char as a space: the plain space, a tab, a newline or the no-break space.

methods.name: IsOneOfThese
methods.brief: TRUE if the char appears in the given list of chars.

parameters.name: pacChars
parameters.role: the list of chars to look in

methods.name: IsWordSeparator
methods.brief: TRUE if the char is in the library's word separators: space . , ; : ! ? the Arabic comma and question mark, the apostrophes and the em dash.

methods.name: IsSentenceSeparator
methods.brief: TRUE if the char is in the library's sentence separators: the full stop, ! , ? and the Arabic question mark.

methods.name: IsLineSeparator
methods.brief: TRUE if the char is the newline, char 10, and nothing else; U+2028 answers FALSE.

methods.name: IsWordNonLetterChar
methods.brief: TRUE if the char is in the library's non-letter word chars: _ - * / \ + and the digits 0 to 9.

methods.name: IsMirrored
methods.brief: TRUE if the char is a bracket pair member the library can mirror, such as ( ) < > [ ] { } or the guillemets.

methods.name: UnicodeOfMirrored
methods.brief: Returns the codepoint of the char's mirror partner, 41 for ( and 62 for <, or the char's own codepoint if it has none.

methods.name: Mirrored
methods.brief: Returns the mirror partner of the char as a char, such as ) for (, or the char itself when it has none.
notes: the partner table is the library's own and short: 22 chars, the brackets, the guillemets and a few more pairs. The Unicode database holds only a mirrored flag, not the partner, so a mirrored char outside the table answers itself

methods.name: IsLatin
methods.brief: TRUE if the engine's Unicode data puts the char in the Latin script, an accented letter included.

methods.name: IsLatinLetter
methods.brief: TRUE if the char is a letter of the Latin script, accented letters included.

methods.name: IsBasicLatin
methods.brief: TRUE if the char lies in the Basic Latin block, U+0000 to U+007F.

methods.name: IsLatin1Supplement
methods.brief: TRUE if the char lies in the Latin-1 Supplement block, U+0080 to U+00FF.

methods.name: IsLatinExtendedA
methods.brief: TRUE if the char lies in the Latin Extended-A block, U+0100 to U+017F.

methods.name: IsLatinExtendedB
methods.brief: TRUE if the char lies in the Latin Extended-B block, U+0180 to U+024F.

methods.name: IsLatinExtendedAdditional
methods.brief: TRUE if the char lies in the Latin Extended Additional block, U+1E00 to U+1EFF.

methods.name: IsLatinExtendedC
methods.brief: TRUE if the char lies in the Latin Extended-C block, U+2C60 to U+2C7F.

methods.name: IsLatinExtendedD
methods.brief: TRUE if the char lies in the Latin Extended-D block, U+A720 to U+A7FF.

methods.name: IsLatinExtendedE
methods.brief: TRUE if the char lies in the Latin Extended-E block, U+AB30 to U+AB6F.

methods.name: IsArabic
methods.brief: TRUE if the engine counts the char as Arabic, by block, so the shaddah, Arabic-Indic digits and U+FEFF answer TRUE.
notes: the script test IsArabicScript differs: it answers FALSE for the shaddah, which is in the Inherited script

methods.name: IsArabicLetter
methods.brief: TRUE if the char is a letter and the engine counts it as Arabic.

methods.name: IsBasicArabic
methods.brief: TRUE if the char lies in the main Arabic block, U+0600 to U+06FF.

methods.name: IsArabicSupplement
methods.brief: TRUE if the char lies in the Arabic Supplement block, U+0750 to U+077F.

methods.name: IsArabicExtendedA
methods.brief: TRUE if the char lies in the Arabic Extended-A block, U+08A0 to U+08FF.

methods.name: IsArabicExtended
methods.brief: TRUE if the char lies in the Arabic Extended-A block, U+08A0 to U+08FF, as the lettered form does.

methods.name: IsArabicPresentationForm
methods.brief: TRUE if the char lies in the Arabic Presentation Forms blocks, U+FB50 to U+FDFF or U+FE70 to U+FEFF.

methods.name: IsArabicPresentationFormA
methods.brief: TRUE if the char lies in the Arabic Presentation Forms-A block, U+FB50 to U+FDFF.

methods.name: IsArabicPresentationFormB
methods.brief: TRUE if the char lies in the Arabic Presentation Forms-B block, U+FE70 to U+FEFF.

methods.name: IsArabicMathAlphabeticSymbol
methods.brief: TRUE if the char lies in the Arabic Mathematical Alphabetic Symbols block, U+1EE00 to U+1EEFF.

methods.name: IsQuranicSign
methods.brief: TRUE if the char is one of the 24 Quranic annotation signs, U+06D6 to U+06ED.

methods.name: IsTurnedNumber
methods.brief: TRUE if the char is a turned digit, U+218A or U+218B.

methods.name: IsCircled
methods.brief: TRUE if the char is a circled digit or a circled Latin letter from the library's list.

methods.name: IsCircledNumber
methods.brief: TRUE if the char is a circled digit, U+2460 to U+2468, or the circled zero U+24EA.

methods.name: IsCircledDigit
methods.brief: TRUE if the char is a circled digit, U+2460 to U+2468, or the circled zero U+24EA.

methods.name: IsCircledLatinLetter
methods.brief: TRUE if the char is a circled Latin letter, capital or small, U+24B6 to U+24E9.

methods.name: IsCircledLatinSmallLetter
methods.brief: TRUE if the char is a circled small Latin letter, U+24D0 to U+24E9.

methods.name: IsCircledLatinCapitalLetter
methods.brief: TRUE if the char is a circled capital Latin letter, U+24B6 to U+24CF.

methods.name: IsOtherCircledChar
methods.brief: TRUE if the Unicode name has the word CIRCLED and the char is not one of the library's circled digits or Latin letters.
notes: circled number ten, a circled ideograph and the circled plus answer TRUE; so do the negative and double circled forms. The library keeps no list of these chars, so the test reads the name from the Unicode database; an unassigned code is FALSE

methods.name: IsPrintable
methods.brief: TRUE if the char is not a control, format, surrogate, private-use, unassigned or line or paragraph separator.
notes: the plain space and the digits are printable

methods.name: IsNonPrintable
methods.brief: TRUE if the char is a control, format, surrogate, private-use or unassigned, or a line or paragraph separator.

methods.name: IsInvisible
methods.brief: TRUE if the char is in the library's invisible list: tab, the no-break space, the spaces and marks of U+2000 to U+200F and a few more.
notes: the plain space and the newline answer FALSE

methods.name: IsVisible
methods.brief: TRUE if the char is not in the library's invisible list, so the plain space and the newline count as visible.

methods.name: IsLocaleSeparator
methods.brief: Returns 1 for a hyphen, 2 for an underscore and 0 for any other char; it is a position in the list, not TRUE.
notes: the pair - and _ separates the parts of a locale code such as en-US or en_US

methods.name: IntroducedInUnicodeVersion
methods.brief: Returns a rough guess of the Unicode version that introduced the char, from a short table of blocks; it is not exact.
warnings: approximation: the Unicode database carries no age per char, so the answer comes from a table of a dozen blocks. Every char outside them, and most inside, answer "0.9", which is not a Unicode version; Hangul answers "1.0". The two emoji blocks U+1F300 to U+1F64F answer "6.0", the version that added them, though some of their chars came later. The version list in the data file is marked #TODO there

methods.name: IsLower
methods.brief: TRUE if the engine counts the char as a lowercase letter.

methods.name: Lowercase
methods.brief: Returns the lowercase form of the char; a char with no case comes back unchanged.

methods.name: IsUppercase
methods.brief: TRUE if the engine counts the char as an uppercase letter; a Roman numeral such as U+2161 counts.

methods.name: Uppercase
methods.brief: Returns the uppercase form of the char; a char with no case comes back unchanged.

methods.name: CharCase
methods.brief: Returns :lowercase or :uppercase, and an empty string for a char with no case.

methods.name: DefaultLanguage
methods.brief: Returns the main language of the char's script, such as english, arabic or hebrew, and undefined for chars shared by scripts.
notes: greek answers ancient_greek and Devanagari answers bhojpuri. A char of the common, inherited or unknown script (a digit, a combining accent, an unassigned code, a private-use char), or of a script the locale table does not list, answers undefined

methods.name: Script
methods.brief: Returns the lowercase name of the char's Unicode script, such as latin, arabic, common or inherited.
notes: a digit, a space or a punctuation mark answers common; a combining accent answers inherited; when a char belongs to several scripts the first is given

methods.name: UnicodeScript

methods.name: ScriptIs

methods.name: IsLetterInScript

classes.name: stzStringCharList
classes.brief: Holds a text as a list of single characters, so that each character can be sorted, reversed, looked up or named on its own.
classes.description: Build it with a text, with a list of single characters or with a list of Unicode code points; the class stzListOfChars is the same class under another name, and StzStringCharListQ(p) builds one in a chain. A Hebrew letter, an Arabic letter, an accented letter and an emoji are one item each, because the text is split into characters and not into bytes. Verbs such as Reverse and ToUpper change the list in place and return nothing, and the forms that end in -ed (Reversed, Uppercased) return a new list and leave the object alone. Unique and the sort methods return their result as ONE joined text inside a one-item list today, not as a list of single characters; RemoveDuplicatesQ and Reversed are the ones to use for a proper list.
classes.example:
? o1.Join()
#--> hello
? @@( o1.Find("l") )
#--> [ 3, 4 ]
o2 = new stzStringCharList("שלום")
? @@( o2.Reversed() )
#--> [ "ם", "ו", "ל", "ש" ]
o3 = new stzStringCharList("a😀b")
? @@( o3.Unicodes() )
#--> [ 97, 128512, 98 ]

notes: same answer as Content, under a name that says the type

methods.name: Chars
methods.brief: Returns the held characters as a plain list, one single-character text per item.
notes: same answer as Content, under the name used when a text is split into characters

methods.name: Names

methods.returns: a list of text, one name per character

extensions.name: UppercaseQ

methods.name: Unique
methods.brief: Returns the distinct characters, each kept at its first occurrence, but joined in one text inside a one-item list.

warnings: the answer is not split into single characters: hello gives [ "helo" ], not [ "h", "e", "l", "o" ], and the same happens for Hebrew, emoji and a list given as input; the engine hands back one text and the splitting finds no separator in it

methods.name: NumberOfUniqueChars
methods.brief: Returns how many different characters the list holds.
notes: hello gives 4

methods.name: SortAsc
methods.brief: Reorders the characters in ascending code point order, in place, but leaves them joined in one item.
notes: Sort does the same
warnings: the list then holds ONE item, the whole sorted text, so NumberOfChars answers 1 afterwards: hello becomes [ "ehllo" ] and not [ "e", "h", "l", "l", "o" ]; the engine hands back one text and the splitting finds no separator in it

methods.name: SortedAsc
methods.brief: Returns the characters in ascending code point order, as a one-item list, leaving the object unchanged.
notes: the same defect as SortAsc
warnings: the answer is one text inside a list: hello gives [ "ehllo" ], not a list of single characters

methods.name: SortDesc
methods.brief: Reorders the characters in descending code point order, in place, but leaves them joined in one item.
notes: the same defect as SortAsc
warnings: the list then holds ONE item, the whole sorted text: hello becomes [ "ollhe" ] and not [ "o", "l", "l", "h", "e" ]; the engine hands back one text and the splitting finds no separator in it

methods.name: SortedDesc
methods.brief: Returns the characters in descending code point order, as a one-item list, leaving the object unchanged.
notes: the same defect as SortAsc
warnings: the answer is one text inside a list: hello gives [ "ollhe" ], not a list of single characters

methods.name: Sort
methods.brief: Reorders the characters in ascending code point order, in place, but leaves them joined in one item.
notes: it calls SortAsc
warnings: the list then holds ONE item, the whole sorted text, exactly as SortAsc does

methods.name: Reverse
methods.brief: Turns the list around, in place, so that the last character comes first.
notes: Hebrew, Arabic and emoji characters stay whole

methods.name: Reversed
methods.brief: Returns the characters in the opposite order as a list, leaving the object unchanged.

methods.name: ToUpper
methods.brief: Changes every character to its capital form, in place, by converting the whole text at once.

methods.name: Uppercased
methods.brief: Returns the characters in their capital form as a list, leaving the object unchanged.

methods.name: ToLower
methods.brief: Changes every character to its small form, in place, by converting the whole text at once.

methods.name: Lowercased
methods.brief: Returns the characters in their small form as a list, leaving the object unchanged.

methods.name: Unicodes

notes: the emoji 😀 is 128512 and the Hebrew letter ש is 1513

classes.name: stzStringChecker
classes.brief: Answers yes/no questions about a text: palindrome, anagram, number form, case, composition, marks and regex match.
classes.description: It is the question-answering helper behind many Is... methods of stzString, which builds one over itself and passes the call on; reach for it directly when you only want the checks and not the whole string API. A question answers 1 or 0 and never changes the text. Every question counts characters, not bytes, so a Hebrew or Arabic word and an emoji are one character each. The number checks that expect a prefix (0b, 0o, 0x, U+) answer 0 without it. The case-flag forms (CS) take 1 to compare with case and 0 to ignore it. HasLeadingChars, HasTrailingChars and HasLeadingAndTrailingChars answer 0 for every text today; use the stzString methods of the same names.
classes.example:
? o1.IsPalindrome()
#--> 1
? o1.IsMadeOf([ "lev", "el" ])
#--> 1
o2 = new stzStringChecker("שלום")
? o2.IsReversedCopyOf("םולש")
#--> 1
o3 = new stzStringChecker("a😀b")
? o3.NumberOfChars()
#--> 3

methods.name: init
methods.brief: Builds a checker over a text, given as a string or as a stzString object.

parameters.name: pStrOrStzStrObj
parameters.role: the text to question, or a stzString whose content is questioned (it is held, not copied)

notes: stzString builds one of these for each of its Is... questions

methods.name: Content
methods.brief: Returns the text being questioned, unchanged.

methods.name: NumberOfChars
methods.brief: Returns how many characters the text holds, counting an emoji or an accented letter as one.

methods.name: IsPalindrome
methods.brief: TRUE if the text reads the same from the right as from the left, letter case counted.
notes: an empty text is a palindrome; IsPalindromeCS(0) ignores case, so Abba passes with it and fails without it

extensions.name: IsPalindromeCS
extensions.adds: takes a case-sensitivity flag

methods.brief: TRUE if the text is made of the same characters as another text, in any order.

parameters.name: pcOtherStr

extensions.name: IsAnagramOfCS

parameters.name: acSubStr

methods.name: RepresentsInteger
methods.brief: TRUE if the text is a whole number, written with an optional leading + or -.
notes: 42, -5 and +5 pass, -3.14 and 0x1F do not

methods.brief: TRUE if the text is a whole number that starts with a + or a - sign.
notes: 42 answers FALSE and -5 answers TRUE

methods.name: RepresentsUnsignedInteger
methods.brief: TRUE if the text is a whole number written without a sign.
notes: 42 answers TRUE and -5 answers FALSE

methods.name: RepresentsNumber
methods.brief: TRUE if the text is a whole or a decimal number, written with an optional leading + or -.
notes: -3.14 and 42 pass, abc does not

methods.name: RepresentsSignedNumber
methods.brief: TRUE if the text is a number, whole or decimal, that starts with a + or a - sign.
notes: -3.14 and +5 answer TRUE, 42 answers FALSE

methods.name: RepresentsUnsignedNumber
methods.brief: TRUE if the text is a number, whole or decimal, written without a sign.
notes: 42 answers TRUE, -3.14 answers FALSE

methods.name: IsListInString
methods.brief: TRUE if the trimmed text starts with a [ and ends with a ], so that it could be read back as a list.
notes: only the two brackets are looked at: the content between them is not parsed

methods.name: RepresentsDecimalNumber
methods.brief: TRUE if the text is a number written with a decimal point, such as 3.14 or -3.14.
notes: 42 answers FALSE: it has no decimal point

methods.name: RepresentsBinaryNumber
methods.brief: TRUE if the text is a 0b or 0B prefix followed by binary digits.
notes: 0b1011 answers TRUE and 1011 answers FALSE: the prefix is required

methods.name: RepresentsHexNumber
methods.brief: TRUE if the text is a 0x or 0X prefix followed by hexadecimal digits.
notes: 0x1F answers TRUE and 1F4a answers FALSE: the prefix is required

methods.name: RepresentsNumberInUnicodeHexForm
methods.brief: TRUE if the text is U+ followed by hexadecimal digits, the way a Unicode code point is written.
notes: U+0041 answers TRUE and 0041 answers FALSE

methods.name: IsCharName
methods.brief: TRUE if the text is the official Unicode name of a character, such as LATIN SMALL LETTER A.
notes: the name is looked up in the engine character database; a letter such as x is not a name

methods.name: IsReversedCopyOf
methods.brief: TRUE if the text is another text read backward, character by character.

parameters.name: pcOtherStr
parameters.role: the text to compare with

notes: works on characters, not bytes: םולש is the reverse of שלום

extensions.name: IsReversedCopyOfCS
extensions.adds: takes a case-sensitivity flag

methods.name: Reversed
methods.brief: Returns the text with its characters in the opposite order, leaving the checked text unchanged.
notes: an emoji or an accented letter stays whole: a😀b gives b😀a

methods.name: IsChar
methods.brief: TRUE if the text is made of exactly one character.
notes: a letter with a separate combining accent counts as two characters, so it answers FALSE

methods.name: IsLetter
methods.brief: TRUE if the string is a single letter.

methods.name: IsADigit
methods.brief: TRUE if the string is a single digit.

methods.name: IsWord
methods.brief: TRUE if the string is a single word.

methods.name: IsCharsSortedAscending
methods.brief: TRUE if the chars are in ascending order.

methods.name: IsCharsSortedDescending
methods.brief: TRUE if the chars are in descending order.

methods.name: HasLeadingChars
methods.brief: Returns 0 today whatever the text is, instead of telling whether the text starts with a repeated character.
notes: stzString.HasLeadingChars is the working one
warnings: answers FALSE for aab and for xxyy alike: it compares two engine handles, which are never equal, instead of the two characters; the stzString method of the same name answers 1 for aab

methods.name: HasTrailingChars
methods.brief: Returns 0 today whatever the text is, instead of telling whether the text ends with a repeated character.
notes: stzString.HasTrailingChars is the working one
warnings: answers FALSE for abb and for xxyy alike: it compares two engine handles, which are never equal, instead of the two characters

methods.name: HasLeadingAndTrailingChars
methods.brief: Returns 0 today whatever the text is, because both of the questions it combines answer 0.
notes: stzString.HasLeadingAndTrailingChars is the working one
warnings: answers FALSE for aabaa: it is the AND of HasLeadingChars and HasTrailingChars, which are always 0

methods.name: Trimmed

methods.name: TrimmedLeft
methods.brief: Returns the text without the blanks at its beginning, leaving the checked text unchanged.

methods.name: TrimmedRight
methods.brief: Returns the text without the blanks at its end, leaving the checked text unchanged.

methods.name: IsBlank
methods.brief: TRUE if the string is empty or whitespace only.

methods.name: IsTitlecase
methods.brief: TRUE if the string is written in Title Case.

methods.name: RepresentsOctalNumber
methods.brief: TRUE if the text is a 0o or 0O prefix followed by octal digits.
notes: 0o17 answers TRUE and 17 answers FALSE: the prefix is required

methods.name: IsIdentifier
methods.brief: TRUE if the string is a valid identifier (letter or underscore first, then letters, digits, underscores).

methods.name: IsPangram
methods.brief: TRUE if the string uses every letter of the alphabet (a pangram).

methods.name: IsIsogram
methods.brief: TRUE if no char repeats in the string (an isogram).

methods.name: IsBalanced

classes.name: stzStringComparator
classes.brief: Compares a text with another: equality, order, shared beginnings and endings, edit distance, phonetic codes and similarity scores.
classes.description: It is the comparison helper of stzString, which builds one over itself for its comparison methods; build one with StzStringComparatorQ (or new stzStringComparator) when you only need the comparisons. It never edits the text, so a stzString passed in stays intact. The other text must be a text: a number ends the Ring process without a message. Comparison is by code point and case counts unless you call the CS form with 0; the CS flag is honoured by the equality, order, contains, prefix and suffix families. Positions and lengths count characters, so Hebrew, Arabic and emoji text is measured as you read it, with three exceptions found today: the case-sensitive CommonCharsWith, CommonalityWith, DiffCharsWith and LongestCommonPrefixWith work on bytes and break such text (the CS 0 forms are right), and Soundex and Metaphone only code Latin letters. The Jaro scores are similarities scaled to 1000, and JaroDistanceWith is the same call.
classes.example:
? o1.CommonPrefixWith("bandit")
#--> ban
? o1.LevenshteinDistanceWith("bandana")
#--> 1
o2 = new stzStringComparator("שלום עולם")
? o2.CommonPrefixWith("שלום יפה")
#--> שלום 
o3 = new stzStringComparator("a😀b😀")
? @@( o3.DiffWith("a😀c😀") )
#--> [ 3 ]

classes.name: stzStringConcat
classes.brief: Extends a text: adds at the end or in front, adds many, repeats it, or puts a separator between its characters.
classes.description: Build one with new stzStringConcat("abc"). Each in-place verb (Concat, Prepend, Append, ConcatMany, RepeatNTimes, JoinWith) changes the text it holds and has a passive twin that returns the new text (Concatenated, Prepended, Appended, ConcatenatedWithMany, RepeatedNTimes, JoinedWith). Characters are whole letters, so Hebrew, Arabic and emoji repeat and join without being cut. JoinWith joins the characters of the text itself, not a list of texts. Do not pass a stzString object you still need: the first in-place edit empties it.
classes.example:
? o1.Concatenated("def")
#--> abcdef
? o1.RepeatedNTimes(2)
#--> abcabc
? o1.JoinedWith("-")
#--> a-b-c
o2 = new stzStringConcat("שלום")
? o2.JoinedWith("·")
#--> ש·ל·ו·ם

classes.name: stzStringCounter
classes.brief: Counts things in a text: a fragment, overlapping fragments, regex matches, graphemes, marks and the characters of one script.
classes.description: It is the counting helper of stzString, which builds one over itself for its Count family; build one with new stzStringCounter("text") when you only need to count. Every count is by characters, so Hebrew, Arabic and emoji text counts as you expect, and every method answers a number and leaves the text alone. The script counts (CountHebrew, CountCyrillic, CountCjk, CountDevanagari, CountThai) and CountMarks, CountControls and GraphemeCount look at the whole text. Found today: CountBetween and CountBetweenCS raise R3 because they call a function that does not exist; CountOverlappingCS ignores its case flag; NumberOfCharsCS with 0 counts distinct letters; CountLeadingChar and CountTrailingChar stop the Ring process on an empty text; and a counter built from a stzString object reads an empty text once that string is appended to or replaced.
classes.example:
? o1.Count("an")
#--> 4
? o1.CountOverlapping("ana")
#--> 4
o2 = new stzStringCounter("שלום עולם abc")
? o2.CountHebrew()
#--> 8
o3 = new stzStringCounter("a😀b😀😀")
? o3.Count("😀")
#--> 3

parameters.role: the text to count in, or a stzString whose engine handle is shared
