classes.name: stzTcpClient
classes.brief: Holds a blocking TCP client connection that connects, sends text, reads text and closes, through the in-tree engine.
classes.description: Every call is synchronous: Connect, Send and Receive return when the operation has finished, and the callbacks set with OnConnect, OnReceive, OnClose and OnError run synchronously just after it. A failure never raises; the client records it in LastError and calls the error callback. Receive and ReceiveWithMax block with no timeout until data arrives or the peer closes, so call them only when data is expected. The documentation was run against a listener started in the same process on the loopback address and stopped afterwards, never against another machine.
classes.example:
? o1.IsConnected()
#--> 0
o1.Send("hello")
? o1.LastError()
#--> Not connected
? o1.LocalAddress()
#--> 127.0.0.1

methods.name: init
methods.brief: Builds a TCP client that is not connected and has no callbacks.

methods.name: Connect
methods.brief: Opens a blocking TCP connection to a host and port, and fires the connect or the error callback.

parameters.name: cHost
parameters.role: the host name or address

parameters.name: nPort
parameters.role: the port number

methods.returns: the client itself, so calls chain
notes: the callbacks are names of functions, called with no argument
warnings: a refusal or an unresolvable host does not raise: the client stays unconnected and LastError names the cause, such as connect failed: ConnectionRefused

methods.name: Send
methods.brief: Sends text on the open connection, reporting a failure through LastError and the error callback.

parameters.name: cData
parameters.role: the text to send

methods.returns: the client itself, so calls chain
warnings: without a connection it sets LastError to Not connected and sends nothing

methods.name: Receive
methods.brief: Reads at most 8192 bytes from the connection into ReceivedData and fires the receive callback.
methods.returns: the client itself, so calls chain
warnings: it blocks until data arrives or the peer closes, with no timeout; an empty ReceivedData and no error means the peer closed

methods.name: ReceiveWithMax
methods.brief: Reads at most that many bytes from the connection into ReceivedData and fires the receive callback.

parameters.name: nMaxBytes
parameters.role: the most bytes to read in this call

methods.returns: the client itself, so calls chain
warnings: it blocks until data arrives or the peer closes, with no timeout; a message longer than the limit is read by several calls

methods.name: ReceivedData
methods.brief: Returns what the last Receive read.
methods.returns: a text; empty before a read and after the peer closed

methods.name: Close
methods.brief: Closes the connection and fires the close callback; closing a client that is not connected does nothing.
methods.returns: the client itself, so calls chain

classes.name: stzTcpServer
classes.brief: Holds a blocking TCP listener that accepts clients one at a time and hands each back as a connected stzTcpClient.
classes.description: Listen starts the listener and returns at once; the application then calls AcceptOne, or AcceptOneWithin to give up after a time, in its own loop. There is no event loop: the Disconnect and Message callbacks are stored and never called. Pass 127.0.0.1 as the host for a local test, because an empty host listens on every interface. The documentation was run only against a client in the same process on the loopback address, stopped afterwards.
classes.example:
? o1.IsListening()
#--> 0
o1.Listen(47315, "127.0.0.1")
? o1.IsListening()
#--> 1
o1.AcceptOneWithin(50)
? o1.AcceptTimedOut()
#--> 1
o1.StopListening()
? o1.IsListening()
#--> 0

methods.name: init
methods.brief: Builds a TCP server that is not listening and has no callbacks.

methods.name: Listen
methods.brief: Starts listening on a port and returns at once, firing the error callback on failure.

parameters.name: nPort
parameters.role: the port number

parameters.name: cHost
parameters.role: the address to listen on, where an empty text means 0.0.0.0, every network interface

methods.returns: the server itself, so calls chain
notes: for a local test pass 127.0.0.1, since an empty host opens the port to the network
warnings: a failure does not raise: IsListening stays FALSE and LastError says why; a second listener on a port already bound reported listening too on this Windows machine, with no error

methods.name: AcceptOne
methods.brief: Blocks until a client connects and returns it wrapped as a connected stzTcpClient.
methods.returns: a stzTcpClient; an empty text when the server is not listening or the accept failed, with LastError saying why

methods.name: AcceptOneWithin

parameters.name: nMs

notes: after a timeout LastError is accept timed out, which AcceptTimedOut tests

methods.name: AcceptTimedOut
methods.brief: TRUE if the last wait for a client ended by timeout and not by failure.

methods.name: StopListening
methods.brief: Closes the listening socket; calling it on a server that is not listening does nothing.
methods.returns: the server itself, so calls chain

methods.brief: Sets the function called each time a client is accepted.

methods.name: OnClientDisconnect
methods.brief: Stores a function name meant to run when a client disconnects.

parameters.name: cCallback

methods.returns: the server itself, so calls chain
notes: it is kept but not used
warnings: the server never calls it today

methods.name: OnClientMessage
methods.brief: Stores a function name meant to run when a client sends a message.

parameters.name: cCallback

warnings: the server never calls it today

methods.returns: the server itself, so calls chain

classes.name: stzText
classes.brief: Holds a text as meaning rather than characters and answers natural-language questions about it: stems, tags, entities, tone, keywords, summaries, readability.
classes.description: A stzString is raw characters; a stzText carries meaning. It builds on stzStringText, which already gives Words, Sentences, the counts and the content, and adds the meaning layer, all computed by the engine: Snowball stemming in 25 languages and lemmatization in three, WordNet synonyms and hypernyms, VADER sentiment, Penn Treebank part-of-speech tags with chunking and a nested parse tree, rule-based named entities, stopwords and Flesch readability, RAKE key phrases, TextRank keywords and summaries, and language detection. Two groups upgrade themselves when a model is loaded for the process: the semantic group (Embedding, SemanticSimilarityWith, Classify, MostSimilarSentenceTo, NamedEntities) uses embeddings and a transformer NER head, and the generative pair (SummarizedAbstractively, AnswerAbout) asks a language model. With no model loaded they fall back to word overlap or answer an empty value, so a call never needs a model to run, with one exception noted on SummarizedAbstractively. The word-list methods work on one word or one sentence at a time and are only as good as the rule-based tagger. Known gaps today, each carried as a warning on its method: SummarizedAbstractively raises error R19 without a model, NamedEntities merges a capitalized word after a full stop into the previous entity, and EntityTypeOf and ClassifiedAs pick the first candidate on a tie.
classes.receiver: o1 = new stzText("The food was terrible. I love this wonderful place.")
classes.example:
? o1.Sentiment()
#--> "positive"
? @@( o1.Nouns() )
#--> [ "food", "place" ]

methods.name: StemmedInLanguage
methods.brief: Returns the text with every word cut to its Snowball stem in a given language; an unknown language gives English stems.

parameters.name: pcLang
parameters.role: A language name or code, as text.

methods.returns: text, such as "run dog were jump happili over better fenc."
notes: A stem need not be a real word, and punctuation stays; an argument that is not text gives English stems

methods.name: Stemmed
methods.brief: Returns the text with every word cut to its English stem, so running becomes run.
methods.returns: text, such as "run dog were jump happili over better fenc."
notes: Stem is the same method; stems like happili are not words, which is what separates this from the dictionary form

methods.name: StemmedWordsInLanguage
methods.brief: Returns the stem of each word, as a list, in a given language; an unknown language gives English stems.

parameters.name: pcLang
parameters.role: A language name or code, as text.

methods.returns: a list of text, one stem per word
notes: A text that is not in the language gets stems that are barely changed

methods.name: StemmedWords
methods.brief: Returns the English stem of each word, as a list.
methods.returns: a list of text, one stem per word
notes: WordsStemmed is the same method

methods.name: SupportedStemmerLanguages
methods.brief: Returns the names of the 25 languages that have a Snowball stemmer.
methods.returns: a list of 25 text values, english first

methods.name: SupportedLemmaLanguages
methods.brief: Returns the names of the languages that have a dictionary-form reducer: english, french and arabic.

methods.name: Synonyms
methods.brief: Returns the WordNet words of the same meaning, all senses mixed, for a text that is one word; [ ] for a phrase or an unknown word.
notes: The text is looked up as a whole, so only a single word answers; for dog the list holds hound, frankfurter and andiron together, because every sense counts. SynonymsQ and SynonymsQQ give the list as an object

extensions.name: SynonymsQ
extensions.adds: does what the method does, then returns the object, so the call can be chained

extensions.name: SynonymsQQ
extensions.adds: chains on the next, more specific type of object (the Q ladder)

methods.name: Hypernyms
methods.brief: Returns the broader WordNet terms, all senses mixed, for a text that is one word; [ ] for an unknown word or one without a parent.
notes: For dog the list holds canine and domestic animal but also fellow and villain, because every sense counts

extensions.name: HypernymsQ
extensions.adds: does what the method does, then returns the object, so the call can be chained

extensions.name: HypernymsQQ
extensions.adds: chains on the next, more specific type of object (the Q ladder)

methods.name: IsSynonymOf
methods.brief: TRUE if WordNet lists the other word as meaning the same as the text, ignoring case; a word is never its own synonym.

parameters.name: pcOther
parameters.role: The other text, to compare with or combine with.

methods.returns: TRUE or FALSE; FALSE when the argument is not text
notes: The text must be a single word, as with the lookup itself

methods.name: HasSynonyms
methods.brief: TRUE if WordNet knows at least one word of the same meaning.

methods.name: LemmatizedInLanguage
methods.brief: Returns the text with every word reduced to its dictionary form in english, french or arabic; another language gives English.

parameters.name: pcLang
parameters.role: A language name or code, as text.

methods.returns: text, such as "le cheval manger un pommer rouge" for French "les chevaux mangeaient des pommes rouges"
notes: An argument that is not text gives English

methods.name: Lemmatized
methods.brief: Returns the text with every word reduced to its English dictionary form, so were becomes be and fences becomes fence.
methods.returns: text, such as "run dog be jump happily over well fence."
notes: Lemma is the same method; unlike stemming the result is made of real words, but better can come out as well

methods.name: LemmatizedWordsInLanguage
methods.brief: Returns the dictionary form of each word, as a list, in english, french or arabic; another language gives English.

parameters.name: pcLang
parameters.role: A language name or code, as text.

methods.returns: a list of text, one form per word

methods.name: LemmatizedWords
methods.brief: Returns the English dictionary form of each word, as a list.
methods.returns: a list of text, one form per word
notes: WordsLemmatized is the same method

methods.name: SentimentScore
methods.brief: Returns the VADER compound score of the whole text, from -1 for the most negative to +1 for the most positive; 0 for an empty text.
notes: SentimentCompound is the same method; The food was terrible. scores -0.48

methods.name: Sentiment
methods.brief: Returns the tone of the text as "positive" at a score of 0.05 or more, "negative" at -0.05 or less, and "neutral" in between.
notes: The table is made of wood. is neutral

methods.name: PositiveScore
methods.brief: Returns the share of the text that VADER counts as positive, between 0 and 1.
notes: The three shares add up to about 1

methods.name: NegativeScore
methods.brief: Returns the share of the text that VADER counts as negative, between 0 and 1.
notes: The three shares add up to about 1

methods.name: NeutralScore
methods.brief: Returns the share of the text that VADER counts as neither positive nor negative, between 0 and 1.
notes: The three shares add up to about 1

methods.name: IsPositive
methods.brief: TRUE if the sentiment score reaches +0.05.

methods.name: IsNegative
methods.brief: TRUE if the sentiment score is -0.05 or below.

methods.name: SentimentExplained
methods.brief: Returns the verdict with its evidence: the overall label and score, then the positive and the negative words with their VADER weights.
methods.returns: a list of three entries: [ "overall", label, score ], [ "positive_words", [ [ word, weight ] ... ] ] and [ "negative_words", [ [ word, weight ] ... ] ]
notes: It is a list, not a sentence; for The food was terrible. the negative words are [ [ "terrible", -2.1 ] ]

methods.name: POSTags
methods.brief: Returns the Penn Treebank part-of-speech tag of each word, in word order.
methods.returns: a list of text, such as "DT", "JJ", "NN", "VBZ"
notes: PartOfSpeechTags is the same method; the tagger is rule-based and can be wrong, for example brown fox comes out as JJ NN NN

methods.name: TaggedWords
methods.brief: Returns each word paired with its part-of-speech tag, in word order.
methods.returns: a list of [ word, tag ] pairs
notes: WordsWithPOS is the same method; the first pair of Running dogs is [ "Running", "VBG" ]

methods.name: Chunks
methods.brief: Returns the runs of words whose tags fit a pattern of Penn tags, scanning left to right and taking the longest run.

parameters.name: pcTagPattern
parameters.role: Penn tags separated by spaces, each with an optional quantifier ? * or +, matched by prefix and without regard to case

methods.returns: a list of text, one per run; [ ] for an empty pattern
notes: The tag NN also covers NNS and NNP; DT? JJ* NN+ finds The quick brown fox and the lazy dog

methods.name: ParseTree
methods.brief: Returns the nested phrase structure of the text as a bracket string, built with a default grammar of NP, PP and VP phrases.
methods.returns: text, such as "(S (NP The/DT quick/JJ brown/NN fox/NN) (VP jumps/VBZ (PP over/IN (NP the/DT lazy/JJ dog/NN))))"
notes: Words that fit no phrase hang directly under S; ParseTreeQ gives the navigable stzParseTree object

extensions.name: ParseTreeQ
extensions.adds: does what the method does, then returns the object, so the call can be chained

methods.name: ParseTreeWithQ
methods.brief: Returns a stzParseTree built by applying your own cascade of phrase rules, in order, over the tagged words.

parameters.name: paGrammar
parameters.role: a list of [ label, tag pattern ] rules, where a later rule may use an earlier label as a tag

methods.returns: a stzParseTree; its ToBracket method gives the bracket string
notes: An empty grammar gives a flat tree with every word under S
warnings: A grammar that is not a list raises error R5

methods.name: NounPhrases
methods.brief: Returns the noun phrases of the text: an optional determiner, adjectives, then one or more nouns.
methods.returns: a list of text, such as "A big red car" and "the old station"
notes: It is Chunks with the pattern DT? JJ* NN+

methods.name: NamedEntities
methods.brief: Returns the people, companies and places found in the text as [ entity, type ] pairs, using a neural NER model if loaded, else rules.
methods.returns: a list of [ entity, type ] pairs with types such as PERSON, ORGANIZATION, LOCATION and ENTITY; [ ] when there is none
notes: Entities is the same method; Barack Obama visited Microsoft in Paris. gives [ "Barack Obama", "PERSON" ] and [ "Microsoft", "ORGANIZATION" ]
warnings: The rule-based recognizer joins a capitalized word that follows a full stop to the entity before it, so Paris. Angela Merkel comes out as one ENTITY (seen on three texts)

methods.name: NeuralEntities
methods.brief: Returns the [ entity, type ] pairs from the loaded transformer NER model, and an empty list when none is loaded.
methods.returns: a list of [ entity, type ] pairs; [ ] without a model
notes: Run without a model here, so only the empty answer was seen

methods.name: RegisterNamedEntities
methods.brief: Adds the named entities to the shared world store of the process, marked with the source ner, and tells how many were new.
methods.returns: a number; 5 the first time for two sentences with five entities, 0 when repeated
notes: It changes the shared world store, not the text; EntitiesToWorld is the same method

methods.name: EntitiesOfType
methods.brief: Returns the entity names of one type, in text order; the type must be written exactly.

parameters.name: pcType
parameters.role: A type name, as text.

methods.returns: a list of text; [ ] for a type that is absent or written in another case
notes: EntitiesOfType("PERSON") finds Barack Obama while "person" finds nothing

methods.name: PersonNames
methods.brief: Returns the entity names typed PERSON.

methods.name: Organizations
methods.brief: Returns the entity names typed ORGANIZATION.

methods.name: Locations
methods.brief: Returns the entity names typed LOCATION.

methods.name: EntityTypeOf
methods.brief: Returns the candidate type whose meaning is closest to an entity name; an empty string when an argument has the wrong type.

parameters.name: pcEntity
parameters.role: the entity name to type

parameters.name: paTypes
parameters.role: the list of candidate type names, each text

methods.returns: text, one of the candidate types
notes: A loaded neural model ranks the candidates by meaning, which was not available here
warnings: Without a neural model a short name scores 0 against every candidate, so the first candidate always wins (Microsoft gets city when city is listed first)

methods.name: EntitiesTypedAs
methods.brief: Returns each named entity with the best candidate type for it, as [ entity, type ] pairs; [ ] when the types are not a list.

parameters.name: paTypes
parameters.role: the list of candidate type names, each text

methods.returns: a list of [ entity, type ] pairs
notes: Needs a loaded neural model to choose by meaning
warnings: Without a neural model every entity gets the first candidate (all five entities of one text came out as city)

extensions.name: EntitiesTypedAsQ

extensions.name: EntitiesTypedAsQQ

methods.name: ContentWords
methods.brief: Returns the words that are not stopwords, in order, keeping their case.
notes: Keywords is the same method; The food was terrible. gives [ "food", "terrible" ]

methods.name: WithoutStopwords
methods.brief: Returns the content words joined by single spaces, with the stopwords and the punctuation dropped.

methods.name: IsStopword
methods.brief: TRUE if the text is a stopword.

methods.name: ReadingEase
methods.brief: Returns the Flesch reading-ease score, higher meaning easier to read; 0 for an empty text.
methods.returns: a number, such as 75.88 for The food was terrible.

extensions.name: KeyPhrasesQ

extensions.name: KeyPhrasesQQ

extensions.name: RankedKeywordsXT

methods.name: WordsThatAre

extensions.name: NounsQ
extensions.adds: does what the method does, then returns the object, so the call can be chained

notes: DetectedLanguage is the same method

methods.name: AutoLemmatized
methods.brief: Returns the text reduced to dictionary forms in its own detected tongue, English when that is unknown.
notes: A French text comes out as le cheval manger un pommer rouge

methods.name: AutoStemmed
methods.brief: Returns the text cut to stems in its own detected tongue, English when that is unknown.
notes: A French text comes out as le cheval mang de pomm roug

methods.name: Profile
methods.brief: Returns a content profile as eight [ name, value ] pairs, from the tongue and the word count to the top keywords and the entities.
methods.returns: a list of eight [ name, value ] pairs
notes: top_keywords holds the five most frequent words once the stopwords are dropped

methods.name: LexicalDiversity
methods.brief: Returns the ratio of different words to all words, between 0 and 1; 0 for an empty text.
notes: TypeTokenRatio is the same method; the the the the gives 0.25

methods.name: StyleProfile
methods.brief: Returns a style profile as [ name, value ] pairs: avg_word_length, avg_words_per_sentence and lexical_diversity.
methods.returns: a list of three [ name, value ] pairs

methods.name: InContextWithWindow
methods.brief: Returns one line for each occurrence of a word, ignoring case: the word with up to a number of words on each side.

parameters.name: pcWord
parameters.role: A word, as text.

parameters.name: nWindow
parameters.role: how many words to take on each side of the word

methods.returns: a list of text; [ ] when the word is absent or not text
notes: A window of 0 gives the word alone
warnings: A window that is not a number raises error R41

methods.name: InContext
methods.brief: Returns every occurrence of a word with 5 words of context on each side, as in a concordance.

parameters.name: pcWord
parameters.role: A word, as text.

methods.returns: a list of text, one line per occurrence
notes: Concordance is the same method

methods.name: ComparedTo
methods.brief: Returns how this text and another compare, as pairs: similarity, sentiment_delta, grade_delta and shared_keywords.

parameters.name: pcOther
parameters.role: The other text, to compare with or combine with.

methods.returns: a list of four [ name, value ] pairs; [ ] when the argument is not text
notes: The two deltas are this text minus the other one; shared_keywords lists the content words both texts hold

methods.name: ShowTagged
methods.brief: Prints the words with their tags as word/TAG on one line, then hands the text object back.
methods.returns: the text object, so calls can be chained
notes: The printed line looks like The/DT food/NN was/VBD terrible/JJ

methods.name: ShowEntities
methods.brief: Prints the text with every named entity wrapped as [entity:TYPE], then hands the text object back.
methods.returns: the text object, so calls can be chained
notes: The wrapping is a plain replace, so an entity inside a longer word is wrapped there too

methods.name: ShowSentiment
methods.brief: Prints one line per sentence, as (tone score) followed by the sentence, then hands the text object back.
methods.returns: the text object, so calls can be chained
notes: The first line looks like (negative -0.53) The food was terrible!

classes.name: stzTextStream
classes.brief: Wraps the RingQt text stream to read text from an attached device, line by line or all at once.
classes.description: It is a thin wrapper over QTextStream and needs RingQt: load guilib.ring before stzlib, otherwise building one raises class not found: qtextstream. Attach a source with SetFromFile (a file path), SetFromProcess or SetFromSocket (any open RingQt device works, such as a QBuffer over a QByteArray), then read with ReadAll, Lines or ReadLine. Reading consumes the device: a second ReadAll finds nothing, and ReadLine takes the whole rest to hand back one line. IsSetFromFile, IsSetFromSocket and IsSetFromProcess tell which kind was attached last, and SourceOfStream names it. The text is decoded with the default codec until SetEncoding names another one: plain ASCII is exact either way, while Hebrew, Arabic or emoji text is read back garbled unless SetEncoding("UTF-8") was called first. SetEncoding applies one of UTF-8, ISO-8859-1 (or latin1), UTF-16, UTF-16LE, UTF-16BE, UTF-32, UTF-32LE and UTF-32BE, whatever the letter case, and refuses every other name. The stream is meant for reading: SetBOM, Reset and Flush are kept for the writing side, which this class does not offer.
classes.example:
oBA = new QByteArray()
oBA.append("alpha" + char(10) + "beta")
oBuf = new QBuffer(NULL)
oBuf.setData(oBA)
oBuf.open(1)
o1.SetFromProcess(oBuf)
? @@( o1.Lines() )
#--> [ "alpha", "beta" ]
? o1.Status()
#--> ok

methods.name: init
methods.brief: Builds a text stream, a thin wrapper over the RingQt QTextStream with no device attached yet.
notes: build it, then attach a source with SetFromFile, SetFromProcess or SetFromSocket
warnings: raises R11 class not found: qtextstream unless RingQt is loaded first with load "guilib.ring", which stzlib does not do

methods.name: SetFromFile
methods.brief: Opens a file for reading and attaches it as the source of the stream, closing any file attached before.

parameters.name: pcFile
parameters.role: the path of the file to read

methods.returns: 1 when the file was opened and attached, 0 when it was not (a missing file, a folder, a path that cannot be read, or a value that is not a text)
notes: the file is opened read-only through a RingQt QFile that the stream keeps, and it stays open until Delete or until another source replaces it, so call Delete when done; a failed call leaves the stream and its flags as they were
warnings: the text is decoded with the default codec: call SetEncoding("UTF-8") for text that is not ASCII

methods.name: SetFromSocket
methods.brief: Attaches an open RingQt socket object as the source of the stream and records the source as a socket.

parameters.name: poQSocket
parameters.role: the RingQt socket object, such as a QTcpSocket

methods.returns: 1 when the object was attached, 0 when the value is not an object
notes: an unconnected QTcpSocket is accepted; a failed call leaves the stream and its flags as they were
warnings: nothing checks that the object is really a socket: any RingQt device object is taken; not run against a connected socket

methods.name: SetFromScocket
methods.brief: Keeps the old misspelled name of the call that attaches a socket, with the same result.

parameters.name: poQSocket
parameters.role: the RingQt socket object, such as a QTcpSocket

methods.returns: 1 when the object was attached, 0 when the value is not an object
notes: kept so that older code still works; write SetFromSocket in new code

methods.name: SetFromProcess
methods.brief: Attaches a RingQt device object as the source of the stream and records the source as a process.

parameters.name: poQProcess
parameters.role: the RingQt device object, a QProcess in intention

methods.returns: 1 when the object was attached, 0 when the value is not an object
notes: an open QBuffer over a QByteArray reads text from memory; a failed call leaves the stream and its flags as they were
warnings: nothing checks that the object is really a process: any RingQt device object is taken; not run with a started process, only with an in-memory QBuffer

methods.name: SetBOM
methods.brief: Sets whether the stream writes a byte order mark when it writes Unicode text.

parameters.name: bTrueOrFalse
parameters.role: 1 to write the mark, 0 not to

notes: the stream is used for reading here, so it has no visible effect

methods.name: SetAutoDetectUnicode
methods.brief: Sets whether the stream recognises UTF-16 and UTF-32 text by its byte order mark when reading.

parameters.name: bTrueOrFalse
parameters.role: 1 to detect, 0 not to

notes: IsUnicodeAutoDetected reads it back: 1 by default, 0 after SetAutoDetectUnicode(0)

methods.name: SetEncoding
methods.brief: Selects the codec the stream decodes its text with, from a fixed list of encoding names.

parameters.name: pcEncodingName
parameters.role: one of UTF-8, utf8, ISO-8859-1, latin1, UTF-16, UTF-16LE, UTF-16BE, UTF-32, UTF-32LE or UTF-32BE, in any letter case

methods.returns: 1 when the codec was applied, 0 when the name is not in that list (or is not a text); nothing changes then
notes: Encoding answers the name that was applied, an empty text before any; UTF-8 makes Hebrew, Arabic and emoji text read back exact, and the call works before or after a source is attached, and survives a later attach
warnings: only the names listed are accepted, though Qt knows more; a name outside the list is refused and never reaches Qt, which would ignore it silently

methods.name: SetStatus
methods.brief: Sets the stream's status to one of four named states, so Status reads it back.

parameters.name: pcStatus
parameters.role: one of the names Ok, ReadPastEnd, ReadCorruptData or WriteFailed

methods.returns: 1; an unknown name raises an error naming it
notes: read the status with Status; Qt keeps the first problem: once the status is not ok, a further SetStatus changes nothing until ResetStatus

methods.name: SetLocale
methods.brief: Sets the locale the stream uses to format and read numbers, from a locale name or a QLocale object.

parameters.name: pcLocale
parameters.role: a locale name such as de_DE or C, or a RingQt QLocale object

methods.returns: 1 when the locale was applied, 0 when the value is neither a text nor an object
notes: Locale().name() reads it back; a name Qt does not know falls back to the C locale

methods.name: Pointer
methods.brief: Returns the RingQt QTextStream object that does the reading.

methods.name: SourceOfStream
methods.brief: Returns the kind of source attached last, as lower-case text.
methods.returns: a text: file, process or socket; an empty text before any source is attached
notes: the text is lower case because the code writes :File, :Process and :Socket

methods.name: IsSetFromFile
methods.brief: Tells whether the source attached last is a file.
methods.returns: TRUE or FALSE, as 1 or 0; 0 before any source is attached
notes: a failed SetFromFile leaves it as it was

methods.name: IsSetFromSocket
methods.brief: Tells whether the source attached last is a socket.
methods.returns: TRUE or FALSE, as 1 or 0; 0 before any source is attached
notes: true after SetFromSocket and after its old spelling SetFromScocket

methods.name: IsSetFromProcess
methods.brief: Tells whether the source attached last is a process.
methods.returns: TRUE or FALSE, as 1 or 0; 0 before any source is attached
notes: a device attached with SetFromProcess counts, whatever it really is

methods.name: IsUnicodeAutoDetected
methods.brief: TRUE if the stream recognises UTF-16 and UTF-32 text by its byte order mark.
notes: 1 on a new stream

methods.name: Encoding
methods.brief: Returns the name of the encoding that SetEncoding applied last, as it was written.
methods.returns: a text; an empty text when SetEncoding has not applied a name, which means the default codec
notes: a refused name does not change it

methods.name: TextEncoding
methods.brief: Returns the RingQt QTextCodec object the stream decodes its text with.
notes: RingQt gives no way to read a codec's name: ask Encoding for the name applied

methods.name: FilePointer
methods.brief: Returns the RingQt device object attached to the stream, whatever kind it is.
notes: the same call as SocketPointer and ProcessPointer; the name does not mean the source is a file

methods.name: SocketPointer
methods.brief: Returns the RingQt device object attached to the stream, whatever kind it is.
notes: the same call as FilePointer and ProcessPointer; the name does not mean the source is a socket

methods.name: ProcessPointer
methods.brief: Returns the RingQt device object attached to the stream, whatever kind it is.
notes: the same call as FilePointer and SocketPointer; the name does not mean the source is a process

methods.name: Status
methods.brief: Returns the stream's status as lower-case text.
methods.returns: a text: ok on a healthy stream, or readpastend, readcorruptdata or writefailed after SetStatus names one
notes: ok on a new stream and after reading to the end

methods.name: Locale
methods.brief: Returns the RingQt QLocale object the stream uses.

methods.name: ReadAll
methods.brief: Reads everything left on the device and returns it as one text, leaving nothing to read.
methods.returns: a text; an empty text when nothing is left or no device is attached
notes: call SetEncoding("UTF-8") first for Hebrew, Arabic or emoji text, which is then exact
warnings: a second call returns an empty text, since the first consumed the device; without SetEncoding, non-ASCII text comes back garbled, each UTF-8 byte read as one Latin-1 character, because the default codec is not UTF-8; ASCII text is exact

methods.name: Lines
methods.brief: Reads everything left on the device and returns it as a list of lines.
methods.returns: a list of text; [ ] when nothing is left
notes: alpha, beta and gamma on three lines give [ alpha, beta, gamma ]
warnings: consumes the device as ReadAll does, so a second call returns [ ]; non-ASCII text comes back garbled as for ReadAll unless SetEncoding("UTF-8") was called

methods.name: ReadLine
methods.brief: Reads everything left on the device and returns the line at a position, discarding the other lines.

parameters.name: n
parameters.role: the 1-based position of the line

notes: take Lines once and index it
warnings: it does not read one line: all the lines are consumed, so a second call finds nothing; a position of 0 or past the last line raises Array Access (Index out of range) (R2); non-ASCII text comes back garbled as for ReadAll

methods.name: Delete
methods.brief: Frees the underlying RingQt QTextStream and closes the file attached by SetFromFile, if any.
notes: the helper must not be used afterwards; a device attached by SetFromProcess or SetFromSocket is not closed, since the caller owns it

methods.name: Flush
methods.brief: Pushes any text waiting in the stream's buffer through to its device.
notes: nothing needs flushing for a reading stream, so it changes nothing visible; it is safe with no device attached

methods.name: Reset
methods.brief: Resets the stream's number and field formatting to its defaults, without rewinding the device.
notes: seek the device back yourself to read again
warnings: after ReadAll, Reset and another ReadAll the second read is empty, and SetAutoDetectUnicode(0) survives it

methods.name: ResetStatus
methods.brief: Resets the stream's status to ok.

methods.name: SetSourceOfStreamTo
methods.brief: Records which kind of source feeds the stream.

parameters.name: pcSource
parameters.role: the kind, File, Socket or Process

notes: it is called by the three SetFrom methods; only the flag of the kind given is 1
warnings: private: calling it from outside raises R26 Calling private method from outside the class

methods.name: ReapplyEncoding
methods.brief: Applies the encoding chosen with SetEncoding again, because attaching a device resets the codec.
notes: it is called by the three SetFrom methods after the device is attached; it does nothing when no encoding was chosen
warnings: private: calling it from outside raises R26 Calling private method from outside the class

methods.name: ReleaseFile
methods.brief: Closes the file that SetFromFile attached, if there is one, and forgets it.
notes: it is called before another source replaces the file and by Delete
warnings: private: calling it from outside raises R26 Calling private method from outside the class

classes.name: stzTheme
classes.brief: Holds a named colour theme as plain data, with every role resolved to hex, and exports it as CSS, JSON or a Ring list.
classes.description: A theme fills in eight roles: primary, success, warning, danger, info, muted, neutral and background. Each role except background carries four steps, surface, border, solid and text, and the colour that reads best on its solid step. Tokens flattens the theme to 43 name and colour pairs and ToCSS, ToJSON and ToRing all write from that one list, so the exports cannot disagree. A misspelt theme raises an error rather than exporting wrong colours. The themes are neutral, light, dark, vibrant, pro, access, print, gray, lightgray and darkgray.
classes.example:
? o1.Name()
#--> pro
? o1.ColorOf(:Primary)
#--> #4D4DC9
? o1.StepOf(:Primary, :Surface)
#--> #EAEDFF
? len(o1.Tokens())
#--> 43
? o1.Tokens()[1][1]
#--> primary
? StzThemeTokenOf(StzThemeFromCSS(o1.ToCSS()), "primary")
#--> #4D4DC9

methods.name: init
methods.brief: Builds a theme by name, keeping its name in lower case.

parameters.name: pcName
parameters.role: the theme name, in any letter case, one of neutral, light, dark, vibrant, pro, access, print, gray, lightgray or darkgray

notes: StzThemeQ builds the same object
warnings: an empty name raises error stzTheme: name a theme, and an unknown name such as nope raises error stzTheme: ... is not a theme, with the list of the ten themes, so a misspelt theme never exports plausible wrong colours

methods.name: Name
methods.brief: Returns the lower-case name of the theme.
methods.returns: the name as text, such as pro

methods.name: Roles
methods.brief: Returns the roles a theme fills in: primary, success, warning, danger, info, muted, neutral and background.
methods.returns: a list of eight role names as text
notes: background is a surface: it has a colour but no steps and no on-colour

methods.name: ColorOf
methods.brief: Returns the colour a theme gives to a role, as a hex code.

parameters.name: pcRole
parameters.role: the role, as a symbol or a text such as :Danger

methods.returns: the colour as text such as #4D4DC9; an empty text for a role the theme does not have
notes: it is always resolved to hex, never left as an expression, because the far side of an export has no resolver

methods.name: StepOf
methods.brief: Returns one of the four steps of a role's colour, Surface, Border, Solid or Text, as a hex code.

parameters.name: pcRole
parameters.role: the role, such as :Danger

parameters.name: pcStep
parameters.role: the step, one of :Surface, :Border, :Solid or :Text

methods.returns: the colour as text; an empty text for an unknown role or step
notes: the steps are the same hue at four lightnesses, from palest to deepest text

methods.name: OnColorOf
methods.brief: Returns the colour that reads best as text on the solid step of a role.

parameters.name: pcRole
parameters.role: the role whose solid step is the background

methods.returns: the colour as a hex code chosen for contrast; an empty text for an unknown role
notes: the choice is measured against the solid step, not guessed

methods.name: Tokens
methods.brief: Returns the whole theme flattened to name and colour pairs, the list every export is written from.
methods.returns: a list of [ name, hex ] pairs: 43 for a theme, each role as role, role-surface, role-border, role-solid, role-text and on-role, and background alone
notes: CSS, JSON and Ring all read this one list, so the three cannot disagree about which tokens exist

methods.name: ToCSS
methods.brief: Returns the theme as CSS custom properties in a :root block, every token under the --stz- prefix.
methods.returns: a text starting with a comment naming the theme
notes: StzThemeFromCSS reads the text back as [ name, hex ] pairs, and StzThemeTokenOf reads one token from them

methods.name: ToJSON
methods.brief: Returns the theme as a JSON object with the theme name and a tokens table, for design tools.
methods.returns: a text holding a theme key and a tokens object

methods.name: ToRing
methods.brief: Returns the theme as the source of a Ring list literal that can be written to a file and loaded.
methods.returns: a text starting with a comment and an assignment named aTheme followed by the capitalised name
notes: a dash in a token name becomes an underscore, as in :primary_surface

classes.name: stzTile
classes.brief: Draws a grid of square cells with box lines, marking the current cell, obstacles and a path, for navigation and puzzles.
classes.description: A stzTile is a stzGrid, so build one with new stzTile([ columns, rows ]) or StzTileQ(...) and use every grid method: AddObstacle, MoveToNode, paths, connected regions (Rooms). The class adds the drawing: Show prints it, ToString returns it, Legend names the characters used, and ShowCustomGrid draws other contents in the same frame. Positions count from 1, with the column first.

methods.name: init
methods.brief: Builds a tile, a grid of square cells drawn with box lines, from its number of columns and rows.

parameters.name: panColRow
parameters.role: a pair of numbers, [ columns, rows ]

methods.returns: nothing; the object is built, current cell at column 1, row 1
notes: everything stzGrid offers (AddObstacle, MoveToNode, paths, regions) is available on a tile
warnings: anything but a pair of numbers raises "Incorrect param type! panColRow must be a pair of numbers."

methods.name: SetObstacleCell
methods.brief: Sets the text that fills an obstacle cell when the tile is drawn, up to 3 characters.

parameters.name: cChar
parameters.role: the text drawn in an obstacle cell, 3 bytes at most

notes: a one-character text is padded with a space on each side the first time the tile is drawn, so Legend afterwards shows " X " for "X"
warnings: A text longer than 3 bytes raises "Incorrect param value! cChar must be a string of maximum 3 chars.", and the size is counted in bytes: one emoji, 4 bytes, is refused although it is one character

methods.name: SetObstacleChar
methods.brief: Sets the text that fills an obstacle cell when the tile is drawn, the same as SetObstacleCell.

parameters.name: cChar
parameters.role: the text drawn in an obstacle cell, 3 bytes at most

warnings: the same byte limit: one emoji is refused

methods.name: Show
methods.brief: Prints the tile on the console: column and row numbers, box lines, the current cell as a heart and the obstacles filled in.
notes: the box characters need a UTF-8 console

methods.name: ToString
methods.brief: Returns the tile drawn as text with box lines and numbers, the current cell marked by a heart, and the obstacles filled in.
notes: the drawing changes with the grid state: obstacles, the current cell and a path if one is shown

methods.name: Legend
methods.brief: Returns a one-line text that names the size of the tile and the characters used for the current cell, the obstacles and the path.
methods.returns: a text that starts "Tile: 4x3" and lists the current, obstacle and path characters

methods.name: ShowCustomGrid
methods.brief: Prints the frame of the tile with the given items in its cells instead of its own state.

parameters.name: aCustomGrid
parameters.role: a list of rows, each a list of the texts to show, with at least as many rows and columns as the tile

notes: the current cell is still marked by the arrow and v, but not by the heart
warnings: A list with fewer rows or columns than the tile raises R2 (Array Access, Index out of range)

classes.name: stzTime
classes.brief: Holds one time of day (hour, minute, second, millisecond) with no date, moves it around the clock, compares it and writes it in several formats.
classes.description: A stzTime is four numbers and never knows the day: adding 10 hours to 14:30 gives 00:30 and 23:00 is not before 01:00. Build it from a text (14:30, 14:30:15.250, 2:30 PM with a space before PM), from a number of seconds since midnight, from a hash with :Hour, :Minute, :Second and :Millisecond, or from an empty text for the clock now (the engine clock, which ran an hour behind Ring time() on this machine). The Add and Subtract methods move the object itself and answer the new HH:mm:ss text (the Q forms answer the object so calls chain); the Next and Previous methods answer a text and leave the object alone. Measure with SecsTo, MinutesTo and HoursTo, compare with IsBefore, IsAfter, IsEqualTo and IsBetween (to the second: the milliseconds are ignored), ask about the day with IsMorning, IsNight, IsWorkHours and PartOfDay, and write it with ToString, ToShort, ToLong or ToStringXT. Hours, Minutes, Seconds and Milliseconds are the parts of the time, not totals. Known gaps today, each carried as a warning on its method: To12Hour, ToSimple and the AP formats keep the 24-hour hour, ToHuman words the quarter-to wrongly at 11:45, 12:45, 23:45 and 00:45, ToRelative reads past as future, new stzTime(0) reads the clock, MSecsTo reads a time text as midnight, and the operators and comparisons refuse a time text such as 15:45 because StzIsTime accepts only one-digit parts.

methods.name: init
methods.brief: Builds the time of day from a time text, a number of seconds since midnight, a hash of parts, or the clock when the text is empty.

parameters.name: pTime
parameters.role: a time text such as 14:30:15.250 or 2:30 PM, a number of seconds since midnight such as 3661, a hash [ :Hour = 8, :Minute = 5, :Second = 9, :Millisecond = 45 ], or an empty text for now

notes: digits after a dot are a whole number of milliseconds, so .5 is 5 ms and .250 is 250 ms; an empty text reads the engine clock, which showed one hour less than Ring time() on this machine; hash keys are the singular :Hour, :Minute, :Second, :Millisecond and a missing one is 0
warnings: the number 0 reads the current clock instead of midnight (0 equals an empty text in Ring); a negative number or one of 86400 and more raises Invalid time provided!; a fraction of a second gives a broken second (01:01:1.50); a plain list [ 8, 5, 9 ] is ignored and gives 00:00:00; 2:30pm without a space before PM raises R41; hour 24, minute 60 and second 60 raise Invalid time provided!

methods.name: ParseStringTime
methods.brief: Sets the time from a text of hours and minutes, with seconds, milliseconds and AM or PM when present.

parameters.name: _cTime_
parameters.role: the time text, such as 07:45:10.500 or 3:15 PM, with a space before AM or PM

methods.returns: nothing; the object changes in place
notes: 12:xx AM becomes hour 0 and a PM hour below 12 gets 12 added; an hour of 13 or more with PM is kept as given
warnings: does not check ranges: 25:61:61 is stored and IsValid then answers FALSE; a text without two or three parts separated by : raises Cannot parse time string

methods.name: AddSeconds
methods.brief: Moves the time forward by n seconds, or back when n is negative, wrapping around midnight, and answers the new time text.

parameters.name: _nSeconds_
parameters.role: the number of seconds to add

methods.returns: the new time as HH:mm:ss text, without milliseconds
notes: changes the object in place and keeps its milliseconds; 23:59:30 plus 45 seconds is 00:00:15; AddSecondsQ answers the object so calls chain
warnings: a fractional count leaves a fractional second in the object (12:00:0.50)

extensions.name: AddSecondsQ
extensions.adds: does what the method does, then returns the object, so the call can be chained

methods.name: AddMinutes
methods.brief: Moves the time forward by n minutes, or back when n is negative, wrapping around midnight, and answers the new time text.

parameters.name: _nMinutes_
parameters.role: the number of minutes to add

methods.returns: the new time as HH:mm:ss text, without milliseconds
notes: changes the object in place; AddMinutesQ answers the object so calls chain

extensions.name: AddMinutesQ
extensions.adds: does what the method does, then returns the object, so the call can be chained

methods.name: AddHours
methods.brief: Moves the time forward by n hours, or back when n is negative, wrapping around midnight, and answers the new time text.

parameters.name: _nHours_
parameters.role: the number of hours to add, a half hour is 0.5

methods.returns: the new time as HH:mm:ss text, without milliseconds
notes: changes the object in place; the date is not tracked, so 14:30 plus 10 hours is 00:30; AddHoursQ answers the object so calls chain

extensions.name: AddHoursQ
extensions.adds: does what the method does, then returns the object, so the call can be chained

methods.name: AddMilliseconds
methods.brief: Moves the time forward by n milliseconds, carrying into seconds and wrapping around midnight, and answers the new time text.

parameters.name: _nMs_
parameters.role: the number of milliseconds to add

methods.returns: the new time as HH:mm:ss text, without milliseconds
notes: changes the object in place; the milliseconds show in ToLong, not in the answer; 23:59:59.900 plus 200 is 00:00:00.100; AddMillisecondsQ answers the object

extensions.name: AddMillisecondsQ
extensions.adds: does what the method does, then returns the object, so the call can be chained

methods.name: SubtractSeconds
methods.brief: Moves the time back by n seconds, wrapping around midnight, and answers the new time text.

parameters.name: _nSeconds_
parameters.role: the number of seconds to subtract

methods.returns: the new time as HH:mm:ss text, without milliseconds
notes: changes the object in place; 00:00:10 minus 20 seconds is 23:59:50; SubtractSecondsQ answers the object

extensions.name: SubtractSecondsQ
extensions.adds: does what the method does, then returns the object, so the call can be chained

methods.name: SubtractMinutes
methods.brief: Moves the time back by n minutes, wrapping around midnight, and answers the new time text.

parameters.name: _nMinutes_
parameters.role: the number of minutes to subtract

methods.returns: the new time as HH:mm:ss text, without milliseconds
notes: changes the object in place; SubtractMinutesQ answers the object so calls chain

extensions.name: SubtractMinutesQ
extensions.adds: does what the method does, then returns the object, so the call can be chained

methods.name: SubtractHours
methods.brief: Moves the time back by n hours, wrapping around midnight, and answers the new time text.

parameters.name: _nHours_
parameters.role: the number of hours to subtract

methods.returns: the new time as HH:mm:ss text, without milliseconds
notes: changes the object in place; 00:30 minus 1 hour is 23:30; SubtractHoursQ answers the object

classes.name: stzTimeLine
classes.brief: Holds a stretch of time with labelled points and labelled spans on it, and answers what is at a date, what overlaps, where the gaps are, and draws it in text.
classes.description: A timeline runs from a start to an end, both dates or dates with a time, and everything on it is kept as text such as "2024-02-14 10:00:00". A point is a single labelled moment; a span is a labelled stretch with a start and an end. Both must lie inside the timeline, and neither may touch the blocked points and blocked spans that reserve parts of it. Labels may repeat. Point labels are stored in capitals and are matched in any case, but a span label keeps the case it was given, and FindSpan, HasSpan, RemoveSpan and RenameSpanLabel compare in capitals, so a span added as "Alpha" cannot be found through them while Span, SpanStart, SpanEnd and SpanDuration, which compare exactly, can. Many alternative spellings exist (moment, instant, period). Durations are whole seconds. ToString draws the timeline with box characters and a table of dates. Known defects, each carried as a warning: HasMoment and its spellings recurse until the stack overflows; WhatsAt for a time of day matches nearly every span; Gaps and UncoveredPeriods are wrong when one span contains others, and UncoveredPeriods answers nothing for a timeline without spans; Distance works only for point labels.

classes.name: stzTimerManager
classes.brief: Runs a loop that ticks timers every few milliseconds, drains pending HTTP requests and stops when there is nothing left to do.
classes.description: Add started timers with AddTimer and call RunLoop. Each pass ticks every timer, drops the finished one-shots, drains the pending asynchronous requests of the stzReactiveHttp you hand in, advances detached timers and waits SetCheckFrequency milliseconds, on a real timer of the reactor if SetReactor gave one and a sleep otherwise. The loop ends when no timer remains and the patience, a count of idle passes, is used up, or when Stop is called. The manager keeps copies of its timers, so a callback stopping its own copy does not stop the manager's, and a loop with a repeating timer runs until the manager itself is stopped.
classes.receiver: $nFired = 0 oEngine = new stzReactive() o1 = new stzTimerManager() o1.SetCheckFrequency(5) o2 = new stzReactiveTimer("first", 20, func { $nFired += 1 }, oEngine, 1) o3 = new stzReactiveTimer("second", 40, func { $nFired += 10 }, oEngine, 1) o2.Start() o3.Start() o1.AddTimer(o2) o1.AddTimer(o3)
classes.example:
o1.RunLoop("")
? $nFired
#--> 11

notes: the manager's loop keeps copies of the timers it is given

parameters.role: the wait in milliseconds, above 0

methods.returns: the manager itself, so calls chain

methods.returns: the manager itself, so calls chain
notes: the default 0 stops as soon as there is no work, like libuv; a count, not a duration

methods.name: SetReactor

parameters.name: poReactor
parameters.role: a stzReactor, or an empty text for the plain sleep

methods.returns: the manager itself, so calls chain
notes: the stored reactor is a copy that shares the engine handle

notes: the manager stores a copy, so later changes to the caller's timer do not reach it; the timer must have been started or it never fires

notes: an unknown id does nothing; when no timer is left the loop is told to stop

notes: it ends when no timer remains, no request is pending and the patience is used up, or when Stop is called; a callback that stops a repeating timer copy does not stop the manager's own copy, so a loop with a repeating timer runs until Stop or StopAllTimers is called on the manager itself

classes.name: stzTimex
classes.brief: Matches a regex-like pattern language for time structures, such as @Event -> @Duration -> @Event, against timelines and lists of dates.
classes.description: A pattern is a sequence of steps joined by ->, each step an @Instant, @Duration, @Event, @Sequence or @Frame with an optional label, a duration constraint and a quantifier (+, *, ?, ~ or a count). The target is a stzTimeLine, a stzCalendar, a list of date texts, or stzDateTime and stzDuration objects: it is first flattened into instants, events and the duration gaps between them. Build one with StzTimexQ, Timex or Tmx. MatchExact needs the pattern to consume the whole target, MatchPartial finds it anywhere, and a success fills MatchedParts. The pattern parser is broken today: the calls to @StzMid pass an end position where it now wants a length, so SplitByOperator never splits, a pattern with several steps is read as one step, labels keep their closing bracket, and a pattern with a parenthesised duration such as @Duration(1h) raises R2 when built. Only single steps without brackets, such as @Instant or @Event, parse correctly. MatchAsYouBuild raises R14 whenever there is no partial match. The matching engine itself (BacktrackMatch) and the constraint check work on hand-built tokens.
classes.example:
? o1.Pattern()
#--> {@Instant}
? o1.MatchExact([ "2025-10-22 09:00:00" ])
#--> 1
? o1.ParseDurationToMinutes("1h30min")
#--> 90

methods.name: init
methods.brief: Builds a time-pattern matcher from a pattern text such as @Event(A) -> @Duration(30m) -> @Event(B), wrapping it in braces if needed.

parameters.name: _cPattern_
parameters.role: the pattern as text

notes: build with StzTimexQ, Timex or Tmx; the debug flag prints the parse
warnings: the parser is broken today, so a pattern holding the arrow -> or a vertical bar is read as ONE token whose label keeps the closing bracket (A) -> ... gives a single event token labelled A)), and a pattern with a parenthesised duration such as @Duration(1h) raises Array Access (Index out of range) (R2) at once; only single tokens without brackets, such as @Instant or @Event, parse correctly; cause: the calls to @StzMid pass an end position where @StzMid now wants a length

methods.name: NormalizePattern
methods.brief: Returns the pattern text trimmed and wrapped in braces when it is not yet.

parameters.name: _cPattern_
parameters.role: the pattern as text

notes: @Event(A) with spaces around gives {@Event(A)}, and {x} stays {x}

methods.name: ParsePattern
methods.brief: Splits a pattern into its tokens, one per arrow-separated step.

parameters.name: _cPattern_
parameters.role: the braced pattern as text

methods.returns: a list of tokens, each a list of [ name, value ] pairs
notes: a single token with no brackets parses correctly
warnings: it never splits: {@Instant -> @Duration(1h..2h) -> @Event(X)} gives one token instead of three, because SplitByOperator does not split

methods.name: SplitByOperator
methods.brief: Returns the whole text as one piece today instead of cutting it at an operator outside brackets.

parameters.name: cStr
parameters.role: the text to cut

parameters.name: cOperator
parameters.role: the operator, such as -> or the vertical bar ParsePattern, ParseAlternation

methods.returns: a list of text with one item
warnings: the brackets are tracked correctly, only the comparison fails
see: it never finds the operator: a -> b(c -> d) -> e
B and C joined by vertical bars each come back whole
because the operator is read with @StzMid(text
which wants a length as its third argument

methods.brief: Reads a bracketed step that offers alternatives, such as event A or event B, into one alternation token.

parameters.name: _cTokenStr_
parameters.role: the text of the alternation, its alternatives written between brackets and joined by vertical bars

methods.returns: a token: [ type alternation, the alternatives, negated 0 ]
notes: the token shape is right: the type is alternation
warnings: it finds one alternative only, since SplitByOperator does not split, and the label keeps the closing bracket (A))

methods.name: ParseSingleToken
methods.brief: Reads one step such as @Event(A)? or @Duration* into a token with its type, label, constraints and quantifier.

parameters.name: _cTokenStr_
parameters.role: the text of one step

methods.returns: a token as a list of [ name, value ] pairs; [ ] for a text that names no known type
notes: types are instant, duration, event, sequence and frame; + means 1 or more, * 0 or more, ? 0 or 1, ~ cyclic
warnings: works for @Instant+, @Duration* and @Frame~ with no brackets; with brackets the label keeps the closing bracket (@Event(X) gives X)); a negation such as @!Event(X) returns [ ]; the numeric quantifier 2-3 gives min 3 and max 3 instead of 2 and 3; @Event(Session:1h) raises Array Access (Index out of range) (R2)

methods.name: ParseConstraints
methods.brief: Reads the text inside a duration step into constraints: a range with an optional step, or one exact duration.

parameters.name: cConstraintStr
parameters.role: the text of the constraints, such as 1h..2h:15min

methods.returns: a list of constraints, each a list of [ name, value ] pairs; [ ] for an empty text
notes: 1h..2h:15min gives a range with start 1h, end 2h and step 15min; 1h gives an exact constraint of 60 minutes
warnings: a set such as {Mon;Wed;Fri} raises Array Access (Index out of range) (R2) instead of returning a set constraint, because it is first read as a duration

methods.name: ParseDurationToMinutes
methods.brief: Returns a duration written as hours and minutes as a number of minutes.

parameters.name: _cDuration_
parameters.role: the duration as text, such as 1h, 30min, 1h30min, 45 or 30m

notes: 1h gives 60, 1h30min gives 90, 45 gives 45 (a bare number is minutes), 2H gives 120

notes: a successful match fills MatchedParts; an empty list gives FALSE

parameters.role: the target, as for MatchPartial

classes.name: stzTotp
classes.brief: Makes and checks RFC 6238 time-based one-time passwords, the second factor of an authenticator app, with the hashing done in the engine.
classes.description: The shared secret is base32, the text a user types into an app; the class decodes it to hex for the engine call, so no raw key bytes cross the text boundary. The defaults, SHA1, 6 digits and a 30-second step, are what Google Authenticator, Authy, 1Password and FreeOTP expect. Verify tolerates a small clock drift, and compares in constant time. A code is not consumed by a check: the same code verifies again within its window, so the caller must remember the last step it accepted to refuse a reuse. The secret itself is shown by Show and Secret and carried in the provisioning address, so treat all three as sensitive. The examples use the public RFC 6238 test secret.
classes.example:
o1.SetDigits(8)
? o1.CodeAt(59)
#--> 94287082
o1.SetDigits(6)
? o1.CodeAt(59)
#--> 287082
? o1.VerifyAt("287082", 59)
#--> 1
? o1.VerifyAt("287082", 119)
#--> 0
? o1.ProvisioningUri("alice", "Softanza")
#--> otpauth://totp/Softanza:alice?secret=GEZDGNBVGY3TQOJQGEZDGNBVGY3TQOJQ&issuer=Softanza&algorithm=SHA1&digits=6&period=30

classes.name: stzTrainer
classes.brief: Trains a stzNeuralNetwork by stochastic gradient descent and keeps the loss of every epoch, so the descent can be watched.
classes.description: The network arrives with each Train call and is changed in place, because an attribute would hold a private copy and training would perfect a clone. The loop and the backpropagation run in the engine; the trained weights are written back through AdoptLayers. The trainer records the loss history, and Why sums the run up: the epochs, the rate, and the first and last loss. Learning is deterministic for a given seed and data.
classes.receiver: o1 = new stzTrainer() o2 = new stzNeuralNetwork([ :Inputs = 2 ])
classes.example:
o2.AddDenseLayer(4, :Tanh)
o2.AddDenseLayer(1, :Sigmoid)
o1.SetLearningRate(0.5)
o1.Train(o2, [ [0,0], [0,1], [1,0], [1,1] ], [ [0], [1], [1], [0] ], 2000)
? len(o1.LossHistory())
#--> 2000
? o1.LossHistory()[1] > o1.FinalLoss()
#--> 1
? o2.Predict([0, 1])[1] > 0.9
#--> 1

classes.name: stzTree
classes.brief: Holds a named tree of nodes and leaf items, and finds, reads and adds nodes and items by name or by path.
classes.description: It extends stzList. A tree is one named root holding nodes, a node being a name paired with a list that may hold items and further nodes: :root = [ :node1 = [ "X", :node11 = [ "A" ] ], :node2 = [ 1, 2 ] ]. A path names the nodes from the root, as in [:root][:node1], and an item path adds the item's position in its node, as in [:root][:node2][1]. Branches and Nodes list them in depth-first order, Find methods return paths, and NodeAt and ItemAt read what a path points to. Node names are matched without regard to case. Adding goes through AddNodeAt and AddItemAt at the end of a node; a path that does not exist changes nothing without any error. Removing goes through RemoveItem, RemoveTheseItems and RemoveAllItems: they take every occurrence of an item out of the whole tree, at any depth, and leave every node and the root in place (a node may end up empty); an item that is absent changes nothing without any error, and removing a node by its name is not written. FindTheseItems repeats the last path of an item that occurs several times, and FindThisItem answers an empty text.

notes: a node is a name paired with a list; what is not a node inside it is an item; the tree is held as a one-item list, so Content answers [ tree ]

methods.name: Nodes

classes.name: stzTruthChain
classes.brief: Tells a boolean narrative about a value, claim by claim, and folds it once into a certain yes or no with its reason.
classes.description: TruthOf(value) opens the chain; IsA, AndIsA and OrIsA add claims about its kind, and Containing and its And and Or forms add claims about what it holds. Holds folds the claims from left to right, so a and b or c reads as (a and b) or c, with no evaluated user text: each kind is a descriptor resolved to an @is predicate. Why() narrates the verdict. Start the chain with exactly one IsA, IsNotA or Containing.
classes.example:
o1.IsA(:Lowercase).AndIsA(:Latin).AndContaining("g")
? o1.Holds()
#--> 1
? o1.Why()
#--> yes: "ring" is lowercase and is latin and containing "g"
? TruthOf("Ring").IsA(:Lowercase).OrIsA(:Uppercase).Holds()
#--> 0

classes.name: stzTSNE
classes.brief: Draws a map of high-dimensional samples in 2 dimensions in which points that are near in the data stay near, using t-SNE.
classes.description: Built for LOOKING at data, not for measuring it: the map is nonlinear, random and one-way, distances and cluster sizes in it mean nothing, and the perplexity changes the picture, so try two values. The usual pipeline is ReduceWithPCA(30) then Fit. The run is seeded: the same SetSeed gives the same embedding, a different one a different layout. Fit refuses a perplexity that is not below the number of samples, so small data needs SetPerplexity first (the default is 30). Ordinary t-SNE can place new rows with Transform only approximately; LearnMapping switches to the parametric variant, whose Transform is exact for the training rows. PreserveDensity adds a term that makes cluster size more readable, and LearnInverse trains a network that goes back from the map to the data. Trustworthiness is the witness that the picture invented no neighbours.
classes.example:
o1.SetPerplexity(3)
o1.SetIterations(120)
o1.Fit()
? o1.IsFitted()
#--> 1
? len(o1.Embedding())
#--> 12
? o1.Trustworthiness() > 0.5
#--> 1

classes.description: The polish is R's medpolish, run in the engine: Data = Fit + Residual, with medians and not means, so one wild cell shows up as a large residual and does not bend the fit.
