methods.name: Check
methods.brief: Returns the largest gap between a cell and its fit plus residual over the table, which is 0 when Data equals Fit plus Residual.
notes: a check of the contract, not of the fit's quality
warnings: Raises an error until Polish has run

methods.name: ResidualScale
methods.brief: Returns the fourth-spread of all the residuals, the scale a coded display bands by.
warnings: Raises an error until Polish has run

methods.name: Diagnostics
methods.brief: Returns the verdicts on the fit in the house rule shape: far-out residuals are errors, a polish stopped at its cap a warning.

parameters.name: pcSubject
parameters.role: what the table is called in the rows

methods.returns: a list of rows [ :rule, :subject, :where, :severity, :message ]; empty when all is well
notes: the rules are far_out and not_converged; when every other residual is 0 any residual counts as far out
warnings: Raises an error until Polish has run

methods.name: Why
methods.brief: Returns one sentence on the fit: the common value, the sweeps, whether it converged, and how well Data equals Fit plus Residual.
methods.returns: a text; before Polish it says the table is not yet polished

classes.name: stzTukeyLine
classes.brief: Fits Tukey's resistant three-group line through paired values, so one wild point barely moves it.
classes.description: The line is R's line(): the points are split into three groups by x, the slope comes from the medians of the outer groups, and passes over the residuals refine it. Call Fit first; Slope, Intercept, Iterations and Residuals raise an error until then. Fit(n) matches R's iter = n + 1. Known defect: points that all share one x give slope 0 and intercept 0 without an error.
classes.example:
? o1.Slope()
#--> 2.00
? o1.Iterations()
#--> 0

methods.name: init
methods.brief: Builds a resistant line to be fitted through paired values, x against y.

parameters.name: paX
parameters.role: the x values, a list of numbers

parameters.name: paY
parameters.role: the y values, a list of numbers of the same length, at least three points

methods.name: Fit
methods.brief: Fits Tukey's three-group line, then improves it with passes over the residuals, as R's line does.

parameters.name: pnIterations
parameters.role: the number of passes over the residuals after the first fit

methods.returns: the line itself, so calls chain
notes: on x 1 to 12 with y near twice x it gives slope 2.0056 and intercept 0.0444 after 5 passes, and one wild y barely moves it
warnings: Fit(0) equals R's line with iter 1 and Fit(1) equals iter 2, so the count here is one less than R's; points that all share one x give slope 0 and intercept 0 with no error, which is a defect

extensions.name: FitQ
extensions.adds: does what the method does, then returns the object, so the call can be chained

methods.name: Slope
methods.brief: Returns the slope of the fitted line.
warnings: Raises an error until Fit has run

methods.name: Intercept
methods.brief: Returns the intercept of the fitted line, its y at x equal to 0.
warnings: Raises an error until Fit has run

methods.name: Iterations
methods.brief: Returns how many residual passes the last Fit made.
warnings: Raises an error until Fit has run

methods.name: Residuals
methods.brief: Returns each y minus the line's value at its x, in the order given.
warnings: Raises an error until Fit has run

methods.name: Why
methods.brief: Returns one sentence that gives the fitted equation and the number of passes.
methods.returns: a text; before Fit it says the line is not yet fitted

classes.name: stzTukeyOneWay
classes.brief: Fits groups of numbers by one-way median polish: a common value, an effect per group and a residual per value.
classes.description: The common value is the median of the group medians, each effect is a group's median minus it, and each residual is a value minus its group's median. Diagnostics does not need Polish: it warns when the spread of the groups grows with their level, with the power to try.

methods.name: init
methods.brief: Builds a one-way table of groups of numbers, to be fitted by median polish.

parameters.name: paGroups
parameters.role: at least two groups, each a non-empty list of numbers, of lengths that may differ

methods.name: NumberOfGroups
methods.brief: Returns how many groups the table has.

methods.name: Polish
methods.brief: Fits the groups by medians: a common value, an effect per group and a residual per value.
methods.returns: the fit itself, so calls chain
notes: for 1, 2, 3 / 4, 5, 9 / 10, 12, 20, 30 the common value is 5 and the effects are -3, 0 and 11
warnings: Common, Effects, Residuals and Check raise an error until Polish has run

methods.name: Common
methods.brief: Returns the median of the group medians.
notes: 5 for the groups above
warnings: Raises an error until Polish has run

methods.name: Effects
methods.brief: Returns each group's median minus the common value.
methods.returns: a list of numbers, one per group
notes: -3, 0, 11 for the groups above
warnings: Raises an error until Polish has run

methods.name: Residuals
methods.brief: Returns each value minus the median of its group.
methods.returns: a list of lists, one per group, in the order given
warnings: Raises an error until Polish has run

methods.name: Check
methods.brief: Returns the largest gap between a value and common plus effect plus residual, which is 0 when Data equals Fit plus Residual.
warnings: Raises an error until Polish has run

methods.name: Diagnostics
methods.brief: Returns a warning when the spread of the groups grows with their level, from the slope of log fourth-spread on log median.

parameters.name: pcSubject
parameters.role: what the groups are called in the rows

methods.returns: a list of rows [ :rule, :subject, :where, :severity, :message ]; empty when the slope is within 0.5
notes: spreads that double with the level, as 10 to 12, 20 to 24, 40 to 48 and 80 to 96, give slope 1 and the power 0, the log
warnings: it does not need Polish; the rule is spread_tracks_level and the message gives the suggested power

methods.name: Why
methods.brief: Returns one sentence on the fit: the common value, the effects, and how well Data equals Fit plus Residual.
methods.returns: a text; before Polish it says the table is not yet polished

classes.name: stzTukeyReexpression
classes.brief: Measures whether a two-way table needs a change of scale, and recommends the power that makes it additive.
classes.description: Each rung of the ladder -1, -0.5, 0, 0.5, 1, 2 is tried and the slope of the residuals on comparison values is measured; a recommendation fires only when the slope at power 1 passes the threshold 0.5. A table that is the product of a row factor and a column factor gives the log. Known defect: a table holding a zero cannot take the negative powers or the log, and Recommend can then fire with power 1, as is.
classes.example:
? o1.Recommend()[:name]
#--> log
? o1.Recommend()[:fires]
#--> 1

methods.name: init
methods.brief: Builds a two-way table whose need for a change of scale is to be measured.

parameters.name: paRows
parameters.role: the table as a list of rows, each a list of numbers

methods.name: Threshold
methods.brief: Returns the measured limit that the slope at power 1 must pass for a re-expression to be recommended.

methods.name: NonAdditivity
methods.brief: Returns the slope of the residuals on the comparison values of the table as it stands, and the power it suggests.
methods.returns: a hash list with the keys slope, intercept, power and ok
notes: a table of 1, 2, 4 / 2, 4, 8 / 4, 8, 16 / 8, 16, 32, a product of a row and a column factor, gives slope 1 and power 0

methods.name: Ladder
methods.brief: Returns every rung of the ladder of powers, from -1 to 2, with the slope and the residual scale found after raising the table to it.
methods.returns: a list of rows [ power, slope, residual scale, ok ]; ok is 0 for a rung that cannot be taken
notes: for the product table above the log rung, power 0, has slope 0 and residual scale 0
warnings: the engine is crossed once and the answer kept

methods.name: Rung
methods.brief: Returns one row of the ladder.
methods.returns: a list [ power, slope, residual scale, ok ]

methods.name: Recommend
methods.brief: Returns the verdict on the table: the power with the flattest slope when the slope at power 1 passes the threshold, else leave it as it is.
methods.returns: a hash list with the keys power, name, slope, fires and evidence
notes: the product table gives power 0, log, fires 1; an additive table 1, 2, 3 / 2, 3, 4 / 3, 4, 5 / 4, 5, 6 gives power 1, fires 0
warnings: when the table holds a zero the negative powers and the log cannot be taken, and the verdict can come out as fires 1 with power 1, as is, which says to re-express and to leave it at once; seen on two tables

methods.name: LadderTable
methods.brief: Returns the ladder as a text table with one line per rung, a star on the recommended one and the evidence beneath.

methods.name: Diagnostics
methods.brief: Returns a warning when the table is not additive enough, with the evidence and the power to try.

parameters.name: pcSubject
parameters.role: what the table is called in the rows

methods.returns: a list of rows [ :rule, :subject, :where, :severity, :message ]; empty when the table is left as it is
notes: the rule is non_additive

methods.name: Why
methods.brief: Returns one sentence on the table's size and the evidence for or against a re-expression.

classes.name: stzTukeySmoother
classes.brief: Smooths a series resistantly with Tukey's medians-of-three family, Hanning and 4253H, and spots a level shift.
classes.description: The kinds 3, 3R, S, 3RSS, 3RS3R and 3RSR are R's smooth, run in the engine; on 4, 1, 3, 6, 6, 4, 1, 6, 2, 4, 2 all six equal R 4.5.1's output. Hanning and 4253H copy their ends, and 4253H equals a hand computation. Rough returns data minus smooth, and Twice adds the smooth of the rough back. ChangePoint is a verdict with a measured threshold, made from 40 values. A series of fewer than 4 numbers is refused.

methods.name: init
methods.brief: Builds a smoother over a series of numbers, kept in the order given, with Tukey's end rule.

parameters.name: paNumbers
parameters.role: the series, a list of at least four numbers

methods.name: Numbers
methods.brief: Returns the series as it was given.

methods.name: Count
methods.brief: Returns how many values the series holds.

methods.name: SetEndRule
methods.brief: Chooses how the two end values of a smooth are treated: Tukey's end-point rule, or copied from the data.

parameters.name: pcRule
parameters.role: Tukey or Copy, in any case

methods.returns: the smoother itself, so calls chain
notes: on 4, 1, 3, 6, 6, 4, 1, 6, 2, 4, 2 the first value of Smooth3 is 3 under Tukey and 4 under Copy

extensions.name: SetEndRuleQ
extensions.adds: does what the method does, then returns the object, so the call can be chained

methods.name: EndRule
methods.brief: Returns the end rule in force.

methods.name: SetSplitEnds
methods.brief: Switches on or off the splitting of two-flats at the ends too, as R's do.ends.

parameters.name: pbOn
parameters.role: 1 to split at the ends as well, 0 for not, the default

methods.returns: the smoother itself, so calls chain
notes: it changed nothing on the series 4, 1, 3, 6, 6, 4, 1, 6, 2, 4, 2

methods.name: Smooth
methods.brief: Returns the smooth of a given kind, as R's smooth does with the end rule and the split-ends setting in force.

parameters.name: pcKind
parameters.role: 3, 3R, S, 3RSS, 3RS3R or 3RSR, in any case

methods.returns: a list of numbers of the same length as the series
notes: on 4, 1, 3, 6, 6, 4, 1, 6, 2, 4, 2 kind 3R gives 3, 3, 3, 6, 6, 4, 4, 4, 2, 2, 2 and all six kinds equal R 4.5.1's

methods.name: Smooth3
methods.brief: Returns the running median of three, taken once over the series.

methods.name: Smooth3R
methods.brief: Returns the running median of three repeated until nothing changes.

methods.name: Split
methods.brief: Returns the series with its flat pairs of equal values split, Tukey's S smoother.
notes: it leaves 4, 1, 3, 6, 6, 4, 1, 6, 2, 4, 2 unchanged, as R does

methods.name: Smooth3RSS
methods.brief: Returns 3R followed by two splitting passes.

methods.name: Smooth3RS3R
methods.brief: Returns 3R, a splitting pass, then 3R again, R's default smoother.

methods.name: Smooth3RSR
methods.brief: Returns 3R then splitting passes repeated until nothing changes.

methods.name: Twice
methods.brief: Returns the smooth of a kind with the smooth of its rough added back, as R's twiceit.

parameters.name: pcKind
parameters.role: 3, 3R, S, 3RSS, 3RS3R or 3RSR, in any case

methods.name: Rough
methods.brief: Returns each value minus its smooth, the part the smooth leaves out, so that Data equals Smooth plus Rough.

parameters.name: pcKind
parameters.role: 3, 3R, S, 3RSS, 3RS3R or 3RSR, in any case

methods.name: Hanning
methods.brief: Returns the series smoothed by the weights 1/4, 1/2 and 1/4, with the two end values copied.
notes: the second value of 4, 1, 3, 6, 6, 4, 1, 6, 2, 4, 2 becomes 2.25

methods.name: Smooth4253H
methods.brief: Returns the 4253H smooth: medians of 4 and 2, then 5, then 3, then Hanning, with the ends copied at every stage.
warnings: needs at least seven values and raises an error with fewer

methods.name: Smooth4253HTwice
methods.brief: Returns the 4253H smooth with the smooth of its rough added back.
warnings: needs at least seven values and raises an error with fewer

methods.name: WindowMedians
methods.brief: Returns the median of every run of consecutive values of a given length, with no end values.

parameters.name: pnK
parameters.role: the span, from 1 up to the count

methods.returns: a list of numbers, count minus span plus one of them

methods.name: ChangePoint
methods.brief: Looks for a level shift: the largest contrast between medians of ten values either side of a cut, over the spread of the steps.
methods.returns: a hash list with the keys contrast, at, scale, threshold, fires, judged and because
notes: a step of 6 in the middle of 60 values gives contrast 3 at index 30, past the threshold 1.8
warnings: a verdict is made from 40 values; under that judged is 0 and because says so; a series with no spread in its differences is not judged either

methods.name: Diagnostics
methods.brief: Returns a warning when a level shift is found, naming where and by how much.

parameters.name: pcSubject
parameters.role: what the series is called in the rows

methods.returns: a list of rows [ :rule, :subject, :where, :severity, :message ]; empty when none is found or the series is too short to judge
notes: the rule is level_shift

methods.name: Why
methods.brief: Returns one sentence on the series: the largest rough under 3RS3R, the kinds available and the change-point verdict.

classes.name: stzTukeyStory
classes.brief: Tells in plain sentences what a median-polish fit and its rule report found, without computing a single number of its own.
classes.description: Every number in the prose is read from the fit (the common value, the effects, the residual scale, the sweeps) or from a finding's message. IsHonest proves it on the story itself: each number in the text must be one the sources carry. The story has a paragraph on the fit, one on the effects, one on the findings when there are some, and a verdict. There is no language-model face on purpose, since templated prose reads well enough. Build it with StzTukeyStoryQ(oFit, oReport) after oFit.Polish().
classes.receiver: oFit = StzTukeyFitQ([ [ 11, 12, 13 ], [ 21, 22, 23 ], [ 31, 32, 33 ] ]) oFit.Polish() o1 = StzTukeyStoryQ(oFit, StzTukeyReportQ("exact", [ oFit ]))
classes.example:
? len(o1.Paragraphs())
#--> 3
? o1.IsHonest()
#--> 1

methods.name: init
methods.brief: Builds the story of a polished median-polish fit and the rule report about it; nothing is computed.

parameters.name: poFit
parameters.role: the stzTukeyFit, already polished

parameters.name: poReport
parameters.role: the stzRuleReport built from it, as StzTukeyReportQ returns

warnings: raises when the first argument is not a stzTukeyFit, when the fit has not been polished, and when the second is not a stzRuleReport

methods.name: Fit
methods.brief: Returns the fit the story is told about.

methods.name: Report
methods.brief: Returns the rule report whose findings the story repeats.

methods.name: Paragraphs
methods.brief: Returns the story as a list of paragraphs: the fit, the effects, the findings when there are any, and the verdict.
methods.returns: a list of text, three or four items

methods.name: Text
methods.brief: Returns the whole story as one text, one paragraph per line.

methods.name: Transcript
methods.brief: Returns the story told on a stzTranscript: each paragraph a system line and the verdict a verdict line of certainty 1.

methods.name: SourceNumerals
methods.brief: Returns every number that the fit and the report carry, written the way the prose writes them.

methods.name: Numerals
methods.brief: Returns the numbers that appear in the prose, in order, as text without signs.

methods.name: Unsourced
methods.brief: Returns the numbers of the prose that no source carries, an empty list when the story is honest.
methods.returns: a list of text; [ ] when every number is sourced

methods.name: IsHonest
methods.brief: TRUE if every number in the story is one that the fit or a finding carries, which proves the story did no arithmetic of its own.

methods.name: Why
methods.brief: Returns one sentence that counts the paragraphs and numbers and says whether each number was read from a source.
methods.returns: a text such as a Tukey story of 4 paragraph(s) and 27 numeral(s), every one read from the fit or a finding

classes.name: stzTukeySummary
classes.brief: Summarises a batch of numbers resistantly: median, hinges, fences, letter values and spread, with no mean and no p-value.
classes.description: The summary is built on medians, so one wild value does not move it. Tukey's fourths are the default hinges and percentile quartiles are available with SetConvention; Why says which is in force. Fences at 1.5 and 3 fourth-spreads give the outside and far-out values, LetterValues gives the ladder from the median outward, and Skewness, TailWeight and Shape read the form of the batch against thresholds measured on seeded batches (a shape verdict is made from 100 values). Diagnostics returns the verdicts in the house rule shape. There is no inference here. Known defect: Skewness, TailWeight, Shape and Diagnostics raise error R2 for a batch of fewer than 5 values. Checked by hand on 2, 4, 4, 5, 7, 9, 12, 25: median 6, fourths 4 and 10.5, quartiles 4 and 9.75, trimean 6.625, MAD 2.5.

methods.name: init
methods.brief: Builds a resistant summary of a batch of numbers, kept in the order given.

parameters.name: paNumbers
parameters.role: the batch, a non-empty list of numbers

methods.name: Numbers
methods.brief: Returns the batch as it was given, in the same order.

methods.name: Count
methods.brief: Returns how many values the batch holds.

methods.name: SetConvention
methods.brief: Chooses which pair of hinges the summary uses: Tukey's fourths, or percentile quartiles.

parameters.name: pcConvention
parameters.role: Fourths, Tukey or Hinges for Tukey's fourths, the default

methods.returns: the summary itself, so calls chain
notes: on 2, 4, 4, 5, 7, 9, 12, 25 the upper hinge is 10.5 under fourths and 9.75 under percentile
warnings: it changes Hinges, FourthSpread, Fences, Outside and FarOut; Fourths and Quartiles always answer their own pair

extensions.name: SetConventionQ
extensions.adds: does what the method does, then returns the object, so the call can be chained

methods.name: Convention
methods.brief: Returns the convention in force for the hinges.

methods.name: Median
methods.brief: Returns the middle value of the batch, or the mean of the two middle values for an even count.

methods.name: Fourths
methods.brief: Returns Tukey's two hinges, the medians of the lower and the upper half including the middle value.
notes: always Tukey's pair whatever the convention in force; [ 4, 10.5 ] for 2, 4, 4, 5, 7, 9, 12, 25

methods.name: Quartiles
methods.brief: Returns the percentile quartiles, read at rank p/100 times n minus 1 with linear interpolation.
notes: always the percentile pair; [ 4, 9.75 ] for 2, 4, 4, 5, 7, 9, 12, 25

methods.name: Hinges
methods.brief: Returns the pair of hinges the convention in force names.
methods.returns: a list [ lower, upper ]: the fourths by default, the quartiles under Percentile

methods.name: FourthSpread
methods.brief: Returns the distance between the two hinges, the spread that the fences are measured in.
notes: 6.5 for 2, 4, 4, 5, 7, 9, 12, 25 under fourths

methods.name: Fences
methods.brief: Returns the lower and upper limits at a multiple of the fourth-spread beyond the hinges, under the convention in force.

parameters.name: pnMult
parameters.role: a positive multiplier of the fourth-spread

methods.name: OutsideFences
methods.brief: Returns the fences at 1.5 fourth-spreads beyond the hinges.

methods.name: FarOutFences
methods.brief: Returns the fences at 3 fourth-spreads beyond the hinges.

methods.name: Outside
methods.brief: Returns the values beyond the outside fences, in the order given.
methods.returns: a list of numbers; empty when none is outside

methods.name: FarOut
methods.brief: Returns the values beyond the far-out fences, in the order given.
methods.returns: a list of numbers; empty when none is far out
notes: none for 2, 4, 4, 5, 7, 9, 12, 25, and 100 when the last value is 100

methods.name: LetterValues
methods.brief: Returns the ladder of letter values from the median outward: depth, lower, upper, mid and spread at each level.

parameters.name: pnLevels
parameters.role: how many levels, from 1 for the median alone

methods.returns: a list of rows [ letter, depth, lower, upper, mid, spread ] with letters M, F, E, D, C and on
notes: for 2, 4, 4, 5, 7, 9, 12, 25: M is 6 at depth 4.5, F is 4 and 10.5, E is 3 and 18.5
warnings: the ladder stops when the depth reaches 1, so a batch of 8 gives 4 rows even when 10 are asked

methods.name: Trimean
methods.brief: Returns Tukey's trimean, the mean of the lower hinge, twice the median and the upper hinge.

methods.name: LetterValueTable
methods.brief: Returns the letter values laid out as a text table with one line per level and a note on how depths are found.

parameters.name: pnLevels
parameters.role: how many levels, from 1

methods.name: Mad
methods.brief: Returns the median absolute deviation from the median, not scaled to estimate a standard deviation.

methods.name: Biweight
methods.brief: Returns the biweight midvariance, a resistant variance that gives distant values little or no weight.

parameters.name: pnC
parameters.role: the tuning constant in units of the MAD

methods.returns: a number in squared units, a variance and not a standard deviation
notes: 16.52 with 9 and 13.5 with 6 for 2, 4, 4, 5, 7, 9, 12, 25; its square root is a spread

methods.name: Skewness
methods.brief: Returns how far the mid-summaries drift from the median, in fourth-spreads; positive leans right.
methods.returns: a number; 0 when the fourth-spread is 0
notes: 0.69 for 2, 4, 4, 5, 7, 9, 12, 25; a shape verdict is made from 100 values
warnings: Raises error R2 (index out of range) for a batch of fewer than 5 values, because it needs four letter values

methods.name: TailWeight
methods.brief: Returns the sixteenth-spread over the fourth-spread, divided by the Gaussian ratio 2.2745; 1 is Gaussian.
methods.returns: a number; 1 when the fourth-spread is 0
notes: above 1.2 counts as heavy tails once there are 100 values
warnings: Raises error R2 (index out of range) for a batch of fewer than 5 values, as Skewness does

methods.name: Shape
methods.brief: Returns the shape in numbers and in words: count, skewness, tail weight, which way it leans and whether its tails are heavy.
methods.returns: a hash list with the keys count, skewness, tailweight, leans, tails and because
notes: under 100 values leans and tails are unjudged, and because says so; from 100, leans is right, left or neither and tails is heavy or not heavy
warnings: Raises error R2 (index out of range) for a batch of fewer than 5 values

methods.name: Diagnostics
methods.brief: Returns the verdicts on the batch in the house rule shape: each far-out value is an error, a lean or heavy tails a warning.

parameters.name: pcSubject
parameters.role: what the batch is called in the rows

methods.returns: a list of rows [ :rule, :subject, :where, :severity, :message ]; empty when all is well
notes: the rules are far_out, skewed and heavy_tailed, and each message names the measurement and its threshold
warnings: Raises error R2 (index out of range) for a batch of fewer than 5 values, through Shape

methods.name: Why
methods.brief: Returns one sentence naming the convention in force, with the hinges, median, fourth-spread and the counts outside and far out.

classes.name: stzTutor
classes.brief: Asks a learner the question that points at the gap in their attempt, and never writes the answer, without any language model.
classes.description: The tutor keeps three rules: it never writes the learner's code before the exercise is passed, never explains ahead of where the learner is, and never answers before the learner has tried. It keeps them by construction: every reply is built from templates that carry no code, and a last filter blanks any word a right answer calls (ForbiddenWords). What it does: it asks one open question, naming the first step of the exercise that the submitted program does not show, in English, French, Arabic or Hausa; with a course laid on, it names a chapter that is ahead of the learner and does not explain it, and recalls a chapter behind with that chapter's own recap. What it does not do: it does not run or understand the program (it matches words the exercise lists for each step), it does not confirm a solution (only the checker's run does), it answers no question about a method, and it uses no language model and no network. The fr, ar and ha wording is a draft: no native speaker has reviewed it (0 of 35 units reviewed in each language). The programs it reads were run on the desktop only, and no institution has adopted the system yet.
classes.example:
? o1.Ask("Give me the answer")
#--> I will not write the answer for you: that is the one thing a tutor must never do. Try first. Write your attempt and submit it; then I will tell you what is still missing, as a question.
o1.WithCourse(oC)
? o1.Ask("How do I use KnowRelation?")
#--> That belongs to chapter 12, 'Teach a world'. You are on chapter 1, and the later chapter stands on what this one teaches, so I will not explain it yet. Which step of your current exercise is still open?
? o1.FilteredCount()
#--> 0

methods.name: init
methods.brief: Builds a tutor for one exercise and one learner's folder, to answer in one language, without any language model.

parameters.name: poExercise
parameters.role: the stzExercise the learner is working on, whose forbidden words the tutor blanks from its replies

parameters.name: pcLearnerFolder
parameters.role: the learner's folder, where the tutor reads the submission and the progress

parameters.name: pcLang
parameters.role: the language of the replies: en, fr, ar or ha

notes: the fr, ar and ha wording is a draft: no native speaker has reviewed it (0 of 35 units reviewed in each language)
warnings: a language other than those four is not refused here: the first reply that needs a text raises the error No text for that key in that language (law 7: a missing translation is red, never English)

methods.name: Language
methods.brief: Returns the language code the tutor answers in.

methods.name: FilteredCount
methods.brief: Returns how many forbidden words the final filter has blanked from replies so far; 0 means the templates alone sufficed.
notes: the tutor's guard asserts 0, to prove the filter never had to act

methods.name: LastGap
methods.brief: Returns the step the last question found missing from the learner's program, or an empty text when it found none.
methods.returns: the name of the exercise's first missing step, such as finds; an empty text when none, or when the question was not answered by looking at the program
notes: it is reset by every Ask

methods.name: ForbiddenWords
methods.brief: Returns the words a right answer calls, which no reply of the tutor may carry.
methods.returns: a list of text taken from the exercise
notes: for the first exercise of the elementary course it holds the class and method names of the right answer and the promised output

methods.name: WithCourse
methods.brief: Lays the course on the tutor, so that it knows where the learner is and what each chapter teaches.

parameters.name: poCourse
parameters.role: the stzCourse the learner follows

warnings: without a course ChapterOn raises error R13 Object is required, and Ask cannot apply rule 2 (never explain ahead of the learner)

extensions.name: WithCourseQ
extensions.adds: does what the method does, then returns the object, so the call can be chained

methods.name: HasCourse
methods.brief: TRUE if a course has been laid on the tutor, which rule 2 needs.

methods.name: LastAbout
methods.brief: Returns the chapter the last question was read as being about, or an empty text when it named none.
notes: it is reset by every Ask

methods.name: ChapterOn
methods.brief: Returns the chapter the learner is on, read from their progress: the first with an exercise not yet passed.
methods.returns: a chapter id, a text; an empty text once every chapter is passed
warnings: raises error R13 Object is required when no course was laid on

methods.name: ChapterAskedAbout
methods.brief: Returns the chapter a question is about, read from the names its cells call, or else from the title words in the tutor's language.

parameters.name: pcQuestion
parameters.role: the learner's question, as typed

methods.returns: a chapter id, a text; an empty text when no course is laid on or nothing matches
notes: a word the question shares with the names a chapter first calls decides first; failing that, two title words that belong to one chapter alone (or the only one when its title has one) decide, so common words like the or that claim nothing

methods.name: Ask
methods.brief: Answers a learner's question with a template question, never code: it names the missing step or a chapter, or says to try first.

parameters.name: pcQuestion
parameters.role: what the learner typed

methods.returns: a text, one reply in the tutor's language
notes: the order of the tutor: first a head, if the question asks for the answer (a refusal) or for confirmation (only the checker confirms); then, with a course, a chapter ahead of the learner is named and not explained, and one behind is recalled with that chapter's own recap, while only the current chapter goes on; then a passed exercise gets the passed sentence; no submission gets try first; an error verdict gets read the first error line; else the gap in the submitted program, or look at what your program printed
warnings: after the exercise is passed every question, whatever it says, gets one sentence inviting the learner to ask about any method, but Ask answers no question about a method (shown with three different questions); a request for the answer or for confirmation is recognized by fixed lists of words in en, fr, ar and ha, so a rephrased one is answered like any other question

methods.name: GapIn
methods.brief: Returns the first step of the exercise that a program text does not show, or an empty text when every step shows.

parameters.name: pcCode
parameters.role: the learner's program, as text

methods.returns: the name of a step of the exercise, such as finds or applies; an empty text when all are shown
notes: a step counts as shown when one of the exercise's words for it occurs in the text, whatever the case, comments included (a program holding only the comment FindDuplicates shows the finds step); the program is not run or understood here, only matched, and the gap is named by the wise-coding conversation of a knowledge space (the attempt asks, finds, applies)

classes.name: stzUiBindings
classes.brief: Binds {name} placeholders in a document's texts to values, so setting a value changes the screen without rebuilding it.
classes.description: A placeholder is an ordinary string with braces in it, so the document format is unchanged. Set gives a name a value and re-renders only the elements that mention it; SetMany does several at once and updates each affected element once; Apply pushes everything. The document survives an update, so there is no re-parse, no new font registration and no rebuilt accessibility tree, and focus and hover stay where they were. Text changes still re-shape the whole document, style changes through SetStyle are surgical. The class substitutes text and sets style properties and computes no meanings. Layout needs the engine and a font, no window.
classes.receiver: oDoc = new stzUiDocument('DEFINE PANEL console ( SIZE [400, 200], DIRECTION column, PADDING 10, CHILDREN [title, readout] ) RATIONALE "A console."' + char(10) + 'DEFINE TEXT title ( CONTENT "NAV - {mode}", SIZE 20 ) RATIONALE "The mode."' + char(10) + 'DEFINE TEXT readout ( CONTENT "BEARING {bearing} RANGE {range} km", SIZE 16 ) RATIONALE "The numbers."') oDoc.UseFont("C:/Windows/Fonts/segoeui.ttf") oPanel = oDoc.ToPanel() o1 = new stzUiBindings(oDoc, oPanel)
classes.example:
? @@( o1.Names() )
#--> [ "mode", "bearing", "range" ]
o1.Set(:bearing, "042.9")
? o1.RenderOf("readout")
#--> BEARING 042.9 RANGE  km
? @@( o1.Unset() )
#--> [ "mode", "range" ]
o1.SetMany([ :mode = "TRACK", :range = "8.20" ])
? o1.RenderOf("title")
#--> NAV - TRACK
? o1.ValueOf("range")
#--> 8.20
? o1.TimesApplied()
#--> 3

methods.name: init
methods.brief: Reads every {name} placeholder out of the text declarations of a document, ready to be given values.

parameters.name: poDoc
parameters.role: the stzUiDocument whose CONTENT strings hold placeholders

parameters.name: poPanel
parameters.role: the stzPanel made from it

methods.returns: nothing; the placeholders are harvested when the object is built
notes: a placeholder is a name of lower-case letters, digits and underscores in braces; a lone brace, an empty pair of braces and braces round anything else, such as {Bad Name}, stay as written
warnings: an argument that is not a document and a panel raises error stzUiBindings: give an stzUiDocument and its stzPanel

methods.name: Names
methods.brief: Returns every placeholder name the document mentions, in the order first met.
methods.returns: a list of text; [ ] when the document has none
notes: a screen can say what it needs before anything is set; a name used in two texts is listed once

methods.name: BoundElements
methods.brief: Returns the text elements that carry at least one placeholder.
methods.returns: a list of element names in declaration order

methods.name: IsBound
methods.brief: TRUE if the document mentions a placeholder with a name.

parameters.name: pcName
parameters.role: the placeholder name, without braces

notes: a name that is not a plain lower-case name, such as Bad Name, is never bound

methods.name: Unset
methods.brief: Returns the placeholders that have not been given a value yet.
methods.returns: a list of text in the order of Names
notes: an unset placeholder renders as empty text, a blank field rather than a screen that refuses to appear

methods.name: ValueOf
methods.brief: Returns the value last given to a placeholder.

parameters.name: pcName
parameters.role: the placeholder name, without braces

methods.returns: the value as text; an empty text for a name never set

methods.name: Set
methods.brief: Gives a placeholder a value and re-renders every element whose text mentions it.

parameters.name: pcName
parameters.role: the placeholder name, without braces

parameters.name: pValue
parameters.role: the value, turned into text

methods.returns: TRUE when every affected element was updated; TRUE also for a name no element mentions, which changes nothing. SetQ returns the bindings for chaining
notes: the value is kept as text, so 7 reads back as 7; SetMany takes a list [ :name = value, ... ] and updates each affected element once, so a line built from three values is set once and not three times

extensions.name: SetQ
extensions.adds: does what the method does, then returns the object, so the call can be chained

extensions.name: SetMany
extensions.adds: works on a collection of items instead of one

extensions.name: SetManyQ
extensions.adds: works on a collection of items instead of one; does what the method does, then returns the object, so the call can be chained

methods.name: Apply
methods.brief: Pushes every bound element to the panel again, whatever changed.
methods.returns: TRUE when every element was updated
notes: what to call after loading a screen, to fill it in one go; ApplyQ returns the bindings for chaining

extensions.name: ApplyQ
extensions.adds: does what the method does, then returns the object, so the call can be chained

methods.name: TimesApplied
methods.brief: Returns how many element updates have been pushed to the panel.
methods.returns: a number, starting at 0; each text element updated and each style change adds one
notes: an honest counter: a binding that matched nothing leaves it unchanged, as Set of a name no element mentions does

methods.name: RenderOf
methods.brief: Returns what a bound element's text would be right now, without touching the panel.

parameters.name: pcElement
parameters.role: the name of the text element

methods.returns: the text with the current values put in; an empty text for an element that is not bound
notes: a placeholder with no value reads as empty text, and braces that are not placeholders are left as written

methods.name: SetStyle
methods.brief: Sets one style property of an element in the panel, directly.

parameters.name: pcElement
parameters.role: the name of the element

parameters.name: pcProperty
parameters.role: the style property, such as color

parameters.name: pcValue
parameters.role: the value, such as #ff0000

methods.returns: TRUE when the panel took it, FALSE for an element it does not know. SetStyleQ returns the bindings for chaining
notes: a style change is surgical: unlike a text change it does not re-shape the whole document; each success adds one to TimesApplied

extensions.name: SetStyleQ
extensions.adds: does what the method does, then returns the object, so the call can be chained

methods.name: ClearStyle
methods.brief: Hands a style property of an element back to the stylesheet.

parameters.name: pcElement
parameters.role: the name of the element

parameters.name: pcProperty
parameters.role: the style property to give back

methods.returns: TRUE when the panel took it, FALSE for an element it does not know
notes: it sets the property to an empty text

classes.name: stzUiDocument
classes.brief: Parses a .panel file, the interface as text, judges it with a court of four birth-checks, and projects it to RML, HTML or a laid-out panel.
classes.description: A .panel file declares the projection only, boxes, sizes and colours, never a meaning. It has four kinds, PANEL (exactly one), BOX, TEXT and STYLE, written DEFINE <KIND> <name> ( fields ) RATIONALE "...", with every box named. The court checks closure (known fields and roles), reference resolution (every name a CHILDREN list gives is declared and placed), duplicate declaration and the round trip. IsClean is its verdict, Report and Diagnostics its findings; ToRml, ToHtml and ToPanel refuse a document that is not clean. ToPanel builds a laid-out stzPanel and opens no window. A CHILDREN cycle ends the process in the constructor today; see the warning on init.
classes.receiver: o1 = new stzUiDocument('DEFINE PANEL p ( SIZE [100, 80], CHILDREN [x] ) RATIONALE "boxes only"' + char(10) + 'DEFINE BOX x ( WIDTH 40, HEIGHT 30, SATISFIES [open_it] ) RATIONALE "a box"')
classes.example:
? o1.IsClean()
#--> 1
? @@( o1.Names() )
#--> [ "p", "x" ]
oP = o1.ToPanel()
? @@( oP.BoxOf("x") )
#--> [ 0, 0, 40, 30 ]
? @@( o1.SatisfiedIntents() )
#--> [ "open_it" ]
? @@( o1.Orphans() )
#--> [ "p" ]
o2 = new stzUiDocument(o1.ToText())
? o2.ToText() = o1.ToText()
#--> 1

methods.name: init
methods.brief: Parses a .panel interface document, from its text or from a file path, and judges it.

parameters.name: pcTextOrPath
parameters.role: the document itself, or the path of a file that holds it

methods.returns: nothing; the object is built, and its verdict is read with IsClean and Report
notes: the court checks that there is exactly one PANEL, that every name a CHILDREN list gives is declared, that no name is declared twice, that every field and every role is known, and that every element is placed by some CHILDREN list
warnings: a path that does not exist is parsed as text: the report then says Character ':' has no place in .panel; a document whose CHILDREN lists contain a cycle (a box that lists itself, or two boxes that list each other) ends the Ring process with Stack Overflow in the constructor, before the CHILD_CYCLE finding can be read, and the same for a panel that lists itself

methods.name: Diagnostics
methods.brief: Returns every finding of the court, errors and warnings, in the order found.
methods.returns: a list of hashlists with the keys code, severity (error or warning), message, line, cites and language
warnings: a colour written as a hex value is a LITERAL_COLOUR warning, accepted for now; it does not make the document unclean

methods.name: Errors
methods.brief: Returns only the findings of severity error.
methods.returns: a list of hashlists, as Diagnostics gives; empty for a clean document

methods.name: IsClean
methods.brief: TRUE if the document has no finding of severity error; warnings do not count.
warnings: ToRml, ToHtml and ToPanel refuse a document that is not clean

methods.name: Report
methods.brief: Returns the findings as text, one line each: severity, code, line number and message.
methods.returns: a text; empty when there is no finding

methods.name: Declarations
methods.brief: Returns every declaration of the document, in file order.
methods.returns: a list of hashlists with the keys kind (PANEL, BOX, TEXT or STYLE), name, fields, rationale and line

methods.name: DeclOf
methods.brief: Returns the declaration with a name.

parameters.name: pcName
parameters.role: the declared name

methods.returns: a hashlist with the keys kind, name, fields, rationale and line; an empty list when the name is not declared

methods.name: PanelDecl
methods.brief: Returns the declaration of the one PANEL, the root of the interface.
methods.returns: a hashlist as DeclOf gives; an empty list when there is no panel

methods.name: Names
methods.brief: Returns the names of all declarations, in file order.

methods.name: TextsToPaint
methods.brief: Returns, for every TEXT, what a caller needs to paint it: id, content, size, colour and whether it is right to left.
methods.returns: a list of [ id, content, size, colour, isRtl ] rows, with the defaults size 14 and colour #e8e8e8
warnings: isRtl is TRUE only for a text that declares TEXT_DIRECTION rtl itself: a text that inherits rtl from its box or panel is reported as 0 while IsRtl answers TRUE for it, on two different documents

methods.name: ToText
methods.brief: Returns the canonical text of the document, which reads back to the same document.
methods.returns: a text: a header line taken from the panel's rationale, then every declaration with one field per line
warnings: the print of a document read from it is the same text, so printing is a fixpoint; it prints even a document that is not clean

methods.name: ToRml
methods.brief: Returns the document as RmlUi markup, a style block and a body, with the divergences between engines already absorbed.
warnings: it raises an error, refusing to project a broken contract, when the document is not clean; a width or height you declare is a floor, written with flex-shrink 0

methods.name: ToHtml
methods.brief: Returns the same document as a complete HTML page, the web projection of what ToRml gives RmlUi.
warnings: it raises an error when the document is not clean

methods.name: ToFixture
methods.brief: Returns the document as an HTML page whose script compares the browser's boxes with the native ones and shows the verdict.

parameters.name: paNativeBoxes
parameters.role: the laid-out boxes of the native panel, as a list of [ name, x, y, w, h ] rows, such as those BoxOf answers

warnings: only boxes with a declared size are compared strictly: the page marks each as strict in width, in height and in position

methods.name: IsStrictWidth
methods.brief: TRUE if the element's width is declared, by itself or by its STYLE, rather than measured from its text.

parameters.name: pcName
parameters.role: the declared name

methods.returns: TRUE or FALSE; FALSE for a name that is not declared

methods.name: IsStrictHeight
methods.brief: TRUE if the element's height is declared, by itself or by its STYLE, rather than measured from its text.

parameters.name: pcName
parameters.role: the declared name

methods.returns: TRUE or FALSE; FALSE for a name that is not declared

methods.name: IsStrictlyPlaced
methods.brief: TRUE if the element's position is certain: its size is declared and so is the size of every earlier sibling.

parameters.name: pcName
parameters.role: the declared name

methods.returns: TRUE or FALSE; FALSE for a name that is not declared

methods.name: DirectionOf
methods.brief: Returns the text direction in force for an element: its own TEXT_DIRECTION, or the nearest ancestor's.

parameters.name: pcName
parameters.role: the declared name

methods.returns: the text rtl or ltr; ltr for a name the panel does not reach
warnings: the map is built when the document is made, so it answers at once, before anything is rendered

methods.name: IsRtl
methods.brief: TRUE if the element reads right to left.

parameters.name: pcName
parameters.role: the declared name

methods.name: UseFont
methods.brief: Records the font file that ToPanel loads for the document's FONT family.

parameters.name: pcPathOrBytes
parameters.role: the path of a font file, kept as given

notes: UseFontQ is the same call and returns the document
warnings: it must be called before ToPanel, which refuses a document that has a TEXT without it, even when no FONT is declared and the family is the default app

extensions.name: UseFontQ
extensions.adds: does what the method does, then returns the object, so the call can be chained

methods.name: FontFamily
methods.brief: Returns the font family the panel declares.
methods.returns: a text; app when the panel declares none or the document has no panel

methods.name: ToPanel
methods.brief: Builds the laid-out stzPanel of the document, ready to be asked for the box of any element.
methods.returns: a stzPanel sized by the panel's SIZE, 800 by 600 when it gives none
warnings: it opens no window; it raises an error when the document is not clean, and when it has a TEXT but no UseFont was called, even with no FONT field, because the text would silently vanish; a panel of boxes only needs no font

methods.name: Roles
methods.brief: Returns the closed vocabulary of roles a ROLE field may name, the accessibility terms.
methods.returns: a list of text, such as group, heading, button and textbox
warnings: a role is a term for the accessibility tree, not a meaning

methods.name: IntentsOf
methods.brief: Returns the intents an element says it satisfies, from its SATISFIES field.

parameters.name: pcName
parameters.role: the declared name

methods.returns: a list of text, in the order written; empty when it names none or the name is not declared
warnings: the names are recorded and never resolved: this plane checks their shape and nothing else

methods.name: SatisfiedIntents
methods.brief: Returns every intent named anywhere in the document, each once, in the order first seen.

methods.name: Orphans
methods.brief: Returns the elements that trace to no intent, the test that every interface element must serve one.
methods.returns: a list of names; styles are never listed
warnings: the panel itself is an element and is listed when it names no intent; there is no warning for an orphan

methods.name: TracesToIntent
methods.brief: TRUE if the element names at least one intent in SATISFIES.

parameters.name: pcName
parameters.role: the declared name

methods.returns: TRUE or FALSE; FALSE for a name that is not declared

classes.name: stzUMAP
classes.brief: Draws a map of high-dimensional samples in 2 dimensions from a neighbour graph, using UMAP, and can place new rows in it.
classes.description: Built for LOOKING at data, not for measuring it: distances and cluster sizes in the map mean nothing, and the neighbour count changes the picture, so try two values. The usual pipeline is ReduceWithPCA(30) then Fit. The default of 15 neighbours needs more than 15 samples, so small data needs SetNeighbors first. The neighbour graph is held in the engine after the first Fit: changing the minimum distance, the spread, the epochs or the seed redoes the layout only, while changing the neighbours, the labels or the PCA step drops the graph. LearnFromLabels reweights the graph with known classes, and the separation it gives is an input, not a finding. Unlike t-SNE, Transform places new rows against the frozen map, and LearnMapping makes that exact for the training rows. PreserveDensity adds the densMAP term, and LearnInverse trains a network that goes back from the map to the data.
classes.example:
o1.SetNeighbors(4)
o1.SetEpochs(100)
o1.Fit()
? o1.HasGraph()
#--> 1
? len(o1.Embedding())
#--> 12
? o1.Trustworthiness() > 0.9
#--> 1

methods.name: init
methods.brief: Builds a UMAP embedding job around a table of samples, one list of feature values per sample.

parameters.name: paData
parameters.role: the samples, a list of equal-length lists of numbers

warnings: an empty list, a sample that is not a list, or samples of different widths raise an error naming the first bad sample

methods.name: NumberOfSamples
methods.brief: Returns how many samples the job was built with.

methods.name: NumberOfFeatures
methods.brief: Returns how many feature values each sample has.

methods.name: HasGraph
methods.brief: TRUE if the neighbour graph of a fit is still held in the engine.
notes: it is false before a fit and after any setting that changes the graph

methods.name: GraphInfo
methods.brief: Returns the size of the held neighbour graph: points, width, neighbours and edges.
methods.returns: a list of four numbers; [ ] before a fit
notes: twelve points of three features with 4 neighbours gave 12, 3, 4 and 26

methods.name: ReleaseGraph
methods.brief: Gives the held neighbour graph back to the engine; the next fit builds it again.

extensions.name: ReleaseGraphQ
extensions.adds: does what the method does, then returns the object, so the call can be chained

methods.name: SetNeighbors
methods.brief: Sets how many neighbours each point looks at, the dial between local detail and global shape; 15 by default.

parameters.name: n
parameters.role: the number of neighbours, 2 or more, anything else is ignored

notes: small values fragment clusters, large values smear detail
warnings: the graph is dropped; Fit refuses to run when the number is not below the number of samples (15 neighbours on 12 samples)

extensions.name: SetNeighborsQ
extensions.adds: does what the method does, then returns the object, so the call can be chained

methods.name: Neighbors
methods.brief: Returns the number of neighbours in force.

methods.name: SetMinDistance
methods.brief: Sets how tightly points may pack in the embedding; 0.1 by default.

parameters.name: n
parameters.role: the minimum distance, 0 or more, a negative value is ignored

notes: a smaller value makes clusters look more separated, an appearance you choose rather than a finding; the graph is kept, so only the layout is redone

extensions.name: SetMinDistanceQ
extensions.adds: does what the method does, then returns the object, so the call can be chained

methods.name: SetSpread
methods.brief: Sets the scale of the embedding that the minimum distance is measured against; 1 by default.

parameters.name: n
parameters.role: the spread, above 0, anything else is ignored

extensions.name: SetSpreadQ
extensions.adds: does what the method does, then returns the object, so the call can be chained

methods.name: SetDimensions
methods.brief: Sets how many coordinates each point gets in the embedding; 2 by default.

parameters.name: n
parameters.role: the number of output dimensions, 1 or more, anything else is ignored

extensions.name: SetDimensionsQ
extensions.adds: does what the method does, then returns the object, so the call can be chained

methods.name: SetEpochs
methods.brief: Sets how many optimisation passes the layout takes; 200 by default.

parameters.name: n
parameters.role: the number of epochs, above 0, anything else is ignored

extensions.name: SetEpochsQ
extensions.adds: does what the method does, then returns the object, so the call can be chained

methods.name: SetSeed
methods.brief: Sets the number that starts the random generator, so a run can be repeated or varied; 42 by default.

parameters.name: n
parameters.role: the starting number

notes: the same value gives the same embedding (twelve points), and the graph is kept

extensions.name: SetSeedQ
extensions.adds: does what the method does, then returns the object, so the call can be chained

methods.name: ReduceWithPCA
methods.brief: Asks for a PCA down to n dimensions before the embedding, the usual first step; off by default.

parameters.name: n
parameters.role: the number of components to keep, 1 or more, anything else is ignored

notes: it removes noise and speeds up the distances, at the cost of any structure the discarded components held
warnings: the graph is dropped; when n is not below the number of features the data goes through unchanged

extensions.name: ReduceWithPCAQ
extensions.adds: does what the method does, then returns the object, so the call can be chained

methods.name: SkipPCA
methods.brief: Turns off the PCA step, so the fit uses the raw features.

extensions.name: SkipPCAQ
extensions.adds: does what the method does, then returns the object, so the call can be chained

methods.name: UsesPCA
methods.brief: TRUE if a PCA reduction has been requested.

methods.name: PCAQ
methods.brief: Returns the PCA that the last fit ran before embedding, so its explained variance can be read.
methods.returns: a stzPCA object; "" before a fit that used PCA

methods.name: LearnFromLabels
methods.brief: Gives one known label per sample so that the neighbour graph weakens links between different classes; -1 marks an unknown label.

parameters.name: paLabels
parameters.role: a list with one label per sample

notes: it does not classify anything: the separation of the classes is an input, not evidence that they are separable
warnings: the graph is dropped; a list of the wrong length raises an error giving both lengths

extensions.name: LearnFromLabelsQ
extensions.adds: does what the method does, then returns the object, so the call can be chained

methods.name: IgnoreLabels
methods.brief: Forgets the labels, so the fit is unsupervised again.
warnings: the graph is dropped

extensions.name: IgnoreLabelsQ
extensions.adds: does what the method does, then returns the object, so the call can be chained

methods.name: IsSupervised
methods.brief: TRUE if labels have been given.

methods.name: Labels
methods.brief: Returns the labels given to LearnFromLabels.
methods.returns: a list; [ ] when there are none

methods.name: SetTargetWeight
methods.brief: Sets how much the labels count against the data's own structure; 0.5 by default.

parameters.name: n
parameters.role: the weight from 0 to 1, anything else is ignored

warnings: the graph is dropped; more weight is not more separation (a code comment reports a peak near 0.2, not run here)

extensions.name: SetTargetWeightQ
extensions.adds: does what the method does, then returns the object, so the call can be chained

methods.name: TargetWeight
methods.brief: Returns the weight given to the labels.

methods.name: PreserveDensity
methods.brief: Turns on the density term (densMAP) so denser regions are drawn tighter; the weight becomes 2, or 0.1 when parametric.
notes: it makes cluster size more readable, at the cost of some separation between clusters

extensions.name: PreserveDensityQ
extensions.adds: does what the method does, then returns the object, so the call can be chained

methods.name: IgnoreDensity
methods.brief: Turns the density term off.

extensions.name: IgnoreDensityQ
extensions.adds: does what the method does, then returns the object, so the call can be chained

methods.name: IsDensityPreserving
methods.brief: TRUE if the density weight is above 0.

methods.name: SetDensityWeight
methods.brief: Sets how hard the density term pushes; 0 turns it off exactly.

parameters.name: n
parameters.role: the weight, 0 or more, a negative value is ignored

notes: with 0 the embedding is identical to the ordinary fit, value for value (twelve points, same seed)

extensions.name: SetDensityWeightQ
extensions.adds: does what the method does, then returns the object, so the call can be chained

methods.name: DensityWeight
methods.brief: Returns the weight of the density term.

methods.name: SetDensityPhase
methods.brief: Sets the last fraction of the epochs during which the density term is active; 0.3 by default.

parameters.name: n
parameters.role: the fraction, above 0 and at most 1, anything else is ignored

extensions.name: SetDensityPhaseQ
extensions.adds: does what the method does, then returns the object, so the call can be chained

methods.name: DensityPhase
methods.brief: Returns the fraction of the epochs during which the density term runs.

methods.name: DensityCorrelation
methods.brief: Returns how closely the drawn local radii follow the original ones at the end of a fit with the density term on.
methods.returns: a number from -1 to 1; 0 when the term is off or before a fit
notes: it is a correlation, not a percentage

methods.name: LocalRadii
methods.brief: Returns the average distance of each sample to its neighbours in the original space, as measured by a fit with the density term on.
methods.returns: a list of numbers, one per sample; [ ] when the term is off

methods.name: LearnMapping
methods.brief: Switches to parametric UMAP, which trains a neural network from features to coordinates instead of moving free points.

extensions.name: LearnMappingQ
extensions.adds: does what the method does, then returns the object, so the call can be chained

methods.name: SkipMapping
methods.brief: Switches back to the ordinary UMAP, where points move freely.

extensions.name: SkipMappingQ
extensions.adds: does what the method does, then returns the object, so the call can be chained
