methods.name: SetHiddenLayers
methods.brief: Sets the widths of the hidden layers of the network of the parametric variant; 50 and 20 by default.

parameters.name: paWidths
parameters.role: the layer widths, a list of numbers, an empty list or another value is ignored

extensions.name: SetHiddenLayersQ
extensions.adds: does what the method does, then returns the object, so the call can be chained

methods.name: HiddenLayers
methods.brief: Returns the hidden layer widths of the parametric variant.
methods.returns: a list of numbers; [ 50, 20 ] by default

methods.name: SetLearningRate
methods.brief: Sets the step size of the network of the parametric variant; 0.01 by default.

parameters.name: n
parameters.role: the learning rate, above 0, anything else is ignored

extensions.name: SetLearningRateQ
extensions.adds: does what the method does, then returns the object, so the call can be chained

methods.name: LearningRate
methods.brief: Returns the step size of the network of the parametric variant.

methods.name: LearnInverse
methods.brief: Trains a second network that maps points of the embedding back to rows of data.
warnings: it needs a fitted job; training is slow with the default 15000 epochs, so a small job sets SetInverseEpochs first

extensions.name: LearnInverseQ
extensions.adds: does what the method does, then returns the object, so the call can be chained

methods.name: HasInverse
methods.brief: TRUE if an inverse network has been trained.

methods.name: SetInverseLayers
methods.brief: Sets the hidden layer widths of the inverse network; 64 and 64 by default.

parameters.name: paWidths
parameters.role: the layer widths, a list of numbers, an empty list or another value is ignored

extensions.name: SetInverseLayersQ
extensions.adds: does what the method does, then returns the object, so the call can be chained

methods.name: SetInverseEpochs
methods.brief: Sets how many epochs the inverse network trains for; 15000 by default.

parameters.name: n
parameters.role: the number of epochs, above 0, anything else is ignored

extensions.name: SetInverseEpochsQ
extensions.adds: does what the method does, then returns the object, so the call can be chained

methods.name: Inverse
methods.brief: Returns rows of data for points of the embedding, using the inverse network.

parameters.name: paPoints
parameters.role: points of the map, each with as many coordinates as the embedding

methods.returns: a list of rows, one per point
notes: the rows come back in the space the fit saw, so with a PCA step they are PCA scores, not the original features
warnings: it raises before LearnInverse, and for a point with the wrong number of coordinates

methods.name: Fit
methods.brief: Builds the neighbour graph if none is held, then lays the points out, and stores the coordinates.
notes: with the parametric variant switched on, a network is trained instead
warnings: it raises an error when the neighbour count is not between 2 and one less than the number of samples; a second fit that only changes the minimum distance, spread, epochs or seed reuses the graph

extensions.name: FitQ
extensions.adds: does what the method does, then returns the object, so the call can be chained

methods.name: IsFitted
methods.brief: TRUE if Fit has run.

methods.name: Embedding
methods.brief: Returns the coordinates of every sample after the fit.
methods.returns: a list with one list of coordinates per sample
notes: distances and cluster sizes in the picture are not meaningful, only which points are near
warnings: it raises Fit() me first. before a fit

methods.name: Trustworthiness
methods.brief: Returns how faithful the embedding is to the neighbourhoods of the original data, from 0 to 1, looking at 5 neighbours.
methods.returns: a number from 0 to 1; 1 means no false neighbour was invented
notes: two separated clusters of six points gave 0.96
warnings: it raises before a fit

methods.name: TrustworthinessAt
methods.brief: Returns the trustworthiness of the embedding for a chosen number of neighbours.

parameters.name: nK
parameters.role: how many nearest neighbours to compare

warnings: it raises before a fit

methods.name: CurveParameters
methods.brief: Returns the two numbers a and b of the curve 1/(1 + a*d^(2b)) that the fit derived from the minimum distance and the spread.
methods.returns: a list of [ key, value ] pairs, a and b
notes: the values were a = 1.58 and b = 0.90 for the defaults
warnings: it raises before a fit

methods.name: Transform
methods.brief: Places new rows in the existing map, by a forward pass when parametric, otherwise by refining each point against the frozen layout.

parameters.name: paRows
parameters.role: the new samples, each with as many feature values as the training samples

methods.returns: a list of coordinate rows, one per new row
notes: the map does not rearrange for the new point: a point unlike the training data is still placed among the nearest training points
warnings: it raises Fit() me first. before a fit, and an error naming the row when a row has the wrong width or the list is empty

methods.name: NewLocalRadii
methods.brief: Returns the local radii of the rows placed by the last Transform.
methods.returns: a list of numbers, one per placed row; [ ] before any Transform
notes: a large value warns that a new row lies outside the region the map was fitted on

methods.name: LocalRadiiOf
methods.brief: Returns how far each given row sits from its neighbours in the training data, without placing anything.

parameters.name: paRows
parameters.role: the rows to measure, each with as many feature values as the training samples

methods.returns: a list of numbers, one per row
warnings: it raises before a fit and for rows of the wrong width

methods.name: Why
methods.brief: Returns one sentence describing the fit: variant, size, neighbours, minimum distance, epochs and PCA step.
warnings: it raises before a fit

classes.name: stzUnicodeData
classes.brief: Looks up characters by their Unicode name and names by their code point, through the engine's Unicode database.
classes.description: A name is the full Unicode name, such as LATIN SMALL LETTER A, compared without regard to case. A code point is given as a decimal number or as hexadecimal text with or without 0x. The search methods take a part of a name and return the matches: names, characters or code points. The database is inside the engine and nothing is loaded from a file.
classes.example:
? o1.CharUnicodeByName("LATIN SMALL LETTER A")
#--> 97
? o1.CharNameByHexCode("0x41")
#--> LATIN CAPITAL LETTER A
? o1.UnicodesOfCharsContaining("BLACK HEART SUIT")[1]
#--> 9829

methods.name: init
methods.brief: Builds the lookup object; there is nothing to load, since the engine keeps the Unicode database itself.

methods.name: ContainsCharName
methods.brief: TRUE if a character has exactly this name, compared without regard to case; a part of a name does not count.

parameters.name: pcCharName
parameters.role: the full Unicode name, such as LATIN SMALL LETTER A

methods.name: FindCharName
methods.brief: TRUE if a character has exactly this name; it is the same answer as ContainsCharName, with a check that the argument is a text.

parameters.name: pcCharName
parameters.role: the full Unicode name

notes: it answers 1 or 0, never a position
warnings: raises Incorrect param type for a name that is not a text

methods.name: SearchCharName
methods.brief: Returns the names that contain the given words, found by a case-insensitive substring search.

parameters.name: pcCharName
parameters.role: the part of a name to look for

methods.returns: a list of text, in table order; [ ] when no name matches

methods.name: CharByName
methods.brief: Returns the character with exactly this name, as a one-character text.

parameters.name: pcCharName
parameters.role: the full Unicode name

warnings: raises Character name not found for a name that does not exist

methods.name: CharHexCodeByName
methods.brief: Returns the code point of a named character as a hexadecimal text with the 0x prefix.

parameters.name: pcCharName
parameters.role: the full Unicode name

methods.returns: a text such as 0x61, and the bare prefix 0x for a name that does not exist
notes: digits above 9 are upper case, 0x1F600
warnings: an unknown name is not reported, it gives the prefix alone

methods.name: CharUnicodeByName
methods.brief: Returns the decimal code point of a named character.

parameters.name: pcCharName
parameters.role: the full Unicode name

methods.returns: a number, -1 for a name that does not exist

methods.name: CharByHexCode
methods.brief: Returns the character at a hexadecimal code point, with or without the 0x prefix.

parameters.name: pcHex
parameters.role: the code point in hexadecimal, such as 0x41 or 05D0

methods.returns: a one-character text such as A

methods.name: CharByUnicode
methods.brief: Returns the character at a decimal code point.

parameters.name: nUnicode
parameters.role: the code point as a number

methods.returns: a one-character text such as a

methods.name: CharNameByHexCode
methods.brief: Returns the Unicode name of the character at a hexadecimal code point, with or without the 0x prefix.

parameters.name: pcHex
parameters.role: the code point in hexadecimal, such as 0x41

methods.returns: a text such as LATIN CAPITAL LETTER A; an empty text for an empty code or an unassigned point

methods.name: CharNameByUnicode
methods.brief: Returns the Unicode name of the character at a decimal code point.

parameters.name: nUnicode
parameters.role: the code point as a number

methods.returns: a text such as BLACK HEART SUIT; <control> for a control character; an empty text for an unassigned point

methods.name: UnicodesOfCharsContaining
methods.brief: Returns the code points of the characters whose name contains the given words.

parameters.name: cPartOfName
parameters.role: the part of a name to look for, a text

methods.returns: a list of numbers; [ ] when none

methods.name: CharsContaining
methods.brief: Returns the characters whose name contains the given words, as a list of one-character texts.

parameters.name: cPartOfName
parameters.role: the part of a name to look for

methods.returns: a list of text; [ ] when none

methods.name: CharsNamesContaining
methods.brief: Returns the full names of the characters whose name contains the given words.

parameters.name: pcPartOfName
parameters.role: the part of a name to look for, in any case

methods.returns: a list of text, in table order; [ ] when none

methods.name: CharNamesContaining
methods.brief: Returns the full names of the characters whose name contains the given words, as CharsNamesContaining does.

parameters.name: pcPartOfName
parameters.role: the part of a name to look for, in any case

methods.returns: a list of text; [ ] when none
notes: the other spelling of CharsNamesContaining, which calls it

methods.name: NumberOfUnicodeChars
methods.brief: Returns how many entries the engine's Unicode table holds, which is not the count of characters.
notes: the two disagree by design of the table; read the global for the count of assigned characters
warnings: the table has one entry per line of the Unicode data file, where a range such as the CJK ideographs is two lines, so the number is far below the 149186 that the global function NumberOfUnicodeChars() gives

classes.name: stzUpdatePlan
classes.brief: Holds the rehearsed operations of a twin as the one artifact that may cross into reality, narrated, ranked for risk and gated.
classes.description: A twin changes only its own memory; reality changes when a plan is executed. The plan can tell its story in plain words (Narration), rank what deserves a second look (Risks), re-check itself against reality as it is now (Validate), let a reviewer reject steps, and say whether its executor may commit at all (MayCommit). Execute then passes each active operation through three gates, the reviewer, the commit scope and the executor's capabilities, before the bridge touches anything, and records every decision in the audit trail. Narrate and rehearse freely; execute with intent.
classes.receiver: v = new stzVirtualFileSystem(); v.CreateFile("/w/a.txt", "alpha"); v.DeleteFile("/w/old.txt"); o1 = v.GenerateUpdatePlan()
classes.example:
? o1.NumberOfOperations()
#--> 2
? @@( o1.Risks() )
#--> [ [ 2, "DESTRUCTIVE: delete file '/w/old.txt'" ] ]
? @@( o1.MayCommit() )
#--> [ 1, "no executor set -- unguarded (a human at the keyboard)" ]

methods.name: init
methods.brief: Builds a plan from rehearsed operations and the bridge that would commit them; nothing is committed until Execute.

parameters.name: paOps
parameters.role: the list of stzVirtualOperation, in the order they were rehearsed

parameters.name: poBridge
parameters.role: the reality bridge that Validate asks and Execute commits through

notes: a twin builds it for you with GenerateUpdatePlan

methods.name: Operations
methods.brief: Returns the operations the plan holds, rejected ones included.

methods.name: NumberOfOperations
methods.brief: Returns how many operations the plan holds, rejected ones included.

methods.name: NumberOfActiveOperations
methods.brief: Returns how many operations would still be committed, which is those not rejected.

methods.name: SetScope
methods.brief: Sets the bound on what the plan may commit.

parameters.name: poScope
parameters.role: the stzCommitScope that checks each operation

methods.returns: the plan itself, so calls chain

methods.name: Scope
methods.brief: Returns the scope set on the plan.
methods.returns: the stzCommitScope; an empty text when none is set

methods.name: SetExecutor
methods.brief: Sets who commits the plan, whose capability kinds gate the crossing.

parameters.name: poActor
parameters.role: the stzSystemActor that commits

methods.returns: the plan itself, so calls chain
notes: without an executor the plan is unguarded, as a human at the keyboard

methods.name: Executor
methods.brief: Returns who commits the plan.
methods.returns: the stzSystemActor; an empty text when none is set

methods.name: SetGovernance
methods.brief: Sets an optional governance that demands a declared trust posture of the executor and keeps the decision lineage.

parameters.name: poGov
parameters.role: the stzGovernance to consult

methods.returns: the plan itself, so calls chain
notes: the plan keeps a copy, so read its lineage through Governance

methods.name: Governance
methods.brief: Returns the governance set on the plan.
methods.returns: the stzGovernance; an empty text when none is set

methods.name: AuditTrail
methods.brief: Returns the decisions the plan took when it was executed.
methods.returns: a list of [ index, outcome, type, actor ] rows, the outcome committed or refused
notes: an operation refused by a scope, or rejected by a reviewer, leaves no row

methods.name: NumberOfAuditEntries
methods.brief: Returns how many decisions the audit trail holds.

methods.name: RejectOperation
methods.brief: Marks one operation as rejected by a reviewer, so Execute skips it.

parameters.name: pnIndex
parameters.role: the position of the operation in the plan, from 1

parameters.name: pcBecause
parameters.role: the reason for rejecting it

methods.returns: the plan itself, so calls chain
notes: the reason is kept with the rejection, and the narration shows the operation with an x

methods.name: IsRejected
methods.brief: TRUE if the operation at that position was rejected.

parameters.name: pnIndex
parameters.role: the position of the operation, from 1

methods.name: Narration
methods.brief: Returns the plan as a plain-language story, one numbered line per operation, rejected ones marked.

methods.name: ShowNarration
methods.brief: Prints the narration of the plan.

methods.name: Risks
methods.brief: Returns the operations that deserve a second look: deletions, moves, removed variables and spawned commands.
methods.returns: a list of [ index, warning ] rows; an empty list when none is risky

methods.name: ShowRisks
methods.brief: Prints the risks of the plan, one line each.

methods.name: Validate
methods.brief: Re-checks the plan against reality as it is now, because reality may have moved since the rehearsal.
methods.returns: a list of [ index, warning ] rows for a delete, copy or move whose target or source is absent; an empty list when all is present
notes: it reads reality through the bridge and changes nothing

methods.name: MayCommit
methods.brief: Tells whether the executor could commit this plan at all, without touching anything.

methods.name: Execute
methods.brief: Commits every active operation through the bridge after the reviewer, scope and capability gates, and returns a summary with the log.
methods.returns: a list [ [ committed, n ], [ skipped, n ], [ log, rows ] ], each row [ index, status, text ] with a status COMMITTED, FAILED, REJECTED, REFUSED-BY-SCOPE or REFUSED-BY-GOVERNANCE
notes: refusals reach the security ledger as scope.refused, capability.refused and posture.refused
warnings: this is the one place reality changes, and with a file or environment bridge it writes the disk or the process: rehearse in the twin and read Narration and Risks first; a governance that finds no declared posture refuses the whole plan with a single row of index 0

methods.name: ExecuteStepByStep
methods.brief: Commits the plan as Execute does, printing each row of the log as it comes.
warnings: the same warning as Execute: it commits for real

classes.name: stzUrl
classes.brief: Parses a URL with the engine and gives its parts, with setters that rebuild the text; it never fetches anything.
classes.description: Reach for it to read or change the scheme, user information, host, port, path, query and fragment of one URL, or to move between a file URL and a local file path. The parse is done by the engine (stz_url) and is lazy: a part is read the first time it is asked. The setters change the object in place and rebuild Content from the parts, leaving out ports 80 and 443. It is not a fetcher (stzHttpClient is) and it does not split a query into pairs. A relative reference parses poorly: d.html has an empty path and sub/d.html is read with sub as the host. The class sits in network/stzUrl.ring, which neither stzlib.ring nor stzBase.ring loads, so a caller loads the file itself.
classes.example:
? o1.Host()
#--> example.com
? o1.Port()
#--> 8080
? o1.FileName()
#--> guide.html
o1.SetQuery("a=2")
? o1.Content()
#--> https://bob:pw@example.com:8080/docs/guide.html?a=2#top

methods.name: init
methods.brief: Builds a URL object by parsing the text with the engine; nothing is fetched, and an empty text builds an empty object.

parameters.name: pcUrl
parameters.role: the URL as text, for example https://example.com:8080/a/b.html?x=1#top

notes: text that does not parse is kept as given: IsValid answers FALSE and the parts are empty
warnings: the class is in network/stzUrl.ring but neither stzlib.ring nor stzBase.ring loads that file, so load it by hand before use

methods.name: Content
methods.brief: Returns the URL as text; when the object is empty it is rebuilt from its parts.
notes: Url and ToString are the same call

methods.name: SetContent
methods.brief: Replaces the URL by parsing new text; every part is read again from it.

parameters.name: pcUrl
parameters.role: the new URL as text

notes: it does what SetUrl does

methods.name: Copy
methods.brief: Returns a new independent stzUrl built from the current text.

methods.name: SetUrl
methods.brief: Replaces the URL by parsing new text, freeing the previous parse and clearing every cached part.

parameters.name: pcUrl
parameters.role: the new URL as text

notes: the new text is parsed at once, so Host, Path and the others answer for it

methods.name: IsValid
methods.brief: TRUE if the engine parsed the text as an absolute URL with a scheme and a host.
notes: a relative reference such as d.html or /a/b?q=1 answers FALSE even though its path and query are read; the empty object and text such as :::: also answer FALSE

methods.name: IsEmpty
methods.brief: TRUE if no URL text is held, which is the case for a new empty object and after Clear.
notes: it reads the held text, so an object built from garbage text is not empty

methods.name: Clear
methods.brief: Forgets the URL and every part, leaving an empty object.

methods.name: Scheme
methods.brief: Returns the scheme, the part before ://, as written in the URL.
methods.returns: a text; empty when there is none
notes: the case is kept: HTTP://h/ answers HTTP, while IsHttp compares without regard to case

methods.name: SetScheme
methods.brief: Sets the scheme and rebuilds the URL text from the parts.

parameters.name: pcScheme
parameters.role: the new scheme, for example https

notes: IsHttps and the other type checks follow at once

methods.name: Host
methods.brief: Returns the host name, without user information or port.
methods.returns: a text; empty when there is none
notes: Domain and Server are the same call

methods.name: SetHost
methods.brief: Sets the host and rebuilds the URL text; the port, path and query are kept.

parameters.name: pcHost
parameters.role: the new host name

methods.name: Port
methods.brief: Returns the port written in the URL, or -1 when none is written.
notes: a URL without a port answers -1 even for http and https

methods.name: PortWithDefault
methods.brief: Returns the port of the URL, or the given number when no port is written.

parameters.name: nDefault
parameters.role: the number to answer when the URL has no port

notes: 0 counts as no port

methods.name: SetPort
methods.brief: Sets the port and rebuilds the URL text.

parameters.name: nPort
parameters.role: the new port number

notes: the text drops ports 80 and 443 whatever the scheme, so SetPort(80) on https removes the port from Content

methods.name: Path
methods.brief: Returns the path, from the first slash after the host up to the query.
methods.returns: a text; empty when there is none
notes: the engine reads a bare reference such as sub/d.html with sub as the host and /d.html as the path; d.html alone has an empty path

methods.name: SetPath
methods.brief: Sets the path and rebuilds the URL text; a missing leading slash is added.

parameters.name: pcPath
parameters.role: the new path

methods.name: FileName
methods.brief: Returns the last segment of the path, the part after the final slash.
methods.returns: a text; empty when the path is empty
notes: Section(n + 1, n) is out of range; /a/b answers b and an empty path answers an empty text
warnings: Raises error today when the path ends with a slash, on /a/b/ and on / alike: the section call is given an end before its start

methods.name: Query
methods.brief: Returns the query, the text between ? and #, without the question mark.
methods.returns: a text; empty when there is none

methods.name: HasQuery
methods.brief: TRUE if the URL carries a query after a question mark.

methods.name: SetQuery
methods.brief: Sets the query and rebuilds the URL text; give it without the question mark.

parameters.name: pcQuery
parameters.role: the new query, for example a=2&b=3

methods.name: Fragment
methods.brief: Returns the fragment, the text after #, without the hash sign.
methods.returns: a text; empty when there is none

methods.name: HasFragment
methods.brief: TRUE if the URL carries a fragment after a hash sign.

methods.name: SetFragment
methods.brief: Sets the fragment and rebuilds the URL text; give it without the hash sign.

parameters.name: pcFragment
parameters.role: the new fragment, for example end

methods.name: UserName
methods.brief: Returns the user name written before the @ of the authority.
methods.returns: a text; empty when there is none

methods.name: Password
methods.brief: Returns the password written after the colon in the user information.
methods.returns: a text; empty when there is none
notes: the password stays readable in Content and Authority: do not log a URL that carries one

methods.name: UserInfo
methods.brief: Returns the user name and password joined by a colon, or the user name alone.
methods.returns: a text; empty when neither is set

methods.name: SetUserName
methods.brief: Sets the user name and rebuilds the URL text with it before the host.

parameters.name: pcUserName
parameters.role: the new user name

methods.name: SetPassword
methods.brief: Sets the password and rebuilds the URL text; it shows only when a user name or password is set.

parameters.name: pcPassword
parameters.role: the new password

methods.name: SetUserInfo
methods.brief: Sets the user name and password from text of the form user:password, or only the user name when there is no colon.

parameters.name: pcUserInfo
parameters.role: the user information, for example zed:pp

notes: text without a colon clears an earlier password

methods.name: Authority
methods.brief: Returns the user information, host and port joined as user:password@host:port, leaving out what is absent.
notes: it prints a port of 80 or 443 when one is set, which Content leaves out

methods.name: SetAuthority
methods.brief: Sets the user information, host and port from text such as kim:k1@host:9000 and rebuilds the URL text.

parameters.name: pcAuthority
parameters.role: the authority as text

notes: the parts that are given replace the old ones; the others stay
warnings: an authority with no user information or no port does not clear the old ones: SetAuthority("plain.net") on a URL that had kim:k1 and port 9000 leaves kim:k1@plain.net:9000

methods.name: IsRelative
methods.brief: TRUE if the URL has no scheme, as /a/b or d.html.

methods.name: IsLocalFile
methods.brief: TRUE if the scheme is file, compared without regard to case.
notes: the same test as IsFileScheme

methods.name: IsHttp
methods.brief: TRUE if the scheme is http, compared without regard to case; https answers FALSE.

methods.name: IsHttps
methods.brief: TRUE if the scheme is https, compared without regard to case.

methods.name: IsFtp
methods.brief: TRUE if the scheme is ftp, compared without regard to case.

methods.name: IsFileScheme
methods.brief: TRUE if the scheme is file, compared without regard to case.
notes: the same test as IsLocalFile

methods.name: IsParentOf
methods.brief: TRUE if the given URL lies under this one, by host and path, and is longer.

parameters.name: oOtherUrl
parameters.role: the stzUrl to test, where anything that is not an object answers FALSE

notes: the scheme, port and query are not compared; http://h/a/b/ is parent of http://h/a/b/c but not of itself, and a path with no final slash also matches a longer name (/a/b matches /a/bc)

methods.name: ResolvedWith
methods.brief: Returns a new stzUrl made of this URL with the path of the given reference put in place of its own.

parameters.name: oRelativeUrl
parameters.role: the stzUrl to resolve against this one

methods.returns: a new stzUrl; an empty one when the argument is not an object
notes: a path that does not start with a slash is joined to the base path up to its last slash, but only when the engine gave it a path
warnings: resolution is right only for a reference with a leading slash (/c/d.html) or a full URL: d.html parses with an empty path and leaves the base unchanged, and sub/d.html is read with sub as the host so it answers http://plain.org/d.html instead of /a/b/sub/d.html

methods.name: ToLocalFile
methods.brief: Returns the file path of a file URL, without the leading slash before a drive letter.
methods.returns: a text; empty when the scheme is not file
notes: file:///C:/data/x.txt answers C:/data/x.txt and file:///tmp/x.txt answers /tmp/x.txt

methods.name: FromLocalFile
methods.brief: Raises error R19 today instead of returning a file URL for the given path.

parameters.name: pcFilePath
parameters.role: the file path to turn into a file URL

notes: the call that was meant to turn backslashes into slashes is the one that fails
warnings: Raises error R19 today whatever the path, on a drive path with backslashes and on /tmp/y.txt: it calls ReplaceSubstring with two arguments where that method takes a start, an end and a replacement

methods.name: ReconstructUrl
methods.brief: Rebuilds the stored URL text from the scheme, user information, host, port, path, query and fragment.
methods.returns: nothing; read the result with Content
notes: every setter calls it; ports 80, 443 and -1 are left out of the text

methods.name: Swap
methods.brief: Exchanges the URLs of this object and the given one, in place on both.

parameters.name: oOtherUrl
parameters.role: the stzUrl to exchange with, where anything that is not an object does nothing

classes.name: stzUUID
classes.brief: Generates a random version-4 UUID and answers questions about it: its text forms, validity, version, variant and bytes.
classes.description: A new object is a fresh random UUID held in upper case with hyphens. The generation and the validity check are done by the engine; the rest is reading the text. Two objects built one after the other differ, and a copy made with Copy holds the same value as the original.
classes.example:
? len(o1.Content())
#--> 36
? len(o1.WithoutHyphens())
#--> 32
? o1.Version()
#--> 4
? o1.Variant()
#--> RFC 4122
? o1.IsValid()
#--> 1

methods.name: init
methods.brief: Generates a new random version-4 UUID, held in upper case with hyphens, such as 3F2504E0-4F89-41D3-9A0C-0305E82C3301.

methods.name: Content
methods.brief: Returns the UUID as 36 upper-case characters with hyphens.

methods.name: Copy
methods.brief: Returns a new stzUUID that holds the same value, so the two are independent objects with one identity.
warnings: the constructor generates a fresh UUID first, which the copy then overwrites

methods.name: WithoutHyphens
methods.brief: Returns the UUID as 32 hexadecimal characters with the hyphens removed.

methods.name: WithHyphens
methods.brief: Returns the UUID in the 8-4-4-4-12 form.
warnings: it returns the same text as Content for a UUID built by this class

methods.name: IsNull
methods.brief: TRUE if the UUID is the nil UUID, all zeros.
warnings: a generated UUID is never nil

methods.name: IsValid
methods.brief: TRUE if the engine reads the value as a well-formed UUID.

methods.name: Version
methods.brief: Returns the UUID version number, 4 for a generated one; 0 when the engine cannot read it.

methods.name: Variant
methods.brief: Returns the name of the UUID variant read from its variant bits: RFC 4122, Microsoft, Reserved (NCS) or Future.

methods.name: Hashed
methods.brief: Returns a small number derived from the 32 characters, for use as a hash key.
warnings: a polynomial hash of the hex text, not a cryptographic one; equal UUIDs give equal numbers

methods.name: ToBytes
methods.brief: Returns the 16 bytes of the UUID as numbers from 0 to 255.

classes.name: stzValidator
classes.brief: Holds named validation rules in the engine, tests values against them, and collects the violations.
classes.description: Add rules with AddMinValueRule, AddMaxLengthRule and their kin; each returns the index of the rule. CheckInt, CheckLength and CheckStringLength answer 1 or 0 for a named rule, but do not record anything: when a check fails, call AddViolation with the rule's index, then read IsValid and RuleMessage. The rules live in the engine and are shared by every stzValidator of the process, so call Clear first. The required-value rule never rejects anything today.
classes.receiver: o1 = new stzValidator() o1.Clear() o1.AddMinValueRule("age_min", 18, "too young") o1.AddMaxLengthRule("name_max", 5, "name too long")
classes.example:
? o1.CheckInt("age_min", 20)
#--> 1
? o1.CheckInt("age_min", 10)
#--> 0
o1.AddViolation(0)
? o1.IsValid()
#--> 0
? o1.RuleMessage(0)
#--> too young
? o1.CheckStringLength("name_max", "Alexandria")
#--> 0
o1.Clear()

methods.name: init
methods.brief: Opens the engine's validation store, one list of named rules and one list of violations that every stzValidator object shares.
warnings: the rules and violations are global to the process, so call Clear first for a clean slate

methods.name: AddRule
methods.brief: Adds a named rule of a given kind with a threshold and a message, and returns its index.

parameters.name: cName
parameters.role: the rule's name, a non-empty text, used by the Check calls

parameters.name: nKind
parameters.role: the kind of rule, 0 required, 1 min value, 2 max value, 3 min length, 4 max length, 5 pattern, 6 custom

parameters.name: nThreshold
parameters.role: the limit the rule compares against

parameters.name: cMessage
parameters.role: the text reported when the rule is violated

methods.returns: the index of the new rule, a number counted from 0
notes: rule names are case-sensitive
warnings: a bad name, kind, threshold or message raises an error; a second rule with an existing name is stored, but the Check calls keep using the first

methods.name: AddMinValueRule
methods.brief: Adds a rule that a number must be at least nMin, and returns its index.

parameters.name: cName
parameters.role: the rule's name, a non-empty text

parameters.name: nMin
parameters.role: the smallest number allowed

parameters.name: cMessage
parameters.role: the text reported when the rule is violated

methods.returns: the index of the new rule, a number

methods.name: AddMaxValueRule
methods.brief: Adds a rule that a number must be at most nMax, and returns its index.

parameters.name: cName
parameters.role: the rule's name, a non-empty text

parameters.name: nMax
parameters.role: the largest number allowed

parameters.name: cMessage
parameters.role: the text reported when the rule is violated

methods.returns: the index of the new rule, a number

methods.name: AddMinLengthRule
methods.brief: Adds a rule that a length must be at least nMin, and returns its index.

parameters.name: cName
parameters.role: the rule's name, a non-empty text

parameters.name: nMin
parameters.role: the shortest length allowed

parameters.name: cMessage
parameters.role: the text reported when the rule is violated

methods.returns: the index of the new rule, a number

methods.name: AddMaxLengthRule
methods.brief: Adds a rule that a length must be at most nMax, and returns its index.

parameters.name: cName
parameters.role: the rule's name, a non-empty text

parameters.name: nMax
parameters.role: the longest length allowed

parameters.name: cMessage
parameters.role: the text reported when the rule is violated

methods.returns: the index of the new rule, a number

methods.name: AddRequiredRule
methods.brief: Adds a required-value rule, with the threshold 0, and returns its index.

parameters.name: cName
parameters.role: the rule's name, a non-empty text

parameters.name: cMessage
parameters.role: the text reported when the rule is violated

methods.returns: the index of the new rule, a number
warnings: the rule answers 1 (passes) for a length of 0, for a length of 4 and for the numbers 0 and 7, so it never rejects an empty value today (checked with CheckLength, CheckInt and CheckStringLength)

methods.name: CheckInt
methods.brief: Tests a number against a named rule and answers 1 if it passes, 0 if it does not.

parameters.name: cRuleName
parameters.role: the name of the rule to test against

parameters.name: nValue
parameters.role: the number to test

notes: a rule of another kind than the value check answers 1
warnings: an unknown rule name raises an error; a failed test is not recorded: call AddViolation to record it

methods.name: CheckLength
methods.brief: Tests a length against a named rule and answers 1 if it passes, 0 if it does not.

parameters.name: cRuleName
parameters.role: the name of the rule to test against

parameters.name: nLength
parameters.role: the length to test

notes: a rule of another kind than the length check answers 1
warnings: an unknown rule name raises an error; a failed test is not recorded: call AddViolation to record it

methods.name: CheckStringLength
methods.brief: Tests the length of a text, counted in characters, against a named rule.

parameters.name: cRuleName
parameters.role: the name of the rule to test against

parameters.name: cString
parameters.role: the text whose length is tested

warnings: counts characters, not bytes: 'Zoé' has length 3

methods.name: AddViolation
methods.brief: Records that a rule was violated, by its index, so IsValid turns FALSE.

parameters.name: nRuleIndex
parameters.role: the index of the rule that was violated, as AddRule returned it

methods.returns: 1 if recorded, 0 if the index names no rule

methods.name: NumberOfViolations
methods.brief: Returns how many violations were recorded.

methods.name: IsValid
methods.brief: TRUE if no violation is recorded.

methods.name: ClearViolations
methods.brief: Forgets the recorded violations and keeps the rules.

methods.name: RuleMessage
methods.brief: Returns the message of the rule at an index, counted from 0 in the order the rules were added.

parameters.name: nIndex
parameters.role: the index of the rule

methods.returns: a text; empty when no rule has that index

methods.name: NumberOfRules
methods.brief: Returns how many rules are stored.

methods.name: Clear
methods.brief: Removes every rule and every violation, for all objects that share the store.

classes.name: stzVaultHttpResolver
classes.brief: Resolves vault-sourced secrets from a real HashiCorp Vault or OpenBao server over its HTTP API, without keeping the token.
classes.description: It satisfies the stzVaultResolver contract, Resolve and Has, so a secret revealed through RevealVia, or the key of a sealed store, comes from the secret manager itself. A locator is path#field; a path holding /data/ is read as KV version 2, any other as KV version 1. It refuses by construction an http address that is not loopback, since the token would cross the network in clear, holds the token only as a stzSecret revealed through the actor gate for each request, and puts it in no message or event. The actor who asks for a secret is gated separately, by the secret's own RevealVia, before the resolver is called. The documentation here was run only against a loopback port that never answers, never against a real vault.
classes.example:
? o1.Address()
#--> https://vault.internal:8200
? o1.LastStatus()
#--> 0
o2 = new stzVaultHttpResolver("http://localhost:8200", StzSecretQ("vault-token"), HumanActor("svc"))
? o2.Address()
#--> http://localhost:8200

methods.name: init
methods.brief: Builds a resolver for a HashiCorp Vault or OpenBao server, refusing an address over which the token would travel in clear.

parameters.name: pcAddress
parameters.role: the server address, https:// or http:// to 127.0.0.1, localhost or [::1] only, with trailing slashes removed

parameters.name: poTokenSecret
parameters.role: a stzSecret holding the token

parameters.name: poActor
parameters.role: the service identity allowed to reveal the token

notes: the token is never kept in this object: it is revealed for each request through the actor gate
warnings: raises an error for any other http address, including lookalikes such as http://127.0.0.1.evil.example and http://127.0.0.1@evil.example, and one for a token that is not an object

methods.name: Address
methods.brief: Returns the server address in use, trimmed of trailing slashes.

methods.name: SetTimeout
methods.brief: Sets how long a request may take before it counts as unanswered.

parameters.name: pnMs
parameters.role: the timeout in milliseconds

methods.returns: the resolver itself, so calls chain

methods.name: LastStatus
methods.brief: Returns the HTTP status of the last request, for diagnosis.
methods.returns: a number; 0 before any request, and -1 when the server could not be reached or did not answer in time

methods.name: Resolve
methods.brief: Reads the field a locator names from the vault, as the vault contract requires, and raises when the value cannot be had.

parameters.name: pcLocator
parameters.role: path#field, the path after /v1/ and then the field

notes: the token goes in the X-Vault-Token header of one request and appears in no message or event; not run against a real vault when documented, only against a loopback port that never answers
warnings: raises an error for a locator without a path or a field, for a refusal (403, noted to the security ledger), for a missing secret (404) and for a missing field; with no answer it raises Vault answered -1, because the did not answer message is written for status 0; the locator is appended to the URL as given, so never build one from untrusted input, and it is quoted in errors without escaping

methods.name: Has
methods.brief: TRUE if the vault holds the path and the field; a missing secret answers FALSE, while a refusal or an unreachable vault raises.

parameters.name: pcLocator
parameters.role: path#field, as for Resolve

notes: a 404 is the only answer that gives FALSE
warnings: raises as Resolve does for a malformed locator, a refusal or no answer, since cannot tell is not absent

classes.name: stzVaultResolver
classes.brief: Holds an in-memory reference vault resolver, the contract between a vault-sourced secret and an external secret manager.
classes.description: A vault resolver is any object with Resolve(locator), which returns the value or raises, and ideally Has(locator). A secret whose source is a vault is fetched through one, passed at reveal time to RevealVia, so nothing holds a live backend handle. This class satisfies the contract for development and tests: you seed it with values. In production replace it with an object that calls your real vault, such as stzVaultHttpResolver; the secret, the store and the actor gate do not change. Locators are written path#field.
classes.example:
o1.Register("secret/data/prod/db#password", "invented-db-pass")
? o1.Has("secret/data/prod/db#password")
#--> 1
? o1.Resolve("secret/data/prod/db#password")
#--> invented-db-pass
? o1.NumberOfEntries()
#--> 1

methods.name: init
methods.brief: Builds an empty in-memory vault resolver with a name, the reference stand-in for a real secret manager.

parameters.name: pcName
parameters.role: the resolver's name, quoted in its messages

methods.name: Name
methods.brief: Returns the name the resolver was built with.

methods.name: Register
methods.brief: Seeds a value under a vault locator, replacing the value already there.

parameters.name: pcLocator
parameters.role: the locator, a path and a field joined by #, such as secret/data/prod/db#password

parameters.name: pcValue
parameters.role: the secret value

methods.returns: the resolver itself, so calls chain
notes: for development and tests only: the value is held in memory in clear, and a real resolver fetches it from the vault instead; use invented values

methods.name: Has
methods.brief: TRUE if a value is registered under that exact locator.

parameters.name: pcLocator
parameters.role: the locator to look for

notes: the match is exact, case and field included

methods.name: NumberOfEntries
methods.brief: Returns how many locators hold a value.

methods.name: Resolve
methods.brief: Returns the value registered under a locator; this is the method the vault contract asks of every resolver.

parameters.name: pcLocator
parameters.role: the locator to read

notes: the locator is quoted in the error as given, so show the message as text and not as markup; the reveal itself is gated by the secret that calls RevealVia
warnings: raises an error naming the resolver and the locator when nothing is registered there

methods.name: Show
methods.brief: Prints the resolver's name and entry count, then each locator with its value masked.
notes: values are never printed

classes.name: stzVectorIndex
classes.brief: Finds the stored vectors nearest to a query vector quickly, with an approximate forest of random trees, and measures what it misses.
classes.description: Build one with new stzVectorIndex(aVectors), one row per vector, all of the same width. Search, SearchWithBudget and SearchExact answer [ index, distance ] pairs, nearest first, indexes from 1, distance the squared Euclidean one; Search is approximate and quick, SearchExact is the full scan, and RecallAgainstExact measures the share of true neighbours the approximate search returns, which is what makes an approximate index honest. SetTrees, SetMetric and SetSeed are chainable and drop the built index, which is rebuilt at the next search. Use SetMetric(:Cosine) for text embeddings.

methods.name: init
methods.brief: Stores the vectors of a corpus to be searched by nearest neighbour; the search structure itself is built at the first search.

parameters.name: paVectors
parameters.role: a non-empty list of vectors, each a list of numbers, all of the same length

warnings: an empty list, a list whose items are not lists, or vectors of different lengths raises an error naming the problem

methods.name: SetTrees
methods.brief: Sets how many random trees the index grows; more trees find the true neighbours more often and take more memory.

parameters.name: n
parameters.role: the number of trees, at least 1

methods.returns: the same object, so calls chain; the default is 10
notes: a value below 1 raises "SetTrees: at least one tree."; the index is dropped and rebuilt at the next search, so it can be called at any time

methods.name: SetMetric
methods.brief: Chooses how closeness is judged: :Euclidean compares positions, :Cosine compares directions after scaling every vector to length 1.

parameters.name: pcMetric
parameters.role: :Euclidean or :Cosine

methods.returns: the same object, so calls chain; the default is :Euclidean
notes: any other value raises "SetMetric: :Euclidean or :Cosine."; text embeddings almost always want :Cosine; the index is rebuilt at the next search

methods.name: SetSeed
methods.brief: Sets the seed of the random trees so that a build, and any recall figure, can be repeated.

parameters.name: n
parameters.role: the seed number

methods.returns: the same object, so calls chain; the default is 42
notes: the index is rebuilt at the next search

methods.name: Trees
methods.brief: Returns the number of trees the index will grow.

methods.name: Metric
methods.brief: Returns the metric in use, in lowercase: "euclidean" or "cosine".

methods.name: Count
methods.brief: Returns how many vectors the index holds.

methods.name: Dimensions
methods.brief: Returns how many components each vector has.

methods.name: Search
methods.brief: Returns the k stored vectors nearest to a query, nearest first, with their squared distances, from an approximate search.

parameters.name: paQuery
parameters.role: the query vector, as many numbers as the stored vectors have

parameters.name: nK
parameters.role: how many neighbours to return, at least 1

methods.returns: a list of [ index, distance ] pairs; fewer than nK when the index is smaller
notes: indexes count from 1; the distance is squared Euclidean (in :Cosine mode 2 - 2 x cosine), so 5 apart reads 25; the distances are exact, and an approximate answer can only omit a true neighbour; Nearest is the same method

methods.name: SearchWithBudget
methods.brief: Returns the k nearest vectors like Search, with the number of candidates examined stated: a bigger budget finds more of the true neighbours.

parameters.name: paQuery
parameters.role: the query vector

parameters.name: nK
parameters.role: how many neighbours to return

parameters.name: nBudget
parameters.role: how many candidates to examine, 0 for the default

methods.returns: a list of [ index, distance ] pairs, nearest first
notes: the budget is the dial between speed and recall

methods.name: SearchExact
methods.brief: Returns the k nearest vectors by scanning every stored vector, the ground truth against which Search is judged.

parameters.name: paQuery
parameters.role: the query vector

parameters.name: nK
parameters.role: how many neighbours to return

methods.returns: a list of [ index, distance ] pairs, nearest first
notes: the cost grows with the corpus; for a large Euclidean corpus the scan may run on the GPU, with distances in single precision; NearestExact is the same method

methods.name: RecallAgainstExact
methods.brief: Returns the share of the true k nearest neighbours that the approximate search finds, over a set of queries; 1 means none missed.

parameters.name: paQueries
parameters.role: a non-empty list of query vectors

parameters.name: nK
parameters.role: how many neighbours to compare

parameters.name: nBudget
parameters.role: the candidate budget, 0 for the default

notes: measure it on your own vectors before trusting a budget; a query of the wrong width or an empty list raises an error

methods.name: CosineFromDistance
methods.brief: Returns the cosine similarity that a stored distance stands for, 1 - distance / 2.

parameters.name: nDist
parameters.role: a distance returned by a search of a :Cosine index

notes: on a :Euclidean index it raises "CosineFromDistance: only meaningful for a :Cosine index."

classes.name: stzVirtualEnvironment
classes.brief: Rehearses changes to variables, the working directory and processes in memory, without touching the real environment.
classes.description: The environment twin of stzVirtualSystem. SetVar, UnsetVar, ChangeDirectory and Spawn read like the real verbs but only record an operation in the twin; Var, HasVar, Cwd and the other readers answer from the twin, not from the process. MirrorReality fills the twin from the live environment first when a rehearsal should start from what is really there. A rehearsal becomes a narrated, reviewable plan with GenerateUpdatePlan, and only executing that plan reaches reality.
classes.example:
o1.SetVar("MODE", "dev")
o1.ChangeDirectory("/srv/app")
o1.Spawn("make test")
? o1.Var("MODE")
#--> dev
? o1.Cwd()
#--> /srv/app
? @@( o1.PendingSpawns() )
#--> [ "make test" ]

methods.name: init
methods.brief: Builds an environment twin with an empty state, a bridge to the live environment and no history.

methods.name: SetVar
methods.brief: Rehearses setting a variable; the real environment is not touched.

parameters.name: pcName
parameters.role: the variable name

parameters.name: pcValue
parameters.role: the value, as text

methods.returns: the twin itself, so calls chain
notes: a variable mirrored from reality keeps its mirrored origin after its value is set

methods.name: UnsetVar
methods.brief: Rehearses removing a variable; the real environment is not touched.

parameters.name: pcName
parameters.role: the variable name

methods.returns: the twin itself, so calls chain
notes: an absent name is recorded as an operation and changes nothing in the state

methods.name: ChangeDirectory
methods.brief: Rehearses changing the working directory; no real directory is entered.

parameters.name: pcPath
parameters.role: the directory to move to, as text

methods.returns: the twin itself, so calls chain

methods.name: Spawn
methods.brief: Rehearses starting a process by queueing its command; nothing is run.

parameters.name: pcCommand
parameters.role: the command line, as text

methods.returns: the twin itself, so calls chain
notes: the command only runs if a plan holding it is executed through the real bridge

methods.name: MirrorReality
methods.brief: Replaces the twin state with a copy of the live environment: its variables and its working directory.
methods.returns: the twin itself, so calls chain
notes: it reads the real environment, which can hold secrets, so show counts and names, never values

methods.name: Var
methods.brief: Returns the value of a variable in the twin.

parameters.name: pcName
parameters.role: the variable name, matched with case

methods.returns: a text; an empty text when the twin has no such variable

methods.name: HasVar
methods.brief: TRUE if the twin holds a variable of that exact name.

parameters.name: pcName
parameters.role: the variable name, matched with case

methods.name: OriginOfVar
methods.brief: Returns where a variable of the twin came from.

parameters.name: pcName
parameters.role: the variable name, matched with case

methods.returns: mirrored for one read from reality, virtual for one set in the twin; an empty text when absent

methods.name: Cwd
methods.brief: Returns the working directory of the twin.
methods.returns: a text; empty until mirrored or changed

methods.name: PendingSpawns
methods.brief: Returns the commands queued by Spawn, in order.

methods.name: NumberOfPendingSpawns
methods.brief: Returns how many commands are queued.

methods.name: Vars
methods.brief: Returns every variable of the twin with its origin.
methods.returns: a list of [ name, value, origin ] rows

methods.name: NumberOfVars
methods.brief: Returns how many variables the twin holds.

methods.name: Show
methods.brief: Prints one summary line of the twin state: variables, directory and queued commands.

classes.name: stzVirtualFileSystem
classes.brief: Rehearses file and folder changes in memory, so a change can be read, narrated and reviewed before the disk is touched.
classes.description: The file twin of stzVirtualSystem. CreateFile, WriteFile, CreateFolder, DeleteFile, DeleteFolder, CopyFile and MoveFile read like the real file verbs but only record an operation in an in-memory tree; Exists, ContentOf, SizeOf, Paths and the other readers answer from the twin, not from the disk. MirrorFile and MirrorFrom start a rehearsal from what the disk holds. GenerateUpdatePlan turns the rehearsal into a narrated plan, and only executing that plan reaches reality. The twin does not check what a verb names: it accepts a copy of a file it does not hold, which the plan's Validate then flags against the disk.
classes.example:
o1.CreateFolder("/w")
o1.CreateFile("/w/a.txt", "alpha")
o1.CopyFile("/w/a.txt", "/w/b.txt")
? o1.Exists("/w/b.txt")
#--> 1
? o1.ContentOf("/w/b.txt")
#--> alpha
? o1.NumberOfOperations()
#--> 3

methods.name: init
methods.brief: Builds a file twin with an empty in-memory tree, a bridge to the disk and no history.

methods.name: CreateFile
methods.brief: Rehearses creating a file with its content; the disk is not touched.

parameters.name: pcPath
parameters.role: the path of the file

parameters.name: pcContent
parameters.role: the content, as text

methods.returns: the twin itself, so calls chain
notes: a path that already exists has its content replaced, without an error

methods.name: WriteFile
methods.brief: Rehearses writing content into a file; the disk is not touched.

parameters.name: pcPath
parameters.role: the path of the file

parameters.name: pcContent
parameters.role: the content, as text

methods.returns: the twin itself, so calls chain
notes: it is recorded as a write, so the narration says write rather than create

methods.name: CreateFolder
methods.brief: Rehearses creating a folder; the disk is not touched.

parameters.name: pcPath
parameters.role: the path of the folder

methods.returns: the twin itself, so calls chain
notes: the folder that holds it is not required to exist

methods.name: DeleteFile
methods.brief: Rehearses deleting a file; the disk is not touched.

parameters.name: pcPath
parameters.role: the path of the file

methods.returns: the twin itself, so calls chain
notes: an absent path is recorded and changes nothing; the plan flags the delete as destructive and Validate flags a target absent from the disk

methods.name: DeleteFolder
methods.brief: Rehearses deleting a folder; the disk is not touched.

parameters.name: pcPath
parameters.role: the path of the folder

methods.returns: the twin itself, so calls chain
warnings: the files below it stay in the twin; delete them first, as the real folder delete refuses a folder that is not empty

methods.name: CopyFile
methods.brief: Rehearses copying a file to another path; the disk is not touched.

parameters.name: pcFrom
parameters.role: the path of the file to copy

parameters.name: pcTo
parameters.role: the path of the copy

methods.returns: the twin itself, so calls chain
warnings: a source the twin does not hold makes an empty file at the destination, which the disk would refuse; Validate catches it against the disk

methods.name: MoveFile
methods.brief: Rehearses moving a file to another path; the disk is not touched.

parameters.name: pcFrom
parameters.role: the path of the file to move

parameters.name: pcTo
parameters.role: the path it moves to

methods.returns: the twin itself, so calls chain
warnings: a source the twin does not hold makes an empty file at the destination, which the disk would refuse; the plan flags a move as removing its source

methods.name: MirrorFile
methods.brief: Reads one real file into the twin, marked as mirrored, so a rehearsal starts from what the disk holds.

parameters.name: pcPath
parameters.role: the real path of the file

methods.returns: the twin itself, so calls chain
notes: it reads the disk and changes nothing; the mirrored file is not counted in the history
warnings: an absent file changes nothing

methods.name: MirrorFrom
methods.brief: Replaces the twin tree with the files of one real folder, each marked as mirrored.

parameters.name: pcDir
parameters.role: the real folder to read, one level only

methods.returns: the twin itself, so calls chain
warnings: it reads the disk and changes nothing; whatever the twin held before is dropped

methods.name: Exists
methods.brief: TRUE if the twin holds a file or folder at that path.

parameters.name: pcPath
parameters.role: the path

notes: it answers from the twin, not from the disk

methods.name: ContentOf
methods.brief: Returns the content the twin holds at that path.

parameters.name: pcPath
parameters.role: the path

methods.returns: a text; an empty text for a folder or an absent path

methods.name: SizeOf
methods.brief: Returns the size of the content the twin holds at that path, in bytes.

parameters.name: pcPath
parameters.role: the path

methods.returns: a number; 0 for a folder or an absent path

methods.name: OriginOf
methods.brief: Returns where a path of the twin came from.

parameters.name: pcPath
parameters.role: the path

methods.returns: mirrored for one read from the disk, virtual for one born in the twin; an empty text when absent

methods.name: Paths
methods.brief: Returns every path the twin holds, in the order added.

methods.name: NumberOfNodes
methods.brief: Returns how many files and folders the twin holds.

methods.name: TreeView
methods.brief: Returns the twin as text, one line per node with its type, its path and its origin.

methods.name: Show
methods.brief: Prints the number of nodes of the twin and its tree view.

classes.name: stzVirtualOperation
classes.brief: Holds one change to a system as an object, with its type, its parameters, who proposed it and why.
classes.description: A twin rehearses operations and a plan commits them, so the change is a value that can be read, narrated, scoped and audited before anything real happens. The type names the change (create_file, write_file, create_folder, delete_file, delete_folder, copy_file, move_file, set_var, unset_var, change_dir, spawn_process) and the parameters are [ key, value ] pairs. Describe writes it in plain words, Impact lists what it touches for a commit scope, and RequiredKind says what a committer must be allowed to do.
classes.example:
? o1.Describe()
#--> copy '/w/a.txt' -> '/w/b.txt'
? @@( o1.Impact() )
#--> [ "/w/a.txt", "/w/b.txt" ]
? o1.RequiredKind()
#--> effectful

methods.name: init
methods.brief: Builds one change as an object: a type and its parameters, to be rehearsed in a twin or committed through a bridge.

parameters.name: pcType
parameters.role: the kind of change, such as create_file, copy_file or set_var, folded to lower case

parameters.name: paParams
parameters.role: a list of [ key, value ] pairs

methods.name: Type
methods.brief: Returns the kind of change, in lower case.

methods.name: Params
methods.brief: Returns the parameters the operation was built with.

classes.name: stzVirtualSystem
classes.brief: Rehearses changes to a system in memory, keeps their history, and turns them into a plan; the generic core of every twin.
classes.description: A twin drives a state object that can apply an operation to itself and clone itself, and a bridge that is the only thing touching reality. ExecuteOperation applies one operation to the state and records it; UndoLast, CreateSnapshot and RollbackTo move back through the history; GenerateUpdatePlan hands the history to a plan. The twin holds no reference to reality, so nothing real changes until a plan is executed. It is domain-agnostic: use a specialization, stzVirtualFileSystem for files or stzVirtualEnvironment for variables, directory and processes.
classes.example:
o1.CreateFile("/w/a.txt", "alpha")
o1.CreateFile("/w/b.txt", "beta")
? o1.NumberOfOperations()
#--> 2
o1.UndoLast(1)
? o1.NumberOfOperations()
#--> 1
? o1.History()[1].Describe()
#--> create file '/w/a.txt' (5 bytes)

classes.name: stzVoice
classes.brief: Turns text into a sound buffer with the machine's speech engine, one language at a time, refusing rather than substituting.
classes.description: The primary verb is ToSoundOf: a voice renders to a buffer, and a buffer is a stzSound, so every verb of the sound plane then applies to speech. The sound carries the engine's own sample rate (22050 Hz here, not 48000), which is stored in a saved file too. UseLanguage tries an exact tag and then the same language with another region, and otherwise refuses and says which languages the machine has. Synthesis is under 1 percent of the output latency, so speech is late because the audio path is long, not because it is computed. Say and ToTransportOf open an audio device and were not run in this reference. The speech has not been heard by a person (UNPERCEIVED): it is checked by frame count, rate, duration and peak level.
classes.example:
? o1.IsUsable()
#--> 1
? o1.UseLanguage("de-DE")
#--> 0
? o1.UseLanguage("en-US")
#--> 1
? o1.ToSoundOf("The disk is nearly full").SampleRate()
#--> 22050

classes.name: stzVoicePool
classes.brief: Fires a sound now, again and again, without building anything: the pool is built once and mixed into one stream.
classes.description: A game fires the same footstep thirty times a minute and two overlap, and building a graph per shot would allocate inside the frame that has to draw. The pool is built once, prepared once and mixed into one stream, and firing a voice is an atomic flag the render picks up at its next block. Slots are the policy: a voice of four slots sounds four times at once and the fifth fire steals the oldest, counted and not hidden. Each voice has its own gain bus so one can be ducked with a ramp, never a jump. The pool runs on a stzSoundTransport, so its position is the plane's one device clock. There is no pitch or volume per shot and no panning. Start opens a sound card: for this reference it was never run, the example builds the pool and reads what needs no device, and nothing was heard (UNPERCEIVED).
classes.receiver: o1 = StzVoicePoolOfQ(48000) oBlip = StzSoundScoreQ().Note(880, 0.2).ToSound() o1.AddVoice(:blip, oBlip, 4) o1.AddToneVoice(:coin, :Square, 880, 0.05, 3)
classes.example:
? @@( o1.VoiceNames() )
#--> [ "blip", "coin" ]
? o1.SlotsOf(:blip)
#--> 4
? o1.SlotsOf(:coin)
#--> 3
? o1.IsStarted()
#--> 0
? o1.FiresOf(:blip)
#--> 0
o1.Fire(:blip)
? o1.LastError()
#--> Fire: call Start() first
? o1.Refusals()
#--> 1
? o1.VoiceGain(:blip)
#--> -1

methods.name: Start
methods.brief: Mixes every voice through its own gain bus, opens the device and starts the render, silent until a voice is fired.
methods.returns: the pool itself, so calls chain
notes: from here the graph shape is frozen; every voice starts spent, rendered past its longest shot and discarded, so the pool makes no noise when it opens; StartQ is the same call
warnings: not run: it opens a sound card; with no voice it counts a refusal and sets LastError to Start: the pool has no voices, which was run, and a pool that cannot start is left not started with the device error in LastError

extensions.name: StartQ
extensions.adds: does what the method does, then returns the object, so the call can be chained

methods.name: Fire
methods.brief: Sounds a voice now, returning at once; the render picks the shot up at its next block.

parameters.name: pName
parameters.role: the voice name

methods.returns: the pool itself, so calls chain; FireQ is the same call
notes: slots are taken in turn, so a voice with four slots can sound four times at once and the fifth shot steals the oldest; a steal is counted from the clock only when the slot had not finished, so a shot that lands on a spent slot is not a steal
warnings: an unknown name counts a refusal and sets LastError to no voice is named ...; a pool not started counts a refusal and sets LastError to Fire: call Start() first, both run; the started path was not run: it posts a trigger to the render thread

methods.name: SetVoiceGain
methods.brief: Ramps the gain of one voice bus, so one voice can be turned down without touching another.

parameters.name: pName
parameters.role: the voice name

parameters.name: pnGain
parameters.role: the gain to reach, 1 for unchanged

parameters.name: pnRampMs
parameters.role: the length of the ramp in milliseconds

methods.returns: the pool itself, so calls chain; SetVoiceGainQ is the same call
notes: the gain is ramped and never assigned, because a step is a click; the write is one atomic store the render reads each block, so nothing is allocated; the ramp after Start was not run
warnings: an unknown name, or a call before Start, counts a refusal and sets LastError to no voice is named ... or SetVoiceGain: the bus does not exist until Start(), both run

parameters.name: pName
parameters.role: the voice name

methods.returns: a number, between the old and the new value during a ramp; -1 for an unknown voice or before Start
notes: -1 before Start was run; read afresh from the engine, not remembered, so a guard can see a ramp both move and arrive

methods.returns: the node number; 0 for an unknown voice or before Start

methods.name: Stop
methods.brief: Stops the transport and marks the pool as not started.
methods.returns: the pool itself, so calls chain

methods.name: Transport

methods.brief: Returns the audio graph the voices are built into.

methods.name: LastError

classes.name: stzWalker
classes.brief: Walks from a start number toward an end number, taking a repeating pattern of steps.
classes.description: A stzWalker holds a start, an end and a pattern of steps; its walkables are the numbers it visits. stzListOfNumbers.Walker() builds the walker that reproduces a list: for [ 1, 2, 5, 6, 9, 10 ] the pattern is [ 1, 3 ], so from 1 it visits 1, 2, 5, 6, 9, 10. classes.name: stzWebBundle
classes.brief: Assembles a deployable web folder from wasm modules: the modules, the stz.js bridge, an HTML shell and a manifest.
classes.description: The web is a composite target, not one binary. stzBuilder compiles the wasm parts; stzWebBundle copies them into one folder together with the bridge that lets JavaScript own the linear memory and call the module's exports, a page that loads the first module and calls its stz_main, and bundle.json. Add modules by path (or hand over a stzBuilder, which is built first), set the title and the output folder, then Build. The default folder is <name>_web in the current folder.

classes.name: stzWebSocket
classes.brief: Declares a WebSocket client built on libcurl, which cannot open a connection today because libcurl is no longer loaded.
classes.description: The rest of the network layer moved to the in-tree engine, but this class still calls curl functions (curl_easy_init, curl_ws_send, curl_ws_recv) that the library does not define. Connect therefore raises error R3, no connection is ever open, and every other call answers as an unconnected client: the send and receive calls set LastError to Not connected. The callback setters store names that are never called. Use stzTcpClient for a raw socket until the class is rewired to the engine.
classes.example:
? o1.IsOpen()
#--> 0
o1.SendText("hi")
? o1.LastError()
#--> Not connected

classes.name: stzWindow
classes.brief: Opens a window where a canvas or a 3D scene is watched live, with a frame loop, keys, mouse and time built in.
classes.description: A picture saved with ToSVG or ToPNG is computed once; a window recomputes it while somebody looks, and it reports what the user did. The loop is explicit: while IsOpen, call Poll, read DeltaTime, KeyPressed or the mouse, update the picture, and call Draw. The picture goes to the screen's own texture, so no pixels travel back across the bus. Show does the whole loop for a still picture, and EachFrame runs a function once per frame. It is not a widget toolkit: it has no buttons, layout or menus. The windowing module may be absent on a headless machine, in which case building a window raises one clear error; ask StzWindowingAvailable() first, and call Free when done. This block has no run example because a window needs a screen.

classes.name: stzWiseCoderAgent
classes.brief: Holds Softanza's own wise-coder agent, which drives a goal's questions in a knowledge graph until the goal is filled or the answers run out.
classes.description: The library consumes its own agent surface here: the agent does not reimplement the elicitation loop, it drives the conversation module as an agent, with a bounded pursuit. The questions come from the gaps of a stzGoal, the answers from a function the caller supplies, and every answer is admitted into the knowledge graph the caller handed over. An empty answer stops the pursuit and leaves the gap for a person. It is the only wired agent of the roster StzOwnAgents lists; asking StzOwnAgent for a reserved one raises an error rather than returning a stub.
classes.receiver: o1 = new stzWiseCoderAgent() o2 = new stzKnowledgeGraph("menu")
classes.example:
o2.Know("margherita", "dish")
o3 = StzGoalQ().RequireEach("dish", "contains")
? o1.PursueGoal(o3, o2, func s, r { return "tomato-sauce" })[:asked]
#--> 1
? o1.Why()
#--> goal filled in 1 question(s), governed admission throughout

methods.name: Name_
methods.brief: Returns the fixed name of this agent, which marks it as owned by Softanza.

methods.name: PursueGoal
methods.brief: Asks the questions that a goal's gaps call for, in a knowledge graph, and fills them from an answer function until none are left.

parameters.role: the stzGoal to fill

parameters.name: poKB
parameters.role: the knowledge graph to ask in, which receives every admitted answer

parameters.name: fAnswerSource
parameters.role: a function of (subject, relation) returning the value as a text, or an empty text to stop

methods.returns: a hash list [ :filled, :asked, :why ]; filled is 1 when no gap remains
notes: an empty answer stops it and leaves the gap for a person: it never invents a fact; each call opens a fresh session named own-wise-coding
warnings: raises an error naming the missing argument when poKB is not a knowledge graph or poGoal is not a goal

methods.returns: a text; empty before the first PursueGoal

methods.name: Why
methods.brief: Returns the sentence that says how the last pursuit ended.
methods.returns: a text; empty before the first PursueGoal

classes.name: stzWordStream
classes.brief: Counts words over text fed in chunks, keeping only the table of distinct words in the engine, so a very large input costs only its vocabulary.
classes.description: Build one with new stzWordStream(), or StzWordStreamCSQ(1) for a case-sensitive count. Feed or FeedMany add chunks at any time; TopWords, WordsAndTheirCounts, MostFrequentWord and the totals can be asked between feeds and the feeding goes on. Words are cut by Unicode word rules (punctuation dropped, emoji not words, Hebrew and Arabic whole) and, by default, counted without regard to case. The counter lives in the engine: call Free when done. SetCaseSensitive discards what was fed, so set the case mode first.
classes.example:
o1.Feed("the cat and the hat")
? o1.TotalWords()
#--> 5
o1.Feed("THE end")
? @@( o1.TopWords(2) )
#--> [ [ "the", 3 ], [ "cat", 1 ] ]
? o1.DistinctWords()
#--> 5
o1.Free()

methods.name: init
methods.brief: Creates an empty word counter in the engine, case-insensitive by default, to be fed with chunks of text.
warnings: the counter lives in the engine until Free is called, since Ring has no destructors

methods.name: SetCaseSensitive
methods.brief: Chooses whether words that differ only by case count as different words, and starts a fresh empty counter.

parameters.name: pCaseSensitive
parameters.role: 1 to count The and the apart, 0 to fold them

methods.returns: the same object, so calls chain
notes: StzWordStreamCS(1) builds a case-sensitive one in a single call
warnings: Discards everything fed so far: call it before the first Feed; after it TotalWords answers 0

methods.name: Engine
methods.brief: Returns the engine handle of the counter, for the engine functions that take it.
notes: not meant for normal use

methods.name: Feed
methods.brief: Adds the words of a chunk of text to the counts, which accumulate over all the chunks.

parameters.name: pcChunk
parameters.role: a text

methods.returns: the same object, so calls chain
notes: FeedChunk and Add are the same method; words are cut by Unicode word rules, so punctuation is left out and emoji are not words

extensions.name: FeedMany
extensions.adds: works on a collection of items instead of one

methods.name: TopWords
methods.brief: Returns the n most frequent words fed so far, each with its count, the most frequent first.

parameters.name: n
parameters.role: how many words to return

methods.returns: a list of [ word, count ] pairs; [ ] before anything is fed
notes: with case folding a word is shown as it first appeared: feeding the cat, then The, gives the with 2

methods.name: WordsAndTheirCounts
methods.brief: Returns every different word fed so far with its count, in the order the words first appeared.
methods.returns: a list of [ word, count ] pairs
notes: the counts add up to TotalWords

methods.name: MostFrequentWords
methods.brief: Returns just the n most frequent words, without their counts, the most frequent first.

parameters.name: n
parameters.role: how many words to return

methods.name: MostFrequentWord
methods.brief: Returns the single most frequent word fed so far.
methods.returns: a text; "" before anything is fed
notes: a tie goes to the word that appeared first

methods.name: TotalWords
methods.brief: Returns how many words have been fed in all, repeats included.
notes: NumberOfWords is the same method; it answers 0 after Free

methods.name: DistinctWords
methods.brief: Returns how many different words have been fed.
notes: VocabularySize and NumberOfDistinctWords are the same method

methods.name: Free
methods.brief: Releases the engine counter, which Ring cannot do by itself; safe to call twice.
notes: afterwards the queries answer 0 or [ ] and Feed has no effect: do not use the object again

methods.name: Release
methods.brief: Releases the engine counter, exactly as Free does.

classes.name: stzWorkerPool
classes.brief: Holds worker profiles, each with its own budget of slots, and runs or queues work against them so a busy kind never starves another.
classes.description: Work is sent to the profile it targets: the profile runs it at once when a slot is free, queues it when not, and sheds it when a bounded queue is full. That is load isolation. A heavy batch of one profile leaves the slots of every other profile alone. Profiles come from a facet catalog the pool owns (AddFacet, SeedAllFacets) or are declared ad hoc (AddProfile). The pool is in-process: work runs in the calling process and no worker process is started.
classes.example:
o1.AddProfile("nlp", [ :sentiment, :classify ], 2)
o1.AddProfile("vision", [ :ocr ], 1)
? o1.Tags()[2]
#--> vision
? o1.ProfileFor(:classify)
#--> nlp
? o1.Acquire("vision")
#--> 1
? o1.Dispatch("vision", func { return 1 })[:queued]
#--> 1
? o1.Dispatch("nlp", func { return 6 * 7 })[:result]
#--> 42

classes.name: stzWorkerProfile
classes.brief: Declares a kind of worker as a tag, the capabilities it serves and a budget of concurrent slots.
classes.description: Specialization is a budget, not a subclass: the resident engine is shared, so what separates one kind of worker from another is only what it serves and how much of the machine it may use at once. A profile admits work while a slot is free and refuses it otherwise, counting every decision, which isolates a heavy profile from a light one. A profile backed by an outside tool, such as OCR, is marked polyglot. A profile only declares and counts: it never starts a process.
classes.example:
? o1.Handles("ENTITIES")
#--> 1
? o1.Acquire()
#--> 1
? o1.Acquire()
#--> 1
? o1.Acquire()
#--> 0
? o1.Narrate()
#--> profile nlp [2/2 slots, serves sentiment, entities]

classes.name: stzWorkflow
classes.brief: Models a business process as steps and arrows, or as a state machine, with actors, durations and SLAs, and reports its critical path, bottlenecks and violations.
classes.description: A workflow is a diagram of one of three types. A sequential workflow is built from steps (AddStepXTT) joined by Then, given actors with AssignStepTo and hours with SetStepDuration and SetStepSLA; it then answers CriticalPath, Bottlenecks, SLAViolations and the three Validate methods, which return the house verdict shape. A state machine is built from AddState and AddTransition, and SetExceptionEvents marks the transitions that mean trouble. A bpmn workflow takes the BPMN notation, and ExpandEndingsPerArrival gives each arrow into an end its own marker. ToWorkflow writes the sequential part as .stzflow text and ImportFlow reads it back. The View methods display the diagram and were not run for this reference. Known today: CriticalPath raises an error when no path has a duration above zero, and for every state machine.
classes.example:
o1.AddStep_("pack")
o1.AddStep_("ship")
o1.Then("pack", "ship")
o1.SetStepDuration("pack", 4)
o1.SetStepSLA("pack", 3)
o1.SetStepDuration("ship", 8)
? o1.TotalDuration()
#--> 12
? o1.SLAViolations()[1][:overrun]
#--> 1
? o1.CriticalPath()[:path][2]
#--> ship

methods.name: init
methods.brief: Builds an empty sequential workflow diagram with the given id, set to be judged by five validators including deadlock and SLA.

parameters.name: pcId

parameters.name: pcTo

parameters.name: pcEvent

methods.brief: TRUE if the transition between two states on an event was marked exceptional.

parameters.name: pcTo
parameters.role: the state it enters

parameters.role: the event

methods.name: State
methods.brief: Returns one state as a hash list of its id, label, isInitial, isFinal and properties.

parameters.name: pcId

methods.brief: Returns all the states in the order they were added.
