methods.name: AddActor
methods.brief: Adds a person or system that can carry out steps, with a role.

parameters.name: pcId
parameters.role: the actor's id

parameters.name: pcName
parameters.role: the actor's name

parameters.name: pcRole
parameters.role: the role they play

methods.name: AssignStepTo
methods.brief: Assigns a step to an actor.

parameters.name: pcStepId
parameters.role: the id of the step

parameters.name: pcActorId
parameters.role: the id of the actor

notes: the actor is not checked to exist

methods.name: Actor
methods.brief: Returns one actor as a hash list of id, name and role.

parameters.name: pcId
parameters.role: the actor's id

methods.returns: a hash list; an empty list for an unknown id

methods.name: Actors
methods.brief: Returns every actor added to the workflow, in the order they were added.

methods.name: SetStepSLA
methods.brief: Sets the longest time a step may take, in hours.

parameters.name: pcStepId
parameters.role: the id of the step

parameters.name: nHours
parameters.role: the allowed time in hours

notes: 0 means no limit

methods.name: SetStepDuration
methods.brief: Sets how long a step takes, in hours.

parameters.name: pcStepId
parameters.role: the id of the step

parameters.name: nHours
parameters.role: the time taken in hours

methods.name: SLAViolations
methods.brief: Returns the steps whose duration exceeds their SLA.
methods.returns: a list of hash lists with the keys step, sla, actual and overrun; empty when none
notes: a step with an SLA of 0 is never a violation

methods.name: SetOrgChart
methods.brief: Links an organisation chart to the workflow, which WorkloadByPosition needs.

parameters.name: poOrgChart
parameters.role: the stzOrgChart to link

notes: the chart is not queried: it only switches workloads on, and the positions come from MapRoleToPosition

methods.name: MapRoleToPosition
methods.brief: Maps a role to a position id of the org chart.

parameters.name: pcRole
parameters.role: the role of actors

parameters.name: pcPositionId
parameters.role: the position id

methods.brief: Returns the position that carries out a step, through the step's actor and that actor's role.

parameters.name: pcStepId
parameters.role: the id of the step

methods.returns: a text; empty when the step is unknown, has no actor, or its role is not mapped

methods.name: WorkloadByPosition
methods.brief: Counts, for each position, the steps assigned to it and their total duration.
methods.returns: a list of hash lists with the keys position, stepCount and totalDuration; empty when no org chart is linked

methods.name: TotalDuration
methods.brief: Returns the sum of the durations of all steps, in hours.
notes: it adds the steps of every branch, so it is not the elapsed time of the process

methods.name: CriticalPath
methods.brief: Returns the longest path through a sequential workflow by total duration.
methods.returns: a hash list with the keys path, a list of step ids, and duration
notes: ViewCriticalPath fails the same way
warnings: it raises error R24 (uninitialized variable _accriticalpath_) today when no path has a duration above 0, as for an empty workflow, a workflow with no durations set and every state machine; the variable is assigned only inside the longest- path test

methods.name: AllPathsFromStartToEnd
methods.brief: Returns every path from a step with no incoming arrow to a step with no outgoing arrow.
methods.returns: a list of paths, each a list of step ids; empty for a workflow that is a cycle

methods.name: Bottlenecks

methods.name: ValidateBottleneck

methods.returns: a hash list with the keys status, domain, ruleGroup, issueCount, issues and affectedNodes

methods.name: ViewCriticalPath

methods.name: ViewBottlenecks
methods.brief: Highlights the bottleneck steps and shows the diagram with a subtitle that counts them.
warnings: it displays the diagram on the screen, which was not done

methods.name: ViewSLAViolations
methods.brief: Highlights the steps over their SLA and shows the diagram with a subtitle that counts them.

methods.name: ViewByRole

methods.name: ToWorkflow

notes: only a sequential workflow lists steps and arrows: a state machine gives its header and actors alone, and a bpmn workflow its header and actors, so its states and transitions are not written

methods.name: ImportFlow
methods.brief: Reads a .stzflow text, or a file whose name ends in .stzflow, and merges its steps, durations, SLAs, arrows and actors into this workflow.

parameters.name: pSource
parameters.role: the .stzflow text, or the path of a .stzflow file

notes: the loaded steps are added to the steps already present

methods.name: LoadFlow
methods.brief: Reads a .stzflow text or file into this workflow, exactly as ImportFlow does.

parameters.name: pSource
parameters.role: the .stzflow text, or the path of a .stzflow file

classes.name: stzWorkflowSimulation
classes.brief: Collects changes proposed to a workflow, a quicker step, a moved step, steps side by side, and shows their effect on a copy.
classes.description: The simulation is built over a workflow and keeps its own copy of it, so the workflow it was built from is never touched. OptimizeStep, ReassignStep and ParallelizeSteps each record one change, checked before it is stored, and Changes returns what was recorded. Apply returns a copy of the workflow with the new durations, the new actors and the new order of the parallel steps in place. The three recording methods return nothing; OptimizeStepQ, ReassignStepQ and ParallelizeStepsQ record the same change and return the simulation, so that calls can be chained. A chain written as one expression records into the simulation it started from, and a Changes or Apply at its end sees every change of the chain; a result kept in a variable is a copy, and from then on the copy and the simulation it came from no longer share their changes, each holds those recorded through its own calls. A simulation built with new stzWorkflowSimulation and no parentheses has no workflow, and each of the three methods then raises an error saying so; with empty parentheses the inherited init raises error R19.
classes.receiver: oWf = new stzWorkflow("order") oWf.AddStep_("pack") oWf.SetStepDuration("pack", 8) o1 = new stzWorkflowSimulation(oWf)
classes.example:
o1.OptimizeStep("pack", 5)
? len(o1.Changes())
#--> 1
oRes = o1.Apply()
? oRes.TotalDuration()
#--> 5
? oWf.TotalDuration()
#--> 8

methods.name: init
methods.brief: Builds a simulation over a copy of a workflow, with no change recorded yet.

parameters.name: poWorkflow
parameters.role: the workflow to try changes on, a stzWorkflow

notes: the simulation keeps a copy, so changing the workflow afterwards does not reach it
warnings: anything that is not a stzWorkflow raises an error saying a stzWorkflow is needed

methods.name: OptimizeStep
methods.brief: Records a new duration for a step, to be tried without changing the workflow.

parameters.name: pcStepId
parameters.role: the id of the step to speed up or slow down

parameters.name: nNewDuration
parameters.role: the duration to give it, in hours, a number of 0 or more

methods.returns: nothing; the change is added to the recorded list; use OptimizeStepQ to chain
notes: the id is checked against the steps of the workflow, in the way the workflow itself compares ids, and a failed call records nothing
warnings: an unknown step, a duration that is not a number or is below 0, or a simulation with no workflow raises an error

extensions.name: OptimizeStepQ
extensions.adds: does what the method does, then returns the object, so the call can be chained

methods.name: ReassignStep
methods.brief: Records a move of a step from one actor to another, to be tried without changing the workflow.

parameters.name: pcStepId
parameters.role: the id of the step to move

parameters.name: pcFromActor
parameters.role: the actor it leaves, a text that is not empty

parameters.name: pcToActor
parameters.role: the actor it goes to, a text that is not empty

methods.returns: nothing; the change is added to the recorded list; use ReassignStepQ to chain
notes: the step is checked to exist, the actors are not, as AssignStepTo does not check them; the actor it leaves is recorded as given and is not compared with the actor the step has now, and only the actor it goes to is applied
warnings: an unknown step, an actor that is not a text or is empty, or a simulation with no workflow raises an error, and a failed call records nothing

extensions.name: ReassignStepQ
extensions.adds: does what the method does, then returns the object, so the call can be chained

methods.name: ParallelizeSteps
methods.brief: Records that steps run side by side instead of one after the other, to be tried without changing the workflow.

parameters.name: pacStepIds
parameters.role: the ids of the steps to run in parallel, a list of at least two texts, in any order

methods.returns: nothing; the change is added to the recorded list; use ParallelizeStepsQ to chain
notes: Apply puts the steps in the same place of the flow: the arrows between two of them are removed, each of them then waits for every step that came before any of them, and every step that came after any of them waits for all of them; an arrow that is there already is kept as it is and never doubled, so a group that already runs side by side changes nothing, and the total of the durations never changes, only the longest path does
warnings: a list of fewer than two steps, a step that is listed twice or is unknown, or a simulation with no workflow raises an error, and a failed call records nothing; the shape of the flow is checked only by Apply, which refuses steps that are linked through another step

extensions.name: ParallelizeStepsQ
extensions.adds: does what the method does, then returns the object, so the call can be chained

methods.name: Changes
methods.brief: Returns the changes recorded so far, in the order they were recorded.
methods.returns: a list of hash lists, each with the key type, optimize_step, reassign_step or parallelize, and the keys of that change: step and newDuration, step, from and to, or steps; empty when nothing was recorded
notes: the list is a copy, so changing it does not change the simulation

methods.name: Apply
methods.brief: Returns a copy of the workflow with the recorded durations, actors and parallel steps in place, leaving the original as it was.
methods.returns: a stzWorkflow; the copy of the workflow as it was when the simulation was built when nothing was recorded
notes: the changes are applied in the order they were recorded, so the last change to a step wins, and a group of parallel steps is put in place on the flow that the changes before it left
warnings: a simulation with no workflow raises an error; so does a group of parallel steps that are linked through other steps, with the message can't parallelize steps that are linked through other steps, and then no copy is returned, the workflow and the simulation are as they were, and the recorded changes are kept

classes.name: stzWorldGraph
classes.brief: Loads the declared world of a project, its symbols and the references between them, and says whether every reference resolves.
classes.description: A world artifact is one derived JSON file with two flat tables: the symbols each court declares, with kind, name and span, and the references between them. The class reads it and never writes it, collects every refusal as a diagnostic instead of raising on the first, and hands back an ordinary stzGraph with one node per symbol and one edge per referenced pair. Kinds are a closed set, ids are the lower-case kind:name, and two symbols that differ only by case are refused. IsLawful is the gate. The class is not loaded by stzlib.ring: load graph/stzWorldGraph.ring first.
classes.example:
? o1.World()
#--> bank
? o1.SymbolCount()
#--> 3
? @@( o1.NamesOfKind(:entity) )
#--> [ "member", "deposit" ]
? len(o1.ReferencesTo("entity:deposit"))
#--> 2
? len(o1.Graph().Edges())
#--> 1
? o1.IsLawful()
#--> 1

methods.name: init
methods.brief: Loads a world artifact, the declared symbols and references of a project, into a stzGraph and collects every refusal.

parameters.name: pSource
parameters.role: the path of a world.json file, or the JSON text itself starting with a brace

methods.returns: nothing; the object is built and never raises on a bad artifact, it records diagnostics
notes: the class is not loaded by stzlib.ring: load graph/stzWorldGraph.ring first; a contract other than 1.0 adds CONTRACT_MISMATCH and the symbols are still read
warnings: text that is not JSON, an empty or unreadable path, and a value that is not text are not raised: they leave the graph empty and add an MALFORMED_WORLD or EMPTY_WORLD diagnostic

methods.name: World
methods.brief: Returns the name of the world the artifact declares.
methods.returns: the name as text; an empty text when the artifact has none or was refused

methods.name: ContractVersion
methods.brief: Returns the contract version the artifact was emitted against.
methods.returns: the version as text, such as 1.0
notes: the loader implements 1.0

methods.name: Graph
methods.brief: Returns the world as an ordinary stzGraph, one node per symbol and one edge per referenced pair.
notes: each node id is the lower-case kind:name; two references between one pair of symbols make ONE edge whose label is the first reference's kind and whose refs property holds every row

methods.name: Symbols
methods.brief: Returns every lawful symbol, each with id, kind, name, type, file, line and rationale.
methods.returns: a list of hash lists in the order they were declared
notes: a refused symbol, unknown kind, bad name or duplicate, is not in it

methods.name: SymbolCount
methods.brief: Returns how many lawful symbols were read.

methods.name: Refs
methods.brief: Returns every lawful reference, each with from, to, kind, file and line.
methods.returns: a list of hash lists in the order they were declared; both ends are lower case
notes: a reference whose end nothing declares is refused and is not in it

methods.name: RefCount
methods.brief: Returns how many lawful references were read.
notes: two references between one pair count twice, though the graph holds one edge for them

methods.name: HasSymbol
methods.brief: TRUE if a symbol with an id exists in the world.

parameters.name: pcId
parameters.role: the id as kind:name, matched without regard to case

methods.name: Symbol
methods.brief: Returns one symbol by its id.

parameters.name: pcId
parameters.role: the id as kind:name, matched without regard to case

methods.returns: a hash list with id, kind, name, type, file, line and rationale; [ ] when the world has no such symbol

methods.name: NamesOfKind
methods.brief: Returns the names of every symbol of one kind.

parameters.name: pcKind
parameters.role: the kind, such as entity or flow, in any letter case

methods.returns: a list of text in declaration order; [ ] for a kind with none
notes: the names are without the kind prefix

methods.name: IdsOfKind
methods.brief: Returns the ids of every symbol of one kind.

parameters.name: pcKind
parameters.role: the kind, such as entity or flow, in any letter case

methods.returns: a list of text such as entity:member, in declaration order; [ ] for a kind with none

methods.name: Kinds
methods.brief: Returns the kinds of symbol that the world actually uses.
methods.returns: a list of text, each kind once, in the order first met
notes: the closed set of kinds is entity, field, type, actor, norm, flow, screen, process, element and state

methods.name: ZuiSymbolTable
methods.brief: Returns the four lists of names that the zui verifier reads for its deeper checks.
methods.returns: a hash list with the keys entities, actors, state and elements, each a list of names
notes: a world with no symbol of a kind gives [ ] for it

methods.name: ReferencesFrom
methods.brief: Returns every reference site that leaves a symbol.

parameters.name: pcId
parameters.role: the id as kind:name, matched without regard to case

methods.returns: a list of reference rows, so two references to one target are two rows; [ ] when none

methods.name: ReferencesTo
methods.brief: Returns every reference site that arrives at a symbol.

parameters.name: pcId
parameters.role: the id as kind:name, matched without regard to case

methods.returns: a list of reference rows; [ ] when none

methods.name: Diagnostics
methods.brief: Returns every refusal and warning found while loading, in the order found.
methods.returns: a list of hash lists, each a diagnostic with code, severity, message, span, cites and language world
notes: the codes are EMPTY_WORLD, MALFORMED_WORLD, CONTRACT_MISMATCH, UNKNOWN_SYMBOL_KIND, MALFORMED_NAME, MISSING_SPAN (a warning), DUPLICATE_SYMBOL, UNKNOWN_REFERENCE_KIND and DANGLING_REFERENCE

methods.name: ErrorCount
methods.brief: Returns how many diagnostics have severity error.
notes: a MISSING_SPAN warning does not count

methods.name: IsLawful
methods.brief: TRUE if loading raised no diagnostic of severity error.
notes: it is the gate a build reads: every reference resolved and no symbol refused

classes.name: stzXml
classes.brief: Holds an XML document as text and reads it by path, with the parsing done by the engine.
classes.description: Reach for it to read values out of an XML document without walking a tree: TextAt, NumberAt and AttributeAt take a path such as library/book[2]/title (names joined by /, an optional [n] index counted from 1, no namespace prefix). NodeQ returns a node that remembers a path, so reads can go deeper step by step. The object keeps only the text and parses it again at each read. A document with a DOCTYPE or an ENTITY declaration is refused on purpose, which closes XXE: IsValid answers 0 and every read answers the empty text. To build XML rather than read it, use stzXmlBuilder; its values are escaped.
classes.example:
? o1.Root()
#--> library
? o1.NumberOf("library/book")
#--> 2
? o1.TextAt("library/book[2]/title")
#--> Emma
? o1.AttributeAt("library/book[2]", "id")
#--> b2
? o1.NodeQ("library/book[1]").NumberOf("price")
#--> 1

methods.name: init
methods.brief: Builds a document object from XML text; the text is kept as given and parsed again at every read.

parameters.name: pcText
parameters.role: the XML document as text

notes: text that is not XML is accepted too: the object is built and IsValid answers 0

methods.name: Content
methods.brief: Returns the XML text the object was built from, unchanged.

methods.name: Text
methods.brief: Returns the XML text the object was built from, unchanged.
notes: it is the same text as Content, not the text inside the elements; use TextAt for that

methods.name: IsValid
methods.brief: Returns TRUE if the engine accepts the text as one well-formed XML document.
notes: a document with a DOCTYPE or an ENTITY declaration is refused on purpose (it closes XXE), so it answers FALSE, as does an unclosed tag or plain text

methods.name: Root
methods.brief: Returns the name of the root element, or the empty text when the document is not valid.

extensions.name: RootQ
extensions.adds: does what the method does, then returns the object, so the call can be chained

methods.name: Size
methods.brief: Returns the length of the XML text in bytes.

methods.name: TextAt
methods.brief: Returns the text of the element at a path; the empty text when there is no such element or it holds only child elements.

parameters.name: pcPath
parameters.role: a path of element names joined by /, with an optional [n] index counted from 1, such as library/book[2]/title

notes: without an index the first match is read; a namespace prefix is not written in a path (use note, not ns:note); & is read back as &

methods.name: NumberAt
methods.brief: Returns the text of the element at a path read as a number; 0 when there is no element or it is empty.

parameters.name: pcPath
parameters.role: a path, as for TextAt

notes: text that is not a number raises the error Invalid numeric string

methods.name: AttributeAt
methods.brief: Returns the value of one attribute of the element at a path; the empty text when it is absent.

parameters.name: pcPath
parameters.role: a path, as for TextAt

parameters.name: pcName
parameters.role: the attribute name

notes: library/book reads the first book, library/book[2] the second

methods.name: NamespaceAt
methods.brief: Returns the namespace URI that applies to the element at a path; the empty text when there is none.

parameters.name: pcPath
parameters.role: a path, as for TextAt

notes: a path is written without the prefix: library/note finds an element written ns:note and answers its URI

methods.name: NumberOf
methods.brief: Returns how many elements match a path.

parameters.name: pcPath
parameters.role: a path, as for TextAt

notes: library/book counts the books under library; library/book/title counts only the titles of the first book

methods.name: Has
methods.brief: Returns TRUE if at least one element matches the path.

parameters.name: pcPath
parameters.role: a path, as for TextAt

methods.name: ChildrenOf
methods.brief: Returns the names of the child elements of the element at a path, in document order, repeats included.

parameters.name: pcPath
parameters.role: a path, as for TextAt

methods.returns: a list of texts; empty when there is none
notes: library with two books and a note gives ["book","book","note"]; a prefix is dropped from the names

methods.name: TextsAt
methods.brief: Returns the text of each element matching a path, as a list.

parameters.name: pcPath
parameters.role: the path of a repeated element, without an index

notes: it indexes the LAST step, so library/book/title gives only the first book's title; to read all titles walk NodesQ("library/book"); a path with [n] gives one item; elements that hold only children give empty texts

methods.name: NodeQ
methods.brief: Returns a node object for the element at a path, to read it and its descendants with shorter paths.

parameters.name: pcPath
parameters.role: a path, as for TextAt

notes: the node only remembers the document and the path, so it is also built for a path that matches nothing (Exists answers 0)

methods.name: NodesQ
methods.brief: Returns one node object for each element matching a path, in document order.

parameters.name: pcPath
parameters.role: the path of a repeated element, without an index

methods.returns: a list of stzXmlNode; empty when none
notes: library/book gives nodes with paths library/book[1] and library/book[2]

methods.name: Pretty
methods.brief: Returns the document laid out with two spaces of indent per level and one element per line.
methods.returns: a text; empty when the document is not valid
notes: it ends with a line break; text and attributes are kept, and & stays escaped

extensions.name: PrettyQ
extensions.adds: does what the method does, then returns the object, so the call can be chained

methods.name: SaveTo
methods.brief: Writes the XML text, as given, to a file and returns the object.

parameters.name: pcPath
parameters.role: the file to write, which is replaced if it exists

notes: it writes the original text, not the pretty form; the folder must exist

methods.name: Show
methods.brief: Prints the document, laid out as Pretty does, to the console.

methods.name: ToStzString
methods.brief: Returns the XML text as a stzString object, to use the string methods on it.

classes.name: stzXmlBuilder
classes.brief: Builds an XML document element by element, escaping every value so a value cannot change the shape of the document.
classes.description: Reach for it instead of pasting strings: the values given to AddElement and SetAttribute are escaped, so & and < stay text. Open and Close nest elements, and Content gives the finished text, or raises an error while an element is still open. Element and attribute names are written as given and are not checked. The Q forms (AddElementQ, OpenQ, CloseQ) return the builder so calls can be chained; the plain forms return nothing.
classes.example:
o1.AddElement("name", "A & B")
o1.Open("items")
o1.AddElementXT("item", "pen", [ [ "qty", "2" ] ])
o1.Close()
? o1.Content()
#--> <shop><name>A & B</name><items><item qty="2">pen</item></items></shop>

methods.name: init
methods.brief: Starts a document with the given root element and nothing inside it; an empty name raises an error.

parameters.name: pcRootName
parameters.role: the name of the root element

notes: the name is trimmed; the error text is stzXmlBuilder: a root element name is required.

methods.name: SetAttribute
methods.brief: Adds an attribute to the root element; the value is escaped.

parameters.name: pcName
parameters.role: the attribute name

parameters.name: pcValue
parameters.role: the attribute value, as text

methods.returns: nothing; the root gains the attribute
notes: it always lands on the root, whatever is open; a name used twice gives the attribute twice

extensions.name: SetAttributeQ
extensions.adds: does what the method does, then returns the object, so the call can be chained

methods.name: AddElement
methods.brief: Adds a leaf element with a text inside the element now open; the text is escaped, so & becomes & and < becomes <.

parameters.name: pcName
parameters.role: the element name

parameters.name: pcValue
parameters.role: the text inside

notes: the element name itself is written as given, not escaped

extensions.name: AddElementQ
extensions.adds: does what the method does, then returns the object, so the call can be chained

extensions.name: AddElementXT
extensions.adds: the extended form: more parameters than the base method

methods.name: AddEmptyElement
methods.brief: Adds an element with no content, written as <name/>, inside the element now open.

parameters.name: pcName
parameters.role: the element name

extensions.name: AddEmptyElementQ
extensions.adds: does what the method does, then returns the object, so the call can be chained

methods.name: Open
methods.brief: Adds an opening tag; every element added until Close goes inside it.

parameters.name: pcName
parameters.role: the element name

notes: Content raises an error while an element is still open

extensions.name: OpenQ
extensions.adds: does what the method does, then returns the object, so the call can be chained

extensions.name: OpenXTQ
extensions.adds: the extended form: more parameters than the base method; does what the method does, then returns the object, so the call can be chained

methods.name: Close
methods.brief: Closes the element opened last.
notes: with nothing open it raises the error stzXmlBuilder.Close: nothing is open.

extensions.name: CloseQ
extensions.adds: does what the method does, then returns the object, so the call can be chained

methods.name: NumberOfOpenElements
methods.brief: Returns how many elements are open and not yet closed.

methods.name: Content
methods.brief: Returns the finished document: the root with its attributes and everything added.
notes: it raises the error stzXmlBuilder: n element(s) still open -- Close them first. while an element is open

methods.name: XmlQ
methods.brief: Returns the finished document as a stzXml object, to be read or pretty-printed.
notes: it raises the same error as Content while an element is open

methods.name: Show
methods.brief: Prints the finished document to the console on one line.
notes: it raises the same error as Content while an element is open

classes.name: stzXmlNode
classes.brief: Points at one element of an XML document by its path, and reads the element and its descendants.
classes.description: A node holds the document text and the path that reaches the element, nothing else, so it stays valid and can be chained: NodeQ(...) on a node adds to its path. It is normally made by stzXml.NodeQ or NodesQ. Reads that find nothing answer the empty text or 0, and Exists tells whether the element is really there. Number raises an error on text that is not a number.
classes.example:
? o1.Path()
#--> library/book
? o1.Attribute("id")
#--> b1
? o1.TextAt("title")
#--> Dune
? o1.NodeQ("price").Number()
#--> 12

methods.name: init
methods.brief: Builds a node object bound to a document text and a path; nothing is checked at once.

parameters.name: pcText
parameters.role: the XML document as text

parameters.name: pcPath
parameters.role: the path of the element, such as library/book[2]

notes: normally made by NodeQ or NodesQ of stzXml rather than by hand

methods.name: Path
methods.brief: Returns the path this node was made with.

methods.name: Exists
methods.brief: Returns TRUE if an element exists at the node path.

methods.name: Name
methods.brief: Returns the element name, which is the last step of the path without its [n] index.
notes: it comes from the path alone, so a path matching nothing still has a name

methods.name: Text
methods.brief: Returns the text of the element; the empty text when there is none or it holds only child elements.
notes: & is read back as &

methods.name: Number
methods.brief: Returns the text of the element read as a number; 0 when it is empty or absent.
notes: text that is not a number raises the error Invalid numeric string

methods.name: Namespace
methods.brief: Returns the namespace URI that applies to the element; the empty text when there is none.

methods.name: Attribute
methods.brief: Returns the value of one attribute of the element; the empty text when it is absent.

parameters.name: pcName
parameters.role: the attribute name

methods.name: ChildNames
methods.brief: Returns the names of the child elements, in document order, repeats included.

methods.name: TextAt
methods.brief: Returns the text of a descendant, found by a path read from this node.

parameters.name: pcRelative
parameters.role: the path below this node, such as title or author/name

methods.returns: a text; empty when there is none
notes: the relative path is added to the node path with a /, so it works for any depth

methods.name: AttributeAt
methods.brief: Returns the value of an attribute of a descendant, found by a path read from this node.

parameters.name: pcRelative
parameters.role: the path below this node

parameters.name: pcName
parameters.role: the attribute name

methods.name: NumberOf
methods.brief: Returns how many descendants match a path read from this node.

parameters.name: pcRelative
parameters.role: the path below this node

methods.name: NodeQ
methods.brief: Returns a node object for a descendant, so reads can go deeper step by step.

parameters.name: pcRelative
parameters.role: the path below this node

notes: it is also built for a path that matches nothing

methods.name: NodesQ
methods.brief: Returns one node object for each descendant matching a path, in document order.

parameters.name: pcRelative
parameters.role: the path below this node, without an index

notes: the paths of the nodes get an index: library/book[1]/title[1]

methods.name: DocumentQ
methods.brief: Returns a document object for the whole text this node belongs to.

methods.name: Show
methods.brief: Prints the node path and its text to the console.

classes.name: stzYielder
classes.brief: Runs map, filter and reduce steps over a list, each chosen by the name of an operation, with the work done in the engine.
classes.description: Reach for it to transform, select or fold a list without writing a loop: Map applies one named operation to every item, Filter keeps the items that pass a named test, Reduce folds the list to one value. The result of Map and Filter is a new list and the held list is unchanged, unless the Q form (MapQ, FilterQ) is used, which keeps the result and returns the object for chaining. A name that is not known does nothing and raises no error. MapIndexed is broken today (it answers the text <list> for each item).
classes.example:
? @@( o1.Map(:Abs) )
#--> [ 1, 2, 3, 4, 5 ]
? @@( o1.Filter(:IsPositive) )
#--> [ 1, 3, 5 ]
? o1.Reduce(:Sum)
#--> 3
? @@( o1.MapFiltered(:IsPositive, :Square) )
#--> [ 1, 9, 25 ]

methods.name: init
methods.brief: Builds a pipeline over a list; any value that is not a list is ignored and the content stays empty.

parameters.name: paList
parameters.role: the list to run the pipeline over

notes: a list argument is stored as given; the operations never change it

methods.name: Content
methods.brief: Returns the list the pipeline holds now.
notes: it shows the effect of the Q forms (MapQ, FilterQ), which replace the content

methods.name: SetContent
methods.brief: Replaces the held list; a value that is not a list is ignored and the old content stays.

parameters.name: paList
parameters.role: the new list

methods.name: NumberOfItems
methods.brief: Returns how many items the held list has.

methods.name: Map
methods.brief: Returns a new list with one named operation applied to every item; the held list is not changed.

parameters.name: pcOp
parameters.role: the operation: :Abs, :Negate, :Double, :Square, :TypeName, :ToString, :ToInt, :ToFloat, :StrLen, :StrUpper, :StrLower, :StrTrim, :StrReverse, :Increment, :Decrement, :IsEven, :Sign (or its code 0-16)

methods.returns: a list of the same length; the content unchanged when the operation name is unknown
notes: an operation that does not suit an item (:Abs on text) leaves the item as it is, and an unknown name returns the content without any message

extensions.name: MapQ
extensions.adds: does what the method does, then returns the object, so the call can be chained

methods.name: MapIndexed
methods.brief: Returns the text <list> for every item today, instead of applying an operation together with each item position.

parameters.name: pcOp
parameters.role: the operation name, as for Map

methods.returns: a list of texts, each the text <list>
notes: do not rely on it until it answers real values
warnings: defect: the result holds the text "<list>" in place of the values, for every operation tried (:Square, :Abs, :Negate, :Increment) and every input; the engine call returns its items in a form the Ring side shows only as that text

extensions.name: MapIndexedQ
extensions.adds: does what the method does, then returns the object, so the call can be chained

methods.name: Filter
methods.brief: Returns a new list of the items for which a named test is true; the held list is not changed.

parameters.name: pcOp
parameters.role: the test: :IsString, :IsNumber, :IsInt, :IsFloat, :IsBool, :IsNull, :IsList, :IsPositive, :IsNegative, :IsZero, :IsNonZero, :IsEmpty, :IsNotEmpty, :IsEven, :IsOdd, :IsTrue, :IsFalse (or its code 0-16)

methods.returns: a list, shorter or equal; the whole list when the test name is unknown
notes: an unknown name returns the content unchanged, without a message; the empty text counts as a string and as empty

extensions.name: FilterQ
extensions.adds: does what the method does, then returns the object, so the call can be chained

methods.name: Reduce
methods.brief: Folds the whole list to one value with a named operation.

parameters.name: pcOp
parameters.role: the operation: :Sum, :Product, :Min, :Max, :Count, :CountStrings, :CountNumbers, :Concat, :AnyTrue, :AllTrue (or its code 0-9)

methods.returns: a number, or 0 when the list is empty or the name is unknown
notes: an empty list answers 0 for every operation, including Product, Min and Max

methods.name: ReduceConcat
methods.brief: Joins every item, written as text, into one text with the separator between them.

parameters.name: pcSep
parameters.role: the text put between two items

notes: numbers are written as text; an empty list gives the empty text

methods.name: MapFiltered
methods.brief: Returns the items that pass a test, each transformed, in one pass; the held list is not changed.

parameters.name: pcFilterOp
parameters.role: the test, as for Filter

parameters.name: pcTransformOp
parameters.role: the operation applied to the survivors, as for Map

methods.returns: a list; the content unchanged when either name is unknown
notes: the test runs first: [1,-2,3,-4,5] with :IsPositive and :Square gives [1, 9, 25]

extensions.name: MapFilteredQ
extensions.adds: does what the method does, then returns the object, so the call can be chained

methods.name: CountWhere
methods.brief: Returns how many items pass a named test.

parameters.name: pcOp
parameters.role: the test, as for Filter

methods.returns: a number; 0 when the test name is unknown

methods.name: Abs
methods.brief: Returns the list with every number replaced by its absolute value; the held list is not changed.
methods.returns: a list of the same length
notes: text items stay as they are

methods.name: Negate
methods.brief: Returns the list with every number given the opposite sign; the held list is not changed.
methods.returns: a list of the same length

methods.name: DoubleValues
methods.brief: Returns the list with every number multiplied by two; the held list is not changed.
methods.returns: a list of the same length

methods.name: Square
methods.brief: Returns the list with every number multiplied by itself; the held list is not changed.
methods.returns: a list of the same length

methods.name: TypeNames
methods.brief: Returns the type of every item as a word: int, float, string or list.
methods.returns: a list of texts, same length

methods.name: StringLengths
methods.brief: Returns the length of every text item; a number item answers 0.
methods.returns: a list of numbers, same length

methods.name: Uppercase
methods.brief: Returns the list with every text item in capitals; numbers stay as they are.
methods.returns: a list of the same length
notes: it works on bytes, so a letter outside ASCII is not changed

methods.name: Lowercase
methods.brief: Returns the list with every text item in small letters; numbers stay as they are.
methods.returns: a list of the same length
notes: it works on bytes, so a letter outside ASCII is not changed

methods.name: Trimmed
methods.brief: Returns the list with the spaces cut from both ends of every text item.
methods.returns: a list of the same length

methods.name: Reversed
methods.brief: Returns the list with the characters of every text item in reverse order; the order of the items is not changed.
methods.returns: a list of the same length
notes: it reverses each item, not the list: " Hello" becomes "olleH "

methods.name: Signs
methods.brief: Returns the sign of every number: 1, -1 or 0.
methods.returns: a list of numbers, same length

methods.name: Strings
methods.brief: Returns only the text items, the empty text included.

methods.name: Numbers
methods.brief: Returns only the number items.

methods.name: Positives
methods.brief: Returns only the numbers above zero.

methods.name: Negatives
methods.brief: Returns only the numbers below zero.

methods.name: Evens
methods.brief: Returns only the even numbers; zero counts as even.

methods.name: Odds
methods.brief: Returns only the odd numbers.

methods.name: NonEmpty
methods.brief: Returns the items that are not empty, so the empty text is dropped and every number stays.

methods.name: Sum
methods.brief: Returns the sum of the numbers in the list.
methods.returns: a number; 0 for an empty list

methods.name: Product
methods.brief: Returns the product of the numbers in the list.
methods.returns: a number; 0 for an empty list

methods.name: MinValue
methods.brief: Returns the smallest number in the list.
methods.returns: a number; 0 for an empty list

methods.name: MaxValue
methods.brief: Returns the largest number in the list.
methods.returns: a number; 0 for an empty list

methods.name: CountItems
methods.brief: Returns how many items the list has, by the engine count.

methods.name: CountStrings
methods.brief: Returns how many items are text.

methods.name: CountNumbers
methods.brief: Returns how many items are numbers.

methods.name: AnyTrue
methods.brief: Returns 1 if at least one item is non-zero, else 0.
notes: the answer is a number, not TRUE or FALSE

methods.name: AllTrue
methods.brief: Returns 1 if every item is non-zero, else 0.
notes: the answer is a number, not TRUE or FALSE

classes.name: stzZipFile
classes.brief: Creates, extends, lists and unpacks a zip archive named by a path.
classes.description: CreateFrom builds an archive from a list of files and AddFile and AddFiles extend an existing one; each file is stored under the path as given, so give relative paths. ListContents, FileCount and Contains read the entry names, and ExtractTo, ExtractHere and ExtractToNewFolder unpack them. CopyTo, MoveTo and Delete act on the archive file itself. Three things do not work today and are warned on their methods: AddString, CreateFromDirectory and a correct Size. Extracting an archive whose entry names are absolute paths ends the Ring process.
classes.example:
? o1.Exists()
#--> 0
? o1.FileCount()
#--> 0
? o1.IsEmpty()
#--> 1

methods.name: init
methods.brief: Builds a handle on a zip archive path; nothing is read or created until a method is called.

parameters.name: cZipFileName
parameters.role: the path of the archive, existing or to be created

methods.name: CreateFrom
methods.brief: Creates the archive, replacing any existing one, from the files of a list that exist; a missing file is skipped without a message.

parameters.name: _aFiles_
parameters.role: the list of file paths

notes: give relative paths to get entries that extract anywhere
warnings: raises Files parameter must be a list for anything else; a path given as absolute is stored as absolute, and extracting such an archive ends the Ring process (see ExtractTo)

extensions.name: CreateFromQ
extensions.adds: does what the method does, then returns the object, so the call can be chained

methods.name: CreateFromSingleFile
methods.brief: Creates the archive from one file, as CreateFrom does for a list of one.

parameters.name: cFileName
parameters.role: the file to store, under the path as given

extensions.name: CreateFromSingleFileQ
extensions.adds: does what the method does, then returns the object, so the call can be chained

methods.name: CreateFromDirectory
methods.brief: Raises error R3 today instead of creating the archive from every file of a folder.

parameters.name: _cDirPath_
parameters.role: the folder meant to be zipped

notes: build the file list yourself and call CreateFrom
warnings: the call FilesInDir does not exist anywhere in the library, so an existing folder raises R3 Calling Function without definition: filesindir; a missing folder raises Directory does not exist

extensions.name: CreateFromDirectoryQ
extensions.adds: does what the method does, then returns the object, so the call can be chained

methods.name: AddFile
methods.brief: Appends an existing file to an existing archive; the same file added twice is stored twice.

parameters.name: cFileName
parameters.role: the file to add, stored under the path as given

notes: use CreateFrom to start an archive
warnings: raises File does not exist for a missing file; on an archive that does not exist yet it returns the path and creates nothing, so no entry is added and no error is raised

extensions.name: AddFileQ
extensions.adds: does what the method does, then returns the object, so the call can be chained

methods.name: AddFiles
methods.brief: Appends the files of a list to an existing archive, skipping those that do not exist; a file already inside is stored a second time.

parameters.name: _aFiles_
parameters.role: the list of file paths, each stored as given

warnings: raises Files parameter must be a list for anything else; like AddFile, it creates nothing on an archive that does not exist yet

extensions.name: AddFilesQ
extensions.adds: does what the method does, then returns the object, so the call can be chained

methods.name: AddString
methods.brief: Raises error R3 today instead of storing a text as an entry of the archive.

parameters.name: cEntryName
parameters.role: the entry name meant for the text

parameters.name: cContent
parameters.role: the text meant to be stored

notes: write the text to a file and use CreateFrom
warnings: the zip_newentry function it calls does not exist (checked by calling it directly), so every call raises R3 Calling Function without definition: zip_newentry

extensions.name: AddStringQ
extensions.adds: does what the method does, then returns the object, so the call can be chained

methods.name: ExtractTo
methods.brief: Extracts every entry under a folder, keeping each entry's own relative path, and returns the folder.

parameters.name: _cTargetDir_
parameters.role: the folder to extract into

notes: create the archive with relative paths, as CreateFrom explains
warnings: raises Zip file does not exist for a missing archive; an archive whose entries have absolute paths ends the Ring process at once with exit 127 and no message when the folder already exists, and extracts nothing when it does not

extensions.name: ExtractToQ
extensions.adds: does what the method does, then returns the object, so the call can be chained

methods.name: ExtractHere
methods.brief: Extracts the archive into the folder that holds it.
methods.returns: the folder path, . when the archive path has none
warnings: raises Zip file does not exist for a missing archive; the same absolute-path risk as ExtractTo

extensions.name: ExtractHereQ
extensions.adds: does what the method does, then returns the object, so the call can be chained

methods.name: ExtractToNewFolder
methods.brief: Extracts the archive into a new folder beside it, named like the archive without its extension.
methods.returns: the folder path, such as here/nf for here/nf.zip
warnings: raises Zip file does not exist for a missing archive; the same absolute-path risk as ExtractTo

extensions.name: ExtractToNewFolderQ
extensions.adds: does what the method does, then returns the object, so the call can be chained

methods.name: ListContents
methods.brief: Returns the names of the entries, exactly as stored, in the order they were added.
notes: a file stored twice is listed twice
warnings: raises Zip file does not exist for a missing archive

extensions.name: ListContentsQ
extensions.adds: does what the method does, then returns the object, so the call can be chained

methods.name: FileCount
methods.brief: Returns how many entries the archive holds, 0 for a missing or unreadable archive.

methods.name: Contains
methods.brief: TRUE if an entry has exactly this name, as stored: a file added by absolute path matches only by that path.

parameters.name: cFileName
parameters.role: the entry name

warnings: raises Zip file does not exist for a missing archive

methods.name: IsEmpty
methods.brief: TRUE if the archive holds no entry, which is also true when it does not exist.

methods.name: Size
methods.brief: Returns the size of the archive file, but 0 for an archive that holds files.
methods.returns: a number; 98 for an archive with no entry, 0 today for a non-empty one
notes: 0 also means the archive does not exist
warnings: the size is counted as characters of the file read as text, which gives 0 for the compressed bytes of a non-empty archive (a 478-byte archive reads 0, an empty one reads 98); use len(read(path)) for the byte count

methods.name: FileName
methods.brief: Returns the archive path given at birth, or the new path after a MoveTo.

methods.name: Exists
methods.brief: TRUE if the archive file exists on disk.

methods.name: Delete
methods.brief: Removes the archive file; an archive that is already gone is not an error.

extensions.name: DeleteQ
extensions.adds: does what the method does, then returns the object, so the call can be chained

methods.name: CopyTo
methods.brief: Copies the archive file to another path and tells whether the copy is there.

parameters.name: cDestination
parameters.role: the path of the copy

warnings: raises Can't create/open the file (R35) when the archive does not exist

extensions.name: CopyToQ
extensions.adds: does what the method does, then returns the object, so the call can be chained

methods.name: MoveTo
methods.brief: Copies the archive to another path, removes the original and makes the object point at the new path.

parameters.name: cDestination
parameters.role: the new path

warnings: raises Can't create/open the file (R35) when the archive does not exist

extensions.name: MoveToQ
extensions.adds: does what the method does, then returns the object, so the call can be chained

classes.name: TableConfigManager
classes.brief: Changes the settings of a table layout in batches, exports and imports them, and is meant to fire a callback on change.
classes.description: It works on a copy of the config it is given, readable as its oConfig attribute: a change made through the manager does not reach the config you built it from. The change callback does not fire today and OptimizeLayout has no lasting effect; the warnings on those methods give the causes.
classes.example:
o1.UpdateSettings([ [ :MinCellWidth, 9 ] ])
? o1.oConfig.aSettings[:MinCellWidth]
#--> 9
? len(o1.ExportConfig())
#--> 2

methods.name: init
methods.brief: Builds a manager that changes the settings of a table layout and fires a callback on change.

parameters.name: oTableConfig
parameters.role: the TableDisplayConfig to manage

warnings: the manager keeps a COPY of the config: every change it makes lands on that copy, readable as its oConfig attribute, and your own config stays as it was

methods.name: SetChangeCallback
methods.brief: Stores a function meant to run after each settings change.

parameters.name: fCallback
parameters.role: the function to call, with no argument

methods.returns: the manager itself, so calls chain
warnings: the callback never runs today: the check compares the type of the stored function with BLOCK, and Ring answers STRING for a function value; confirmed on UpdateSettings, ImportConfig and OptimizeLayout

methods.name: UpdateSettings
methods.brief: Applies several settings at once, then recomputes the layout.

parameters.name: aNewSettings
parameters.role: a list of [ name, value ] pairs, such as [ [ :MinCellWidth, 9 ] ]

methods.returns: the manager itself, so calls chain
warnings: it changes the manager's own copy of the config, not yours

methods.name: OptimizeLayout
methods.brief: Rebalances the computed widths towards their average and scales them down when the table is wider than MaxTableWidth.
methods.returns: the manager itself, so calls chain
warnings: it has no lasting effect today: the last step recomputes the whole layout and overwrites the adjusted widths, so the widths after it are the ones a plain recomputation gives, with a MaxTableWidth of 20 as with the default; it works on the manager's own copy of the config

methods.name: ExportConfig
methods.brief: Returns the current settings and the computed layout as one list.
methods.returns: a list [ Settings, Layout ] holding the aSettings and aCalculatedLayout of the managed config

methods.name: ImportConfig
methods.brief: Applies the settings found in a list made by ExportConfig, then recomputes the layout.

parameters.name: _aConfig_
parameters.role: the list, with a Settings entry holding [ name, value ] pairs

methods.returns: the manager itself, so calls chain
warnings: it changes the manager's own copy of the config, not yours

classes.name: TableDisplayConfig
classes.brief: Measures a two-dimension pivot table and computes the width of every column, the layout a console renderer draws from.
classes.description: It is built from the pivot as a list of rows: a header row (the row labels, one dim1|dim2 header per data column, the total label), the data rows and a row of totals. It measures the content into aContentDimensions, then turns measures and settings into aCalculatedLayout; both are attributes you read directly. The settings are in aSettings (MinCellWidth, MaxCellWidth, MaxHeaderWidth, DefaultPadding, CellGrowthRatio and others), and SetSetting recomputes after each change. Known limits: it needs exactly two column dimensions, and today the width of a data column ignores its content, which the warnings on CalculateLayout and MeasureContentDimensions explain.
classes.example:
? @@( o1.GetUniqueColumnDimensionValues() )
#--> [ [ "2024" ], [ "Q1", "Q2" ] ]
? @@( o1.aCalculatedLayout[:RowLabelWidths] )
#--> [ 11 ]
? o1.aCalculatedLayout[:TotalColumnWidth]
#--> 8
o1.SetSetting(:MinCellWidth, 8)
? o1.aSettings[:MinCellWidth]
#--> 8

methods.name: init
methods.brief: Builds the layout of a console pivot table from its data: measures the content, then computes every width.

parameters.name: aPivotTable
parameters.role: the pivot as a list of rows: a header row (the row labels, then one header per data column holding the two column values joined by a vertical bar, such as 2024 then Q1, then the total label), the data rows, and a last row of totals

parameters.name: aRowDims
parameters.role: the names of the row dimensions

parameters.name: aColDims
parameters.role: the names of the two column dimensions

parameters.name: cTotalLbl
parameters.role: the label of the total column and of the total row

notes: the measures land in aContentDimensions and the final widths in aCalculatedLayout, two attributes you can read
warnings: it needs exactly two column dimensions: one raises error R2, an empty pivot raises it too, and a third is ignored

methods.name: MeasureContentDimensions
methods.brief: Measures the natural width of the row labels, column headers, data cells and totals, and stores them in aContentDimensions.
warnings: the width kept for a data column is that of the LAST data row, not the widest: a column holding 20 and then 2 is stored as 1 wide; the test that should keep the maximum asks whether a number is a hashlist, which is always false

methods.name: GetUniqueColumnDimensionValues
methods.brief: Returns the distinct values of each column dimension, read from the two-part headers of the pivot.
methods.returns: a list with one list of text per column dimension, in the order of first appearance

methods.name: CalculateLayout
methods.brief: Computes the final widths from the measures and the settings, and stores them in aCalculatedLayout.
warnings: the measured data-cell widths are never used: each data column gets the MinCellWidth setting grown by CellGrowthRatio plus padding, however wide its content, because the lookup asks whether a number is a hashlist; row labels and the total column do use their measures

methods.name: GetDimensionGroupWidth
methods.brief: Raises error R5 today instead of returning the width of one group of columns.

parameters.name: nDimIndex
parameters.role: the column dimension to measure, which the body does not read

methods.returns: nothing; it raises Can't access the list item, Object is not list
warnings: it reads a variable that belongs to CalculateLayout and is empty here; the same error for 1 and for 2

methods.name: GetCellWidth
methods.brief: Returns the MinCellWidth setting, whatever the pair of values, instead of the width computed for that data column.

parameters.name: _dim1_
parameters.role: the value of the first column dimension, such as 2024

parameters.name: _dim2_
parameters.role: the value of the second, such as Q1

warnings: the lookup asks whether a width, which is a number, is a hashlist, which is always false, so the fallback is always taken; with MinCellWidth 5 it answers 5 while the layout holds 8

methods.name: SetSetting
methods.brief: Sets one display setting, then recomputes the layout.

parameters.name: cSetting
parameters.role: the name of the setting, such as MinCellWidth or DefaultPadding

parameters.name: _value_
parameters.role: the new value

methods.returns: the config itself, so calls chain
warnings: the settings are in aSettings: MinCellWidth, MaxCellWidth, MaxHeaderWidth, DefaultPadding, CellGrowthRatio, RowLabelGrowthRatio, MaxTableWidth and others

methods.name: GetLayoutValue
methods.brief: Returns one entry of the computed layout, but only when that entry is itself a hashlist.

parameters.name: _cKey_
parameters.role: the layout key, such as DataColumnWidths or TableWidth

methods.returns: the hashlist of data column widths for DataColumnWidths; an empty text for every other key, numbers and lists included
warnings: TableWidth, TotalColumnWidth, LeftPadding and RowLabelWidths all answer an empty text; read aCalculatedLayout directly for them

methods.name: Recalculate
methods.brief: Measures the content again and recomputes the layout, after the data or a setting changed.
methods.returns: the config itself, so calls chain

methods.name: DebugLayout
methods.brief: Prints the computed dimensions: row label widths, data column widths, total column, table width and left padding.
warnings: the Data Column Widths part prints no line today, for the same hashlist test as GetCellWidth

classes.name: TableRenderer
classes.brief: Prints a pivot table as text from a TableDisplayConfig: borders, two header lines, the data rows and the total row.
classes.description: It reads the widths already computed by the config and prints with the question-mark statement, one line at a time, using box-drawing characters that a theme can swap for plain ones. It keeps a copy of the config it is given, so build it after the settings are final. Today the printed table does not line up: the header block is narrower than the data rows and the total row falls below the bottom border (see the warning on RenderTable).
classes.example:
? classname(o1)
#--> tablerenderer

methods.name: init
methods.brief: Builds a renderer over a table layout, to print the pivot table as text.

parameters.name: oTableConfig
parameters.role: the TableDisplayConfig that holds the data, the settings and the computed widths

warnings: the renderer keeps a COPY of the config: a setting changed on your own config afterwards does not reach it, so build the renderer after the settings are final

methods.name: RenderTable
methods.brief: Prints the whole table: the headers, the data rows and the footer.
warnings: the printed table does not line up today: the top border and the two header lines are as wide as the column groups alone, narrower than the data rows, the separators of the headers do not sit above those of the rows, and the grand-total row is printed under the bottom border; the same on two different pivots

methods.name: RenderTableHeaders
methods.brief: Prints the top border, the two header lines (first and second column dimension), and the separator above the data rows.
warnings: the widths used for each data column come from a lookup that always falls back to MinCellWidth, so these lines are narrower than the data rows under them

methods.name: RenderDataRows
methods.brief: Prints one line per data row, with the first row label shown only when it changes and an empty line between two groups.
warnings: it shows at most two row labels per line, and groups by the first

methods.name: RenderEmptyRow
methods.brief: Prints one blank line inside the table's side borders, used between two groups of rows.

methods.name: RenderTableFooter
methods.brief: Prints the bottom border, then the total row when the config shows it.
warnings: the total row is printed below the bottom border, without a left border

classes.name: TableThemeManager
classes.brief: Holds named looks for a table layout, four built in and any you create, each a set of widths, padding and border characters.
classes.description: The built-in themes are Default (rounded box-drawing borders), Simple and Compact (plain plus and dash characters), and Elegant (square box-drawing corners). ApplyTheme sets the theme's settings and border characters and recomputes the layout. Like the other managers it works on a copy of the config it is given, readable as its oConfig attribute.
classes.example:
? @@( o1.ListThemes() )
#--> [ "default", "simple", "compact", "elegant" ]
o1.ApplyTheme(:Compact)
? o1.oConfig.aSettings[:DefaultPadding]
#--> 0
? o1.oConfig.aDecorators[:BorderChars][:TopLeft]
#--> +

methods.name: init
methods.brief: Builds a manager of named looks, set of widths and border characters, for a table layout.

parameters.name: oTableConfig
parameters.role: the TableDisplayConfig the themes are applied to

warnings: the manager keeps a COPY of the config: a theme applied lands on that copy, readable as its oConfig attribute, and your own config stays as it was

methods.name: ApplyTheme
methods.brief: Applies a named theme's widths, padding and border characters to the config, then recomputes the layout.

parameters.name: _cThemeName_
parameters.role: the theme's name, such as Default, Simple, Compact, Elegant or one made by CreateTheme, without regard to case

methods.returns: the manager itself, so calls chain
warnings: an unknown name prints Theme not found and applies Default; the theme lands on the manager's own copy of the config, not yours

methods.name: CreateTheme
methods.brief: Adds a named theme, or replaces one, from a list of settings.

parameters.name: _cThemeName_
parameters.role: the new theme's name

parameters.name: aThemeSettings
parameters.role: a hashlist of settings, such as [ :MinCellWidth = 12 ], with an optional BorderChars hashlist

methods.returns: the manager itself, so calls chain

methods.name: ListThemes
methods.brief: Returns the names of the themes available, the four built in and those created.
methods.returns: a list of text in lower case, such as default, simple, compact, elegant

classes.name: WITH
classes.brief: Names the intermediate table of an SQL statement so that later code can read it, as a SQL WITH clause does.
classes.description: WITH(name).As(...) stores the current intermediate result under the name, as the rows and as the table. The SQL emulation is a set of functions on global state: CREATE_TABLE, INSERT_INTO, VALUES, SELECT, FROM_, WHERE_ and ORDER_BY. Only the registration is shown here, from an intermediate table set directly. See the warning of As for what is broken today.
classes.example:
_oIntermediateTable = new stzTable([ :ID = [1, 2], :NAME = [ "a", "b" ] ])
o1.As([ 1 ])
? v("big")[2][2]
#--> b

methods.name: init
methods.brief: Builds the statement part that names a result set, from the name it will be given.

parameters.name: pcSQL
parameters.role: the name to give the intermediate result, such as recent

warnings: raises Incorrect param type for a name that is not a text

methods.name: As
methods.brief: Registers the intermediate table under the name, as four named variables: the name, nameData, nameTable and nameObject.

parameters.name: paParams
parameters.role: a list of one to three items, read only for its length

notes: the first call is the only one that works; the rows read back with v(name)
warnings: a second call with a name already registered writes all four values into the slot of the first, which then reads nameObject, and a third call raises on the hash list; CREATE_TABLE itself raises today on an stzTable, so the pipeline that feeds the intermediate table does not run end to end
